We introduce an additive thermodynamic correction layer that shifts phase free energies towards an assessed reference without retraining or modifying the base potential. A first order thermodynamic construction converts the required phase free energy shifts directly into configuration energy targets, which are fitted using a linear atomic cluster expansion and refined iteratively from measured free energies. We apply the method to melting and solid to solid transformations across elements with different crystal structures using a foundation GRACE model. After the correction, all transformation temperatures lie within the prescribed tolerance of the assessed values, including Ca, Ti, and Zr, where a solid to solid transition and melting are corrected together. Static energy curves, bulk moduli, and liquid structure remain close to those of the base model. Vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density depend on the corrected phase balance and change where the correction is large. The method requires neither retraining, differentiable dynamics, nor access to the parameters of the base potential. It provides a modular route for combining transferable atomistic models with assessed phase thermodynamics.
authors: Sarath Menon, Braulio Sanchez Ortega, Ralf Drautz

articles.title: Spontaneous magnetic diode effect in Co₁/₃TaS₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co₁/₃TaS₂, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.
authors: Yining Hu, Taikang Chen, Jan Priessnitz, Zili Feng, Takashi Kurumaji, Linda Ye, Libor Šmejkal, Chunyu Mark Guo, Philip J. W. Moll

articles.title: Non-magnetic impurities as a quantum microscope of finite size effects in spin chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-size effects are ubiquitous in quantum matter, yet typically invisible in the thermodynamic limit; when system size is restricted, boundaries and confinement reveal modified spectra, correlations, and emergent phenomena. With growing access to well-controlled few-spin systems, these effects are now directly observable and offer a route to probing universal physics and enabling quantum information applications. Here, we study finite-size physics in the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet Ba(Co₁₋ₓMgₓ₎₂V₂O₈ with x = 2% and x = 5%, where non-magnetic Mg²⁺ ions fragment the Co²⁺ spin chains into finite segments. Combining inelastic neutron scattering and numerical calculations, we identify distinct regimes with fundamentally different low-energy quantum excitations: spinons confined to chain boundaries, and a cluster mode in shorter chains corresponding to a collective reversal of the Néel-ordered segment without classical analogue. Our results demonstrate how chemical substitution acts as a quantum microscope providing direct access to boundary-shaped excitations in strongly correlated spin systems.
authors: Quentin Faure, Shintaro Takayoshi, Virginie Simonet, Béatrice Grenier, Stéphane Raymond, Eric Ressouche, Xavier Fabrèges, Pascal Lejay, Thierry Giamarchi, Sylvain Petit

articles.title: Synthetic staggered fields switch Neel vectors probed by magnetic resonance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrical detection of antiferromagnetic order is a critical challenge for antiferromagnetic spintronics owing to their vanishing macroscopic magnetisation. While magnetic resonance has demonstrated sub-terahertz antiferromagnetic spin pumping and nonlinear magnon dynamics, its application to electrically contacted on-chip devices has room for further exploration. Here we show that magnetic resonance enables direct electrical detection of Néel vector states. A 180ⁱ̧rc reversal in synthetic antiferromagnets is realised by current-driven effective fields with opposite polarisation acting on each magnetic sublayer, which we term synthetic staggered fields. The switching induces a π phase shift of precessional motion in time, producing hysteretic rectified voltages in our phase-sensitive detection scheme. Angular-dependent resonance analysis offers further insight into the Néel vector directions, pointing to a model beyond the macrospin formalism. We address this by defect-incorporated micromagnetic simulations that reveal fragmented domain states after current excitation. An extracted current density of 7.4×10⁹ A/m² is, to our knowledge, the lowest reported value for the room-temperature Néel vector switching and we show that it scales with the in-plane uniaxial anisotropy both experimentally and numerically. Synthetic staggered fields and the resonance-based methodology provide a research platform for nanoscale characterisation of electrically driven antiferromagnetic textures, guiding the development of high-frequency on-chip spintronic architectures.
authors: Yifang Hao, Zhiyi Che, Jack Brierley, Aakanksha Sud, Satoshi Iihama, Rishi Siddani, Chenghao Yang, Charlie W. F. Freeman, Troy Dion, Daniel Prestwood, Zekun Xue, Tianyi Wei, Murat Cubukcu, Craig Barton, Shunsuke Fukami, Shigemi Mizukami, Hidekazu Kurebayashi

articles.title: Reference-state dependence and interface scaling of superfluid response in a two-dimensional crystal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grain boundaries modify both transport paths and the surrounding crystal, making their contribution to superfluid stiffness difficult to isolate. We quantify these contributions in stationary two-dimensional soft-core Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) crystals using tensor response, independently prepared bicrystals, and measured interface lengths. A one-percent change of lattice spacing alters the bulk stiffness by approximately 5--9%, comparable to the boundary contribution. For the same defective state, two bulk references give relative excesses of 0.027% and 4.15%. Matching the comparator to grain strain and chemical potential yields positive diagonal excesses in paired preparations at three interaction strengths. Within a twelve-state family with comparable grain interiors, the excess is robust to 288 bulk substitutions and follows an approximate length-per-area relation. Independent fixed-area pairs yield a line-response coefficient 3.1% higher than the three-size estimate. Size and directional dependence restrict this relation to the specified crystal conditions. Reduced link networks relate the directional response to the organization of boundary connections but do not accurately resolve every small bulk-subtracted excess. The results distinguish boundary enhancement from changes in the surrounding crystal and establish a quantitative comparison protocol for superfluid transport in defective crystals.

articles.title: Magnetoelectric Exchange Spring for Spin-Wave Logic with Ultralow Energy Consumption
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin waves (magnons) are intrinsically free of Joule heating during their propagation in magnets. Exploring, understanding, and manipulating such quasiparticles not only helps reveal the exotic magnonic phenomena in condensed matter physics but also underpins the development of information devices with low energy consumption. However, achieving low-power and scalable control of spin-wave propagation remains a critical challenge. Herein, a magnetoelectric exchange spring has been artificially designed and constructed across an interface between ferroelectric BaTiO3 and ferromagnetic (La,Sr)MnO3 with low magnetic damping, in which polarization-modulated orbital reconstruction tailors local magnetic anisotropy and enables reversible control of spin-wave propagation. By successfully deviating from the Janovec-Kay-Dunn law, reversal polarization of engineered BaTiO3 (Ps~1.2 uC cm⁻², Vc~0.4 V) is sufficient to switch the coherent magnon transport in the (La,Sr)MnO3, indicating the magnetoelectric heterointerface may serve as a promising candidate for atto-joule control of spin-wave propagation (normalized to a 10*10 nm² device). Furthermore, taking advantage of amplitude, phase, and frequency to encode spin waves, all 16 compact Boolean logics with ultralow energy consumption have been designed. The artificial magnetoelectric exchange spring can be broadly applicable to various material choices, offering a versatile platform for developing energy-efficient and integrated magnonic devices.
authors: Aiji Wang, Mingming Li, Yuben Yang, Hanchen Wang, Yuelin Zhang, Liang Yang, Kai Liu, Sheng Cheng, Yang Yang, Yu Yun, Tianxiang Nan, Ka Shen, Tao Zhu, Xiufeng Han, Haiming Yu, Ce-Wen Nan, Jinxing Zhang

articles.title: Optimised growth of epitaxial D019 Mn3Ge(0001) thin films via single target sputtering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials with chemical identity Mn3X, where X is Sn, Ga, or Ge, are Heusler alloys with intriguing properties that are fundamentally and technologically interesting. They have topological properties with a non-trivial band structure that identify them as Weyl semimetals in the bulk. Their magnetic properties, which give rise to the topological band structure through spin-orbit coupling, are determined by their Kagome lattice structure, making them chiral non-collinear antiferromagnets. Among these materials, Mn3Ge is particularly interesting because it has a larger Berry curvature, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity and motivating potential spintronic applications. The desirable properties are only obtained when Mn3Ge has the D019 crystal structure, so producing an easily reproducible growth recipe is the main objective of this paper. Here we show that ultra-high-quality thin films of Mn3Ge with D019 symmetry can be grown from a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3(0001) substrate with a Ru(0001) seed layer. The expected non-collinear antiferromagnetic order was confirmed by the finding of weak zero-field magnetisation (0.0086 +/- 0.0002) mu_B/Mn that does not saturate at high magnetic fields and has a Neel temperature of (291 +/- 2) K.
authors: Servet Ozdemir, Ping-Luen Ho, Callum Brennan-Rich, Matthew Rogers, Philippa Shepley, Ahmet Yagmur, Ismet Gelen, Sehwan Song, Zabeada Aslam, Mannan Ali, Shelly Conroy, Sandrine Heutz, Gavin Burnell, B J Hickey

articles.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. Through the combined operation of these layers, the device achieves a large memory window, an on/off current ratio exceeding 10⁶, stable multilevel conductance states, and reliable retention over 10⁴ s. Broadband visible-to-near-infrared optical excitation enables controllable synaptic weight modulation and the emulation of essential synaptic functions, including short- and long-term plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, and pulse-amplitude- and pulse-duration-dependent plasticity. Optical potentiation and electrical depression further enable bidirectional modulation of synaptic weights. Beyond these synaptic functions, the device demonstrates higher-order learning through associative and discrimination conditioning inspired by the Pavlovian learning paradigm, as well as reconfigurable Boolean logic driven by electro-optical inputs. These results establish a multifunctional van der Waals floating-gate platform that integrates nonvolatile memory, broadband optoelectronic learning, and adaptive information processing within a single transistor, providing a promising strategy for compact, energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware.
authors: Thi Phuong Anh Bach, Sangeun Cho

articles.title: Electronic Responses in Solid Oxygen with Coexisting Structural and Magnetic Orders
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solid oxygen provides a unique platform for studying the interplay between structural and magnetic degrees of freedom, as each O₂ molecule possesses an S=1 spin and weak intermolecular van der Waals interactions allow substantial structural flexibility. In addition, because of its small intermolecular hopping integrals, this system is known to be a strongly correlated electron system with a multiorbital nature. In this study, we examine electronic states and magnetic and dielectric responses using a multiorbital Hubbard model with Peierls-type electron-lattice coupling. This model provides a minimal description of the interplay between structural and magnetic degrees of freedom in solid oxygen. We apply the Hartree-Fock approximation to obtain the ground-state phase diagram. Antiferromagnetic order appears when the onsite Coulomb interaction is strong, whereas three nonmagnetic bond-ordered states emerge when it is weak. At intermediate interaction strengths, antiferromagnetic order coexists with each of the three bond orders. These three coexistence phases all break time-reversal symmetry; one preserves spatial inversion symmetry, whereas the other two also break it. The two inversion-breaking phases exhibit linear magnetoelectric responses, whereas the inversion-symmetric phase exhibits altermagnetic spin splitting and a piezomagnetic response. These responses may provide experimental signatures of coexisting magnetic and structural orders in high-pressure solid oxygen suggested by recent experiments.
authors: Naomichi Sato, Makoto Naka, Joji Nasu

articles.title: Magnetic susceptibility and superfluid density of inhomogeneous superconducting films: the Tc-mosaic model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whole-sample and mutual-inductance part-sample measurements of the linear magnetic susceptibility, ḩi, of superconducting films are routinely used to obtain the London penetration depth, łambda(T), assuming uniform superconductivity. However, spatially resolved probes show that many films of current interest are inhomogeneous on micrometer scales. Here we ask whether a distribution of local transition temperatures in a fully gapped film can produce an apparent line-nodal, T-linear łambda(T). The film is modeled as a random Voronoi mosaic of domains with T_c distributed between Tc,ₘᵢₙ and Tc,ₘₐₓ with s-wave (also d-wave, for comparison) London response inside each domain. We show that detectable screening appears only below the percolation temperature, Tₚ, and the transition broadens with the spread of T_c. For s-wave domains, łambda(T) remains activated for any Tc,ₘᵢₙ>0. Only for Tc,ₘᵢₙ=0 does it become a power law, Δłambdapropto Tⁿ with napprox1.7, but then the onset of screening drops to Tₚ₌Tc,ₘₐₓ/2. Weighting the Tc distribution towards T_c→0 (more low-Tc domains) can bring n closer to 1 (napprox1.2), but simultaneously pushes the apparent transition, Tₚ, more than an order of magnitude below Tc,ₘₐₓ. For d-wave domains, the linear term survives, and its relative slope is enhanced almost fourfold for Tc,ₘᵢₙ=0. Hence, a T-linear łambda(T) measured in a film with screening onset within a factor of a few of Tc,ₘₐₓ by whole-sample or mutual-inductance part-sample measurements cannot originate from T_c mosaicity in a fully gapped superconductor.

articles.title: Equivalent Pseudo-angular Momentum Governs Selective Magnon-Phonon Hybridization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnon-phonon hybridization provides a powerful route to couple spin and lattice excitations, yet the symmetry principle governing mode selectivity remains unclear. Here, we show that crystalline pseudoangular momentum provides a general criterion for selective magnon-phonon hybridization in noncollinear multisublattice magnetic systems. The rotation eigenvalue associated with pseudoangular momentum encodes polarization transformations, sublattice permutations, and Bloch phases, requiring magnetoelastic coupling between modes belonging to the same rotation sector. We illustrate this principle in a stacked kagome model with noncollinear spin order. An out-of-plane magnetic field tunes one magnon sector into resonance with a degenerate phonon doublet, yet only the pseudoangular-momentum-matched phonon develops a pronounced avoided crossing while the other remains nearly unmixed. Field reversal switches the selected rotation sector and reverses the rotational polarization of the hybridized phonon component without changing the hybrid-mode energies. Our results reveal pseudoangular-momentum matching as a general framework for understanding and controlling mode-selective spin-lattice hybridization.
authors: Hong Sun, Hao Chen, Lifa Zhang

articles.title: Dynamic helimagnetism via charged spin current
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a theoretical and numerical study of classical, localized spins coupled to conduction electrons that carry both charge and spin currents, deriving the effective equations of motion from the s-d exchange Hamiltonian. Applied to a periodically arranged one-dimensional spin chain, these equations yield two current-driven helical phases: a static helix stabilized by a pure spin current alone, and a coherently precessing helix that appears once a small charge-current component is added. For a given helical wavenumber, the precession angular frequency ømega and the canting ratio Δ toward the hard axis follow analytically from the equations of motion, while the wavenumber qₘ̊ ₕₑₗᵢₓ of the precessing helix is selected by a heuristically constructed effective Lagrangian. Direct numerical integration of the same equations of motion reproduces all three observables wherever it yields a coherent helix. The helix chirality is set by a long-range, current-generated Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM)-type coupling rather than an intrinsic DM interaction, so materials without bulk or interfacial DM interactions could also host current-controlled helical order. Because the helical pitch, precession frequency, and canting ratio are all continuously tunable by the current amplitudes, these helices could serve as probes of spin currents.

articles.title: Trajectory Functionals in the Thermodynamics of Radiation-Induced Damage in Structural Materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper delivers a novel self-consistent non-local kinetic framework based on dose-dependent semi-Markov renewal transport and the generalized Doob's h-transform to evaluate the structural degradation of WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings. By leveraging the Feynman-Kac formalism, we map the continuous microscopic defect path trajectories generated by the Liouville operator directly onto the evolution of the macroscopically integrated damage potential. The framework accounts for long-range memory effects in the degradation kinetics via a non-vanishing structural commutator of the path Liouville operator and Zwanzig-Mori projection operators, which mathematically links the spatial restrictions of microscopic sinks to energetic path penalties. Spatial profiling of the cladding's mean lifetime, demonstrates a distinct sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory encompassing distinct incubation, linear growth, and avalanche breakdown stages. The numerical results reveal an abrupt, localized reduction in the operational lifespan near the cladding boundaries. This marginal vulnerability is shown to be a direct physical consequence of boundary stress field singularities at the fuel cladding interface and localized embrittlement. The developed path integral architecture provides a strict thermodynamic link between non-equilibrium fluctuations and the global Griffiths macro-barrier, offering a robust predictive tool for high-burnup nuclear fuel safety assessments.

articles.title: Rigid Band Shift in Electron-Doped Kagome Metal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the effects of Sn-site doping on the electronic structure of nonmagnetic kagome metal YV₆Sn₆₋ₓSbₓ by infrared spectroscopy and density-functional theory. The results for samples with x = 0 and 1.4 demonstrate that partial substitution of Sn by Sb acts as a rigid shift of the Fermi level while leaving the band dispersion largely intact. Our findings establish Sn-site substitution in YV₆Sn₆ as a route to systematically investigate band-filling-dependent electronic properties of nonmagnetic kagome metals.
authors: M. Pinterić, E. Uykur, S. Salters, G. Pokharel, S. D. Wilson, M. Dressel, M. Wenzel

articles.title: Temperature-dependent magnetic properties of the antiferromagnet Mn₂Au
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mn₂Au is one of the most promising materials for antiferromagnetic spintronics due to its high Néel temperature, moderate anisotropy, layered spin structure allowing current induced spin-orbit-torques, and ultrafast spin dynamics. Further understanding and control of the magnetic order in Mn₂Au for ultrafast spintronics applications via ultrashort electric/optical means requires accurate understanding of how its magnetic properties depend on temperature. Here we present atomistic spin dynamics simulations of the temperature-dependent macroscopic magnetic properties of Mn₂Au single crystals. We introduce a spin Hamiltonian based on previous ab initio calculations which produces temperature-dependent scaling of the anisotropy constants with magnetisation consistent with Zener-Akulov-Callen-Callen power laws. The calculated temperature dependence of exchange stiffness follows a scaling law with magnetisation of m¹.⁸³ₑ , and predicts a temperature-dependent domain wall width that agrees very well with direct simulation. Our model provides an understanding of temperature-dependent magnetic properties of Mn₂Au that enables large-scale simulation of the working conditions of spintronic devices.
authors: Jackson L. Ross, Sarah Jenkins, Ricardco Rama-Eiroa, Paul-Iulian Gavriloaea, Jack Collins, Unai Atxitia, Oksana Chubykalo-Fesenko, Karin Everschor-Sitte, Rubén M. Otxoa, Roy W. Chantrell, Richard F. L. Evans

articles.title: Control of the Electronic and Atomic Structure of the Altermagnetic α-MnTe Surface via Substrate-Induced Surfactants
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnets are a novel class of materials with unique momentum dependent spin-polarization of the electronic band structure, which opens up new avenues for spintronic devices. Altermagnetic α-MnTe is particularly interesting for such applications due to its giant spin splitting and the persistence of altermagnetic order up to room temperature. Growth of thin films is, however, challenging and governed by interactions with the substrate. As a result, the surface of α-MnTe thin films exhibits very different atomic structures in dependence of the substrate material. Whereas on SrF2(111) an atomically clean, perfectly (2x2) reconstructed surface forms, on InP(111)A the MnTe surface is always InTe terminated due to super-segregation of In from the substrate to the surface. Most strikingly, the InTe surfactant layer displays a quasi-periodic dislocation network to accommodate the InTe/MnTe lattice mismatch. This leads to the emergence of distinct surface states in dependence of surface termination that strongly affect the electronic band structure at the surface as shown by angle resolved photoemission and tunneling spectroscopy. Thus, control and characterization of the atomic structure of the surface is fundamentally important for understanding the properties of altermagnets and provides room for engineering and tailoring of spin-polarized states in actual devices.
authors: Martin Heinrich, Mahdi Hajlaoui, Takuya Takashiro, Tetiana Zakusylo, Petr Babor, Ondrej Caha, Dawid Wutke, Natalia Olszowska, Gunther Springholz, Matthias Muntwiler

articles.title: Flexural Altermagnetism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish flexural deformation as a versatile route for engineering altermagnetism in two-dimensional collinear antiferromagnets. By tailoring the flexure, we selectively break different symmetries to realize altermagnetic states with distinct wave symmetries and reverse their spin splitting. A tight-binding model and first-principles calculations for monolayer MnPS3 demonstrate d- and i-wave states and a switchable transverse spin current in the d-wave state.
authors: Songbo Li, Jinxiong Jia, Zeyu Li, Xudong Zhu, Jiaqi An, Feitong Chu, Songbo Zhang, Wenguang Zhu, Hualing Zeng, Zhenhua Qiao

articles.title: High-Q, high-power spin Hall nano-oscillators with thick NiFe layers enabled by SiC substrates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) are nanoscale microwave sources with potential applications in local spin excitation, neuromorphic computing, and oscillator-based Ising machines. Further improvements in output power and coherence are essential for these applications, and increasing the thickness of the ferromagnetic layer offers a promising route toward this goal. However, this comes at the cost of higher drive currents, which increase Joule heating and can degrade device performance. Here, we show that this bottleneck can be overcome by SiC substrates. By comparing otherwise identical W/NiFe nanoconstriction SHNOs on Al2O3, Si, and SiC, we find that the high thermal conductivity of SiC enables stable auto-oscillations in NiFe layers as thick as 10 nm, while the optimum performance occurs at 7 nm. The best SiC device reaches an average output power of 13.1 pW and a mean quality factor of Q = 23,000, representing the highest reported simultaneous output power and coherence for a single free-running SHNO. These results establish SiC and thermal substrate engineering as a route to thick-ferromagnet spintronic oscillators for coherent microwave generation in nanoscale devices.
authors: Maha Khademi, Akash Kumar, Martina Ahlberg, Artem Litvinenko, Xiaotian Zhao, Saroj P. Dash, Johan Åkerman

articles.title: Orbital-selective correlations in kagome flat bands of Co₃Sn₂S₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometrical flat bands provide an ideal platform for studying electronic correlations and quantum-geometric effects. Although the ferromagnetic Weyl semimetal CoSnS is generally considered a moderately correlated system, recent spectroscopy experiments have revealed a flat-band feature near the Fermi level (EF) that is absent in conventional density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Using DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory and a minimal kagome model, we show that this feature arises not from heavy-fermion-like dynamical band renormalization, but from the shifting of a dₓ^₂₋y^₂ dominated geometrical kagome flat band toward EF driven by orbital- and spin-dependent self-energies. The relocated flat band enhances the local Berry curvature near EF, resulting in a strongly energy-dependent anomalous Hall conductivity and a giant anomalous Nernst effect. Our findings establish an orbital-selective correlation mechanism for positioning geometrical flat bands at EF, and propose anomalous thermoelectric transport as a sensitive probe of flat band induced topology.
authors: Rongxiang Zhu, Huaiqiang Wang, Haijun Zhang, Jianzhou Zhao

articles.title: Higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation by a superconducting antenna with vortices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interaction between superconductivity and magnetism provides new routes for controlling nonlinear excitations in hybrid systems. While dc-driven Abrikosov vortices (fluxons) are known to interact with spin waves, the ability of confined, nearly harmonic vortex oscillations to generate higher-frequency spin-wave modes remains unexplored. Here, by combining time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau modeling with spectral analysis of the microwave near field, we demonstrate higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation driven by a superconducting microstrip antenna in the Shubnikov phase. Unlike conventional harmonic-generation mechanisms associated with nonlinear magnetization dynamics, the magnetic layer remains a linear receiver, whereas the superconducting antenna generates the nonlinear microwave field. We show that nearly sinusoidal vortex motion and the accompanying redistribution of superconducting screening currents produce higher harmonics that couple to spin-wave modes. This response arises from spatial-to-temporal transduction, whereby harmonic vortex motion and the associated redistribution of screening currents convert a spatially nonuniform magnetic-field profile into higher temporal harmonics. Magnetic flux quanta thus act as active nonlinear elements for frequency conversion, extending the accessible spin-wave frequency range in superconducting--magnonic hybrids.
authors: Anton Pokusinskyi, Paweł Gruszecki, Julia Kharlan, Oleksandr Dobrovolskiy, Jarosław W. Kłos

articles.title: Investigation of the Microstructural and Magnetic Properties of Ni on GeSn Layers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermal processing of nickel (Ni) layers on germanium-tin (GeSn) can strongly modify the Ni film and the Ni/GeSn interface within a restricted thermal budget; however, the influence of GeSn crystalline quality on Ni-Ge-Sn interfacial evolution and the magnetic response of the Ni layer remains incompletely understood. Here, Ni (15~nm)/Ge₁₋ₓSnₓ/Ge/Gd₂O₃/Si(111) heterostructures (x = 0.08 and 0.10) were investigated following rapid thermal annealing at 573 and 973~K for 10~s using X-ray diffraction, pole-figure analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, and temperature- and field-dependent magnetization measurements. Annealing at 573~K preserves the crystallographic texture of Ge₀.₉₂Sn₀.₀₈, whereas Ge₀.₉₀Sn₀.₁₀ exhibits microtwin formation and reduced structural integrity. Annealing at 973~K, employed as a severe upper-bound thermal reference, causes extensive structural degradation in both heterostructures, with substantially greater deterioration in the higher-Sn sample. XPS depth profiling reveals progressive Ni-Ge-Sn intermixing accompanied by pronounced Sn surface segregation with increasing annealing temperature. Magnetization measurements show coexisting ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic contributions in the as-deposited and 573~K samples, whereas annealing at 973~K strongly suppresses the ferromagnetic response, producing highly unsaturated M(H) loops together with reduced saturation magnetization and coercivity. These magnetic changes are consistent with extensive interfacial alloying and dilution of the metallic Ni layer. This study establishes a direct correlation between GeSn crystalline quality, interfacial diffusion, and magnetic behavior.
authors: Tharundev V V, Dushyant Singh, Subha Maity, Vigneshwari S R, Dhammapriy Gayakwad, Shivesh Yadav, Krista R Khiangte

articles.title: Anisotropic magneto-elastic coupling in the quasi-2D Ising magnet Li₂FeSiO₄ and thermodynamic signature of low-energy orbital excitations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The relevance of spin, lattice and orbital degrees of freedom in the quasi-2D Ising-like magnet Li₂FeSiO₄ is demonstrated by thermal expansion and specific heat measurements supported by numerical studies. By means of thermodynamic and Grüneisen analysis, we separate the orbital signatures and quantify the energy gap and its pressure dependence from the experimental data as Δsim 300 - 350 K and partial łn Δ/partial pₘ̊ c approx -4.6 %/GPa). Both values excellently agree with the theoretical DFT predictions. The thermal expansion anomalies associated with the onset of long-range magnetic order imply significant magneto-elastic coupling and are used to determine the anisotropic uniaxial strain dependencies of Tₘ̊ N. They are dominated by the in-plane (i.e., c axis) response (partial łn Tₘ̊ N )/partial pₘ̊ c simeq 15 %/GPa while the (negative) a axis and (positive) out-of-plane (b axis) pressure dependencies are much smaller. Short-range magnetic order extends well above Tₘ̊ N but is not driven by the same energy scale as Tₘ̊ N as evidenced by the observation of non-monotonic in-plane distortion, sign-change of the Grüneisen parameter, and failure of Grüneisen scaling.
authors: Waldemar Hergett, Kevin Ackermann, Sven Spachmann, Martin Jonak, Mahmoud Abdel-Hafiez, Hend Shahed, Michael Merz, Maurits W. Haverkort, Rüdiger Klingeler

articles.title: Direct observation of a spin-polarized surface Dirac gap in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator NdBi
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A gapped Dirac cone in antiferromagnetic topological insulators (AFM-TIs) is essential for realizing the quantized anomalous Hall effect, yet its intrinsic magnitude remains controversial. In the prototypical AFM-TI MnBi2Te4, however, the observed Dirac gap is significantly smaller than theoretical predictions or nearly absent, highlighting a long-standing discrepancy. Here we demonstrate that NdBi hosts a spin-polarized topological surface Dirac cone with a sizable gap of 17 meV at the Dirac point, in excellent agreement with density functional theory predictions (12 meV). This direct observation is enabled by high-resolution 7 eV laser-based spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which unambiguously disentangles the spin-polarized surface Dirac cone from bulk-derived states. Furthermore, through temperature dependence and controlled surface contamination, we establish a direct linkage between surface magnetism and the Dirac gap, demonstrating that the gap opens only in the presence of surface magnetic order. These results provide definitive spectroscopic evidence for an intrinsic Dirac gap in AFM-TIs and establish NdBi as a model platform to resolve the long-standing discrepancy between experiment and theory in AFM-TIs.
authors: Yuto Fukushima, Hiroyuki S. Suzuki, Masayuki Ochi, Takuma Nishida, Toshiya Ikenobe, Hiraku Saito, Yuto Kinoshita, Kaishu Kawaguchi, Hiroaki Tanaka, Ayumi Harasawa, Takushi Iimori, Koichiro Yaji, Masashi Tokunaga, Taro Nakajima, Kiyohisa Tanaka, Takahiro Morimoto, Ryo Mori, Takeshi Kondo

articles.title: Rigid Particle-Induced Anomalous Softening in Elastomer Composites
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Particle-filled soft composites generally stiffen as particle loading increases, imposing a trade-off between functionality and compliance. Here, we show that this trade-off can be overcome by designing particles to actively direct gelation rather than act as passive fillers. In a sol-rich elastomer matrix, sol-phase kinetics redirect network formation towards particle-mediated assembly, yielding anomalous softening despite increasing particle content. This response is governed by topological reconfiguration of the load-bearing network during gelation rather than by filler loading alone. A structure-based model captures the composition-dependent onset of this behaviour, and the same response is reproduced across distinct particle systems. The resulting materials combine functionality with softness, energy dissipation, and recoverability under large deformation. These findings establish topology-guided gelation as a general strategy for engineering compliant functional composites for soft robotic actuation, conformal interfaces, and other systems that require both deformability and embedded material functionality.
authors: Yonghyun Cho, Hyeongho Min, Hongdeok Kim, Dongeun Lee, Minjune Kim, Siyeon Jang, Ali Amini, Zitang Wei, Hosub Lim, Hwan-ho Cho, Bo-yong Park, Sang Won Lee, Joonmyung Choi, Metin Sitti, Sangyul Baik

articles.title: Zeeman-field-induced three-spin interactions and relativistic coupling to the scalar spin chirality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic fields are commonly incorporated in atomistic spin models through the Zeeman energy of individual magnetic moments. Starting from a microscopic electronic Hamiltonian, we show that the Zeeman coupling of conduction electrons also generates field-linear three-spin interactions, the lowest-order corrections allowed by time-reversal symmetry. Using a Green-function expansion of the grand potential, we identify two classes of interactions. Isotropic terms of the form (mathbf Sᵢḑotmathbf Sⱼ₎₍mathbf Sₖḑotmathbf B) exist without spin-orbit coupling, and their total strength obeys a sum rule involving the three-site electronic loop at the Fermi energy. Relativistic terms require spin-orbit coupling and include mathbf Kᵢⱼₖḑotmathbf B,ḩiᵢⱼₖ, where ḩiᵢⱼₖ=mathbf Sᵢḑot(mathbf Sⱼ×mathbf Sₖ₎ is the scalar spin chirality. We show that this coupling is forbidden in the spin channel without spin-orbit coupling, whereas the orbital channel recovers the orbital-flux mechanism of Mott insulators. Exact diagonalization of the Hubbard trimer confirms the independence and additivity of both channels. For magnetic trimers in Rashba electron gases, we derive analytical expressions showing that mathbf Kᵢⱼₖ lies in-plane at first order in spin-orbit coupling but vanishes for C₃ᵥ-symmetric trimers, where an out-of-plane component emerges at second order. These interactions can shift magnetization-step fields and modify field-induced noncoplanarity. In the continuum limit, the chirality coupling splits skyrmions from antiskyrmions, while the relativistic terms generate a field-dependent Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

articles.title: Microscopic Derivation of Stochastic Thin-Film Equation and Extensions to Two-Layer and Evaporating Films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While classical thin-film hydrodynamics models widely govern macroscopic fluid layers, they fail to capture the molecular-level thermal fluctuations that dictate nanoscale interfacial dynamics. Standard stochastic extensions rely on the long-wave approximation of the continuum fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations; however, this top-down paradigm lacks a formal connection to microscopic particle trajectories and cannot readily accommodate complex, non-equilibrium boundary mechanisms. We resolve this limitation by deriving the stochastic thin-film equation directly from the exact underlying N-particle Hamiltonian dynamics. This is achieved via a systematic, bottom-up coarse-graining framework based on a generalized fluctuating dynamic density-functional theory. Crucially, this first principles formulation offers unparalleled flexibility, enabling the seamless integration of multi-layered interfaces and non-conserved dynamics such as evaporation. For these complex configurations, our framework rigorously yields entirely novel stochastic thin-film equations featuring emergent noise terms that encapsulate microscopic fluctuations missing from classical top-down models.

articles.title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Defect engineering of memristive materials offers a powerful strategy for regulating ionic transport and analog resistive switching required for neuromorphic computing. Here, we report a wet chemical synthesis route for chloride-vacancy (VCl) engineering in lead-free all-inorganic KCuCl3-x thin films and establish a direct correlation between defect concentration, electronic structure, transport dynamics, and neuromorphic performance. Controlled precursor-ratio variation systematically tunes the VCl concentration in KCuCl3-x thin films, driving preferential vacancy formation at the terminal chloride sites, band-gap narrowing, and enhanced electronic disorder. W/KCuCl3-x/FTO memristors exhibit stable bipolar VCM-type resistive switching, with increasing VCl concentration promoting forming-free operation. An optimal VCl concentration (~ 1.3*10²¹ cm⁻³⁾ provides a balance between ionic mobility and defect controllability, resulting in highly linear potentiation/depression characteristics and superior pulse endurance (>104 cycles). When the experimentally measured conductance characteristics of the optimized memristor are implemented as synaptic weights in artificial neural network simulations, recognition accuracies of 98.96% and 91.82% are achieved on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, respectively. These findings establish precursor ratio-controlled VCl engineering as an effective strategy for simultaneously optimizing ionic transport, analog switching, and neuromorphic learning in lead-free halide perovskite memristors, providing a general materials design principle for energy-efficient neuromorphic electronics.
authors: Chinmayee Mandar Mhaskar, Sangeeta Roy Chaudhuri, Ayan Roy Chaudhuri

articles.title: Pulsed Laser Deposition of Ferroelectric SrTiO3 Shells Enables Polarization-Controlled Charge Separation in TiO2 Photoanode
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ferroelectric polarization offers a powerful route to govern the interfacial charge separation in photoelectrodes; however, chemically converted ferroelectric shells lack sub-nanometer thickness control, coherent strain retention, and chemically clean interfaces. Here, we use pulsed laser deposition to fabricate stoichiometric SrTiO3 shells on hydrothermally grown TiO2 nanorod arrays, achieving atomically defined core-shell architectures while preserving the one-dimensional transport geometry. The photocurrent density followed a volcano-shaped dependence on shell thickness and reached 1.9 mA cm-2 at 1.23 V versus RHE under AM 1.5G illumination for the optimized 15-mins sample, exceeding the established hydrothermal benchmark. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a tetragonally distorted, oxygen-stoichiometric shell, identifying coherent interfacial strain rather than defect dipoles as the origin of the ferroelectric order. Kelvin probe force microscopy directly imaged a polarization-induced built-in electric field whose magnitude scaled with charge-transfer efficiency and photocurrent density. Together, these complementary structural, chemical, electrostatic, and device-level measurements established a quantitative strain-polarization-built-in field-charge separation relationship. This work transforms ferroelectric photoanode engineering from empirical optimization into an atomically controllable and predictive materials strategy for high-efficiency solar water-splitting devices. This approach is readily extendable to visible-light absorbers and complex ferroelectric heterostructures.
authors: Yiqi Jin, Weizeng Zheng, Beibei Wang, Lei Zhao, Binmin Wu, Leonhard Mayrhofer, Xiangjian Meng, Hao Shen, Xiaodan Wang, Weiguang Huang, Junhao Chu

articles.title: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization reveals HiPIMS deposition rates exceeding direct current sputtering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pulsed sputter processes are essential for a wide range of applications from hard coatings to microelectronics. High power impulse magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS) offers unique possibilities for process design due to its high ionized flux fraction. Because of the high peak-current densities involved, correspondingly high plasma densities generate many ions. This enables tuning of kinetic energies by applying accelerating bias potentials. However, some HiPIMS processes have low deposition rates due to the back-attraction these ions experience with the negatively charged sputter target. Recent work in HiPIMS has targeted this problem, exploring complex pulsing schemes such as bipolar, multi-pulse, or chopped HiPIMS. These pulsing schemes introduce another problem: process complexity. As such, the process space, even with coarse intervals quickly blows up to 1E5-1E20 possible process combinations. This calls for efficient and intelligent sampling, which can be enabled by machine-learning algorithms such as Bayesian optimization. In this work we use multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) to efficiently sample the process space of pulse-packets, targeting high ionization flux fractions and deposition rates. Over 2,000 distinct processes were sampled during this exploration. Surprisingly, we found that many HiPIMS processes, including single pulse, can achieve deposition rates higher than DC references. In fact, at a working pressure of 1.0 Pa and moderate ionization rates of 5-20% we found that ms-scale pulses were ideal. We hypothesize these processes maximize gas rarefaction, creating a low-collision channel between the target and the substrate. These results showcase previously unreported behavior of pulsed sputter processes and challenge a long-held trade-off between film quality and speed in thin-film manufacturing.
authors: Nathan Rodkey (Empa, Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology, Laboratory for Surface Science and Coating Technologies, Überlandstrasse 129, 8600 Dübendorf, Switzerland), Felix Thelen (Materials Discovery and Interfaces, Institute for Materials, Ruhr University Bochum, 44801 Bochum, Germany), Alfred Ludwig (Materials Discovery and Interfaces, Institute for Materials, Ruhr University Bochum, 44801 Bochum, Germany, Center for Interface-Dominated High-Performance Materials), Sebastian Siol (Empa, Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology, Laboratory for Surface Science and Coating Technologies, Überlandstrasse 129, 8600 Dübendorf, Switzerland)

articles.title: High-efficiency solid-state electrochemical thermal switching through phonon engineering of 2D materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reversible solid-state thermal switches with large thermal contrasts remain rare, yet are essential for advanced thermal management. Using universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) and density functional theory (DFT), we screen 57 transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), spanning the 1T and 2H phases with Li and Mg intercalation. Among the candidates, LiₐZrS₂ combines exceptional thermal conductivity switching with low heat capacity. Lithiation to Li₀.₁₂₅ZrS₂ reduces the cross-plane thermal conductivity from approximately 3.7 to 0.05 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. The switching behaviour exceeds that of previously reported solid-state electrochemical thermal switches. Device-level modelling further demonstrates the potential for waste-heat recovery, with a pulsed system capturing 86% of the energy recovered by an ideal switch. We attribute the switching behaviour to substantial softening of the Zr--Zr framework, with the mean force constant decreasing from approximately 4.2 to 1.2 eV mathrmmathringA⁻², alongside enhanced scattering of heat-carrying acoustic phonons. These findings establish electrochemical intercalation as a promising route to engineering thermal transport in layered materials.

articles.title: Giant third-order nonlinearity amplifies second-harmonic transport in Ca3Ru2O7
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear electrical transport enables the conversion and detection of electromagnetic signals, supporting wireless energy harvesting, sensing and frequency conversion. Achieving both a large response and electrical tunability remains a central materials challenge. Here we harness giant third-order nonlinearity to amplify and electrically control second-harmonic transport in the correlated polar metal Ca3Ru2O7. Superposing a dc bias on an ac excitation enhances the second-harmonic signal by more than an order of magnitude. The bias controls the polarity of the induced response and activates channels forbidden by symmetry at zero bias. Both transverse and longitudinal components scale quadratically with the ac excitation and are odd in the dc bias, with angular dependences consistent with third-order conductivity. The underlying third-harmonic electric-field responsivity reaches 4.5 × 10-6 m2V-2 at 3 K, providing a quantitative measure of the strong nonlinearity. The induced response emerges below the spin-reorientation transition near 48 K, linking its enhancement to the reconstructed low-temperature electronic state. Theoretical calculations identify quantum-geometric contributions to the nonlinear conductivity and reproduce the observed response symmetry. These results demonstrate how strong higher-order nonlinearity can amplify an effective second-order response, providing a route to electrically tunable nonlinear transport in correlated materials.
authors: Subin Mali, Yufei Zhao, Yu Wang, Binghai Yan, Zhiqiang Mao

articles.title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adapting a pre-trained machine-learning interatomic potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity requires improving defect accuracy without degrading the near-equilibrium elastic and vibrational response. Here we achieve this balance for the aluminium MACE potential QP17 by integrating conditional readout uncertainty, iterative full-parameter updates and protocol-compatible relative-energy anchoring. Sensitivities over 144 linear readout weights guide acquisition, with within-batch covariance updates and evolving neural representations. After four active-learning rounds (32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates), force-uncertainty acquisition reduces mean development force error from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Angstrom, outperforming random sampling (22.70), geometry-diversity selection (22.46) and uniform training across all 104 candidate labels (22.71) under the same update budget. All three force-uncertainty runs satisfy bulk-mechanical retention criteria: historical relative-energy error decreases from 0.375 to 0.207 meV/atom, while harmonic phonon root-mean-square drift remains below 0.05 THz. Matched objective ablations reveal that relative-energy anchoring suppresses harmonic drift. Out-of-sample evaluations across planar faults, twin boundaries and grain boundaries demonstrate transferable gains in defect energies and deviatoric stresses, even though virial stresses are never fitted. A closed-loop molecular dynamics and density functional theory (MD-DFT) pilot confirms that automated acceptance gating intercepts updates that violate historical elastic-group energy or vibrational tolerances. Together, these components establish a retention-constrained fine-tuning protocol for improving plastic-deformation observables while preserving the tested bulk mechanical response.
authors: Yue Wu, Yuan Tian, Deng Pan, Mingwei Chen

articles.title: Local Broadband Gigahertz Spectroscopy via SQUID-on-Tip DC Readout
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting microwave circuits are shaped by their local electromagnetic environment, yet standard microwave measurements do not resolve the local fields and device features that govern their behavior. Here, we combine microwave spectroscopy, nanoscale magnetic sensing, and topographic imaging in a single tapping-mode SQUID-on-tip microscope. The nonlinear Josephson response converts local GHz excitations into Shapiro steps, enabling quantitative measurements of microwave frequency signals and their excitation strength using only DC readout. Applied to a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator, local spectroscopy reproduces the power-dependent resonance and nonlinear bifurcation observed in microwave transmission measurements. Spatially resolved measurements map the microwave response while simultaneously recording topography and static magnetic features, including vortices and Meissner screening currents. Electromagnetic simulations reveal how coupling through the superconducting probe leads limits spatial resolution and guides localized detector designs. Together, these capabilities establish a platform for correlating microwave circuit dynamics with the local structural and magnetic environment of superconducting devices.
authors: Senne Vervoort, Lukas Nulens, Julia Baumgarten, Daan B. Boltje, Jessalyn DeVine, Alejandro V. Silhanek, Joris Van de Vondel, Kaveh Lahabi

articles.title: Growth Phase Map of α and beta Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of α-Ta(110), α-Ta(111), and metastable β-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al₂O₃₍₀₀₀₁₎ at 300-900 ⁱ̧rcC while varying the O₂ partial pressure from a 5.5×10⁻¹¹ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to 2.23×10⁻⁴ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio (2ΦO_₂/ΦTₐłeq4.8×10⁻⁶ to 19). Without added oxygen, α-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O₂ pressure of only 2.5×10⁻⁹ Torr (2ΦO_₂/ΦTₐ=2.2×10⁻⁴), α-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 ⁱ̧rcC, decreasing to 65% at 900 ⁱ̧rcC. Substantial β-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 ⁱ̧rcC and disappearing at 900 ⁱ̧rcC. The apparent β(001)/α(110) selection energy of 1.07±0.16 eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.
authors: Marius O. Eji, Tyler J. Kirkpatrick, Ty J. Cawein, Joseph P. Corbett

articles.title: The fate of s± superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La₃Ni₂O₇
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La₃Ni₂O₇ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an s_± superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like d-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full SU(2) particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual U(1) treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La₃Ni₂O₇, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of s_± symmetry in favor of d-wave pairing.

articles.title: Collinear and Coplanar Altermagnetism in a Penrose Quasicrystal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize the previous group-theory based classification of collinear magnetism in the quasicrystal (QC) to general magnetic states. Taking the Penrose lattice as an example, we find that all magnetic states belonging to 2D irreducible representations (IRRPs) of the D₅ point group, including collinear states and coplanar ones, correspond to altermagnetism (AM). Unlike conventional collinear AM wherein zero magnetism is protected by, e.g. rotation or mirror reflection, which globally flip the spin in the magnetic pattern, the zero magnetism in these 2D-IRRP states is instead protected by a special group-theory-orthogonality theorem that basis functions belonging to different IRRPs are always mutually orthogonal. Taking the single-orbital Penrose-Hubbard as an example, our linear-response theory based calculations show that the largest portion of the parameter space is occupied by these 2D-IRRP states, and our further Ginzburg-Landau theory based analysis reveals that the polarization directions of the two basis magnetic states in the 2D IRRPs can be either parallel or perpendicular, leading to collinear or coplanar magnetic states. The special group-theory-orthogonality compensation mechanism and the absence of the PT symmetry finally leads to AM states, which are to be verified by the spin split in the spin-dependent angle-resolved-photoemission-spectrum and the spin conductance. These intriguing collinear and coplanar AM can also emerge in other QCs.
authors: Bai-He Yao, Zhi-Yan Shao, Ye Cao, Fan Yang

articles.title: Study of localization properties under subsystem periodic driving
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Periodic driving provides a powerful route for controlling localization and engineering effective Hamiltonians in quantum systems. A localized one-dimensional Aubry-André chain can be driven into a fully delocalized phase when the entire system is driven below a critical frequency. Here, we ask whether such delocalization can be achieved by driving only a part of the system. We address this question using a two-leg ladder comprising an Aubry-André chain coupled to a periodically driven clean tight-binding chain. Exact numerical calculations show that, starting from a localized static ladder, subsystem driving below a critical frequency cannot achieve complete delocalization. Instead, a mixed phase emerges, with localized and delocalized states coexisting and the fraction of delocalized states varying nonmonotonically with the driving frequency. This behavior can be understood using local effective Hamiltonians. Although these effective Hamiltonians are derived analytically in the high-frequency regime, they can nevertheless predict the localization transition occurring in the moderate-frequency regime. In fact, by quantifying the emergent nonlocality of the Floquet Hamiltonian, we show that these effective Hamiltonians provide a valid description up to a crossover frequency that is lower than the critical frequency associated with the localization transition. Our results demonstrate an alternative route to Floquet engineering, in which the transport properties of a quantum lattice system can be modified by driving only a subsystem.
authors: Arpita Goswami, Ranjan Modak, Shaon Sahoo

articles.title: Autonomous atomistic-continuum coupling through uncertainty-aware active learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling approach for coupling an atomistic kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) surface-chemistry solver with a continuum multi-species fluid dynamics solver across disparate physical length and time scales. The surrogate model predicts boundary mass fluxes for six species and their uncertainties, which the continuum solver monitors to automatically trigger additional KMC simulations when new training data are needed. This enables efficient multiscale coupling and maintains a user-specified level of accuracy. We demonstrate the approach for reactive halide-perovskite vapor deposition, which involves a multi-species vapor jet impinging on a reactive substrate. The KMC solver uses a DFT-calibrated energetics model that we construct as part of this work and provides net deposition and desorption rates for six species. With a conservative uncertainty threshold, the surrogate-coupled approach reproduces cumulative mass fluxes of the directly coupled approach with errors typically within 10-20%, while capturing the non-monotonic dependence of net deposition on species partial pressure. Importantly, the results show that detailed crystal structure need not be explicitly represented to predict quantities exchanged between atomistic and continuum solvers; species-resolved mass fluxes provide a sufficiently low-dimensional representation of the atomistic response. For this accuracy target, the autonomous online-learning approach reduces the number of required atomistic simulations by two to three orders of magnitude relative to direct multiscale coupling.
authors: Daniel Abdulah, Hariswaran Sitaraman, Ross E. Larsen, Kevin Patrick Griffin, Grace Wei, Janelle Domantay, Ethan Young, Marc T. Henry de Frahan

articles.title: Ubiquity of ocular resonances in scattering phenomena
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate how quantum mechanical scattering off a potential with a characteristic surface generically leads to a family of resonances in the complex momentum plane clustered near a roughly eye-shaped curve centered on the origin and formed by anti-Stokes lines. A particularly interesting class are potentials that are more singular than 1/r² at short distance, where the scattering surface is the separatrix between captured and deflected classical trajectories. These resonances have been recently shown to play an important role in low energy nucleon scattering, and can be related to ``creeping waves'' familiar from classical diffractive scattering and analyzed by means of Regge poles.

articles.title: A neural accelerated surface-roughness-based Discrete Element Method (SR-DEM) for modeling granular systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Discrete Element Method (DEM) is an indispensable tool for modeling and understanding the basic mechanical behaviors of (dry) granular media, a class of disordered material systems of significant interest to multiple scientific domains from (geo-)physics to (chemical) engineering. At the core of all present DEM frameworks is a phenomenological friction law--commonly chosen to be of the Amontons-Coulomb type--that models the frictional interaction among constituent grains. Here, inspired by research in the tribology community, we present an alternative, fundamentally different framework, termed surface-roughness-based DEM (SR-DEM), in which contact friction is handled in a more physics-based manner. In this framework, instead of using a friction law, we explicitly resolve the surface topography of each grain and let friction emerge from collective frictionless interactions of surface asperities. In essence, we trade phenomenology for physics at the cost of an increased computational demand. To mitigate the cost, we introduce an FE²⁻like algorithm and a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM)-based neural network surrogate, both of which are parallelized on GPU to accelerate contact computation. Crucially, using this framework in 2D, we (1) demonstrate the possibility of recovering a two-body-based Amontons-Coulomb-type friction behavior using a simple representation of surface topography, and (2) identify many-body-based frictional behaviors--more specifically, the angle of repose values--that cannot always be captured by current DEM frameworks under the same level of model complexity. We conclude by discussing future directions for SR-DEM, as well as exciting new opportunities it could unlock for a wide range of emerging applications, including (designing) suspension rheology and metamaterial mechanics.

articles.title: Path space large deviation on a lattice for interacting particle systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33524v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the path space large deviation principle (LDP) for a class of interacting particle systems on a fixed finite discrete torus. As an illustrative example, we use the partial exclusion process with maximal occupation of s particles. We first verify the standard Kurtz-type law of large numbers for the original and tilted processes, thereby identifying the deterministic flows around which the large deviations are formulated. We then establish the path space LDP, with speed s, and identify the associated rate function in variational form as the Legendre transform of a nonlinear Hamiltonian. The proof relies on martingale techniques, exponential tightness, and a change-of-measure argument based on exponential tilting, which renders atypical trajectories typical under a modified dynamics. We also explain how the same strategy extends to further interacting particle systems. The inclusion process illustrates the conservative non-compact finite-jump case. The harmonic process is qualitatively different: a single transition may move a variable number of particles, and the limiting Hamiltonian is logarithmic with a non-trivial domain. This places the harmonic process outside the usual finite-reaction framework for density-dependent Markov jump processes. Finally, we discuss continuous-state energy-exchange models, such as the Brownian energy process and an integrable heat-conduction model, to indicate how the same Hamiltonian large-deviation formalism appears beyond discrete-state particle systems.

articles.title: Axion Quasibound States in the Continuum and Their Enhanced Axion Nonlinearity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamical axion quasiparticles (DAQs) in condensed-matter systmes have emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring axion physics and nonlinear optical phenomena. However, the amplitude of the coherent oscillating θ field is even smaller than that of the static counterpart, making the experimental observation of DAQs particularly challenging. Here, we introduce symmetry-sensitive bound states in the continuum (BICs) physics to enable the all-optical detection of DAQs and enhance DAQ-mediated second-harmonic generation (SHG). Specifically, we uncover that DAQs induce optical shear that breaks the C₂z symmetry of metagratings without geometric engineering, thereby converting symmetry-protected BICs into axion quasi-BICs (qBICs). In this context, the evolution of the quality factor and topological charge in momentum space, together with the appearance of optical resonances in far field associated with axion qBICs, offers achiral optical signatures for DAQ detection beyond the widely used Kerr and Faraday effects. Furthermore, by exploiting axion qBICs in the critical coupling regime to enhance fundamental optical field, we show that the SHG efficiency can be enhanced more than 10⁵⁻fold compared to bulk axion materials, achieving a conversion efficiency exceeding 10⁻⁶~W⁻¹. The SHG is governed by the magnetoelectric coupling, which differs from that in conventional SHG materials. Our findings establish a new approach for probing DAQs via achiral optical effects, while providing a versatile route for reconfigurable photonics and terahertz nonlinear optics.
authors: Chang-Yin Ji, Chong Wang, Jiafang Li, Yugui Yao

articles.title: MatOS: An Agent Operating System for Materials Research
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Materials research relies on scattered and growing data, knowledge, and simulation tools, and a single study often spans multi-day workflows across literature analysis, computation, and experiment. Large language model agents can now retrieve materials data, operate simulation codes, and close design-synthesis-characterization loops with autonomous laboratories. However, extending these agents with new capabilities, keeping long-running tasks on track, and letting them learn from past tasks and user feedback remain difficult. Here we present MatOS, an agent operating system for materials research with three core components: (1) a layered scientific asset graph that organizes data, knowledge, tools, skills, roles, and workflows as reusable assets; (2) a stateful adaptive workflow that runs tasks as explicit execution graphs with scientific checks, so that they can be resumed and traced; and (3) evidence-driven asset evolution, which revises these assets from execution records and user feedback. On ResearchClawBench, MatOS improves on the previously best-performing agent by 11.15% with the same base model and extends the cost-score Pareto frontier. With a common base model, it outperforms Codex CLI and Claude Code, exceeding Codex CLI by 2.13% on MatTools and 4.17% on SciAgentGym. In eight research cases, MatOS narrowed more than 30 million candidate structures to 97 solid-electrolyte candidates, identified 89 halide variants with higher computed conductivity than their parent structures, linked the force errors of 11 pretrained interatomic potentials to local atomic environments, and supported two new methods that reduce errors by 3.1% and 13.6% relative to their baselines. These results show that organizing research capabilities as reusable, evolving assets enables agents to carry out long, multistage materials studies. Code is available at https://github.com/DingyangLyu/MatOS.
authors: Dingyang Lyu, Jing Gao, Zhonghao Chang, Jingjie Huang, Xiangran Cheng, Xin He, Yongda Huang, Zefeng Li, Jiahui Liu, Jian Wen, Feng Yu, Bonan Zhu, Yongheng Li, Hongwei Du, Baole Wei, Ziheng Lu

articles.title: kstress: a LAMMPS package for calculating the 2D wavevector-dependent stress tensor and its anisotropy in amorphous solids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34206v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The stress tensor resolved in wavevector qvec and time t, σαβ(qvec,t), gives access to the elastic moduli of amorphous solids as a function of the probed length scale, and to the long-range stress correlations that distinguish an amorphous solid from a liquid. Its evaluation requires the contribution of every interacting pair and therefore an interface to the force loop of the molecular dynamics code. In the current work, we present: i) an optimized implementation of the LAMMPS~i̧telammps module for calculating σαβ(qvec,t), in which trigonometric functions are calculated only for the basic wavevectors and, in addition, all the relevant wavevectors are supplied as an explicit list rather than generated as a full grid, so that only the wavevectors of interest are computed and stored, and ii) a validation protocol for the code illustrated for a two-dimensional polydisperse Lennard-Jones (2DpLJ) glass-forming liquid. Based on these technical achievements we elucidated how the affine moduli for the 2DpLJ model depend on the norm q of the wavevector. In particular, we demonstrate that the longitudinal affine modulus shows a minimum near qₘₐₓ corresponding to the main peak of the structure factor. Our data also point to the peaks in the q-dependencies of vibrational frequencies well below qₘₐₓ for both transverse and longitudinal modes. The potential relevance of this feature to the ``boson peak'' is discussed as well.
authors: Olivier Benzerara, Jörg Baschnagel, Alexander N. Semenov, Liudmyla Klochko

articles.title: Boundary-condition independence of infinite-chain ground states in the S=1 J-D antiferromagnetic chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extending the analytic machinery and using the numerical inputs from OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we study infinite-chain ground states of the S=1 J-D antiferromagnetic model H=sumⱼ{boldsymbol Sⱼḑotboldsymbol Sⱼ₊₁+D(Sⱼmathrm z)²} for sufficiently small |D|. We consider two finite-volume settings: periodic chains with an even number of sites, and open chains with an odd number of sites and the same positive magnetic field in the mathrm z direction at both endpoints. We prove that the ground states in each setting have an infinite-chain limit along the full sequence, without passing to a subsequence, and that the two limiting states coincide. Convergence is uniform in D on a fixed neighborhood of zero. The common limit is a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, and its local expectation values depend continuously on D. These conclusions concern the two specified constructions, not uniqueness among all infinite-chain ground states. They provide the input for the study of a topological phase transition in a forthcoming revision of our companion paper. The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the inductive estimates and to completing the proof.

articles.title: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine. By performing unitary evolution on semantic quantum states, the mechanism implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention computation, eliminating the need to decompose continuous semantic streams into discrete matrices for explicit matrix multiplication, with the measurement results naturally satisfying the normalization condition. Specifically, this work rigorously derives the computational principle of the self-attention mechanism based on FC-QBM, and demonstrates that this mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism. The mathematical principles governing the training and generation of FC-QBM-LM are thoroughly derived, and the two corresponding algorithms are subsequently developed. An 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM is finally constructed and trained on the corpus of Tang poetry. Under the 8-qubit setting, the quantum layer implements the entire positional encoding and self-attention computation pipeline with only 44 parameters. In the noiseless scenario, the model exhibits favorable convergence. Furthermore, the quantum circuit proposed in this work, which terminates with Y-axis rotation gates, achieves better convergence than the counterpart terminating with X-axis rotation gates. Under the small-sample regime and across eight distinct noise intensity levels, the model demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless convergence performance. Experiments on five-character quatrain generation reveal that the model preliminarily exhibits three core capabilities: associative and divergent thinking, content generation across imagery and human-aligned word ordering.

articles.title: Physical Adjoint Learning in Wave Systems with Asymmetric Couplings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Developing self-optimizing physical systems that learn directly from their response to external stimuli offers a promising route toward adaptive and intelligent machines. A key ingredient is the ability to evaluate optimization gradients within the physical hardware, bypassing the need for accurate numerical models. In wave systems, in-situ adjoint methods provide this capability by exploiting reciprocity to physically realize the adjoint dynamics. However, this approach generally breaks down in nonreciprocal systems, where the adjoint field cannot be directly accessed through the original device. Here, we develop an in-situ adjoint optimization framework that extends physical gradient computation to wave systems with asymmetric couplings through computationally low-cost similarity transformations between the forward and transposed operators. We utilize available degrees of freedom like tailored injected excitations, targeted measurements, and tunable parameters, to enable adjoint field reconstruction through forward experiments on the same physical platform. We demonstrate the versatility of the protocol through broadband transmission and isolation, coherent perfect absorption, programmable wavefront shaping, and spatially selective sensing. Our results provide a route to self-optimization in complex nonreciprocal wave systems through efficient physical gradient-based learning. The number of experiments required by the protocol does not increase with the number of optimization parameters, and the method remains applicable even when parts of the system are completely inaccessible.
authors: Lucas J. Fernández-Alcázar, John Guillamon, Krishna Joshi, Tsampikos Kottos

articles.title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.
authors: Roberto Onofrio, Kamel Ourabah, Carlo Presilla

articles.title: Quantum state revivals, time quasicrystals, and entanglement steering in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model
