A pore is modelled as a cylindrical magnetic flux tube with smoothly varying radial profiles of magnetic field and density, subject to the constraint that its temperature is lower than that of the surrounding atmosphere. For finite plasma-β, the linearised equations governing sausage-mode perturbations are derived, and an initial-value problem is solved numerically to obtain the full spatio-temporal evolution of the waves. The applicability of the analytical cut-off relation derived for a flux tube with step-function equilibrium profiles is examined, revealing that its predictions depend on the equilibrium parameters. The simulations reveal distinct wave behaviours across different parameter regimes, including the simultaneous excitation of trapped fast and slow sausage waves for a representative photospheric parameter set. Viscous damping is further investigated through the temporal evolution of the wave energy. Energy dissipation increases with decreasing viscous Reynolds number, increasing longitudinal wavenumber, and increasing radial magnetic-field contrast. These trends are consistent with enhanced viscous damping associated with increasingly fine spatial gradients generated through phase mixing. The findings highlight the importance of radial equilibrium structure in assessing sausage-wave trapping and demonstrate the sensitivity of wave-energy dissipation to the physical parameters of photospheric magnetic pores.

articles.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motion perception is fundamental to computer vision and physical AI, and plays a central role in robotics, autonomous vehicles, human-computer interaction, and video compression. Traditional approaches such as background subtraction, frame-differencing and optical flow algorithms often struggle in complex or dynamic scenes, typically sacrificing spatial resolution for computational tractability. Here we introduce MoViD (Motion estimation via Virtual dispersion and phase Detection), a physics-inspired algorithm grounded in the principles that govern photonic time stretch - a highly successful ultrafast realtime data acquisition platform. Drawing inspiration from the optical physics therein, MoViD treats video as a collection of optical time series waveforms associated with pixels. Motion of an object through a pixel broadens the time series spectrum and, after group delay dispersion, induces a temporal phase that exists only if there is motion. Spatiotemporal group delay dispersion templates, corresponding to dielectric functions, classify specific motion trajectories. Unlike conventional empirical phase-based motion-analysis pipelines that require narrow-band spatial channelization and pyramid reconstruction, the physics-based MoViD operates directly on the broadband video signal, vastly increasing its computational speed. The resulting algorithm achieves unprecedented performance in both motion characterization and motion magnification, providing full-resolution motion mapping in real time at nearly 200 frames per second at 4K resolution and 70 frames per second for 8K video - orders of magnitude faster than classical optical flow approaches or learning-based methods. Notably, such extreme performance enables real time motion analysis at ultrahigh resolution for motion detection and compensation in robotics and other autonomous devices.
authors: Callen MacPhee, Yiming Zhou, Bahram Jalali

articles.title: A Global Magnetohydrodynamic Simulation of the Birth and Cannibalism of Homologous Coronal Mass Ejections
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Homologous coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are sequential eruptions from the same active region. They are of particular space weather interest because they can interact and coalesce into compound ejecta, potentially amplifying their geomagnetic impact. Yet the full chain from recurrent initiation to magnetic merging has not been captured self-consistently in a single global simulation. We present a three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic model that generates three homologous CMEs from a bipolar active region by recurrent photospheric shearing. All three eruptions follow the same initiation mechanism by tether-cutting reconnection within a recurrently formed sigmoid, while the later CMEs propagate significantly faster than the first. We demonstrate that this speed hierarchy arises from progressive coronal preconditioning; preceding eruptions evacuate the overlying corona, reducing both mass loading and ambient drag. The faster later CMEs catch up with their predecessors, and the compression between them forms inter-CME current sheets. Reconnection within these current sheets then progressively merges the interacting flux systems, completing the cannibalistic process. Synthetic coronagraph images reproduce the apparent coalescence of multiple white-light fronts. This simulation provides the first self-consistent global view of the birth, preconditioning, and cannibalistic interaction of homologous CMEs, bridging recurrent eruption initiation and inter-CME magnetic merging in the near-Sun corona.
authors: Lijun Cai, Chaowei Jiang, Zhenhua Liu, Xueshang Feng

articles.title: Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulation of molecular vibrations is emerging as a promising application of quantum computing in quantum chemistry. In this work, we develop new strategies for block-encoding the second-quantized n-mode representation of the vibrational Hamiltonian, whose algebraic structure closely parallels that of the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. We derive linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) representations of this Hamiltonian based on Pauli decomposition and tensor hypercontraction (THC) and construct efficient circuits for the corresponding block encodings. We also extend the Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) technique to vibrational Hamiltonians, yielding a lower LCU 1-norm and, consequently, a lower overall circuit cost. For the molecules considered here, BLISS-THC reduces the Toffoli cost of quantum phase estimation by more than two orders of magnitude relative to existing block-encoding approaches. In comparison with recent Trotter-based methods, it shows up to a ninefold reduction in the T-gate count, with the relative savings tending to increase with system size. Asymptotically, and up to polylogarithmic factors, both the Pauli and THC LCUs trade additional ancillas for a quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modes, while THC provides an additional quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modals. These results highlight the importance of Hamiltonian factorizations and Toffoli-qubit tradeoffs for reducing the computational cost of quantum simulations of molecular vibrations.
authors: Shashank G. Mehendale, Ignacio Loaiza, Shreyas Malpathak, Stepan Fomichev, Danial Motlagh, Artur F. Izmaylov

articles.title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the global V-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential u (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time V-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.

articles.title: Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Network for Single-Shot 3D Reconstruction from Fringe Patterns
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning facilitates rapid single shot three dimensional (3D) reconstruction using fringe projection profilometry (FPP), but recovering accurate surface height from a single high frequency fringe image remains challenging because both long-range spatial consistency and fine geometric details must be preserved. Convolutional networks are limited in modeling long range dependencies, whereas window-based Transformers establish global interactions only progressively with increasing depth. To address these limitations, a hybrid Mamba Transformer network is proposed for fringe to height regression. The network adopts a Swin based U shaped architecture and introduces visual state space modeling at the intermediate resolution encoder stage. An axial and dilated vision state space (ADVSS) block is further developed to enhance prescan feature encoding through local, dilated, and axial depthwise convolutions while retaining four directional selective scanning. This design combines linear complexity long range modeling with direction aware preservation of local fringe structures. Experiments on a publicly available FPP dataset show that the proposed method outperforms hNet, SwinConvUNet, UHRNet, and HiDNet in mean absolute error(MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), absolute relative error, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Using only one deformed fringe image, the proposed method achieves an RMSE of 0.548 mm and an SSIM of 0.9985, reducing RMSE by 65.2% and 59.6% relative to UHRNet and HiDNet, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining selective state space modeling with hierarchical window based attention for accurate single-shot FPP reconstruction.

articles.title: Magnetic Topological Evolution and the Predictive Role of Winding-flux-based Masked PILs in Extreme Solar Flares from AR13664 and AR13842
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using vector magnetogram data from the Helioseismic Magnetic Imager (HMI) on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), we present detailed case studies of precursor activity in Active Regions (ARs) 13664 and 13842, which produced several intense flares. We examined the spatiotemporal evolution of key magnetic topological parameters, including winding, helicity, winding-flux-based masked polarity inversion lines (PILs), and PIL gradients, from the precursor to the post-flare phases. The temporal evolution of the winding flux showed a significant enhancement during the precursor phase, and this trend was consistent across the seven X-class and five M-class flares (>= M5.0). The spatial distribution of both raw and Gaussian-smoothed winding-flux enhancement is co-located with flare footpoint regions of highly twisted core fields, as indicated by the photospheric magnetic topology. The winding-flux-based masked PILs that persisted around the flare locations showed a significant increase in strength and area during the precursor activity. These masked PILs spatially coincide with regions likely hosting non-potential core magnetic fields associated with the observed flares. Furthermore, the gradient of strong PILs extracted from the ARs was positively correlated with flare-associated locations and typically increased several hours (approx. 3-5 h) before flare onset. By imposing a gradient threshold on strong PILs, we isolate magnetic regions repeatedly associated with flare initiation, providing useful constraints in regimes where current flare-forecasting models remain uncertain. Therefore, the combined analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution of different magnetic topological parameters enhances our understanding of intense solar flare forecasting and the identification of potential triggering sites, thereby contributing to improved space weather prediction frameworks.
authors: Prithish Halder, Sudheer K. Mishra, Abhishekh K. Srivastava, Ayumi Asai, Peter A. Dowben

articles.title: Magnetic switchback development from the evolution of torsional Alfvén waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34518v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic switchbacks are mostly Alfvénic local deflections, or even reversals, of the ambient magnetic field of the solar wind. Despite intense research their origin remains unclear and is highly debated. Here we describe a new simulation study demonstrating how torsional Alfvén waves can evolve into switchbacks. We use surface rotational motions to launch torsional Alfvén waves into the super-radially expanding magnetic field of a coronal hole. The simulations demonstrate that in such an expanding wind, the waves initially steepen as they propagate while also inducing a cylindrical parallel plasma jet. A combination of shear from the jet and wave evolution under the constraint of approximate spherical polarisation (|B|approx const.) then leads to the formation of switchbacks in a ring configuration. We explore the 3D nature of the switchbacks, how and where they from, and present scalings for their peak deflection and parallel and perpendicular length scales. We also derive an expression for switchback deflection in the linear regime which we contrast against our results. The results are discussed in relation to recent observations and previous switchback formation studies.
authors: Peter F Wyper, Etienne Pariat, Lorenzo Matteini, Jonathan Squire, Jade Touresse

articles.title: LHμC: A high energy, high luminosity muon-hadron collider at CERN
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The latest developments regarding the feasibility of muon-hadron collisions, achieved through the major reuse of LHeC infrastructure, are presented - at the LHμC, a 1 or 2 TeV μ⁺ beam collides with a 7 TeV proton beam, resulting in the μ⁺p centre-of-mass energy of 5.3 or 7.5 TeV, respectively, at an average luminosity close to 10³⁴cm⁻²s⁻¹. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including exceptional prospects for neutrino science, and is followed by a presentation of the LHμC concept in a nutshell - from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations regarding the machine-detector interface and the general-purpose detector are also presented. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying unique and powerful synergies between the LHμC, LHeC, FCC and Muon Collider projects.

articles.title: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35204v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning molecular models of RNA requires simulation data that capture conformational variability and provide consistent physical training signals. Here, we introduce mdRNAcat, a curated dataset of all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 48 RNA systems selected to promote sequence diversity. Each system is simulated using replica-exchange with solute scaling (REST2), with 32 Hamiltonian states and production lengths of 200-300 ns per state. The dataset provides atomic coordinates, instantaneous forces, and forces reevaluated under the unscaled reference Hamiltonian, together with structural annotations and replica-exchange metadata. Coordinates and forces are available at 1 ps intervals for the reference state and 100 ps intervals across all states in a standardized HDF5 format. We characterize conformational sampling, exchange behavior, base pairing, and sugar-pucker distributions to document the properties of the simulated ensembles. mdRNAcat provides a reusable resource for developing and evaluating data-driven RNA models, including coarse-grained force fields.
authors: Anton E. Dorn, Emile de Bruyn, Fabrice von der Lehr, Philipp Knechtges, Stefan Kesselheim, Alexander Schug

articles.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interaction of strong (a₀>1), superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves with magnetized pair plasma falls into two regimes set by ǎrepsilonₘ̊ Bequiv a₀ømegaₘ̊ B/ømega₀, the ratio of the wave strength parameter to its frequency, in units of cyclotron frequency. For ǎrepsilonₘ̊ B<1 the wave propagates until induced scattering disrupts it. Using analytical theory and kinetic simulations, we show that the background magnetic field introduces a restoring frequency Ømegaₘ̊ B to scattering; when Ømegaₘ̊ B exceeds the scattering rate, the unattenuated length grows from simeqǎrepsilonₘ̊ ₚ⁻²/³ to simeqǎrepsilonₘ̊ B¹/²/ǎrepsilonₘ̊ ₚ wavelengths (ǎrepsilonₘ̊ ₚequiv a₀ømegaₘ̊ ₚ/ømega₀; ømegaₘ̊ ₚ is the plasma frequency). When a₀²>ǎrepsilonₘ̊ B>1, the plasma current is nonlinear, and the wave is damped while riding a motional electric field, so one half-cycle appears attenuated. This framework has implications for the duration of fast radio bursts and whether they can escape their surroundings.

articles.title: Omnigenous stellarators with improved ideal and kinetic ballooning stability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2410.04576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Omnigenity is a property of a magnetic field which ensures confinement of trapped particles. It is a necessary requirement for any high-performance stellarator. After creating an omnigenous equilibrium, one must also ensure reduced transport resulting from kinetic and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities. To this end, we leverage the GPU-accelerated DESC optimization suite, which is used to design stable, finite-β omnigenous equilibria with poloidal, toroidal, and helical symmetry, achieving Mercier, ideal ballooning, and as a consequence, improved kinetic ballooning stability. We discover stellarators with second stability, a regime of large pressure gradient where an equilibrium becomes ideal ballooning stable, and demonstrate and explore both using theory and gyrokinetic simulations the connection between ideal and kinetic ballooning stability.
authors: Rahul Gaur, Rory Conlin, David Dickinson, Jason F. Parisi, Dario Panici, Daniel Dudt, Patrick Kim, Kaya Unalmis, William D. Dorland, Egemen Kolemen

articles.title: Landscape of scattering universality with general dispersion relations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.01782v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Universality in physics describes how disparate systems can exhibit identical low-energy behavior. Here, we reveal a rich landscape of new universal scattering phenomena governed by the interplay between an interaction and a system's density of states. We investigate one-dimensional scattering with dispersion relations ϵ(k)=|k|^m and ϵ(k)=øperatornamesgn(k)|k|^m for any real m>1. For emitter scattering and separable potentials, including contact potentials, we classify the zero-energy S-matrix limits. These universal S-matrix fixed points depend solely on the dispersion exponent m and a finite set of integers characterizing the low-momentum interaction structure. This classification extends far beyond the standard quadratic-dispersion case (m=2). We further derive a generalized Levinson's theorem relating the total winding of the S-matrix determinant to the number of bound states. Finally, for contact potentials and analytic monomial dispersions, we analyze the leading low-energy expansion of the scattering phase near these fixed points and extract the corresponding Wigner-delay scaling. Our findings are directly relevant to synthetic quantum systems, where engineered dispersion relations in atomic arrays and photonic crystals offer a platform to explore these universal behaviors.
authors: Yidan Wang, Xuesen Na, Michael J. Gullans, Susanne Yelin, Alexey V. Gorshkov

articles.title: Voltage-Dependent Photocurrent and Crossover Behavior in Crystalline Silicon Solar Cells
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.27577v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Contrary to the conventional assumption of voltage-independent photocurrent, we show that the photocurrent in monocrystalline silicon p-n junction solar cells depends explicitly on voltage. By applying physically realistic boundary conditions to the classical p-n junction solar-cell model, we derive an analytical expression for the photocurrent that incorporates both the built-in potential and the applied voltage. The model predicts a crossover point between the dark and illuminated I-V characteristics, irrespective of illumination intensity. This prediction is experimentally validated by lock-in measurements on a commercial monocrystalline silicon solar cell. These results establish a more consistent understanding of the quantitative role of the built-in potential in the photovoltaic effect.

articles.title: Ultra-broadband Mid to Long-wave Infrared Spintronic Poisson Bolometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.11733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Infrared detectors have traditionally been divided into two fundamental classes, mid-wave (MWIR, 3-5 um) and long-wave (LWIR, 8-14 um). Integrating MWIR and LWIR within a single device is challenging due to distinct materials, cooling needs, and detection mechanisms, while such integration is critical for improved object recognition, temperature estimation, and environmental sensing. In this work, we demonstrate a Spintronic Poisson (SP) bolometer enabling room-temperature ultra-broadband sensing across 3-14 um. Unlike conventional bolometers that rely on continuous analog signals, the SP bolometer implements a Poisson-counting detection paradigm, encoding temperature in discrete stochastic events, which turns thermal noise from a limitation into the basis of the estimator itself. We fabricate the SP bolometer using a spintronic transduction layer integrated with a plasmonic nanoantenna array to enhance broadband infrared absorption. Using spintronic transduction, the device achieves the noise-equivalent temperature difference (NETD, thermal sensitivity metric) of 80-100 mK at 300 K, surpassing uncooled detectors and approaching cooled technologies. This work establishes a statistical detection paradigm for room-temperature infrared sensing with broad application potential.
authors: Mohamed A. Mousa, Leif Bauer, Daien He, Sakshi Gupta, Shubhankar Jape, Utkarsh Singh, Bhagwati Prasad, Partha P. Mukherjee, Angshuman Deka, Zubin Jacob

articles.title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Designing building energy systems is a high-dimensional, mixed-integer search problem: when each design is evaluated by a year-long simulation, black-box optimizers typically need hundreds of evaluations. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, a framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over previous simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism automatically reverts unsuccessful changes. The agent couples a reasoning model with an explicit memory organisation (procedural, semantic, episodic and reflective), a constrained action interface and an environment-grounded keep/revert signal. The simulator covers eight technologies (photovoltaics, micro-wind, combined heat and power, solar thermal, gas boilers, batteries, heat pumps and inverters) and computes the 25-year Net Present Cost (NPC), including capital and operating costs and salvage value. On a case study with measured building load profiles, the agent, run with Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (ten runs of 50 simulations each), is compared with random search, Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization and a (1+1) evolution strategy sharing the agent's acceptance rule (300 evaluations, ten seeds). With all three models the agent reaches an NPC of about 3.53 MEUR, 1.20% below the best TPE result and 0.23% below the best evolution-strategy result. It comes within 1% of this design after a median of 18 (Opus) to 27.5 (Haiku) simulations, whereas among the baselines only the evolution strategy does so, in half of its seeds and after a median of 192 evaluations. Opus reaches the best design in all ten runs, Sonnet in six (two runs never come within 1%), and Haiku comes within 1% in every run but reaches it exactly only once. Every decision is recorded in an auditable trace.
authors: Amedeo Buonanno, Salvatore Fabozzi, Maria Valenti

articles.title: Repulsive Ensembles for Bayesian Inference in Physics-informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2505.17308v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have proven an effective tool for solving differential equations, in particular when considering the inverse problem. When inferring solutions and parameters of the differential equation from data, uncertainty estimates are preferable to point estimates, as they give an idea about the accuracy of the solution. In this work, we consider the inverse problem for a selection of basic differential equations and employ repulsive ensembles of PINNs (RE-PINN) to obtain such estimates. The repulsion is implemented by adding a particular repulsive term to the loss function, which has the property that the ensemble predictions correspond to the true Bayesian posterior in the limit of infinite ensemble members. Where available, we compare the ensemble predictions to Monte Carlo baselines. Whereas the standard ensemble tends to collapse to maximum-a-posteriori solutions, the repulsive ensemble produces significantly more accurate uncertainty estimates and exhibits higher sample diversity. The experimental results demonstrate that RE-PINN can accurately infer the Bayesian posterior in low-dimensional problems, establishing repulsive ensembles as a promising framework for uncertainty quantification in PINNs.
authors: Philipp Pilar, Markus Heinonen, Niklas Wahlström

articles.title: Determinantal sampling on general spaces: fast approximation via diffusion geometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.06644v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) have recently emerged as a kernel-based alternative to standard independent sampling for constructing efficient minibatches, coresets, and other compact representations of large-scale datasets. One of the key strengths of DPP based samplers is that they can be deployed over very general spaces, in contrast to more classical sampling methods beyond i.i.d. which tend to be tailored to particular well-structured settings, principally Euclidean spaces. In this work, we establish explicit rate guarantees for determinantal sampling in spaces that extend far beyond known Euclidean setups, focussing on spectral kernels obtained from eigenspaces of naturally associated Markov diffusion operators, including in particular the Laplacian on manifolds and nearest-neighbour type graphs on data point clouds and the discrete Schrodinger operator on large scale networks. This covers, in particular, the settings of Riemannian manifolds and discrete networks, as well as the problem of batch sampling from discrete datasets. Overall, our approach achieves guarantees comparable to big(sample sizebig)⁻frac¹²⁻frac¹²dᵢₙₜ , which match with the rates for well-known determinantal samplers on Euclidean spaces of comparable dimension. In terms of techniques, we connect to the celebrated Weyl's Law for spectra on general spaces, and leverage tools from the theory of Markov diffusion operators and Dirichlet forms, which could be of independent interest in this area. Our approach is applicable to a very wide plethora of ambient spaces beyond Euclidean as soon as these ingredients are available, including e.g. fractals, leading to guarantees that will be governed by the intrinsic structural constants of such spaces.
authors: Hoang-Son Tran, Pranav Gupta, Subhroshekhar Ghosh

articles.title: Biogeographic divergence in mangrove resilience to accelerating sea-level rise
articles.abstract: Mangrove forests raise their soil surface in response to relative sea-level rise (RSLR), a biogenic capacity that underpins their value for coastal protection and blue-carbon storage. Whether this capacity is approaching its upper limit, and whether that limit differs between the far-field Indo-West Pacific and intermediate-field Atlantic-East Pacific settings distinguished by Holocene stratigraphy, has not been tested against contemporary observations at a global scale. Here we synthesise for the first time the global mangrove surface elevation table–marker horizon (SET-MH) record: 601 stations across 141 sites in 21 countries, of which 480 resolve an elevation trend. Mangrove surface elevation gain (3.59 ± 9.51 mm yr⁻¹) lagged behind mean RSLR of 5.21 3.42 mm yr⁻¹. The capacity to build elevation was constrained by a non-linear increase in shallow subsidence with accretion. Structural equation modelling revealed tidal range as the dominant control on this constraint. An elevation deficit becomes very likely (P ≥ 0.90) at 8.1 mm yr⁻¹ of RSLR in the Indo-West Pacific but at 6.3 mm yr⁻¹ in the intermediate-field Atlantic-East Pacific sites sampled, and at only 2.4 mm yr⁻¹ in reef settings, mirroring the relative vulnerability to RSLR inferred from palaeo-stratigraphy. Elevation deficit, rather than RSLR itself, predicts conversion to open water across the network of Surface Elevation Tables. Mangrove resilience to sea-level rise is therefore bounded and regionally unequal, and in intermediate-field Caribbean settings and on reef islands this limit is a present condition rather than a future projection.

articles.title: Experimental zero-added-loss multiplexing Bell-pair source for long-haul quantum networks
articles.abstract: Boosting the communication rate of quantum networks is a central challenge in quantum information science. Recently, an efficient entanglement distribution scheme employing quasi-deterministic Bell-pair sources based on time-frequency multiplexing, referred to as zero-added-loss multiplexing~(ZALM), has been proposed. Its implementation, however, requires high-fidelity entanglement swapping across densely multiplexed time-frequency modes, which has remained an experimental challenge. Here we demonstrate entanglement swapping across 16 parallel frequency modes with a high average fidelity of 93.9±SI1.4%. Notably, polarization-entangled photon pairs in each frequency mode are spectrally single-mode using only off-the-shelf 50-GHz dense wavelength-division multiplexing~(DWDM) filters, eliminating the need for additional narrowband filtering. Furthermore, in order to fully exploit the temporal degree of freedom, the pump pulse is operated with a repetition frequency of SI3.0GHz. By combining the frequency and time multiplexing, the total swapping rate reaches 5.38±0.17,sipairs,s⁻¹, which corresponds to the ZALM Bell-pair rate of SI8.2e2pairs,s⁻¹. Our results establish the key experimental capabilities required for ZALM and demonstrate a scalable route toward practical high-rate quantum repeaters and long-haul quantum networks.

articles.title: When Does the Non-Hermitian Effective Description Fail? A Finite-Size Reliability Map
articles.abstract: The no-click (postselected) non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (:Hₑff=H-fraci2sum:ⱼwⱼLⱼ†Lⱼ) is an exact unraveling of the Lindblad equation, but nothing in that unraveling says how far the postselected state may drift from the unconditional one. We measure the drift, over one period (:T) and averaged over initial states, by the trace distance (:Ddyₙ=frac12hspace0.17emøverline{parallel:h̊o:ᵤₙcₒₙdłeft(Ti̊ght)-Pcłeft(Ti̊ght)parallel:ₜᵣ}) ((:Pc): the normalized conditional projector), and show that its leading coefficient in (:Kₙ=γ:/ømega:) is fixed by the fluctuation of the jump operators along the unitary orbit, computable without any dissipative simulation. For excitation-number-conserving systems whose jump operators are ladder-type (each shifting the conserved excitation number by a nonzero integer) we prove a conservation-integral theorem reducing the dimensionless coefficient to (:2π:wNₑₓc) ((:w): dimensionless channel weight; (:Nₑₓc): conserved excitation number; time-integral form (:2π:wNₑₓc/ømega:)), verified to the (:10⁻⁵) level or better across spin chains and chiral waveguide pairs, and, for gain–loss cavities with non-uniform channel weights, through the block-diagonal lemma, with no microscopic parameters beyond (:Nₑₓc). The crossing scale degrades with system size as (:KD*łeft(Ni̊ght)propto:N⁻¹), confirmed by exact diagonalization and corner-space calculations up to (:N=12) and by single-parameter data collapse. The result yields platform-independent design rules—maximum dissipation, postselection cost and an explicit switch criterion—and a guide for exceptional-point experiments.

articles.title: Quantum-Inspired Deep Spatio-Temporal Network for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Turbofan Engines
articles.abstract: Accurate Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of aircraft turbofan engines under dynamic, multi-regime operating conditions is vital for industrial prognostics and safety management. However, existing data-driven methods struggle with multimodal sensor feature distributions, unmodeled cross-sensor spatial correlations, and symmetric loss functions that treat safety-critical over-predictions and conservative under-predictions equally. To address these challenges, this paper introduces the Quantum-Inspired Deep Spatio-Temporal Network (QIDSTN), a compact and safety-aware architecture. The proposed model incorporates an operating condition-aware preprocessing module using K-Means clustering and RobustScaler normalization to eliminate operational bias in heterogeneous datasets. Feature representations are enriched via a novel Quantum Rotation Layer employing learnable trigonometric transformations inspired by quantum rotation gates, without requiring quantum hardware. A dual spatial-temporal attention pipeline, combined with parallel multi-scale convolutions and bidirectional gated recurrent units, effectively captures multi-resolution spatio-temporal dynamics. Furthermore, a composite asymmetric loss function penalizes dangerous over-predictions while prioritizing near-failure engine states. Evaluated across all four NASA C-MAPSS benchmark subsets, the model achieves root mean square errors (RMSE) of 14.84, 17.39, 15.58, and 17.31 on FD001 through FD004, respectively, maintaining a coefficient of determination exceeding 0.83 with only 180,000 to 220,000 parameters. On the complex multi-regime FD004 dataset, it reduces RMSE by 16.6% and NASA score by 86.6% compared to standard baseline models, demonstrating competitive accuracy, safety-oriented error alignment, and practical CPU-level industrial deployability.

articles.title: Predictive value of current HEC-RAS 2D water levels for machine learning flood postprocessing in southeastern Louisiana
articles.abstract: Machine-learning postprocessing quantified information in current water-surface elevation (WSE) and its recent history from the Hydrologic Engineering Center's River Analysis System (HEC-RAS 2D). The analysis used 130 hydrographs and 5,134 paired 3-h records from eight southeastern Louisiana floods. Cross-validation excluded one complete flood from training per outer test fold. Event-macro hydrograph root-mean-square error (RMSE), which weighted floods equally, was 1.63 m for uncorrected HEC-RAS and 0.81 m for a model using forcing, time, location, and static descriptors without time-varying WSE. Adding current WSE reduced RMSE to 0.67 m and improved all eight floods. Adding recent history reduced RMSE to 0.62 m and improved seven floods. When each test gauge was excluded from training, models without WSE, with current WSE, and with current plus history scored 1.62, 0.96, and 0.87 m, respectively. The history model improved on uncorrected HEC-RAS at only 16 of 33 gauges, and the largest gains occurred at deeply incised lower-Amite mapped cells. WSE-informed hydrograph models improved high-water and centered errors but not exact 3-h changes, peak magnitude, or peak timing. A separate exploratory peak-magnitude model reduced mean absolute error from 0.48 to 0.44 m but did not estimate peak time. One-third of scheduled mapped outputs lacked supported WSE. Current WSE supplied the largest and most consistent increment, while recent history added a smaller and less consistent benefit. The analysis used completed floods and did not evaluate hydraulic-model validity or future-flood forecasts.

articles.title: Knee extension motor imagery paired with single-pulse TMS facilitates corticospinal excitability in the tibialis anterior muscle, but not in the rectus femoris muscle
articles.abstract: The rectus femoris (RF) muscle is recruited during a wide range of movements and restoring its function is relevant to both rehabilitation and sports performance. However, previous studies have reported difficulty in inducing facilitatory changes in corticospinal excitability of the RF muscle. We investigated whether and how a method combining motor imagery and transcranial magnetic stimulation (MI+TMS), which has been effective for low plasticity muscles in the upper limbs, modulates the corticospinal excitability in the RF muscle and other lower limb muscles. Twenty healthy participants underwent an MI+TMS protocol consisting of 120 repetitions of knee extension MI paired with single-pulse TMS. Motor evoked potentials (MEPs) were recorded from the RF, biceps femoris (BF), tibialis anterior (TA), and soleus (SOL) muscles at baseline (Pre), immediately after (Post 0), and at 15 (Post 15) and 30 minutes (Post 30) post-MI+TMS. MI+TMS did not significantly modulate MEPs in the RF muscle, an agonist for knee extension, and RF muscle activity during maximum voluntary contraction was significantly reduced. By contrast, MEPs in the TA muscle were significantly increased at Post 0 and Post 15 compared to Pre, whereas no significant changes were observed in the BF and SOL muscles. Additional measurements with 15 participants in the MI-only condition showed no significant changes in MEP amplitude in any muscle. These findings indicate that MI+TMS facilitates corticospinal excitability in a muscle specific manner and suggest that the corticospinal pathway to the RF muscle may be less susceptible to facilitatory plastic changes.

articles.title: X-ray investigations of stainless steel 316L produced via directed energy deposition
articles.abstract: Directed energy deposition (DED) can produce complex pore populations and residual stress states in stainless steel 316L (SS316L), requiring quantitative evaluation to assess suitability for high-consequence structural applications. This work combines laboratory X-ray computed tomography (XCT) with X-ray diffraction (XRD) to characterize 18 DED-fabricated SS316L specimens produced over a range of laser power, scan speed, and powder feed conditions. XCT, with a voxel size of ~ 8µm/voxel, imaged the specimens and analyzed the porosity while XRD measurements evaluated phase constitution, texture, and near-surface residual stress. A sparse-view machine-learning image processing workflow reduced XCT acquisition from 4801 to 481 projections, corresponding to an 89% reduction in scan-time while maintaining 90% flaw detection. Porosity was observed to range from 0.01 to 6.77 vol%, with 16 of the specimens below 0.5 vol%. The largest porosity occurred in low-energy, low-power conditions near the build plate. XRD confirmed a single-phase face-centered-cubic structure with persistent (111)-type preferred orientation, with integrated intensity ratios of (111)/(200) of ~ 1.6–2.8. Residual stresses were predominantly compressive and non-equibiaxial. The largest in-plane stress component was between − 200 and − 450 MPa. The combined XCT-XRD workflow provides quantitative, spatially resolved evidence linking DED processing conditions to defect formation, texture, and residual stress.

articles.title: Carbon nanotubes and cubic silsesquioxanes nanohybrids as a new potential platform for dipyrone sensing
articles.abstract: This study reports the synthesis, characterization, and electroanalytical application of a nanohybrid platform based on carboxylated carbon nanotubes functionalized with octa(aminopropyl)silsesquioxane and copper(II) hexacyanoferrate(III) for dipyrone determination. The material, designated CNTmSCuH, was prepared through the coordination of Cu²⁺ ions onto the silsesquioxane-modified carbon nanotube surface, followed by reaction with hexacyanoferrate(III). Structural and surface characterization by FTIR-ATR, TEM, XPS, and N₂ physisorption confirmed the successful formation of the bimetallic complex, the presence of cubic nanostructures, Cu/Fe species, and mesoporous features. When incorporated into a graphite paste electrode, the CNTmSCuH/CPE exhibited well-defined electrochemical behavior associated with the Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ redox couple and favorable stability under optimized conditions. The modified electrode showed electrocatalytic activity toward dipyrone oxidation, shifting the oxidation potential to lower values compared with the unmodified electrode. Under optimized conditions using 1.0 mol L⁻¹ KCl at pH 7.0 and a scan rate of 20 mV s⁻¹, the sensor presented a linear response from 5.0 × 10⁻⁴ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ and a detection limit of 5.69 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹. The platform was successfully applied to commercial pharmaceutical samples by the standard addition method, demonstrating its potential for dipyrone sensing.

articles.title: Adaptive Shot Allocation for Recursive QAOA via Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) solves combinatorial optimization problems by using shallow quantum circuits to estimate pairwise correlations and recursively eliminate variables until a classical solver can handle the residual instance. Each elimination step requires measurement shots, and the total shot cost grows with the number of recursive stages. On near-term quantum devices, increasing shot counts can translate directly into greater exposure to hardware-level noise sources such as readout errors and decoherence, making shot-efficient execution not merely a cost-reduction measure but a factor with direct implications for solution reliability. While shot reduction has been studied broadly across NISQ algorithms, step-wise measurement control inside the recursive loop of RQAOA has received little attention.We formulate this step-wise allocation as a sequential decision problem and propose two complementary strategies for depth-1 RQAOA on weighted Max-Cut instances. A hand-crafted heuristic assigns shots based on local indicators of step difficulty, and a tabular Double Q-learning agent learns a residual policy that adjusts this baseline under a Lagrangian-constrained objective. Both methods are evaluated under a fixed-cap fairness protocol that equalizes the per-step budget across all strategies, and the elimination rule itself is kept unchanged so that the contribution of adaptive measurement control can be isolated.On a diverse set of weighted graph instances spanning a range of sizes and structures, the heuristic reduces total shots by approximately 23% relative to uniform allocation, and the RL policy achieves a 36% reduction with a lower effective shots per success ratio than both baselines. The improvement persists on problem sizes not seen during training, suggesting that reinforcement learning can serve as an effective tool for discovering efficient, instance-adaptive measurement strategies in recursive quantum optimization.

articles.title: SAM-NeuroAdapt: an atlas-guided, training-free pipeline for skull-stripping in infant and adult MRI
articles.abstract: Skull-stripping, the removal of non-brain tissue from magnetic resonance images, is an early step of most neuroimaging pipelines whose errors propagate to later measurements. However, current methods such as HD-BET, SynthStrip and LifespanStrip depend on task-specific training on large image collections. To test how much of this benefit survives without training, this study presents SAM-NeuroAdapt, a training-free pipeline. First, an age-matched template is selected from a library of 21 atlases and registered to the image. The registered atlas then supplies the prompts of a frozen Segment Anything Model 2, and the mask is refined by classical boundary correction. The pipeline was compared with HD-BET on three whole-head benchmarks, with multiplicity-adjusted p-values. On infants (Baby Open Brains, 71 visits, 51 participants), it achieved higher Dice (0.920 versus 0.905) and a lower average symmetric surface distance (ASSD; 2.07 versus 5.11 mm). On adults, no Dice difference was detected; ASSD was ower on Mindboggle-101 (n = 101) and, under one of two adjustment procedures, on IBSR-20 (n = 20). Furthermore, an ablation showed that the age-matched atlas alone reached the infant Dice of the complete pipeline (0.923 versus 0.920), while the remaining stages reduced infant surface distances by 36–46%; without atlas guidance, 26–100% of cases failed. These findings indicate that atlas matching, rather than the foundation model, drives overlap accuracy and that a well-matched atlas is a competitive training-free baseline. Two eval-uation pitfalls are also documented: a surface-distance definition that rewards over-segmentation and benchmarks distributed already skull-stripped

articles.title: Flux Cycling and Voltage Pulse Generation in Nanostructured Gapless Superconductors: A Time-Dependent Ginzburg-Landau Study
articles.abstract: Fluxonic devices explore the interaction of quantized magnetic fluxes in superconductors with their surroundings to perform logical operations, magnetic field sensing and photon detection, among other applications. Therefore, knowing in detail the physics governing flux motion is highly important. More specifically, it is important to understand the main set of parameters that affect the thermoelectromagnetic response of the system to dynamic external fields and to be able to predict the feasibility and limitations of certain phenomena for applications. In this work, we applied the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau formalism to study the trajectories of vortices and the characteristic voltage curves for a particular magnetic field cycle longitudinally applied to a cylindrical superconducting sample. We showed how these cycles vary with different types of impurities and studied whether this approach might produce practically measurable voltage signatures. In fact, we found a characteristic pattern in these signatures that occurs regardless of the number of vortices that penetrate the sample within the cycles.

articles.title: A Meshless Collocation Framework for Free Vibration Analysis of Multilayer Functionally Graded Hyperelastic Beams with Experimental Validation and ANN Prediction
articles.abstract: This research investigates the free vibration characteristics of hyperelastic functionally graded material (FGM) beams through an integrated numerical and experimental framework. The governing equations of the hyperelastic beam are formulated based on the Neo-Hookean strain-energy model in conjunction with Timoshenko beam theory and subsequently solved using the meshless collocation method (MCM). The reliability of the proposed numerical approach is assessed by comparison with experimental modal testing and finite element method (FEM) simulations. The investigation considers a square-cross-section rubber-based FGM beam composed of six different material compositions. The mechanical characteristics of the individual layers are experimentally evaluated through uniaxial tensile testing in accordance with the ASTM D412 standard. A detailed parametric investigation is then conducted to examine the effects of material parameters, geometric dimensions, and incompressibility coefficients on the dynamic response of the beam. The numerical findings obtained from the MCM show strong agreement with the FEM predictions. Furthermore, the discrepancy between the MCM results and the experimental modal measurements remains below 6.63%, demonstrating the validity of the proposed approach. Finally, a neural network (NN) model is incorporated as a complementary predictive tool to estimate the vibrational response of the investigated structure. The results confirm that the proposed neural network can effectively approximate the natural frequencies of the hyperelastic FGM beam with high accuracy.

articles.title: Separating portal and hepatic veins on CT with a TotalSegmentator-compatible model trained only on public data: external validation and release
articles.abstract: Purpose Liver surgery planning requires separating the portal and hepatic veins on CT, yet, to the author's knowledge, no deep learning model for this has been released under a permissive license. Such a model was developed from public data, validated externally, and released.Methods An nnU-Net model, OpenPVHV, was trained on 224 cases of the public HVM dataset (Hepatic Vessel Map) with the configuration of the TotalSegmentator liver-vessel task. Fifty-six HVM cases formed the internal and the 40 VEELA cases the external test set; predictions for the 20 cases with hidden labels were scored by the challenge server. Metrics were the official centerline Dice (clDice), intersection over union (IoU), and normalized surface distance (NSD). Comparators were the general-purpose model VoxTell, the TotalSegmentator liver-vessel task, the challenge participants, and a model trained with 62 added CRLM (colorectal liver metastases) cases.Results Mean clDice of OpenPVHV (portal/hepatic) was 0.750/0.786 internally, 0.723/0.662 on the public external cases, and 0.734/0.732 on the hidden cases, where the portal vein ranked first on all three metrics above every team at the deadline and the organizers' baseline. OpenPVHV exceeded VoxTell on all six comparisons on the internal and public external cases, and the TotalSegmentator liver-vessel task on all vessels combined (clDice 0.784 vs 0.528 internally, 0.706 vs 0.501 externally). Adding CRLM lowered all six values on the public external cases.Conclusion OpenPVHV separates the portal and hepatic veins on external data and may replace the vessel output of the TotalSegmentator liver-vessel task. Code and weights are released under Apache-2.0.

articles.title: The influence of Emotional Intelligence on Group Malevolent Creativity: Evidence from fNIRS hyperscanning
articles.abstract: The relationship between emotional intelligence and creativity is a hot topic in the fields of emotion and innovation; but previous research has paid little attention to how emotional intelligence influences the group creative process, particularly this specific form of creativity known as group malevolent creativity. We employed functional near-infrared spectroscopy hyperscanning in 60 dyads (120 participants) to investigate the effect of emotional intelligence on group malevolent creativity and its neural mechanisms. Results revealed that emotional intelligence can reduce group malevolent creativity; groups with high emotional intelligence exhibited greater inter-brain synchrony (IBS) in the prefrontal cortex and right temporoparietal regions. Furthermore, IBS increments were negatively correlated with malevolent creativity; the pattern of IBS increments in the prefrontal cortex mediated the relationship between emotional intelligence and group malevolent creativity. Our findings suggest that emotional intelligence may attenuate the emergence of group malevolent creativity, and this effect is accompanied by enhanced inter-brain synchrony in the prefrontal-right temporoparietal region. This study revealed the neural interaction basis underlying the association between emotional intelligence and group malevolent creativity, offering a new perspective on understanding the complex relationship between emotional intelligence and malevolent creativity.

articles.title: CrystalREPA: Transferring Physical Priors from Universal MLIPs to Crystal Generative Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.08960v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Crystal generative models mainly learn what stable crystals look like, with little explicit supervision for what makes them stable. We reveal a substantial representation gap between state-of-the-art crystal generative models and pretrained universal machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) via energy probing, and show this gap can be closed by a simple training-time alignment. We propose Crystal REPresentation Alignment (CrystalREPA), a plug-and-play framework that aligns the atom-wise hidden states of generative encoders with frozen MLIP representations through an element-aware contrastive objective, transferring stability-aware atomistic priors with marginal training overhead and no additional inference cost. Across three generative frameworks, ten MLIP teachers, and two benchmark datasets, CrystalREPA consistently improves the thermodynamic stability, structural validity, and structural fidelity of generated crystals. Equally important, we find that an MLIP's transfer effectiveness is poorly predicted by its accuracy on standard leaderboards (e.g., Matbench Discovery) but strongly predicted by the distinguishability of its atom-wise representation space, yielding a practical, accuracy-independent criterion for selecting MLIP teachers for generative transfer. Code is available at https://github.com/Chengqian-Zhang/CrystalREPA.
authors: Chengqian Zhang, Yucheng Jin, Duo Zhang, Tiejun Li, Han Wang

articles.title: Chirality-Resolved Spectroscopy of Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon States in Multiband FeTe₁₋ₓSeₓ Superconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.03637v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We employ terahertz Faraday magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe the relaxation dynamics of quantized helical Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon (CdGM) states in epitaxial FeTe₁₋ₓSeₓ thin films, nodeless multiband superconductors with short coherence lengths in the moderately clean limit. By exploiting polarization-selective optical transitions, we directly resolve the helicity and band origin of vortex-core quasiparticles. We observe long-lived CdGM resonances with opposite circular polarizations for electron- and hole-like bands. This enables independent, band-resolved determination of quasiparticle lifetimes, vortex masses, coherence lengths, and upper critical fields, and reveals their systematic evolution with isovalent substitution. The results establish terahertz magneto-optics as a direct probe of helical vortex-core excitations and provide dynamical evidence for multiband CdGM states in iron-based superconductors.
authors: T. Rõõm, A. Glezer Moshe, R. Nagarajan, U. Nagel, Hee Taek Yi, Seongshik Oh, G. Blumberg

articles.title: Why Fe doping kills photoluminescence in CsPbCl₃ but not in CsPbBr₃: Role of midgap Fe 3d states and electron-phonon coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.04714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding the impact of transition-metal doping on the optoelectronic properties of halide perovskite nanocrystals is essential for their rational design in photonic applications. We establish the microscopic origin of photoluminescence (PL) quenching in Fe-doped CsPbCl₃ using spin-polarized density functional theory calculations. The emergence of Fe 3d midgap states creates efficient electron-trapping centres that drive nonradiative recombination, accounting for the reduced PL intensity. Extending this analysis to Fe-doped CsPbX₃ (X = Cl, Br), we show experimentally that although PL intensity is suppressed in both systems relative to their pristine counterparts, their high-doping behaviour diverges: CsPbCl₃ becomes completely non-emissive, whereas CsPbBr₃ retains a finite, saturated PL intensity. Despite this contrast, electronic structure calculations reveal nearly identical midgap states in both materials, indicating that electronic effects alone cannot explain the distinct PL responses. Phonon calculations likewise fail to capture this difference. In contrast, electron-phonon coupling calculations based on the deformation potential approach reveal significantly stronger coupling in Fe-doped CsPbCl₃, enabling efficient dissipation of electronic excitation energy into lattice vibrations and leading to complete PL quenching. These results identify electron-phonon coupling as the key factor governing halide-dependent PL quenching and provide a unified microscopic framework for dopant-induced nonradiative processes in halide perovskites.
authors: Arpan Das, Saptarshi Chakraborty, Ranjani Viswanatha, Shobhana Narasimhan

articles.title: Open Wilson chain numerical renormalization group approach to steady-state non-equilibrium quantum transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.14635v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The numerical renormalization group (NRG) approach was developed to identify and quantify different equilibrium regimes of quantum impurity systems (QISs) with unprecedented accuracy by a tailored finite size representation. Out of equilibrium, the steady-state density operator is not of the Boltzmannian form but one that is determined by the imposed boundary conditions. We extend the NRG to the nonequilibrium setting by augmenting each Wilson site with a reservoir, whose coupling functions are calculated via a continuous fraction expansion in order to recover the continuum limit exactly. The nonequilibrium parameters such as a finite bias as well as a finite temperature gradient enters through the Bloch-Redfield tensor (BRT), whose zero eigenvector gives the steady-state density operator. We used the resulting open chain full density matrix (OC-FDM) approach with an effective single lead description to investigate the charge and spin transport through a quantum dot (QD) under finite bias and temperature gradient. The influence of lead asymmetry and an external magnetic field on the transport properties are also studied. For completeness, we have also investigated local properties of the QD, such as charge fluctuations and find excellent agreement with real-time quantum Monte Carlo (RT-QMC) data. The OC-FDM approach was able to explore Kondo energy scales as low as T_K/D approx 10⁻⁸ in the non-equilibrium regime, as well as show convergence with the established equilibrium benchmarks, such as a quantitative agreement with full density matrix numerical renormalization group (FDM-NRG) and Fermi-liquid scaling at small bias and temperature. Owing to the effective single lead description, a single OC-FDM data point takes orders of magnitude less time on a standard laptop, compared to other state-of-the-art numerical methods.

articles.title: Evaluating the Structural Basis for Polar Altermagnet Candidate Ca₃(Ru,Ti)₂O₇
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.16181v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The interplay between polar and altermagnetic orders remains largely unexplored in the broader landscape of correlated electron systems. Density functional theory (DFT) within the PBEsol + U treatment propose Ca₃Ru₂O₇ as a polar altermagnet, reliant on the transformation of the experimentally reported Bb2₁m phase to a lower symmetry Pn2₁a structure. Here, we perform a targeted search for the Pn2₁a phase using synchrotron X-ray diffraction on single crystals of Ca₃Ru₂O₇ and Ca₃(Ru₀.₉₉Ti₀.₀₁)₂O₇. No diffraction signature of the Pn2₁a structure is detected down to 20 K within experimental limits. Through diffraction simulations, we translate this result into a quantitative upper bound on the symmetry breaking distortion amplitude, which we find to be significantly smaller than the DFT predicted distortion. Our DFT calculations further motivate dilute Ti substitution (łesssim 2%) as an alternative route to stabilize the low symmetry phase, for which we again find no clear evidence for this putative Pn2₁a structure that hosts altermagnetism. Our findings indicate that PBEsol + U over-stabilizes a Pn2₁a distortion, and the measured bounds provide benchmark for future calculations. Ti substitution exceeding sim3% reveals a chemically tunable polar altermagnetic phase within the Bb2₁m structure and we theoretically demonstrate that the spin-splitting can be tuned by Ti substitution. By combining DFT, diffraction simulations and synchrotron X-ray measurements, our study demonstrates a general methodology to quantify subtle structural distortions that underlie emergent electronic and magnetic phases.
authors: Akash Saha, Yihuang Xiong, Vladimir A. Stoica, Subin Mali, Aaron Pearre, Saugata Sarker, Huaiyu Wang, Yufei Zhao, Evguenia Karapetrova, Yu Wang, Jadupati Nag, Zachary W. Hazenstab, Seng Huat Lee, Long-Qing Chen, Geoffroy Hautier, Binghai Yan, Zhiqiang Mao, Venkatraman Gopalan

articles.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for coupled stiff transport systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.21236v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) struggle with stiff, regime-changing transport equations due to instability, loss imbalance, and violations of physical consistency. This paper investigates these failures through the Marshak wave equations, a canonical benchmark from radiative transport, where initial and boundary conditions differ by up to 12 orders of magnitude, and proposes modifications to the standard PINN framework to overcome them. Three modifications are introduced: a ScaledSigmoid final activation enforcing physical bounds and positivity of the unknowns; a logarithmic MSE loss replacing the standard quadratic loss for initial and boundary conditions, enabling training across extreme scale disparities; and explicit enforcement of global conservation laws as an additional physics loss term. Monte Carlo sampling with exponential time weighting is used throughout. The proposed framework recovers the Marshak wave dynamics - including the hot, cold, and wave-front regions - in good agreement with a reference Implicit Monte Carlo solution (sub-millimeter absolute error on the front position, although the relative error remains substantial at early times), with run times under 5 minutes. Ablation studies confirm that each ingredient is essential: linear activation, absence of the logarithmic loss, or removal of the PDE term each independently cause the method to fail qualitatively. This work identifies and resolves three concrete failure modes of standard PINN on stiff hyperbolic systems with nonlinear coupling. The combination of bounded activations, scale-aware loss functions, and conservation law enforcement constitutes a framework validated on the present one-dimensional Marshak wave problem, with potential extension to other coupled stiff transport systems in engineering.

articles.title: Interlayer Phase Locking and Sliding Select Topological Melting Channels in Superconducting Bilayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.12401v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological transitions in coupled superconducting layers are intertwined: an elementary vortex in one layer carries both common and relative phase winding. We study a Josephson-coupled bilayer in an in-plane magnetic field using renormalization-group analysis and Monte Carlo simulations of the compact layer phases. The field drives Pokrovsky--Talapov (PT) entry of interlayer solitons, and free-energy calculations in fixed soliton sectors show PT square-root scaling over the sampled densities at finite temperature. Interlayer phase locking and sliding then select distinct Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT)-like melting channels. The locked commensurate phase melts through same-vorticity layer pairs when the geometric-mean common helicity modulus Upsilon₊,g reaches T/(2π), with layer correlation exponent ηₗ₌₁/4. A stable sliding incommensurate phase melts through elementary layer vortices on a line of BKT fixed points, where Upsilon₊,g+Upsilon₋,g=2T/π and ηₗ is set by the ratio of the relative and common moduli. When the relative helicity modulus is identified with the relative-phase stiffness, our simulations agree with this prediction, and the common superfluid stiffness at incommensurate melting is nearly twice its value at commensurate melting. Near soliton entry, however, the dilute sliding state is unstable to opposite-vorticity layer pairs. Our results connect PT soliton entry with field-tunable BKT-like melting and identify the pair-stability condition that links them.

articles.title: Cavity control of quantum phase transitions in a two-dimensional Kondo lattice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.03714v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cavity quantum electrodynamics offers a route to control quantum phases by using vacuum fluctuations of confined electromagnetic fields. In particular, planar cavities based on polar van der Waals materials can generate strongly confined modes and are promising for controlling two-dimensional correlated materials. Recently, moiré materials have become central platforms for studying two-dimensional heavy-fermion systems and their quantum phase transitions. Kondo lattices provide a prototypical model for studying quantum phase boundaries, driven by competition between Kondo screening and the ordering of local magnetic moments. We show that a cavity-induced interaction can shift the quantum phase transitions between a heavy-fermion phase and an antiferromagnetic phase in a two-dimensional Kondo lattice through a momentum-dependent self-energy of the conduction bands. For the longitudinal projected field motivated by h-BN hyperbolic phonon polaritons, the self-energy favors Kondo hybridization and expands the heavy-fermion region. Transverse and circular in-plane model structures give distinct effects, with the transverse case relatively favoring the magnetically ordered phase and the circular case lying between the longitudinal and transverse cases. These results indicate that electromagnetic vacuum fluctuations can effectively modify the control parameters of strongly correlated two-dimensional Kondo materials.
authors: Jun Mochida, Atac Imamoglu, Yuto Ashida

articles.title: Raman Signatures of Lithium Ion Dynamics in LLZO Garnet Electrolytes: Atomistic Insights from MD-Raman Calculations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.04690v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lithium lanthanum zirconate (LLZO) garnets are among the most promising solid electrolytes for next-generation batteries owing to their high ionic conductivity, chemical stability, and compatibility with lithium metal. Raman spectroscopy is commonly employed to distinguish the highly conductive cubic phase from the poorly conductive tetragonal phase of LLZO, yet the atomistic origin of these spectral differences and their direct connection to Li-ion transport remain unresolved. Here, we close this gap by comparing computed and experimental Raman spectra for the tetragonal, cubic, and Ta-doped variants of LLZO, with the computed spectra obtained from the MD-Raman approach that combines machine-learning molecular dynamics with first-principles polarizability calculations. We show that the contrasting ionic transport behavior across these LLZO variants is encoded in the vibrational dynamics of the lithium sublattice and gives rise to distinct features in their Raman spectra. A symmetry-resolved analysis further reveals that experimentally observed Raman peaks do not correspond to individual normal modes, but instead arise from overlapping contributions of multiple symmetry channels, challenging conventional peak-assignment approaches. By explicitly connecting experimentally accessible Raman signatures to the underlying atomic-scale dynamics, our results show how Raman spectroscopy can move beyond empirical phase identification toward a microscopic probe of Li-ion dynamics in lithium garnet electrolytes.
authors: Takeru Miyagawa, Willis O'Leary, Manuel Grumet, Hyunwon Chu, Jennifer L. M. Rupp, Waldemar Kaiser, David A. Egger

articles.title: Parity-equivariant prediction of conformer-resolved electronic circular dichroism spectra accelerates absolute configuration assignment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.21892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electronic circular dichroism (ECD) is a key experimental probe for assigning the absolute configuration of chiral molecules, but interpreting measured spectra often requires costly time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The few existing machine learning methods for ECD prediction are faster, but their accuracy still falls well short of that required for experimental applications. Here we introduce PhysECD, a parity-aware E(3)-equivariant framework that builds the spectrum from its underlying quantum-chemical quantities, ensuring correct chiroptical symmetry by construction. To improve generalization and support experimental applications, we construct SCECD, a conformer-resolved dataset of 578,104 computed spectra spanning diverse natural products with one to five stereocentres. PhysECD predicts ECD spectra from conformer geometries in milliseconds, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on the CMCDS benchmark and SCECD. Validation against 77 experimental spectra further demonstrates that PhysECD can serve as a fast alternative to TDDFT for assigning the absolute configuration of complex chiral molecules.
authors: Yi Jiang, Letian Chen, Runhan Shi, Lea Bae, Zheng Ling, Dong Ha Kim, Tong Zhu, Yang Yang

articles.title: Machine learning kinetics from molecular dynamics data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.17736v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most molecular transitions occur on time scales far beyond direct molecular dynamics simulations. The committor, the probability that a configuration reaches a product state before a reactant state, is a central kinetic statistic, providing a mechanism-independent reaction coordinate and a foundation for transition path theory and the calculation of rates. This review surveys modern approaches for estimating the committor and related kinetic statistics from molecular simulations, with an emphasis on self-supervised methods that learn solutions of their defining dynamical equations rather than relying on labeled shooting data. We develop a common operator viewpoint connecting generator-based partial differential equations, variational principles, Markov state models, dynamical Galerkin approximation, and neural networks. Empirical and theoretical evidence points to the efficiency of these methods. We provide theoretical and practical guidance for realizing their full potential in applications, including strategies for treating non-Markovian effects and for sampling. We conclude by identifying opportunities for further research, including connections to reinforcement learning and generative modeling.

articles.title: Attosecond Charge Migration Induced by Core-Level Ionization: A Relativistic Real-Time Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory Perspective
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.18428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Core-ionization induced charge migration in molecular systems has been widely studied, but the influence of relativistic effects on such dynamics remains relatively unexplored from a relativistic theory perspective. This issue is particularly important because core orbitals exhibit strong scalar-relativistic and spin-orbit imprints, and these effects are further enhanced in heavy-element systems, where relativistic signatures also alter the valence orbitals. To address this, we formulate four-component Dirac-Coulomb and two-component atomic mean-field exact two-component Hamiltonian approaches for studying charge migration within real-time time-dependent density functional theory. The time-dependent induced electric dipole moment is used as a marker of the characteristic charge-migration time scales. We apply the method to nitrosobenzene (N 1s electron removal), iodoacetylene (I 2p electron removal) and interhalogen series (I 2p, Cl 2p electron removal). For iodoacetylene, the charge migration timescale is relatively insensitive to the choice of Hamiltonian but they show weak relativistic phase and amplitude modifications. However, it would be misleading to conclude that relativistic effects are generally unimportant. In interhalogen systems, we observe significant deviations between relativistic and non-relativistic dynamics. These results demonstrate that relativistic signatures in core-ionization-induced charge migration are not determined by heavy-atom core ionization alone, but by the relativistic sensitivity of the valence orbital manifold that drives core-hole screening and charge redistribution. Moreover, consistently across all systems, we observe a delay in the emergence of the relativistic imprints.
authors: Torsha Moitra, Lukas Konecny, Michal Repisky

articles.title: Disentangling spin polarization from driven circular ionic motion in EuTiO₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.28214v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherently driven circular ionic motion has been reported to produce large helicity-dependent optical responses attributed to transient magnetization. However, the microscopic nature and magnitude of this phenomenon, sometimes referred to as dynamical multiferroicity, remain strongly debated. Here, we directly study the connection between ionic circulation induced by a high-field circular terahertz (THz) drive and its effect on the spin system of EuTiO₃ using X-rays. This material exhibits an optical response consistent with the putative magnetic signal observed in related non-magnetic materials. Furthermore, the presence of Eu²⁺ ions enables the use of X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) to test for the creation of transient spin polarization. Simultaneously, ultrafast X-ray diffraction (XRD) measures the circular ionic motion from which we determine the mechanical angular momentum. We find a classical ionic contribution of 3×10⁻⁸~μ_B from XRD and upper limits of 0.03~μ_B and 0.11~μ_B from the sensitivity of XMCD at the europium M₅ and L₂ edges, probing the 4f and 5d shells of Eu²⁺, respectively. These observations show that large-amplitude circular ionic motion in this system is not accompanied by a detectable spin polarization despite the clear signature in the optical data, with the XMCD upper bounds and classical contribution differing by many orders of magnitude.
authors: Clifford J. Allington (Sin-Hang), Matthew J. Lutz (Sin-Hang), Enoch (Sin-Hang), Ho, Fabian Graf, Martina Basini, Hiroki Ueda, Michael Grimes, Alexander B. Elliott, Megan F. Biggs, Ravi Finn, Shih-Wen Huang, Merideth A. Henstridge, Matthias C. Hoffmann, Takahiro Sato, Roberto Alonso-Mori, Diling Zhu, Quynh L. Nguyen, Vincent Esposito, Jeffrey T.
