Johnson, Jeremy A. Johnson, Urs Staub

articles.title: Thermodynamic compatibility, holographic property and wave-function representation of generalized weakly nonlocal self-gravitating non-relativistic fluids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2504.07296v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two pillars of physics---gravity and quantum mechanics---are usually formulated in entirely separate languages. Surprisingly, both can be expressed in the language of a fluid: a self-gravitating fluid for Newtonian gravity, and a quantum-pressure-carrying fluid for the Schrödinger equation. In this work we show that this resemblance can be understood within a common framework based on how the Second Law of Thermodynamics constrains the class of non-dissipative continua considered here. Using a transparent thermodynamic procedure, we derive the most general fluid model within a chosen constitutive state space involving density, velocity, energy, an internal scalar field, and their spatial gradients. The framework recovers, as special cases, the Euler equations, a restricted family of Korteweg fluids (including the hydrodynamic form of the Schrödinger and Gross--Pitaevskii equations), Newtonian self-gravitating fluids, and the Schrödinger--Newton system. We identify the conditions under which perfect fluids exhibit emphclassical holography: the pressure-tensor divergence can then be represented by the gradient of a scalar potential. Classical holography yields a vorticity transport law that preserves sufficiently regular, initially irrotational flows and, under additional assumptions, enables a single complex-valued Schrödinger-like representation. While gravitational and quantum-hydrodynamic theories were investigated separately in our previous works, the present study develops a substantially more general scalar-internal-variable construction, refines its perfect-fluid analysis, and systematically embeds the earlier models within a unified framework. The framework also identifies a thermodynamically admissible density--gravity coupling that connects classical and quantum self-gravitating fluids, although its stability, and observational consequences remain to be explored.

articles.title: Ab initio calculations of ²²⁹Th band-to-band internal conversion rate in ²²⁹ThO₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.08941v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an ab initio calculation of the band-to-band internal-conversion rate of the hbarømegaₘ̊ ₙᵤc approx 8.35 eV isomeric transition in ²²⁹ThO₂. Because the nuclear transition energy exceeds the electronic band gap of ThO₂, the isomer can decay nonradiatively by resonantly promoting a valence electron into the conduction band. We formulate this process as a Brillouin-zone sum over vertical interband transitions weighted by local Th-centered hyperfine matrix elements, which are evaluated directly from all-electron full-potential linearized augmented-plane-wave Bloch spinors. A finite nuclear magnetization model is included to regularize the short-range hyperfine interaction and to account for the Bohr-Weisskopf effect. After applying scissor shifts to span the experimentally reported ThO₂ band gaps, we find calculated internal-conversion lifetimes in the range of 1-16~μm̊ s. The lifetime increases strongly as the band gap approaches ømegaₘ̊ ₙᵤc because the resonant interband phase space at the nuclear transition energy is reduced. For the larger reported ThO₂ gaps, the calculated lifetime is comparable to the measured conversion-electron Mössbauer lifetime [Nature 648, 300 (2025)]. Our analysis implies that choosing solid-state hosts with band-gap values slightly lower than ømegaₘ̊ ₙᵤc can optimize solid-state nuclear clock performance with internal-conversion electron readout.
authors: Udeshika C. Perera, H. B. Tran Tan, H. W. T. Morgan, Eric Hudson, Daniel A. Rehn, Andrei Derevianko

articles.title: First-Principles Wannier Representation of Proximity Effects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.25690v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Proximity effects in layered heterostructures are commonly represented by static parameters fitted to first-principles band structures, an approximation that usually discards the energy dependence of interlayer hybridization, momentum transfer, and spatial structure. We address this limitation by deriving a dynamical proximity operator directly from density functional theory by downfolding the heterostructure Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian onto a fixed low-energy target Wannier subspace. We demonstrate the method for three different graphene heterostructures coupled to magnetic and semiconducting substrates. Graphene/hBN/Co(0001) exhibits proximity-induced exchange resonances driven by hybridization with Co states. Graphene/PtSe₂ develops a sublattice-selective, intervalley-coherent, proximity-induced coupling. For graphene/WSe₂, we identify the spatial modulation of both Rashba and valley-Zeeman proximity-induced spin-orbit couplings. The method determines the full microscopic structure of the proximity coupling from first principles, providing input for transport and correlated-phase calculations.
authors: Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Johan Félisaz, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Denis Kochan, Oleg V. Yazyev

articles.title: Multiphysics simulation of all-optical switching and sequential magneto-optic readout in an integrated Si₃N₄/GdFeCo waveguide
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.22969v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In an integrated all-optical magnetic device, a guided pulse writes a magnetic state and a later optical signal reads it out. We study both steps for an 8 nm GdFeCo film inserted across a Si₃N₄ waveguide. A three-dimensional dispersive finite-difference time-domain calculation gives the energy absorbed from an 800 nm pump pulse. This energy drives a four-temperature model and calibrated stochastic two-sublattice Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch dynamics. After relaxation, a separate 532 nm probe is propagated through the fixed magnetic state for the optical readout. At the reference pump fluence, the model reverses 0.859 of the film from either saturated state. The switched fraction remains within 0.81-0.87 over a 2.4-fold range of incident fluence. A threshold rule applied to the local absorption map reproduces the five three-dimensional simulation points to within 8×10⁻⁴, showing that, within the model, incomplete reversal results from non-uniform guided-mode absorption. When the film starts from zero magnetization, thermal noise orients the recovered local moments at random; over 16 realizations, 0.502 ± 0.004 of the cells end with a negative x component of the FeCo moment. Among the simulated states, the probe transmission, reflection, and absorption fractions vary by at most 0.02. The magnetic Faraday and Kerr rotations are much more sensitive and become about 12 and 130 times smaller, respectively, in the stochastically recovered state than in a saturated film. The reflected signal also contains a magnetization-independent geometric background, which can be removed by subtracting a reference signal. These results link the switching efficiency to the guided-mode absorption profile and predict polarization-based readout of the simulated magnetic states. The model assumes a homogeneous film and neglects spatial exchange stiffness and subsequent domain coarsening.
authors: Muhammad Arief Mulyana, Budi Adiperdana, Ayi Bahtiar

articles.title: An Energy-Based Conservative-Dissipative Latent Neural Evolution Operator for Magnetization Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.04530v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a reduced-order learning framework that couples a convolutional autoencoder to a structured latent neural ordinary differential equation. A learned scalar generates the latent dynamics through an antisymmetric operator and a positive-definite dissipative operator. The antisymmetric component permits motion along scalar level sets, while the dissipative component decreases the scalar. Adding a coercive quadratic term gives bounded continuous-time latent trajectories and approach to the scalar's critical set under the stated assumptions. The scalar provides a structural constraint rather than an approximation of physical energy. The encoder, decoder, scalar, and operators are trained jointly on short snapshot windows without time-derivative supervision, physical-energy labels, or dissipation penalties. At inference, one initial state is encoded and evolved continuously in latent space, with decoding only at requested times. We demonstrate the framework on micromagnetic magnetization trajectories from NIST μMAG Standard Problem 4 and compare it with dissipative-only dynamics and an unstructured latent neural differential equation. Repeated training runs show competitive observed-horizon accuracy, while selected longer rollouts illustrate improved retention of approximately stationary states relative to the unstructured baseline. These results motivate scalar-generated latent dynamics as an inductive bias for reduced-order prediction and other learning tasks where bounded evolution and equilibrium behavior are important.

articles.title: Shannon Entropy as an Order Parameter for the Two-Dimensional Confined Coulomb Systems: Exact Balance Law, Topological Charge Sum Rule, and Boundary Saturation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.15428v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a complete information-theoretic framework for the minimum-energy configurations of the two-dimensional Thomson problem on a hard-wall disk, based on the Shannon entropy of the Voronoi topological charge distribution. Two exact identities are proven and verified to machine precision for all studied systems of size N=12-10⁵. First, an entropy balance law decomposes the total entropy into bulk, boundary, and mixing contributions without approximation. Second, a topological charge sum rule fixes the total charge at twice the number of boundary particles plus six; together with the disjointness of bulk and boundary coordination sets - justified analytically via the Delaunay empty-circumcircle criterion and elastic disclination splitting - it relates the three- and four-coordinated boundary populations directly to the bulk charge. Applying Euler's theorem to the outermost Delaunay annulus yields an exact shell-mismatch identity: the four-coordinated boundary population equals the adjacent interior shell population, whereas the three-coordinated population equals their step mismatch, directly detecting third-shell nucleation at N=30. Furthermore, we prove that the boundary entropy is bounded by łn2 and that its saturation is equivalent to the bulk charge per boundary particle approaching -1/2, a regime restricted self-consistently to boundaries of at least 12 particles. Numerically, we locate bulk nucleation at N=56, maximal global disorder at N=146, and boundary saturation above Nsim10³, with a direct extension to spherical geometry.
authors: Georgiy K. Lavrov, Eduard G. Nikonov

articles.title: Chern non-trivial two-dimensional square-net nodal line semimetal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional pₓₚ_y square-net tight-binding model with two sublattices and introduce a symmetry-informed, momentum-dependent spin-orbit coupling (SOC) with a finite-range real-space hopping representation. Its two components jointly gap the nodal line, while one breaks time-reversal symmetry, producing a Chern-insulating phase with an occupied band Chern number C=2. Nanoribbon calculations reveal edge-localized states traversing this gap, with two net chiral modes per edge. We further show that the conserved spin sectors are unitarily equivalent and therefore have equal Chern numbers, ruling out a nontrivial time-reversal-protected Z₂ phase within this ansatz. Our results establish a phenomenological route to Chern topology in square-net two-dimensional systems and clarify the symmetry constraints governing the accessible insulating phases.
authors: Kendall Ramos, Salvador Barraza-Lopez, Elias Andrade

articles.title: Controlling transport with structured long-range hopping
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The combined effects of disorder and long-range hopping play an important role in determining localization and transport in low-dimensional quantum systems. We study transport in a one-dimensional disordered chain with nearest-neighbor hopping supplemented by a long-range hopping term. The long-range coupling is characterized by site-dependent amplitudes that may be either uniform or random. We investigate the interplay between diagonal disorder and long-range hopping, characterizing the resulting transport efficiency. We find that nearest-neighbor hopping in the presence of uniform long-range hopping amplitudes strongly suppresses delocalization over a range of weak disorder. The disorder-enhanced transport regime, established in previous studies, can be understood here as the recovery of delocalization from this strongly suppressed regime. An analytical solution in the Anderson eigenstate basis reveals the microscopic origin of this behavior. In particular, we show that the low-disorder regime of strongly suppressed delocalization can be eliminated by introducing randomness into the long-range hopping amplitudes, providing an additional mechanism for enhancing transport and qualitatively changing the response of the system to disorder.

articles.title: Dephasing-powered open quantum-dot battery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a simple realization of an open quantum battery powered by local dephasing. The setup consists of a triple-quantum-dot chain coupled at one end to a thermal reservoir, with the dot at the opposite end strongly detuned to form a high-energy storage element. Local dephasing populates this highly excited state and autonomously drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with high ergotropic efficiency. We find a limit where the ergotropic efficiency approaches unity, while the ergotropy itself approaches one-third of the energy detuning. We characterize the battery through its energy-storage performance, charging time, and stability, showing that the charged state remains long-lived after the dephasing source is switched off. We then demonstrate two complementary protocols for extracting the stored energy. First, nearly all the available ergotropy can be recovered through a simple cyclic unitary protocol involving only modulation of the detuned-dot gate. Second, coupling the detuned dot to an electronic load allows the extraction of electrochemical work exceeding the initial ergotropy, thereby accessing part of the battery's passive energy. Our results establish local dephasing as an autonomous resource for charging open quantum batteries and demonstrate simple routes for extracting the resulting stored energy in experimentally accessible mesoscopic platforms.
authors: Alok Nath Singh, Rafael Sánchez, Andrew N. Jordan

articles.title: Chemical Substitution as a Route to Anomalous Surface Superconductivity in NiBi₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stabilizing two-dimensional superconductivity in a bulk superconducting material provides a unique route to exploring the interplay between superconducting condensates of different dimensionalities. Here, we present evidence for a distinct surface-associated superconducting state in Pb-substituted NiBi₃. NiBi₂.₈Pb₀.₂ exhibits a resistive onset at Tc,ₒₙₛₑₜ*approx8.1~K, nearly twice the bulk superconducting transition temperature of approximately 4.1~K. The absence of a corresponding Meissner response or specific-heat anomaly at the higher-temperature transition supports its non-bulk origin. A cusp-like angular dependence of the critical field, well described by the two-dimensional Tinkham model, together with nonlinear current--voltage characteristics and signatures of a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, establishes the low-dimensional character of this superconducting state. Remarkably, the surface-associated superconductivity persists well beyond the bulk upper critical field, reaching a maximum ratio of Hc₃/Hc₂approx4.3, far exceeding the conventional Saint-James--de Gennes value of 1.695. These results demonstrate that Pb substitution can stabilize an anomalously enhanced low-dimensional superconducting state in NiBi₃, providing a platform for investigating superconductivity at the boundary of a bulk superconductor.
authors: Anupam Barik, Subhadip Chakrabarty, Achintya Low, Sudip Pal, Setti Thirupathaiah

articles.title: Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can the correlations favoring electron crystallization also generate superconductivity in the neighboring metal? We investigate this possibility in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with repulsive Coulomb interactions. Self-consistent Hartree--Fock calculations identify a commensurate triangular Wigner-crystal state. To investigate pairing on the metallic side, we construct a crossing-symmetric particle--hole vertex using coupled parquet and Bethe--Salpeter equations, incorporating exchange vertex corrections beyond polarization-bubble screening. Near crystallization, the enhanced electronic correlations generate an effective attraction favoring chiral f-wave pairing. Superconductivity is confined to a narrow metallic region adjacent to the crystal, qualitatively consistent with the superconducting sleeve observed near an insulating regime in rhombohedral graphene. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.

articles.title: Momentum-selective graphene spectroscopy of moiré excitons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Far-field photoluminescence probes only the light-cone corner of an exciton's momentum content, whereas energy transfer to nearby graphene integrates in-plane momenta up to the inverse spacer thickness 1/z. For a WSe₂/MoSe₂ heterobilayer we build the transition polarization bmPₙ₍qv) of each localized moiré exciton from the registry-dependent vector dipole texture and use each bmPₙ for both baths. The two baths rank the states differently: the graphene-rate ratios differ from the optical ones, their ordering inverts with spacer thickness, and the distance exponents at z=10,nm spread by more than two units. These ratios are independent of the transition-dipole prefactor. Within the C₃₋ₛymmetric leading-harmonic model the chiral p₊ and d₋ states are also dark at normal incidence yet transfer to graphene at rates comparable to the bright ground state. Their graphene rate depends on the sign of the texture phase, a quantity invisible in far-field emission, which we determine from first principles. In a device this prediction requires a splitting, larger than the symmetry-breaking mixing, that protects the chiral partners. Graphene proximity thus acts as a momentum-selective near-field probe of moiré excitons, and we propose its use as a practical spectroscopy.

articles.title: Electrically Reversible Layer-Tensor Responses in Bilayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The layer Hall effect provides a prototypical example of a hidden layer response in van der Waals bilayers: opposite layers carry compensating Hall currents at zero out-of-plane electric field, while an applied out-of-plane electric field E_z selects one layer over the other and switches the net Hall response. Here we show that this field-switching mechanism is not restricted to Hall transport, but follows from a general symmetry principle for response tensors. We formulate a selection rule for the layer tensor effect (LTE) using Jahn symbols. For a tensor with Jahn symbol J and rank r, the stacking operation that exchanges the two layers acts as a coset representative relating the +E_z and -E_z states. Tensor components that are odd under this operation are forced to cancel between layers at E_z=0, and acquire a macroscopic response satisfying T_α(+E_z)=-T_α(-E_z). This criterion allows us to enumerate the symmetry-allowed electrically reversible tensor components associated with different Jahn symbols and to identify their physical realizations in common response tensors. We apply the theory to representative anomalous Hall, shift-current, nonlinear Drude, piezoelectric, spin Hall, and spin-photocurrent channels. Model calculations and first-principles simulations further confirm the predicted field-odd responses. Our results establish an electrically switchable LTE framework, providing a unified route to multifunctional layertronic responses in bilayer materials.
authors: Zehou Li, Shenda He, Pan Zhou, Baoru Pan, Rui Tan, Lizhong Sun

articles.title: Virtual defect mediated quantum melting in supersolids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The current understanding of supersolid melting is largely based on mean-field theories predicting that such transitions arise from a structural energy minimization mechanism. Here, we show that soft-core quasi-one-dimensional supersolids stabilized by a shallow external lattice can instead melt at zero temperature into a superfluid phase with quasi-long-range positional order through the proliferation of virtual soliton--antisoliton pairs, leading to a Kosterlitz--Thouless transition. We derive the corresponding Renormalization Group equations from first principles and use them to determine the critical properties of the system. Remarkably, the proliferation of topological defects near criticality strongly renormalizes both the density modulation and the superfluidity behavior. The transition described is intrinsically a beyond mean-field effect, since the external lattice produces only a smooth crossover between weakly and strongly modulated states at the mean-field level.
authors: Lazaros Tsaloukidis, Matheus Grossklags, Luca Salasnich, Alejandro Mendoza-Coto

articles.title: Tilt-Controlled Multi-Gap Superconductivity in Type-II Weyl Semimetals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In type-II Weyl semimetals, strongly tilted Weyl cones produce coexisting electron and hole pockets, a natural multi-band setting for superconductivity, yet how the tilt controls the number and relative size of the superconducting gaps remains unclear. Here we classify the symmetry-allowed on-site pairing channels of a simple time-reversal symmetric tilted Weyl-semimetal model with D₄ symmetry and identify the fully symmetric A₁ channel as the leading instability for attractive on-site interactions, supporting a fully gapped two-gap state. The tilt acts as a microscopic control parameter, redistributing the band-resolved pairing susceptibility between the two Fermi-surface sectors rather than simply rescaling the total density of states. Once the tilt sufficiently enhances the secondary channel, a robust secondary gap develops and can exceed the primary gap even at weaker effective coupling, while inter-gap coupling locks both gaps to a common critical superconducting temperature. The Weyl cone tilt thus controls the emergence and hierarchy of multi-gap superconductivity.
authors: Mingyu Lee, Myungjun Kang, Sangmo Cheon

articles.title: Universal Scaling of the Little-Parks Oscillation Amplitude
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Little-Parks effect played a pivotal role in establishing fluxoid quantization in doubly connected superconductors and providing early evidence for electron pairing, central to BCS theory. More recently, it has emerged as an important phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order. Yet the amplitude of the Little-Parks oscillation has never been fully understood theoretically, as the conventional mean-field Ginzburg-Landau description does not account for its pronounced temperature dependence. Here, we develop a universal theoretical framework incorporating thermal fluctuations in reduced-dimensional superconducting rings. By analyzing Little-Parks measurements across multiple superconductors, we show that the resulting scaling quantitatively captures the temperature-dependent oscillation amplitudes over a broad range of materials and device geometries, resolving the long-standing discrepancy between theory and experiment.
authors: Yuelin Shen, Zixuan Huang, Xiaoying Xu, Wei Qin, Yufan Li

articles.title: Fermionic superfluid transition and pairing scale separation in the kagome flat band
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flat-band systems provide a promising platform for exploring exotic correlated phases owing to quenched kinetic energy and enhanced interaction effects. In this work, we investigate the flat-band superfluid transition in the attractive kagome Hubbard model using large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations accelerated by fast Fourier transforms and delay updates. Through systematic calculations of the transition temperature, spin susceptibility, and density compressibility, we establish the finite-temperature phase diagram at the flat-band filling h̊o=5/3 and find a clear linear scaling of the superfluid transition temperature with the interaction strength, Tc=0.0314|U|. Our results reveal a wide separation of temperature scales between local pair formation and global phase coherence, which stabilizes a broad intermediate supercompressible bosonic fluid region of preformed pairs that bridges the normal Fermi gas and the flat-band superfluid. We further demonstrate that both the transition temperature and density compressibility are significantly enhanced in the flat band compared to van Hove fillings. Our findings highlight the essential role of flat-band-enhanced pair-density fluctuations in separating the pairing and phase-coherence scales, offering clear experimental signatures for probing flat-band superfluidity and superconductivity in cold-atom and kagome-material platforms.

articles.title: Nodeless d-wave pairing in monolayer FeSe revealed by intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Josephson effect provides a direct phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order and has played a central role in identifying unconventional pairing symmetries1-6. Conventional Josephson interferometry, however, extracts phase information through engineered junction geometries and crystallographic orientations, rather than by resolving the internal phase structure of the pair state within a single unit cell. Here, we use a superconducting Nb tip to realize atomic-scale Josephson interferometry in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3. Despite a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum, the local Josephson response exhibits a striking intra-unit-cell pattern, with maxima centred on Fe-Fe bonds and robust nodal lines along the Fe-Se directions. We show that these nodal lines arise from destructive interference between Josephson tunnelling amplitudes associated with opposite-sign pairing components. Microscopic calculations reproduce the observed spatial pattern and identify it as a fingerprint of nodeless d-wave pairing. Our results establish intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry as a local phase-sensitive probe of pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors.
authors: Runxin Li, Yuchen Huo, Jiong Mei, Ming-Qiang Ren, Miaomiao Wang, Quanxing Wei, Fengyu Yao, Maowen Zheng, Qing Qu, Cui Ding, Hongtao Yuan, Zhuoyu Chen, Wei-Qiang Chen, Kun Jiang, Qi-Kun Xue, Yu-Jie Sun

articles.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.
authors: Gabriele Bellomia, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Massimo Capone, Adriano Amaricci

articles.title: From Autonomous Knowledge Generation to Generalizable Property Prediction: A Precision-First Pipeline for Electro-Optic Materials Discovery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electro-optic materials, whose refractive index changes linearly with an applied electric field (the Pockels effect), set the speed and energy of optical modulators and microwave-to-optical links for quantum computing. Designing better materials requires optimizing composition alongside temperature, strain, and bias field. However, general repositories lack electro-optic tensor data. We present a pipeline that builds such a database from literature following the rule: "no value is better than a wrong value." The pipeline has five stages: physics-aware acquisition, layout-aware extraction via LLM and deterministic table parsers, a three-tier verification gate, cross-paper consensus using median and median absolute deviation, and a noise-robust surrogate model audited by leave-one-material-out (LOMO) testing. Physics enters directly: notation is mapped, point-group symmetry-forbidden Pockels components are rejected, equivalent labels are merged, and values carry provenance tags. In a run over 49 publications, the gate processed 816 candidates into 414 accepted, 215 held for review, and 187 rejected. Against a hand-certified gold standard of 303 values from 16 papers, the run achieved a precision of 0.51 and recall of 0.48 for exact record matches. Across four database snapshots, held-out materials where the surrogate model beat a predict-the-mean baseline grew from 1 of 4 to 9 of 13 as the database expanded from 10 to 22 materials. While not a controlled comparison, this trend supports the premise that a precision-oriented, physics-checked database can power forward models beyond its training set and clarifies requirements for inverse material design.

articles.title: Helicity-Selective Electron-Phonon Coupling Between PT-Partner States in 2H-bilayer MoS₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotational symmetry (Cₙ₎ constrains chiral phonons, but how other symmetries affect their interactions remains largely unexplored. We perform a theoretical and computational study of chiral phonon coupling to parity-time (PT)-degenerate electron doublets in 2H-bilayer MoS₂. Although PT suppresses phonon singlet chirality, chiral phonon doublets can helically interact with PT-partner electronic states via a mechanism similar to pseudospin. Selection rules are then analyzed with the interplay of PT and C₃. Our computational results of 2H-bilayer MoS₂ suggest chiral phonons may be used to resolve intravalley electronic states in PT systems.

articles.title: Momentum-resolved thermodynamics and barrier-free order-parameter collapse in spin-orbit-coupled superconductors under a Zeeman field
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can enhance the critical Zeeman field of clean superconductors beyond the Pauli limit. We develop a momentum decomposition of the zero-temperature free energy to investigate spin-singlet s-wave superconductors with general time-reversal-symmetric SOC. The SOC component perpendicular to the Zeeman field enhances the critical field and suppresses first-order features, whereas the parallel component favors Pauli-limited thermodynamic behavior. Applying this framework to Rashba superconductors and Ising superconductors with weak Rashba SOC, we identify the origin of the abrupt collapse of the superconducting order parameter at the critical field. Competing angular contributions produce a nearly flat free-energy landscape, allowing a barrier-free order-parameter collapse distinct from the conventional Pauli-limited first-order transition.
authors: Xusheng Wang, Gaomin Tang, Lianyi He, Shuai-Hua Ji

articles.title: Information-theoretic entropy imaging of quantum matter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase transitions can generate intricate spatial organization invisible to spatially averaged probes, yet quantitative measures of this organization remain limited. Here we develop "entropy imaging," an information-theoretic technique that harnesses lossless compression to quantify spatial complexity, predictability, and order in quantum materials. Using this approach, emergent spatial textures can be imaged and converted into an experimentally-accessible observable: the computable information density (CID), a compression-based measure of information complexity that approaches the Shannon entropy rate in the large-system limit. Applied to millikelvin microwave impedance microscopy of graphene, the method reveals a pronounced maximum in the CID near quantum Hall transitions, a quantitative measure of the information-rich spatial organization of the critical landscape. A disordered Hofstadter model reproduces this behavior and shows that the CID can identify the quantum critical point from a sequence of images, without ensemble averaging over disorder realizations. The same framework tracks fractional quantum Hall transitions and resolves isolated fractional puddles that coexist with a disordered background. By contrast, the trivial band-edge crossover in a MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer exhibits qualitatively different behavior, suggesting that the pronounced CID enhancement observed at the quantum Hall critical point is not simply a generic feature of a conductive-insulating crossover. We further show that the geometric information encoded in CID is not reducible to a correlation length, and it can even distinguish spatial textures with identical multifractal statistics. Together, these results establish lossless compression as a framework for quantifying emergent spatial organization in quantum materials, with portability across imaging modalities and physical systems.
authors: Chen Wu, Leonard W. Cao, Lingyuan Lyu, Liam Cohen, Jiahui Nie, Can Uzundal, Yujia Hu, Quanjin Wang, Ziying Yan, Sneh Pancholi, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Feng Wang, Andrea F. Young, Tarun Grover, Monica T. Allen

articles.title: Modeling the CNOT gate in Germanium double quantum dots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We model a controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate mediated by exchange interactions in a realistic Ge/GeSi hole spin-qubit device. We use for that purpose a computationally efficient framework based on a compact dressed basis of many-body singlet and triplet states, which enables fast time-dependent simulations that would be prohibitive within a conventional configuration-interaction approach. We discuss the dominant sources of infidelity in ideal (noise-free) devices. On the one hand, the nonadiabaticity of the tunnel barrier ramps, enhanced by the transverse component of the exchange interaction, imposes limits on the speed of the CNOT gate. On the other hand, the AC Stark shift of the conditional resonance and the off-resonant driving of the complementary transition can significantly degrade the gate fidelity and call for a careful optimization of the driving conditions. Finally, we investigate the impact of quasi-static charge noise on the fidelity of the CNOT gate. We find that the capture of charges near the qubits can strongly disrupt the conditional operation, while the nanometer-scale motion of charges results in a loss of fidelity that sensitively depends on the position and strength of the corresponding dipole. Our results quantify the requirements on barrier control, microwave driving, and charge-noise stability for high-fidelity two-qubit operations in Ge/GeSi hole-spin qubits.

articles.title: Quantum Reversibility Meets Classical Reverse Diffusion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.18512v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayes' rule connects forward and reverse processes in classical probability theory, and its quantum analogue has been discussed in terms of the Petz (transpose) map. For quantum dynamics governed by the Lindblad equation, the corresponding Petz map can also be written in Lindblad form. In classical stochastic systems, the analogue of the Lindblad equation is the Fokker-Planck equation, and applying Bayes' rule to it yields the reverse diffusion equation underlying modern diffusion-based generative models. It is known that a semiclassical approximation of the Lindblad equation yields the Fokker-Planck equation for the Wigner function, which is a quasiprobability distribution defined on phase space as the Wigner transform of the density operator. Here we demonstrate that applying the same approximation to the Lindblad equation associated with the Petz map produces an equation that coincides with that obtained from the Fokker-Planck equation via Bayes' rule. This finding establishes a direct correspondence between the Petz map and Bayes' rule, unifying quantum reversibility with classical reverse diffusion.
authors: Ryota Nasu, Gota Tanaka, Asato Tsuchiya

articles.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a C^*-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra A is realized as the twisted group C^*-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module P endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of P: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a C^*-diagonal of A, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is T₀, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.
authors: Cathy Cheng, Nigel Higson, Danilo Polo Ojito, Emil Prodan

articles.title: Hidden Fisher Information in Many-Body Quantum Sensors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) determines the ultimate precision of a quantum sensor after optimization over all allowed measurements, but it does not quantify how difficult the optimal readout is to implement. We introduce a moment Fisher hierarchy F_M⁽k⁾, which measures the fraction of QFI accessible to collective spin moments up to degree k, together with a readout-complexity scale k₉₀ defined by the minimum degree required to recover 90% of the QFI. Applying this framework to a nonlinear collective-spin sensor, we show that many-body dynamics can preserve large QFI while transferring the optimal readout into high-rank SU(2) tensor sectors inaccessible to low-order collective observables. For system sizes up to N=100, first moments access only sim 10⁻² of the available QFI, while the degree required to recover 90% of it grows to k₉₀simeq 28. A rank-resolved analysis of the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) under weak damping shows that the nonlinear protocol pushes the optimal readout toward the highest available tensor ranks while strongly depleting its low-rank weight. These results identify nonlinear tangent-space shear as the mechanism behind a finite-size readout-complexity bottleneck in many-body quantum metrology.
authors: Atta ur Rahman, Muhammad Noman, Samira Elghaayda, Saeed Haddadi

articles.title: Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with wᵢₙfty gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level κ. At large |κ|, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent z=2-tfrac32|κ|⁻¹. We speculate that unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when κ drops below a critical value.

articles.title: Real-Time Correlation of Relaxation, Dephasing, and Two-level System Dynamics in Transmon Qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Materials improvements in transmon qubits have yielded remarkable advances in qubit lifetimes (T1)and coherence times (T2). However, state-of-the-art superconducting qubits experience temporal fluctuations in their performance, which limit gate fidelities and quantum processor performance. We observe correlated increases in qubit relaxation and dephasing rates that last for minutes to hours, which we call T1 and T2 excursions. Using interleaved lifetime and coherence time measurements, noise spectroscopy, and two-level-system (TLS) spectroscopy, we find that these excursions are caused by single or few strongly-coupled TLS defects that spectrally diffuse into resonance with the qubit frequency. Our measurement protocol provides a powerful tool for understanding the noise sources that cause temporal fluctuations in superconducting qubit performance.
authors: Ambrose Yang, Alexander M. Young, Paal H. Prestegaard, Atharv Joshi, Matthew S. Ai, Q. Rumman Rahman, Faranak Bahrami, Matthew P. Bland, Jui-Lin Niu, Ourania-Maria Glezakou-Elbert, Ray D. Chang, Jocelyn Liu, Zhengyi Lu, Robert J. Cava, Nathalie P. de Leon, Andrew A. Houck

articles.title: External-field-modified entropic exchange in confined quantum systems: static versus time-dependent electric fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review how external electric fields reshape the information content of spatially confined atoms, and we contrast the response to a uniform static field with that to a monochromatic, time-dependent laser field. The central quantities are the Shannon entropies in position and momentum space, Sr and Sp, and their sum ST = Sr +Sp, which obeys the BBM bound. Using the confined hydrogen atom (CHA) and the particle in a spherical box (PISB), its tight confinement limit, as reference systems, we first show that the field-free total entropy of the CHA depends non-monotonically on the confining radius whereas that of the PISB is strictly scale invariant. We then present Stark maps of the entropies for the ten lowest m = 0 levels at the confining radius of 6 a.u. The ground-state polarizability is reduced from the free-atom value 4.5 a.u. to 4.06 a.u. in the CHA but is 46.8 a.u. in the PISB, and the entropic response of the two systems differs correspondingly.

articles.title: Multipartite dynamics beyond bipartite entanglement equilibration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35377v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Entanglement equilibration need not mark the end of quantum-information dynamics in quantum thermalization. We show that the complete Schmidt spectra of a fixed tripartition can become stationary while its multipartite correlation structure, distinguished by local-unitary invariants, continues to evolve. This separation occurs exactly within a finite window in self-dual kicked-Ising dynamics and asymptotically in Haar-random circuits. We further demonstrate an independently tunable timescale for multipartite dynamics using quantum-error-correcting codes. When coupled to a locally scrambling bath, ordinary entanglement approaches equilibrium through rapid local scrambling, while weak logical--bath coupling drives a slower reorganization of multipartite correlations. These results reveal a deeper distinction than the ordering of equilibration times: bipartite entanglement and multipartite correlation structure can probe distinct physical channels of quantum-information dynamics, rather than merely different stages of the same relaxation process.
authors: Yan Liu, Ya-Wen Sun, Ren-Jie Ying, Jun-Yuan Zeng

articles.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35524v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power p close to -1. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that at finite disorder strength W of moderate strength, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, this power p₁ vanishes and the spectrum features a very accurate power behavior with p<0 on an interval around E = 1 spreading increasingly closer to E=0 and E = infty with increasing W. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings t in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant 1/t distribution regularized via t in [e⁻W/², eW/²], and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. We show that łimW → ᵢₙfₜy p(W, E)=-1 for all energies accessible by our data. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff W, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant 1/t noise into a scale-invariant 1/E distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, to model the IR sector of the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be viewed as descending from the randomness strength W rather than the lattice size L.
authors: Jiří Adam, Andrei Alexandru, Navdeep Singh Dhindsa, Ivan Horváth, Frank X. Lee, Nilmani Mathur

articles.title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.
authors: Zhi-Yao Ning, Zi-Xiang Li, Naoki Kawashima

articles.title: Anomalous mass renormalization in two-dimensional electron systems on ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor β-Ga₂O₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.16137v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-dimensional electron systems (2DESs) at wide-bandgap semiconductor surfaces and interfaces are fertile ground for emergent quantum phenomena. Here, we use micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to resolve the momentum-space electronic structure of a surface 2DES in β-Ga₂O₃, an ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor with a band gap of 4.7 eV. In situ electron doping of cleaved, high-purity β-Ga₂O₃ single crystals produces an essentially circular Fermi surface. With the self-consistent Poisson-Schrödinger model, the 2D electrons are estimated to be confined within approximately 1.2 nm beneath the surface, with an internal electric field of approximately 18 MV cm⁻¹. Our analysis based on ARPES measurements reveals nearly a twofold increase in the electron mass at high sheet carrier densities. This trend deviates from the conventional behavior reported for wide-bandgap semiconductors and indicates mass renormalization beyond the conventional screening-based picture. Our results provide quantitative momentum-space benchmarks for the Fermi-surface geometry and density-dependent quasiparticle dispersion of the β-Ga₂O₃ 2DES, opening a route to studying density-tunable interfacial quantum states in the UWBG regime.
authors: Ryu Yukawa, Hiroshi Mizuseki, Suryo Santoso Putro, Yé-Jin L. Lee, Yuuki Masutake, Hinako Telengut, Boxuan Li, Hajime Yamamoto, Tadashi Abukawa, Junya Yoshida, Vladimir V. Kochurikhin, Taketoshi Tomida, Masanori Kitahara, Takahiko Horiai, Akira Yoshikawa, Nobuhiko Sarukura, Noriko Chikumoto, Toshihiko Shimizu, Marilou Cadatal-Raduban, Yoshiyuki Kawazoe, Ryuhei Kohno, Hiroshi Kumigashira, Takuto Nakamura, Tatsuhiko Kanda, Akira Yasui, Akihiro Koide, Miho Kitamura, Hideaki Iwasawa, Koji Horiba, Kenichi Ozawa

articles.title: Space-time Floquet operator: Nonreciprocity and fractional topology of space-time crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.16562v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a space-time Floquet operator for crystals whose spatial and temporal translations are intertwined. Unlike the conventional Floquet operator, which describes evolution over a full time period, the space-time Floquet operator evolves the system over a fraction of the period paired with a spatial shift that generates the primitive space-time unit cell. Its eigenmode spectrum defines a space-time band structure that unfolds conventional Floquet bands to reveal the consequences of the intertwined crystal symmetry in reciprocal frequency-wavevector space. We relate the topology of these space-time bands to quantized transport phenomena, such as Bloch oscillations and adiabatic charge transport, and uncover an intrinsically fractional charge pump enabled by the primitive space-time cycle. Numerical simulations quantitatively support these predictions with small deviations controlled by the speed of the modulation. We also demonstrate how nonreciprocal parametric resonances are naturally anticipated and accurately predicted by our framework. Our approach applies broadly to both classical and quantum systems with space-time symmetry, including non-Hermitian crystals.

articles.title: Sound waves in a backreaction-affected analogue spacetime: acoustic metric, mass, and correlations in Bose-Einstein condensates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.24233v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Analogue gravity describes sound as a field propagating on an effective spacetime set by the background flow, which is usually treated as given; in reality, however, quantum fluctuations also feed back on the medium that defines this spacetime. This raises the question of whether a condensate modified by this backreaction still defines a spacetime for the quantum field, which has not been established so far. Using a number-conserving expansion of a Bose-Einstein condensate, which keeps the classical background and the quantum fluctuation distinct while retaining their mutual coupling, we show that in the sound-wave and eikonal approximations the first-order phase fluctuation still propagates on an acoustic metric of the backreaction-corrected condensate, but is no longer massless: it obeys a Klein-Gordon equation with a spacetime-dependent mass that is generated by the backreaction sources in the continuity and Euler equations and cannot be absorbed into the metric. Backreaction in a Bose-Einstein condensate is thus a change of the analogue spacetime, supplemented by a mass term that has no geometric counterpart. Solving the coupled condensate-Bogoliubov dynamics for a finite, quasi-one-dimensional gas quenched from a noninteracting state, we find that, while the depletion remains below 2%, backreaction enhances the canonically normal-ordered equal-point phase correlation by about 10% in the bulk and up to about 20% near the walls, and that the bulk enhancement survives a finite-resolution imaging model.

articles.title: An Efficient Quantum Spectral-Galerkin Method for Linear Elliptic Equations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an efficient quantum spectral-Galerkin method for constant-coefficient second-order linear elliptic equations. The method employs a boundary-adapted Jacobi tensor-product basis that incorporates the boundary condition into the approximation space and produces Galerkin systems with polynomially bounded condition numbers and sparsity. For analytic solutions satisfying a suitable uniform regularity condition, spectral convergence allows the normalized Galerkin coefficient state to be prepared with complexity poly(d,łog(1/ϵ)), where d is the spatial dimension and ϵ is the error tolerance, under standard sparse-access and state-preparation assumptions. At the state-preparation level, this improves the precision dependence over fixed-order finite-difference and finite-element discretizations. We further show how to estimate prescribed linear functionals of the solution, with an additional O(1/ϵ) factor arising from norm and inner-product estimation.

articles.title: Preparing State-Selected Molecular Beams with high Efficiency using Quantum Cascade Lasers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the ro-vibrational state-selective preparation of CO molecules (v = 0, J = 0 i̊ghtarrow v = 1, J = 1) in an internally cold molecular beam using a continuous-wave, narrow-linewidth distributed feedback type quantum cascade laser, with an output wavelength of 4.65 μm. Using a modulation-free wavelength stabilization scheme, we show that population transfer to near saturation levels can be obtained with sufficient long term stability, as needed for state-resolved scattering experiments. We show preliminary results of CO molecules prepared in the v = 1 state, scattering from a clean Cu(100) surface. This study showcases the promise of QCL based excitation for state-selected molecular beam based scattering experiments, especially involving transitions in the mid-infrared domain (łambda > 4.5 μm) which are otherwise difficult to access using conventional sources.
authors: Ardra P. S., Pranav R. Shirhatti

articles.title: HarP: a simulation tool for high-order harmonic generation and propagation in gases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurately simulating high-order harmonic generation (HHG) for attosecond science requires connecting the microscopic single-atom quantum dynamics and the macroscopic propagation of intense driving laser fields. HarP is an open-source Python code designed to address this multiscale problem. It solves the wave equations for both the driving laser field and the generated harmonics, using precomputed dipole tables for the nonlinear polarization density. This tabulation enables the direct integration of accurate microscopic models while avoiding costly calculations during the propagation. The methodology builds upon the approach of [L'Huillier et al. (1992) PRA 46, 2778] and has already facilitated multiple studies on phase matching, propagation effects and HHG optimization. This paper presents the underlying physical model, its numerical implementation, and comparison against alternative simulation frameworks.
authors: Mattys Pouyez, Dominika Maslarova, Linus Hagedorn, Patrik Jansson, Robin Weissenbilder, Stefanos Carlström, Anne L'Huillier, Tünde Fülöp

articles.title: Chirpons: elementary local phase oscillations associated with complex zeros
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complex wave, the local phase variation provides the instantaneous frequency in time, the local wavenumber in space, and the local momentum in quantum mechanics. Here we study this quantity from the complex-zero structure of the analytic continuation of the wave. A single nonreal zero produces a localized Lorentzian phase variation on the real axis, whose position, width, sign, amplitude, and integrated phase are fixed by the zero itself. We call this elementary zero-associated oscillation a chirpon. The representation is exact for finite products and finite Fourier sums, and extends to entire and band-limited functions through canonical factorization. We illustrate the construction with superoscillatory sequences and discrete Fourier sums, showing how local anomalous oscillations can be reconstructed from periodic families of complex zeros. We further show how linear systems transform chirpons through the displacement of their associated complex zeros, and illustrate this dynamics for quadratic dispersive propagation and a resonant harmonic oscillator. This establishes a direct relation between local phase structure and the amplitude and phase response of the transfer function, suggesting a zero-based form of spectroscopy in which system parameters can be inferred from the motion, width, and orientation of chirpons. More broadly, the chirpon description provides a unified framework for instantaneous frequency, local wavenumber, superoscillation, backflow, and other local phase phenomena, while offering a new route for probing linear systems through the dynamics of their complex zeros.
authors: Enrique G Neyra, Laureano A Bulus Rossini, Pablo A Costanzo Caso, Marcelo F Ciappina, Lorena Rebón

articles.title: Kaonic Atom Measurements with the SIDDHARTA-2 Experiment at the DAΦNE accelerator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kaonic atoms provide a unique experimental tool to investigate low-energy strong interactions in systems containing strangeness and, through high-lying transitions, to test bound-state quantum electrodynamics. The SIDDHARTA-2 experiment at the DAΦNE electron--positron collider performs high-precision X-ray spectroscopy of kaonic atoms using low-momentum charged kaons produced in φ-meson decays. Its primary goal is the study of kaonic deuterium through the measurement of X-ray transitions to the ground state, providing direct access to the low-energy K⁻d interaction. In parallel, SIDDHARTA-2 has carried out a broad experimental programme with gaseous targets, including kaonic helium-4 and kaonic neon, as well as measurements of high-n transitions in intermediate-mass kaonic atoms formed in the materials of the experimental setup. In this paper, the main SIDDHARTA-2 measurements and their physics motivations are reviewed, together with the experimental strategy developed for kaonic deuterium and the future perspectives of the collaboration within the EXKALIBUR programme.
authors: D Sirghi, L Abbene, F Artibani, M Bazzi, G Borghi, D Bosnar, M Bragadireanu, A Buttacavoli, M Carminati, A Clozza, F Clozza, L De Paolis, R Del Grande, K Dulski, C Fiorini, I Friščić, C Guaraldo, M Iliescu, M Iwasaki, A Khreptak, S Manti, J Marton, P Moskal, H Ohnishi, K Piscicchia, F Principato, A Scordo, F Sgaramella, M Silarski, F Sirghi, M Skurzok, A Spallone, K Toho, J Zmeskal, C Curceanu

articles.title: Beyond Exact Recovery: Operational Success Probability and Sampling Cost for Approximate Quantum Optimization under Stochastic Uncertainty
articles.abstract: Approximate optimization algorithms are commonly evaluated through exact optimum recovery or objective-space approximation, although these criteria need not coincide with the quality of the resulting decision in its downstream operating environment. This paper develops an end-to-end evaluation framework that separates three notions of solver success: exact recovery of the mathematical optimum, near-optimality with respect to the optimization surrogate, and operational acceptability under stochastic downstream evaluation. We study the framework using a small binary inventory-control benchmark represented by a calibrated and held-out-validated QUBO surrogate and solved with exact enumeration, greedy search, simulated annealing, uniform feasible sampling, and ideal QAOA at depths p=1,2,3. The results show that mathematical near-optimality and downstream operational acceptability define distinct solution sets. For QAOA, the probability mass assigned to operationally acceptable solutions can differ materially from both exact-recovery and QUBO-near-optimal probability, producing substantial differences in the number of measurements required to observe an acceptable solution. For n=8 at p=2, the median number of shots required for 95% observation probability decreases from 392 under exact recovery to 84 under QUBO near-optimality and 31 under the operational criterion. However, operational success alone can be misleading when acceptable states are abundant. We therefore use a descriptive enrichment comparison against uniform feasible sampling. Statistically supported enrichment is observed only in selected regimes, while classical greedy and simulated-annealing baselines outperform QAOA on these small instances. The results therefore do not indicate quantum advantage; rather, they show that solver evaluation can change materially when success is defined in terms of downstream decision consequences rather than surrogate-objective recovery alone. The QAOA statevector implementation and selected frozen confirmatory cases were independently reproduced with Qiskit and Qiskit Aer to floating-point precision.

articles.title: Tuning in Dielectric and Electrical Transport Properties of CuFe2O4 with Incorporation of Metal oxides (ZnO, WO3 & MgO) Nanostructures
articles.abstract: Copper ferrite (COF) nanocomposites with different weight fractions (10 to 50 wt. %) of metal oxides (MOs; M = Zn, Mg & W) were synthesized by powder mixing method. The phase analysis and microstructure were examined by XRD, SEM and TEM techniques. The XRD analysis showed the formation of required nanocomposites without any other impurities. The examination of microstructure revealed the different morphology like; spherical, nano-discs, nano-plates and nano-spindle etc. The bahavior of dielectric constant (ε′), and dissipation factor (tanδ), of (MOs)x/(COF)1−x are consistent with Maxwell-Wagner polarization and Koop’s phenomenological theory. Moreover, the ε′ & tanδ show decreasing behavior with incorporation of MOs nano-structures. The a.c. conductivity with frequency follow the dynamical law σ (ɷ) = A ɷs. Finally, the incorporation of MOs wt. fractions reduce the conductivity due to substitution of Fe3+ and Fe2+ ions by metal cations (Zn2+, Mg2+ and W3+) from lattice site.

articles.title: Towards optimal preparation of triangular quantum cycle shifts
articles.abstract: An algorithm for the optimal preparation of triangular quantum cycle shifts is presented. Through theoretical analysis, it is shown that any optimal sequence of powers of two that sum to the fixed integer shift step must guarantee the exhaustive application of four local exchange rules, leading to the non-adjacent form of that integer step. Based on this, it is shown that the optimal form exists in the search sub-space formed by just considering the two closest powers of two from a given signed integer remainder, and that it can be reached via exhaustive depth-first search but also by a simpler approach, nicknamed “Domino”. Experimental comparisons between Domino and previously studied preparators for triangular quantum cycle shifts verify that the former always identifies the optimal sequence. Notably, the proposed approach achieves the same benefit in quantum cost as the previously studied dynamic programming algorithm, at more than 8 times the speed. Experiments on noisy backends further imply that Domino becomes asymptotically superior in noise resistance to the other methods as the register width grows, retaining a roughly 9% fidelity lead. These results establish Domino as an appealing choice for maximum-performance triangular quantum cycle shift preparation.

articles.title: Quantum Counting in the Rydberg Blockade
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.19298v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a quantum algorithm for approximately counting the number of solutions to planar 2-satisfiability (2SAT) formulas natively on neutral-atom quantum computers (NAQC). Our algorithm maps Boolean variables to atomic registers arranged in space according to a given formula, so that 2SAT constraints are enforced via the Rydberg blockade between neighboring atoms. A quench of an initial computational basis state then produces a superposition of all solutions after sufficiently long evolution. For almost uniform superpositions, a polynomial number of measurements is enough to estimate the solution count up to any constant multiplicative factor via sampling-based counting. Numerical simulations show that the protocol leads to almost uniform solution sampling in 1D and 2D grids and produces accurate counts for small random 2SAT instances on punctured grids. We implement our algorithm on Pasqal's Orion Alpha NAQC and demonstrate approximate counts within small multiplicative factors of the exact count for a planar grid instance with 81 atoms.
authors: Joseph Gibson, Victor Drouin-Touchette, Stefanos Kourtis

articles.title: Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.14314v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive. The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the Z_N-particle exhibiting ZN× gcd₍₂,N₎ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the Z_N-membrane possesses ZN× gcd₍₃,N₎ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of (5+1)D 1-form Z_N symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the Z₃ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic Z₂ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit Z₃ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial Z₃ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to Z₂ × Z₃, with the Z₃ sector consistently captured by this process.
authors: Yitao Feng, Hanyu Xue, Yuyang Li, Meng Cheng, Ryohei Kobayashi, Po-Shen Hsin, Yu-An Chen
