articles.title: 2D pores offer an optimal balance of charge storage and charging kinetics
articles.abstract: Electrolyte-filled conducting nanopores are central to applications ranging from energy storage to neuromorphic computing, yet the influence of pore geometry and structure on ion confinement remains insufficiently understood. Here, we combine theoretical calculations and molecular simulations to investigate how nanopore charging depends on pore dimensionality and morphology, considering nanostructured electrodes comprising cylindrical (1D) and slit-shaped (2D) pores, as well as 3D disordered porous electrodes exemplified by a carbide-derived carbon (CDC) structure. We show that in 1D confinement, the equilibrium stored charge exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on pore size, whereas 2D pores generally provide higher charge and energy densities per unit surface area. Somewhat counterintuitively, charging dynamics in 2D pores can slow down with increasing pore size but remain substantially faster than in disordered 3D electrodes. Although counterion saturation at high cell voltages reduces the energy stored by subnanometer 2D pores relative to CDC electrodes, this limitation can be overcome by matching the pore width to the operating voltage. Overall, our results indicate that 2D pores offer an optimal balance between charge storage and charging kinetics, highlighting their potential for high-performance capacitive energy storage.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Calculation of salt solubility in aqueous electrolyte solutions based on a thermodynamic ion-aggregation model
articles.abstract: Based on a thermodynamic self-association model in salt solutions, new attempts have been made to predict salt solubility in NaCl solutions and other electrolyte solutions by incorporating potential of mean force (PMF) analysis from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. It was demonstrated that salt solubility is closely associated with critical ion aggregation concentration (CIAC) in the thermodynamic ion aggregation process. The CIAC is determined by estimating effective binding energy between a cation and an anion or a mean equilibrium constant in ion association process. The calculated salt solubilities in various alkali halide solutions are consistent with the experimentally measured values. Combined MD simulations and graph-theoretical analysis revealed that, in NaCl solutions, most ions remain isolated at lower salt concentrations, whereas various-sized ion aggregates emerge as the salt concentration increases. As the salt concentration rises beyond the CIAC, large aggregates are formed, eventually leading to liquid–solid phase separation in NaCl–water mixtures. It is anticipated that this salt solubility prediction approach, based on the thermodynamic ion self-association model, may also contribute to estimating the solubility limit of various solute molecules in aqueous solutions, such as alcohols, osmolytes, and peptides.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Intracavity photon statistics from correlated molecular electronic structure
articles.abstract: Quantum optics characterizes light through photon correlations, motivating their connection to correlated ab initio molecular electronic structure. In this study, intracavity photon statistics of cavity-coupled molecules are computed from QED coupled-cluster (QED-CCSD-22) densities and validated against exact diagonalization of the Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian. A change of coordinate origin or dipole convention displaces the ground state coherently, so second-order and higher cumulants of the cavity field are independent of these conventions even for molecular ions. The photon subsystem of QED Hartree–Fock is exactly coherent, so the invariant statistics describe fluctuations beyond this electron–photon product reference. The field fluctuations are super-Poissonian, and their degree of second-order coherence depends primarily on cavity frequency in the tested weak-coupling regime, falling from 18.5 to 4.9 for H 2 as the cavity is detuned from 5 to 20 eV. The third cumulant identifies non-Gaussian fluctuations and changes sign under reversal of the coupling direction.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Correcting basis-set errors due to the absence of the electron–electron cusp using an adiabatic connection
articles.abstract: This article proposes an analytical method to address the slow convergence of electronic structure calculations caused by the inability of finite one-particle basis sets to describe the electron–electron cusp. (Small Gaussian basis set errors are often constructed or used with the objective to reduce computational effort, and may contain other sources of errors.) A model correspondence is established between a calculation using a finite basis set with the physical Coulomb interaction and a calculation using a complete basis set with a model interaction (specifically, the error-function screened Coulomb potential characterized by a range-separation parameter μ ). By leveraging the adiabatic connection formalism, a simple correction formula is derived. It does not contain any fitting to reference experimental or calculated data. It depends only on the on-top pair density and a locally defined range-separation parameter ( μ ) derived from the basis set itself. This “adiabatic connection based basis-set error correction” is derived from the asymptotic expansion of the wave function at large μ for small inter-electronic distances. Therefore, it is applicable to both ground and excited states without the restriction imposed by the Hohenberg–Kohn theorem. Numerical tests illustrate that the method achieves chemical accuracy (energy errors <1 kcal/mol) using smaller basis sets than typically required.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. To address all these challenges, this work demonstrates the usage of Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the solution of the drift-diffusion equations with errors comparable to traditional simulation software using advanced training techniques to solve problems beyond the well-behaved equilibrium regime. For this study, we specifically choose an abrupt PN-junction in both one and two dimensions that features extreme gradients of the carrier concentrations at the Ohmic contacts and an abrupt discontinuity in the doping profile. Using the proposed PINN architecture, we are able to retrieve accurate results for all observables under all bias conditions. Additionally, we apply the PINN solver towards the inverse problem of retrieving doping profiles directly from desired electric field distributions or electrostatic potentials under non-zero applied biases. Our work establishes a powerful PINNs-based approach for semiconductor device modeling with the ability to solve inverse problems under non-equilibrium conditions for microelectronics research and discovery.
authors: Luke Ragan, Matteo G. C. Alasio, Enrico Bellotti, Luca Dal Negro

articles.title: Neural-DISCO: Source-Conditioned Counterfactual Editing of Neural Population Activity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how neural activity encodes behavioral and sensory variables is a key challenge in systems neuroscience. This requires models that go beyond predicting activity from labels and instead support source-conditioned counterfactual editing: given a recorded source response, we should be able to edit one measured behavioral or stimulus label and predict how neural activity would change while preserving other observed labels and source-specific variability not explained by the labels. Here, we introduce Neural-DISCO, a disentangled representation learning framework for counterfactual modeling of neural activity. Neural-DISCO partitions the latent space into label-specific components, each associated with an observed behavioral or stimulus label, together with a residual latent that captures variability not supplied through observed labels. Across simulated and real neural recording datasets, we show that this structure enables selective editing of measured labels to generate counterfactual neural responses while preserving the remaining content of the original activity. Further, to gain insight into how behavioral and stimulus labels are encoded at single-neuron resolution, we pair this disentangled framework with feature attribution methods that identify which neurons are most important for each label. We find that disentanglement enhances the recovery of known functional cell roles in both synthetic and real data. Together, these results support Neural-DISCO as a framework for counterfactual modeling of neural activity and provide a practical interface for probing how neural populations encode behavior and sensory information. Code is available at https://github.com/TangLab-UBC/Neural-DISCO-neurips.
authors: Nico Policzer, James Ho, Joseph Soo, Xin Tang

articles.title: RadonBench: A Benchmark of Classical and Learning-Guided Search Techniques for Problems in Combinatorial Geometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical optimization and learning-guided search offer complementary approaches to open problems in discrete mathematics, but their outputs are difficult to compare when search spaces, validity checks, and stopping rules differ. We present emphRadonBench, a benchmark for constructing maximum-cardinality Radon-free lattice configurations: finite subsets of Z^d admitting no integral Radon partition. It remains open whether Radon-free configurations with 11 points in Z³ or 21 points in Z⁴ are possible. If they exist, they would improve the corresponding lower bounds on the integer Radon numbers. We compare exhaustive extension, greedy local search, PatternBoost, AlphaZero, and AlphaEvolve. All outputs use one success predicate: a convex target-sized configuration succeeds exactly when its number of integral Radon points is zero. PatternBoost and AlphaZero construct verified Radon-free configurations of sizes 10 and 20, one point short of the respective targets; AlphaZero's best convex target terminals have two integral Radon points in both dimensions. Exhaustive extension over fixed seeds and declared finite search boxes likewise reaches a minimum of two integral Radon points. Greedy local search and AlphaEvolve each produce target-sized near misses with one integral Radon point. No audited run reaches zero. These results establish reproducible near-miss baselines over explicitly scoped search domains.
authors: Xiaoan Xu, Ethan X. Fang, Jesus A. De Loera, Junwei Lu, Luze Xu

articles.title: FG-ConvNO: A Geometry-Aware Neural Operator for Propeller CFD Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is essential in contemporary engineering design, yet it remains expensive to compute and can take thousands of CPU/GPU hours or more for a single high-fidelity simulation. Recent developments in machine learning for scientific modeling have led to powerful surrogate frameworks that can approximate flow fields and physical quantities by using a fraction of the computational cost. However, most of these methods require largescale homogeneous datasets or simple geometries, exhibiting severe generalization gaps when applied to complex and data-scarce configurations. To address this, we propose the Factorized Geometry Convolutional Neural Operator (FG-ConvNO) for robust geometry-aware propeller pressure prediction under limited training data. We introduce geometryaware encoding, efficient interpolation-based decoding, and auxiliary global quantity supervision. In addition, we incorporate DISCO blocks that use discrete continuous convolutions to make the model discretization agnostic. In our experiments, FG-ConvNO achieves the highest accuracy for both surface pressure and global thrust prediction on a procedurally generated propeller CFD dataset. Geometry-aware encoding and architectural simplification improve stability, while random vertex subsampling enhances robustness. Overall, adding geometric priors to grid-based convolutional operators reduces overfitting on complex propeller geometries and improves generalization in low-data regimes.
authors: Yichen Di, Valentin Duruisseaux, Di Zhou, Xinyi Li, Daniel Leibovici, Jean Kossaifi, Anima Anandkumar

articles.title: Collective Collaboration of Recursive Autonomous Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Smart factories must translate order-level objectives into production tasks at multiple scales and combine the capabilities of individual units into an overall delivery capability. To address repeated adaptation of organizational mechanisms across equipment, workshops, and factories, as well as coordination across levels under changing production conditions, this paper develops a framework for the collective collaboration of recursive autonomous agents (RAAs). A common task and capability interface supports the recursive decomposition of production objectives from the top down and the aggregation of conditional capabilities through peer collaboration from the bottom up. Composite units can therefore participate in higher-level organizations as agents of the same kind. We formulate organizational models for leaf and composite units, specify interface closure under composition and conditions for finite task expansion, and develop operational mechanisms linking task decomposition, resource commitments, result aggregation, and coordination within the scope affected by change. A production network integrating machining, inspection, and logistics across multiple workshops illustrates how a common organizational kernel is instantiated at the equipment-service, workshop, and factory scales. The framework connects recursive organization with explicit task responsibilities, capability conditions, and execution interfaces for manufacturing systems.
authors: Ziqing Zhou, Linqiang Hu, Yuning Chen, Hongda Zhang, Zhao Huang, Ding Zhou, Haining Xu

articles.title: Nowcasting aerosol particle size distributions from PM2.5 with physics-regularized flow matching
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The mass concentration of particles smaller than 2.5um (PM2.5) is cheap to measure and widely monitored, whereas the particle number size distribution (PSD) requires costly instruments and is measured at only a few research stations. Yet many aerosol effects, such as vapor uptake, cloud droplet formation and deposition in the human respiratory tract, depend on the PSD rather than on mass. We explore whether recent generative deep learning models can nowcast the PSD: from the PM2.5 record and eight meteorological parameters over a 24h window, a model generates an ensemble of plausible hourly size distributions for the same window, reflecting that one mass can arise from many size distributions. Rather than proposing a single best model, we use two contrasting Finnish stations, the boreal forest site Hyytiälä and the urban site Kumpula, as a controlled testbed. On it, we benchmark six generative models against deterministic and climatological baselines, locally and after transfer between sites, and test physical constraints for neural network training. Flow matching performs best overall; its guided variant has the lowest continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) at both sites. A constraint based on a reduced aerosol general dynamic equation (GDE) lowers the CRPS by 5.5-11.5% at the training site and reduces errors after transfer between sites. Transfer remains harder than local estimation, identifying training on large multi-station data sets as the next step towards PSD estimates at unmonitored locations. This benchmark establishes physics-informed generative models as a promising route from routine air-quality monitoring to size-resolved aerosol information.
authors: Zhi-Song Liu, Jenni Köykkä, Wenqing Peng, Ammar Kheder, Petri Clusius, Michael Boy

articles.title: Multitask Interactions in Recurrent Dynamics across 100 Cognitive Tasks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The brain continually learns tasks with very different computational demands. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have been used as dynamical surrogates for studying task solutions, with recent work extending this approach to joint training on multitask batteries. However, it remains unclear how tasks interact as these batteries grow in scale and heterogeneity: under what conditions do they transfer or interfere with one another, and how do these effects relate to task complexity and model structure? We study this question by simultaneously training hierarchical Almost-Linear RNNs (AL-RNNs) on 100 tasks spanning a wide range of cognitive demands. AL-RNNs allow us to vary the amount of nonlinearity in the recurrence, while hierarchical task features provide a low-dimensional interface for task-specific adaptation within shared dynamics. On this task battery, performance improves with both nonlinear capacity and task-feature dimensionality, with the joint hierarchical model outperforming both individually trained models and a single unstructured joint model. Many tasks are individually solvable with linear dynamics, yet cannot be solved together by a shared linear model. Through hierarchical task features, task-specific linear region usage, and task geometry, the trained model provides several related but distinct measures of task similarity that capture how computations are separated and combined within the shared backbone. Across a series of experiments, we relate these representations to individual task complexity, joint solvability, pairwise transfer learning, and leave-one-out adaptation. Together, our experiments characterize task interactions in multitask recurrent learning while demonstrating both the potential and the challenges of reusable dynamical backbones for cognitive computation.
authors: Sílvia García-Hernández, Leema Hamid, Manuel Brenner

articles.title: Cross-User Adaptation for sEMG Gesture Recognition via Continual Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prosthetic and assistive interfaces increasingly depend on decoding hand gestures from surface electromyography (sEMG). Because the signal is shaped by person-specific factors, the recurrent neural networks (RNNs) commonly used to model these temporal streams must adapt to new wearers and new gesture classes after deployment. Continual learning (CL) enables this adaptation without retraining from scratch, yet applying it to recurrent sEMG models is not straightforward. Standard recurrent training practices can destabilize learning, and which CL strategy holds up under realistic cross-user drift is unestablished. We evaluate three representative CL strategies under domain- and class-incremental drift on NinaPro DB1, and find experience replay to outperform elastic weight consolidation (EWC) and naive fine-tuning. It reaches 83.3% final accuracy for class-incremental drift while limiting forgetting to 1.8-5.8% accuracy drop, as against 16.2-28.5% for EWC and naive training. We further show these models must be trained on shuffled, independently-windowed segments. Streaming windows in temporal order collapses the network into predicting a single dominant gesture, while a shuffled, stateless regime trains stably. Finally, hand-crafted time-domain features raise per-task accuracy by up to about 40% over raw signals, but only replay preserves that gain under class-incremental drift.
authors: Aran Ramakrishnan, Shubhi Mishra, Tyler Ham, Assel Kembay, Jason Eshraghian

articles.title: Single-Cycle Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction with Compressed Continuous Wavelet Features and Deep Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in industrial applications, but their performance gradually degrades over time, making accurate lifetime prediction important for safety and reliability. However, reliable lifetime assessment generally requires extensive degradation testing, which is both costly and time-consuming. To reduce this burden, recent data-driven approaches have sought to predict the end-of-life cycle of batteries from only the initial few cycles. Nevertheless, identifying reliable degradation patterns from such limited early-cycle data remains challenging because early aging dynamics are often subtle and nonlinear. To address this issue, we adopt the continuous wavelet transform to convert cycle-wise voltage, current, and capacity signals into time-frequency representations, enabling multi-resolution characterization of degradation behavior. Building on this representation, we apply scale compression to reduce redundancy while preserving structural information in the scalograms. We evaluate the proposed framework on eight benchmark datasets derived from seven public battery datasets covering diverse electrode chemistries, cell form factors, and cycling protocols. Experimental results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms prior approaches in single-cycle remaining useful life prediction and remains robust as the number of input cycles increases from 1 to 100. In addition, redundancy-fidelity analysis characterizes the trade-off introduced by scale compression, and gradient-based visual explanations indicate that the model focuses on localized time-frequency regions associated with structured signal transitions during charge-discharge operation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed framework for early-cycle battery remaining useful life prediction.
authors: Sungeun Kim, Mingyu Jung, Yuri Kim, Jin-Sung Park, Jongbin Ryu

articles.title: MOFjson: An Explicit Topological Representation of Metal-Organic Frameworks for Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) rely on formats that separate atomic geometry from structural topology, forcing models to choose between unstructured coordinate lists and non-spatial string identifiers[1]. We present MOFjson, the first representation separating structural data into a raw atomic layer with explicit bond shift vectors and a derived layer exposing secondary building units (metal nodes and organic linkers) and network topology. Additionally, we introduce a benchmark with crystal-derived ground truth across four question categories. Across four models, MOFjson beats all three baselines in every category: 100% vs. 18-47% on reaching a block's nearest periodic copy, 96% vs. 71% on crystal system characterisation, and 60% vs. 48% on metal node and organic linker coordination. Ablating shift labels drops accuracy to 12.7%, proving models read the periodic graph rather than the surface format. MOFjson gives language models structure to read rather than reconstruct, establishing a foundation for agentic tool workflows and constrained MOF generation.
authors: Anabel Yong, Matthew Hart, Philippe Schwaller

articles.title: MINT: Mitigating Structural Inconsistency via Attentive Message Passing for Financial Anomaly Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Illicit account detection is a critical task for financial risk control systems, aiming to pinpoint malicious actors within transaction networks. Existing efforts typically recast transaction networks into directed multigraphs and leverage graph neural networks (GNNs) to detect anomalies via topological structures under the homophily assumption. However, directly grafting GNNs onto transaction graphs is faced with at least two pivotal challenges, i.e., structural inconsistency and label scarcity. The former arises from deceptive connections forged by malicious actors, while the latter stems from the lack of annotated data. In light of these, we introduce MINT, a novel graph neural framework that mitigates structural inconsistency via an attentive message-passing scheme on transaction graphs. Specifically, MINT introduces a discrepancy-aware feature propagation, which tracks malicious actors by quantifying deviations between nodes across bi-directional transaction flows. A transaction salience module is proposed to mitigate structural inconsistency by adaptively regularizing the interaction strength between nodes. Furthermore, to alleviate label scarcity, MINT is optimized via Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning, which exploits only a minority of illicit nodes coupled with a majority of unlabeled ones. Extensive experiments conducted on three financial transaction benchmarks, including two large-scale public and one in-house real-world datasets, validate the superior effectiveness of MINT over several cutting-edge baselines.
authors: Yin-Ju Wu, Bi-Cheng Yan, Berlin Chen

articles.title: A JiT-Based Denoising Defense Method Against Adversarial Examples for Radio Signal Automatic Modulation Classification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) of radio signals is a core technology for spectrum monitoring and electromagnetic situational awareness. Deep neural networks (DNNs) play an important role in this field owing to their powerful feature extraction capabilities and end-to-end learning paradigm. However, their vulnerability to adversarial attacks poses serious security challenges to practical deployment. Adversarial training, a common defense, has limitations including poor generalization across attack types and high training costs. Inspired by Just image Transformers (JiT), a diffusion generative model that directly predicts clean images, this paper proposes a JiT-based denoising defense against adversarial examples for radio signal modulation classification. During training, a signal-specific 1D Transformer denoising network is optimized via flow matching to directly predict clean signal samples. It thereby learns a mapping that projects arbitrary examples back onto the low-dimensional manifold of clean signal examples. During inference, arbitrary examples are fed into the trained network and directly projected onto this manifold. This enables denoising defense without prior knowledge of attacks. Experiments on the RML2018.01A dataset were conducted without attack information, using a single empirically selected, fixed denoising start time. Compared with PGD-based adversarial training, the proposed method achieves a relative improvement of at least 20.58% in robust accuracy under PGD attacks. It also achieves a relative improvement of 10.20% in classification accuracy on clean examples. When evaluated against attack types unseen during adversarial training, the proposed method provides stronger defense than adversarial training. In particular, at higher attack strengths, it achieves a relative improvement of at least 39.72% in robust accuracy.
authors: Shiwei Liu, Linyuan Wang, Nuolin Sun, Libin Hou, Bin Yan

articles.title: Accelerating SO(2)-Equivariant Materials Models through Low-Precision Emulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotationally equivariant architectures improve the physical fidelity of machine-learned (ML) universal materials models based on graph neural networks (GNNs). However, their scalability is limited by the use of non-trivial, high-precision tensor operations during both training and inference. Adopting the reduced-precision formats of matrix multiplication units (MMUs), e.g., FP8 instead of FP32, provides massive increases in throughput, up to 30x (60x) on NVIDIA Hopper (Blackwell) GPUs, but may lead to drastic loss of accuracy. Here, we introduce tailored 'emulated' low-precision operations under the integer Ozaki scheme to accelerate the 'SO(2)-equivariant' processing layers of GNNs, which dominate the runtime of (1) many state-of-the-art ML interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and (2) most universal ML Hamiltonian (MLH) models. Our framework, FlashSO(2), outperforms TF32, the most accurate native low-precision MMU format, in throughput, accuracy, and memory footprint at once. At the SO(2) layer level, it reaches 40x (7x) the throughput of MALOQ's (UMA's) reference implementation, an MLH (MLIP) model, sustaining up to 236 (232) effective Tflop/s on an NVIDIA GH200, 3.5x the FP32 peak. At the model level, FlashSO(2) helps train MALOQ 3.9x faster than its pure-FP32 version while reducing peak memory by 58% at no loss in accuracy. In molecular dynamics simulations with UMA, the speedup factor is 3.3x, and the peak memory is reduced by 51%. FlashSO(2) thus pushes the speed-accuracy Pareto frontier of equivariant materials models beyond the native low-precision formats and substantially lowers the resources required to exploit their scaling laws.
authors: Denghui Lu, Alexander Maeder, Alexandros Nikolaos Ziogas, Mathieu Luisier, Manasa Kaniselvan

articles.title: Multi-Horizon Future Discovery for Physics-Informed Exploration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exploration in physical control environments requires agents to identify actions whose consequences reveal previously unexplored aspects of the underlying dynamics. However, many intrinsic motivation methods rely on immediate prediction errors, state novelty, or local physical changes, which may overlook informative outcomes that emerge across extended temporal horizons. We investigate whether learning structured representations of reachable futures can provide a more effective basis for exploration. To this end, we introduce Hamiltonian Temporal Contrastive Curiosity (HTC²⁾, a framework that combines multi-horizon temporal representation learning with Hamiltonian phase-space structure. A horizon-conditioned contrastive critic learns temporal relationships from future-state pairs sampled within the same episode. The distance between positive-pair representations is then used as an intrinsic reward, encouraging the agent to explore futures that remain insufficiently organized in the learned representation. To incorporate information about physical dynamics, we additionally modulate this reward using bounded multi-step Hamiltonian variation, rather than directly rewarding changes in the Hamiltonian itself. We integrate HTC² with both Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and evaluate it across six DeepMind Control Suite tasks. Comparisons with ICM, RIDE, E3B, Plan2Explore, and a single-step Hamiltonian curiosity baseline are complemented by state-coverage evaluations, component ablations, and phase-space diagnostics to characterize the contributions of temporal learning and physical structure to exploratory behavior.
authors: Shuwei Wang, Qiang Guan, Brian Qiu, Haoxiang Huang, Haoxi Wang, Chenyu Li, Bo Xu, Sen Cui

articles.title: Physics-Informed Graph-Based Safe RL with Constraint-Specific Critics for Community Battery Coordination in Distribution Network
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High penetrations of distributed energy resources (DERs) and fast-varying electric vehicle (EV) charging intensify voltage and line-limit violations in distribution networks (DNs), making safe, low-cost operation increasingly challenging. This paper proposes a physics-informed safe deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for coordinating community battery energy storage systems to mitigate constraint violations while minimizing operating cost. To represent nonlocal spatiotemporal interactions, we develop a dual-level physics-informed graph representation in which line impedance and capacity shape spatial information propagation, while power-balance, voltage-profile, and flow-reconstruction losses regularize the latent state toward control-relevant physical consistency. Building on this representation, we develop Lagrangian Dedicated-Critic PPO (LDCPPO), which implements constraint-specific value decomposition: independent reward and cost critics preserve heterogeneous voltage- and line-loading-related learning signals and combine their advantages only during the Lagrangian policy update. Case studies on DNs with high rooftop photovoltaic penetration and EV charging demonstrate that the proposed method reduces the key voltage-violation degree by up to 80.5% compared with the tested baselines, while also achieving the lowest voltage-violation count and line-overload degree with competitive operating cost.
authors: Chenghao Huang, Yue Yang, Hao Wang

articles.title: Movable-Element Multi-Functional RIS-Assisted Hybrid RSMA-NOMA: A Constrained Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we propose a movable-element (ME) multi-functional reconfigurable intelligent surface (MF-RIS) architecture, termed MM-RIS, which integrates element mobility with adaptive signal reflection, transmission, amplification, and energy harvesting (EH) to enhance communication flexibility and energy self-sustainability. A hybrid rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) transmission scheme is further designed to improve spectral efficiency. We formulate an energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem by jointly optimizing transmit beamforming, power and rate allocation, MM-RIS configurations, panel deployment, and ME positions. To address the resulting non-convex mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem, we propose constrained hybrid deep reinforcement learning with federated transformer and parametrized sharing (CRAFTS). CRAFTS integrates multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) and multi-agent deep Q-networks (MADQN) through bi-directional parametrized sharing to handle continuous and discrete actions, respectively. Moreover, a transformer-based architecture and federated learning (FL) are incorporated to enhance state representation and distributed knowledge sharing, whilst a Lagrangian-based adaptive penalty mechanism facilitates the constraint satisfaction. Simulation results have demonstrated that the proposed MM-RIS architecture and CRAFTS framework substantially improve EE and constraint satisfaction compared to the benchmarks in the open literature. Moreover, the results validate the benefits of spatially reconfigurable MM-RIS, hybrid RSMA-NOMA transmissions, and intelligent collaborative learning, highlighting the potential of the proposed framework for energy-efficient and adaptive next-generation wireless networks.

articles.title: Infinity Machine: a self-improving AI agent for research
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the Infinity Machine, a self-improving AI agent that we use for research on problems whose answers aprogram or data can check. Each candidate solution is produced by a full tool-using agent that works for up to an hour in a fresh sandbox; proposers see only a public score, and a private split decides what counts. The harness itself(prompts, tools, skills, playbook, meta agent) is an editable genome, changed only through a kernel-enforced gate with held-out and cost checks. An autonomous mode goes from a plain-text goal to a verified report with no human step: an agent picks an open problem and writes its verifier, the kernel calibrates it, an adversarial agent audits it, and an agent that never sees the verifier re-checks the result. Across fourteen problems in six days, for about 180 of model usage, the system produced four results beyond the published state of the art on catalogued open problems in quantum information: a certified depolarizing-channel threshold point p = 0.064966, a qutrit positivity frontier of 0.2910672, a 44-gate depth-6 Golay state preparation, and a stabilizer-rank bound chi(T⁷⁾ <= 10. It also cut SABRE qubit-routing overhead from 68,559 to 12,087 added gates. In hardware, it cut the energy per MAC of an open 8x8 INT8 systolic tile by 77.7% through a full open RTL-to-GDS flow, bit-exact. Three fully autonomous runs ended in honestties with public records; one audit caught a stale record, and one agent-written score pointing the wrong way went unnoticed. We report the failures as carefully: the one self-derived harness generation was rejected on cost, proposers gamed lenient scorers four times, and operator changes were decisive for several results.

articles.title: KDHNet: A Knowledge-Driven Hybrid Network for Limited-Calibration SSVEP Decoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) achieve high information transfer rates but often require sufficient subject-specific calibration data for reliable decoding. Analytical spatial filters are effective with limited data, but their linear formulations constrain representation capacity. Deep models learn more flexible representations but are prone to overfitting when calibration data are scarce. We propose KDHNet, which combines knowledge-driven analytical processing with data-driven representation learning. After filter-bank preprocessing, cascaded task-discriminant component analysis (TDCA) and task-related component analysis (TRCA) extract discriminative and trial-reproducible components. Learnable sub-band weighting then fuses spectral information, and an SSVEPformer decoder learns temporal and spectral representations for classification. For inter-subject decoding, a target-guided least-squares transformation aligns source trials using one labeled target trial per class. Extensive experiments were performed on three public datasets, covering intra- and inter-subject protocols, five analysis windows, and multiple calibration ratios. In intra-subject evaluation, KDHNet achieved the highest mean accuracy and information transfer rate in 14 of 15 window settings and all ten calibration-ratio settings. In inter-subject evaluation, KDHNet obtained the best or second-best performance, and the gains were generally larger with less calibration data. Ablation studies indicated that the estimated TDCA projection performed better when fixed than when optimized from analytical or random initialization. Combining fixed knowledge priors with trainable neural modules is effective for low-calibration SSVEP decoding. This framework supports more practical, robust, and plug-and-play BCIs. Code is available at https://github.com/2665023991/KDHNet.
authors: Zhentao He, Ziwei Wang, Dongrui Wu

articles.title: Multilayer PDMS/PMMA@MXene composite films for dual-functional electromagnetic shielding and photothermal conversion
articles.abstract: Flexible multifunctional polymer-based films for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding are of great value in 5G communication technology, wearable electronics, and related fields. Here, a series of PDMS/PMMA@MXene multilayer composite films was constructed on the basis of an alternating P–M–P design, with PMMA microspheres serving as spacers; the preparation combined vacuum-assisted filtration with spray coating and curing. In such a porous, multilayer architecture, the film containing seven MXene layers (M7) delivered an EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE) of up to 57.4 dB at 10 GHz in the X-band (8.2–12.4 GHz), and the shielding was dominated by absorption loss. The films also converted light into heat efficiently: under an irradiance of 1000 W/m², the saturation temperature reached 61°C, and the photothermal response stayed stable over repeated cycles. These flexible multilayer films, which combine effective EMI shielding with photothermal conversion, are promising candidates for electromagnetic protection of electronic devices and for solar thermal utilization.

articles.title: Seasonal Prediction of Summer Accumulated Cyclone Energy over the Western North Pacific Using Causality-Informed Predictor Selection and a Convolutional Neural Network
articles.abstract: Accumulated cyclone energy (ACE) over the western North Pacific (WNP) is an important metric of basin-scale tropical cyclone (TC) activity and is essential for seasonal prediction and disaster risk reduction. In this study, empirical orthogonal function (EOF) analysis was applied to May–August WNP ACE anomalies, identifying two leading modes: a basin-wide mode and a dipole mode, which together explain 20.71% of the total variance. The basin-wide mode is associated with a sea surface temperature (SST) pattern resembling the developing phase of El Niño, whereas the dipole mode is linked to a developing Pacific Meridional Mode (PMM)-like SST pattern. Using the information flow method, physically meaningful predictors were selected from SST, subsurface ocean temperature, and major air–sea climate indices. These predictors were then used to develop month-specific convolutional neural network (CNN) forecast models for PC1 and PC2. Independent forecasts for 2024–2025 show that PC1 and PC2 maintains useful skill at lead times of 1–4 months. The EOF-based reconstruction using CNN-predicted PCs captures part of the observed spatial variability of summer WNP ACE anomalies, with relatively high skill over key TC-active regions, especially east of the Bashi Strait. The 2026 forecast suggests an enhanced ACE anomalies from May to July, then weaken in August. These results suggest that information-flow-based predictor selection combined with CNN modeling provides a useful framework for seasonal WNP ACE prediction.

articles.title: Superconductivity of abnormal magic-stoichiometric Na 3 Cl and Li 3 Cl salt crystals at normal pressure
articles.abstract: The identification of new materials with superconducting properties is the pursuit in the realm of superconductivity research. Here, we excitingly show that the simplest salt used daily can be made a superconductor at normal pressure only by adjusting its stoichiometry of Na, Li, and Cl as Na 3 Cl or Li 3 Cl at normal pressure based on first-principles calculations. These abnormal Na–Cl stoichiometric crystal of 3:1, the first “magic” ratio, include metallic atoms (Na, Li) in the core as well as hybridization of ionic and metallic bonding, facilitating the electron–phonon coupling for superconductivity with a critical temperature T c of 0.13 and 1.17 K. The flat bands and van Hove singularities near the Fermi level produce large densities of states, which is beneficial for the emergence of superconductivity. The crystal with abnormal Na (Li)–Cl magic stoichiometry is a precisely tunable, purely sodium (lithium) and chloride-based, which is, therefore, an ideal material for designing and understanding abnormal stoichiometric crystals. The methodology of constructing this abnormal crystal may be general to almost all elements, which could lead to insights into the physics of other conventional superconductors and even high-critical-temperature superconductors.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: A quantum k-nearest neighbors implementation using magnitude-aware comparisons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Much attention has recently been devoted to the k-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm as a case study for quantum computing algorithms. Several algorithms have devised methods to compute a similarity metric to solve Quantum KNN (QKNN). This paper presents a practical quantum encoding technique that enables Euclidean distance calculation between vectors with different L2 norms by appending a single component to each vector, then uses it in the QKNN problem. It is arguably simpler to understand and implement than comparable methods and uses fewer qubits. Further, an implementation of this algorithm is provided and is used to benchmark it against a recent Euclidean-distance QKNN method on standard labeled datasets. In addition to demonstrating proper formulation, the results show marked improvement over similar implementations during simulation with realistic noise due to the use of fewer qubits and thus more coherent circuits.

articles.title: Polynomial Time Quantum Approximation Schemes for Constrained Optimization
articles.abstract: When does a noisy quantum sampler enable an end-to-end polynomial-time algorithm with performance guarantees? Building on the instance-dependent finite-depth, finite-shot guarantees in the Constraint-Enhanced QAOA (CE--QAOA) studied in Ref.~i̧teonahfinite, we answer this question for a complete quantum--classical pipeline executed on near-term quantum devices. The analysis of Ref.~i̧teonahfiniteprovides conditions under which the ideal CE--QAOA sampler can assigninverse-polynomial probability(p₀₌Ømega(n⁻k))to the set of optimal solutions. Here, we extend this analysisand show that, with independent-shot amplification, polynomial-timefeasibility repair, and exact scoring, the resulting pipeline recoversan optimum with high probability in polynomial runtime. Ittherefore gives a quantum-powered fully polynomial randomizedapproximation scheme, which we call antextbfFPRAStextsubscriptq.We next show that this guarantee can survive device noise within an instance-dependent window. For effective circuit depth(G(n,p)=Θ(pn)), retaining a (G(n,p)⁻¹) fraction of the idealoptimal mass is sufficient to recover an optimum with probability atleast (1-δ) using[O!łeft(pnk⁺¹łog(1/δ)i̊ght)]shots. Outside this exact-hit window, deterministicrepair continues to guarantee feasibility and yields aninstance-dependent ((1+ǎrepsilon))-approximation scheme wheneverthe repair-induced objective inflation is controlled. We term this the  ǎrepsilon-Polynomial-Time Quantum Approximation Scheme (ǎrepsilon-PTQAS). We also place our hybrid algorithm within the Chen--Cotler--Huang--Li oraclemodel~i̧teChenCotlerHuangLi2023NISQ and locate the source of thequantum--classical separation. On anyNP-hard kernel-admissible promise family, no polynomial-time classicalsampler can reproduce the inverse-polynomial optimal overlap of NP-HQunless(NPsubseteqBPP),even when granted the same classical repair and perfect access to theconstraint structure. The separation therefore lies in generating thesampling distribution, not in classical processingFinally, we introduce Heavy-Hitter QAOA (HH-QAOA), a geometry-informed filtering refinement that preserves theseconditional guarantees while reducing the retained candidate set from(O(nk⁺¹)) to (O(n^k)) and the classicalpost-processing cost by one power of (n). We demonstrate the completepipeline on 127-qubit IBM Eagle-r3 processors using textscQOptlib~i̧teOsaba2024Qoptlibtravelling-salesman instances with up to 100 logical variables,matching or improving the published reference tours in every testedcase.

articles.title: Observation of gapped Dirac magnons in a Co bilayer grown on Ru(0001)
articles.abstract: Author(s): Khalil Zakeri, Arthur Ernst, and Christopher Hins Long celebrated in graphene, Dirac physics inspires the search for similar phenomena in magnonic systems. Here, the authors experimentally demonstrate that magnons in an epitaxial Co bilayer on Ru(0001) exhibit Dirac properties near the Brillouin zone corner. Remarkably, the substrate does not destroy the essential physics; despite breaking sublattice symmetry and opening a gap, local valley topology remains intact. Beyond opening possibilities for discovering Dirac magnons in other ultrathin 3 d magnetic films, these findings hold promise for on-chip magnonic applications. [Phys. Rev. articles.title: Phonon evidence for a partial, re-entrant spin reorientation near room temperature in LaFe₁₋ₓNiₓO₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin reorientation near room temperature offers a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order, yet LaFeO3, which lacks a magnetic rare-earth ion, is generally expected to retain its spin orientation along the a axis below Tmathrm Napprox740~K. Here, we investigate LaFe₁₋ₓNiₓO₃ (x=0 and 0.1) using temperature-dependent magnetization and Raman spectroscopy over 200--400~K. Both compositions exhibit magnetic anomalies at 285.6 and 323~K, respectively, accompanied by correlated deviations of 12 Raman modes from their conventional anharmonic behavior. Principal component analysis and a global fitting approach reveal a common temperature-dependent phonon response, with mode-dependent amplitudes and signs. To interpret these anomalies, we develop a Landau-based spin-phonon coupling model describing complete, partial re-entrant, and incipient spin reorientation. Comparison with the experimental Raman profiles favors a partial, re-entrant rotation of the N'eel vector in both compositions, centered near 290~K. Ni substitution narrows the characteristic reorientation interval from approximately 116 to 84~K and enhances the magnetization anomaly by a factor of four. An additional feature near 262~K in LaFeO₃ is consistent with the Morin transition of trace α-Fe₂O₃. These findings suggest that partial spin reorientation can emerge without magnetic rare-earth ions and establish collective Raman phonon anomalies as a sensitive indirect probe of magnetic anisotropy changes in orthoferrites.

articles.title: Altermagnetism in Folded Iron Chain Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnetism, a moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting, has so far been realized primarily in Néel-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron-chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g., p̆arrow p̆arrow downarrow downarrow). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) case, altermagnetism is forbidden by the [C₂||a̧l T] symmetry, but it can emerge when such chains are stacked into a quasi-1D array. To generate altermagnetic spin splitting via this chain-stacking mechanism, two essential ingredients are required: a block-type spin order that spontaneously breaks the combined parity-time reversal symmetry, and finite inter-chain hopping. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the K₃Fe₂Se₄ family as a promising platform that realizes this mechanism, hosting a d-wave altermagnet even without lattice C₄ symmetry. Moreover, owing to its lower symmetry, the block-type folded chain exhibits an isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting, which may manifest as an altermagnetic wrapping effect. Our findings unify real-space block magnetism and reciprocal-space altermagnetism, establishing folded iron chains as a tunable platform for zero-moment spintronic applications.
authors: Ling-Fang Lin, Yang Zhang, Satoshi Okamoto, Adriana Moreo, Lun-Hui Hu, Elbio Dagotto

articles.title: Thermoelectric properties and modulation doping of ultrawide-bandgap nitride monolayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional III-nitride alloys provide a composition-tunable platform for exploring thermoelectric transport and intrinsic electric-field tolerance. We combine first-principles electronic-structure calculations with semiclassical transport for ordered monolayer BₓAl₁₋ₓN and BₓGa₁₋ₓN. State-dependent momentum relaxation times computed with AMSET include acoustic deformation-potential and piezoelectric scattering. Using a common, temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity of 550 W/mK, we predict maximum thermoelectric figure of merit ZT>2.5 for selected p- and n-type monolayers and ZT>2 at 300~K for n-type B₀.₂₅Ga₀.₇₅N. Composition-dependent band curvature, screening, and scattering help interpret the different p- and n-type responses. Vacuum-referenced band alignments identify candidate modulation-doping partners for both carrier types; explicit hGaN/V₂O₅ calculations yield a hole surface density of approximately 1.6×10¹⁴ cm⁻². A separate phenomenological model using the band gap and maximum phonon frequency predicts intrinsic breakdown fields of 20.06 and 20.74 MVcm for the Al- and Ga-containing x=0.75 alloys, respectively. These results motivate further investigation for thermoelectric and high-field power-electronic applications. The ZT values apply to the specified scattering and lattice-conductivity models, while the breakdown estimates require validation for monolayers and do not resolve field direction.

articles.title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO₃ and BaTiO₃₎, halide perovskites (CsPbBr₃, CsSnBr₃, and CsGeBr₃₎ and double halide perovskites (Cs₂AgAlBr₆ and Cs₂AgBiBr₆₎. By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.
authors: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor

articles.title: Optical signatures of Rashba--Dresselhaus coupling across Franz--Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. In crossed fields, the in-plane electric field generates an effective spin-orbit drift field that modifies the Landau spectrum and spinor states, while at zero magnetic field the problem maps onto Landau--Zener spin dynamics.At zero external fields, the total joint density of states above the band gap remains unchanged, while characteristic subgap structures appear. Pure Rashba coupling produces an inverse square root singularity, whereas a finite Dresselhaus term gives a step and a logarithmic peak, allowing the two couplings to be distinguished optically. At zero magnetic field, the Franz--Keldysh response shows a crossover from diabatic to adiabatic spin dynamics as the electric field is reduced. In the weak-field Rashba regime, the field-free singularity becomes a finite peak whose height scales as mathcal E⁻¹/³ and whose position approaches E_g-Eₘ̊ SO, providing a direct measure of the Rashba energy. In a perpendicular magnetic field, spin-orbit coupling shifts and splits the Landau absorption lines and produces anticrossings without changing their total weights. The Rashba splitting changes from a sqrtB dependence at weak fields to a linear dependence at strong fields. Finally, in crossed electric and magnetic fields, the electric field broadens the Landau lines and drives a continuous crossover toward the Franz--Keldysh regime, while spin-orbit coupling produces opposite shifts and different widths for the two members of each doublet.
authors: Bahruz Suleymanli, Samir Tariverdiev, B. Tanatar

articles.title: Heat current and noise in a point-like junction between normal metal and fractional quantum hall edge state with ν = 1/3
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we investigate heat current correlations between two edge states coupled through a constriction in the fractional quantum Hall regime at filling factor ν = 1/3. This configuration allows us to map the system onto an interacting Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid with a local impurity, where the interaction parameter takes the value κ = 1/2. This specific parameter value enables the application of the refermionization method. By solving the refermionized Hamiltonian, we compute the heat current and evaluate the finite-frequency heat auto- and cross-correlation functions. Our results reveal asymmetric behavior with frequency, corresponding to absorption and emission noise, respectively. Furthermore, we examine several limiting cases, including low- and high-temperature limits as well as strong- and weak-backscattering regimes. In the weak backscattering regime, the Lorenz number approaches 4L₀ at high voltage, suggesting a rescaling of the Wiedemann-Franz law due to interactions. A detailed study of the heat current fluctuations has made it possible to identify and derive expressions for the dominant contribution in the various regimes of interest, and to reveal the predominance of partition noise.
authors: Redouane Zamoum, Houssam Eddine Farhi, Abdellah Touati, Adeline Crépieux

articles.title: Visualization of Single Spin-chain Propagation using Bragg Coherent Diffraction Imaging
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain wall dynamics and their manipulation in finite-size systems serve as a promising platform for beyond Moore's law applications. Yet, the imaging techniques to track their motion in real-space and time are limited. Here, we use magnetic domain walls formed in permalloy artificial square lattice to demonstrate that single-shot Bragg coherent diffraction imaging (BCDI) is a powerful approach for this purpose. Our BCDI reconstructed images revealed milliseconds time-scale dynamics of the antiphase magnetic domain walls traveling through an antiferromagnetically ordered sample.
authors: Xiaoqian M. Chen, Justin S. Woods, Ulrich Welp, Wai-kwong Kwok, Ralu Divan, David A. Czaplewski, Scott Dhuey, Sujoy Roy, Rajesh V. Chopdekar, Lance E. De Long, Andi Barbour, Claudio Mazzoli, Ian Robinson, J. Todd Hastings

articles.title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. We leverage a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model to analyze polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) from molecular thin films. This new analysis establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states as a function of depth with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit via locking energy and polarization through the optical model. From our analysis, we discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from the interface, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics and contradicting hypotheses of substrate patterning. This nondestructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final state opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.
authors: Harlan Heilman, Em Biegler, Sushil Adhikari, Victor Murcia, Tanner Melody, Fred Woodall, Lars Thomsen, Obaid Alqahtani, Brian A. Collins

articles.title: Dipole chains of Bloch point singularities revealed by X-ray magnetic tomography
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bloch point singularities play an important role in magnetic systems, mediating changes in topology in three dimensional configurations. However, until now they have only been observed as isolated objects or as part of individual topological textures. Here we present the experimental observation of a 1D dipole chain of Bloch points in an anisotropic chiral magnet using soft X-ray magnetic vector tomography. We identify that the chain of Bloch point singularities lies along a boundary between regions of opposite chirality and that neighbouring Bloch and anti-Bloch points are stable at separations down to 60 nm. The stability of the Bloch points is determined to be closely related to the surrounding topology of the magnetisation configuration and a threshold separation for the spontaneous annihilation of Bloch point-anti-Bloch point pairs within chiral domain walls is identified to be approximately 90 nm in distance. This observation of a chain of Bloch points and the insight into their stability, offers a route to explore the correlative behaviour of such topological point defects. The behaviour and control of such point defects is of relevance for the control of 3D magnetisation configurations, and provides a new route towards the creation of correlated configurations of singularities in a magnetic system.
authors: Jeffrey Neethirajan, Rikako Yamamoto, Marisel Di Pietro Martínez, Luke A. Turnbull, Praveen Vir, Chandra Shekar, Claudia Felser, Luis Carlos Colocho Hurtarte, Benedikt J. Daurer, Majid Kazemian, Burkhard Kaulich, Claire Donnelly

articles.title: Spatiotemporally-resolved differential dynamic microscopy reveals strain-induced deformations in heterogeneous soft materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the microscopic behavior of materials in response to mechanical perturbations is a central challenge in soft matter, yet existing methods, which typically rely on microscopy-based imaging, often struggle with spatial heterogeneity and low signal-to-noise that are characteristic of many soft and biological materials. Additionally, many existing rheo-optical methods focus on the response to macro-scale forces rather than localized perturbations despite the importance of local stresses in biological and industrial applications of soft materials. Here, we present STroboscopically Averaged, time-Resolved Differential Dynamic Microscopy (starDDM) to investigate a sample's deformation across time and distance due to a cyclically applied local force. As proof-of-principle, we use this model-independent and tracer-free approach to map the motions of active cytoskeleton composites imposed by the movement of an optically trapped probe particle embedded within the complex network. We reveal how motor-driven restructuring and varying strain rates tune the magnitude and propagation of the response, which we further show decays with distance from the perturbation. This analytical platform fills a critical gap in micro-rheology, offering a versatile tool for probing the non-equilibrium dynamics of soft materials ranging from biopolymer networks to 3D-printed materials and soft robotics.
authors: Aysan Razzaghi, Mehrzad Sasanpour, Jasmine Ren, Caidric Gupit, Matthew E. Helgeson, Megan T. Valentine, Rae M. Robertson-Anderson, Ryan McGorty

articles.title: Boundary shape controls the stress distribution in two-component elastic materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how the shape and arrangement of high-stiffness regions govern stress redistribution in two-component triangular elastic spring networks subjected to spatially correlated and uncorrelated random prestress. We compare boundary roughness, partitioning into disconnected regions, and graded transitions between regions of different stiffness. Our simulations identify interface bonds as channels for energy transfer: increasing their number provides additional transfer paths and reduces stress concentration in mechanically rigid regimes, while offering little benefit in compliant subnetworks. This is analogous to defects in naturally occurring crystal structures, where the defects themselves isolate stress. At a fixed fraction of high-stiffness material, partitioning reduces stress concentration for both correlated and uncorrelated prestress. The benefit diminishes with further subdivision as the number of interface bonds becomes comparable to the number of interior nodes. Stress reduction, however, depends on the spatial correlations of the imposed prestress: random prestress generally yields a stronger effect, though the difference diminishes in some regimes. Graded interfaces further reduce peak stress by distributing the stiffness transition over a broader region. Together, these results suggest design strategies based on increasing interface area, matching subdivision scale to prestress correlations, and grading stiffness transitions. This minimal framework identifies how internal structure controls energy transfer and stress redistribution, suggesting design principles for mechanical robustness under both internal and external loading.
authors: Kyungeun Kim, Adam Clare, Miranda Holmes-Cerfon

articles.title: Zeeman Shift and Injection Currents under Light Irradiation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The conversion of light into electrical currents enables energy harvesting and photodetection. Conventional second-order dc photocurrents are driven by the electric component of light through electric-dipole coupling and require broken inversion symmetry. Here, we show that the electric and magnetic components of light jointly generate Zeeman shift and injection currents. Using quantum perturbation theory, we derive explicit microscopic expressions for their conductivity tensors. We systematically classify the symmetry constraints on these responses and show how they differ from those governing conventional photocurrents. In particular, both responses can occur in centrosymmetric systems with spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order, irrespective of time-reversal symmetry. A centrosymmetric kagome model exhibits broadband responses. First-principles calculations for Mn₃Sn further predict Zeeman injection and shift current densities of 10²-10³~mathrmA/m² and 1-10~mathrmA/m², respectively, under illumination with an electric-field amplitude E=10⁴~V/m. These magnitudes place both currents within experimental reach.
authors: Ruizhi Dong, Yihua Xiao, Pengfei Wang, Ruixiang Fei

articles.title: Compass Correlations in a Square-Lattice Magnet
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The square-lattice compass model is a paradigm of bond-dependent frustration, yet experimental evidence for its characteristic spin correlations has remained elusive. Here we identify compass correlations in the square-lattice intermetallic ErRu₂Si₂ using single-crystal neutron diffuse scattering. Comparative measurements on the isostructural compounds NdRu₂Si₂ and ErRu₂Si₂ reveal a pronounced contrast between nearly uniform diffuse rings in the former and strong intensity modulation between Brillouin zones in the latter. Through the magnetic neutron polarization factor, this modulation reveals compass correlations that couple moment orientation to the correlation wavevector. Crystal-field spectroscopy identifies four preferred in-plane orientations for the Er³⁺ moments. A minimal compass-Heisenberg model incorporating this anisotropy quantitatively reproduces the diffuse scattering and accounts for the double-Q vortex-antivortex ground state. Fits with the compass couplings fixed at values set by the dipolar energy scale retain good agreement with the data, supporting a substantial dipolar contribution to the bond-dependent interactions. Our results establish a square-lattice platform for compass physics and suggest that dipolar interactions, acting together with local crystal-field anisotropy, can shape directional magnetic correlations alongside conduction-electron-mediated exchange.
authors: Otkur Omar, Matthias D. Frontzek, Gabriele Sala, Junying Shen, Xinmin Wang, Ze Hu, Zhuang Xu, Zecong Qin, Xin Tong, Joe Paddison, Max Hirschberger, Shinichiro Seki, Masaaki Matsuda, Matthew B. Stone, Andrew D. Christianson, Nguyen D. Khanh, Shang Gao

articles.title: Intrinsic Paramagnetism of Optical Phonons and Thermal Hall Effect in Quantum Paraelectrics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a microscopic theory of the phonon-mediated thermal Hall effect in quantum paraelectrics, driven by the intrinsic paramagnetism due to quantum fluctuations of the (nearly) critical optical phonon modes. The effective magnetization due to temporal fluctuations of the assosciated dipoles couple to an external magnetic field resulting the magnetoelectric term H ḑot (P × dotP) in the effective Lagrangian density of the polarisation field P. This coupling splits the transverse optical phonon spectrum into right- and left-circularly polarized chiral branches. Using the chiral phonon Green's functions and the Kubo formalism, we derive the thermal Hall conductivity κₓy from the heat-current correlation function. We observe that κₓy is proportional to the difference in spectral weights of the two chiral modes, κₓy propto A₊² - A₋², establishing a direct microscopic link between phonon chirality and transverse heat transport. Our theory predicts three key observations: (i) a linear-in-magnetic-field response κₓy propto H at low fields, evolving into nonlinear behavior at higher fields (ii) a non-monotonic temperature dependence of κₓy with a peak arising from the competition between thermal population and phonon scattering and (iii) strong enhancement of κₓy near the quantum critical point ømega₀ → 0, it exhibits power-law scaling κₓy propto Tα with α approx 0.41. Our findings provide an understanding of thermal Hall transport in quantum paraelectrics due to intrinsic paramagnetism and is aligned with the observed behaviour in SrTiO₃ and related materials.
authors: Harsh Jain, Manideep Gone, Nabyendu Das

articles.title: Interface Control of Second-Harmonic Generation in Layered CuInP2S6 via PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 Domain Wall
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The control of nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale offers opportunities for developing two-dimensional integrated nanophotonics with programmable functionalities. In this work, we report the first realization of nanoscale nonvolatile control of the amplitude and polarization of second-harmonic generation (SHG) response in layered CuInP2S6 (CIPS) via the domain structure in an interfacial PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 (PZT) thin film. The SHG intensity at CIPS/PZT heterointerface is continuously modulated, either substantially enhanced or almost entirely quenched, by the circular domain walls in underlying ferroelectric oxide. The interfacial coupling of CIPS polar axis with in-plane polarization of PZT domain walls tailors the SHG light polarization into two-fold (C2V) symmetry, which is well modeled by nonlinear electromagnetic theory. Overall, this study enables nonvolatile programmable design of nonlinear light intensity and polarization in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale.
authors: Dawei Li, Juhe Liu, Yifei Hao, Qiuchen Wu, Xi Huang, Jesse Stebbing, Xinyi Hou, Gaolei Zhao, Kun Wang, Yongfeng Lu, Xia Hong

articles.title: Intrinsic Raman Modes and Crystal Symmetry of Altermagnetic α-MnTe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor α-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. Here we combine high-resolution Raman and second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to distinguish intrinsic lattice excitations from Te-derived spectral contributions and to examine bulk inversion symmetry of α-MnTe. We show that several prominent Raman features previously assigned to α-MnTe instead originate from segregated Te clusters or precipitates. The remaining intrinsic Raman response consists of a single Raman-active mode assigned to the calculated E₂g phonon, consistent with the centrosymmetric D₆ₕ symmetry. The SHG response agrees with surface electric-dipole and bulk electric-quadrupole contributions expected for a centrosymmetric D₆ₕ crystal, supporting the preservation of bulk inversion symmetry in α-MnTe. Our findings revise the Raman assignments in α-MnTe and provide a basis for interpreting its altermagnetic properties within the appropriate crystal-symmetry framework.
authors: Yunpeng Cui, Shuai Zhang, Jia-Liang Xie, Jinxuan Liang, Hao Lin, Miao Qin, Jiawei Shao, Gongling Chen, Yidian Li, Yixuan Luo, Deng Hu, Bingru Lu, Hao Li, Xiang Li, Tiantian Liu, Haodong Yu, Hongyun Zhang, Shuyun Zhou, Zhiwei Wang, Yanfeng Guo, Tiantian Zhang, Miao-Ling Lin, Ping-Heng Tan, Feng Jin, Luyi Yang

articles.title: Triplon dynamics from partial Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The partially disordered (PD) phase, in which magnetically ordered and Kondo-screened sites coexist, has been proposed as a possible ground state of geometrically frustrated heavy-fermion systems. We investigate its dynamical properties in the half-filled periodic Anderson model on a triangular lattice by calculating the dynamical spin susceptibility within the random-phase approximation built on a self-consistent Hartree-Fock solution. We show that successive quantum phase transitions from the Kondo-insulating phase to the PD phase and to a magnetically ordered phase are driven by the condensation of triplon modes originating predominantly from the Kondo-screened sites. In the PD phase, magnons and triplons coexist and hybridize, leading to characteristic level repulsion in the excitation spectrum. These results reveal how triplet excitations evolve into collective magnetic modes across the successive phase transitions and highlight the dynamical interplay between magnetic order and Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems.
authors: Hiroki Nakahara, Masahito Mochizuki, Rintaro Eto

articles.title: Low-Temperature Hybrid Monte Carlo for Perylene and Corannulene: Stabilizing Determinant and Force
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a real world physics study of the molecules perylene and corannulene at different doping levels, and calculating selected one-, two- (exciton) and three-body (trion) correlators. This has been done by performing Hubbard-model simulations near room temperature. We find, between charge neutral and doubly charged plateaus of perylene, an interaction-induced Δ Q = 1 plateau whose width grows with interaction strength and in which the ground state is a spin doublet rather than a singlet. The algorithmic advancement enabling this study simultaneously stabilizes the determinant and force calculations to machine precision at room temperature, while scaling as well as standard determinant Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of these systems. Furthermore, our formalism retains the full time-displaced (2-point) Green's function, allowing us to construct any n-body correlator, including those that contain disconnected diagrams.
authors: Petar Sinilkov, Thomas Luu, Johann Ostmeyer, Finn L. Temmen, Marcel Rodekamp

articles.title: Quantum Landau Lifshitz Gilbert equation in ferromagnetic conductors and magnetic insulators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the microscopic origin of magnetic damping is essential for describing magnetization dynamics in nanoscale magnetic systems. In this work, we develop a microscopic framework to derive Gilbert damping terms from specific interactions in ferromagnetic conductors and magnetic insulators. In ferromagnetic conductors, magnetic damping is dominated by the s d exchange interaction between the localized magnetic moments and the itinerant electrons, which is effectively equivalent to an electronmagnon interaction. From the spin diffusion equation and the spin transfer torque therein, we obtain the corresponding quantum LLG equation. In magnetic insulators, where free electrons are absent, spin phonon interactions become the primary source of the damping.Starting from an effective spin phonon interaction and using linear response theory, we derive a quantum LLG equation with a Gilbert damping tensor analytically. Our results demonstrate that different microscopic interactions lead to qualitatively different structures of magnetic damping. Instead of being described by a universal scalar parameter, Gilbert damping can exhibit spatial dependence and tensorial characteristics determined by the underlying microscopic interactions.
authors: Ji Yang Zhu, Zheng Chuan Wang

articles.title: Electron Wavefronts Capture Nanoscale Movies of Hypersound at Surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acoustic waves transport mechanical energy and elastic strain through solids, with material composition and shape governing their propagation. In the gigahertz hypersound regime, acoustic wavelengths reach tens to hundreds of nanometres, comparable to nanoscale device dimensions. Harnessing these waves underpins high-frequency signal processing, sensing, electromagnetic coupling and quantum control. Acoustic metrology probes elastic modes and internal interfaces. Yet directly imaging how nanoscale acoustic waves interact with local structure remains challenging, requiring picometre displacement sensitivity combined with high spatiotemporal resolution. Here we demonstrate full-field imaging of laser-induced hypersound at surfaces using reflected electron wavefronts.
