Yet prevailing formulations neither guarantee that small PDE-residual losses imply small solution errors nor scale effectively with increasing problem size. Here we present the neural basis method (NBM) as a new approach for Navier--Stokes dynamics. NBM is built on a ``representation-then-projection'' principle: fixed neural bases define the representation space, while projection of the governing equations determines the expansion coefficients. The same bases define common coordinates for the parametric solution manifold, recasting operator learning as a parameter-to-coefficient mapping and enabling scalability by removing explicit spatial dependence. For incompressible flow, NBM yields a velocity-only formulation whose residual provides an a posteriori velocity-error estimate, establishing a certified, data-free training objective for coefficient learning. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, generalization, and scalability of NBM, with substantial improvements over baselines.
authors: Yuhe Wang, Zhu Wang, Min Wang

articles.title: CoPiT: A conditional Position-induced Transformer for aerodynamic field prediction on unstructured meshes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) simulations remain a standard tool for aerodynamic analysis, yet each solve on an unstructured mesh is computationally expensive, making many-query tasks such as design exploration, optimization, and multi-condition evaluation costly. Neural operators provide mesh-flexible surrogates for mapping geometry and operating conditions to flow fields; however, in many existing architectures, global parameters such as the freestream state and design variables are concatenated with pointwise inputs, leaving their influence on intermediate features implicit. This paper proposes CoPiT, a Conditional Position-induced Transformer that builds on the Position-induced Transformer (PiT) as its geometric backbone and injects a global condition vector through multi-stage feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), thereby making parametric modulation explicit while preserving geometry-based attention weights. The model is evaluated on two-dimensional AirfRANS airfoil fields, including scarce-data and extrapolation regimes, and on three-dimensional BlendedNet++ blended-wing-body surfaces. On the AirfRANS full-data test set, CoPiT reduces surface and volume losses by approximately 54% and 24% relative to Transolver, respectively, and achieves the lowest overall normalized test MSE among the compared baselines on BlendedNet++. Matched ablations show that FiLM conditioning generally improves upon input concatenation, while the preferred placement is task-dependent. CoPiT thus provides a practical operator-learning surrogate for parametric aerodynamics on unstructured meshes.
authors: Junfeng Chen, Yongchen Fan, Zhonghua Qiao, Kailiang Wu

articles.title: PULSES: multi-agent AI for autonomous excited-state model building and dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating molecular excited-state processes requires resolving electronic and nuclear dynamics, but the cost of direct quantum-chemical calculations limits accessible system sizes and timescales. Machine-learning models can extend these simulations, yet they often need to be tailored to specific molecular systems and scientific objectives. Building and deploying such models requires coordinated decisions across conformational sampling, quantum-chemical labelling, model training, validation and dynamics. Here we introduce Paired agents for Unified Learning and Simulation of Excited States (PULSES), a multi-agent system that automates this workflow within expert-approved boundaries. A human expert and planner define the scientific objective, methods and decision boundaries, while an orchestrator coordinates domain agents and artifact-specific scientific assurance during execution. We evaluate PULSES on 15 computational chemistry tasks and demonstrate end-to-end applications to perylene exciton Hamiltonians, solvent-dependent biphenyl relaxation, and excited-state proton transfer in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline. These results demonstrate traceable, expert-bounded construction and deployment of specialized excited-state models, while retaining scientific validation as a requirement rather than assuming that successful execution establishes correctness.
authors: Fangning Ren, Lechen Dong, Xu Chen, Weilin Zou, Bushra Alam, Fang Liu

articles.title: Perfectly aperiodic asymmetric scalable metasurface based on the hat monotile
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurfaces are conventionally designed on periodic lattices, which renders their electromagnetic response spatially uniform and leaves the spatial arrangement itself unused as an information-bearing design resource. In this study, we propose and numerically validate a metasurface built on an aperiodic monotile: the recently discovered "hat" polykite, a single tile mathematically guaranteed to tile the plane only nonperiodically. The twelve distinguishable orientations of the hat serve as a natural design basis; each carries resonant elements tuned to one of twelve absorption frequencies between 4.600 and 4.914 GHz, transcribing the provable aperiodicity and mirror asymmetry of the geometry into the electromagnetic response. Gaussian-beam scanning over a compositionally unique 6 times 6 grid yields irregular, position-dependent electromagnetic signatures whose pairwise separations reach beyond 6 dB. In particular, coherence-guided selection of multiple frequencies increases the stable rank of the position-signature matrix from 1.0 to approximately 1.6 with three frequency components, whereas the accumulation of mutually similar electromagnetic features fails to add effective dimensions, demonstrating that properly selected multifrequency characteristics enhance the spatial distinguishability embedded in the surface. A shift-correlation analysis in which the cosine similarity never exceeds 0.5 confirms that the response inherits the absence of translational order from the tiling. Compatible with standard printed-circuit fabrication, the aperiodic metasurface design establishes a deterministic route toward position-identifiable electromagnetic environments for localization, chipless identification, and integrated sensing and communication.

articles.title: From Hollow Waveguides to Mie Voids: Low-Index Light Confinement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The confinement of light within optically thin media challenges the conventional view that optical localization requires high-index dielectric materials and total internal reflection. Over the past decades, a broad range of photonic phenomena has demonstrated that electromagnetic energy can also be guided and localized inside low-index regions or nanoscale void cavities. What first appears to be a curiosity is, in fact, highly relevant: The interaction between light and matter lies at the heart of much in optics and photonics. It enables sensing, nonlinear optical phenomena, and optical manipulation, yet it also inevitably introduces absorption, dissipation, and loss. Pushing localized, enhanced, or guided energy into a lower-index space thus offers entirely new possibilities for light-matter interaction and dispersion control. In this review, we discuss some of these counterintuitive structures, starting with light guidance within optically thin media, such as hollow-core photonic crystal fibers or antiresonant reflecting optical waveguides. We then discuss the optics of bubbles, that is, low-index inclusions in a higher-index surrounding, and ultimately arrive at the so-called Mie void resonators, optical resonators that support localized electromagnetic modes confined within a region of lower refractive index. All these systems demonstrate that there are (resonant) optics beyond simple total internal reflection. Absence can itself become a functional photonic degree of freedom, opening opportunities across sensing, quantum nanophotonics, metasurfaces, and programmable optical matter.
authors: Dominik Ludescher, Ivan Toftul, Harald Giessen, Yuri Kivshar, Mario Hentschel

articles.title: Development of an Analog Front-End Using NINO ASIC for Mini-ICAL
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The mini-ICAL was supposed to be a pre-prototype detector of the Iron CALorimeter (ICAL) of the India-based Neutrino Observatory (INO) project. Resistive Plate Chamber (RPC) was the active element of these detectors. As this detector operates in avalanche mode, one needs a very fast pre-amplifier for signal processing. NINO ASIC developed for the ALICE time-of-flight detector was a potential chip to be used as the analog-front end. This paper presents an 8-in-1 pre-amplifier board developed using the NINO ASIC, a single-ended to differential signal conversion using the differential driver chip manufactured by Texas Instruments, production of the boards, lessons learned during production, testing of these boards, and interface with RPCs. Finally, its performance based on strip rates and efficiency of the detector will also be discussed.
authors: Ravindra R Shinde, Punnet Kanwar Kaur, Gobinda Majumder, S Pethuraj, K C Ravindran, Mandar Saraf, B Satyanarayana

articles.title: Low-variance force estimators for nuclear quantum mean forces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum equilibrium structure can be sampled using classical molecular dynamics with a learned effective potential for a single path-integral replica, but the primitive mean-force estimates obtained from path-integral molecular dynamics with that replica held fixed are noisy. We derive a scaled-gradient estimator with zero sampling variance for a one-dimensional harmonic oscillator and an estimated 4.7--57.5-fold reduction in constrained-sampling time for the molecular tests. The resulting potentials can be trained on these forces like standard machine-learning interatomic potentials and yield stable production simulations from which quantum expectation values of position-dependent observables are obtained as classical ensemble averages.

articles.title: A Compact Single-Beam Optically Pumped Magnetometer Based on Absorption Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. The residual magnetic field is actively minimized to below 400 pT through a combination of mu-metal magnetic shielding and internal compensation coils. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz¹/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm³. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. Two coil configurations patterned directly on the FPCB were investigated. Under optimized operating conditions, the OPM prototype achieved a sensitivity of 66 fT/Hz¹/2. These results demonstrate that high-buffer-pressure single-beam OPMs can achieve excellent sensitivity, establishing a pathway toward compact and scalable arrays.
authors: Jia-You Liou, Yi-Hsuan Chen, Hsiang-An Chuang, Chih-Hsuan Huang, Zong-Hsin Liu, I-Chiao Tsai, Kai-Hsin Peng, Yi-Hsin Chen

articles.title: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In distributed quantum computing, quantum networks provide a potential infrastructure for long-range quantum information processing. Controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) is a key practically relevant protocol that can connect two parties on a network and enables a third party, the controller to allow or abort the secure teleportation of an arbitrary single-qubit state between the two parties. We investigate the robustness of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise. Using the Kraus-operator formalism, we characterize the noisy resource through multipartite quantum discord, genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity. We also outline a proof-of-concept photonic implementation for preparing the three-qubit GHZ resource and realizing the CQT protocol, which could enable experimental investigation of the effects of noise. Our results show that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise generally preserve useful mutipartite quantum correlations over broader noise parameter ranges. Interestingly, multipartite discord exhibits freezing under bit-flip noise over a finite parameter regime. Moreover, discord can persist beyond the sudden death of genuine multipartite entanglement, revealing the distinct robustness of nonclassical correlations. We further demonstrate that CQT fidelity which characterizes the performance of CQT can exceed the classical threshold even after GMC vanishes, while LE more closely reflects the operational usefulness of the noisy resource. These findings highlight the complementary roles of quantum correlations and entanglement in assessing the resilience of GHZ-based protocols.
authors: S. Archana, Aditi Das, Venkat Abhignan, R. Muthuganesan

articles.title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32840v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular clouds exhibit complex, multi-scale dynamics driven by the interplay of turbulence, self-gravity, and gas pressure. Modelling these systems with conventional grid-based methods becomes increasingly expensive as spatial resolution and dimensionality increase. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free alternative by incorporating the governing equations directly into the training objective, but their ability to model realistic turbulent self-gravitating flows remains largely unexplored. We apply PINNs to isothermal molecular clouds initialized with astrophysically motivated turbulent velocity fields, considering subsonic and supersonic evolution in two and three dimensions. We benchmark the predicted density and velocity fields against the finite-volume code Athena++. PINNs accurately recover the global evolution of the flow over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities. Their training cost also exhibits weak dependence on spatial resolution, increasing by less than 25% from 128³ to 1024³ in our experiments. These results demonstrate that PINNs can model substantially more realistic self-gravitating turbulent flows than previously explored and provide a promising complementary framework for studying these systems.
authors: Tirthankar De, Sayantan Auddy, Ramit Dey, Shantanu Basu

articles.title: Deterministic Ground-State Search in a Spatial Photonic Ising Machine by Phase Retrieval
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.16474v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A spatial photonic Ising machine (SPIM) solves large-scale combinatorial optimization problems by computing the Ising Hamiltonian through an optical Fourier transform. However, the ground-state search relies on annealing, in which spins are optimized stochastically and sequentially. We propose a ground-state search based on phase retrieval (PR), in which all spins are updated simultaneously and deterministically. Imposing an amplitude constraint in the Fourier plane guides the modulated phase distribution, which encodes the spin configuration, toward the optimal solution. We numerically demonstrate that the proposed scheme reaches the ground state of rank-one Ising Hamiltonians with 10⁴ spins in a single iteration for all trials. Moreover, a radial rearrangement of the amplitudes and an appropriately designed target pattern alleviate search stagnation and improve the optimization of spin configurations. The collective and deterministic spin update by phase retrieval enables a fast ground-state search for large-scale combinatorial optimization.
authors: Suguru Shimomura, Jun Tanida, Yusuke Ogura

articles.title: Adding slow magnetoacoustic mode to the HLL-type multi-state approximate Riemann solution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.17049v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-state HLL-type approximate Riemann solutions of ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) typically assume that the medium within the Riemann fan is incompressible, and thus the slow magnetoacoustic mode cannot be included in their space-time wave configurations for the intermediate states. We propose a new strategy to design multi-state HLL-type solutions, allowing for the medium within the Riemann fan to be compressible. In particular, for the complete seven-wave configuration of the MHD Riemann problem, we estimate the slow magnetoacoustic speeds and a longitudinal flow speed between the slow modes, whose compressibility is estimated based on the relations between fast, Alfvén, and slow speeds. Then, following the conservation laws and Rankine-Hugoniot jump relations across the fast, Alfvén, and slow waves, we calculate all the intermediate states within the Riemann fan. Moreover, we discuss the solutions when certain wave modes degenerate, ensuring well-posedness and smooth transitions between complete and degenerate wave configurations. Numerical simulations using a Finite Volume solver show that the proposed approximate Riemann solution is less diffusive than the classic HLLD scheme, particularly for slow mode waves. For example, in a 1D test case with a strong longitudinal magnetic field, the new scheme needs one order of magnitude fewer grid cells compared to the classic HLLD scheme to resolve all wave modes.
authors: Fan Zhang, Stefaan Poedts, Andrea Lani

articles.title: QubiC 2.0: An Extensible Open-Source Qubit Control System Capable of Mid-Circuit Measurement and Feed-Forward
articles.abstract: arXiv:2309.10333v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Researchers manipulate and measure quantum processing units via the classical electronics control system. We developed an open-source FPGA-based quantum bit control system called QubiC for superconducting qubits. After years of qubit calibration and testing experience on QubiC 1.0, we recognized the need for mid-circuit measurement and feed-forward capabilities to implement advanced quantum algorithms, and upgraded the system to QubiC 2.0 on an AMD ZCU216 RFSoC evaluation board with all these enriched features. The system uses portable FPGA gateware with a simplified processor to handle commands on-the-fly. For design simplicity and straightforward scaling, we adopted a multi-core distributed architecture, assigning one processor core per qubit. The pulses combine the unique pulse envelope and carrier information specified in a command. Each pulse envelope is pre-stored in the FPGA's block RAMs, ensuring speed and reusability throughout the quantum circuit, while pulse parameters including amplitude, phase, and frequency can be updated from pulse to pulse. The software stack is developed in Python, running on both the FPGA's ARM core and a host computer via XML-RPC. Quantum circuits can be described in a high-level language supporting both pulse-level and native-gate-level programming with high-level control flow constructs, and are compiled into binary commands loaded into the FPGA. With QubiC 2.0, we achieved multi-FPGA synchronization and low-latency data communication, and demonstrated feed-forward experiments on conditional circuits. The system also serves as a platform for artificial intelligence and machine learning driven quantum control, such as FPGA-based real-time quantum state discrimination. The enhanced QubiC system provides researchers with powerful tools to explore and implement advanced quantum algorithms and applications.
authors: Yilun Xu, Gang Huang, Neelay Fruitwala, Neel R. Vora, Abhi D. Rajagopala, Akel Hashim, Larry Chen, Noah Goss, Kasra Nowrouzi, Ravi K. Naik, Christopher Spitzer, David I. Santiago, Irfan Siddiqi

articles.title: Agents and Tokens: Multi-Agent Autonomous Reasoning over a Hydrodynamic Token Store
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.01102v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models and the agents built on them are the most capable reasoning machines ever built, and science is beginning to put them to work. Atmospheric and oceanic sciences are starting to see agentic integration, but coastal hydrodynamics remains largely untouched by AI. Simply, agents cannot easily read its data products without saturating their context windows. A time frame from a coastal model can hold hundreds of megabytes, and if the archive's chunking does not suit the query, the agent will spend more time downloading and compacting than gaining insights. After all, the archives were designed for storage, not for the fast, on-the-fly access agents need. Speech and music once hit the same wall. A minute of audio is millions of numbers, yet today's audio models hold conversations and write music. They "learned" to do this by "listening" to tokens. Neural audio codecs turn waveforms into short sequences of discrete symbols that a model reads like words and decodes back into sound. Coastal water is a similar signal: dense, finely sampled, and repeatable. We are convinced it has an analogous compact native representation that preserves the salient physics. Tokens are that representation: small integers, light enough for an agent to sweep six months of a coastline in seconds. Agents can then do more than simple lookup-related tasks; they can form and test their hypotheses as they explore the tokenized representation efficiently. Herein, we build this framework, using vector quantized variational autoencoders to compress tide level, the non-tidal residual, and surface wind speed into 16x16 grids of tokens along the US Atlantic and Gulf coasts. Agents traverse and explore these grids (e.g., tracking, spatiotemporal trend analysis) considerably faster than raw archives in both on-prem and off-prem modalities, while correctly answering several types of under-specified queries.
authors: Jinpai Zhao, Albert Cerrone, Joannes Westerink, Clint Dawson

articles.title: Cautious Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient Methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are indispensable tools for modeling complex phenomena in physics and engineering. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a powerful alternative to traditional numerical solvers by directly incorporating physical constraints into neural network loss functions. Despite their advantages, PINN training requires multi-objective optimization, which often leads to significant gradient conflicts among boundary, initial, and residual loss terms. The Conflict-Free Inverse Gradient (ConFIG) method addresses these conflicts; however, integrating ConFIG with adaptive optimizers such as Adam introduces a critical vulnerability: the conflict-free direction generated by ConFIG is further processed by the optimizer, and the resulting weight update may no longer be conflict-free with respect to the task gradients. To address this issue, Cautious ConFIG is proposed as a concise three-line extension to the ConFIG algorithm that empirically restores the conflict-freeness guarantee prior to the weight update. The method is evaluated on three PINN benchmarks: the 1D Viscous Burgers' equation, the 1D Nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and the 2D Kovasznay flow. Experimental results demonstrate consistent performance improvements over the standard ConFIG baseline. Additionally, the stabilizing effect of cautious masking and its reaction to conflict severity, task number, and optimizer lag are investigated using a simple toy system.
authors: Damian Hattler, Qiang Liu, Nils Thuerey

articles.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce TWIG (Tree-structured Weights with Inherited Gates), a representation in which every weight of a neural network is the end of a path of small discrete decisions: a sign, a shift by a power of two, a zero gate, an index into a shared table. Weights that belong together share the upper part of their paths, and each decision is inherited by every weight below it, so it is stored once and applied once. This simple change has three consequences. Any trained network can be written as a TWIG, and when the decisions are powers of two its weight layers become circuits made almost entirely of wires and adders, suited to chips whose weights are fixed at fabrication. Pruning, quantization, low-rank factorization, codebooks and weight sharing become edits of one object, so a single optimizer can choose among all of them for a whole network. And choosing the decisions is the ground-state problem of a higher-order Boltzmann machine whose interactions follow the paths of the tree, the problem class that annealers and quantum optimizers are built to solve. Today these questions are handled apart: each compression method brings its own format and solver, a circuit with fixed weights needs a dedicated constant multiplier for every weight, and discrete solvers reach only narrow subproblems such as rounding. Weight formats have long been moving toward shared decisions, through group scales, shared exponents, microexponents and sparse weights; TWIG takes this trend to its end, and every common format is a shallow TWIG at no extra cost. On five weight matrices of a large language model, a flat tree whose signed power-of-two terms are chosen per weight for circuit cost, with no group scales, needs 9--15% fewer additions than GPTQ at equal layer error at 3- and 4-bit accuracy on typical matrices, and 20--55% fewer on matrices with strong outliers.

articles.title: Earth embeddings are decomposable records of the land surface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ecological monitoring, carbon accounting and biodiversity assessment increasingly rely on annual Earth embeddings--learned vectors that compress a year of satellite observation for every ten-meter pixel on Earth, consumed in place of the imagery itself. What these vectors mean has not been established. Here we decompose two widely used embedding products and show that they contain individual ecological features, including fire, forest clearing and crop type, validated against independent reference data on events across six continents. The recovered concepts date abrupt canopy loss to the first post-disturbance growing season and resolve severity well enough to separate prescribed fire from wildfire. Small fires that recover quickly are detectable in one product but not the other, which instead separates crops more strongly.

articles.title: Recommender regret for improving regularised RL estimation with bandits and MCTS
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms rely on estimators, like Monte Carlo tree search or one-step look-ahead, to provide policy, value, or Q-value estimates in training and inference. However, existing bandit-based estimation frameworks evaluate sampling efficiency, not the quality of estimates. We address this by formalising estimate generation as a recommendation process, treating bandit-based sampling as an improvement operator. To evaluate the quality of a recommendation (estimate), we define regulariser-aware recommender regrets, analysing their lower bounds, and proving that simple algorithms like uniform sampling can achieve these bounds. Finally, we unify bandit- and search-based target improvement under recommender MCTS. Across synthetic trees, arcade games, and scientific discovery tasks, recommenders often yield faster target convergence and superior downstream performance. Our experiments characterise for the first time the potential of regularised MCTS in scientific applications.
authors: Danilo Vucetic, Alexandre Larouche, Mohammad Pedramfar, Audrey Durand, Gauthier Gidel

articles.title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-constrained machine learning (PCML) integrates domain knowledge, first-principles, and physical constraints into AI/ML models. In this work, we present a step-by-step tutorial of a modular PCML framework, KKT-HardNet, and illustrate how it could be used for hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization and model predictive control in a single platform. KKT-HardNet combines fast inference capabilities of neural networks with guaranteed satisfaction of algebraic constraints through differential projection. It can handle heterogeneous data and enforce both linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. The modular design supports custom neural-network backbones and user-defined projection mechanisms for PCML. To enable efficient end-to-end training, KKT-HardNet exploits implicit function theorem to backpropagate through the projection layer. This avoids computationally expensive automatic differentiation. This work also introduces an exact reduced-order Fischer-Burmeister reformulation and a primal-dual interior-point method as an alternative projection solve strategy. We also provide a diverse set of benchmarking problems for PCML in engineering applications. KKT-HardNet achieves orders of magnitude better performance in terms of both constraint satisfaction and inference time. The KKT-HardNet code and the benchmark datasets are available at https://github.com/souls-tamu/kkt-hardnet .
authors: Rahul Golder, Bimol Nath Roy, MM Faruque Hasan

articles.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized C. elegans nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.
authors: Aaditya Prasad, Steven W. Flavell, Brian DePasquale

articles.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.
authors: Xi Chen, Fengqi Hu, Zeyu Shen, Jiaying Xu, Shangding Gu, Pan Xu, Anqi Liu, Laixi Shi

articles.title: Autoregressive Physics-Informed Neural Operator Surrogates and Joint 4-D Seismic-Production Bayesian History Matching
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31677v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a surrogate-accelerated Bayesian history-matching framework, demonstrated on a realistic synthetic model (N=100,188 cells). The forward map G is replaced by a Fourier neural operator G_θ trained in a closed loop, hatxₙ₊₁=G_θ(u,hatxₙ₎, with the discrete black-oil residual R(xₙ₊₁,xₙ₎ as a physics-informed neural operator (PINO) penalty, truncated backpropagation and noise injection. We assimilate production data and 4-D seismic using adaptive regularised ensemble Kalman inversion (aREKI), and synthesise Δ Vₚ inside the rollout via a closed-form Gassmann transform of the surrogate, under a two-stage schedule (aREKI on production, then an ensemble smoother with multiple data assimilation, ES-MDA, on both). To temper the ill-posedness, we invert (łog K,φ) not in R²N, where Nₑłl 2N leaves a rank-deficient covariance and a null space the data never inform, but on a chart u=Ψ(tilde m), tilde minRd, dłl 2N, given by a Parseval-exact truncated cosine transform or a variational auto-encoder decoder. The ensemble then spans its own search space; the directions the data cannot constrain are cut to those the chart can express, and every member decodes to a geologically plausible field. For the rollout we prove an exposure bound W₁łesumⱼ L,ⁿ⁻¹⁻jEeⱼ, a physics-penalty contraction |DₓG_θ|łeα<1 under a small residual defect, and an O(h̊o^K) truncation bias. A Loewner-order inequality IₚpreceqIₚ₊Iₛ explains why joint assimilation is no less informative. On held-out data, G_θ attains R²>0.999 on pressure and saturation and rolls out in 0.579 s, a sim2500× speed-up, bringing an Nₑ₌₁₉₀₋ₘₑₘber, Nₐ₌₁₀₋ᵢₜₑᵣₐₜᵢₒₙ joint inversion within one GPU-hour.
authors: Clement Etienam, David Blom, Hari Pattathil, Tsubasa Onishi, Harpreet Sethi, Lalson Vincent, Suraj Pawar, Kishan Ramesh Kumar, Pandu Devarakota, Faruk O. Alpak

articles.title: RADIANT: Object-Centric Feed-Forward Global Illumination
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32075v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Feed-forward neural renderers synthesize global illumination across novel 3D scenes without per-scene optimization or runtime ray tracing. Existing transformer-based renderers tokenize individual triangles, so self-attention scales quadratically with mesh resolution. Yet macroscopic radiative transport is governed by the underlying surface geometry and object arrangements rather than a particular mesh discretization; finer tessellation can thus inflate token counts without changing the underlying transport physics, motivating a discretization-agnostic and object-centric representation. We introduce RADIANT (RADiance-based Inter-Actor Neural Transformer), an object-centric architecture for feed-forward global illumination from point inputs. By representing each object with a compact budget of 32 surface-patch tokens, RADIANT decouples attention sequence length from polygon counts. In a single network, an inter-object scene transformer models 3D radiative exchange and a view decoder renders images at target camera poses. To capture light transport without materializing O(N²⁾ bias matrices, invariant form-factor attention embeds geometric distances and surface orientations directly into query-key dot products as SE(3)-invariant inner products weighted by learned area and material gains. For primary visibility without mesh connectivity, camera rays cross-attend scene tokens guided by depth-tested point splats in a shared spherical frame. Across a 1.03M-scene benchmark under matched model capacity, RADIANT reaches 25 dB tone-mapped PSNR in 5x fewer training steps than RenderFormer, and achieves 32.2 dB at 600k steps (+3.3 dB over RenderFormer and +7.6 dB over RenderFormer-V2). We further demonstrate the scalability of RADIANT, which completes a 512x512 forward pass of a 500-object scene in 0.83 s, with computational cost scaling with the number of objects rather than polygons.
authors: Sarah Zhang, Zhiyang Dou, Minghao Guo, Benjamin Tod Jones, Wojciech Matusik

articles.title: Ψ-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Humans reason about the physical world by flexibly combining different forms of inference as a problem unfolds. Achieving this flexibility is a major open challenge in AI: capabilities often remain separated across specialized models, limiting how they can be composed and jointly adapted to a task. We introduce Ψ-0.6, a unified vision-language world model that adaptively composes perception, language, geometry, and simulation within a shared reasoning process we call streams of thought. These streams interleave images, text, and explicit representations of geometry and motion, all of which the model can generate and interpret through a shared token interface. Ψ-0.6 surpasses leading open-weight models zero-shot on multi-view spatial reasoning, with further gains from reasoning through geometric intermediates. It also supports counterfactual simulation: generating and interpreting imagined scenes to determine, for example, whether moving an object would obstruct a pathway. Reinforcement learning from task feedback jointly optimizes the selection, generation, and use of intermediate representations, improving visual question-answering accuracy with gains that transfer to unseen benchmarks. Ψ-0.6 offers a path toward adaptive physical reasoning -- not only predicting the physical world but also choosing the representations through which to reason.
authors: Khai Loong Aw, Klemen Kotar, Baihan Zhang, Yifan Liu, Lilian Chen, Atlas Kazemian, Rahul Venkatesh, Daniel Yamins

articles.title: Depth-Dependent Safety Geometry in Vision-Language Models: Layer-Wise Localization and Bidirectional Refusal Control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32182v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are widely deployed, yet the internal mechanisms behind their safety behavior remain poorly understood. We present a lightweight inference-time framework for localizing and manipulating safety-sensitive representations in frozen VLMs, without retraining or modifying parameters. On Qwen3-VL-4B, layer-wise activation divergence analysis reveals non-uniform safety geometry across depth. Causal interventions show that early vision layers support strong bidirectional refusal control through activation steering along a learned safety direction, with unsafe rejection spanning 6%-96%, whereas later layers respond more to activation magnitude scaling and exhibit a substantial safety-selectivity trade-off. Deeper layers remain well separated along the safety direction yet are largely insensitive to steering, distinguishing representational separability from causal controllability. InternVL2.5-4B shows qualitatively similar depth-dependent activation geometry despite differences in layer location and magnitude. Our results expose a white-box, representation-level refusal-bypass attack surface in VLM vision encoders and motivate inference-time stabilization of safety-sensitive representations.
authors: Muhammad Zeeshan Karamat, Syed Talal Hassan, Christiana Chamon Garcia

articles.title: RoboCode: Learning Reusable Action Primitives for Robot Manipulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent robot manipulation policies commonly predict continuous action chunks directly from observations, without explicitly modeling reusable structure in the action space. However, manipulation demonstrations often contain recurring short-horizon motion patterns that are shared across tasks. We introduce textscRoboCode, which learns these patterns through a shared soft-gated primitive action interface. Rather than assigning each action chunk to a single discrete code, textscRoboCode represents it as a soft composition of multiple learned primitives, providing a flexible intermediate representation of short-horizon actions. The primitive interface is learned from action chunks pooled across multiple tasks and then frozen while task-specific state encoders are trained to map current state inputs into the shared latent space. Experiments on five ManiSkill manipulation tasks address three questions. First, the learned primitive interface reconstructs action chunks with an average reconstruction MSE of 0.0187. Second, analysis of code activations reveals structured code reuse across tasks. Third, textscRoboCode achieves the highest or tied closed-loop success rate on all evaluated tasks, with an average success rate of 75.6%, compared with 68.8% for ACT and 41.6% for the larger Diffusion Policy baseline. These results suggest that soft-gated primitive codebooks provide an effective and interpretable intermediate action representation for robot manipulation.
authors: Xianyue Peng, Devi Amarsaikhan, Iman Soltani

articles.title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wireless electromyography (EMG) interfaces must balance electrode coverage against transmission bandwidth. Here, we show that compact EMG tokens substantially reduce payload while retaining information for three-dimensional hand-pose decoding. We evaluate two causal tokenizers fitted without pose labels: an encoder pretrained to reconstruct EMG spectra and one based on SPAR, an engineered spectral-spatial representation of neighbouring electrodes. In personalized, within-session experiments with 320-channel EMG from nine participants, we compare tokenized and continuous features using matched decoder architectures and training procedures. Averaged across decoders, tokenization changed mean error by +0.01 mm for SPAR (95% confidence interval: -0.12 to 0.14) and +0.45 mm for the learned representation (0.10 to 0.82). Both increases met a 1 mm non-inferiority criterion. Stored token arrays reduced payloads 41-fold relative to raw EMG and 36-fold relative to continuous SPAR features. On sampled windows of the public emg2pose benchmark's test partition, absolute differences in mean error between learned tokens and continuous features were below 0.05 mm across 176 participants and in the subset of 20 participants unseen during training. Electrode coverage, calibration, and unseen recordings affected SPAR decoding more than quantization did. In a computational benchmark, optimized SPAR generated tokens for 63 channels within 20 ms on a Cortex-M55 microcontroller. These findings support tokenization as a compact interface between wearable sensing and movement decoding, allowing decoders to be updated while the wearable encoder and transmitted representation remain fixed.
authors: Raul C. Sîmpetru, Amin Olamazadeh, Devon Rohlf, Vlad Cnejevici, Alessandro Del Vecchio

articles.title: Sparse Bayesian Neural Networks via Sticky Piecewise Deterministic Markov Processes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There is growing evidence that the performance of a neural network depends largely on a small subset of its weights, which are typically identified by training a dense network and pruning it afterwards. Within a Bayesian framework, pruning can be directly incorporated through a spike-and-slab prior, providing a proper treatment of the uncertainties involved, both with respect to pruning and to parameter uncertainty. In Bayesian neural networks (BNNs), sampling by MCMC is notoriously hard. We demonstrate that modern Monte Carlo methods based on piecewise deterministic Markov processes (PDMPs) can be used to sample posteriors of BNNs asymptotically exact whenever numerically constructed rate bounds hold. Spike-and-slab priors can be incorporated through sticky versions of the PDMPs, setting weights exactly to zero during sampling. We examine the predictive performance and convergence of the samplers, and show that sparse BNNs sampled this way can be more robust to input noise than dense ones.
authors: August Arnstad, Geir Olve Storvik, Filippo Pagani, Leiv Rønneberg

articles.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.
authors: Amber Xie, Jiawei Fu, Xiaofeng Guo, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi, Haozhi Qi

articles.title: FC-PINO: High Precision Physics-Informed Neural Operators via Fourier Continuation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2211.15960v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The physics-informed neural operator (PINO) is a machine learning paradigm that has demonstrated promising results for learning solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs). It leverages the Fourier Neural Operator to learn solution operators in function spaces and leverages physics losses during training to penalize deviations from known physics laws. Spectral differentiation provides an efficient way to compute derivatives for the physics losses, but it inherently assumes periodicity. When applied to non-periodic functions, this assumption can lead to significant errors, including Gibbs phenomena near domain boundaries which degrade the accuracy of both function representations and derivative computations. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the FC-PINO (Fourier-Continuation-based Physics-Informed Neural Operator) architecture which extends the accuracy and efficiency of PINO and spectral differentiation to non-periodic and non-smooth PDEs. In FC-PINO, we propose integrating Fourier continuation into the PINO framework, and test two different continuation approaches: FC-Legendre and FC-Gram. By transforming non-periodic signals into periodic functions on extended domains in a well-conditioned manner, Fourier continuation enables fast and accurate derivative computations. This approach avoids the discretization sensitivity of finite differences and the memory overhead of automatic differentiation. We demonstrate that standard PINO fails (without padding) or struggles (even with padding) to solve non-periodic and non-smooth PDEs with high precision, across challenging benchmarks. In contrast, the proposed FC-PINO provides accurate, robust, and scalable solutions, substantially outperforming PINO alternatives, and demonstrating that Fourier continuation is critical for extending PINO to a wider range of PDE problems when high-precision solutions are needed.
authors: Adarsh Ganeshram, Valentin Duruisseaux, Haydn Maust, Zongyi Li, Yixuan Wang, Daniel Leibovici, Oscar Bruno, Thomas Hou, Anima Anandkumar

articles.title: Learning Bidirectional Causal Interactions with Heteroscedastic Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.22313v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Estimating contemporaneous bidirectional interactions from observational data is difficult because each outcome is endogenous to the other, while flexible regressions may capture only reduced-form dependence. This paper proposes SEM-DNN, a heteroscedastic neural simultaneous-equation estimator that learns reciprocal structural interactions without external instruments. Identification exploits conditional covariance diagonalization: when structural shocks have zero conditional means, are conditionally uncorrelated given predetermined covariates, and exhibit nonproportional conditional variances, only the true interaction coefficients diagonalize the conditional residual covariance across the feature space. The method jointly approximates nonlinear structural mean functions and feature-dependent variances using a diagonal Gaussian quasi-likelihood that incorporates the simultaneous-system Jacobian. We establish unique identification and positive-definite local curvature of the profiled population criterion and show that, under neural-profile compatibility conditions, the implemented neural criterion inherits this curvature despite nonunique network parameterizations. The coefficients admit a causal interpretation when the structural equations represent autonomous mechanisms that remain invariant under the relevant interventions. Monte Carlo experiments with nonlinear, high-dimensional nuisance functions and non-Gaussian shocks show that SEM-DNN recovers structural effects more reliably than parametric, kernel-based, and separate-equation neural alternatives as information increases, although at greater computational cost. An application to ready-to-eat cereal scanner data illustrates how the method can study contemporaneous price-sales feedback and assess identification strength, residual diagonalization, variance calibration, and optimization sensitivity.

articles.title: From Dueling Bandits to Episodic MDPs: Learning with Adversarial Preference Feedback
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.11706v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In dueling bandits, the learner compares two arms in each round and observes only which one is preferred. This paper asks what changes when the compared pair also affects the next state, as in a recommendation interface where the pair shown to a user affects the user's next context. We formulate this problem as a state-wise preference-based MDP, an episodic tabular MDP in which the learner selects a pair of arms at each visited state, observes only a noisy comparison between them, and moves to a next state that may depend on the pair. The preferences may change adversarially across episodes, and the loss of a pair is defined through Borda scores. We show that the minimax regret of this problem under known transitions is tildeΘ(minHT,(H³SK)¹/³T²/³), where H, S, K, and T are the numbers of steps per episode, states, arms, and episodes, and that this rate is achieved by an algorithm based on online linear optimization over the set of occupancy measures. If the pair did not affect the next state, each state would be a separate dueling bandit, and the T²/³ term of the minimax regret would be smaller by a factor of H¹/³, demonstrating the cost of having action-dependent state transitions. We also give a policy optimization algorithm with closed-form updates, whose regret is tildeO((H⁴SK³⁾¹/³T²/³) up to lower-order terms, and we extend both algorithms to unknown transitions.
authors: Taira Tsuchiya, Shinji Ito, Haipeng Luo

articles.title: PPO vs. SAC: A Comparative Study for Cooperative Motion Control of Dual-Arm Space Robots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing population of orbital debris has intensified interest in active debris removal and on-orbit servicing, for which dual-arm space manipulators offer improved grasping stability and load distribution relative to single-arm systems. However, coordinating two manipulators under inter-arm collision avoidance, orientation alignment, and sensing uncertainty remains challenging. This paper develops a coordinated reinforcement learning framework for cooperative motion planning of a dual-arm space manipulator in a target-reaching task with inter-arm collision-avoidance constraints. A centralized state representation combines joint-space, end-effector, and target-relative information, while a multi-objective reward function promotes target-reaching accuracy, orientation alignment, motion smoothness, synchronized task completion, and collision avoidance. Within this framework, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) are compared as representative on-policy and off-policy algorithms, and the learned policies are further evaluated for generalization to previously unseen target configurations. Across five random seeds, SAC substantially outperforms PPO within the considered fixed-base simulation scenarios: it reaches an 80% success threshold in every seed (median 1.6M environment steps) whereas PPO does not reach it within a 4M-step budget, and it attains a higher mean success rate (78.6% versus 7.4%) with lower position and orientation errors and tighter bimanual synchronization. Both algorithms degrade on unseen boundary targets, but SAC retains most of its performance while PPO's collapses. The results also expose a failure mode of PPO: under the two-phase shaped reward, it tends to converge to a reward-loitering local optimum rather than committing to the precision task. This behavior highlights the sensitivity of on-policy learning to reward shaping.

articles.title: Spatial Heuristic Strategy based Diffusion Reinforcement Learning for Online 3D Bin Packing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional heuristic methods have accumulated mature experience in core objectives, such as space utilization and layout compactness of 3D bin packing, relying on artificially designed rule-based logic. However, they exhibit obvious limitations in generalization ability and adaptability to dynamic scenarios. Diffusion reinforcement learning, which integrates the spatial search capability of reinforcement learning and the data distribution modeling capability of diffusion learning, has achieved certain progress in action distribution modeling and decision compliance constraints. Nevertheless, there remain issues including insufficient perception of the spatial topological structure in 3D bin packing and limited layout optimization capability. To address these problems, we propose a diffusion reinforcement learning method integrated with spatial heuristic strategies, which combines classical bin packing heuristic rules with a diffusion reinforcement learning framework. Specifically, it compresses the action space through heuristic action pre-screening, introduces a graph neural network to model the spatial structure, and designs a composite reward function incorporating flatness to suppress spatial fragmentation, thereby realizing the organic integration of prior knowledge and adaptive optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the pro

articles.title: Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent - and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems that discover scientific relations now generate candidate "laws" at scale, but the bottleneck has shifted from generation to vetting: which candidates deserve belief? We show that a deployed self-improving science agent - one that has admitted 252 relations through held-out prediction courts - already computes the quantity that answers this question: the Minimum Description Length compression ratio used for model selection doubles, when read under discrete accounting, as an unsupervised epistemic grader. The compression-ranked top band of the agent's ledger recovers exactly the canonical laws among its discoveries (vis-viva across seven planets, Balmer/Rydberg) plus cross-measurement identities - enrichment p=3.6×10⁻¹² under a hypergeometric test - with zero counterexamples and physically coherent band structure. The same lens retroactively reveals that 86% of the ledger compresses nothing (crapprox 1): the agent had been recording statistical regularities, including a learned predictor with held-out R²⁼⁰.541 admitted through the prediction gate, under a narrative of compression as the unified value of knowledge - a narrative that was never true for them. We formalize the resulting dual-axis bookkeeping - prediction value (R²⁾ and compression value (cr) as nearly decoupled axes of knowledge - demonstrate its robustness to quantization, and register forward falsifiable predictions. The episode is, to our knowledge, the first measured instance of a discovery agent auditing its own knowledge ledger by an internal measure and finding itself over-claiming.

articles.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent-evolution methods use execution feedback to improve prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration, but their implementations often rebuild the same experimental machinery. We present RSIHub, an open-source framework for building, comparing, and extending these methods on shared infrastructure. Recipes compose reusable operators and declare mutable resources; RSIHub supplies execution, evaluation, recovery, and lineage. Researchers can focus on evolution policy while evaluation stays outside the mutable surface and results remain tied to candidates and evaluation conditions. We instantiate AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, and GEPA without modifying the framework core, keeping method-specific logic in recipes and operators. We evaluate them with MiniSWE and Codex on Terminal Bench 2 and τ³ Banking under fixed model and evaluator configurations. The largest observed overall pass@1 gain is 13.5 percentage points, while method rankings vary across settings and optimization gains do not always transfer to held-out tasks. RSIHub provides a common protocol for comparing evolution policies, inspectable candidate histories, and reusable components for developing new methods.
authors: Zimu Wang, Xiaobo Wang, Siyu Ye, Jiaqi Li, Silin Chen, Yuling Shi, Ruobing Wang, Jingjing Zhang, Chaofan Wang, Kai Wu, Mengnan Qi, Kai Cai, Xiaodong Gu, Zilong Zheng

articles.title: Adaptive Control of Scientific Instruments with Nonstationary Responses through Multimodal Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling scientific instruments requires parameters to be adjusted progressively in response to feedback from successive operations. When unobserved operating conditions evolve with operational history, responses become nonstationary, and a static mapping from actions to responses becomes inadequate for decisions across shots. Shot-to-shot tuning of neutral beam injection (NBI) ion sources in magnetic confinement fusion devices is representative of this class of problems: the conditions of electrode surfaces and vacuum are difficult to observe directly, discharge outcomes vary between shots, and experiments are costly and carry operational risks. We propose a physically grounded multimodal agent with three independently auditable components. Deterministic algorithms extract symbolic physical quantities and visual evidence from multichannel waveforms; a memory with two layers organizes trajectories from the current task, experience from earlier tasks, and procedural knowledge, from which a multimodal large language model (MLLM) generates candidate actions; and an independent action feasibility check enforces action constraints before execution. In a strictly chronological replay of 455 shots from four EXL-50U platforms, physical symbols alone outperformed waveform images alone by 0.21-0.32 in macro-F1 for quality classification across all four evaluated models. Retrieved context increased the mean agreement with historical action directions by 22.4-42.7 percentage points, whereas the contribution of visual evidence varied across models. Under supervised operation on five ion sources, the system achieved a beam-extraction rate of 86.80% across 409 executed shots. These results demonstrate the engineering feasibility of the framework for supervised sequential tuning on a physical scientific instrument.
authors: Guoyang Shi, Hongwen Li, Yiding Yu, Zhuang Fu, Siqi Ding, Zhengyuan Chen, JianGuo Chen, Hanyue Zhao, Tianyuan Liu

articles.title: IGG: A Benchmark for Interactive GUI Grounding under Visibility Constraints
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI grounding benchmarks ask whether an agent can localize a target that is already visible in a static screenshot. Real interfaces often violate this assumption: a target may be off-screen, appear only after a state change or hover, remain occluded, or become actionable after a delay. This leaves the ability to recover target visibility unevaluated. To measure this reveal step, we introduce Interactive GUI Grounding (IGG), a benchmark in which an agent must first make the target visible through interaction and then click it. IGG contains 601 tasks across 16 controllable GUI environments and seven visibility-constraint sub-types, with a compact action space of scrolling, moving, dragging, waiting, and clicking. In our human study, participants achieve 94.6% accuracy, while GPT-5.5 reaches 79.4% and the strongest evaluated open-source VLM reaches only 31.6%. To identify the source of this gap, we conduct two controlled interventions. Telling Qwen3-VL which interaction to perform raises its accuracy only from 30.8% to 33.9%, whereas performing the interaction for the model raises it to 81.9%. The bottleneck is executing the reveal interaction, not recognizing the target once it is exposed. We further show that this capability is learnable, demonstrating that visibility recovery can be strengthened consistently across model families.
authors: Kyeongseon Kim, Jiyeon Son, Tae-Hyun Oh

articles.title: A Foundation Model for Policy In-Context Longitudinal Causal Effect Estimation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Longitudinal causal effect estimation is complicated by time-varying confounding and treatment-confounder feedback loops. Existing methods generally require data-specific nuisance-model fitting, and many are tailored to prespecified treatment sequences or prediction horizons, leading to time-consuming computation at deployment. We introduce *Policy In-Context Longitudinal causal Effect estimation with Prior-data Fitted Networks* (**PICLE-PFN**), the first foundation model for longitudinal causal effect estimation that supports *dynamic* treatment policies. PICLE-PFN represents target policies through in-context history-decision demonstrations, providing a unified interface for a broad class of treatment policies. Pretrained over synthetic data sampled from longitudinal structural causal models, PICLE-PFN amortizes causal effect estimation across datasets, policies, and horizons. Given a new observational dataset and target policy, it directly predicts conditional average potential outcomes (CAPOs) in one forward pass without task-specific training or hyperparameter tuning. Across synthetic and semi-synthetic longitudinal benchmarks, PICLE-PFN achieves competitive RMSE and substantially improved uncertainty calibration with a fraction of deployment runtime, compared to state-of-the-art conventional estimators trained and tuned separately for each dataset.
authors: Wenxin Chen, Kyra Gan, Mingyu Lu, Zilin Jing, Fei Wang, Hoifung Poon, Tristan Naumann, Peniel Argaw

articles.title: Modifying the Surface of Silica-Coated Magnesium Cobalt Ferrite with Curcumin to Eliminate Pb(II) and Cd(II) from Different Environmental Water Samples
articles.abstract: Water contamination is a crucial ecological concern impacting aquatic ecosystems and human health, particularly because of heavy metals entering water bodies from the industrial, agricultural, and mining activities. To address this, magnesium-doped cobalt ferrite nanoparticles (MgCoFe2O4@SiO2-CPTMS-Cur) were expanded for effective heavy metal removal from wastewater. These nanoparticles were made initially through coprecipitation technique and then were coated with silica and modified with 3-chloropropyltrimethoxysilane (CPTMS) and curcumin (Cur) to improve the adsorption capabilities. The as-synthesized product was fully characterised by FTIR, EDX, XRD, TEM SEM, BET, TGA and VSM, showing a crystalline structure and a porous surface with a BET surface area of 24.176 m2/g. The adsorption experiments showed an effective removal of Lead Pb(II) and Cadmium Cd(II), with a maximum abilities of 259.50 mg/g for Pb(II) and 208.35 mg/g for Cd(II). Kinetic testing revealed that the adsorption followed a second-order kinetic model, despite the Langmuir isotherm model accurately representing the equilibrium data. The adsorption process was endothermic, spontaneous, and beneficial, according to thermodynamic study. Research on regeneration demonstrated the durability and reusability of the composite over four cycles, highlighting its promise as a frugal and operative adsorbent for heavy metal extraction in environmental cleanup. The effective removal of Pb(II) and Cd(II) metal ions from tap, groundwater, and lake water was achieved utilising this innovative adsorbent.

articles.title: Application of Remote Sensing and Geographic Information System in Groundwater Potential Assessment of Palladan, Zaria, Northwestern Nigeria
articles.abstract: Groundwater is an important source of water for domestic, agricultural, and industrial activities, particularly in basement complex terrains where its occurrence is controlled by surface and subsurface geological conditions. This study assessed the groundwater potential of Palladan, Zaria, Northwestern Nigeria, using remote sensing and Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques. Landsat 9 Operational Land Imager (OLI) satellite imagery and Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data were acquired and processed to generate thematic layers, including land use/land cover, lineament density, drainage density, and slope. The Landsat 9 imagery was processed using ENVI software, while ArcGIS was employed for spatial analysis, thematic mapping, and integration of the groundwater-influencing factors. Land use/land cover classification was performed using the Maximum Likelihood Classification technique, whereas lineaments were extracted from enhanced satellite imagery using directional filtering and PCI Geomatica. The thematic layers were reclassified according to their relative suitability for groundwater occurrence and integrated using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and weighted overlay techniques to produce a Groundwater Potential Zonation (GWPZ) map. The results revealed that built-up areas constituted approximately 50% of the study area, bare land 33%, vegetation 15%, and water bodies 2%. The AHP analysis assigned the highest weight to slope (0.5016), followed by drainage density (0.2630), land use/land cover (0.1591), and lineament density (0.0768), with a consistency ratio of 0.051. The resulting groundwater potential assessment identified areas of varying groundwater suitability, with approximately 60% of the study area classified within good to excellent groundwater potential zones. These zones were predominantly associated with gentle slopes, high lineament density, low drainage density, and favourable land cover conditions.

articles.title: The RegTech Paradox: Balancing Compliance Costs and Digital Synergies in Indian Banking
articles.abstract: This study empirically investigates the impact of regulatory technology (RegTech) adoption on the financial performance of Indian commercial banks. Utilizing a comprehensive panel dataset of 32 listed banks from 2016 to 2025, the research employs Python-based text-mining techniques on published annual reports to construct a novel RegTech adoption index, which is bifurcated into Core Regulatory Technology and RegTech Enabling Technology. To account for the dynamic persistence of bank profitability and resolve potential endogeneity issues, the study utilizes a two-step System GMM estimator alongside baseline Random Effects modeling. The empirical results reveal a significant asymmetrical relationship. Investments in RegTech Enabling Technology such as artificial intelligence and big data yield a strong, positive, and statistically significant enhancement to the Return on Assets (ROA). Conversely, Core Regulatory Technology dedicated strictly to automated compliance acts primarily as a mandatory operational safeguard, demonstrating a statistically insignificant impact on overall profitability. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis uncovers that the financial benefits of foundational enabling technologies are heavily concentrated among large institutions and private sector banks, whereas the substantial capital expenditures required for core compliance systems actively compress the asset returns of large banks. These core findings are rigorously validated through extensive robustness checks, including the use of alternative dependent variables (ROE), lagged effects, outlier removal, and a Monte Carlo placebo test. Ultimately, this research provides vital strategic insights for bank management and policymakers regarding the operational costs and monetization potential of digital compliance infrastructures.

articles.title: Microstructure Evolution and Synergistic Optimization of Mechanical Properties and Thermal Conductivity in Mg-xSn-0.2Ca-0.5Zr Alloys
articles.abstract: To address the challenge of the trade-off between mechanical properties and thermal conductivity in magnesium alloys, Mg-xSn-0.2Ca-0.5Zr alloys (x = 3, 4, 5 wt.%) were investigated in this work. Permanent mold casting, semi-solid rheo-die casting, and heat treatment were employed to tailor the microstructure of the alloys. The inherent correlations between microstructure evolution, mechanical properties, and thermal conductivity were systematically explored. The results reveal that as Sn content increases in permanent mold cast alloys, grain refinement occurs and the volume fraction of secondary phases rises. Nevertheless, excessive Sn induces coarsening of grain-boundary Mg2Sn, thereby degrading both ductility and thermal conductivity. Among the permanent mold cast alloys, Mg-4Sn-0.2Ca-0.5Zr exhibits optimal overall performance, with an ultimate tensile strength of 137 MPa, yield strength of 71 MPa, elongation of 7.6%, and thermal conductivity of 86.12 W/(m·K), and is accompanied by the lowest hot-tearing susceptibility. Near-spherical α-Mg grains are obtained in the semi-solid rheo-die cast Mg-4Sn-0.2Ca-0.5Zr alloy. After T6 heat treatment, fine Mg2Sn precipitates are dispersed throughout the matrix. The ultimate tensile strength, yield strength, and elongation are improved to 202 MPa, 112 MPa, and 11.7%, respectively. Meanwhile, aging facilitates the precipitation of Sn from the α-Mg matrix and reduces electron scattering, contributing to an elevated thermal conductivity of 110.68 W/(m·K). Regulation of the solidification microstructure enables the simultaneous enhancement of strength, ductility, and thermal conductivity for Mg-Sn-Ca-Zr alloys.

articles.title: Synthesis, Structural Studies and Cytotoxic Activity of six Novel Mononuclear Metal(II) Complexes with a Tridentate N3-Donor Schiff Based Ligand
articles.abstract: In this work, Six mononuclear novel metal complexes with octahedral geometry were synthesized using the tridentate N3-donor Schiff base ligand N′-Phenyl-N″(phenyl(pyridin-2-yl)methylene)ethane-1,2-diamine (L) and the general formula of the six complexes is [M(L)2](ClO4)2. 2H2O (M = Cu, Ni, Mn, Co, Zn and Cd). Their structures and properties were characterized by elemental analysis, IR, mass and electronic spectroscopy, conductivity measurements and magnetic studies. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that [Ni(L)2](ClO4)2.2H2O and [Zn(L)2](ClO4)2.2H2O complexes have distorted octahedral coordination around the metal center. Cytotoxic activity of the all complexes showed dose depended toxicity and among them Cu(II) and Mn(II) complexes have very low IC50 value.

articles.title: Representation-Covariant Scale Exponents under Fisher-Induced Whitening: Identifiability, Profile Likelihood, and Adaptive Estimation
articles.abstract: The KA (Kerimov--Alekberli) model posits that Fisher Information spectral projections obey a Generalized Gaussian Distribution (GGD) whose scale and shape parameters follow power laws of the corresponding eigenvalue, with exponents ν and α. We characterise which exponents are representation-covariant artefacts under Fisher-induced whitening and which are intrinsic. Proposition~1 establishes an exact, finite-sample, distribution-free identity: the OLS estimate of ν shifts by exactly~1/2 under whitening, for any data and any shape parameter. Theorem~1 extends this to the profile likelihood: the profile log-likelihood is equivariant under whitening, so the profile MLE satisfies hnu^P_w = hnu^Pᵣₐw + 1/2 and halpha^P_w = halpha^Pᵣₐw exactly. Thus α is representation-invariant; ν is representation-covariant with a universal +1/2 shift. and power 1.00 for α≥ 0.20. A Monte Carlo benchmark over 360 cells (36,000 runs) confirms all results at machine precision: Gate~1 maximum deviation łeq 5.6× 10⁻⁹; profile RMSE 4--8× smaller than OLS. The BIS demonstration validates pipeline executability only; the LLM-0 protocol is a prospective specification for future empirical work.

articles.title: Climatological Characteristics and Mechanisms of the South China Sea Winter Monsoon Onset
articles.abstract: The South China Sea Winter Monsoon (SCSWM) plays an important role in shaping the physical environment and ecosystem in the South China Sea (SCS). Based on pentad-averaged data from 1980 to 2024, this study found that the transition from the SCS summer monsoon to the winter monsoon progresses from north to south, at a rate comparable to that of the reverse transition. Therefore, analogous to the established term “SCS Summer Monsoon onset”, the establishment of the SCS winter monsoon can be referred to as “SCSWM onset”. The onset time of the SCSWM can be defined as the first pentad when the northeasterlies are established over the deeper sea in the central SCS (8°–18°N, 110°–119°E), with a climatological mean onset around pentad 57 in early October. Further analyses reveal that the southward migration of the deep atmospheric convection center from the Philippine Islands to Borneo is the dominant mechanism governing the SCSWM onset. This migration is primarily driven by the seasonal southward shift in solar radiation during boreal autumn. Positive (negative) sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies around the Philippine Islands in late August to early September enhance (weaken) local convection, thereby contributing to a later (earlier) SCSWM onset. These local SST anomalies can be traced to the tropical Atlantic SST anomalies in early boreal summer, providing new insights into the mechanisms and potential predictors for the SCSWM onset.

articles.title: SoFIC Orchestrates Physical Barriers and Metabolic Homeostasis to Counter Phage Infection
articles.abstract: Bacteria have evolved numerous defense systems to counter persistent phage infections. In this study, we characterize SoFIC, a protein encoded by E. coli E5 that catalyzes various post-translational modifications and coordinates a multilayed antiviral defense system by reshaping extrabacterial barriers and intracellular metabolism. Our results show that SoFIC is widely distributed across multiple bacterial phyla (particularly Proteobacteria) and exhibits diverse domain architectures; nonetheless, all variants contain a conserved Fic catalytic motif essential for anti-phage activity. Using the native host E. coli E5 and its cognate short-tailed phage DE5 as a model, knockout and complementation experiments demonstrated that the anti-phage function of SoFIC requires an intact Fic catalytic motif. Extracellularly, SoFIC physically hinders initial phage adsorption by maintaining surface structures such as fimbriae and biofilms. Intracellularly, once phages breach this barrier, SoFIC specifically interacts with key host proteins involved in DNA homeostasis (HupA, SbmC), transcription elongation (NusB), nucleotide metabolism (PyrB), and oxidative stress defense (Bfr, MsrA), preventing the host cell from entering a metabolic state conductive to phage proliferation. Furthermore, SoFIC exhibits time-dependent functional interactions with multiple endogenous defense systems, including Septu I, RM III, PsyrTA and Retron VI, collectively enhancing host immunity. Taken together, this study establishes SoFIC as a central coordinator of both physical and physiological antiviral barriers, reveals an extracellular and intracellular dual-layer defense model, and positions SoFIC as a key node in the multilayered bacterial immune network. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding the defense mechanisms of Fic family proteins and offer fundamental insights for engineering phage-resistant bacterial chassis.
