articles.title: Green ZnO NPs from Trichoderma and Their Effects on Zucchini and Beet
articles.abstract: Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) are promising nano-fertilizers for improving zinc delivery and crop performance. This study investigated the biogenic synthesis of ZnO NPs using Trichoderma and evaluated their effects on seed germination and early seedling growth of zucchini (Cucurbita pepo L.) and beet (Beta vulgaris L.). Fourteen Trichoderma isolates were recovered from rhizosphere soils across ten Egyptian governorates and characterized morphologically and by ITS analysis. Most isolates were identified as Trichoderma harzianum. Five isolates (1, 2, 4, 6, and 9) showed superior ZnO biosynthesis, and T. harzianum MNF-SHS-Tricho 9 was selected for optimization. Maximum production was obtained using 10 mL cell-free culture filtrate with 5 mM zinc acetate at pH 8 and 28°C. ZnO NP formation and zinc and oxygen composition were confirmed by UV–Vis, FTIR, and EDX analyses. Transmission electron microscopy showed spherical nanoparticles with a mean size of 60.99 ± 26.12 nm. Dynamic light scattering indicated a hydrodynamic diameter of 1038 nm and a high polydispersity index (0.737), reflecting aggregation, consistent with the weak negative zeta potential (− 6.92 ± 3.21 mV). Seed germination and seedling growth showed concentration-dependent responses, with 5 mM ZnO NPs producing favorable effects. In zucchini, seedling vigor index and germination rate increased to 51.0 and 17.4, respectively, compared with 29.7 and 13.4 in controls. In beet, corresponding values increased to 33.3 and 8.5 versus 21.8 and 7.3. Higher concentrations reduced germination and seedling vigor. These findings demonstrate the potential of T. harzianum-mediated ZnO NPs as biological nano-zinc inputs for early crop development.

articles.title: Spectroscopic, Light-Harvesting, and Quantum Mechanical Studies of a TDMIM·BF 4 Ionic Liquid Crystal-ZnO Cluster Hybrid for Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Context- The present study reports a comprehensive theoretical investigation of the spectroscopic, light-harvesting, and quantum mechanical properties of a novel hybrid system consisting the ionic liquid crystal (ILC) 1-tetradecyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate (TDMIM·BF₄, C₁₄MIM·BF₄) and ZnO clusters. The hybrid network architecture combines the electronic properties of the ILC with the semiconducting characteristics of ZnO, with the aim of improving the performance of dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs). Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were performed to investigate the structural stability, electronic structure, and optoelectronic behaviour of the TDMIM·BF4-ZnO hybrid conformations. The influence of ZnO incorporation on the structural, electronic, spectroscopic, and optoelectronic properties of the ILC-ZnO hybrid conformations was investigated. Particular attention was given to changes in the electronic distribution and charge-transfer characteristics using frontier molecular orbital (FMO) analysis and energy-gap calculations, while molecular electrostatic potential (MESP) and work-function analyses were employed to examine the modified surface electronic environment and charge-transport characteristics. The photovoltaic relevance of the hybrid systems was further examined through light-harvesting efficiency (LHE), open-circuit voltage (Vₒc), and fill factor (FF) under AM 1.5G solar irradiation. The study provides insight into the role of ZnO incorporation in enhancing the optical and electronic characteristics of TDMIM·BF₄ and its potential applicability in the design of hybrid DSSC materials.Methods- Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed using Gaussian 09 to optimize C14MIM.BF4, ZnO clusters, and C14MIM.BF4-(ZnO)ₙ (n = 2–8) hybrid conformations. Geometry optimizations were carried out using the B3LYP functional with the 6-311 + + G(d,p) basis set for H, C, N, O, and F atoms, while the LANL2DZ effective core potential was employed for Zn.

articles.title: Theoretical prediction of masses and decay constants of bottomonium and bottom-charm mesons with spin dependent Cornell potential
articles.abstract: We investigate the bound-state spectrum and decay properties of mesons using a spin-dependent Cornell potential within first-order perturbation theory. Analytical expressions for the energy eigenvalues are obtained, and the model is validated by considering the spin-independent limit, where the results reproduce the standard Cornell potential spectrum and show good agreement with existing calculations based on artificial neural networks, the asymptotic iteration method, and the matrix Numerov approach. The parameters of the spin-dependent potential are determined by fitting the resulting analytical mass-spectrum equation to experimental data. These parameters are then used to calculate the masses and decay properties of bottomonium and bottom-charm mesons for low-lying quantum states. For the bottomonium states, an average percentage absolute deviation of approximately 0.15% from the experimental masses is obtained, demonstrating an improvement over several previous theoretical predictions while the bottom-charm masses aligned with other theoretic values in the literature. The vector and pseudoscalar decay constants are calculated from the corresponding wave functions at the origin and exhibit a decreasing behavior with increasing principal quantum number, The pseudoscalar di-photon and vector leptonic decay widths are subsequently evaluated using the leading and first-order Van Royen–Weisskopf formula. The predicted decay constants are found to be generally consistent with available experimental data and previous theoretical results. Furthermore, incorporating the QCD running strong coupling at appropriate renormalization scales improves the description of the decay properties, emphasizing the sensitivity to the wave function at the origin. The results demonstrate that the perturbative spin-dependent Cornell potential provides a simple and effective phenomenological framework for describing the mass spectra and decay properties of bottomonium and bottom-charm mesons.

articles.title: Auditable Corridor Shortlisting under Partial Observability: A Systems Approach to Ranking Human Trafficking Origin–Destination Links
articles.abstract: International human trafficking is only partially observed at the corridor level: a small number of origin–destination (OD) pairs appear in public victim-case compilations, while the space of possible corridors is vast. We treat corridor pri-oritization as a systems problem and present an auditable ranking loop that maps sparse observed ODs, country-level covariates, and an explicit graph representation into a shortlist of corridors for subsequent review. The system couples three inference pathways (tabular attributes, graph neural message passing, and a temporal world model) under a frozen holdout and hard-matched negatives. Assurance is provided by a falsification battery (label destruction, structural nulls, graph rewiring, world-model ablations), calibration diagnostics, multi-seed stability checks, and prospective recovery of Counter-Trafficking Data Collabo-rative (CTDC) corridors first observed after year cuts. Across three seeds, the core battery passes on average 6.33 of 8 controls; graph-rewire tests pass on one of three seeds and are reported as unstable, and world-model interventions pass only on training-loss gaps. The tabular pathway is the strongest ranker (edge precision–recall area under the curve, PR-AUC, 0.59 ± 0.17 versus 0.48 ± 0.10 for the graph neural network), but test splits contain roughly a dozen positives and seed variance is large. In prospective recovery, tabular recall@20 averages 0.50 over seeds and cuts, against chance PR-AUC of 0.25–0.37. The deliverable is not a certified map of trafficking routes but a reproducible shortlist with an attached verification record, designed to interface with external review.

articles.title: Wide-Swath Altimetry over Rivers Reveals Natural and Regulated Seasonality Patterns Globally
articles.abstract: The seasonal pulse of rivers migrates across the planet, shaped by atmospheric circulation, basin memory and human control, with river discharge carrying this movement along valley corridors globally. Three years of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission global discharge product reveal these dynamics, their reorganization by climate teleconnections, and disruption by regulation. Seasonal activation emerges and evolves through the year: tropical activation reaches +64% above the annual mean in the northern Amazon and monsoon activation +52% in the Ganges in 2024. These patterns are undersampled by sparse and transboundary in-situ networks; SWOT's dense sampling reveals a misrepresentation of basin dynamics of up to 27%. The SWOT period spans the transition from the strong 2023 El Niño to neutral and La Niña conditions in 2025, when seasonal discharge shifts by roughly twice its typical year-to-year variation in the northern Amazon-Orinoco system, while the strengthening 2025 La Niña drives the Congo down by about four-fifths of a typical year's variation. SWOT further exposes where regulation breaks seasonal regimes: the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam delays the Blue Nile by 2.8 months and dampens it by 46%, while the Aswan High Dam shifts the downstream Nile by 6 months and dampens it by 59%. SWOT thus opens a new view of the global river network, following water movement as it emerges, shifts, and is interrupted across continents.

articles.title: Influence of Crystallographic and Microstructural Features on Magneto-crystalline Anisotropy and Magnetization Reversal in Al-Doped Ni Thin Films
articles.abstract: The role of controlled doping in tuning magneto-crystalline anisotropy and magnetization reversal in polycrystalline Ni nanocomposite thin films through crystallographic and microstructural modification remains inadequately addressed. This study examines magnetron-sputtered Al-doped Ni thin films containing 0, 2, 3, and 5 wt.% Al deposited on Si/SiO₂ substrates. Al incorporation progressively contracts the Ni lattice and refines the crystallite size while increasing microstrain, dislocation density, and mosaic spread, collectively degrading the crystallographic texture. These structural changes arise from substitutional lattice distortion and solute-limited adatom mobility, which suppress grain growth and promote re-nucleation. XRR and AFM further show that Al reduces film density and produces a non-monotonic surface roughness, with the smoothest and most uniform surface at the intermediate composition. The resulting magnetic behavior is non-monotonic. The undoped film exhibits a preferred 0° direction with a loop displacement of approximately 48 Oe, arising from interfacial exchange coupling with a naturally formed antiferromagnetic NiO layer. At 5 wt.% Al, the balance between reduced pinning and moderate structural disorder produces the most favorable response, with the lowest easy-axis coercivity (80.0 ± 0.5 Oe), highest squareness (0.708 ± 0.003), and highest initial susceptibility (0.0208 ± 0.0005 Oe⁻¹). Beyond this optimum, excessive lattice strain and defect accumulation broaden the distribution of local switching fields, increasing coercivity to 128.0 ± 0.5 Oe and promoting multistep reversal. The results further show that coercivity deviates from classical grain-size scaling and is governed more strongly by mosaic spread and defect density, while surface roughness limits the low-field susceptibility. These findings demonstrate that moderate Al incorporation provides effective control over magnetic anisotropy and reversal, whereas excessive doping destabilizes the reversal pathway through disorder-dominated pinning.

articles.title: Finite-copy optimal cloning of mixed qudit states: exact optima, a closed-form cloner, and the structure of covariant sector channels
articles.abstract: Copying is the most basic operation on information, and the no-cloning theorem is the sharpest statement of how quantum information differs from classical. The best approximate copier of pure states has been known for decades, and the asymptotic theory of cloning mixed states at fixed gain γ=m/n was recently completed by Schur--Weyl methods, which give closed-form limiting fidelities and an asymptotically optimal ``Schur--Cartan'' cloner. Whether those constructions are also good at the finite copy numbers available in experiments, and what the finite-copy optimum is, was unknown. We show that the finite-copy optimum is a concave program over Young-label transition rules and extremal covariant maps between irreducible sectors, solve it exactly for qubits up to n=40 and for qutrits and ququarts at small n, and show that the asymptotically optimal cloners lose up to 0.11 in root fidelity at nłe 20, while purify--clone--trace fails at the degenerate spectrum. The loss is entirely in the label rule: the Cartan sector channel is finite-copy optimal for qubits, and in higher dimension it coincides with the lowest-Casimir (minimal Parthasarathy--Ranga Rao--Varadarajan) component, which is within 10⁻³ of optimal. A closed-form cloner, a Knothe--Rosenblatt coupling of the input and target label laws followed by lowest-Casimir channels, is asymptotically optimal, improves the Schur--Cartan cloner by up to 0.115, and comes with Karush--Kuhn--Tucker and Frank--Wolfe certificates bracketing the true optimum to 10⁻³ without semidefinite programming. The analysis isolates a single representation-theoretic question, the pairwise optimality of the PRV channel at intermediate spectral mixedness, settled here in the cold and hot limits and for single-copy inputs, which governs how much coherent cloning advantage survives at the copy numbers of near-term quantum networks.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting Wavelength- Dependent Optical Modulation of Neuronal Activity
articles.abstract: Wavelength-dependent optical stimulation may also be a potential method for non-invasive modulation of neural activity, but the effects of this stimulation are controlled by a series of factors that include the energy of the photons, the optical properties of the tissue, the optical dose delivered, wavelength sensitivity, and neuronal characteristics. This work introduces a physics-informed machine learning framework to explore the responses of neurons across different wavelengths and to measure predictive uncertainty, in an explainable manner. Two optical features derived from experimental measurements and physics modelling were combined with the biological sensitivity descriptors and tested on a data set of 100,000 samples across two subsets of neuronal phenotypes and across a 400–700 nm wavelength range using multiple regression models. Wavelength grouped validation and locked test set were used in model evaluation. Using the full mechanistic feature set increased the locked-test coefficient of determination (:R²) from 0.012 for the data-only feature set to 0.035, and the RMSE and MAE for primary endpoint: percentage change in firing rate were 8.00 percentage points and 6.35 percentage points, respectively. The modest increase in predictive value from the mechanistic features suggests incremental value, but the modest (:R²) suggests that there was still significant variation in firing-rate modulation that wasn't predicted. Explainability analysis revealed that the most important predictive features were photo-modulation gain, biological optical dose, wavelength sensitivity, tissue scattering, and peak wavelength. Predictive performance was endpoint dependent; the modulation of membrane-potential was the best with (:R²) 0.388. Split-conformal calibration resulted in an empirical coverage of 90.2% for nominal 90% prediction intervals, whereas increasing the input noise resulted in a reduced performance of the model. In summary, the framework allows for an interpretable computational method to investigate neuronal responses across all wavelengths, to characterize endpoint-specific predictability and to assess uncertainty. It needs to be validated by independent experiments to determine its generalizability to real neuronal systems.

articles.title: Deposit-Architecture-Dependent Trade-Off Between High-Temperature Wear and Chloride Corrosion of Electroless Ni-P-B And Ni-P-B-W Coatings
articles.abstract: Electroless Ni-P-B (ENPB) and phosphorus-graded Ni-P-B-W (ENPBW) coatings were examined to determine how tungstate-induced changes in deposit architecture couple interfacial damage accommodation with electrochemical protection. Previously published as-deposited characteristics and room-temperature wear data were used only as referenced baselines. The present work combines post-sliding X-ray diffraction, reciprocating dry sliding at 300°C, static electrochemical testing, post-exposure microscopy, apparent water-contact-angle measurements, and comparative tribo-electrochemical testing in 3.5 wt. % NaCl. At 300°C, ENPBW reduced the mean coefficient of friction from 0.505 ± 0.10 to 0.415 ± 0.12 and the specific wear rate from 18.5 × 10− 5 to 13.9 × 10− 5 mm3 N− 1 m− 1 relative to ENPB. Static polarization produced the opposite ranking: ENPB exhibited Ecorr = -0.289 V versus Ag/AgCl and icorr = 0.0411 µA cm− 2, compared with − 0.342 V and 0.851 µA cm− 2 for ENPBW. During sliding in NaCl, ENPB also showed a smaller cathodic potential excursion and more complete post-sliding recovery. The opposing rankings reveal a bath- and architecture-dependent trade-off: hierarchical, chemically graded ENPBW better accommodated high-temperature sliding damage, whereas the finer and more uniformly covered ENPB surface provided the more favorable electrochemical response. Because the independent material-loss terms required by ASTM G119 were not measured, the tribo-electrochemical results constitute a comparative assessment rather than a quantitative wear-corrosion-synergy analysis.

articles.title: Diamond defects confirm 80-year-old theory of crystal stress
articles.abstract: For the first time, researchers in Japan have directly mapped several components of the stress field surrounding an atomic-scale flaw in the crystal structure of diamond. Led by Tokuyuki Teraji at Japan's National Institute for Materials Science, the team achieved its result using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, whose spin states respond differently to stress depending on how they are oriented relative to the stress field.

articles.title: One extra quantum dot helps balance speed and stability in spin qubits
articles.abstract: Quantum computers need qubits that can be controlled both quickly and reliably. Yet making semiconductor spin qubits faster often makes them more sensitive to electrical noise, creating a difficult trade-off.

articles.title: Supercurrent enables the reading of quantum information without destroying it
articles.abstract: One of the fundamental challenges of quantum computing is obtaining information from a quantum bit, or qubit. Unlike a conventional bit, which can be read repeatedly without altering its content, direct measurement of a quantum system typically causes the state to collapse before it can be determined. In other words, reading the information modifies it.

articles.title: Physics consistent conditional flow matching model as a plasma physics surrogate model
articles.abstract: Physics-informed surrogate modeling for steady-state systems often struggles with data scarcity and optimization instabilities from soft penalty losses. Unlike prevailing physics-informed generative methods that rely on explicit, differentiable PDE residuals during training, our framework targets systems where closed-form governing equations are unavailable or non-differentiable. We introduce a unified continuous-time conditional flow matching (CFM) framework for surrogate modeling and sparse data assimilation, evaluated on low-temperature plasma dynamics. By combining data-dependent interpolants with dynamic masking, our approach handles unconditioned prediction and missing-data imputation within a single architecture. We replace standard velocity matching with a direct state-prediction ( -prediction) objective, eliminating variance-induced sampling inefficiencies in deterministic regimes. For inference, the formulation supports both time-dependent ODE integration (CFM- ) and an autonomous regime (CFM- ) that enables measurement conditioning via anchor substitution. Global conservation laws are enforced via post-hoc geometric projections rather than loss regularizers. Results show that both CFM variants achieve superior accuracy, sample efficiency under data scarcity, and raw physical consistency over standard regressors. Furthermore, macroscopic constraints alone yield negligible reductions in test error, confirming the necessity of a data-driven generative prior over the physical manifold.
authors: José Afonso, Pedro Viegas, Rodrigo Ventura and Vasco Guerra

articles.title: Lattice Symmetry Remnants in Spatial and Temporal Entanglement of Quantum Critical Spin Chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum critical lattice models carry universal information beyond the bulk data of their infrared conformal field theory (CFT): microscopic lattice symmetries constrain how the CFT is realized. We probe these remnants through the spatial and temporal entanglement of two Euclidean-evolved states from the same critical model. In the finite-length scaling regime, a conformal boundary encodes the long-distance effect of the short-range initial state, and boundary CFT (BCFT) organizes the universal low-lying entanglement spectrum. We formulate the temporal state as a uniform infinite matrix product state evolved by a symmetry-preserving infinite matrix product operator, using a local factorization regular even at arbitrarily small Trotter steps. For the Ising and three-state Potts chains, whose relevant symmetries are onsite, the spatial and temporal constructions approach the same BCFT structure; varying the initial state engineers conformal boundaries distinguishable spectroscopically. The spin-1/2 XXZ chain instead realizes a Lieb--Schultz--Mattis (LSM) constraint between internal U(1) symmetry and one-site translation. A U(1)-preserving short-range spatial state accommodates it through a doubled unit cell and inequivalent entanglement cuts, whereas the temporal state remains uniform along Euclidean time. Successive spatial transfer steps pump the temporal entanglement spectrum between translation-related Dirichlet sectors, equivalently between integer and half-integer compact-boson zero modes. Breaking U(1) removes both the zero mode and the alternation. Continued evolution at fixed bond dimension crosses over from the finite-length BCFT regime to a finite-entanglement regime generated by symmetry-allowed relevant deformations. Thus microscopic symmetry and anomaly data remain visible in universal entanglement by constraining the boundary realization of the infrared CFT.

articles.title: Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range charge stripes and hence reflect the unconventional nature of superconductivity developing inside the charge-stripe state.
authors: Hongyu Li, Shuikang Yu, Huachen Rao, Zhuying Wang, Xingchen Zhou, Houpu Li, Yunmei Zhang, Zhao Gong, Xin Yu, Rui Wu, Tao Wu, Zhenyu Wang, Ziji Xiang, Xianhui Chen

articles.title: Bose-Einstein condensate in a shell: nonlinear modes and symmetry breaking
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The state of a quantum particle confined to a spherical surface is commonly described using spherical harmonics, which play a crucial role in solving many scientific problems featuring spherical symmetry. A mean-field description of a system of many interacting quantum particles confined to a spherical shell naturally leads to nonlinear generalizations of spherical harmonics. In this study, we analyze the emergence of such nonlinear modes in a shell-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with both repulsive and attractive two-particle interactions. We find several classes of nonlinear modes. The first kind is an analytical continuation of a single spherical harmonic or their superposition for nonvanishing atom-atom interaction. Some of these solutions have planar counterparts in the form of Townes solitons and Townes vortices, which either appear stable even in the case of attractive interactions or can be stabilized by three-particle interactions. The second kind originate from symmetry-breaking bifurcations in the case of a repulsive interaction, and therefore have no linear counterparts. Moreover, we demonstrate the existence of a breathing dynamics that oscillates primarily between an unstable soliton and a stable vortex necklace state. Our findings show that the physics of nonlinear matter waves on curved geometries differs substantially from that in planar systems, suggesting the feasibility of observing these unconventional wave patterns experimentally.
authors: Alexander Wolf, Vladimir V. Konotop, Maxim A. Efremov

articles.title: Existence and Absence of Spin-Glass Phases on Migdal--Kadanoff Hierarchical Lattices: A Complete Classification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Ising spin-glass model on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices, characterized by the fractal dimension d=1+łog s/łog b, where s and b denote the number of parallel branches and the number of bonds in series within each branch, respectively. For independent Gaussian couplings, we rigorously establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for arbitrary integers b,sge2. We prove that a finite-temperature spin-glass phase exists whenever [ fracbsqrts łeft( fracbsqrts(s-1)bs-1 i̊ght)s⁻¹<1. ] In particular, this condition holds for all three-dimensional MK hierarchical lattices (d=3, or equivalently s=b²⁾, regardless of the choice of b. Conversely, we prove the absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for fractal dimensions d<1+łog17/łog6approx2.58, as well as in the large-b limit for any fixed d<3. In the intermediate regime 1+łog17/łog6łe d<3, we provide a finite-step procedure to determine the presence or absence of spin-glass order, which depends on b and s. Our results provide a complete characterization of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices.

articles.title: Flexo-Photoresponses from First Principles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many functionally important materials, such as silicon, possess high-symmetry crystal structures that forbid even-order nonlinear optical responses, thereby limiting their application in e.g., photonics and optoelectronics. Strain gradients can effectively break symmetries, activating otherwise forbidden optical responses. Although such flexo-photoresponses have attracted considerable interest recently, a comprehensive microscopic theoretical framework is still lacking. Here, we develop a first-principles approach that can systematically evaluate a wide range of flexo-photoresponses in realistic materials. By mapping strain gradients to long-wavelength phonons within the established theory of electron-phonon coupling, our approach captures the nonlocal quantum-mechanical effects of lattice deformations on nonlinear optical responses. Applying the framework to prototypical centrosymmetric materials, including Si, cubic m̊ SrTiO₃, and monolayer black phosphorus, we demonstrate that a strain gradients of 10⁵sim10⁶~m̊ m⁻¹ can induce flexo-second-harmonic generation and flexo-bulk photovoltaic effects comparable to the intrinsic responses of non-centrosymmetric crystals. Our work establishes a rigorous foundation for strain gradient engineering of light-matter interactions, opening new avenues for nanoscale optomechanics, optoelectronics, and beyond.
authors: Zhichao Guo, Hua Wang, Haowei Xu

articles.title: Strain-tunable van Hove singularity and superconducting dome in monolayer kagome metal CsTi₃Bi₅
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recently discovered titanium-based kagome metal CsTi₃Bi₅, which exhibits superconductivity without an accompanying charge density wave, provides an ideal platform to investigate the intrinsic electronic structure and superconductivity. Moreover, it enables the exploration of superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit of the kagome lattice. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of biaxial mechanical strain (ǎrepsilon) on the electronic structure and superconductivity of monolayer CsTi₃Bi₅ using first-principles calculations. We demonstrate that the prominent van Hove singularity (VHS) at the M point can be monotonically tuned to the Fermi level by tensile strain. Furthermore, the superconducting transition temperature T_C exhibits a dome-shaped dependence on strain, reaching a maximum of 3.6 K at an optimal tensile strain of ǎrepsilon=+2%. The average superconducting gap magnitude is 0.35 meV, with an orbital-dependent and anisotropic distribution. Our results provide a detailed understanding of the superconductivity of monolayer CsTi₃Bi₅ and show that strain is an effective, continuous tuning knob for manipulating the electronic structure and superconductivity.
authors: Run Lv, Wenqian Tu, Dingfu Shao, Yuping Sun, Wenjian Lu

articles.title: Electronic structure of a persistent excitonic fluid far beyond the Mott limit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Excitons are conventionally expected to destabilize at high photoexcitation densities, as screening weakens the electron-hole attraction. Recent studies, however, challenge this paradigm, suggesting that excitons generated by strong optical pumping can remain stable even beyond the onset of population inversion. Here, using time- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy on 2D hybrid perovskites, we provide direct evidence for such a high-density excitonic state, characterized by a distinctive Mexican-hat dispersion. Remarkably, this excitonic band reconstruction endures for orders of magnitude longer than the optical coherence time, revealing a population-sustained electronic structure that survives well into the incoherent regime. The excitonic resonance also persists far beyond optical saturation, at densities where exciton wavefunctions strongly overlap. Our findings reveal a long-lived, high-density quantum fluid of excitons with characteristics reminiscent of a BCS condensate, an electronic structure markedly different from that of the dilute limit.
authors: Weiyan Qi, Stefano Ponzoni, Ashim Pramanik, Vitaly Gorelov, Yannis Laplace, Gianluca Stefanucci, Enrico Perfetto, Esteban Morcos, Marino Marsi, Steven Francis Udaundo, Sebastian Maherlein, Amina Taleb-Ibrahimi, Kaibo Zheng, Tonu Pullerits, Luca Perfetti

articles.title: Interplay of Chemical Disorder, Vortex Pinning, and Electron Correlations in the Mechanically Robust Medium-Entropy Alloy Superconductor Nb₀.₄₅Ta₀.₂₅Ti₀.₁₅Hf₀.₁₅
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medium and high-entropy alloys have emerged as a promising class of superconducting materials because their intrinsic chemical disorder can simultaneously enhance mechanical robustness and modify superconducting properties. Here, we present a combined experimental and first-principles investigation of the structural, superconducting, electronic, and local lattice-distortion characteristics of the mechanically robust medium-entropy alloy Nb₀.₄₅Ta₀.₂₅Ti₀.₁₅Hf₀.₁₅. The material shows type-II superconductivity with a transition temperature T_Coⁿset approx 7.8 ~K. A high critical current density of J_c = 0.48 × 10⁶~A/cm² is observed, and this is attributed to strong vortex pinning at grain boundaries. Specific-heat analysis indicates a strong electron-phonon coupling (łambda = 1.07) with a large isotropic s-wave superconducting gap. Density functional theory calculations explicitly model the intrinsic chemical disorder, predict a stable body-centered cubic phase. These calculations further reveal a metallic electronic structure with substantial Ti- and Ta-derived states at the Fermi level. Additionally, our results quantify a pronounced disorder-induced local lattice distortion (Δ d = 0.086 A), providing a microscopic basis for the experimentally observed enhanced vortex-pinning landscape. Remarkably, the alloy also exhibits an unusually large Kadowaki-Woods ratio, placing it close to the heavy-fermion regime and indicating enhanced electronic correlations beyond conventional alloy superconductors. Our results demonstrate that entropy-engineered chemical disorder can stabilize robust superconductivity, promote strong flux pinning, and induce correlated electronic behavior, establishing refractory medium-entropy alloys as a promising platform for next-generation superconducting materials.
authors: Pooja Chourasia, Samiul Sk, Nikita Sharma, B. Vignolle, Abhishek Sarkar, Olivier Toulemonde, Sanjoy Mahatha, S. K. Panda, Sourav Marik

articles.title: Effect of oxygen plasma treatment on the structural and superconducting properties of atomic-layer-deposited NbN thin films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface oxidation is a common concern for ultrathin NbN superconducting devices, yet which superconducting properties it affects has not been established for films grown by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. We expose NbN films about 11.4 nm thick to an O₂ plasma for 0 to 60 s, which oxidizes the surface without etching the film, and characterize the same sample series by X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and transport measurements on 500 nm wide nanowires. XPS of the surface and the underlying layer shows that the plasma converts the surface to Nb₂O₅, whereas the bulk of the treated film is chemically identical to that of the untreated film. Crystalline δ-NbN remains intact. During exposure, the total film thickness rises and saturates between 40 and 60 s, indicating self-limiting surface oxide growth. The normal-state resistivity rises by 21% (dc) and 25% (optical) with the plasma dose, while the critical temperature and transition width are unchanged. The switching current densities of 4.9-6.2 MA/cm² at 4.2 K show no systematic dependence on the plasma dose. Their temperature dependence follows the dirty-limit depairing current of Kupriyanov and Lukichev, and the extrapolated switching currents reach 39-46% of the depairing current calculated from the optical resistivity and diffusion coefficient, in agreement with the width dependence reported for nanowires from the same process. The oxygen signature is confined to temperatures near T_c, where the supercurrent of the treated wires vanishes at least 0.5 K earlier than that of the untreated wire, consistent with a partially oxidized surface layer that acts on the film by the proximity effect. At these doses, oxygen narrows the temperature range of the supercurrent from above but does not systematically reduce the low-temperature current-carrying capacity of the wires.
authors: Nitesh Yerra, Mustafa Teke, Felix Otto, Marco Diegel, Detlef Born, Uwe Hübner, Nan Du, Mario Ziegler, Sahitya Varma Vegesna, Heidemarie Krüger

articles.title: Nano-ARPES observation of a flat band at the barM point in 2.4deg twisted bilayer graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at the so-called magic angle reveals a range of intriguing phases, such as superconductivity and Mott insulating states, resulting from electrons entering a correlated state. This establishes twisted bilayer graphene as an excellent platform for exploring correlation effects in many-body phases and across various twist angles. However, in most cases, the twist angle is not an easy parameter to control because it exhibits structural instabilities such as relaxation and reconstruction that reduce the correlation effects. Here, we report the unexpected appearance of a flat band at the barM point far from the Fermi level in a 2.4deg twisted bilayer graphene, directly visualized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. Our work is the first observation of flat bands away from the barK point in twisted bilayer graphene and highlights the need to probe the entire Brillouin zone to fully capture electronic states in twisted structures.
authors: Giovanna Feraco, Przemysław Przybysz, Oreste De Luca, Ying Wang, Pavel Dudin, José Avila, Jianting Ye, Paweł Dkabrowski, Paweł J. Kowalczyk, Jagoda Sławińska, Petra Rudolf, Antonija Grubišić-Čabo

articles.title: Spontaneous Decay of High Energy Composite Fermions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An electron, when added to a fractional quantum Hall fluid, famously splits into fractionally charged composite-fermion quasiparticles. We show here that a high energy composite fermion carrying a fractional charge decays into a collection of particles, including quasiparticles, quasiholes, and even whole electrons.

articles.title: Majorana Edge-to-bound State Transition in Interferometric Superconductor Rings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manipulating flux quanta in topological superconductors is central to vortex braiding in quantum computing. Their interferometric superconducting rings can host either topologically protected edge states with fluxes confined inside the central hollow area or vortex bound states in flux cores at the annulus walls. Here we demonstrate a strategy to drive topological edge states into vortex bound states by tuning the relative scale of vortex size and annulus width in nano-ring interferometric device on 2M-WS₂ topological superconductor. Near its superconducting transition where the coherence length exceeds the annulus width, Little-Parks oscillations exhibit expected periods for flux bundles in ring-center, consistent with edge states residing at inner and outer rims of the annulus. Upon cooling, where the coherence length shrinks below the annulus width, the unexpectedly increased oscillation period reflects multiple fluxes distributed along annulus region in flux necklace configuration, implying a transition from extended edge states to localized vortex bound states. Ginzburg-Landau simulations and local density-of-states calculations with Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations reveal that large values for both Ginzburg-Landau parameter and flux-pinning energy are vital for such a transition. Our findings provide a novel strategy for understanding flux manipulation towards flux braiding and topological quantum computing.
authors: Xiangyu Bi, Aoshen Yang, Hongzi Cao, Ganyu Chen, Yuqiang Fang, Zeya Li, Qizheng Sun, Junwei Huang, Da Wang, Fuqiang Huang, Toshiya Ideue, Qianghua Wang, Yoshihiro Iwasa, Hongtao Yuan

articles.title: Finite-Temperature Transconductance of Multiterminal Josephson Junctions with Topological Andreev Spectra
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.
authors: Gleb S. Seleznev, David C. Ohnmacht, Wolfgang Belzig

articles.title: Non-singlets and the phase diagram of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantum mechanics of one N× N Hermitian matrix in the infinite N limit is well known to define a two-dimensional string theory when the quartic coupling constant g is tuned to a special negative value g_*. We study the thermodynamics of this Matrix Quantum Mechanics (MQM), treating the SU(N) symmetry as a global symmetry. Crucially, the non-singlets, i.e. states in non-trivial representations of SU(N), implement the effects of vortices on the discretized worldsheets. This random lattice model has the low-temperature c=1 and high-temperature c=0 phases, with the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition separating them. We map out the phase diagram in the coupling--temperature plane, which is separated by the critical stability curve T_c(g) extending from g_*< g <0. We study this curve using the non-perturbative matrix bootstrap and low- and high-temperature perturbation theory, which explain the thermal instability. At low temperatures, thermally excited non-singlets backreact on the Fermi sea of matrix eigenvalues, causing it to spill over. At high temperatures, the theory is described by an effective matrix integral obtained by dimensional reduction on the thermal circle; the eigenvalue distribution of the zero mode becomes unstable at the critical coupling. We conjecture that the BKT transition occurs at a special point on the critical curve and estimate its position. Finally, we switch to the regular square lattice and study the MQM-inspired Villain model, where the link factor is the one-dimensional propagator on a circle. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we map out the BKT transition in this model.
authors: Igor R. Klebanov, Henry W. Lin, Pavel Meshcheriakov, Jessica Yeh

articles.title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) is conventionally used to probe elementary excitations and correlations in quantum materials. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material. An incident X-ray photon is coherently split by a beam splitter into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends. This protocol is the X-ray, solid-state analogue of the Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller (DLCZ) heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states. We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. (2) An open tight-binding chain exhibits reflection-parity-dependent interference, providing a benchmark for the interferometer's coherence. (3) A spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain yields an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. We also discuss practical considerations and challenges for realizing the protocol in X-ray experiments.
authors: Chunjing Jia, Valentin Walther, Laimei Nie

articles.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32973v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.
authors: François Gay-Balmaz, Tudor S. Ratiu, Cesare Tronci

articles.title: Kagome goldene with flat bands and Dirac nodal line fermions via line-graph epitaxy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2503.07945v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The kagome lattice has emerged as a promising platform for investigating exotic quantum phases. However, achieving a single-atomic-layer kagome lattice in elemental materials remains a significant challenge. Here, we introduce line-graph epitaxy, a novel approach that enables the atomic-scale synthesis of goldene, a monolayer of elemental gold atoms arranged in a kagome lattice. Through scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate the formation of kagome goldene, featuring a flat band with a van Hove singularity approximately 1.1 eV below the Fermi level, signaling strong electron correlation effects. Notably, the flat band is disrupted at the zigzag edges of goldene nanoflakes, revealing substantial edge effects. Furthermore, our calculations show that weak interlayer interactions between goldene and the underlying Au2Ge substrate generate dual Dirac nodal lines through a proximity effect. These findings offer not only a novel strategy for constructing elemental kagome lattices, but also a generalizable framework for fabricating and controlling line-graph materials. This research advances the exploration of quantum phases driven by strong correlations and the design of materials for next-generation quantum technologies.
authors: Qiwei Tian, Sahar Izadi Vishkayi, Chen Zhang, Jiang Zeng, Bo Li, Li Zhang, Long-Jing Yin, Yuan Tian, Meysam Bagheri Tagani, Lijie Zhang, Zhihui Qin

articles.title: Resonant dielectric amplification of superconductivity at the FeSe:SrTiOT₃ interface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.09063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Epitaxial monolayers of FeSe grown on SrTiO₃ (STO) and related polar substrates exhibit superconducting transition temperatures of 65-70 K, far above the ~8 K value of bulk FeSe. Although coupling to interfacial Fuchs-Kliewer (FK) phonons is widely believed to contribute to this enhancement, the apparent universality of high=T_c superconductivity across polar interfaces presents a striking puzzle. Here, we identify the lower-energy FK mode near 59 meV, associated with the bulk longitudinal optical resonance of STO, as a conduit through which the substrate dielectric response enhances pairing in FeSe. Within a phenomenological Migdal-Eliashberg framework, incorporating the measured dielectric response of STO selectively amplifies the pairing interaction near this resonance and raises the theoretical upper bound of T_c into the experimentally observed range. A similar enhancement is reproduced for FeSe on BaTiO₃, while related polar substrates such as TiO₂, LaFeO₃, and EuTiO3 possess the same key electrodynamic ingredients. We refer to this effect as resonant anti-shielding (RAS). More broadly, RAS identifies the bulk electrodynamic response of the substrate as a pairing amplifier, opening a route toward designing superconducting heterostructures through control of their dielectric environment.
authors: Krzysztof Kempa, Michael J. Naughton, Hanno H. Weitering

articles.title: Unifying description of competing chiral and nematic superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.06550v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We reveal a striking correspondence between electron- and phonon-driven pairing in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) by mapping an atomistic electronically driven pairing model onto an effective inter-valley, intra-Chern description, originally proposed for phonon-mediated superconductivity. Within the unified framework of intra-Chern pairing, we then analyze the competition between nematic and chiral d-wave superconducting states. The latter corresponds to the extreme Chern-polarized limit and hosts unpaired flat bands within the superconducting gap, which generally disfavors it relative to the nematic states. Crucially, nematic order is locally preferred at each momentum, but the optimal nematic directions are incompatible across the Brillouin zone due to the broken rotation symmetry. This momentum-space frustration still enables a chiral ground state at large fillings or weak interactions in a symmetric parent state. Including heterostrain or inter-valley coherence further stabilizes the nematic ground state and sets the nematic direction. Under heterostrain, this direction shows a double winding with the strain axis, revealing the d-wave nature of the pairing, while inter-valley coherence makes it filling dependent. Our results thereby provide a unified understanding of superconductivity in TBG, in which electron- and phonon-mediated pairing cooperate, and clarify the microscopic origin of the competition between the chiral and nematic superconducting states.
authors: Lucas Baldo, Patric Holmvall, Annica M. Black-Schaffer

articles.title: Freezing and Shielding under Global Quenches for Long-Range Interacting Many-Body Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2407.06072v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate how local perturbations spread on long-range interacting spin chains and show how their nonequilibrium behavior exactly matches the one of a Fermi-Hubbard model with long-range hoppings. We then focus on the thermalization of the fermionic model following a sudden quench of local interactions between two distinct fermionic species. For both models, the quasiparticle spectrum consists of gapped low-energy levels, while the high-energy ones accumulate at a single point. When the low-energy gaps are large enough, turning on the local interactions does not effectively mix high- and low-energy modes, resulting in a freezing of the dynamical evolution. In general, the states within the excited subspace are shielded from the long-range signatures of the model, which are responsible for the low-energy extended states, and the dynamics effectively look as if long-range couplings were absent. This shielding mechanism becomes evident in the presence of disorder. It is shown that shielding and freezing are a universal feature of long-range interacting systems, and their relation to the existence of quasistationary states is conjectured.

articles.title: Succession of Ising criticality and its threshold in critical quantum Ising model subject to X+ZZ decoherence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.17871v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a mixed state quantum criticality in the Ising model under X+ZZ decoherence. In the doubled Hilbert space formalism, the decohered state resides on the self-dual critical line of the quantum Ashkin-Teller (qAT) model, as a result of the specific choice of the decoherence channel. On the other hand, since the mixed state under X+ZZ decoherence satisfies the Kramers-Wannier self-duality in a weak sense, the Ising criticality of the pure state can be partially preserved in the mixed system. By making use of the combination of the doubled Hilbert space formalism and matrix product states, a numerical study is carried out. We numerically find that, up to moderate decoherence strength, the behavior of the mixed states on the critical line is consistent with Ising-like scaling within the accessible system sizes, with the effective central charge and critical exponents close to the Ising-CFT values c=1/2, η=1/4, and η_X=2. Our results of the central charge and critical exponents contradict the ones in the c=1 orbifold boson CFT describing the critical state of the qAT model. In addition, we also numerically observe the flow of the central charge up to strong decoherence. The strong decoherence washes out the remnant Ising criticality and induces strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking.
authors: Yoshihito Kuno, Takahiro Orito, Ikuo Ichinose

articles.title: Eigenstate condensation in quantum systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.18869v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Random quantum states drawn from the Haar ensemble with a constraint on the energy expectation value Eₐᵥ = łangle ψ | H | ψångle display eigenstate condensation: for Eₐᵥ below a critical value E_c, they develop macroscopic overlap with the ground state. We study eigenstate condensation in systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. These systems display three phases: a ground-state phase, in which energy-constrained random states have macroscopic overlap with the ground state; a high-temperature phase, in which they have exponentially small overlap with each energy eigenstate; and an anti-ground-state phase, in which they have macroscopic overlap with the most highly excited state. In local spin systems the ground-state and anti-ground-state phases approach the middle of the spectrum as 1/[system size], but -- because the condensation phase transitions have exponential, rather than polynomial, finite-size scaling -- the crossover becomes exponentially sharp in system size and the high-temperature phase is best understood as an extended phase.
authors: Christopher David White, Michael Winer, Noam Bernstein

articles.title: Multiport photonic routing with a single cavity-based electro-optic phase shifter per port
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Programmable photonic meshes can perform general linear transformations, but universal transformations on N modes require O(N²⁾ programmable phase shifters, which cannot simultaneously achieve low drive voltage, gigahertz speed, zero static power, lossless modulation, and a compact footprint. Signal routing does not require universal transformations, which allows considerable circuit simplifications. We present a compact reflective circuit architecture that connects all input-output pairs across N modes in N steps using only O(N) programmable phase shifters. The circuit comprises a single passive N× N interferometer and a single column of programmable reflective phase shifters. We demonstrate the architecture by implementing a 3× 3 router in x-cut thin-film lithium niobate with a passive multimode interferometer and phase shifters based on single-sided photonic-crystal nanobeam cavities. Our programmable devices exhibit a 1.92 GHz/V resonance tuning efficiency via the Pockels effect, a footprint of 100,μm², sub-5-V drive voltage, and a 6.2 GHz electro-optic bandwidth. Through voltage-space characterization and physical modeling, we identify routing states with extinction ratios exceeding 11 dB at each output and demonstrate sequential routing at an equipment-limited speed of 10 MHz. Our results establish cavity-enhanced Pockels switching as a routing layer for classical and quantum computing interconnects across visible and near-infrared wavelengths.
authors: Alessandro Buzzi, Bjarke A. Frederiksen, Dashiell L. P. Vitullo, Mikkel Heuck, Dirk R. Englund

articles.title: Photoelectrons resolve the phase-dependent variance of bright squeezed vacuum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The variance of bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) is not only strong but also phase dependent, yet recent strong-field experiments with BSV have recorded only its magnitude. A coherent field of the same color provides the phase reference that resolves this phase-dependent noise. Strong-field ionization of xenon by this light shows that the photoelectron yield follows the BSV quadrature along the coherent field, and that the nonlinearity of ionization amplifies the quadrature noise many times over in the electron yield. The noise is moreover distributed unevenly over the photoelectron momentum distribution, differing by an order of magnitude between ionization channels. Strong-field ionization thus offers a phase-sensitive, channel-resolved detector of quantum light, while the quadrature noise of quantum light offers a probe of the intensity dependence of individual ionization pathways.
authors: Haoran Ma, Yihe Wang, Chuan Cheng, Ian Gabalski, Aaron M. Ghrist, Eleanor Weckwerth, Mohammed Th. Hassan, Philip H. Bucksbaum

articles.title: Zero photoemission from icosahedral superatoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoemission is expected to occur when the photon energy exceeds the binding energy of an electron, with the photoemission yield generally remaining non-zero above this threshold. Yet, it can be suppressed at specific photon energies, a phenomenon known as the Cooper minimum. Although complete suppression represents an extreme limit of this phenomenon, such zero photoemission has previously been reported only for atoms with an outermost s-type orbital and has never been observed in non-atomic systems. Here, we demonstrate the deliberate realization of zero photoemission from Ag12W-, an artificial icosahedral superatom, by observing a vanishing photoemission cross section 0.85 eV above the detachment threshold and reproducing this behavior in theoretical simulations. These simulations predict that zero photoemission can be common in nearly spherical nanoclusters, a prediction we experimentally confirm using Ag12Mo-, an isoelectronic counterpart of Ag12W-. Because superatoms offer systematic control over both size and elemental composition using the periodic table, our findings establish a route toward active control of photoemission in finite-size quantum systems and stimulate further investigations of underexplored physical phenomena such as nondipole effects.
authors: Yuta Suzuki, Mamoru Tanaka, Yoshi-ichi Suzuki, Akira Terasaki, Takuya Horio

articles.title: Heat vortices and the vorticity triplet in kinetic phonon transport: a fluid-dynamical perspective
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From a novel fluid-dynamical perspective, the present study investigates the heat-current vortices and heat vorticity in heat conduction process of solid materials. The heat vorticity bmømega, defined as the curl of the heat-flux field, is decomposed into the orbital-rotation bmR and spin bmS, which collectively constitute the heat-vorticity triplet (bmR,bmS,bmømega), extending beyond the existing single-vorticity research paradigm. As an illustrative example, kinetic phonon transport in a 2D porous solid structure is examined based on the numerical solutions of the Peierls-Boltzmann equation under the Callway dual-relaxation-time approximation. The physical characteristics of heat vortices and the vorticity triplet patterns are analyzed across different kinetic regimes in the phase diagram of the normal (N) and resistive (R) scattering processes.... In the hydrodynamic limit, the boundary generation mechanism of heat vorticity is further elucidated based on the Guyer-Krumhansl (G-K) equation generated from the truncated Chapman-Enskog (C-E) expansion. The boundary heat vorticity flux (BHVF) is proposed as a new concept for describing the local rate at which heat vorticity is generated at the boundary of a solid material. The general expression for the BHVF is rigorously derived for phonon hydrodynamics, and for the 2D steady hydrodynamic phonon transport case, we find that the BHVF is solely attributed to the tangential component of the net heat flux deviating from the classical Fourier heat flux. Furthermore, we show that the total vorticity contained in a control volume arises from the spatiotemporal accumulation of the BHVF, weighted by the memory kernel arising from the R scattering. The proposed theory and findings herein could be valuable for understanding the diverse vortical-flow phenomena in condensed matter systems.
authors: Tao Chen, Chuang Zhang, Tianshu Liu

articles.title: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. Due to the geometry of the laser beams, the generalized Hahn echo also realizes a three-path Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometer with two independent interferometric phase differences. Our results therefore establish SU(3) control for dynamical decoupling of qutrits and multi-path atom interferometers, with the latter opening the possibility for vector force measurements and interferometric tests of the validity of Born's rule.
authors: Chirantan Mitra, Lucas Gabardos, François Impens, David Guéry-Odelin, David Wilkowski, Chang Chi Kwong

articles.title: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two SI10m̆-long devices with widths of SI3.2m̆ and SI6.4m̆ are characterized under pulsed SI515nm excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to (n=8). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to (n=7) and (n=8), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is (2.15), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of (99.6%). The EMG exponential-tail parameter (τₙ) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter (μₙ) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.
authors: Hsin-Yeh Wu, Shu-Xiao Liu, Boris Tuchming, Xavier-François Navick, Pu-Kai Wang, Yi-Ren Wu, Jia-Wern Chen, Marc Besançon, Jean-François Glicenstein, Pisin Chen, Yu-Jung Lu, Stathes Paganis

articles.title: High Resolution Hyperspectral Quantum Infrared Imaging with Undetected Photons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum sensing in the infrared regime often demands the use of expensive and cryogenically operated detectors. Nonlinear interferometry has paved the way for information transfer from the infrared to the near--infrared or visible regime in various quantum technologies. A particularly interesting application of these interferometers involves spectrally--resolved quantum imaging using undetected photons, enabled by the use of temperature--tunable parametric amplifiers. In this work, we demonstrate spectrally resolved transmission imaging with undetected photons around 1550 nm using a spontaneous parametric down conversion based folded nonlinear interferometric scheme, registering the attenuation of a zebrafish larva as a biological feasibility test. We characterize and calibrate the interferometer, having achieved spectrally resolved interference fringes with a maximum baseline visibility of sim 74% in the near--infrared regime. Phase--stepped readout of a grating spectrometer gives a resolving power of sim1460 (from the spectrometer's point spread function) at 1550 nm, and sim 730 from the coherence length, the finest reported for imaging with undetected photons, over an instantaneous spectral window of approx 51 cm⁻¹.
authors: Aadi Suketu Bharatia, Vidya Prakash Muppalla, Ananya Asthana, Priyanka Kandankel, Tanmoy Chakraborty, Sreelaja Nair, Anshuman Kumar

articles.title: QuantumBilliards.jl: An extensible, user friendly, high-performance Julia library for the large scale computation of spectra and eigenstates of quantum billiards and related problems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present QuantumBilliards.jl, an open-source Julia library providing a suite of numerical solvers for the two-dimensional interior Helmholtz eigenproblem with Dirichlet boundary conditions, a paradigmatic model in quantum chaos. The library implements conventional wavenumber-sweep techniques together with several accelerated eigensolvers: the Vergini--Saraceno scaling method, the expanded boundary integral method (EBIM), Beyn's contour-integral method, and the Compact Rational Krylov (CORK) method. It provides a common framework for constructing billiard geometries, exploiting discrete symmetries, computing eigenvalues and eigenstates, and treating smooth, cornered, and multiply connected domains. The library further includes reconstruction of eigenfunctions from boundary normal derivatives and the computation of Poincaré--Husimi (PH) phase-space representations. Available at: https://github.com/Quantum-Chaos-Julia/QuantumBilliards.jl.

articles.title: Quantum-Classical Link Prediction on Dark Web Hyperlink Graphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze HTML content and hyperlinks from an offline Tor crawl containing 383 onion hosts and 2,067 directed cross-host links. The study combines semantic analysis with degree-controlled quantum--classical link prediction. Two directory groups emit 94.8% of the observed host links. Directed preferential attachment reaches ROC-AUC 0.976 with random non-edges, but falls to 0.550±0.014 under source-conditioned target-degree matching. With disjoint training and test pairs, multimodal logistic regression reaches 0.672±0.021, GAE 0.899±0.016, and VGAE 0.906±0.016. A four-qubit variational quantum classifier (VQC) comparison tests two encodings across 20 disjoint-pair graph splits under exact and 1,024-shot simulation, with classical controls using the same inputs and training examples. Its best exact mean ROC-AUC is 0.549±0.023, compared with 0.551±0.016 for RBF SVC and 0.573±0.029 for a 16-parameter MLP on the same inputs and training examples. These results support predictive signal in combined graph/content features and show why degree control, feature compression, and optimization conditions matter in quantum--classical comparisons.
authors: Vojtěch Novák, Radovan Rečka, Ondřej Knebl, Aktham Youssef, Ivan Zelinka

articles.title: Receiver-Limited Fisher Information for Quantum Sensors under Realistic Readout
articles.abstract: Quantum Fisher information quantifies the sensitivity encoded in a parameter-dependent quantum state, whereas the performance of a practical sensor is limited by the information that survives the physical channel and can be extracted by the available receiver. We introduce an accessible Fisher-information framework based on a physically admissible family of measurements and use it to separate state-level sensitivity, channel degradation, and receiver limitations. The framework is applied to Ramsey and NOON interferometry, squeezed-state displacement sensing, two-level thermometry, and multiparameter qubit sensing. We show that resource normalization, finite visibility, readout errors, measurement rank, shot allocation, calibration uncertainty, and nuisance parameters can substantially modify the experimentally available advantage. For squeezed-state sensing, homodyne-axis misalignment produces a finite optimal squeezing, while bounded calibration uncertainty leads to a robust operating rule. In the pure-loss model considered here, attenuation reduces the attainable information without shifting this optimum. The results provide practical design rules that connect quantum-enhanced state preparation with realistic measurement constraints and experimentally extractable sensing performance.

articles.title: Finite Local Information Capacity in Continuum Dynamics
articles.abstract: Finite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces are widely used as microscopic regulators and have also been proposed as a fundamental information-capacity property of space-time. A finite local dimension, however, is not equivalent to a spatial lattice spacing, and neither is equivalent to a coarse-graining scale. We formulate a regulator-resolved framework that keeps these three notions separate and defines finite-information deviations operationally as the failure of microscopic and effective time evolution to commute with a specified coarse-graining channel. The resulting deviation is a state- and observable-dependent quantity in a common effective state space, rather than a formal subtraction of generators acting on different domains. We derive a decomposition into capacity, spatial-discretization, and coarse-graining contributions; a finite-time capacity bound controlled by discarded state weight and leakage through the cutoff boundary; observable error bounds; and a sharp continuity bound for subsystem entropies. We further show that block entropy and averaged one-cell entropy differ by a relative-entropy measure of total correlation and therefore cannot be interchanged. An information-geometric expansion of neighboring reduced states yields a nonlinear sigma-model effective action on the manifold of coarse-grained states. A single entropy field follows only under an additional one-dimensional closure condition. Finally, we test the framework in an exactly evolved periodic Klein--Gordon chain with independently variable lattice spacing and local number-state cutoff. Spectral peaks are extracted from dynamical matrix elements rather than imposed. Ground-state, dispersion, reduced-state, and entropy errors converge rapidly with local capacity, while the remaining lattice--continuum discrepancy persists at fixed spacing. The results provide a controlled mathematical and numerical foundation for finite-information models without claiming a unique microscopic theory of quantum gravity.

articles.title: Quantum Entanglement Optimization and Prototype Design in Positronic Simulation Frameworks
articles.abstract: We present a simulation-driven framework for optimizing quantum entanglement in engineered positronic substrates. Using high-resolution parameter sweeps of a coupling coefficient g and ensemble time-domain traces, we identify a reproducible global entanglement maximum at g ≈ 32.786 and robust secondary plateau regions near g≈60 and g≈100. We quantify entanglement using concurrence-like measures and present a prototype architecture that implements adaptive feedback to maintain maximal entanglement under dynamic perturbations. The archive includes full simulation code, figure-generation scripts and prototype design notes to enable reproducible experimental follow-up.

articles.title: Navigating the BERMUDA triangle of scientific software: A modular approach to data, hardware, and algorithm design in quantum chemistry and its realization in Python
articles.abstract: Modern quantum-chemistry software must support increasingly complex methods, heterogeneous hardware, reusable data structures, and user-facing workflows without losing maintainability. Using PyBEST as a case study, this work discusses how such complexity can be organized within the Python programming language through modular interfaces rather than scattered across method-specific implementations. The central motif is the B alanced pythonic E nvironment for R esearch with M odular U nified D esign and A bstractions (BERMUDA) Triangle : data representation, computational execution, and algorithmic organization, showcasing how implemented components and ongoing architectural developments—including backend-independent tensor contractions, an effective-Hamiltonian infrastructure, a domain-aware linear-algebra layer, the DAISpY charge-transfer analysis, and graphical input preparation—can be organized within one coherent ecosystem. The resulting perspective treats scalability not only as a numerical goal, but also as a software-design property: scientific codes remain sustainable when new features can be added without obscuring the route from theory to implementation and interpretation.

articles.title: Casimir force screening by a quantum Boltzmann plasma
articles.abstract: We develop a finite-temperature field-theoretical description of the Casimir interaction between two perfectly conducting boundaries with the intervening gap filled by a two-component quantum Boltzmann plasma embedded in a homogeneous dielectric background. The quantum motion of the charged particles is represented by imaginary-time worldlines, while the electromagnetic field is treated in the Gaussian approximation. The resulting partition function contains distinct longitudinal and transverse response contributions and an additional quantum-induced source term with no classical counterpart. In the classical limit, the theory reduces to the usual Casimir-screening picture: the static longitudinal mode is Debye screened, whereas the transverse electromagnetic sector is unaffected by classical mobile charges. Finite thermal de Broglie wavelengths modify the nonzero Matsubara response and produce the leading quantum correction to the force. In the static long-wavelength limit, the longitudinal dielectric function has, through the leading quantum correction, the same expansion structure as the Lindhard response of a degenerate electron gas under the correspondence k TF ↔ κ D and kF↔λdB−1. In contrast, the static transverse response reproduces the leading high-temperature Landau orbital diamagnetic susceptibility. We investigate the crossover between classical and quantum plasma behavior in a regime where these corrections become appreciable while the plasma remains approximately nondegenerate and can still be treated, at leading order, within Maxwell–Boltzmann statistics. We illustrate this crossover for a weakly coupled electron–proton plasma and an effective Li + –solvated-electron plasma in liquid ammonia. The latter yields a sub-percent quantum correction to the force gradient for the parameters considered.

articles.title: Semiclassical initial value representation in curvilinear coordinates
articles.abstract: A semiclassical propagator originally defined on Euclidean space is systematically extended to general curvilinear coordinate systems. This method time-evolves nuclear wave packets on the fly in curvilinear coordinates, without prior construction of global potential energy surfaces or complicated kinetic energy operators, and enables dimensionality reduction by isolating the physically essential degrees of freedom through coordinate constraints. By propagating the dynamics in a redundant coordinate space, the coordinate singularities inherent to curvilinear systems are circumvented in a numerically robust manner. In addition, the topology of each coordinate—such as its periodicity and boundary conditions—is properly taken into account by modifying the coherent state basis of the propagator. We applied this approach to molecular motions that are difficult to describe in conventional normal coordinates—pure rotation of hydrogen and methane, rovibrational dynamics of hydrogen, and large-amplitude torsional motion of butane—and reproduced reference eigenenergies and the characteristic features of the corresponding spectra.
