articles.title: Dataset merging strategy for efficient construction of a machine-learning force field: A case of CeO 2 surfaces with an oxygen vacancy
articles.abstract: The accuracy and transferability of machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) critically depend on the quality of the training database. Here, we propose a dataset merging strategy for efficiently constructing a transferable MLFF for pristine and oxygen-defective CeO 2 surfaces. The proposed strategy is based on three key elements: (1) initiating on-the-fly training from small, less stable slab models to accelerate early stage convergence by sampling diverse high-energy configurations; (2) sampling diverse local structures by gradually increasing the temperature during molecular dynamics simulations while avoiding excessively rapid atomic motions and unphysically short contacts; and (3) merging independently generated datasets from slab models with different thicknesses and defect conditions to improve transferability. The resulting MLFF is validated on larger slab models containing 144 atoms and applied to structural optimization of pristine and oxygen-defective surfaces as well as lattice oxygen diffusion pathways on defective surfaces. The predicted pathways and energy barriers are in good agreement with density functional theory results, particularly for pathways involving relatively large structural and energetic changes. Furthermore, the merged MLFF was applied to ideal CeO 2 (111) slabs containing up to 5183 atoms, yielding only weak size dependence of the predicted vacancy-migration barrier. These results highlight that systematic dataset merging across model sizes and configurations provides a practical route to constructing transferable MLFFs for complex oxide surfaces.

articles.title: Analytical nuclear gradients for the CC2 method using pair-natural orbitals based on localized virtual molecular orbitals for ground states
articles.abstract: Analytical nuclear energy gradients are indispensable for geometry optimizations and potential-energy-surface explorations, yet their development for pair-natural-orbital (PNO)-based methods remains limited. In this work, we present the analytical nuclear gradient theory for the ground-state PNO-based second-order approximate coupled cluster (CC2) model using localized virtual molecular orbitals (LVMOs). The gradient theory is formulated within the Lagrangian framework as an extension of our previously developed LVMO-based PNO-MP2 analytical gradient theory. Although the use of LVMOs requires additional localization constraints in the Lagrangian, orthonormal LVMOs simplify the coupled-perturbed equations and energy gradient expressions, and these advantages are exploited in the PNO-CC2 analytical gradient formulation. The implementation is extended to the spin-component-scaled variant. To facilitate the development and implementation, we extended our previously developed automated symbolic derivation framework, which systematically generates the derivative expressions for gradient calculations. Benchmark calculations on phenylalkane chains demonstrate favorable scaling of the analytical gradient evaluation. Gradients vary smoothly along a bond-dissociation coordinate of a ketene derivative, indicating that PNO orbital truncation does not introduce noticeable artifacts. Geometry optimizations of difluorodiene reproduce the characteristic elongation of electron-rich bonds observed for the CC2 theory relative to the MP2 theory. Applications to intermolecular complexes show that the PNO-CC2 framework provides optimized structures and binding energies comparable with those from the PNO-MP2 framework. Single-point gradient calculations for realistic molecular systems of around one hundred atoms demonstrate applicability of the implementation. This work establishes the analytical gradient formulation for ground-state PNO-CC2 theory and provides a foundation for future extensions to excited states.

articles.title: Analysis of transition dipole moments of band-progression peaks of fluorocarbons: Fundamentals and application to orientation analysis of fluoropolymers
articles.abstract: Perfluoroalkyl chains give infrared spectra involving a dominant absorption peak corresponding to the CF 2 symmetric stretching vibration mode. The direction of the transition dipole moment of this mode is approximately perpendicular to the chain axis, that is, the vibrational motion belongs to the E 1 symmetry species. Accordingly, the band progressions of this mode have also been considered to have the same property. In the present study, we have investigated the properties of the band progressions in detail using the p-polarized multiple-angle incidence resolution spectrometry on an oriented n-C 20 F 42 monolayer. We found that the surface selection rule of band progressions is the same as that of the CF 3 symmetric stretching vibrational mode with the aid of quantum chemical calculations. This indicates that the transition dipole moment of the band progressions does not correspond to the E 1 mode but is instead oriented predominantly parallel to the chain axis. We also show that this distinction is important for determining the orientation of perfluoroalkyl chains.

articles.title: Thymol–Menthol Deep Eutectic Solvent as a Functional Additive for PEO-Based Solid Polymer Electrolytes
articles.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as an alternative strategy to enhance electrolyte performance when employed as additives. In the present study, a new solid-state polymer electrolyte based on polyethylene oxide (PEO) doped with thymol–menthol deep eutectic solvents (T:M DESs) was successfully prepared via solution casting technique. Prior to incorporation into the PEO matrix, the physical and spectroscopic properties of the T:M DES additives were investigated using density, surface tension analysis, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The results revealed that the T:M 1:4 composition exhibited the density (0.91 g cm− 3) and surface tension (30 mN m− 1), due to higher menthol content which enhances intermolecular interactions, leading to a more organized molecular arrangement within the DES structure. The PEO-T:M electrolyte was analysed through FTIR, Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS). FTIR analysis confirmed the successful incorporation of T:M DES into the PEO matrix through broadening and shifting of the hydroxyl (–OH) stretching band, indicating strong hydrogen bonding interactions between T:M and PEO. EIS revealed that the ionic conductivity of the PEO electrolyte increased gradually upon the incorporation of T:M DES additives. Among the various additive compositions, ratio 1:4 of T:M DES additive exhibited the highest ionic conductivity of 1.28 × 10⁻⁶ Scm− 1. Overall, these findings highlight the promising role of thymol–menthol DES additives in improving the physicochemical properties and electrochemical performance of PEO-based electrolytes for potential electrochemical application.

articles.title: Extreme temperature gradient drives substantial thermoelectric current in additive manufacturing
articles.abstract: Thermoelectric effects are commonly neglected in engineering alloys because their Seebeck coefficients are small. Here we show that this material-centred assumption fails under the extreme temperature gradients of additive manufacturing (AM). Combining in situ measurements of transient potential with multiphysics simulations under representative conditions of laser-powder-bed-fusion and laser-directed-energy-deposition.In our experiments we find that temperature gradients of ~10⁵–10⁸ K m⁻¹ generate current densities of ~10⁶–10⁸ A m⁻² in melt pool of AlSi10Mg, despite its Seebeck coefficient of only ~2 μV K⁻¹. These values match or exceed current densities in some conditions ofthermoelectric materials. Additionally, we established a fully coupled thermoelectric magnetohydrodynamic (TEMHD)model that incorporates complete thermoelectric effects, and investigated the influence of thermoelectric source terms on the multi-physics coupling process. The currents are strongly anisotropic and spatially heterogeneous within the melt pool. The resulting Joule and Thomson heat terms locally rival or exceed heat losses from the melt-pool surface, changing regional temperature gradients by ~1–10% and current densities by ~2–15%, whereas the Peltier term remains weak. Although the specific microstructural consequences remain to be established, the magnitude, localization and thermal feedback of thermoelectriccurrents identify them as an inherent non-negligiblecomponent of melt-pool dynamics and solidification in AM, and as a pre-existing electrical background for magnetically or electrically assisted process. Our high‑fidelity TEMHD model provides an effective tool for studying this class of problems.

articles.title: More about Spin-Spin Dipole-Dipole Interactions Contributions to the Shapes of Nitroxide EPR Spectra in Solution
articles.abstract: In this work, experimental data were obtained confirming unusual contribution of dipole-dipole interaction between unpaired electron of the radical and its own ¹⁵N nucleus (DD1) to EPR resonance line shapes in solutions of ¹⁵N-Tempol radicals. One might expect that the random modulation of DD1 by rotational diffusion leads to spectral diffusion of the resonance frequencies: DD1 randomly flips the orientation of the nitrogen nuclear spin, causing the electron spin to randomly change frequencies and jump from one hyperfine component to another. Spectral diffusion is expected. This is an expected process in the case of the interaction of a nuclear spin with the lattice or with electrons in other radicals, or in the case of spin diffusion within the nuclear spin system. In this case, the electron spin facilitates flipping of the nuclear spin, and resonant frequency of that electron changes. As Marsh demonstrated, the elementary process is not limited merely to the nuclear spin flip. In addition to the frequency shift, spin coherence of unpaired electron acquires an extra phase of π. It should be noted that a similar effect was previously predicted by Salikhov and experimentally confirmed in studies by Bales and colleagues regarding paramagnetic relaxation associated with the dipole-dipole interaction of unpaired electrons in dilute solutions of nitroxide radicals (DD2). In this work, we present experimental data demonstrating negative interference between contributions of DD1 and DD2 paramagnetic relaxation mechanisms, on the one hand, and paramagnetic relaxation caused by spin exchange during random bimolecular collisions of radicals, on the other. Spin exchange leads to spectral diffusion without π-phase jumps of spin coherence.

articles.title: Physics-Coupled Task Allocation for Collaborative Robotic Welding of Dissimilar Steel Joints Using an α-Potential Game and a Physics-Informed Neural Network Surrogate
articles.abstract: Collaborative robotic welding of dissimilar steel joints involves coupled decisions concerning task assignment, welding sequence, thermal interaction, energy consumption, and production time. Conventional distance-based allocation methods do not explicitly account for the fact that neighboring welding operations may modify the thermal state and mechanical response of subsequent operations. This study proposes a physics-coupled task-allocation framework in which collaborative welding robots are modelled as players of an α-potential game and the thermo-mechanical response is evaluated using a physics-informed neural-network (PINN) surrogate. The α-potential formulation represents the bounded discrepancy between individual utility changes and changes in a common potential function resulting from non-additive thermal interactions. A sufficient equilibrium result is established: under a finite feasible strategy space, a global maximizer of the α-potential is an α-Nash equilibrium. Log-linear learning is employed as a stochastic strategy-update mechanism, while finite-time convergence results from the potential-game literature are invoked only for the exact-potential case and under their stated assumptions. The PINN incorporates the transient heat-conduction and mechanical-equilibrium equations into its training objective and provides a reduced-cost approximation of repeated thermo-mechanical evaluations. In the computational study, the proposed framework reduced normalized makespan and energy consumption relative to the distance-driven allocation strategy while simultaneously accounting for residual stress and carbon redistribution. The results indicate that coupling physical response with distributed task allocation can improve the quality of multi-robot welding decisions. The reported numerical values are computational predictions and should be independently validated experimentally before being generalized to industrial welding applications.

articles.title: Q-IDS Bench: Reproducible and Resource-Aware Evaluation of Quantum-Inspired Intrusion Detection Across Five Network and IoT Datasets
articles.abstract: Very high IDS scores are frequently reported, but one ac curacy measure does not by itself show whether a detector will remain reliable under a different split, preprocess ing pipeline, or deployment budget. Q-IDS Bench exam ines this issue by benchmarking nine quantum-inspired intrusion-detection system (IDS) configurations on five datasets, all implemented on classical hardware. The data are divided into training, validation, and test sets before fitted preprocessing, and each experiment is repeated with five random seeds. Performance is assessed with weighted F1, AUPRC, MCC, false-positive rate, attack recall, and model-side inference latency. The best weighted-F1 values range from 98.86% to 99.95%, but the leading architecture depends on the dataset. The key result is therefore not a universal winner but the reproducibility of the compari son: model rankings are dataset-specific, and hybridisation alone does not guarantee better performance. The study provides a baseline for future comparison with genuine quantum machine learning (QML) implementations.

articles.title: Multi-Dimensional Structural Fingerprinting for Quantitative Polymorph Comparison: A Comprehensive Topological Analysis of Sulfathiazole, Galunisertib and Aripiprazole Polymorphs
articles.abstract: Polymorphism in organic molecular crystals presents significant challenges for pharmaceutical and materials science applications, requiring robust methods for quantitative structural comparisons. We present a multi-dimensional topological fingerprinting approach that quantifies structural relationships through five complementary categories: crystal packing, intermolecular interaction networks, molecular conformation, fragment orientation, and spatial geometry. Distribution-based similarity metrics enable ranking and clustering of structurese̊v{, and every descriptor is independent of the unit cell, space-group setting and Cartesian frame.We demonstrate the approach on three pharmaceutical polymorph families: five DFT-optimized sulfathiazole polymorphs, ten experimental galunisertib polymorphs and nine experimental forms of the flexible, partly non-aromatic aripiprazole. Which categories are conserved depends on the molecule. For sulfathiazole, spatial geometry is the most consistent category (0.78--0.86), whereas conformation and interaction networks separate Forms II, III and IV from Forms I and V. For galunisertib, spatial geometry and conformation are the most consistent, crystal packing varies most. For aripiprazole, spatial geometry is much less conserved (0.41--0.74), and the decomposition distinguishes forms that share their packing but not their conformation (Forms I and X) from forms that share their conformation but not their lattice (Forms III, IV and V). The overall similarity agrees with COMPACK cluster matching for sulfathiazole (Spearman ρ=-0.89 with RMSD) and follows the number of matched molecules for galunisertib (ρ=0.44) and aripiprazole (0.67). Compared with the invariant descriptors AMD, PDD and SOAP, the fingerprint identifies the form of 47 sulfathiazole and 21 aripiprazole structures equally reliably and ranks distinct polymorphs closer to COMPACK cluster matching (aripiprazole: ρ=0.67 versus 0.14--0.37), though not to simulated PXRD similarity. Rankings are robust to coordinate perturbations and cutoff choices, except where an H-bond lies at the criterion or few aromatic contacts occur. The framework supports polymorph classification, structural relationship analysis, validation of crystal structure prediction and solid-form screening.

articles.title: Experimental and Computational Investigation of Thermal Conductivity in Porous Silicon: Doping-Dependent Performance of Molecular Dynamics and Physics- Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: Porous silicon (pSi) is a highly promising material for nanoscale thermal management, but predicting its thermal conductivity remains challenging due to complex structure-property dependencies. In this work, we present a comprehensive multiscale investigation of heat transport in pSi, combining experimental gas-microphone photoacoustic (PA) measurements with atomistic Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations and continuum-level Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Mesoporous pSi layers with porosities ranging from 48% to 75% were fabricated via electrochemical etching of highly doped p+-type silicon, and their effective thermal conductivity was experimentally determined. Our findings reveal that the thermal properties are fundamentally governed by the initial substrate doping, which dictates the formation of either isotropic sponge-like or anisotropic columnar morphologies. We demonstrate that MD simulations accurately capture the thermal behavior of heavily doped samples by explicitly accounting for phonon confinement, whereas the PINN approach excellently models percolation and macroscopic heat flux in stochastic networks typical of lightly and moderately doped silicon. By integrating these computational and experimental datasets with literature values, we utilized symbolic regression to derive a generalized analytical expression for the effective thermal conductivity of pSi as a function of porosity and temperature. This hybrid multiscale framework connects nanoscale phonon mechanics to macroscopic thermophysical properties, providing a predictive tool for the design of porous silicon-based thermoelectric and thermal-insulation devices.

articles.title: Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Galvanic Corrosion in Coupled AA7025 and SS304L for Marine Applications
articles.abstract: This study investigates the galvanic corrosion of AA7025 aluminum alloy coupled with 304L stainless steel (SS) fasteners in marine structures, using a multi-methodological approach involving analytical modeling, SolidWorks 3D modeling, COMSOL Multiphysics simulations, and experimental validation. The AA7025-304L SS couples were tested in tap water, 3.5% NaCl, and 1M H₂SO₄ for 30 days. Corrosion rates increased significantly due to galvanic coupling: 4.92× in tap water, 3.16× in NaCl, and 4.26× in H₂SO₄, with predictive models accurate within 5% error. H₂SO₄ caused the highest hardness loss (10.97%) and a corrosion depth of 100.4 µm. Microstructural analysis showed CaCO₃ scaling in tap water, severe pitting in NaCl, and generalized dissolution in H₂SO₄. COMSOL simulations identified an Al-5Zn sacrificial anode as an effective mitigation strategy, providing a protective current density of 0.84 A/m² and a polarization potential of -1.08 V, significantly reducing AA7025 corrosion in marine-relevant environments.

articles.title: Investi̇gati̇on of Radi̇ati̇on-Induced Heterogeneous Processes İn the Nax + H₂o System by Electron Paramagneti̇c Resonance Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: This study investigates radiation-induced heterogeneous processes in the NaX zeolite–H₂O system using Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy. Radiation-induced paramagnetic centers and free radicals were characterized using Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, while the molecular hydrogen formed was analyzed by gas chromatography. It was established that an increase in the water content leads to a decrease in the concentration of hole centers in NaX zeolite and an increase in the concentrations of H and OH radicals. The kinetics of the accumulation of these species were studied, and their radiation-chemical yields were determined. Based on the experimental observations, a reaction mechanism describing charge carrier localization, water radiolysis, and molecular hydrogen formation is proposed. The findings demonstrate that NaX zeolite provides an efficient catalytic environment for radiation-assisted water splitting and hydrogen production while contributing to a better understanding of radiation-catalytic processes occurring in heterogeneous systems.

articles.title: Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for Compressive Strength Prediction of 3D-Printed Fiber-Reinforced Concrete
articles.abstract: Accurate prediction of compressive strength is essential for the development and performance assessment of 3D-printed fiber-reinforced concrete (3DP-FRC), where mixture composition, fiber characteristics, curing age, and loading direction generate complex nonlinear relationships in strength response. This study develops an explainable machine-learning framework for predicting the compressive strength of 3DP-FRC using 299 experimental observations and 16 input variables. Four regression models, namely Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), CatBoost, and Natural Gradient Boosting (NGBoost), were optimized and evaluated using repeated five-fold cross-validation and an independent 20% testing dataset. NGBoost achieved the highest testing R² of 0.9877 and the lowest RMSE of 4.9036 MPa, together with a maximum prediction error of 13.6904 MPa, whereas CatBoost produced the lowest testing MAE of 3.8031 MPa. SHAP, LIME, and partial dependence analysis identified the water-to-binder ratio, water content, silica fume, and superplasticizer as the most influential predictors, while loading direction and fiber volume fraction also contributed substantially to compressive-strength prediction. The explainability analyses revealed pronounced nonlinear relationships and interaction effects among mixture composition, fiber characteristics, and processing-related variables. NGBoost was subsequently integrated into an interactive graphical user interface to provide direct strength prediction, uncertainty estimation, and feature-contribution analysis. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential of explainable machine learning for reliable compressive-strength prediction and data-driven assessment of 3DP-FRC. The developed tool provides an accessible platform for model interpretation and preliminary strength assessment, while further independent experimental validation is required before its use in structural design applications.

articles.title: Energy-Efficient Tri-State Quantum Scheduling for Sustainable 6G Base Stations
articles.abstract: The rapid densification of sixth-generation (6G) radio access networks is expected to increase the operational energy demand of cellular infrastructure, making energy-aware base station (BS) sleep scheduling an important research challenge. Conventional BS control mechanisms commonly rely on binary ON/OFF operation or static threshold policies, which provide limited flexibility in balancing energy consumption and service responsiveness under time-varying traffic. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Tri-State Quantum Rotation Scheduler (TQRS) for energy-aware 6G BS management. The framework represents each BS using three operating states, namely deep sleep, light sleep, and active mode, and employs a probability-based search mechanism with rotation-inspired updates to explore the resulting scheduling space. A feasibility-repair mechanism is used to maintain service constraints during candidate evaluation, followed by local refinement of the selected scheduling solution. The scheduling objective considers energy consumption and service delay while enforcing zero unserved traffic. The proposed scheduler is evaluated using a frozen 24-slot traffic trace and a common 15-BS network environment. The evaluation includes conventional reference policies, an internal Greedy+Repair heuristic, population-based metaheuristics including Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Differential Evolution (DE), and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and deep reinforcement learning baselines including Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Deep Q-Network (DQN). In the frozen comparative experiment, TQRS consumes 19,053 Wh, corresponding to a 47.0750% reduction relative to the Always Active reference of 36,000 Wh, while maintaining zero unserved traffic and a normalized mean delay of 0.929060, corresponding to approximately 18.5812 ms. WOA and the internal Greedy+Repair heuristic obtain lower energy consumption in this single-run comparison, with 17,692 Wh, and also slightly lower mean delay. Therefore, the study does not claim numerical superiority of TQRS over all competing methods. Instead, the results evaluate TQRS as a feasibility-aware tri-state scheduling framework and examine whether its probability-based search mechanism can provide a useful alternative operating strategy under time-varying traffic. The results also highlight the importance of realistic traffic validation, robustness analysis, and broader network modeling for practical 6G deployment.

articles.title: Physics-informed latent space dynamics identification for time-dependent NLTE atomic kinetics
articles.abstract: Non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) calculations remain a major computational bottleneck in radiation–hydrodynamics, while most existing machine-learning surrogates treat NLTE as a static input–output mapping rather than a kinetic evolution problem. Here, we present a physics-informed latent space dynamics identification framework specifically designed for NLTE atomic kinetics, which captures the time-dependent atomic kinetics of non-equilibrium plasmas through an explicit reduced governing equation. To ensure the physical reliability of the reduced model, we impose physics-informed loss terms that enforce macroscopic consistency, dynamical stability, and convergence to the correct steady state during long-time integration. Applied to tin NLTE population data generated along hydrodynamically modeled temperature–density trajectories relevant to extreme ultraviolet lithography plasmas, the model accurately reproduces charge-state evolution and mean charge state with errors below 2%, achieves speedups of approximately – , and remains stable beyond the training time window under fixed plasma conditions by converging toward physically admissible states and the correct steady-state solution. These results show that careful physics-informed design of the latent dynamics, rather than data fitting alone, is essential for constructing fast, stable, and physically reliable surrogates with long-time consistency for time-dependent NLTE kinetics.

articles.title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO₃: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Donor substitution can tune the coupled ferroelectric, dielectric, electronic, and optical properties of perovskite oxides by modifying lattice distortions and electronic screening. We investigate these effects in La-doped BaTiO3 using density functional theory, density-functional perturbation theory, and the Berry-phase formalism for polarization. For a model with 12.5% La substitution at the Ba site, La incorporation induces anisotropic lattice contraction, reduces tetragonality and Ti off-centering, and weakens the energetic stabilization of the tetragonal ferroelectric phase. The accompanying reduction in polarization is associated with enhanced electronic screening and reduced anomalous Born effective charges. Phonon calculations indicate that the relaxed doped structure is dynamically stable, while hardening of a low-frequency polar mode is consistent with weakened ferroelectricity. The high-frequency dielectric response increases moderately, whereas the static dielectric response decreases as the lattice contribution is suppressed. Electronic-structure calculations show a Fermi-level shift toward the conduction band without mid-gap defect states. The optical spectra exhibit an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein-Moss-type mechanism, enhanced near-edge transparency, and reduced birefringence. Together, these results suggest a microscopic connection between donor-induced screening, polar-mode hardening, reduced dynamical charges, polarization suppression, and decreased optical anisotropy. The conclusions apply to the investigated 12.5% composition; calculations at additional concentrations are needed to establish quantitative doping trends.
authors: Sikandar Azam, Muhammad Fareed, Qaiser Rafiq, Jan Minar, Abed Alataway

articles.title: Vacancy-driven topological transition of a Chern insulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a microscopic description of the strong-disorder transition in a Chern insulator using the in-gap ring states bound to individual vacancies. Using Green's function formalism, we construct an energy-dependent Hamiltonian describing their hybridization. In a commensurate periodic vacancy lattice, a Dirac inversion of the zero-energy vacancy kernel accounts for the change in the occupied-state Chern number of the full system. We treat weak positional disorder using the self-consistent Born approximation and numerical disorder averaging, and study independently distributed vacancies using transfer-matrix and multifractal scaling. The local Chern marker and current textures track the transition in real space. Together, these results highlight the role that nonperturbative ring states have as microscopic degrees of freedom through which strong disorder destroys the Chern phase.

articles.title: π-Flux Tuning of Quantum Paramagnetism in the Triangular-Lattice Hubbard Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare two time-reversal-symmetric triangular-lattice Hubbard models at half filling: the zero-flux model and a staggered π-flux model with zero and π flux through oppositely oriented triangles. Although both reduce to the same Heisenberg model at leading order in the strong-coupling limit, their distinct charge fluctuation profiles yield different quantum paramagnetic regimes. Combining a strong-coupling expansion with infinite density matrix renormalization group (iDMRG) calculations, we find that the positive ring-exchange of the zero-flux model promotes spontaneous chirality, consistent with its notion of a chiral spin liquid at intermediate coupling. In the staggered-π-flux model, whose noninteracting limit is a Dirac semimetal, the ring exchange changes sign and disfavors chiral order and we find no resolvable scalar chirality. This renders flux-tuned ring-exchange an efficient discriminator between chiral and non-chiral quantum paramagnets at finite coupling.
authors: Zhaochen Liu, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Ronny Thomale

articles.title: Non-adiabatic Optimisation via Localisation-Delocalisation Transitions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The promise of efficiently solving classical optimisation problems on quantum computers is tantalizing. As many such problems can be mapped to approximating the ground state of spin-glasses, paradigmatic models for studying many-body localisation, it is natural to ask if some of the intuition coming from quantum statistical mechanics can help guide the construction of novel quantum optimisation algorithms. In this work, we discuss how continuous reverse quantum annealing crossing a many-body localisation transition can be accelerated by considering the density of Landau-Zener crossings as the system is quenched. We provide an interpretation of this behaviour in terms of an effective Fokker-Planck equation for the success probability of the algorithm. This interpretation suggests an improvement in the required annealing time as a function of the system size N, which goes from O(m̊ poly(N)) to O(1) for reference states with non-vanishing energy density. We show that the continuous dynamics can be Trotterised with a number of steps that remains modest as system size increases, making it appealing for near-term devices. For the resulting circuit implementation, we provide a quantitative strategy for determining the parameters of the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We compare the performance of our digitised algorithm, which we call FRIO, against that of the QAOA for finding the ground state of spin-glass problems, in particular the SK model. The numerical results suggest that with suitably selected circuit parameters which can be efficiently found using thermalizing dynamics, FRIO almost always outperforms the conventional QAOA ansatz with pre-optimized angles.
authors: Ryan Smith, Sabrina Yue Wang, Filippo Maria Gambetta, Raul A. Santos

articles.title: Domain walls in R3c-structured NaNbO₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we undertake a systematic first-principles study of structural domain walls in the low-temperature rhombohedral R3c phase of perovskite oxide NaNbO₃. Employing a group-theoretic classification, we introduce eight unique classes of domain walls in the R3c structure, four of which have a domain wall orientation determined uniquely by the conditions of elastic compatibility and charge neutrality, and perform structural relaxations for each representative domain wall class. We find that one class of 109deg domain walls has a notably low energy of 9 mJ m⁻², comparable to the low-energy ferroelectric walls in BaTiO₃. Finally, we find that this class of 109deg walls is compatible with the crystal twinning observed in experiments on the R3c phase, and propose an atomistic mechanism for the R3c łeftrightarrow Pbcm phase transition.
authors: Jack G. Nedell, Craig J. Fennie

articles.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform d-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At 1/8 doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform d-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-t energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.
authors: Ao Chen, Johnnie Gray, Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

articles.title: Kinetic-inductance Parametric Amplification in Superconducting Hybrid Magnonics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric amplification enables sensitive microwave detection and signal processing by amplifying weak signals with minimal added noise. Here, we demonstrate kinetic inductance mediated parametric amplification in a hybrid magnonic system comprising a nonlinear NbN nanowire resonator strongly coupled to a yttrium iron garnet sphere. The resonator exhibits four wave mixing and nonlinear frequency pulling, enabling parametric amplification both away from and within the magnon-photon strong coupling regime. In the magnon detuned regime, we observe 7 dB gain, while coupling to the YIG magnon shifts the parametric amplification response by ~20 MHz and yields 3.4 dB gain in the hybrid mode. Thus, magnon photon coupling provides a route to magnetically tune the spectral position of kinetic inductance parametric amplification. At higher pump powers, the system transitions to a self oscillatory regime featuring comb-like sidebands and probe activated nonlinear mode mixing. These results establish hybrid magnonics as a platform for tunable nonlinear microwave amplification and dynamics.
authors: Pratap Kumar Pal, Moojune Song, Jinho Lim, Juliang Li, Serhii Kruhlov, Ralu Divan, Ulrich Welp, Clarence Chang, Kab-Jin Kim, Valentine Novosad, Axel Hoffmann, Yi Li

articles.title: Emergent altermagnetism in (LaVO₃₎ₙ/(LaNiO₃₎ₘ superlattices from interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using first-principles calculations, we show that altermagnetism emerges in (LaVO₃₎ₙ/(LaNiO₃₎ₘ superlattices, with (n,m) = (1,1), (2,2) and (2,4), from the interplay of interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts. Charge transfer drives the system towards the V⁴⁺ and Ni²⁺ configuration, turning the otherwise paramagnetic nickelate layers into a magnetically active sublattice. The resulting C-type antiferromagnetic order, combined with a⁻b⁺c⁻ or a⁻b⁻c⁻ octahedral tilts, links opposite-spin sublattices only through nonsymmorphic operations, yielding a d-wave spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. Within DFT+U, the splitting reaches 118 meV in the insulating (LVO)₁/(LNO)₁ superlattice, about twice that calculated for bulk LaVO₃, and decreases as the nickelate layers become thicker. Our findings indicate that this splitting is hosted by both the V and Ni sublattices, with nearly half of its weight on oxygen 2p states through p-d covalency. Interfacial charge transfer thus emerges as a design principle for engineering altermagnetism in oxide heterostructures.
authors: Gustavo H. Cassemiro, Walber H. Brito

articles.title: Nonlinear Canonical Transformations for Studying Spin-1/2 Hamiltonians
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories are promising, they are not yet black-box methods and require system-specific development. The XXZ and J₁₋J₂ spin models provide demanding benchmarks. Spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster methods may require high excitation ranks to recover the exact ground-state physics in strongly correlated regimes. We introduce a nonlinear spin-fermion-spin (SFS) transformation designed to map a strongly correlated spin Hamiltonian into a new spin Hamiltonian whose ground state is more accurately described at the mean-field level. For a representative SFS transformation, we identify a compact Clifford circuit that maps transformed product states to circuit-dressed, generally entangled states in the original representation. The transformed Hamiltonian can then be treated using broken-symmetry mean-field theory and post-mean-field methods. Benchmarks for the XXZ and J₁₋J₂ Hamiltonians show that spin mean-field theory in the transformed representation reduces the energy error relative to conventional spin-BCS mean field. The spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster calculations for the one-dimensional XXZ model provide substantially improved accuracy relative to the corresponding untransformed methods. In 2D, the accuracy of the transformed mean-field solutions depends on the site ordering and boundary conditions, as nonlocal strings can appear. These results show that exact transformations of operator representations can serve as many-body preconditioners for mean-field and low-rank coupled-cluster approximations to strongly correlated spin systems.
authors: Swarnamoy Ghosh, Thomas M. Henderson, Gustavo E. Scuseria

articles.title: Microstructural Generative Inverse Models for Additive Manufacturing Digital Twins
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metal additive manufacturing (AM) offers substantial advantages to the fabrication of complex structural components, but its widespread adoption is slowed due to complexities in the process-structure-property relations which is the cause for uncertainty and drives risk. Accurately quantifying these complex relations solely via experimental workflows is time consuming and costly. Integrated computational materials and engineering (ICME) frameworks address this challenge by leveraging advanced computational tools, such as crystal plasticity finite element models (CPFEM), to predict critical mechanical properties directly from microstructural data. However, these frameworks require a large datasets that are often difficult to obtain, and their predictive accuracy depends on the availability of realistic AM microstructure representations. Generative deep learning models are a promising approach towards synthesizing AM microstructures which contain complex morphological and crystallographic features. Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs), in particular, show a strong potential to capture the inherent complexities of AM structures. In this work, we demonstrate that DDPMs can reliably synthesize digital-twin orientation-imaging micrographs, and we support this claim with quantitative evidence of the fidelity of the generated samples. Additionally, we establish a classifier-free guidance framework for solving complex inverse problems such as property-to-structure and process-to-structure mappings, and we showcase a potential application on a qualification-relevant uncertainty quantification problem. Our work highlights the potential of AI-based generative modeling as a key component of computational frameworks for accelerating AM materials qualification and certification.
authors: Pablo Luna Falcon, Jason Mayeur, Amirkoushyar Ziabari, Vincent Paquit, Patxi Fernandez-Zelaia

articles.title: Nonlinear and Chaotic Dynamics of Two Dipolar-Coupled Anisotropic Spins under Periodic Excitation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the non-linear magnetization dynamics of two identical anisotropic macrospins coupled by dipolar interaction and subjected to periodic transverse excitation. The coupled Landau- Lifshitz-Gilbert equations are solved numerically using a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. By combining bifurcation diagrams, local-maxima analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and two-dimensional stability maps, we characterize how dipolar coupling, transverse driving amplitudes, and uniaxial anisotropy govern the long-time dynamics. The results reveal a non-monotonic reorganization of dynamical regimes, with alternating intervals of enhanced and suppressed instability. Analysis of symmetric and antisymmetric coordinates distinguishes the collective and relative spin responses, while Fourier spectra and three-dimensional trajectories provide complementary frequency-domain and geometrical characterizations. Simultaneous positivity of the two largest Lyapunov exponents identifies parameter regions consistent with hyperchaotic dynamics. Finally, analytical linearization and ferromagnetic-resonance calculations reveal the distinct coupling dependence of the collectivemode frequencies and clarify the limitations of the linearized description beyond the stability thresholds of the collinear reference state. These findings establish a unified framework for understanding the interplay of dipolar coupling, anisotropy, and periodic excitation in the non-linear dynamics of a minimal interacting-spin system.

articles.title: Design of Nuclear and Magnetic Scattering Length Density Profiles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scattering length density (SLD) profile of a sample can be deliberately designed to enhance the information of interest obtained from neutron reflectometry. Here, we demonstrate this approach using amorphous FeₓCoyAl₈Zr₂ thin films. Four samples, each comprising ten repetitions of an AlZr spacer layer and a magnetic layer, were prepared with magnetic-layer compositions of Fe₈₀Co₁₀Al₈Zr₂, Fe₇₀Co₂₀Al₈Zr₂, Fe₆₀Co₃₀Al₈Zr₂, and Fe₄₅Co₄₅Al₈Zr₂, and characterised using X-ray and polarised neutron reflectometry. Across the series, the nuclear SLD of the FeCoAlZr alloy decreases approximately linearly from 7.14 × 10⁻⁶ to 4.63 × 10⁻⁶ mathringA⁻² with increasing Co content, while the magnetic SLD is approximately 4.3-4.5 × 10⁻⁶ mathringA⁻². These results demonstrate that the nuclear and magnetic contributions can be controlled largely independently, with composition primarily tuning the nuclear SLD and the applied magnetic field offering, in principle, additional control of the magnetic contribution.
authors: Alexandros Barnasas, Edward J. Stuckey, Alexei A. Vorobiev, Joashaniel F. K. Cooper, Sjoerd Stendahl, Björgvin Hjörvarsson

articles.title: Spin polarization in a chiral ladder: elastic and inelastic environments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how the transport window and environmental reinjection determine the spin polarization transmitted through a minimal two-leg chiral ladder. The model contains time-reversal-invariant helical spin--orbit coupling, spin-independent interchain hopping, and nonmagnetic contacts with two orbital modes per lead. Sublattice symmetry makes the coherent spin-transmission kernel exactly odd in energy. A window centered on the symmetry point therefore gives zero integrated spin current, whereas a displaced window selects an uncanceled spectral interval. The resulting polarization reverses between enantiomers and vanishes in the decoupled-chain, zero-spin--orbit, and equivalent-strand limits of this model. We compare uniform absorption, energy-resolved elastic probes, and thermalized voltage probes at the same finite bias, including reinjection whenever probes are present. Charge conservation alone does not prohibit enhancement of the integrated spin signal: the elastic-probe response can increase at finite bias even where its linear-response counterpart decreases. Thermalized probes can also lift the centered-window zero that elastic probes preserve. Absorption and reinjection also change the transmitted charge, so enhancement of spin current and enhancement of normalized polarization must be distinguished. Static onsite disorder produces sample-dependent fluctuations; its signed ensemble mean is reported with uncertainty and is not forced to vanish in a displaced window. These results identify the energy interval and reservoir prescription that must be controlled when interpreting dephasing trends in minimal models relevant to chirality-induced spin selectivity.
authors: D. T. Verrilli H., Jorge Cardenas-Gamboa, Mayra Peralta, Claudia Felser, José H. Garcia, Solmar Varela, Nelson Bolívar

articles.title: Finite-width altermagnetic quantum rings: angular-channel hybridization and Aharonov--Bohm physics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a finite-width two-dimensional quantum ring with a quadratic d-wave altermagnetic term, Tan--Inkson confinement, a perpendicular magnetic field, and independently tunable Aharonov--Bohm (AB) flux. The altermagnetic interaction mixes m and m±2 angular channels while preserving their parity. Circular symmetry renders the crystal orientation spectrally irrelevant and makes the two spin blocks exactly isospectral. The resulting same-parity anticrossings are resolved at low filling, and multichannel mixing is found near the Fermi level of highly occupied rings. Independent converged calculations for Nₑ₌₁₄₀₀ and 1800 establish the reconstructed Fermi edge and magnetic response in a finite field window and the persistent current over a full AB flux period. The analytic conventional reference separates radial-subband depopulation (dHvA-type cycles) from finer finite-ring shell oscillations; we do not assign a global Fourier spectrum to unverified altermagnetic field scans. The few-electron thermal response is obtained from an exact fixed-particle-number canonical partition function, avoiding finite-system errors of a fixed-mean-number approximation. The circular model supports an equilibrium charge current but no persistent spin current.

articles.title: Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer. NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50--60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel. The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35--40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity. Under applied perpendicular magnetic fields, the interplay between the external field and the magnetic stray fields modifies the flux-flow instability and the apparent instability velocity inferred from transport, with values below those reported for bare NbN films. These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.
authors: Juan C. Zapata, Emilio De Biasi, Martin Sirena, Jeehoon Kim, Nestor Haberkorn

articles.title: Decoding Composition-Structure-Performance Relations in Sodium Layered Oxide Positive Electrode Materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, NaₓTMO₂, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds. We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten NaₓTM₀.₅TM'₀.₅O₂ oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. The phase diagrams explain the observed O3/P3/O1 sequences and voltages, and the O3-to-P3 competition hinges on ordering energies of a few meV per atom that scalar descriptors, such as the cationic potential and the interlayer-slab distance, miss. Our extensive analysis reveals that the redox couples form a nearly partner-independent ladder, Ti³⁺/⁴⁺ < Mn³⁺/⁴⁺ < Co³⁺/⁴⁺ < Ni²⁺/³⁺ < Fe³⁺/⁴⁺, explaining pristine charge transfer and the oxidation sequence. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO₆ octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn³⁺ and Ni³⁺ through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers. We formulate an energy-density-versus-strain map that yields a design rule: a high-voltage couple without Jahn--Teller strain, which Mn⁴⁺/Ni²⁺ charge transfer realizes in NaₓMn₀.₅Ni₀.₅O₂, the most practical composition. We release the ordering-resolved dataset as a training set for subsequent training of accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials.
authors: Yunyeong Choi, Hasindhi H. Lokuge, Joshua D. Bocarsly, Pieremanuele Canepa

articles.title: Hierarchical Reduction of Invariant Subspaces: From Fragmentation to Many-Body Scars
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a hierarchy of invariant Hilbert-space structures connecting Hilbert-space fragmentation, partial solvability, and quantum many-body scars. For spin chains with fragmented spin-1/2 subspaces and their local deformations, we show, using the spin-1 XXC chain as a representative example, how successive local deformations reduce extensive irreducible-string fragmentation through an implicitly embedded spin-1/2 invariant space and ultimately to a single scar tower, connecting the XXC, perturbed XXC, and spin-1 XY scar models. Through the intermediate embedded space, local dynamics couples states from distinct frozen irreducible-string sectors and selects a new decomposition into representations, from which smaller invariant spaces can be retained. We also establish a rigidity constraint on isolating nonsymmetric towers and a constructive correspondence that transfers a reduction between locally realizable representations of the embedded dynamics. The latter demonstrates that the reduction hierarchy can be transferred through a unitary transformation within the embedded subspace, yielding an exact scar tower built on a Néel reference state without requiring unitary equivalence of the full Hamiltonians.

articles.title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we theoretically study the structural transformations occurring in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) subjected to strong deformations. The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. Depending on the direction and the type of the strain, the simulations reveal different types of structural transformations in two-dimensional (2D) h-BN associated with the elastic failure. It is found that, under certain shear strains, there can form an ordered 2D orthorhombic phase with the 2D layer space symmetry pmmm. Thermal stability of the latter up to ~900 K is demonstrated by first-principle Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. The examination of electronic structure indicates that, in contrast to the conventional h-BN, which is an insulator with the wide band gap, the predicted orthorhombic phase is expected to be a semiconductor with the narrow band gap of ~ 0.65 eV.
authors: O. Bystrenko, B. Ilkiv, S. Petrovska, O. Foia, T. Bystrenko, O. Khyzhun

articles.title: How good are universal MLIPs for alloys? A benchmark is only as trustworthy as its controls
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) are ranked by their formation-energy error against a DFT database, as if that database were ground truth, but independent DFT databases disagree. We benchmark fourteen uMLIPs on 1.45 million ordered intermetallics against AFLOW, which none trained on, and compare every energy and stability error with that disagreement. For half the structures, AFLOW, Alexandria, and OQMD differ by less than 6-8 meV/atom, but a minority differ by far more, raising the average to 16-30. That disagreement sets a floor on any model's measurable error. Re-referenced, the best uMLIP agrees with AFLOW as closely as Alexandria does, and the next four sit 2-7 meV/atom above the floor. Once broken elemental references are screened, the energy and stability rankings agree almost everywhere. Three apparent model failures shrink or vanish under the right control: poorly correlated shear moduli, thousands of "bad" DFT references, and the leader's inflated lead.
authors: Gus L. W. Hart, Jacob N. Pursley

articles.title: From phase analysis to phase tracking: a robust approach to atomic-scale strain mapping
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomic-scale strain governs the electronic, ferroic and mechanical properties of materials, and atomic-resolution microscopy measures it most directly. Geometric phase analysis (GPA) is the standard tool, but it fails when a Bragg reflection moves outside its fixed Fourier aperture under large strain or rotation, or in misoriented grains. Here we introduce geometric phase tracking analysis (GPTA), whose Fourier aperture tracks the Bragg reflection at each pixel in real space. A narrow aperture can therefore reject noise without losing a displaced reflection. On 13,795 simulated and experimental atomic-resolution images under various imaging conditions, GPTA reduces GPA's failure rate from 27% to 11.5% with up to 335 times better accuracy. It also gives strain and dislocation maps across grains, resistance to dynamical-scattering extinction, and a confidence map, capabilities that GPA lacks. Tracking the aperture combines reciprocal-space dose efficiency with real-space spatial resolution and extends atomic-scale strain metrology to beam-sensitive materials and challenging imaging conditions.

articles.title: Impact of localized 4f magnetism on Berry curvature and the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in CeRu₂Si₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE), originating from Berry curvature, has been extensively studied in f-electron systems, including Ce-based compounds. However, how the magnetism of localized f electrons affect the intrinsic AHE remains unclear. Here, we investigate this issue in CeRu₂Si₂ by calculating the intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) for several occupied Ce-4f states using first-principles LDA+U calculations combined with Wannier interpolation method. We find that the intrinsic AHC remains finite even when the Ce-4f states are localized and do not contribute directly to the Fermi surface, and that its magnitude depends on which Ce-4f state is occupied. We show that localized 4f-electron magnetism induces exchange splitting in the conduction bands, generating Berry curvature in specific regions near the Fermi surface. This mechanism enables conduction bands that are derived from nonmagnetic orbitals and form the Fermi surface to contribute to the intrinsic AHE, suggesting a route to realizing large intrinsic AHE in f-electron materials.
authors: Takehiro Kobayashi, Shunsuke Hirai, Ibuki Terada, Michi-To Suzuki

articles.title: Ferroelastic Reversal Magnon Thermal Hall Effect in a Fully Compensated Ferrimagnet
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnons offer a charge-neutral channel for spin and heat transport, yet reversible and nonvolatile control of their thermal Hall response poses a fundamental challenge in systems with zero net magnetization. Here, we establish ferroelastic switching as an effective route to manipulate magnonic transverse responses in fully compensated ferrimagnets. A minimal Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model reveals that ferroelastic switching can re-orientate the lattice anisotropy, which reconstructs the chirality-resolved magnon bands and Berry curvature distribution. Consequently, the two orthogonal fully compensated ferrimagnetic variants related by [C2||C4z] exhibit magnon thermal Hall responses with opposite signs, whereas the response vanishes in the intermediate altermagnetic phase. First-principles calculations further identify monolayer V2SSe as a promising material candidate for realizing the proposed ferroelastic control of transverse magnon transport. Remarkably, ferroelastic switching drives a dual magnonic-electronic band reconstruction, enabling nonvolatile reversal of the magnon thermal Hall effect while producing anisotropic orbital Hall responses and distinct magneto-optical spectra as complementary transport and optical fingerprints. Our findings establish ferroelasticity as an effective route to nonvolatile magnon control and multichannel state identification in zero net magnetization systems.
authors: Yingxi Bai, Zihan Chen, Chengwang Niu, Ming Yang

articles.title: Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling 1/3 in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. From the microscopic wave functions, we derive the commutator of its guiding-center coordinates, set by a many-body Berry curvature that governs its wave packets. A modulation with two flux quanta per unit cell splits the quasihole band into bands with Chern numbers 6 and -3; such opposite signs are generic as long as a weak modulation opens a gap between the anyon bands. In the C=-3 band, the quasihole drifts against E×B, although the magnetic field has the same sign everywhere. Perturbation theory in the modulation explains these results, and large-scale Monte Carlo calculations confirm them. Anyon bands thus acquire their own topology, which controls anyon motion and may shape the phases of itinerant anyons.
authors: Zhenyu Xiao, Minxuan Wang, Shinsei Ryu

articles.title: Coulomb-Driven Electronic Textures in Lightly Hole-Doped Cuprates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by recent experiments on Ca₂CuO₂Cl₂, we present a comprehensive study of the interplay between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets in lightly hole-doped cuprates. Owing to the poorly screened Coulomb potential, the interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets favor asymmetric electronic configurations characterized by effective electric "dipoles". Using the MPS-based Lanczos method, we show that these localized holes give rise to in-gap bound states within the charge-transfer gap. When tunneling matrix-element effects are included, the bound states exhibit a characteristic 4a₀ × 2a₀ internal structure, consistent with experimental observations. Our results suggest that Coulomb interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets, together with tunneling matrix-element effects, provide a microscopic mechanism for the observed 4a₀ electronic structures.
authors: Wei-Wei Yang, Yang Shen, Yuxin Wang, Pengfei Li, Mingpu Qin, Kun Jiang

articles.title: Thermal expansion mechanisms, heat transport, and band-gap renormalization in strongly anharmonic Rb₂SO₄, Rb₂Ca₂₍SO₄₎₃, and Ba₃Lu(BO₃₎₃ from machine-learned interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rb₂SO₄, Rb₂Ca₂₍SO₄₎₃, and Ba₃Lu(BO₃₎₃ are structurally complex materials whose thermal expansion has been interpreted, on the basis of high-temperature x-ray diffraction, in terms of specific polyhedral rearrangements. We study their lattice dynamics and its consequences for thermal and electronic properties using molecular dynamics with actively learned moment tensor potentials trained on density-functional theory data. The anharmonicity measure σ^A (compares the anharmonic contribution to the interatomic forces with the total forces acting on atoms) reaches approx0.3-0.5 for β-Rb₂SO₄, Rb₂Ca₂₍SO₄₎₃, and Ba₃Lu(BO₃₎₃ and approx0.75 for orientationally disordered α-Rb₂SO₄, and the imaginary harmonic modes of Rb₂Ca₂₍SO₄₎₃ and α-Rb₂SO₄ are stabilized at finite temperature. The simulations reproduce the measured thermal expansion and support the mechanisms proposed from diffraction: expansion along c in β-Rb₂SO₄ arises from both elongation and straightening of corrugated Rb chains, BO₃ reorientation accompanies the anisotropic expansion of Ba₃Lu(BO₃₎₃, and bending of polyhedral linkages limits expansion along the weakly expanding directions and in cubic Rb₂Ca₂₍SO₄₎₃. Green-Kubo lattice thermal conductivities differ by more than an order of magnitude between compounds with comparable σ^A, showing that the anharmonicity measure alone does not determine heat transport. Phonon-induced band-gap renormalization, including lattice thermal expansion, reaches 2.7 and 1.7 eV at 1250 K in Rb₂Ca₂₍SO₄₎₃ and Ba₃Lu(BO₃₎₃ and 1.4 eV at 650 K in β-Rb₂SO₄, with zero-point renormalizations of 0.64, 0.70, and 0.31 eV for β-Rb₂SO₄, Rb₂Ca₂₍SO₄₎₃, and Ba₃Lu(BO₃₎₃, respectively.
authors: Ekaterina Spirande, Rustam Arabov, Sofya Demina, Nikita Rybin, Alexander Shapeev

articles.title: Piezo-Kerr effect in altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry is usually viewed as a constraint on physical responses, but it can also be used to design the fields that control them. Here, we adopt the representation-matching principle used to identify conjugate fields of order parameters and apply it to response tensors. A linear coupling, the key ingredient for sign-switching control, is symmetry-allowed when a component (or a combination of components) of the control field and the selected response component share the same irreducible representation of the magnetic point group (MPG) of the system. Applied to the magneto-optical Kerr effect, this principle yields a piezo-Kerr effect, in which specific strain combinations activate a Kerr response forbidden in the unstrained state. Enumerating all 122 MPGs, we identify 16 groups in which the unstrained Kerr response is forbidden while a linear strain-induced contribution is allowed. These groups are realized by altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets with symmetry-enforced vanishing net magnetization. The active strain channels and the associated first-order sign reversals follow directly from symmetry. First-principles calculations for bulk MnTe₂ and CoF₂, and Cr₂Se₂O and Cr₂Te₂O monolayers confirm these predictions. In these materials, the Kerr rotation vanishes without strain, whereas 0.5-3% strain produces rotations ranging from tens to hundreds of millidegrees, and reversing the matched strain channel reverses the Kerr sign. These results establish a general route to large and switchable Kerr responses emerging from symmetry-forbidden states in compensated magnets.
authors: Yuqi Liu, Qiu-Shi Huang, Xinfeng Chen, Yilin Han, Run-Wu Zhang, Zhi-Ming Yu, Yugui Yao

articles.title: Active phase separation from concentration-dependent diffusion in chemical networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active phase separation in living systems is ubiquitous, yet the microscopic origins of the non-equilibrium terms in active field theories remain largely unknown. Here, starting from stochastic mass-conserving reaction-diffusion dynamics of two interacting chemical species, we perform a systematic slow-mode reduction and derive the complete Active Model B+ field theory, with all phenomenological coefficients expressed in terms of microscopic parameters. We identify concentration-dependent diffusivities and asymmetric inter-species chemotactic couplings as the minimal microscopic ingredients generating the genuinely non-equilibrium coefficient responsible for microphase separation, cluster phases, and arrested coarsening. Our framework recovers the equilibrium limit consistently and is validated by stochastic numerical simulations. These results establish a direct, bottom-up link between the architecture of chemical reaction networks and the universality class of their emergent large-scale dynamics.

articles.title: Nitrogen vacancy cluster-mediated ferroelectric domain growth in wurtzite AlN
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aluminum nitride-based ferroelectrics combine high remanent polarization, thermal stability, weak size effects, a wide bandgap and back-end process compatibility, making them promising for high density non-volatile memory. However, their high coercive field (E_c) and unclear polarization switching mechanism limit further applications. Theoretical predictions indicate preferential reversed domain growth along the polar axis, whereas experiments show nearly isotropic growth or preferential growth perpendicular to this axis. Here, we combine density functional theory, Deep Potential molecular dynamics and experimental characterization to determine how nitrogen vacancies (V_N) regulate domain growth and E_c. In ideal crystal, strong lattice coupling along the polar axis drives preferential domain growth in this direction. V_N locally weakens this coupling and promotes polarization nucleation. The spatial distribution of V_N and the temporal sequence of vacancy induced switching jointly determine the direction and morphology of reversed domain growth. We further show that scandium doping promotes V_N formation, thereby enhancing defect mediated nucleation and reducing E_c. These findings establish a multiscale mechanism governing thin-film domain-growth kinetics and macroscopic E_c, reconciling experimental observations with ideal crystal simulations and providing defect engineering principles for low-voltage, reliable and scalable ferroelectric devices.
authors: Zijian Zhou, Kan-Hao Xue, Ziqi Pang, Heng Yu, Shanzhong Xie, Hang Liu, Haiming Qin, Yi Tong, Bowen Su, Yi Yang, Tian-Ling Ren, Xiangshui Miao

articles.title: Interaction-enhanced antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate magnetic correlations in the two-leg Kondo-Hubbard ladder using the density-matrix renormalization group method. We focus on a parameter regime in which the noninteracting electronic system has a narrow indirect band gap. In this regime, there is no Fermi surface, and the conventional Fermi-surface-based Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida picture is not directly applicable; magnetic correlations between localized spins become weaker as the noninteracting band gap increases. We find that a moderate on-site Coulomb interaction enhances the antiferromagnetic correlations between localized spins. This enhancement, which is also seen in the staggered magnetization induced by a pinning field at the edges, occurs for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo couplings. Our results show that electron-electron interactions can enhance magnetic correlations between localized spins even when the underlying noninteracting electronic structure is gapped, suggesting an interaction-driven route to magnetic instabilities in narrow-gap Kondo-lattice systems.
authors: Tatsuya Kaneko, Ritsuki Hirabayashi, Yutaka Akagi

articles.title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local polar distortions, their collective ordering, and their field-driven reversal have been studied extensively in ferroelectric perovskites for decades. Here we identify an unusual behavior in the ferroelectric halide perovskite CsGeBr3 using large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials. In its nominally cubic phase the Ge off-centering forms one-dimensional polar chains that extend over at least tens of nanometers and relax on nanosecond timescales, four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 in between. The cubic CsGeBr3 phase is a dynamically disordered state in which oppositely polarized chains flip throughout the crystal, and a long-lived one-dimensional local polarization coexists with zero net polarization. A simple three-dimensional perovskite thus hosts long-ranged one-dimensional polar correlations with remarkably slow dynamics. In the ferroelectric phase the same chains set a one-dimensional switching mechanism, in which the polarization reverses chain by chain.
authors: Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Priyanka Deswal, Ethan Berger, Nicholas C. Bristowe, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor

articles.title: Mn-deficient Ni-Mn-Ga alloys: phase transitions, magnetic properties, and disappearance of martensitic transformation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Composition gradients formed during directional solidification are generally considered undesirable in Ni-Mn-Ga magnetic shape-memory alloys. However, these gradients offer a highly effective platform for systematically investigating composition-property relationships under identical growth and heat-treatment conditions. To exploit this approach, one Mn-deficient and two near-stoichiometric Ni-Mn-Ga oligocrystals were grown by optical zone remelting and characterized by X-ray fluorescence mapping, optical microscopy, X-ray diffraction, low-field magnetic measurements, and vibrating-sample magnetometry. The ingots contained elongated grains and axial compositional gradients, primarily associated with the redistribution of Mn and Ga, whereas Ni remained relatively uniformly distributed. The martensitic and premartensitic transformation temperatures generally increased with increasing Mn content. Neither transformation was detected between 10 and 400 K in specimens containing 20.5-22.0 at.% Mn, all of which had e/a < 7.40. In contrast, both transformations were observed in the investigated specimens containing at least 22.1 at.% (e/a ≥ 7.46). This abrupt change may indicate a possible electron-concentration threshold for the occurrence of these transformations. Saturation magnetization increased with Mn content up to 25.8 at.%, reaching 96.9 A m²/kg at 10 K and 71.2 A m²/kg at 300 K. Post-growth annealing increased the transition temperatures and changed the low-field magnetic response. The results indicate that composition-gradient oligocrystals serve as an effective platform for investigating the relationships between composition, structure, and magnetic properties in Ni-Mn-Ga alloys with the same processing history.
authors: Valentina Moskvina, Jaroslav Čapek, Michal Rameš, Denys Musiienko, Petr Veřtát, Alexej Perevertov, Ladislav Straka, Oleg Heczko

articles.title: Scalable Neural Wave Functions via Information Mixing and Hierarchical Network Architectures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Numerically simulating quantum many-body systems is one of the central challenges in modern physics, as the exponential growth of the Hilbert space with system size renders large-scale exact solutions intractable. Over the past decade, generative artificial neural networks have emerged as powerful wave function ansätze that have powered advances in finding ground state representations, reconstructing quantum states from data, and modeling dynamics in quantum many-body systems. While recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are computationally efficient, the recurrent nature can limit their capacity to capture long-range correlations. Transformer models with their underlying self-attention mechanism excel at capturing these long-range correlations, but incur increased computational requirements, restricting applications to small physical systems. In this work, we address these limitations by exploring the multi-layer perceptron (MLP) mixer model as a wave function ansatz. By mixing information globally and locally through the system via a computationally lightweight mixing strategy, this architecture promises to combine the ability to capture long-range correlations with low computational costs. We benchmark the model on finding ground state representations of two-dimensional quantum many-body systems in various phases of matter and investigate the behavior of representational accuracy and computational efficiency for different physical system sizes. By comparing its performance to RNNs and transformer models with single-site and patched input definitions, we demonstrate that the MLP mixer architecture performs competitively with state-of-the-art network models. We further show that a hierarchical combination of this model with the transformer model outperforms other state-of-the-art architectures for large-scale quantum systems, opening new avenues for investigating quantum phases of matter.

articles.title: Delta-Doped GeV⁻ in diamond with isotope resolvable optical spectra
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Group IV color centers in diamond -- silicon, germanium, tin, and lead-vacancy centers -- are a promising platform for quantum networking. Typical Group-IV creation utilizes ion implantation during diamond growth that leaves the color centers with a broad depth distribution and damage-induced strain inhomogeneity. Deterministic placement and damage reduction in Group IV generation are essential for improving this platform. In this letter, we report on the localization of germanium-vacancy (GeV⁻⁾ to a < 10 nm layer via the timed injection of GeH₄ during microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition. In this layer we have realized 17 ppm of Ge and a strain-free environment for the GeV⁻. Subsequent electron irradiation and annealing have generated a sheet density of 0.12 GeV⁻/μm². The minimal damage from color center generation mitigates spectral inhomogeneity and allows spectral resolution of isotopic clusters, with the best cluster having an inhomogeneous distribution of 2.14 GHz and an average linewidth of 47 ± 11 MHz. Our study gives insight into formation dynamics of GeV⁻ in delta-doped systems and estimates our vacancy to GeV⁻ yield to be ≥ 90%, establishing an athermal nearest-neighbor formation model. We further characterized the spin T₂^* and set a lower bound of 730 ns, limited by a paramagnetic defect.
