These bounds are controlled by the distance of the normalized density profile from the Poincaré density manifold times the number of particles. In particular, these bounds show that the TFW approximation is exact on the Poincaré manifold. We then show that, in the periodic setting, the distance between the Kohn-Sham potential and the inverse TFW potential in the natural dual Sobolev space can also be controlled by explicit density dependent constants times the distance to the Poincaré manifold. As a corollary, we prove that for a fixed density profile, the Kohn-Sham potential converges towards the inverse Thomas--Fermi potential in the high-density limit N i̊ghtarrow infty with asymptotic rate of order N⁻². This rate is shown to be optimal.

articles.title: Anisotropic spin hydrodynamics in a magnetized medium: entropy-current formulation and minimal linear modes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31408v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate anisotropic relativistic spin hydrodynamics in a parity-even magnetized medium using an Israel--Stewart entropy-current construction. Treating the magnetic field at leading order in the gradient expansion reduces the rotational symmetry to SO(2) and separates spin susceptibilities and dissipative transport into longitudinal, transverse, and mixed channels. A restricted quadratic entropy current yields transient equations for the retained dissipative stresses and spin fluxes. We analyze a minimal linear closure around an unpolarized homogeneous equilibrium, retaining dynamical magnetic-flux perturbations but no explicit spin-magnetization coupling; spin and magnetic fluctuations mix through the fluid variables. Infrared coefficient equations and ultraviolet characteristic expansions organize the magnetosonic and Alfvén-like spectra together with spectator spin-flux poles. The first-order truncation exhibits unstable boost-sector poles and superlinear large-wave-number branches, interpreted as diagnostics of the truncated equations rather than microscopic dispersion predictions. For the baseline parameters, finite relaxation times yield asymptotically linear propagation branches and finite relaxation poles, with no growing modes found on the sampled grid. The characteristic speeds depend nonmonotonically on spin transport and provide necessary light-cone diagnostics, without establishing general stability or strong hyperbolicity.
authors: Yiwei Qiu, Duan She, Defu Hou

articles.title: In-Situ Differential-Light-Shift Cancellation for Trapped-Atom Clocks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.26398v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Differential light shifts (DLS) induced by optical trapping fields fundamentally limit the stability and accuracy of trapped-atom microwave clocks. We demonstrate an in-situ method to cancel DLS by simultaneously interrogating multiple spatially separated atomic ensembles at different trap intensities generated from a common light source. By operating the ensembles at set intensity ratios and performing Ramsey spectroscopy, the intensity-dependent frequency shifts are measured within each experimental cycle and extrapolated to the zero-intensity limit. This approach effectively enables shot-to-shot determination of a DLS-free frequency without requiring magic wavelengths or species-specific cancellation schemes. We validate the method for Rb atoms trapped in time-averaged potentials by introducing controlled variations of the total trap power and show that the extrapolated frequency remains insensitive to these fluctuations. The technique is general and can be extended to other systematic shifts, providing a scalable route toward improved stability and accuracy in compact trapped-atom clocks and related quantum sensors relying on optical dipole traps
authors: Jan Simon Haase, Alexander Fieguth, Igor Bröckel, Jens Kruse, Carsten Klempt

articles.title: Geodesic torsion of the magnetic field line and other predictors of coil non-planarity in QI stellarators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.26763v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stellarator magnetic fields are often realized with non-planar modular coils with their out-of-plane bending being one of the main engineering challenges. We ask whether the non planarity of the fialment can be predicted from the equilibrium alone. We look at a dataset of coils for stellarator equilibira and find that the geodesic torsion of the magnetic field line is a strong and robust predictor in a wide range of coil feasibility requirements. We compare the performance of the geodesic torsion against other equilibrium and surface geometry properties and find it to be a superior predictorv hardly replaceable by other quantities we considered in this dataset. The ranking it induces also reproduces the ordering of four published configurations --- precise QA, precise QI at nfp 2 and 3, and W7-X. Our conclusions suggest that geodesic torsion of the magnetic field line may be considered as a cheap and robust candidate for a stage-one non-planarity proxy.
authors: Andrea Pavone, Sehyun Kwak, Felix Warmer

articles.title: Exact and Asymptotically Complete Robust Verifications of Neural Networks via Ising Solvers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.00408v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an Ising-compatible framework for formal neural-network robustness verification under bounded input perturbations. For piecewise activations (both continuous piecewise-linear and discrete piecewise-constant), the Exact Logarithmic Piecewise Model (Log-PW) provides an exact, sound, and complete formulation with a state-optimal logarithmic encoding, reducing the binary variables per neuron from linear O(κ) to information-theoretically minimal logarithmic complexity O(łceil łog₂ κ c̊eil) via logarithmic SOS2 (Log-PWL) and SOS1 (Log-PWC) constraints. For general element-wise activations, the Asymptotic Step-Envelope Model (Step-Env) leverages Log-PWC to construct sound, refinable endpoint enclosures. An exact monotonic reduction based on Jordan decomposition further extends this framework to arbitrary non-monotonic activations. We further develop a hybrid Benders solver with output-sensitive iteration bounds, leveraging a Helly-based conflict compression theory to avoid generic exponential cut explosion. In particular, for shallow networks with fixed input dimension, this establishes an unconditionally polynomial Benders iteration complexity in network size. Interval pruning, certificate transfer for pruned networks, and layerwise classical--Ising partitioning further reduce spin requirements. Experiments demonstrate exact certification fidelity for piecewise-linear networks and near-reference accuracy for non-linear activations under compact spin budgets. On MNIST benchmarks, Log-PW halves binary decision spins over One-Hot formulations, while Helly-based cuts achieve up to a 13.41× speedup and an 87.6% reduction in master queries over standard baselines.
authors: Wenxin Li, Wenchao Liu, Anzhe Jiang, Weihao Li, Chuan Wang, Qi Gao, Yin Ma, Hai Wei, Kai Wen

articles.title: A coupled finite element formulation for chemo-mechano-thermodynamical contact and its application to bonding and debonding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.12375v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work presents a finite element formulation for coupled chemo-mechano-thermodynamical large deformation contact. The formulation is based on the contact theory of Sauer et al. (2022) that contains six coupled (but separate) fields: the deformation and temperature of the two contacting bodies, as well as an interfacial bonding field and interfacial temperature. The latter is governed by the chemical and mechanical energy dissipation at the interface. Here the focus is placed on the evolution of bonding and debonding, and how it is coupled to the mechanical and thermal contact state. Several elementary models are proposed for this based on a quadratic contact potential. The resulting contact formulation becomes very general and versatile, which is illustrated by several challenging examples. They include pressure- and gap- dependent bonding, exothermic bonding reactions, thermal hardening and thermal expansion, as well as simultaneous bonding and debonding. They are based on a monolithic finite element implementation using classical and isogeometric shape functions together with implicit time integration. Its full linearization, required for the Newton-Raphson solution method, is also provided for the six-field problem, as well as for several of its simplifications. If bonding sites are material points, the bonding variable can be condensed-out locally.

articles.title: Filament Formation via Collision-induced Magnetic Reconnection -- Kinematic Features
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.16205v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Collision-induced Magnetic Reconnection (CMR) mechanism has recently been proposed as a filament formation model that emphasizes the active role of magnetic fields. To enable better observational tests with data from modern telescopes, we provide more specific observable predictions for filaments formed via CMR. Two types of CMR kinematics are revealed in position-velocity (PV) diagrams. First, due to the nature of CMR, the midplane contains a it converging motion close to the filament and two it diverging motions farther from the filament. They exhibit a blueshift, redshift, blueshift, redshift (BRBR) velocity pattern along the line-of-sight when the collision midplane is inclined, giving rise to a special pattern in the PV-diagram. Second, the longitudinal PV-diagram along the filament spine exhibits a velocity oscillating pattern, which is currently attributed to the magnetic transport of gas clumps in the it converging motion. The first type of pattern involves emission primarily outside the filament, which can be confused with the environment. The second type, however, mainly emerges from gas inside the filament, thus more robust for observational tests. Both the integral-shaped filament and the Stick filament in the Orion A cloud show the velocity oscillation in PV-diagrams, although the spatial oscillation frequency and their velocity spread differ.
authors: Shuo Kong, Griselda Arroyo-Chávez, Volker Ossenkopf-Okada, Héctor G. Arce, Ralf S. Klessen, Duo Xu, Szu-Ting Chen

articles.title: AI Mindmeld: A Latent Interconnect Protocol
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs can act as scientific agents using tools to consult specialists and run experiments. Yet specialist information must enter their context, generally as text, images, audio or video: a bottleneck between models with rich, high-dimensional representations. We advocate direct representation exchange: a mindmeld conveying many properties, including information an LLM would not think to request. It should be extensible to new specialists, flexible across questions and tasks, and compositional across independently connected specialists without joint training. The Latent Interconnect Protocol (LIP) learns connectors mapping specialist representations into LLM internal states. Training only connectors keeps this practical as LLMs grow and evolve. We connect three protein and three small molecule specialists to Gemma 3 (4B and 12B parameters) and Kimi K2.6 (1T total, 32B active), freezing all pretrained models. Independently trained connectors provide useful information without changing the LLM or existing connectors, supporting familiar and new question types about unseen objects. We demonstrate zero-shot transfer to cross-domain tasks without joint training. Task performance and compositionality generally improve with LLM capability, with especially strong gains in zero-shot task transfer. Limitations remain: current LLMs were not trained for specialist representations as native inputs; access does not ensure reliable interpretation, integration or use in reasoning. We call on specialist developers to provide consistent representation interfaces and, especially, on LLM developers to train models to receive, combine and reason with these inputs. These efforts could expand scientific agents' information while preserving conventional tools' flexibility. Data, pretrained connectors, and code for training, evaluation and interactive inference: https://github.com/PolymathicAI/AI-Mindmeld
authors: Siavash Golkar, Jake Kovalic, Shirley Ho

articles.title: Generalizing Metropolis-Hastings for DAG Sampling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fundamental challenge in Bayesian network structure learning lies in efficiently approximating the posterior distribution of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). For large, high-dimensional datasets, the task remains beyond the capabilities of current methods. This work advances Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms by introducing novel moves that simultaneously resample the parents for multiple nodes of the DAG. At the core of these moves is duet sampling, a new generalization of the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm that selects two proposal distributions from a pool at each iteration. One is used for generating a candidate state of the Markov chain and another for evaluating the return to the current state; both are ingredients of an appropriately crafted acceptance criterion. Pairing different proposal distributions provides additional freedom and enables constructing Markov chains that mix more efficiently than their basic Metropolis-Hastings counterparts, at no additional computational cost. Experiments show that our new moves, both individually and in combination, outperform the previous state of the art, which relies on a more restrictive pool of moves. This advantage persists even when letting the previous methods leverage duet sampling to enhance their performance.

articles.title: Probing and Steering for Safety-Relevant Behaviours in Large Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Activation probes are computed directions in a language model's residual stream, used both to detect safety-relevant behaviours and, by adding their direction back into the stream, to steer them. We explore how the main design choices behind such probes interact, within one pipeline, on one model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), and across three behaviours: deception, high-stakes awareness and sycophancy. The pipeline crosses two estimators (difference-of-means and logistic regression) with three token-pooling schemes (last, mean and learned attention), selects appropriate layers to detect or steer a behaviour, and evaluates every direction twice: as a detector of the behaviour, and as a steering vector to push outputs towards the behaviour. Prior work read together suggests a read/write dissociation, in which logistic regression reads (detects) best but difference-of-means directions write (steer) best. We find that it holds for deception and high-stakes but not for sycophancy, where the pattern reverses. The reversal appears to follow partially from the data rather than from the estimators. The best pooling technique and the layer choice depend on the behaviour and data, and the layer that steers best can sit well before the layer that detects best. The right steering metric to use between changing a model's perception and eliciting behaviour depends on the task - and the two can disagree outright. The exported probes and directions power an interactive interface through which a user can score and steer text directly.

articles.title: Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap: Persistent Homology Enables Cross-Species Ion Channel Classification via Multimodal Graph Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protein classifiers are highly sensitive to evaluation protocol: random train/test splits induce phylogenetic leakage, allowing models to exploit taxon-specific correlations and substantially overestimate out-of-distribution performance. This issue is particularly acute for venom compound classification by ion-channel target (Ca2+, K+, Na+), where reported accuracies of 80-90% do not reflect generalization to unseen taxa. We formulate cross-species prediction as a structured distribution shift in which taxonomic identity acts as a confounder, requiring representations that capture structural features invariant across phylogeny. Using a shared multimodal backbone that fuses ESM-2 sequence embeddings with a disulfide-aware graph attention network, we systematically compare five structural inductive biases (spectral, Riemannian, SE(3)-invariant, statistical-manifold, and persistent-homology representations) under a leave-one-taxon-out evaluation protocol on a benchmark of 1,373 ColabFold-predicted venom compounds spanning five taxa. The persistent-homology representation summarizes backbone geometry through topological descriptors that are robust to local structural perturbations, providing an inductive bias toward phylogenetically invariant learning. Under conventional i.i.d. splits, all models achieve similar accuracy (81-86%), masking differences in inductive bias. Under taxonomic shift, this parity collapses: a sequence-only baseline drops to approximately 30%, the remaining geometric priors cluster at 54-55%, while our persistent-homology model (PH-GNN) achieves 63.4%, outperforming the next-best method by over 8 percentage points. These results demonstrate that random-split evaluation obscures meaningful differences in representation quality and identify topological representations as an effective inductive bias for learning under structured biological distribution shift.
authors: Arezoo Bybordi, Favour Achimba, Mariam Gelashvili, Jessy Ramirez, Weigang Qiu, Mandë Holford, Anita Raja

articles.title: Memory-Augmented Online Test-Time Adaptation for EEG Motor Imagery via Perturbation Consistency and Confidence Calibration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, electroencephalography (EEG)-based brain--computer interfaces (BCIs) have gained traction as portable neural measurement systems. However, the practical deployment of these instruments is often hindered by nonstationarity and cross-subject distribution shifts, which lead to significant intersubject inconsistency. Existing adaptation methods remain impractical for real-time measurement scenarios, as they typically require offline access to source or aggregated target data. To address these challenges, this article proposes memory-augmented online test-time adaptation (OTTA) with perturbation consistency and confidence calibration (MOPC), a source-free framework designed to enhance the reliability of BCI instrumentation. MOPC enables the measurement system to update its decoding parameters on the fly during the inference stage, facilitating single-pass adaptation without accessing sensitive source data. We introduce random-mask perturbations to enforce prediction consistency against inherent EEG signal noise and acquisition artifacts. Furthermore, a confidence-calibrated reweighting loss is designed to integrate feature-space similarity, effectively mitigating unreliable pseudolabels and class imbalance during continuous signal acquisition. To ensure system stability and prevent the catastrophic forgetting of established neural patterns, a lightweight memory module is incorporated to regularize parameter updates within a tight latency budget. Evaluated on the BCI IV IIb and OpenBMI datasets, MOPC achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming prior methods by 2.22~% and 3.67~%, respectively, while keeping the per-trial adaptation latency to approximately 40--60 ms. This study provides a robust, recalibration-free solution for real-time EEG decoding, marking a significant advancement in the precision and usability of practical BCI measurement instruments.
authors: Kunkun Zhang, Kehao Wu, Zhitao Chen, Haigen Hu, Qianwei Zhou

articles.title: Ground-Truth-First Benchmarking of Reinforcement Learning via Converse Optimality: From Smooth, Fully Observed Systems to Non-Smooth or Partially Observed Tasks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmarking in reinforcement learning is usually relative: algorithms are ranked by returns on environments with unknown optima. Distance to optimality remains unobservable, while conclusions may depend on reward design, stochasticity, hyperparameters, environment selection, and simulator details. We develop a ground-truth-first framework based on converse optimality, constructing each task with a certified optimal value function and policy withheld from learners and used only for evaluation. The framework unifies two modes: sensitivity benchmarking samples certified environments from continuous-time generators to assess robustness to task variation, while oracle-referenced comparison uses native discrete-time generators to evaluate policies via optimality gap, regret, and policy error. Continuous-time models support physically interpretable sensitivity studies but introduce dependence on the simulator step (Δ t) and numerical scheme. Native discrete-time models align the environment, oracle, and learner on the same transition law, eliminating external integration choices as a confounder. We reproduce quantitative results covering optimizer sensitivity and oracle-referenced comparisons on serial planar arms, dynamically extended nonholonomic vehicles, and quadrotor-inspired tasks. The methodology extends beyond smooth affine Gaussian systems: virtual-input pullback handles non-affine raw-action interfaces and finite-covariance non-Gaussian disturbances. A non-smooth converse optimality formulation enables certified benchmarks with kinked value functions and switching surfaces. For partially observed evaluation, an information-state formulation reduces benchmarking to converse optimality on a sufficient statistic and provides an information-penalty reference. Code, fixtures, and diagnostics are available on the public project page.
authors: Grégoire Ouerdane, Sinan Ibrahim, Stefan Streif, Pavel Osinenko

articles.title: Multi-Token Prediction and Alternative Tokenization Improve Learning Latent Multi-Hop Graph Search at Scale
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an unseen graph, a start node, s, and an end node, t, can a language model generate the shortest path from s to t? Prior work has found that models fail to learn this task as the graphs scale. We show that this failure has two causes: the supervision signal and the tokenization. First, we theoretically establish and empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of multi-token prediction (MTP), and show that the benefits of MTP are topologically agnostic. Second, we introduce alternative tokenizations and show that the two causes are orthogonal. Using these methods, we break through the scaling wall observed by prior work, consistently and stably learning to solve the task at scales far beyond previous limits.
authors: Arvid Frydenlund, FuTe Wong, Katherine Lambert, Frank Rudzicz

articles.title: PYTHIA, a transferable machine learning framework for simultaneous defect and adsorption site optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning has permeated material optimization, providing high value. Nevertheless, its re- liance on a high number of samples limits its applicability to relatively explored material families. In this paper we extend the applicability of machine learning to novel and understudied materials through the PYTHIA (Probabilistic Yet Transferable Hierarchical Interaction Architecture) framework. Pythia utilizes two of the most powerful machine learning concepts, foundational models and transfer learning. We employ a complex foundational model trained on a large dataset of chemically similar molecules, on a target that is physically close to our prediction target. Then, we freeze the weights and perform subspace alignment with the use of a transformer layer and add uncertainty quantification with gaussian processes. These two layers can be trained on a limited dataset yet allow us to leverage the gained knowl- edge and the studied materials and complex architectures. The resulting model is used as a surrogate for a Bayesian Optimization scheme. To showcase the robustness of the framework, we applied it to the investigation of adsorption and defect optimization of two distinct systems. Not only were we able to correctly and efficiently identify the optimal adsorption sites of even complex a
authors: Ioannis Kouroudis, Zhaosu Gu, Poonam, Leon Muller, Alessio Gagliardi

articles.title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass (sim220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.
authors: Qian Zhang, Shanqing Liu, Jerome Darbon, George Karniadakis

articles.title: Bridging Number-Theoretic Primality Testing And Algorithmic Optimization: An Adaptive Cryptographic Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The security of modern public-key cryptographic systems, such as RSA, Diffie-Hellman, and ECC, depends entirely on the computational intractability of the integer factorization and discrete logarithm problems. For these asymmetric algorithms to operate, a core requirement is that the system must be capable of generating, testing, and simultaneously proving the primality of extraordinarily large numbers. To meet those requirements, this study proposes a comprehensive framework, bridging clas- sical number theory with modern machine learning models and optimization algorithms. Specifically, the paper delineates an adaptive, arbitrary-precision architecture dedicated exclusively to primality testing. Concurrently, the research deeply analyzes the theoretical foundations of testing methods (both deterministic and probabilistic), hardware-level optimization techniques, and the application of quantum-secured entropy sources, while providing rigorous mathematical proofs to guarantee security even when the prime distribution is biased.
authors: Tran Minh Thanh, Vo Hoai Viet

articles.title: DRAFT: Decoding and Reconstructing 3D Room Layouts from fMRI and Camera Trajectories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31108v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) decoders reconstruct images and 3D objects, recovering the metric geometry of rooms from a moving viewpoint remains an open challenge. We introduce, to our knowledge for the first time, the task of reconstructing 3D layouts of held-out scenes using only the known camera trajectories and the fMRI signals of participants watching indoor walkthroughs, without any visual frames. The task is hard because of the temporal mismatch between rapid visual changes and blurred fMRI signals. Our method, DRAFT (Decoding and Reconstructing 3D room lAyouts from fMRI and Trajectories), extracts a compact layout representation from the early visual cortex and fuses this neural code with the geometric free space derived from camera motion. To evaluate it, we propose layout r, the Pearson correlation between predicted and ray-cast log depths. On ten held-out scenes (20 participants), DRAFT reaches a layout r of 0.480, outperforming the camera path alone (0.446) and seven fMRI decoders (at most 0.429). DRAFT also works as a plug-in that improves all seven decoders without retraining, raising their layout r from 0.171-0.429 to 0.487-0.493. Brain activity and camera motion can thus recover the metric layout of unseen rooms, a first step toward reconstructing the 3D spaces people see.
authors: Chi-Wei Lee, An-Kai Chen, Cheng-Han Chiang, Yi-Chun Chang, Po-Chih Kuo

articles.title: Can Entanglement-Induced Feature-Map Designs Improve Projected Quantum Kernels?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Projected quantum kernels (PQKs) have emerged as a notable approach to circumvent the hardness of machine learning tasks arising from the exponential dimensionality of the quantum Hilbert space. However, recent PQK studies often rely heavily on extensive classical hyperparameter tuning of the radial basis function (RBF) kernel parameter and the support vector machine regularization parameter. The extensive tuning can mask the true representational power of the underlying PQKs induced by quantum feature maps, which has not been explored in detail. Thus, this work aims to expose the structural capabilities of PQKs by isolating and evaluating their native inductive bias through comparisons between untuned and tuned PQKs against the RBF baseline. Furthermore, we propose novel quantum feature maps that leverage two-qubit entanglement to capture multivariate correlations in IoT data. The results show that extensive tuning can lead to competitive performance architectures, while our proposed entanglement topologies exhibit a significantly stronger native inductive bias. This reveals that superior quantum architectural design can yield structurally better PQKs with improvements arising from quantum-mechanical properties rather than from classical hyperparameter tuning.
authors: Ravi Kumar Jha, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes

articles.title: Automatic Differentiation for Inference on Partially Observed Markov Process Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2407.03085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automatic differentiation (AD) has driven recent advances in machine learning, including deep neural networks and Hamiltonian Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods. Partially observed nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems have proved resistant to AD techniques because widely used particle filter algorithms yield an estimated likelihood function that is discontinuous as a function of the model parameters. To resolve this, we create a theoretical framework that embeds two existing AD particle filter methods within a new class of algorithms. This new class permits a bias-variance tradeoff and hence a mean squared error substantially lower than the existing algorithms. This allows us to develop likelihood maximization algorithms suited to the Monte Carlo properties of the AD gradient estimate. Our algorithms require only a differentiable simulator for the latent dynamic system; by contrast, most previous approaches to AD likelihood maximization for particle filters require access to the system's transition probabilities. Numerical results indicate that a hybrid algorithm, using AD to refine a coarse solution from an iterated filtering algorithm, shows substantial improvement on current state-of-the-art methods on a challenging scientific benchmark problem.
authors: Kevin Tan, Aaron J. Abkemeier, Kunyang He, Giles Hooker, Edward L. Ionides

articles.title: Reducing QPU Calls in Variational Quantum Algorithms via Classical Offloading of Gradient Computation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2503.16361v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are a promising approach for leveraging near-term quantum computers, but trainability and quantum-resource costs remain major challenges. Here we address these challenges with the Hardware Efficient and dynamical LIe algebra supported Ansatz (HELIA) and two training methods combining the classical-enhanced g method with the quantum-based Parameter-Shift Rule (PSR). This distributes gradient estimation and training across classical and quantum hardware. We evaluate ground-state estimation of 6- to 18-qubit Hamiltonians using the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and quantum phase classification for Hamiltonians up to 12 qubits. For VQE, our methods improve accuracy and success rates, with a mean reduction in estimated logical quantum evaluations of up to 60% relative to Full-PSR training of the same ansatz. For classification, the largest improvement in mean peak test accuracy relative to Full-PSR is 2.8 percentage points. We also use these methods as a warm-start pretraining strategy for Hamiltonians with exponential-dimensional dynamical Lie algebras. Gradient diagnostics for the studied Hamiltonian configurations show slower gradient-variance decay than the selected deep hardware-efficient reference over the simulated system sizes, potentially paving the way for training large-qubit quantum models.
authors: Rahul Bhowmick, Harsh Wadhwa, Avinash Singh, Tania Sidana, Quoc Hoan Tran, Krishna Kumar Sabapathy

articles.title: Nested Sampling: A Critical and Comprehensive Theoretical Guide
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.17916v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The nested sampling (NS) technique has gained widespread attention, particularly in cosmology and astronomy, due to its ability to efficiently explore high-likelihood regions - a feature akin to an implicit likelihood optimization that underlies its success. While the full theoretical derivation of NS is complex and involves several approximations, the central challenge lies in sampling from the likelihood-constrained priors, which is crucial for its performance. This work provides a comprehensive and detailed exposition of NS derivation, clarifying both its theoretical foundations and practical challenges. We provide a thorough description of the NS procedure, emphasizing both its strengths and potential limitations. The connections between NS, importance sampling (IS), and vertical Monte Carlo are also discussed in detail. In doing so, this work seeks to deepen understanding of the method and to foster the development of future enhancements, novel variants, and more efficient implementations across a wide range of scientific applications. Thus, the main contribution of this work is twofold: it serves both as a tutorial for newcomers to the field and as a critical review for experienced practitioners.

articles.title: Accelerating Wildfire Hazard Mapping Across Canada with an AI Surrogate Modelling Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Canada's increasing wildfire activity requires frequent national hazard mapping to guide proactive mitigation, including fuel management, land-use planning, infrastructure protection, and evacuation routing. However, process-based wildfire simulation frameworks (e.g., BurnP3 and BurnP3+) rely on computationally intensive Monte Carlo simulations to model burn probability, fire intensity, and rate of spread. These workflows can take days to weeks to process a single regional modelling unit. To overcome these computational bottlenecks, we present three contributions developed through collaboration between AI researchers and wildfire modelling experts: (a) a standardized framework for training, fine-tuning, and evaluating AI surrogate models against process-based wildfire simulators; (b) a multi-task deep learning surrogate trained on national-scale data to emulate burn probability, mean fire intensity, and mean rate of spread at a fraction of the computational cost (seconds); and (c) domain-specific metrics and counterfactual evaluation protocols to probe out-of-distribution generalization. Integrating geospatial data (fuel, terrain, ignition likelihood) and regional weather, our model approximates BurnP3+ simulation outputs, achieving strong performance across agreement, rank-correlation, error, and spatial-overlap metrics. It preserves downstream hazard classifications and produces physically plausible responses to expert-informed counterfactual interventions. On a representative region, the surrogate achieves 806-fold end-to-end CPU acceleration and uses 13% of BurnP3+'s host memory, facilitating rapid scenario analysis.
authors: Hager Radi Abdelwahed, Toluwaleke Olutayo, Chirag Goel, Jana Osea, Aldo Zaimi, Tom Swystun, Sandy Erni, Francisco Emiliano Lopez Saavedra, Yan Boulanger, Gaétan Marceau Caron

articles.title: Reducing Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Forecast Error through Tree-Anchored Expert Combination
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A strong direct tree model may remain the best standalone photovoltaic forecaster, yet a weighted combination can reduce its residual errors. We examine whether complementary temporal predictors can lower the tree's mean absolute error (MAE) over 15--240 minutes without weaker ensemble members degrading performance. The candidate bank contains LightGBM and seven neural implementations with different temporal representations. A combiner fitted to MAE has nonnegative weights that sum to one. Unhelpful candidates can receive zero weight, while the tree anchors the combination and provides a development-stage fallback. The main design shares weights across horizons; horizon-specific weights and alternative losses test whether further complexity is needed. On 56,078 windows from two co-located public PVDAQ systems, the historical shared-MAE policy reduces scaled MAE by 3.21% relative to the tree. The latest bounded neural correction does not reduce MAE further than this static combination. The results support selective combination of complementary predictions in this bank rather than equal averaging or indiscriminate addition of modules. Both analyses reuse a previously inspected evaluation period. They do not establish independent replication, weather-specific causation or universal gains from eight experts.
authors: Sun Ze, Zhou Liguo, Xu Yuqing, Yu Lei, Jiang Mingming, Alois Knoll

articles.title: Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Individual preferences often become visible only after deployment, when a user accepts one decision or revokes it in favor of another. Jev-style typed interfaces make this feedback explicit by identifying the selected action and, under revocation, the decision it replaces. We study how these consequences persist across requests as Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback (Jev-DLC). Jev-DLC treats each correction as both evidence about a recurring action identity and a directed relation between the preferred and rejected choices. It preserves these signals in complementary bounded channels above a frozen scorer and combines their scores to shape the next decision. The method retains no raw interaction history, adds no scorer call, and performs no runtime language-model backward pass. We also introduce TCPA-Bench, a chronological suite that credits a correction only through its effect on later decisions. On TCPA-Repeat, Jev-DLC reaches 44.83% user-macro accuracy overall, 2.43 points above Recent-4 history replay. After at least two earlier feedback events, it reaches 56.07%, a 7.54-point margin over the strongest reported comparison at this depth. These results show how explicit typed corrections can become compact causal state for continual personalization.
authors: Yangyang Feng, Jianle Gan, Zhuoyan Feng, Chengwei Qin

articles.title: Who Is Sycophantic to Whom? Confident LLMs, Human Deference, and the Collapse of Trust Calibration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Research on sycophancy asks whether large language models (LLMs) bend towards what their users want to hear. We ask the reverse question: when an LLM is confident, consistent, and wrong, do users bend towards it? In a within-subjects experiment, 32 participants learned up to five science topics by chatting with five assistants built on the same model (GPT-5-mini). Unknown to participants, each assistant's briefing had 0, 25, 50, 75, or 100% of its facts replaced by plausible falsehoods, and every assistant spoke with full confidence. A surprise quiz after each topic offered the correct fact, the planted falsehood, and two distractors, with a confidence rating for every answer. Across 104 quizzes and 1,040 answers, scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10, and the planted option was chosen on 60% of falsified items against 11% of correctly taught ones (odds ratio 12.5). Transcript coding showed that whenever the assistant stated a falsehood, it was adopted about 65% of the time at every falsification level. Absorbed falsehoods were held with high confidence (8.4/10), the modeled confidence advantage of right over wrong answers vanished, and the discrimination of confidence for correctness fell from an AUROC of 0.70 to chance, while post-task trust ratings barely moved. Participants tended to return to the chat more when the assistant was worse, but returning went with more absorption, not less, and 30% of all turns pasted quiz questions back to the source being checked. The assistant itself was almost never sycophantic and never conceded under pushback. We introduce a baseline-corrected Human Deference Index to quantify this human-side sycophancy and argue that trustworthiness is a property of the human-AI pair, that sycophancy evaluations should measure both directions, and that learning interfaces must make reliability legible claim by claim.
authors: Deepthika S, Pawni Yadav, B. Sankar

articles.title: The roles of nonharmonic damping and spatial correlation of atomic movements in determining the amplitudes and attenuation frequencies of electro-optic coefficients
articles.abstract: Large electro-optic coefficients make ferroelectric materials attractive for high-speed optical modulation in optical communication. However, in materials like barium titanate this coefficient decreases markedly with increasing modulation frequency. This decrease can limit the bandwidth of electro-optic modulators, making it essential to understand the underlying attenuation mechanism. In this paper, we find that it is the nonharmonic damping of the phonon modes, instead of the phonon mode frequency itself, that plays an important role in determining both the amplitude of the low-frequency electro-optic coefficient and its attenuation frequency. Furthermore, we find that spatial correlations in atomic movements across many unit cells play an important role in determining both the static electro-optic coefficient and its attenuation frequency. We tested this hypothesis in tetragonal BaTiO3, where the electro-optic coefficient is experimentally well determined. Molecular-dynamics simulations using a machine-learned HSE potential give a low-frequency electro-optic coefficient of 590 pm/V and an attenuation frequency of approximately 137 GHz, both comparable to the experimental values.

articles.title: The Partial-Accelerator Picture of Magnetic Reconnection in Solar Flares: Four Results from Order-of-Magnitude Physics
articles.abstract: We apply the competing-balance methodology of order-of-magnitude physics to particle acceleration and radiation in solar-flare magnetic reconnection, taking as the unifying basis the fact that flare-accelerated electrons are only a few percent of the total electron population. Four results follow. (1) An explicit scaling of the thick–thin transition energy with plasma beta, Ec ∝ β1/2 B L1/2 T−1/2. (2) An energy-budget check showing that in the best-measured events the nonthermal electrons carry only ~10−3 of the released magnetic energy, so the percent-level efficiency is a supply problem rather than an energy problem. (3) A closure test: with the magnetic field and the reconnection electric field taken from direct measurements, MA ≈ 2 × 10−2 follows, and requiring the inflow to supply the fitted nonthermal injection rate fixes the supply area at 1.3 × 1019 and 8.7 × 1018 cm2—regions 35 and 29 Mm across, i.e. areas agreeing to a factor of 1.45. The constraint on beta is one-sided, since low beta facilitates collisionless reconnection; what replaces the withdrawn lower limit is a budget requirement rather than a ceiling, driving a low-beta source to β ~ 1 calling for the local dissipation of about three quarters of its magnetic energy density. In this reading β is an output of the flare, which quenches its own reconnection once the heated plasma reaches the pinching threshold. (4) A supply-limited Fermi scaling of the hard X-ray photon index, γ − 2 ∝ (MA/10−2)−(q−p), whose normalisation agrees with the fitted kappa index to within a factor of three, which reproduces the slope of the published cross-event regression and predicts its curvature, and which predicts that q − p is of order unity across events but vanishes in time within one event. The results are self-consistent to within one order of magnitude and yield five falsifiable predictions.

articles.title: Neutral Morphological Masking: Constructive Neutral Evolution of Chiral Scaffolds for Information-Maintaining Artificial Cells
articles.abstract: A minimal synthetic cell that completes a full replication–growth–division cycle still demonstrates nothing about self-maintenance unless it also carries a state variable that can degrade under a genuine environmental stress and be actively defended. Our earlier proposal (Sandler, 2026b) specified such a module — chiral order Uχ as a programmable memory, D-glucose glycation as a stress channel, and circular dichroism (CD) as a sensor — but treated the robustness that protects Uχ as a static, hand-designed surface property, uₛ. That is an adaptationist assumption dressed as an engineering parameter, and it is also why the initial submission read as disconnected from current artificial-life research: a designed robustness knob does not need to cite the literature on how robustness actually arises in living systems. This revision addresses both problems by fusing the chiral-order module with Constructive Neutral Evolution (CNE), the framework in which biological complexity accumulates through selectively neutral steps rather than adaptive design (Stoltzfus, 1999), and specifically with the interlocking-masking mechanism recently formalized for multi-subunit complexes in the Quandary Den artificial-life model (Walsh, 2026). In the synthesized framework, random neutral mutations introduce structural protrusions in one subunit of a multi-subunit chiral scaffold; complementary recesses that neutrally arise in partner subunits mask these protrusions to preserve packing order, and the accumulated interlocking geometry incidentally occludes the scaffold's glycation-vulnerable amine sites. Geometric surface uniformity, uₛ, is therefore reframed as an emergent, unselected byproduct of a masking ratchet rather than a design input. We give the resulting multi-subunit dynamical system, retain the original module's mechanistic lattice Monte Carlo and site-diluted XY-model machinery as validation of the underlying stress–state–repair physics, and add a new toy evolutionary simulation demonstrating the internal consequences of the proposed masking rules: a one-directional ratchet in interlocking complexity, an incidental decline in the emergent glycation-rate constant, and accidental cross-protection against a novel stress shock in lineages that accumulated complexity under no direct selection for glycation resistance. We situate the proposal explicitly against current artificial-life and synthetic-biology literature on self-maintaining and homeostatic artificial cells, give an expanded, falsifiable prediction set, and lay out a staged validation roadmap.

articles.title: Satoyama destruction and homogeneity as sources of environmental vulnerability in Tokyo
articles.abstract: Satoyama are marginal areas located between foothills and arable land in Japan. These landscapes support a wide range of species and are regarded as indicators of biodiversity and sustainable agriculture. However, deforestation in these areas has increasingly threatened local ecosystems. This study examined the ecological and environmental effects of Satoyama degradation and urban landscape homogenisation in Tokyo and surrounding areas using a “surface-to-line” analytical framework. Landscape analysis showed reductions in forested and vegetated areas between 1976 and 2024, accompanied by increased urban development and the expansion of concrete-covered surfaces. Meteorological data indicated increasing temperatures and declining humidity in Tokyo since the 1990s. Field observations showed altered behaviour of Japanese pygmy woodpeckers following the removal of large trees. Overall, current urban-development and land-management practices contribute to increasing ecological and landscape homogeneity, potentially reducing environmental resilience. The findings suggest that development projects in Satoyama may be deviating from their original social and ecological purposes.

articles.title: Mn-Driven Structural Modulation and PANI-Assisted Charge Transfer in WO₃-Based Supercapacitor Electrodes
articles.abstract: Electrodes with fast kinetics of electron transfer, many electrochemically active sites and stable structure are needed for fabrication of highly efficient electrochemical energy storage devices. Tungsten oxide (WO₃) can be considered as potential pseudocapacitive material; but rather low electrical conductivity and restricted number of active sites negatively influence on electrochemical properties of this compound. In our work, Mn-doped tungsten oxide nanomaterials were fabricated and studied as electrode materials for supercapacitors. The formation of highly crystalline tungsten oxide with monoclinic structure was proved by X-ray diffraction studies, while the presence of Mn in tungsten oxide structure was confirmed by the structural and vibrational characteristics, observed in FTIR spectroscopy, namely W–O, W = O and Mn–O bonds. The results of electron microscopy studies showed that the particles were uniformly dispersed, with average particle size of 19.86 nm. It should be noted that the electrode showed a high specific capacitance value of 1756 F g⁻¹ with 1 A g⁻¹ current density, along with an energy density of 61 Wh kg⁻¹ and a power density of 1784 W kg⁻¹. Additionally, cycling stability was evident for the electrode, which indicates the capability of the material to function properly in terms of energy storage capacity. The improved electrochemical performance can be associated with the combined effects of Mn doping such as enhanced conductivity, larger electrochemically available surface area, and creation of additional redox centers. Thus, the presented study proves the capability of Mn doping in tuning the structural and electrochemical properties of WO₃.

articles.title: Quantum Algorithms for Computational Economics: A Critical Review of Simulation, Optimization, and Near-Term Evidence
articles.abstract: Quantum computing is increasingly discussed as a possible source of new computational methods for economics, but its relevance depends on whether economic bottlenecks match quantum algorithmic primitives. This critical review evaluates that match for computational economics. It synthesizes work on quantum amplitude estimation and quantum Monte Carlo for simulation and risk measurement; quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO), Ising formulations, quantum annealing, and the quantum approximate optimization algorithm for discrete optimization; and quantum linear-algebra and machine-learning primitives for econometrics and model solution. The review argues that there is no general-purpose quantum algorithm for economics analogous to Shor's algorithm for factoring. Credible claims are problem-class specific and depend on state preparation, output requirements, conditioning, hardware noise, embedding overhead, and comparison with strong classical and quantum-inspired baselines. The most mature economic applications are derivative pricing and financial risk, payment-system liquidity optimization, quantum Monte Carlo for stress testing, and early quantum-annealing formulations of dynamic programming. Transportation and infrastructure applications are relevant mainly as networked economic optimization problems. The article proposes an evidence ladder for quantum computational economics and a research agenda centered on reproducible benchmarks, economically meaningful objective functions, end-to-end resource accounting, and evaluation by economic value rather than hardware novelty. JEL Classification: C02; C15; C61; C63; C88; E37; G11; G17; R41

articles.title: Intrinsic Vectorial Gradiometry via Quantum Control of a Spin-based Sensor
articles.abstract: Gradiometry provides a versatile alternative to passive environmental shielding in quasi-static magnetometry, effectively suppressing background noise through differential signal extraction. Nevertheless, traditional implementations rely on multi-sensor architectures restricted to spatial gradients, where subtracting signals from independent detectors involves imperfect suppression of common-mode noise and artifacts, limiting their sensitivity. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a quantum control sequence that enables intrinsic temporal and spatial vectorial gradiometry of magnetic fields using a single quantum sensor. Our method provides direct access to first and higher-order derivatives of the magnetic field and extended applicability via auxiliary nuclear spin memory. We showcase this protocol on an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond and combine it with mechanical control to realize high-precision differential sensing. Through detailed numerical simulations, we demonstrate the performance of our scheme in two critical DC magnetometry applications: (i) vector magnetic anomaly detection and (ii) non-invasive gradiometry of neuronal action potentials.

articles.title: Physics-Informed AI Surrogate Modelling of Thermal and Hydraulic Losses in Omani Crude Oil Pipelines Using RHLI-Based Analysis, Uncertainty- Quantification, and Explainable AI
articles.abstract: Efficient crude-oil pipeline transportation is central to the energy supply chain, yet thermal and hydraulic energy losses raise pumping-energy demand, operating cost, and associated emissions. Predicting these losses normally relies on high-fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), which is too slow for real-time operational decision-making. This study develops a physics-informed artificial-intelligence surrogate that predicts Total Heat Loss, Head Loss, and Total Power Loss for Omani crude-oil pipelines transported under non-isothermal, viscoplastic (Bingham–Papanastasiou) conditions. A dataset of 962 high-fidelity COMSOL simulations across a three-segment serial pipeline was used to engineer physically interpretable features such as Reynolds number, Bingham number, a Thermo-Hydraulic Ratio, and a novel Rheological Heat-Loss Index (RHLI), and to train and cross-validate machine-learning and ensemble models. Under five-fold cross-validation, tree-based ensembles achieved high accuracy, with Heat Loss the most learnable target (cross-validated R² ≈ 1.0) and the Stacking Ensemble providing the most stable performance across all three targets. Uncertainty quantification through quantile regression, conformal prediction, and calibration analysis yielded reliable prediction intervals (Mean Calibration Error 0.0211; empirical 95% coverage 97.4%), while SHAP analysis identified Ambient Temperature as the dominant driver of Heat Loss, consistent with heat-transfer physics. The framework offers a fast, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware surrogate to support energy-efficient pipeline operation and real-time digital-twin monitoring.

articles.title: Can Regulatory Technology (RegTech) Boost Financial Performance? Evidence From Indian Commercial Banks
articles.abstract: This study empirically investigates the impact of regulatory technology (RegTech) adoption on the financial performance of Indian commercial banks. Utilizing a comprehensive panel dataset of 32 listed banks from 2016 to 2025, the research employs Python-based text-mining techniques on published annual reports to construct a novel RegTech adoption index, which is bifurcated into Core Regulatory Technology and RegTech Enabling Technology. To account for the dynamic persistence of bank profitability and resolve potential endogeneity issues, the study utilizes a two-step System GMM estimator alongside baseline Random Effects modeling. The empirical results reveal a significant asymmetrical relationship. Investments in RegTech Enabling Technology such as artificial intelligence and big data yield a strong, positive, and statistically significant enhancement to the Return on Assets (ROA). Conversely, Core Regulatory Technology dedicated strictly to automated compliance acts primarily as a mandatory operational safeguard, demonstrating a statistically insignificant impact on overall profitability. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis uncovers that the financial benefits of foundational enabling technologies are heavily concentrated among large institutions and private sector banks, whereas the substantial capital expenditures required for core compliance systems actively compress the asset returns of large banks. These core findings are rigorously validated through extensive robustness checks, including the use of alternative dependent variables (ROE), lagged effects, outlier removal, and a Monte Carlo placebo test. Ultimately, this research provides vital strategic insights for bank management and policymakers regarding the operational costs and monetization potential of digital compliance infrastructures.

articles.title: High-Accuracy Prediction of Complex Permittivity in Ternary Composites Using Parameters Provided by Binary Systems
articles.abstract: Accurate prediction of the frequency-dependent complex permittivity of ternary composites remains challenging because constituent parameters obtained through inverse modeling are model dependent and are often re-estimated for different composite systems. Here, a binary-informed mixing-law framework was developed for polyaniline (PANI)/carbonyl iron powder (CIP)/polyurethane (PU) composites over 2–18 GHz. Maxwell–Garnett (MG), coherent-potential (CP), and Bruggeman (BR) models were first compared using the same PANI/PU dataset, and MG provided the most consistent overall performance for retrieving the model-dependent effective constituent response of PANI. The retrieved PANI response was examined using a modified Debye–conductivity model and independently assessed through cross-matrix prediction of PANI/paraffin composites without parameter recalibration. The binary-derived effective constituent responses of PANI and CIP were subsequently used as fixed inputs in an MG-based ternary expression. Without fitting the ternary dielectric spectra, the model reproduced the measured complex permittivity of five PANI/CIP/PU formulations at a fixed total filler loading of 30 wt.% and one PANI/PU binary endpoint with good overall agreement. The resulting R² values were 0.9891–0.9953 for ε′ and 0.9375–0.9963 for ε″. The corresponding NRMSE values were 5.62–11.71% for ε′ and 12.74–18.95% for five of the six ε″ datasets, while one narrow-response dataset exhibited a higher NRMSE of 35.12%. These results demonstrate that binary-derived effective constituent parameters can support forward permittivity prediction without ternary-specific recalibration, providing a practical basis for reducing experimental screening and guiding composition selection along the investigated composition path.

articles.title: SoK: Secure Software-Based Multi-Domain Data Segregation
articles.abstract: Modern mission-critical coordination demands seamless communication across multiple domains. Traditionally, Voice Communication Systems (VCS) have relied on physically separated Red/Black architectures to ensure voice and data segregation. While these hardware-based methods provide strong security assurances and remain foundational in high-security contexts, they can introduce significant complexity and scalability challenges as mission parameters expand into highly dynamic, multi-domain integrations. As defence, emergency response, and critical infrastructure operations increasingly require interoperable, flexible, and cost-efficient communication environments, there is a growing need to understand whether software-based approaches can provide comparable assurance while supporting modern operational requirements. This SoK characterises a transition to software-based Multi-Domain Data Segregation (MDDS) by integrating systems security, networking, and cryptography. Its goal is to consolidate existing research, identify shared architectural patterns, and address the security challenges facing next-generation high-assurance software-based VCS architectures. By assessing software-defined and virtualized approaches, this SoK supports the development of scalable, high-assurance VCS architectures that facilitate secure real-time coordination across diverse operational domains. Specifically, this SoK examines the security implications of Software-Defined Networking, Network Slicing, Separation Kernels, and Cross-Domain Solutions while addressing challenges posed by quantum computing through Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). As the first comprehensive synthesis of the shift from hardware-enforced isolation to software-based segregation, this SoK serves as an essential foundation for researchers and industry stakeholders seeking to advance secure, adaptable, and future-ready VCS infrastructures for mission-critical operations.

articles.title: Proteomic and functional insights into spinal neuroimmune maladaptation: dual-level modulation of mast cell-neural crosstalk by ultramicronized palmitoylethanolamide
articles.abstract: Repeated morphine administration drives spinal neuroimmune mechanisms contributing to analgesic tolerance and hyperalgesia. We investigated the contribution of mast cell-derived mediators to spinal neuroinflammation and the homeostatic effects of ultramicronized palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) using rat organotypic spinal cord slice cultures. Slices exposed to morphine were treated with conditioned medium from activated RBL-2H3 mast cells. Mast cell-derived conditioned medium induced a robust neuroinflammatory response, upregulating IL-6, IL-1β, CCL2, and PTX3 expression, and markedly enhancing the release of the pro-nociceptive neuropeptide CGRP. These alterations were accompanied by reduced neuronal marker expression and impaired astrocytic reactivity in the spinal dorsal horn. Notably, upstream mast cell pretreatment with PEA modified their secretory activity, blunting subsequent spinal inflammatory cascades. Quantitative proteomic analysis revealed that conditioned medium derived from PEA-treated RBL-2H3 cells extensively reshaped the spinal microenvironment, rescuing extracellular matrix components (such as collagen VI), downregulating neurodegenerative markers (including SIRT2 and BIN1), and inducing protective regulators like LGALS1. Downstream tissue-level application of ultramicronized PEA directly to the spinal slices replicated these beneficial actions, significantly attenuating inflammatory transcription and CGRP release while restoring neuronal and astrocytic homeostatic profiles. Collectively, these findings suggest that mast cell-derived factors promote spinal neuroimmune maladaptation, which is effectively countered by ultramicronized PEA via a dual-level mechanism acting on both the mast cell secretome and the spinal tissue interface. This integrated approach offers a promising translational strategy to preserve opioid efficacy and mitigate central sensitization.

articles.title: Experiment shows when quantum 'cat' states stop bouncing back
articles.abstract: Quantum systems can occupy superpositions, quantum states that combine different possibilities. For instance, a microwave field can be prepared in a superposition of an empty state and a state that contains microwave light.

articles.title: Quantum interference traps electron waves in metal for first time
articles.abstract: Ever since quantum mechanics first described particles, like electrons, as rippling waves, researchers have wondered if those waves could be trapped in place. Writing today in Science a century later, a team of Columbia University researchers reports waves of electrons becoming trapped for the first time in a metal called Pd₅AlI₂.

articles.title: Nature of the bosonic edge phase in a double quantum spin Hall insulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Field-theoretic analysis has predicted that the edge of a double quantum spin Hall insulator (DQSHI) can undergo an interaction-driven transition from a phase with fermionic edge modes into one with only bosonic modes. All single-fermion edge excitations are gapped in this bosonic edge phase, but fermion pairs remain gapless, leading to distinct experimental signatures. We numerically simulate the interacting DQSHI edge and verify the existence of the bosonic edge phase. This calculation requires an explicit bulk embedding of the DQSHI edge, due to its mixed anomaly between charge and S^z conservation. We hence employ segment DMRG on an infinite two-dimensional cylinder, where the DQSHI bulk is modeled in terms of two copies of the spin-up lowest Landau level, combined with their time-reversed counterparts. We find that interactions can open a single-fermion gap at the DQSHI edge while fermion pairs remain gapless, matching the predictions for the bosonic edge phase. We find the scaling of the single-fermion gap with interaction strength to be consistent with field-theoretic calculations, and discuss the relevance of the bosonic edge phase to twisted homobilayers of WSe₂ and MoTe₂. We elaborate on the methodological extension of the segment geometry used here to other topological phases with edge anomalies.
authors: Andreas Feuerpfeil, Ronny Thomale, Trithep Devakul, Nicolas Regnault, Julian May-Mann

articles.title: Discrete time liquids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response. We identify these switches as time-solitons: topological defects in temporal order that preserve local period doubling while destroying long-range temporal coherence, thereby producing the time liquid state. We propose a minimal model which reproduces the distribution of temporal correlations of the many-body system, suggesting a general description of the time liquid as a time crystal with a finite density of time-solitons. Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.
authors: Zuo Wang, Paul M. Schindler, Marin Bukov, Marios H. Michael

articles.title: Charge-monitored Luttinger liquid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss phases of interacting fermionic Luttinger liquids without particle number conservation, such as those in proximity to a superconductor, subjected to weak continuous measurements of their particle density, in the regime where the bosonization approach is applicable. We show that the phases of these systems are controlled by the competition between measurements, which favor the area-law phase and particle tunneling in and out of the Luttinger liquid, which favors the volume-law phase. The volume-law phase in this system is always charge fuzzy. We show that within this framework, the phase boundary between the two phases is given by a universal dependence of the Luttinger parameter on the measurement rate. This behavior can be contrasted with the non-universal phase boundaries in more generic highly excited one dimensional systems whose behavior is no longer captured by the Luttinger liquid framework.

articles.title: Charge Density Waves and In-Gap States in Coupled Chains and Moiré Superlattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge density waves (CDWs) arise from the interplay between electrons and lattice distortions and are a hallmark of low-dimensional systems. Here we study coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains, both lattice-matched ladders and lattice-mismatched moiré superlattices, and find a rich set of CDW phases together with symmetry-protected bound states. In lattice-matched chains, the competition between electron-phonon coupling and interchain tunneling drives a sequence of CDW phases, including staggered dimers, trimers, and incommensurate states. These phases are generally gapped and host bound states protected by crystalline symmetries rather than chiral symmetry, and are therefore not pinned to zero energy. Lattice mismatch further reconstructs these phases into long-period supermoiré CDWs, with an ordered array of defects, pinned to the moiré length scale, that host localized electronic states. Interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch thus emerge as natural control parameters for CDW order and bound states in one-dimensional chains.

articles.title: Quantum Phases and Structural Transitions of Bosons in Bubble-Shaped Confinements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structural properties and superfluid behavior of soft-core bosons confined in a spherical bubble trap at large particle numbers (N łe 1800). Using Path Integral Monte Carlo simulations with worm algorithm sampling in continuous space, we show that increasing N drives a sequence of layering transitions: beyond the established bilayer supersolid, a third concentric layer of clusters emerges at N approx 1800. By analyzing the distribution of permutation cycles distribution, we demonstrate that a finite superfluid fraction (fₛ approx 10%) persists even in this multi-layer regime. These findings clarify the role of particle number in driving layer formation on curved manifolds, offering a concrete guide for future experiments with bubble-trapped bosons.
authors: Fabio Cinti, Gabriele Costa, Giuseppe Pellicane, Santi Prestipino, Matteo Ciardi

articles.title: Unrestricted Binary Tree State for the Fermionic Hubbard Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary tree states have been introduced as compact correlated pair wave functions that improve upon the antisymmetrized geminal power by adding variational flexibility. Here, we extend the binary tree state to the fermionic half-filled Hubbard model using restricted and unrestricted orbitals. Although the ansatz is seniority zero in its optimized pairing basis, its expansion in the original Hubbard site basis can contain nonzero site- seniority character, while unrestricted orbital optimization provides additional flexibility through independent spin-up and spin-down orbitals. This provides a mechanism for a paired ansatz to describe the singly occupied configurations that dominate the repulsive Hubbard model at large U/t. We find that unrestricted BTS closely approaches optimized DOCI in the repulsive regime, substantially improves upon AGP, and reproduces DOCI density correlations more accurately than pCCD
authors: Mahroo Mirabdolhagh Hazaveh, Armin Khamoshi, Fei Gao, Thomas M. Henderson, Gustavo E. Scuseria

articles.title: Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction i[Pₓ,P_y] alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, łanglei[Pₓ,P_y]ångle=-sqrt3p²łangle O₃ångle. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with nₘ̊ ₑₓproptoτ_Q⁻¹, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.

articles.title: Cluster property and entanglement in the superconducting state
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the conditions for satisfying the cluster property in the superconducting state. Using these conditions, we show that the cluster property employed when deriving the order parameter of the superconducting state (OPSS) holds true, and that the OPSS is given by {}_Słangle Ψ | hatψ(x)hatψ(x') | Ψ ångle_S, where |Ψångle_S is the superconducting state, and where hatψ(x) is the field operator of superconducting electrons. This provides a resolution to the long-standing concern raised by Leggett et al. regarding particle-number fluctuation in the superconducting state. In addition, by considering the entanglement between two particles composed of the maximum geminal of the BCS ground state [J. Phys. Commun. 5, 095003 (2021)], it is confirmed that the larger the deviation from the conditions for satisfying the cluster property becomes, the greater the magnitude of the entanglement becomes. This shows not only the effectiveness of the conditions for satisfying the cluster property but also the justification of the OPSS that has been commonly used.

articles.title: String Order in Quench Dynamics as a Probe of Quantum Phase Transitions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the anisotropic XY chain in a transverse field by introducing a global string order parameter and examining its equilibrium behavior and its quench dynamics from a fully polarized initial state. The corresponding string operator is defined as the product of local projected spin operators over the entire chain. The nonequilibrium order parameter is the long-time average of the logarithm of the string-operator expectation value per site after the quench.For the ground state, its field derivative is singular on the Ising critical lines; after the quench, the steady-state response also records the field boundaries and the anisotropy transition. We derive analytically the nonanalytic behavior of the order parameter at the quantum critical lines. Our results reveal a hidden nonlocal order underlying this paradigmatic model of conventional quantum phase transitions. They also connect measurable spin populations with equilibrium and dynamical topological structure.

articles.title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random InₓGa₁₋ₓN alloys. Increasing the In content from x=13.5% to x=22% progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. This generates additional low-Q components and enhances the Auger coupling by more than five orders of magnitude relative to pristine GaN. Thus, we provide a microscopic explanation for the competing trends in radiative and Auger recombination. More broadly, our results establish localization contrast as a mechanism through which disorder can control optical and carrier-carrier interactions in semiconductors.
authors: Arsineh Apelian, Tanay Tak, Xuance Jiang, Tsung-Yin Tsai, James S. Speck, Vojtech Vlcek

articles.title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solution-phase synthesis of monolayer hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites is constrained by rapid out-of-plane crystal growth, uncontrolled nucleation, and strong interlayer aggregation, yielding flakes of only a few μm. We introduce a steric-engineering ternary-solvent growth strategy to synthesize monolayer and few-layer A2MX4 hybrid perovskites with exceptionally large surface areas. By combining alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive, out-of-plane stacking is suppressed. Using (PEA)2CuCl4 as a model system, monolayers with lateral areas exceeding 1000 μm2 are achieved, representing a massive dimensional increase over conventional methods.
