Molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations show that longer-chain alcohols reorganize precursor solvation, while solvent volatility prolongs edge-mediated precursor transport during annealing. This strategy demonstrates universal applicability across diverse organic spacer cations (PEA+, F-PEA+, PentA+), metal centers (Cu2+, Mn2+, Pb2+), and halides (Cl-, Br-, I-). The large lateral dimensions enable direct, solvent-free electrical contact fabrication via physical shadow masking, bypassing chemical degradation from solvents used in conventional lithography. Planar devices fabricated from isolated ultrathin (PEA)2PbI4 channels exhibit ultra-low dark currents down to the 10⁻¹⁵ - 10⁻¹³ A range, enabling femtowatt-to-picowatt static power consumption, ~ 0.2 pW at 5 V, a 250-fold reduction relative to drop-cast films, while maintaining a high light-to-dark current ratio of 4.3 x 102. This work establishes precise steric and solvation control as a paradigm for scalable, compositionally diverse, low-static-power monolayer 2D perovskite optoelectronics.
authors: Shankeerthan Kalyanasundaram, Swarit Dwivedi, Sanje Mahasivam, Christopher R. McNeill, Sudha Mokkapati

articles.title: Fit-error corrected auxiliary master equation approach for low-temperature nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The auxiliary master equation approach (AMEA) is a nonperturbative impurity solver for steady-state nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). It replaces the physical hybridization function by that of a small auxiliary open quantum system, whose parameters are fitted to reproduce it, and then solves the resulting many-body problem essentially exactly. AMEA's accuracy is thus limited by the quality of this fit: since the fastest-varying part of the hybridization is set by the distribution function, whose Fermi edges sharpen at low temperature, the fit tends to overestimate the temperature, especially for weak reservoir coupling. For the auxiliary hybridization itself, however, AMEA's self-energy is essentially exact. We correct for the fit error by estimating, via an approximate solver applicable to arbitrary hybridization functions, the ratio between the self-energies of the physical and auxiliary hybridizations, and using it to extend AMEA's self-energy from the auxiliary to the physical case. This fit-error correction becomes exact whenever either the fit or the approximate solver is exact. We benchmark the scheme using the nonequilibrium Kajueter-Kotliar iterated perturbation theory (IPT), generalized here to spin-polarized solutions, as the approximate solver; other approximate solvers, such as the noncrossing approximation, can be used as well. Applied to an Anderson impurity model with a spin-polarized bath, and within DMFT to a Hubbard layer weakly coupled to two metallic reservoirs, the correction largely removes the spurious heating from the AMEA fit and from insufficient thermalization by the reservoirs, while preserving the correct description of the Mott insulator, which IPT alone cannot fully recover.
authors: Sebastian Alois Fuchs, Enrico Arrigoni, Tommaso Maria Mazzocchi

articles.title: Broadband emitter localization and prefabrication two-photon interference from InAs/InP quantum dots monolithically grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a monolithic telecom C-band single-photon platform based on low-density InAs/InP quantum dots grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector, with simulated upward light-extraction efficiency exceeding 10% within the 40 nm spectral band. Enhanced light extraction is crucial for wide-field photoluminescence imaging, enabling approximately 3 nm statistical centroid-localization precision of QD emitters due to improved signal-to-noise ratio. The identified charged exciton emitting at 1549.5 nm exhibits single-photon emission purity up to 94.7%, validated by a raw peak-area integration under pulsed quasi-resonant excitation. Under these conditions, photons emitted sequentially from the unprocessed planar structure reveal a raw two-photon interference visibility of 51% of the photon wave packet within the 2 ns time window and 41% over a 4 ns integration window, all without Purcell enhancement typical for cavity-embedded emitters. Combining broadband extraction, high photon coherence, and emitter preselection on a native III-V wafer, this architecture paves the way for marker-based deterministic fabrication of high-quality monolithic nanophotonic devices.
authors: Paweł Mrowiński, Jan Śmigiel, Mikołaj Badura, Beata Ściana, Wojciech Kijaszek, Emilia Zikeba-Ostój, Paweł Holewa, Marcin Syperek

articles.title: Chiroptical Valleytronic in SnSe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum geometric properties of Bloch electrons play a central role in governing light-matter interactions and transport phenomena in solids. Here, we report quantum-geometric chiroptical selection rules that generate a helicity-dependent momentum-space population imbalance in the group-IV monochalcogenide SnSe. By combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with ab initio real-time simulations of photoexcited carrier dynamics, we identify valley-selective excitation at opposite crystal momenta arising from the breaking of time-reversal symmetry under circularly polarized illumination. We theoretically demonstrate that the magnitude of valley circular dichroism is strongly constrained by crystal symmetry through its influence on the quantum geometric tensor, the key quantity underlying valley optical selection rules. The resulting chiroptically induced valley polarization decays on sub-picosecond timescales through intervalley scattering mediated by electron-phonon coupling. Furthermore, we show theoretically that the population imbalance between valleys at opposite momenta gives rise to a helicity-reversible transient photocurrent. These findings provide microscopic insight into how quantum geometry governs valley-selective light-matter interactions, valley polarization, and photocurrent generation in van der Waals materials exhibiting hidden and transient symmetry breaking.
authors: Yiming Pan, Sotirios Fragkos, Umberto Dellasette, Quentin Courtade, Dominique Descamps, Stéphane Petit, Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu

articles.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

articles.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.
authors: Wan-Ling Yang, Shao-Bo Liu, Xiang Luo, Chao Yang, Hai-Lin Li, Yu-Zhou Yang, Yong-Kui Wang, Bing Yang

articles.title: Spin-Dependent Transport in One-Dimensional Mercury- and Silver-Mediated DNA Nanowires
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating dispersive, metal-centered conduction bands rather than isolated localized states. Driven by enhanced inter-layer coupling, where second nearest-neighbor hopping plays a crucial role: the conduction bandwidth can approach 1 eV, more than double that of canonical DNA. These broad bands suggest enhanced robustness of transport against structural fluctuations. As a result of relativistic effects, in these quasi-one-dimensional materials, spin-orbit (SO) coupling enhances band dispersion and governs spin-dependent transport. We predict that although ligand hybridization reduces atomic SO splitting, the effective SO splitting in these nanowires is comparable to the next-nearest-neighbor hopping strength, which results in considerable spin mixing. We find that Hg2+-coordinated nanowire exhibit pronounced spin-flip conductance comparable to spin-conserving conductance across the LUMO manifold. This efficient spin conversion remains robust over extended molecular lengths and is accompanied by a set of highly delocalized unoccupied states with oscillating nodal structures, readily accessible under low-bias transport measurements. In contrast, the Ag+-coordinated nanowires exhibit weak spin-flip scattering that is more than an order of magnitude smaller than spin-preserving transport. This duality establishes the choice of coordination metal as a decisive parameter to govern metal-metal interaction, electron delocalization, and spin-dependent transport. Overall, our findings demonstrate how relativistic effects and quantum confinement intersect in these bio-templated, quasi-one-dimensional molecular conductors.
authors: Arpan De, William Livernois, Simon Vecchioni, Yoel P. Ohayon, M. P. Anantram

articles.title: Sign-problem-free Bosonic Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sign problem poses a fundamental barrier to numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, severely hindering our understanding of quantum many-body physics across disciplines ranging from condensed matter to particle and nuclear physics. Geometrical frustration makes this barrier especially acute for interacting bosons. Here, we develop a bosonic auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (BAFQMC) method and rigorously prove that time-reversal symmetry and reflection positivity each provide a general sufficient condition for sign-problem-free simulations. Crucially, under either criterion, BAFQMC evades the sign problem even on frustrated lattices where conventional world-line and stochastic-series-expansion methods fail. Benchmarking our approach on a two-flavor Bose-Hubbard model on the triangular lattice yields excellent quantitative agreement with finite-temperature exact diagonalization. By establishing unifying principles to solve the sign problem in BAFQMC, our work substantially expands the reach of unbiased, numerically exact simulations for frustrated bosonic matter.
authors: Yin-Kai Yu, Zhong-Chao Wei, Zi-Xiang Li

articles.title: Breathing and quadrupole modes in squeezed Bose-Bose liquid drops
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the lowest excitation modes of binary ³⁹K ultradilute droplets confined harmonically in one direction, which reduces the critical number of particles needed to sustain a self-bound state. Using the density functional built from first-principles quantum Monte Carlo calculations (QMC), which incorporates the effects of finite range interactions, we study the crossover of the oscillation modes from three to two dimensions. For weak squeezing, we observe the coupling between breathing and quadrupole modes, resulting from the breaking of spherical symmetry. Increasing the squeezing, the higher-frequency mode corresponding to three-dimensional breathing mode becomes unstable. For squeezings stronger and comparable to experiments, we analyze the dependence of the excitation modes on the droplet size for several interactions and show the reduction of the number of particles needed to sustain stable oscillations. The differences between the results obtained with the QMC functional and the extended Gross-Pitaevskii theory are increased with respect to the case of previously studied spherical droplets.
authors: Marko Korda, Leandra Vranješ Markić, Jordi Boronat

articles.title: Maxwell-Chern-Simons-Matter in AdS₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS₃ coupled to N complex scalars or Dirac fermions, including sextic and Gross-Neveu interactions, respectively. First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large N with κ=k/N and α=Ne² fixed, where k is the Chern-Simons level. We determine the corresponding phase diagrams, and we resum matter insertions to obtain the photon propagator at leading order in large N, exactly in α and κ. Its poles determine the spin-one boundary spectrum, split into two helicity sectors by the Chern-Simons interaction. With Dirichlet boundary conditions, the unHiggsed scalar phase contains a protected chiral current, which is lifted by Higgsing. In the fermionic phases, the current persists for nonzero effective Chern-Simons level, with helicity determined by the induced level shift. At bulk conformal points, we extract large-N BCFT data for the critical and tricritical scalar theories, as well as for the regular fermion and Gross-Neveu theories.

articles.title: Memory--Transport Competition in Physical Two-Bath Quantum Reset Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherence preservation and environmental renewal offer competing ways of controlling quantum memory and transport. We show that a seemingly natural protocol which exactly replaces the bath occupations while preserving arbitrary system--bath coherences need not correspond to a physical fermionic state. We instead construct a two-reservoir protocol with independent, number-conserving thermal attenuators, for which complete positivity and fermionic admissibility hold by construction. Physical attenuation necessarily modifies bath populations as well as cross correlations; the coherence control is not an independent hard-reset knob. Quadratic dynamics reduces the stroboscopic problem to an exact matrix fixed-point equation without a weak-coupling or Markov approximation. Analytically, coherence retention enhances the leading short-cycle transfer rate, including the complete-erasure limit; no general endpoint-vanishing theorem exists. An exact stationary continuity theorem forces the through-current to vanish whenever either reservoir is left entirely unrefreshed, although no analogous theorem suppresses it at complete erasure. For biased structured reservoirs, exact finite-chain calculations display distinct coherence-, current-, and signed energy-transfer operating points; a resolved high-retention boundary layer exposes strong finite-size sensitivity of the coherence peak. The model provides a microscopic, fermion-admissible benchmark for the interplay of reservoir coherence, particle transport, and energetic exchange.
authors: Jishad Kumar, Achilleas Lazarides, Tapio Ala-Nissila

articles.title: Probing quasiperiodic spectral accessibility with a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quasiperiodic systems combine sharply different spectral and localisation regimes with a dense hierarchy of dynamical time scales. We show that a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle can use this structure as a thermodynamic probe, revealing which parts of the spectrum become dynamically accessible and thermodynamically relevant during a driven transformation. For a generalised Aubry-André-Harper chain, the resulting response is not determined by the static quasiperiodic regime alone: extended, near-critical, and crossing protocols do not exhibit universal ordering of work fluctuations. Instead, the statistics reflect transition pathways that are simultaneously dynamically coupled, thermally occupied, and energetically significant. The same spectral accessibility separates thermodynamic recovery from microscopic adiabatic recovery. Positive mean work can reappear while the population transfer dynamics remain strongly nonadiabatic because finite-rate population transfer is redistributed toward energetically less costly channels rather than suppressed. The full work distribution reveals a further separation, with a finite rate window in which positive-work cycles form a majority although the mean work remains negative. This behaviour persists in finite-size analysis. A thermally weighted spectral susceptibility connects these effects to a distributed hierarchy of dynamically active spectral regions rather than to a single minimum-gap bottleneck. Finite thermal contacts preserve this picture while introducing a second time scale and intercycle memory. Quantum Otto cycles can therefore provide a fluctuation-resolved thermodynamic probe of quasiperiodic spectral accessibility, complementary to direct spectroscopic and eigenstate-resolved diagnostics.
authors: Shujie Cheng, Lucas C. Céleri, Norton G. de Almeida, Gao Xianlong, G. D. de Moraes Neto

articles.title: Time-reversal-based quantum metrology in a central-spin architecture: from SATIN to butterfly echo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced time-reversal-based metrology using the central spin model, in which a single ancilla spin of magnitude Sₘ̊ cₑₙ mediates interactions between N bath spins through a star-graph topology. We demonstrate that the SATIN (Signal Amplification Through Time-reversal Interaction) echo protocol can be implemented in this setup to achieve a Fisher information of N²/e with the collective łangle J_yångle readout, corresponding to a 4.34,dB offset from the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we establish that this platform provides a pathway to perform the butterfly echo protocol by conjugating each evolution step with a random collective bath rotation, thereby achieving axis-agnostic Heisenberg-scaled sensing. Crucially, with a small N-independent number of random steps, the butterfly echo reaches a Fisher information of N²/4 (6,dB below the Heisenberg limit) for any unknown encoding axis, with the plateau gain tracking the Haar limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the central-spin magnitude Sₘ̊ cₑₙ provides a powerful knob to reduce the optimal protocol timescale without altering the metrological ceiling or the circuit depth required to reach isotropy. The proposed scheme is relevant to cavity QED and NMR quantum processors, where the central spin architecture arises naturally.

articles.title: Scale-free localization in pseudo-Hermitian quantum walk
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31067v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scale-free localization is a distinctive phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems, where specific eigenstates, known as scale-free localized states (LSs), possess localization lengths that scale linearly with the system size. Here, we show that a single non-Hermitian defect in one-dimensional quantum walks (QWs) induces scale-free localization. Driven by non-Hermiticity, the QW system undergoes a pseudo-Hermitian (PH) phase transition and the PH symmetry breaking is accompanied by the emergence of scale-free localization. As non-Hermiticity is further increased, the system undergoes a second phase transition, marked by the emergence of two pairs of bound states. Crucially, we identify the critical points of both transitions using localization properties. Furthermore, we extend our investigation to two-dimensional QWs, where a single non-Hermitian defect also induces scale-free localization, thereby demonstrating the universality of this phenomenon. Our work provides a valuable perspective for further exploring defect physics and a type of novel LS in non-Hermitian quantum systems.
authors: Haiting Zhang, Lei Xiao, Cui-Xian Guo, Quan Lin, Peng Xue

articles.title: Fluctuation-free Quantum Battery Charging Enabled by Bell-like Entangled and Separable Charger States
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The implication of entanglement in quantum battery charging remains poorly understood. In addition, intrinsic quantum randomness poses a fundamental challenge to charging uniformity across distinct trials. To address these issues, we study a three-qubit system within a cascaded collision frame, with two qubits acting as the charger and the third serving as the battery. After each collision, an adaptive measurement is performed on the charger, yielding four conditional post-measurement battery states with identical expected stored energy. For arbitrary fixed charger states, we derive analytical expressions for the recurrence relation of stored energy. We find that stored-energy fluctuations depend on whether the dynamics relies on the battery phase (γₙ). For two Bell-like families of entangled states, together with their computational basis states termed Bell-like separable states, the dynamics is (γₙ)-independent and fluctuations vanish, whereas for other entangled and separable states, fluctuations emerge. These insights establish a paradigm for engineering charger states to design uniform-charging quantum-battery architectures despite inherent quantum randomness.
authors: Longyan Gong, Jing Zhang, Yongtao Li

articles.title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix. In realistic quantum systems, however, noise is unavoidable and the projected states are generally mixed. Whether mixed-state deep thermalization admits an analogous universal limiting distribution has remained unclear. Here we answer this question for quantum dynamics containing local quantum channels, i.e., errors. We show that the late-time mixed-state projected ensemble is completely determined by the normalized Choi state of the error channel and is universal, independent of the microscopic details of the underlying unitary dynamics. We establish this result analytically for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar-random dynamics, and local Haar-random circuits at large local dimension, and verify it numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics. In a solvable setting, we further find exponentially fast convergence to the limiting ensemble. Our results extend deep thermalization to noisy quantum dynamics and establish a direct correspondence between quantum errors and universal random mixed-state ensembles.

articles.title: The ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene: Dynamical skyrmion lattices and their excitations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.07402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce an interacting ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene in which interactions spontaneously generate a correlated Chern insulator. Our analysis reveals that this Chern insulator can be understood as a layer-pseudospin skyrmion lattice stabilized by electronic interactions, and that it gives rise to genuine skyrmion lattice physics, complete with dynamics. This dynamical skyrmion lattice naturally leads to experimentally measurable consequences. In particular, we identify new collective excitations corresponding to chiral shape deformations of the skyrmions, and propose a new positively charged quasiparticle, the skyrmion vacancy. These results establish a qualitatively new form of moiré Chern physics in rhombohedral graphene: an interaction-generated skyrmion lattice whose skyrmions are dynamical low-energy degrees of freedom.
authors: Tixuan Tan, Patrick J. Ledwith, Trithep Devakul

articles.title: Sampling from Spherical Spin Glasses in Total Variation via Algorithmic Stochastic Localization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2404.15651v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the problem of algorithmically sampling from the Gibbs measure of a mixed p-spin spherical spin glass. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that samples from the Gibbs measure up to vanishing total variation error, for any model whose mixture satisfies  ξ''(s) < frac1(1-s)², qquad forall sin [0,1).  Our algorithm follows the algorithmic stochastic localization (SL) approach introduced in (Alaoui, Montanari, Sellke, 2022) and in fact achieves a more difficult task. Namely, it (approximately) generates a sample path (boldsymbol yₜ₎ₜgₑ ₀ from the SL process. For large T, boldsymbol y_T/T is an approximate sample from the target Gibbs measure, and hence we solve the original problem as a special case. We provide evidence that the condition ξ''(s) < (1-s)⁻² is sharp for the task of sampling SL sample paths. Furthermore, we prove that it is optimal within a class of generalized SL processes. Remarkably this threshold is close to the conjectured threshold for sampling from the original Gibbs measure. In particular, for the pure p-spin glasses it is within an absolute (p-independent) constant of the so-called shattering phase transition. Earlier work on related models was suboptimal by a factor diverging polynomially in p. A key step of this approach is to estimate the mean of a sequence of tilted measures. We produce an improved estimator for this task by identifying a suitable correction to the TAP fixed point selected by approximate message passing (AMP). As a consequence, we improve the algorithm's guarantee over previous work, from normalized Wasserstein to total variation error. In particular, the new algorithm and analysis open the way to perform inference about one-dimensional projections of the measure.
authors: Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham

articles.title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation with Quantum Feedback
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.22651v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fluctuations are intrinsic to microscopic systems and impose fundamental limits on nonequilibrium precision, as captured by the thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR), which links current fluctuations to entropy production. While feedback control is expected to further suppress fluctuations, its role within the TUR framework has remained unclear, particularly in quantum systems where control is inherently information-driven. In this Letter, we consider open quantum systems weakly coupled to a thermal environment, in which quantum jumps are continuously monitored, and Markovian feedback is applied. Using quantum mutual information to quantify the information contribution induced by feedback, we derive a finite-time TUR for arbitrary time-integrated currents in terms of entropy production and mutual information. Our results uncover how feedback control suppresses fluctuations together with thermodynamic cost and establish a fundamental precision bound imposed by information-based control. As an application, we analyze a quantum clock model and demonstrate that the clock precision can be enhanced by feedback control in the presence of a single thermal reservoir.

articles.title: A Photonic Tautochrone: Spatiotemporal Beam Focusing for Enhanced Nonlinear Response
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.03691v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose to implement an optical analogue of the tautochrone property of the cycloid to allow the focusing of ultrashort pulses inside photonic systems. This allows to enhance nonlinear effects, resulting in orders of magnitude increase of nonlinearity-induced phase shifts, while employing low irradiances. Building upon the optical-mechanical analogy, we show how to produce optical limiters for temporal light pulses, and how to implement temporal bistability and even multistability with large numbers of states. Finally, we move this concept to the quantum realm and predict a tautochrone quantum blockade regime with a stronger antibunching.
authors: W. Verstraelen, S. Zanotti, N. W. E. Seet, J. Zhao, D. Sanvitto, J. Zuñiga-Perez, K. Dini, Y. G. Rubo, T. C. H. Liew

articles.title: Automated generation and execution of large-scale semidefinite programs for variational two-electron reduced density matrix theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The variational two-electron reduced density matrix (v2RDM) method provides a wave-function-free approach to the description of strong electron correlation whose computational cost scales polynomially with the number of correlated orbitals. Here, we present an automated pipeline for the generation and execution of semidefinite programs (SDPs) associated with the v2RDM problem. Algebraic constraints encoding ensemble N-representability conditions are generated via the p^daggerq second-quantized algebra package, and the p^daggerq-generated expressions are automatically translated into a sparse-matrix representation that can be digested by an appropriate SDP solver. We have implemented a boundary-point SDP (BPSDP) solver in the libsdp package that can execute the v2RDM SDPs on either CPU or GPU hardware. We apply the code in several contexts. First, two-particle conditions are used to describe the 76-orbital model of the iron-molybdenum cofactor (FeMoco) of nitrogenase, the simulation of which requires roughly 25 hours of compute time on a single Nvidia H100 GPU. Second, the performance of high-order (four-particle positivity) conditions is evaluated on a challenging two-dimensional H₁₀ cluster problem. Lastly, new classes of positivity constraints for mixed fermion-boson systems are generated and applied within the context of ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics simulations.
authors: A. Eugene DePrince III, Nicholas C. Rubin

articles.title: QuDPy-FDGF: A Python-Based Tool for Computing Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Responses Using Frequency Domain Green's Functions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present QuDPy-FDGF, an open-source Python framework that evaluates Liouville-space pathways as hybrid chains of time propagators and frequency-domain Green's functions. Frequency-resolved intervals are computed directly through shifted linear systems, without time propagation followed by a Fourier transform, while other intervals may remain in the time domain. A model-agnostic block interface separates the physical model from pathway construction, numerical propagation, and detection. The released implementation provides an explicit dense Liouville-space backend for reference calculations and a sector-resolved sparse backend using matrix-free generator actions, Krylov time propagation, and generalized minimal residual (GMRES) resolvent solves. Its observable layer reuses propagated pathway responses to evaluate operator expectation values, action-detected readout interactions, instantaneous jump rates, and integrated mean jump counts. The framework is assessed on an analytically solvable open two-level system and on two examples of increasing complexity: the complete third-order rephasing response, with its eight sequences, of a thermally initialized anisotropic Heisenberg (XXZ) spin chain with unequal excitation sectors, and two coupled dissipative anharmonic modes whose spectra depend on the detected observable, with the fifth-order double-quantum response of their closed limit. The calculations reproduce the analytical two-level response, check the matrix-free sparse evaluation against the dense assembly of the generator, and recover the harmonic-limit cancellation of the fifth-order signal when the required three-excitation manifold is retained. QuDPy-FDGF therefore provides a unified framework for pathway- and observable-resolved nonlinear spectroscopy in finite or truncated Hilbert spaces with unitary or Markovian Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) dynamics.
authors: Mathieu Desmarais, Simón Paiva-Ortega, Félix Brunell, Eric R. Bittner, Hao Li, Carlos Silva-Acuña

articles.title: All-photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz signal core at room and cryogenic temperatures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects. Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. Here, we show a monolithic lithium tantalate photonic chip, termed a signal core, which generates, modulates, routes, and detects continuous-wave signals at discrete frequencies between 100 GHz and 2.5 THz. The architecture integrates high-frequency functional modules on chip and uses exclusively fiber-based optical interfaces. Bidirectional coherent electro-optic conversion enables signal generation, detection, and nanosecond-scale amplitude and phase modulation, while micro-coplanar striplines interconnect the modules into an end-to-end signal chain on a single chip. Our modules achieve single-photon electro-optic coupling rates of g₀/2π=10 kHz and peak drive-power-normalized photon-flux conversion efficiencies of 1.0%/mW for generation and 0.5%/mW for detection. It also operates at 4 K in a dilution refrigerator through the same fiber-only optical links. Together, these capabilities establish an all-photonic platform for millimeter-wave-to-terahertz systems and offer a broadly applicable architecture for applications constrained by electrical-interconnect loss, heat load, and footprint.
authors: Jiawen Liu, Chengli Wang, Aleksei Gaier, Tianyi Zhang, Gabriel Jülg, Yazan Lampert, André Garcia Primo, Alessandro Tomasino, Hua Li, Xin Ou, Ileana-Cristina Benea-Chelmus

articles.title: A Personal History in Quantum Foundations: an Oral History Interview
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This oral history interview provides Yakir Aharonov's personal and conceptual recollections from the 1950s to the 2000s, focusing on his academic trajectory, some of his major contributions to quantum foundations, and his perspective on the development of the field. The interview traces Aharonov's academic career through the Technion, University of Bristol, Brandeis University, Yeshiva University, University of South Carolina, Tel Aviv University, George Mason University, and Chapman University. The interview also traces the development of Aharonov's work and collaborations on the EPR paradox, time-energy uncertainty relations, quantum measurement theory, quantum frames of reference, the two-state vector formalism, weak values, protective measurements, and several other contributions. It includes recollections of meetings and discussions with David Bohm, Niels Bohr, John Clauser, Paul Dirac, Rudolf Peierls, Aage Petersen, and Abner Shimony. Also mentioned: David Albert, Jeeva Anandan, Peter Bergmann, Gideon Carmi, Avshalom Elitzur, Dave Finkelstein, Vladimir Fock, Itzhak Kalugai, Ed Lerner, Joel Lebowitz, Stanley Mandelstam, Yuval Ne'eman, Sandu Popescu, Maurice Pryce, Daniel Rohrlich, Nathan Rosen, Joseph Safko, Paul Singer, Daniele Struppa, Leonard Susskind, Lev Vaidman, Chien-Shiung Wu.

articles.title: Second- and third-order nonlinearities in silicon nitride waveguides via heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate membranes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thick, dispersion-engineered silicon nitride is a leading platform for integrated third-order nonlinear optics, supporting supercontinuum and frequency comb generation. However, it lacks the second-order nonlinearity required by many applications. Here we bond pre-fabricated x-cut thin-film lithium niobate membranes onto finished silicon nitride waveguides as a back-end step, compatible with commercially fabricated waveguides. A single silicon nitride waveguide generates an octave-spanning supercontinuum and, through the lithium niobate membrane, concurrent second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation. These results open new possibilities for thick silicon nitride photonics, from visible light generation to on-chip f-2f comb self-referencing, a key step towards miniaturised timing and navigation quantum technologies.
authors: Natale G. Pruiti, Cosmin Suciu, Eugenio Di Gaetano, Jonathan M. Silver, Douglas J. Paul, Marc Sorel

articles.title: Unifying Time-Independent and Time-Dependent Franck--Condon Pictures in Quantum Mechanochemistry via the Linear Coupling Approximation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum chemistry has achieved impressive results in modeling and interpreting mechanochemical transformations at the molecular level. An essential question, the time profile of force application, has however attracted less attention. Here, the Franck--Condon theory of quantum mechanochemistry, previously formulated for the sudden-force limit, is generalized to arbitrary time-dependent force profiles using the linear-coupling approximation. Solving the driven harmonic oscillator yields a closed-form, time-dependent effective Huang--Rhys factor: a natural measure of vibrational excitations upon force application. It is governed by the Fourier transform of the force derivative and recovers the sudden- and fixed-force limits. At the conceptual level, this linear coupling picture links mechanochemistry to vibronic spectroscopy and Marcus electron theory. For a shock-front force ramp, vibrational excitation is shown to be suppressed in frequency, only low-frequency modes being excited under realistic laser-shock-peening conditions.

articles.title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a Qḑot f-product of 2ḑot 10¹⁴Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.
authors: Alexander Jung, Anastasiia Ciers, Hannes Pfeifer, Albert Hansson, Johanna Örgård, Daniel Stachanow, Viktor A. Lilja, Philippe Tassin, Witlef Wieczorek

articles.title: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The emergence of entangled quantum optical states in high-harmonic generation raises a fundamental problem about its characterization, namely, how can entanglement of extreme-ultraviolet radiation be certified for attosecond light fields? Here, we provide experimentally accessible separability tests, particularly showing that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides a direct solution to this problem. This is achieved by a quantum optical treatment of mapping photoelectron interferometry to the measurement of optical correlation functions. This yields a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements. We evaluate both witnesses on explicit optical states and identify how the protocol can be extended to XUV-XUV entanglement certification. Hence, we establish attosecond photoelectron interferometry as a general framework for entanglement certification across a wide range of optical frequencies.

articles.title: Enhanced Whispering Gallery Mode Phase Shift using Indistinguishable Photon Pairs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2404.17409v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a theoretical investigation of a whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonator coupled to a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) and show a bimodal coincidence transmission spectrum when the input state is an indistinguishable photon pair. This is due to the doubled WGM phase shift experienced by the path-entangled state in the interferometer. Further, we model the noise in a WGM resonance shift measurement comparing photon pairs with a coherent state. At least a four-fold improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is possible, with clear implications for quantum-enhanced WGM sensing.
authors: Callum Jones, Antonio Vidiella-Barranco, Jolly Xavier, Frank Vollmer

articles.title: OQMD: Single-Qubit Rotation Control Improves Low-CNOT Multiclass Quantum Classification
articles.abstract: Near-term variational classifiers incur substantial error and latency from two-qubitgates, yet practitioners often assume that additional entangling depth is the defaultroute to higher accuracy. This work studies Optimal Quantum Measurement Decoding(OQMD): optimizing how quantum outcomes are mapped to classical labels by train-ing a readout layer before measurement, jointly with the variational circuit, withoutadding CNOTs. Experiments use trainable triple single-qubit rotations as one con-crete, hardware-native realization of OQMD; other single-qubit parametrizations fitthe same classical outer loop. On the Iris benchmark with a 30-point stratified testsplit, the best observed 0-CNOT configuration with OQMD reaches 83.33% accuracy,with a 96% accuracy at 9 CNOTs, exceeding the best 18-CNOT controls (56.67%)and the best 18-CNOT configuration with OQMD (66.67%) under a common proto-col. A six-point CNOT-depth series from 0 to 18 (fixed optimizer, iteration budget,random-seed count, and ZXZ readout) shows that the highest raw scores need notoccur at the largest template, so aggregate complexity is not summarized by CNOTcount alone. Because run-level accuracies are discrete and non-Gaussian, we empha-size best-observed scores and, where a global comparison of pooled runs is required,Mann–Whitney U tests rather than parametric tests on means. Across architectures,OQMD shows statistically consistent but magnitude-dependent gains: large peak liftson minimal circuits coexist with a small pooled mean shift on complex 18-CNOT runs(p ≈ 0.03) that is not “universal” in the sense of uniformly large practical effects.

We show that the squared coordinates of (:X) are read off from (:h̊o:X) by single determinants, (:XI²=łeft|Xi̊ght|²detłeft(łeft(Id+h̊o:XDIi̊ght)/2i̊ght)), where (:DI) is the diagonal sign matrix of the blade (:eI). articles.title: Reconfigurable high-power Kerr optical parametric oscillators with sub-hertz linewidths
articles.abstract: Integrated coherent light sources combining broad wavelength tunability, narrow-linewidth, and high output power are essential for precision spectroscopy, coherent communications, and quantum information processing, yet remain challenging to realize simultaneously. Kerr microresonator optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) provide coherent wavelength access beyond conventional gain media, but their oscillating signal-idler pairs are typically fixed by the dispersion and loss of the fabricated resonator, while pump-noise transfer and nonlinear mode competition limit coherence and power scaling. Here, we demonstrate post-fabrication reconfiguration of Kerr OPOs through coherent feedback enabled by mode-selective sideband self-injection locking, without the need for resonator redesign. By tuning the relative effective gain of competing parametric channels, coherent feedback makes a selected signal-idler pair dominant over the free-running state. At a fixed pump wavelength, our method enables stepwise sideband selection across 1.27 THz and continuous tuning over 202.17 GHz, while joint tuning of the pump and feedback-selected sideband extends the accessible span beyond 23 nm. The same feedback reduces the intrinsic linewidth of the selected sideband to sub-hertz, corresponding to a ~ 30,000-fold reduction from the free-running OPO and suppresses cluster-comb formation to deliver more than 42 mW on-chip sideband power. Our work establishes coherent feedback as a new control degree of freedom for reconfiguring nonlinear oscillation states in integrated Kerr photonics.

articles.title: Anomalous Thermal Conductivity Reversal Driven by a Fluctuating Charge Density Wave
articles.abstract: For more than a century, the lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline solids has been known to decrease with increasing temperature, as the phonons that carry heat scatter more strongly via Umklapp processes. Here we report a pronounced violation of this rule in the layered charge-density-wave (CDW) metal 2H-TaSe₂. Its in-plane thermal conductivity is strongly nonmonotonic: it peaks sharply at the 122 K ordering transition, collapses to a deep minimum near 210 K, and then anomalously reverses, rising with temperature to at least 350 K. Such a high-temperature reversal, in which a crystal conducts heat more efficiently as it is heated, is rare in crystalline solids. Its thermal conductivity minimum lies deep in the disordered phase well above the ordering transition, unlike the weak, transition-centered anomalies of other charge-density-wave systems, pointing to heat conduction governed by fluctuating rather than established order. Combining inelastic X-ray scattering, selected-area electron diffraction, and synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we attribute the reversal to phonons scattering off persistent, fluctuating charge order that survives more than 150 K above the long-range transition, to at least 300 K. A phenomenological phonon–CDW scattering model, tied directly to the measured diffraction linewidth and intensity, quantitatively reproduces the entire nonmonotonic curve. We also reveal that the charge order melts not abruptly but through a fluctuation- and defect-driven, weak first-order process, leaving short-range correlations far above the transition. This work establishes fluctuating charge order as a sensitive control knob for thermal transport in quantum materials and thermal conductivity as a powerful probe of the hidden charge order.

articles.title: Magnetic symmetry implications of the zero- and applied-field Hall effect of UNi₄B
articles.abstract: Author(s): Z. W. Riedel, W. S. Simeth, S. M. Thomas, F. Ronning, and E. D. articles.title: An enhanced adaptive finite element method with linear scaling for 3D Hartree–Fock equation
articles.abstract: The Hartree–Fock equation serves as a fundamental theoretical tool in quantum chemistry and condensed matter physics for describing the ground–state electronic structure of multi–electron systems. Despite its significance, the numerical solution faces challenges due to its complex mathematical structure. This paper presents an efficient adaptive finite element method for solving the 3D Hartree–Fock equation, incorporating three acceleration techniques: a multilevel correction scheme, a two-level nested self-consistent field iteration, and a density fitting strategy. The method aims to enhance computational efficiency, reduce memory consumption, and improve the parallel scalability. By reformulating the problem into a sequence of large-scale boundary value problems and small-scale eigenvalue problems, our algorithm drastically reduces computational load and storage demands. Notably, it achieves linear computational complexity O ( NN k ), with the coefficient depending on the number of wavefunctions N rather than the correction space dimension N H , representing a significant improvement over the O (( N + N H ) N k ) complexity in prior work [Xu et al. , J. Chem. Phys. 164 , 074111 (2026)] that proposed a simplified multilevel correction algorithm (yielding up to fivefold speedup in numerical simulations). Furthermore, the correction process is tailored for each wavefunction independently, endowing it with substantial potential for parallel computation. Numerical experiments conducted on various molecular systems demonstrate the superior precision, efficiency, and memory savings of the proposed algorithm compared to the direct adaptive finite element method.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Quenched fluctuation-induced force arising from polarization disorder
articles.abstract: We investigate the zero-temperature behavior of the fluctuation force induced by the quenched disorder of electric dipoles frozen randomly into a material. Examples of such materials include relaxor ferroelectrics. In terms of the setup and geometry, we focus on a layered system comprising two coplanar semi-infinite slabs separated by a distance ℓ , as well as a system comprising a neutral atom in the vacuum located at a distance ℓ above the surface of a semi-infinite slab. For both systems, we consider the cases where the quenched random dipolar disorder occurs inside the bulk as well as on the surface of the slabs. In all of these cases, we find that the bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced force grows with the mean square quenched electric dipole moment per unit volume (area). The bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced pressure between two semi-infinite single-layered slabs decays with ℓ −3 ( ℓ −4 ), whereas the bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced force on an atom in the vacuum near a slab containing the disorder decays with ℓ −4 ( ℓ −5 ). We also find that the quenched dipolar disorder-induced force between two coplanar slabs can be repulsive in a three-layered dielectric system that obeys a zero-frequency analog of the Dzyaloshinskii–Lifshitz–Pitaevskii condition and serves to enhance the “nanolevitation effect” if the latter is present in the disorder-free system.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Q-Chem/CP2K software interface for projection-based, pseudoperiodic wavefunction-in-DFT embedding
articles.abstract: We report an implementation of projection-based quantum embedding that combines periodic density functional theory in the CP2K code with correlated wavefunction calculations in the Q-Chem program. Using this interface, correlated wavefunction methods can be applied to a subset of molecular orbitals, selected in an automated manner based on a user-defined list of nuclei, with an embedding potential that provides electronic coupling to the remaining orbitals that comprise the environment. Our implementation uses exact projection, without the need for any level-shift operator, and is “pseudoperiodic” in the sense that periodic boundary effects are implicit in the orbitals used in the (non-periodic) wavefunction calculation. Convergence tests demonstrate that computed properties are faithful to the corresponding periodic quantities, provided that the high-level subsystem is spatially localized and small, relative to the periodic simulation cell. Spectroscopic examples for aqueous chromophores demonstrate converged results using a very limited subset of water molecules in the simulation cell, decoupling the choice of excited-state method and basis set from the functional that is used to propagate ground-state ab initio molecular dynamics. Solvatochromic shifts for aqueous uracil are converged using equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory, without the need for solvent molecules in the wavefunction calculation, and the embedded calculation captures solvent effects that are absent in gas-phase “microhydration” studies. Additional applications include adsorption of CO on a slab model of Si(100) and bond dissociation in a one-dimensional periodic polymer. In both of the latter cases, the system/environment partition crosses a covalent bond; these applications demonstrate that pseudoperiodic embedding can be applied to realistic systems in materials science.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Singlet and triplet excitations in C 5 F 10 O induced by electrons and photons: Spectroscopy and dynamics
articles.abstract: C 5 F 10 O [heptafluoroisopropyl(trifluoromethyl)ketone] has emerged as a promising alternative to sulfur hexafluoride for the use in gas-insulated switchgears. Despite its technological relevance, its interactions with low-energy electrons remain largely unexplored. Electron impact can populate both singlet and triplet electronically excited states, potentially initiating dissociation pathways that yield toxic or technologically undesirable products. Here, we combine vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS), and theoretical modeling to characterize the electronically excited states of C 5 F 10 O and the dynamics initiated by these excitations. We report the first VUV absorption spectrum of C 5 F 10 O and directly compare it to EELS recorded at multiple scattering angles and residual energies. The spectra are compared with high-level ab initio calculations. To obtain the inelastic electron scattering cross sections, we use our implementation of the Born approximation coupled with the algebraic diagrammatic construction of the second order method. An ad hoc extension of this approach is introduced to account for the exchange-mediated spin-forbidden transitions in the spectra of backscattered electrons. Finally, nonadiabatic molecular dynamics coupled with time-dependent density functional theory is used to identify reaction channels initiated in different singlet and triplet excited states. Overall, we provide a state-resolved framework to study electronic excitation and subsequent reactivity, with implications for plasma modeling and the design of next-generation high-voltage insulation media.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Low-energy electron attachment, autodetachment, and electron-induced processes in the smallest helicene molecules
articles.abstract: Free low-energy (0–14 eV) electron attachment and electron-triggered processes in the gas-phase carbohelicene molecules containing five and six ortho-fused benzene rings are studied using dissociative electron attachment spectroscopy under single-collision conditions. The long-lived molecular negative ions (MNIs) are the most abundant species detected in the negative ion mass spectra of both compounds. Their electron detachment times are measured to be 50–70 μ s. On this basis, the adiabatic electron affinity of [6]helicene is estimated to be 0.81 eV in excellent agreement with the B3LYP/6-31+G(d) value (0.79 eV). The most intriguing finding is a sharp increase in the electron detachment time of [5]helicene MNI observed in the range 0.25–0.5 eV that contradicts the obvious tendency of electron detachment times to decrease as incident electron energy rises. This unusual effect is explained by the formation of the most stable re-arranged planar MNI, which loses its initial chirality, a process being supposed to be possible only in [5]helicene MNI initially formed through the π 3 * shape resonance. The present findings can be of importance to understanding the spin-filtering effects produced by helical molecules since transmission of low-energy photoelectrons through ordered enantiopure molecular layers can be considered as the formation of the temporary negative ion states and their decay by electron detachment.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: The collective role of bending, stretching, and polydispersity in microtubule mechanics and hydrodynamics
articles.abstract: Microtubules (MTs) organize into various structures by modulating their physico-chemical and electro-mechanical properties. Their size and flexibility are crucial for maintaining the cell’s mechanical strength and its ability to respond to external forces. Translational and rotational diffusion enhance MTs’ capacity to locate and bind to targets. In addition, cells regulate asymmetric MT length growth and polydispersity to maintain proper cytoskeletal organization in response to functional demands. Therefore, understanding these properties accurately is essential for grasping their critical roles in cellular functions. In this study, we develop a comprehensive framework to characterize the collective effects of hydrodynamic interactions, polydispersity, bending, and stretching on the hydrodynamic and mechanical properties of MT solutions. The approach integrates dynamic light scattering (DLS), a reliable sample preparation protocol, and an optimized scattering theory for polydisperse semiflexible polymers, yielding accurate, reproducible results from autocorrelation functions measured under conditions that simulate the physiological environment. Overall, the approach offers an alternative to conventional post-analysis DLS tools for analyzing experimental autocorrelation data in filamentous systems with variable stiffness and length and under various intracellular conditions, thereby providing a close relationship among the biophysical parameters describing filaments, their surrounding environment, and their influence on the complex and dynamic behavior of these systems.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Structural transition in one-dimensional water unveils the origin of multifurcated hydrogen bond weakening
articles.abstract: Water confined to low dimensions exhibits even more anomalous behavior than bulk water. Since these anomalies are primarily dictated by hydrogen bonds (hbs), we investigate hb behavior in quasi-one-dimensional water chains using density functional theory. We show that a water chain with two molecules per unit cell transforms from a single-file (low-linear-density) to a double-file (high-linear-density) structure under uniaxial compression. Furthermore, we show that repulsive interactions emerge when hbs become multifurcated. These additional repulsive forces weaken the hbs and play a crucial role in driving the structural transition. We demonstrate that the many-body interactions associated with hb cooperativity, as well as the repulsive forces from multifurcated hbs, are captured by classical dipole–dipole interactions. This indicates that both hb cooperativity and the weakening of multifurcated hbs are classical electrostatic phenomena, even though quantum effects dictate the strength of the effective dipoles involved. Finally, we discuss how these results provide insights for understanding the flow mechanism of water along pores of sub-nanometer diameter and aid in developing a simple, universal water model.

articles.title: One-pot synthesis of carbon nanotube/graphene composite phase change materials based on Pickering emulsion for solar thermal storage
articles.abstract: The practical deployment of phase change materials (PCMs) is frequently constrained by two intrinsic drawbacks. respectively low thermal conductivity and susceptibility to leakage during solid–liquid phase change. To address these issues, this study reports the synthesis of composite PCMs comprising hexadecanol encapsulated within a three-dimensional carbon nanotube (CNT)/reduced graphene oxide (RGO) network, fabricated via a one-pot Pickering emulsion method using graphene oxide (GO) as the stabilizer. The resulting CNT/RGO scaffold concurrently enhances thermal transport and structural integrity. Specifically, the thermal conductivity of the composite reaches 125.40% of that of pristine hexadecanol, while the latent heat capacity is substantially retained. Furthermore, the composite exhibits improved photothermal conversion efficiency. These characteristics render the developed material a promising candidate for solar thermal storage applications .

articles.title: QPotatoNet-A Hybrid Quantum Transformer Context for Haplotype-Aware Genomic Prediction and Accelerated Polyploid Potato Breeding
articles.abstract: Genomic selection has revolutionized the pace of crop breeding, but the cultivated potato (Solanum tuberosum, 2n = 4x = 48) still stands as a challenge: the accuracy of linear models like GBLUP, and of conventional deep learning is reduced by autotetrasomic inheritance, double-reduction, complex non-additive gene action, and small training populations. Approach: Results: We present QPotatoNet, a hybrid quantum–Transformer model that integrates a dosage-aware genomic Transformer encoder and a haplotype-block encoder with an 8-qubit variational quantum layer via cross-attention.tetrasomic SNP dosages and LD-defined phased haplotypes are simultaneously tokenized and processed to simultaneously predict genomic-estimated breeding values (GEBVs) for eight key agronomic traits. Results. On a 3,012-clone tetraploid panel (21,432 SNP loci), QPotatoNet attained a mean prediction accuracy of r = 0.734 across eight traits, improving on the best deep-learning baseline by 9.2% and on GBLUP by 22.6% on average, with the largest gains for low-heritability and non-additive traits. The variational quantum layer and the haplotype encoder led to the largest improve of accuracy in both cases when the ablation was executed. Conclusions. Through the integration of tetrasomic dosage structure and haplotype context into a quantum-enhanced attention mechanism, QPotatoNet closes the polyploid predictive gap and provides a feasible way for potato breeding cycle reduction.

articles.title: Structural, Electrical and Optical Properties of Zno and Zno:co Nanostructures Thin Films for Optoelectronic Applications
articles.abstract: This study comparatively evaluates the influence of Co incorporation on these properties in films deposited onto glass, titanium and Silicon substrates by DC magnetron co-sputtering. Structural, compositional, morphological, optical, and electrical characteristics were investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), Ultraviolet–Visible–Near-Infrared (UV–Vis–NIR) spectroscopy, current/voltage (I-V) measurements, cycling-endurance tests, and temperature dependent conductivity analysis. The hexagonal wurtzite structure was retained after Co incorporation, but diffraction-peak shifts are evidenced, vibrational-band modifications, and a rougher granular morphology indicated lattice perturbation and increased local disorder. XPS measurements support the presence of cobalt as a dilute dopant in the ZnO-based film. Also, the optical band gap narrowed from 3.16 eV to 2.70 eV and the estimated film thickness from 100.57 to 93.04 nm, using an iterative Bhattacharyya method. The ZnO:Co device exhibited a wider separation between the high and low resistance states (HRS/LRS) and bipolar resistive switching and a thermally activated transport, with SET and RESET transitions near − 0.9 V and + 0.5 V, respectively although progressively increase of resistive levels during the endurance tests. A thermally activated transport mechanism at high temperatures was shown, with an activation energy of 44.7 meV for ZnO and 242.91 meV for ZnO:Co. These results demonstrate that dilute Co incorporation simultaneously modifies the structural, optical, and electrical response of ZnO thin films, offering a promising pathway for the design of multifunctional optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Dynamical Tunneling Blockade in Layer-Pseudospin Ferromagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double-layer systems with narrow or flat electronic bands may exhibit spontaneous interlayer coherence, described by a layer-pseudospin ferromagnetic order parameter. In modern realizations of layer-pseudospin ferromagnets, the electrons carry additional valley degeneracies, endowing each layer with a valley-pseudospin degree of freedom. We study their nonequilibrium steady states driven by a static interlayer voltage bias in the presence of interlayer tunneling. While in the low-bias regime, the system is in a static state with parallel valley pseudospins between the two layers, we show that in the high-bias regime, the dynamical precession of the layer-pseudospin stabilizes the valley pseudospins in the antiparallel configuration, strongly suppressing the interlayer tunneling. This dynamical tunneling blockade leads to an absence of ac current and a sharp drop of the dc tunneling current to a tiny value, in stark contrast to conventional quantum Hall double layers.
authors: Lingxian Kong, Yuta Murakami, Ryuichi Shindou, Zhiyuan Sun

articles.title: Paramagnetic phase of MnTe₂: complete one phonon Raman spectrum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study we present a complete first-order Raman scattering spectrum of paramagnetic phase of MnTe₂₋ a material, where new type of spin texture induced by noncoplanar antiferromagnetic ordering below the Néel temperature (T_N approx 90 K) gives rise to unconventional scenario of magnetism. Basic properties of all five phonon modes (A_g, E_g and three T_g) predicted by the group theory have been successfully approached through polarization, excitation and temperature dependent measurements. In particular, the ever-missing phonon mode of T_g symmetry has been unambiguously resolved in the room temperature Raman spectrum at approximately 107 cm⁻¹, just 1.5 cm⁻¹ higher in frequency compared to the E_g mode. Density functional theory calculations reproduce the observed Raman-active phonon spectrum and support the assignment of all five first-order Raman modes, including the near-degeneracy of the E_g and one of the T_g vibrations. The calculations further reveal a dense manifold of low-energy antiferromagnetic spin configurations, separated from the ground state by only a few meV per formula unit. Furthermore, strong signals of inelastically scattered light from the paramagnetic (PM) phase of MnTe₂ were acquired with long wavelength excitations, i.e. 633 nm and 785 nm, revealing the 2A_g overtone at approx. 360 cm⁻¹. The enhanced absorption of the light in the near infrared range could be a putative reason behind the anomalous angular dependence of scattered intensity of the highest frequency T_g phonon mode (183 cm⁻¹) measured in PM MnTe₂ with parallelly aligned polarizers. Finally, upon cooling just below the T_N, the measured properties of phonons remained basically unperturbed by the incipient long-range antiferromagnetic ordering.
authors: Taras Palasyuk, Dominik Kurzydłowski, Ashutosh S. Wadge, Rajmund Bacewicz, Madhavi H. Dalsaniya, Michał Wierzbicki, Daniel Jastrzebski, Andrzej Wiśniewski, Wojciech Szuszkiewicz, Igor Antoniazzi, Bruno Camargo, Maciej R. Molas, Adam Babiński, Krzysztof Zberecki, Cezariusz Jastrzebski

articles.title: Two quantum skyrmions form a magnon Josephson junction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two quantum skyrmions in a frustrated spin-1/2 magnet bind into a molecule, and the molecule acts as a magnon Josephson junction: the relative helicity θ and the number n of magnons transferred between them obey H=E_Cn²⁻Wo̧sθ. DMRG on the J₁₋₋J₂ triangular lattice gives E_C as the curvature of the skyrmion energy at its natural size of seven flipped spins, and the measured helicity coherence fixes Wsimeq0.02J₁, half the skyrmion--antiskyrmion tunnel splitting and independent of the anisotropy. Two helicity qubits side by side are thus strongly coupled by their own interaction.

articles.title: Ultrafast and Anisotropic Exciton Transport in Layered NbOI₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions. Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI₂ is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed. The diffusion coefficient of about 160 cm² s⁻¹ along the nonpolar crystal axis is among the highest reported for van der Waals semiconductors. The transport exhibits an approximately twofold in-plane anisotropy between the polar and nonpolar directions, reflecting the intrinsic low-symmetry crystal structure of NbOI₂. The environmental stability of NbOI₂ is further investigated, and fabrication and encapsulation conditions required to achieve long-term sample stability are identified. These results establish NbOI₂ as a promising platform for studying anisotropic exciton transport and highlight the critical role of interface protection in air-sensitive van der Waals materials.
authors: Salman Ahsanullah, Neema Rafizadeh, Hui Zhao

articles.title: Josephson effect in symmetry-mismatched van der Waals hybrid junctions of NbSe2-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and NbSe2-Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coupling superconductors of different symmetries may lead to emergent quantum phenomena but experimental studies on heterojunctions made of lattice-mismatched crystals are scarce. Here, we fabricate Josephson junction by van der Waals stacking NbSe2 flakes on freshly cleaved surfaces of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y. We obtain pronounced Josephson currents across the heterojunctions at temperatures below 7 K. The Josephson coupling strength, characterized by the product of the critical Josephson current I_c and the normal state resistance Rₙ, can reach about 0.3 mV, much exceeding the values previously reported in Pb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Nb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x junctions. Microwave irradiation induces integer Shapiro steps. We also observe the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern by applying an in-plane magnetic field. We compare our results with the theoretical calculations that take into account the coherent tunneling and the order parameter mixing. Our work demonstrates the hybrid junctions as a distinctive platform for addressing pairing symmetry and emergent quantum phenomena.
authors: Yuying Zhu, Ziye Liu, Hongtao Yan, Lin Zhao, Xingjiang Zhou, Qi-Kun Xue, Ding Zhang

articles.title: Characterizing universal topological phases beyond spatial embedding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although Hamiltonians govern wave-matter interactions, conventional characterizations of topological phases of matter require more than the Hamiltonian alone, relying on global invariants defined on closed reciprocal-space manifolds or local commutation relations with position operators. This spatial dependence precludes a unique characterization of topological phases on an abstract platform, whose Hamiltonian can be defined independently of its spatial embedding. Here we establish a framework for characterizing universal topological phases, grounded in the invariance of topological features under arbitrary Hamiltonian-preserving deformations. We construct a Hamiltonian-based spatial embedding that groups a system's constituents according to their connectivity. This embedding, which reproduces the results of conventional topological diagnostics in established systems, enables a coherent extension of topological phases to complex networks using the Hamiltonian alone, further highlighting exceptional robustness in small-world networks. Our results reshape the conceptual foundations of topological physics by decoupling topological characterization from prescribed physical platforms.
authors: Sunkyu Yu, Xianji Piao, Namkyoo Park

articles.title: Ubiquitous topological materials protected by hidden partial symmetries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetries play a crucial role in protecting the topological phases of insulators, ensuring the robustness of their surface states against perturbations. Traditionally, these symmetries have to be obeyed by the system as a whole, which is a rather strong constraint. In this work, we demonstrate that topological effects can also be realized through a substantially weaker form of symmetry that we coin emphpartial latent symmetries. For these, invariance is required only at certain energy scales of an effective Hamiltonian, rather than for the object as a whole. Applying this idea, we construct weak-symmetry versions of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger and Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes models. These weak-symmetry models behave in many aspects just like their conventional brethren---in particular, they host robust edge states---, though the corresponding topological invariants are only emphapproximately quantized. We conclude this work by experimentally realizing Hermitian and non-Hermitian versions of such approximate topological insulators and probe their edge states. Overall, given the ubiquity of symmetry in all areas of physics and engineering, we foresee our work to serve as a cornerstone for exploring how conventional, strong symmetry requirements can be replaced by weak-symmetry ones.
authors: Lumen Eek, Xuelong Chen, Malte Röntgen, Wenlong Gao, Cristiane Morais Smith

articles.title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. Particular attention is given to the combined use of photoluminescence and absorption-related spectroscopy, electrostatic gating, polarization analysis, excitation-power and temperature dependences, magnetic fields, and time-resolved measurements to establish microscopic assignments. The role of alloying as an additional degree of freedom for engineering the excitonic hierarchy, spin-valley configuration, and magneto-optical response is also highlighted. By organizing the rapidly expanding phenomenology around experimentally accessible fingerprints rather than individual material systems, this Review aims to provide a practical and broadly applicable guide for identifying, comparing, and engineering excitonic states in high-quality two-dimensional semiconductors.

articles.title: Algebraic criteria for complete relaxation in autonomous and periodically driven open quantum systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive sufficient criteria that guarantee convergence of open quantum system dynamics to a unique long-time state independent of the initial conditions. We refer to this behavior as complete relaxation. Focusing on systems described by Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equations on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, our approach uses only elementary mathematical arguments. For autonomous systems, we recover three previously derived relaxation criteria, which can be expressed as algebraic conditions on the Lindblad operators and the Hamiltonian entering the GKSL equation. For periodically driven systems, we obtain a new criterion involving a similar algebraic condition and a local continuity requirement on the time-dependent GKSL generator. This result implies an earlier criterion for complete relaxation formulated in Ref. [J. Phys. A 52, 43LT01 (2019)]. We also discuss implications of our approach for periodically modulated classical master equations, as well as extensions to driven systems without a periodicity constraint.

articles.title: Magnetization and Josephson current coupling drives the Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 van der Waals junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Josephson diode effect (JDE) reflects symmetry breaking in the current-phase relation (CPR) of Josephson junctions, yet establishing its microscopic origin is often challenging. We investigate the mechanism of the JDE in van der Waals Josephson junctions based on FeTe0.55Se0.45, a platform where superconductivity, topology, and magnetism may coexist at the interface. Our devices exhibit a robust zero-field diode response with asymmetric switching currents. Magnetic-field measurements reveal a hysteretic Fraunhofer pattern and magnetic-resonance-induced voltage feature, evidencing interfacial magnetism coupled to the Josephson current. Microwave response further shows half-integer Shapiro steps with asymmetric evolution, demonstrating contributions from both a second harmonic and a magnetization-induced phase shift in CPR. Numerical simulations combining magnetization dynamics and Josephson phase dynamics reproduce these features, confirming that the JDE originates from interfacial coupling between magnetization and Josephson current. This work provides a transport-based route to pinpoint the microscopic mechanism of the JDE, establishing a platform for exploring magnetically active interfacial superconductivity, and enables the design of nonreciprocal superconducting devices in clean, interface-engineered van der Waals systems.
authors: Seung-Hyun Shin, Cheong-Eung Ahn, Chang-Won Choi, Taekoo Oh, Si-Young Choi, Genda Gu, Gil Young Cho, Gil-Ho Lee

articles.title: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field.
