articles.title: Probabilistic Human Health Risk Assessment of Potentially Hazardous Elements in Urban Park Soils. Implications for Risk-Based Environmental Management: A Case Study in the Municipality of Caldas, Colombia
articles.abstract: Urban recreational soils can retain potentially hazardous elements (PHEs), but concentration contrasts alone do not establish their sources or health implications. This study characterized As, Cd, Ni, Pb, Cr, Zn, and Cu in surface soils from five urban parks and one rural reference site in Caldas, Colombia. articles.title: Lost Schrödinger manuscript reveals his true view of quantum randomness
articles.abstract: Unlike classical physics, quantum mechanics generally cannot tell us exactly what will happen in an individual event. Instead, it predicts the probabilities of different outcomes. As one of the theory's early pioneers, Erwin Schrödinger played a key role in debates about what this randomness really means. However, part of his contribution has stayed hidden for more than 80 years.

articles.title: Laser-made lattice reveals discrete light solitons in tunable atomic vapor
articles.abstract: Scientists from the Quantum Technologies Group at the Institute of Physics Zagreb, in collaboration with a colleague from the Physics Department at the Faculty of Science (PMF), have experimentally demonstrated for the first time the existence of discrete one-dimensional (1D) solitons in an optically induced photonic lattice in warm rubidium vapor.

articles.title: Theory of the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall responses in time-reversal symmetry breaking superconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining the symmetry of the Cooper pairing in superconductors is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. Time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) is among the most distinctive symmetry-breaking pattern of a superconductor. An important subset of TRSB pairing states, including the topological pₓ₊ᵢₚ_y pairing, is expected to exhibit the optical anomalous Hall effect. However, the microscopic ingredients that enable the Hall response and their underlying organizing principle in clean superconductors remain unelucidated. Here, we develop a unified theory for TRSB multiband superconductors possessing inversion symmetry, and establish their intrinsic optical Hall response as fundamentally a quantum-geometric phenomenon. We distinguish unitary and nonunitary TRSB states. Diagrammatically, we identify two classes of processes: single-electron tunneling and Cooper-pair tunneling. Both involve at least one interband tunneling event driven by the interband velocity-which is closely tied to the interband Berry connection. We rigorously prove that interband pairing is a prerequisite for unitary states to generate intrinsic Hall response, whereas it is not absolutely needed for nonunitary states. In nonunitary states with intraband pairing alone, the Hall effect can arise through single-electron tunneling, provided spin-orbit coupling is present. An effective theory obtained by integrating out the hole degrees of freedom reproduces these results and shows how pairing may endow electrons with effective Berry curvature. Finally, through symmetry analysis, we show that intrinsic resonances near the superconducting gap edge are allowed in nonunitary states but forbidden in unitary states. Our work thus establishes quantum geometry as a unifying principle for the intrinsic Hall response in superconductors and provides a guide for distinguishing different candidate TRSB pairings.

articles.title: Exotic vortex states and enhancement of orbital upper critical fields in an s-wave quasicrystalline superconductor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasicrystals possess long-range order without translational symmetry, giving rise to intrinsically inhomogeneous superconducting states. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes mean-field theory, we investigate vortex states in an s-wave quasicrystalline superconductor on the Ammann-Beenker tiling, with particular emphasis on the high-field regime. We find that the vortex configuration can differ qualitatively from the Abrikosov triangular lattice. In particular, at filling ν=0.8, vortices preferentially penetrate weak-pairing regions centered on sites with coordination number 8, indicating that their spatial organization is strongly influenced by the local geometry. Furthermore, we observe an enhanced upper critical field. At ν=0.8, where the enhancement is particularly pronounced, the spatially averaged order parameter exhibits a plateau-like field dependence accompanied by the formation of vortex clusters. These clusters accommodate additional flux in locally weak superconducting regions, providing a microscopic interpretation of the plateau-like behavior. Moreover, the upper critical field increases upon cooling toward zero temperature without a clear sign of saturation.
authors: Takumi Fukushima, Yuki Yamamoto, Nayuta Takemori, Shiro Sakai, Masanori Ichioka, Anuradha Jagannathan

articles.title: Interaction-Induced Bloch Geometry and Transverse Thermoelectric Transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electron--electron interactions can reconstruct Bloch wave functions, changing their geometry and the associated thermoelectric response. We derive the linear thermoelectric response within the Hartree--Fock (HF) approximation using the thermal length-gauge density-matrix approach, resolving Drude, symmetric quantum-metric, and antisymmetric Berry-curvature contributions. In a noninteracting Bloch eigenbasis, we separate the reconstructed Berry connection into the noninteracting connection and an interaction connection. This gives bare, coherence, and interaction-connection contributions to the anomalous thermoelectric response. We determine the constraints imposed by spatial inversion, rotational, time-reversal, and combined symmetries on the three transport channels. In the relaxation-time approximation, the leading weak-broadening behavior is Γ⁻¹ for the Drude contribution, Γ for the quantum-metric contribution, and Γ⁰ for the Berry-curvature contribution. The interband scalings apply away from band degeneracies. Self-consistent calculations for the triangular-lattice extended Hubbard model illustrate how interactions generate Berry curvature and a quantum metric, change the symmetry of the system, and thereby contribute to transverse thermoelectric transport.
authors: Heng-Yu Di, YuanDong Wang, Zhen-Gang Zhu, Gang Su

articles.title: Superconductivity via repulsive interaction in the model with electrons and holes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a toy model of the 2D electron gas including electron-like and hole-like charge carriers hybridized between each other. Electrons and holes can move either in different layers or in the same layer. Undoped system is an insulator. Slight doping brings extra charge carriers having large density of states. We show that the screened Coulomb interaction is enough to stabilize the superconductivity in the slightly doped system. The symmetry of the order parameter corresponds to the spin-triplet p-wave order. For realistic values of the model parameters the superconducting transition temperature can reach the value of 150 kelvin.

articles.title: Electric-field tunable spin texture in dual-gated HfS₂/graphene van der Waals heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-charge interconversion provides the essential link between spin information and electrical signals in spintronic devices. In spin-orbit coupled systems, spin-charge interconversion can contain multiple components associated with different spin-polarization directions, reflecting the underlying spin texture. Tuning this spin texture therefore provides a way to control not only the magnitude of spin-charge interconversion, but also the balance among its different components. Graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures provide an attractive platform for this purpose because interfacial spin-orbit coupling can host multiple spin-charge interconversion channels that couple to different spin-polarization directions. Here, we demonstrate electric-field control of spin texture in a dual-gated HfS₂/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field allows us to disentangle electrostatic doping from electric field-induced spin-orbit effects. Nonlocal spin precession measurements show that near zero vertical electric field, spin-charge interconversion is dominated by a spin Hall component with out-of-plane spins. Increasing the vertical electric field enhances additional in-plane spin components with Rashba-Edelstein-like character, including both parallel and perpendicular to the charge current contributions. These results provide experimental evidence that a vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture and control the corresponding spin-charge interconversion components, demonstrating electrical tunability of spin-orbit functionalities.
authors: Haozhe Yang, Zhendong Chi, Eoin Dolan, Josep Ingla-Aynés, Beatriz Martín-García, Witold Skowroński, Marco Gobbi, Andrey Chuvilin, Luis E. Hueso, Fèlix Casanova

articles.title: Quantum criticality in a two-component two-dimensional nematic metal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nematic fluctuations alter the low-energy electronic behavior and reshape the mean-field phase diagram. We study a two-dimensional nematic metal with a two-component internal degree of freedom. Near the quantum critical point (QCP), longitudinal nematic fluctuations generate the non-Fermi-liquid self-energy propto|ømega|²/³, whereas transverse fluctuations give a subleading logarithmic, marginal-Fermi-liquid correction. Nevertheless, the transverse sector dominates the correction to the phase diagram through a quantum order-by-disorder mechanism: the emergent nematic background reshapes the electronic spectrum, alters the decay of nematic bosons, and produces a negative singular free-energy correction. This correction reconstructs the phase diagram, drives the transition first order, and is described by a scaling function whose two asymptotic limits define two critical regimes with free-energy corrections scaling as R⁸/³ and R³, respectively, where R is the order-parameter magnitude; their powers follow from the competition between the characteristic momentum of normal-state nematic fluctuations and that of the ordered-state background. These two regimes are experimentally distinguishable through nematic-susceptibility hysteresis measurements. The corrected phase diagram shows that the enlarged nodal α phase masks the otherwise bare QCP, making it inaccessible; consequently, the logarithmic self-energy correction is by no means negligible at low energies.

articles.title: Charge Density Wave transient states induced by ultrashort hard X-ray pulses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interaction of quantum systems with ultrashort laser pulses may lead to transient states far from equilibrium. Among these, Charge Density Wave (CDW) systems offer very rich non-equilibrium physics when submitted to ultrashort optical excitations in the infrared regime. In this Letter, we show that CDW systems pumped by ultrashort x-ray pulses excite the system in very different way. The x-ray pump, 6000 times more energetic than a laser pulse, pumping and probing the whole bulk system simultaneously, drives CDW systems in a novel reversible out of equilibrium state. The successive CDW states observed in the NbSe₃ system with respect to the arrival of x-ray pulses follow a non-thermal kinetic path. It is characterized by a change in 2k_F wavevector, correlation lengths and electronic gap, as well as a change of dimensionality, all of this takes place within a very long recovery time ranging from 450ns to 0.01s. Several scenarios are proposed, including transient nucleation and recombination of charged topological objects.
authors: D. Ghoneim, E. Bellec, L. Ortega, V. L. R. Jacques, A. A Sinchenko, P. Wzietek, U. Boesenberg, K. Kazarian, J. Moeller, J. D. Moore, A. Rodriguez-Fernandez, R. Shayduk, A. Zozulya, A. Madsen, D. Le Bolloc'h

articles.title: Unambiguous determination of the THz conductivity in driven YBa₂Cu₃O₆₊ₓ
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mid-infrared pump, THz probe experiments in YBa₂Cu₃O₆₊ₓ yield evidence of a high-temperature transient state of the material with the optical properties of a superconductor. However, there are ambiguities in the extracted transient c-axis THz optical properties, primarily resulting from the sublinear growth of the THz response with increasing mid-infrared pump fluence. It was proposed that this effect may be related to saturation of the material's response, which would then perturb its spatial profile and lead one to overestimate the induced change in the transient optical properties. Yet, sublinear growth of the signal could also arise from other effects unrelated to saturation, for example from a change in reflectivity or deposition depth for the pump pulses. Here, we remove this ambiguity by experimentally measuring the fluence-dependent complex optical constants at the 15-20 THz frequencies of the pump. We show that the observed sublinear growth is to be attributed in large part to the enhanced reflection and reduced penetration depth of the pump field at high fluences. When taking into account these findings, we confirm the original interpretation of a light-induced superconducting state both qualitatively and quantitatively.
authors: K. Kaj, K. H. Martens, D. Choi, M. Buzzi, D. Nicoletti, Y. Liu, B. Keimer, A. Cavalleri

articles.title: Projective symmetry groups beyond spin-1/2: Classifying integer-spin quantum spin liquids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wen's projective symmetry group (PSG), introduced a quarter of a century ago, reduced the classification of symmetric quantum spin liquids to an algebraic problem and has guided the study of spin-1/2 models and materials ever since. Many current candidate materials and quantum simulators, however, have spin-1 or larger moments, and no comparable classification exists for them. We formulate the PSG for fermionic partons of arbitrary spin S. Integer and half-odd-integer spins already differ in their gauge structure. Half-odd-integer spins give the familiar SU(2), U(1), and Z₂ invariant gauge groups, while integer spins give a different hierarchy that includes U(1)t̊imesZ₂ and Z₂×Z₂; the latter has no spin-1/2 counterpart. Three lattice-independent results follow for integer spin. Singlet pairing of the partons is odd under site exchange. A lattice symmetry can exchange the particle and hole representations of the local constraint, which forces symmetry-related sites into opposite constraint sectors. And a time-reversal-symmetric U(1) state with the same constraint on every site can be gapped only if the number of sites per unit cell is a multiple of 2S+1. We apply the formalism to the spin-1 diamond lattice, realized in frustrated A-site spinels, and find ten fully symmetric Ansätze up to second neighbors. In the J₁₋J₂ Heisenberg model at the mean-field level, the ground state depends on how the constraint is imposed. With the particle and hole representations, the lowest states are fully gapped U(1) states whose two sublattices sit in opposite constraint sectors, and one of them is gauge equivalent to a paired Ansatz. The classification provides a starting point for integer-spin quantum spin liquids on other lattices and in other materials.
authors: Atanu Maity, Chunxiao Liu, Rhine Samajdar, Yasir Iqbal

articles.title: Methods for Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations from the Dynamics of Quantum Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.

articles.title: Quantum-Enhanced Matterwave Interferometry in a Ring Waveguide
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a quantum-enhanced matter-wave interferometry protocol based on fractional-revival dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a ring, combined with a controlled interaction quench. Using the Truncated Wigner Approximation, we show that nonlinear evolution to the quarter revival generates modest spin squeezing of -2.03±0.28;dB, which subsequently degrades under further nonlinear evolution. In contrast, starting from a non-interacting condensate, a controlled interaction quench applied after the initial quarter-revival beam-splitter operation generates substantially stronger spin squeezing of -14.57±0.27;dB. We further show that phase control at t=3Tᵣ/8 rotates the squeezed quadrature onto the phase-sensitive direction hatJ_y, producing a phase-squeezed state at t=Tᵣ/2. The subsequent quarter-revival evolution converts this phase-squeezed state into a number-squeezed state, enabling population-difference readout. The resulting sequence provides a route to quantum-enhanced interferometry using the intrinsic fractional-revival dynamics of a ring together with controlled interaction and phase operations.

articles.title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29998v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift β→β-p. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.

articles.title: Fast and Sensitive Readout of a Semiconductor Quantum Dot Using an In-Situ Microwave Resonator with Enhanced Gate Lever Arm
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.00765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report an experimental study of a Si/SiGe double quantum dot (DQD) directly coupled to a niobium superconducting coplanar stripline (CPS) microwave resonator. This hybrid architecture enables high-bandwidth dispersive readout suitable for real-time feedback and error-correction protocols. Fast and sensitive readout is achieved primarily by optimizing the DQD gate lever arm, guided by MaSQE quantum dot simulations, which enhances the dispersive signal without requiring high-impedance resonators. We demonstrate a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of unity with an integration time of 34.54 nanoseconds, corresponding to a system bandwidth of 14.48 MHz and a charge sensitivity of 0.000186 e per square root hertz. Analysis of the voltage power spectral density (PSD) of the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) baseband signals characterizes the system's readout noise, with the PSD's dependence on integration time providing insight into distinct physical regimes.

articles.title: Resonating-valence-bond superconductor from small Fermi surface in twisted bilayer graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.26801v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding the mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is a central challenge in correlated moiré materials. The most intriguing question is about the nature of the normal state: is the Cooper pair formed from small Fermi surface or large Fermi surface? Here, we propose a unified theoretical framework describing a symmetric pseudogap metal with small hole pockets, dubbed the second Fermi liquid (sFL), which is topologically distinct from the conventional Fermi liquid. Our theory shows that superconductivity in TBG emerges from the sFL phase, with local moment pairing transferred to mobile carriers, giving rise to a smaller nodal superconducting gap on the small hole pockets. This framework simultaneously explains the pseudogap metal above the transition temperature and the two-gap nematic superconductivity below it, providing a comprehensive understanding of correlated physics in TBG.

articles.title: Atomic thermometry in optical lattice clocks: model discrepancies and their impact on lattice light shifts
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.08164v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate measurement of atomic temperature is fundamental for a wide range of applications, from quantum sensing to precision metrology. In optical lattice clocks, precise characterization of atomic temperature is required to minimize systematic uncertainties at the 10⁻¹⁸ level. In this work, we investigate atomic temperature measurements in the ytterbium optical clock developed at INRIM, IT-Yb1, employing sideband and transverse Doppler spectroscopy across a wide range of trapping conditions in a one-dimensional optical lattice. By implementing clock-line-mediated Sisyphus cooling [Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 053401 (2024)], we reduce the atomic temperature and enable operation at shallower lattice depths down to D = 50,E_R, where E_R is the photon recoil energy. We compare temperature estimates obtained from the perturbed harmonic oscillator model with those derived using a Born-Oppenheimer model [Phys. Rev. A 101, 053416 (2020)]. Discrepancies of up to a factor of four are observed between the temperature estimates obtained with the two approximations. We assess the impact of these modeling differences on the evaluation of lattice light shifts and find relative frequency deviations of up to 8×10⁻¹⁷. Although sufficiently low atomic temperatures and the consistent use of theoretical models reduce these discrepancies to the low 10⁻¹⁸ level, these results motivate further investigations that will be relevant to state-of-the-art optical lattice clocks.
authors: Irene Goti, Tommaso Petrucciani, Stefano Condio, Filippo Levi, Davide Calonico, Marco Pizzocaro

articles.title: Fermionic Condensation as the Universal Order Parameter for Mass Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fermion bilinear acquiring a non-zero vacuum expectation value and generating a mass gap underlies the Peierls instability, BCS superconductivity, the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio mechanism, and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model. These mechanisms are usually discussed separately, and their structural similarities have been noted only in passing. We argue here that the correct universal object is not the bosonic order parameter but the fermionic condensate, and we show that the four mechanisms fall into two universality classes distinguished by a single dimensionless parameter, r = hat m_φ² / hat y², the ratio of the scalar mass to the Yukawa coupling. The classes are separated by a critical line r_c(N_f) in the plane of r and the fermion flavour number N_f; they correspond to two distinct infrared fixed points of the renormalisation-group flow and differ in their critical exponents. We derive the classification from a large-N_f expansion followed by a functional renormalisation-group analysis using the Wetterich equation, which gives the finite-N_f correction hat y_*²⁽N_f) = 0.1125/N_f + 0.0023/N_f², a 12.5% enhancement over the leading-order prediction. The classification is predictive for systems whose class is not already known; for the organic conductor (TMTSF)₂PF₆ under pressure, we predict that both the spin-density-wave and superconducting phases lie in the fermion-bilinear class. We discuss the Standard Model Higgs as a borderline case in the scalar-primary class, and identify the composite-Higgs scenario as the particle-physics realisation of the fermion-bilinear class. A self-consistent Su--Schrieffer--Heeger calculation for polyyne chains realises the Peierls mechanism concretely, and we list five falsifiable predictions, two within reach of current techniques.

articles.title: Recovering What Breaks in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulation of a Lattice Gauge Theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A recent trapped-ion experiment realised a lattice gauge theory with the gauge field in the internal states of the ions and bosonic matter in their vibrations. We showed earlier that its noise damage can be predicted. Here, we show that most of it can be undone. The conservation law of the theory is a parity of each vibrational mode, which heating flips, so a heating event leaves a mark that can be read without disturbing the physics. We keep only the runs in which this mark never changed. With equal heating rates and continuous monitoring, the kept runs reproduce the heating-free dynamics exactly, with a closed-form yield. Reading the mark at finite intervals introduces a small bias linear in the interval, which we derive and bound. At the reported rates, a single final check removes most of the heating and preparation damage while accepting eight runs out of ten.

articles.title: Towards a Complete Kerr Soft-Hair Theory: Integrability, Counterterm Equivalence,and Quantum State Counting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The horizon symmetry construction of Haco, Hawking, Perry, and Strominger yield two Virasoro central charges 12J after a specified Wald-Zoupas correction. Turning that calculation into a black hole microstate theory requires separate control of nonlinear charge integrability, the allowed counter-term class, and quantum state multiplicities. We formulate exact local and global integrability tests, prove uniqueness of the counter-term coefficients within a one-parameter ansatz, and identify the quotient in which a physically meaningful uniqueness theorem must be stated. A coadjoint-orbit model supplies globally defined classical moment maps, while unitary highest-weight modules supply an explicit algebraic quantum realization for macroscopic positive angular momentum, neither construction is proved equivalent to the gravitational phase space. A character calculation shows why a single Virasoro representation, despite having the desired central charge, does not provide the required large-central-charge entropy. We derive a curvature improvement invisible to the constant mode, quantize a regulated area-boost corner polarization, and find a continuous kinematic spectrum with divergent Gibbs trace. Explicit local modular CFT spectra with identical central charges yield different finite-temperature entropies, demonstrating that the available symmetry and quantum consistency data do not select the microscopic theory. We give a conditional sufficiency theorem and a concrete sequence of calculations needed to establish a gravitational completion.

articles.title: Coupled Loop-within-Loop Resonators at the near-field: Extended Bandwidth and Short Pulse Response upon Parametric Conversion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric frequency conversion have seen a renewed interest, specifically in superconducting quantum circuits at GHz range. These nonlinear convertors are typically narrow band and one may wish to extend their frequency range. Here, two coupled resonators are investigated: a loop-within-loop structure, whose gap is coupled by short, a diode, or simply left open. While simulations and experimental results are limited to GHz range, the concept is general. On their own, the loops exhibit natural frequencies of ca, f=1.5 GHz and f/2=0.73 GHz, respectively; the coupling modifies the resonance frequencies and increases its bandwidth. In one example, signal is fed from one loop and is received by the other. In another example, the input signal is provided across a coupling diode and is received by either loops. It is shown that in the case of nonlinear coupling, the frequency bandwidth can be as large as 3 GHz. Such bandwidth is associated with a very narrow temporal response of less than 150 ps, suggesting coherent effects through high-harmonic excitations at the near-field.

articles.title: Coherent dynamics and ultrafast evolution of optical nonlinearity of self-hybridized exciton-polaritons in WSe2
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exciton-polaritons (EPs) are valuable for investigating macroscopic quantum coherent phenomena. However, overcoming the rapid decoherence of EPs under ambient conditions is challenging, even using delicately fabricated optical cavities. Here, we show pronounced coherent dynamics in thin flakes of WSe2 supporting self-hybridized EPs. Ultrafast two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) resolves two types of quantum beating: Rabi oscillation with a period of ~ 24 fs and a slower, ~ 50 fs period oscillation, revealing coherent coupling not only between excitons and cavity, but also between polaritons and dark states. Rapid evolution of 2DES line shape indicates a change of dominant optical nonlinearities from Rabi contraction of polaritons to many-body interactions of excitons in the first 100 fs, marking the transition from coherent to incoherent polariton excitations. The results are rationalized by a three-coupled oscillator model considering the inhomogeneous cavity field distribution. We also demonstrate coherent quantum beating between A exciton and its excited Rydberg state A* under ambient conditions. Our results shed light on the coherent control in readily accessible semiconductor thin flakes.
authors: Niu Xu, Jin Yang, Kaizhen Liu, Jianghao Shen, Weiming Song, Abbas Chimeh, Daniel Timmer, Jinhui Zhong

articles.title: Quasi-Phase-Matched Second Harmonic Generation in Poling-Free Lithium Niobate Microrings with Surface Molecular Pattern
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising integrated photonic platform owing to its large quadratic nonlinearity enabling vital applications such as second-harmonic generation (SHG), optical parametric amplification, and spontaneous parametric down-conversion. However, to achieve high SH conversion efficiency, quasi-phase matching (QPM) through periodic electrical poling is typically required, which remains challenging in certain applications like multiple-ring coupled devices. Here, we demonstrate a surface molecule patterning strategy to enable QPM in a poling-free TFLN microring for SHG. An on-chip normalized conversion efficiency of approximately 11.5%/W is obtained in the poling-free TFLN microring with surface molecular pattern, showing an approximate 400-fold improvement compared to the same microring without surface molecular pattern. This approach offers a versatile route to engineer interfacial nonlinear interactions for nonlinear optics and quantum photonics applications and may be extended to multiple-ring coupled resonators and other platforms.
authors: Jinsong Cheng, Simin Yu, Jiahe Wang, Yilun Zhang, Juanjuan Lu, Xiaoqin Shen

articles.title: Spin-Adapted Spin-Flip Tamm-Dancoff Approximation (XSF-TDA) for Singlet-Triplet Gaps in MR-TADF and INVEST Emitters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we assess the recently introduced spin-adapted TDA for spin-flip-down excitations (XSF-TDA) [Mol. Phys. e2631735 (2026)] as a practical approach to this problem. Starting from a high-spin restricted open-shell Kohn--Sham reference, XSF-TDA generates spin-adapted low-spin roots arising from open--open (OO), core--open (CO), open--virtual (OV), and core--virtual (CV) types of spin-flip-down excitations. Across four application sets comprising 243 benchmark cases, XSF-TDA substantially reduces the systematic positive bias observed for TDA and unrestricted spin-flip TDA (USF-TDA). With the B3LYP functional, XSF-TDA reduces the equal-set-weighted macro-MAE relative to USF-TDA from 0.252 eV (0.158 eV) to 0.102~eV (0.056~eV) with the ALDA0 (multicollinear) kernel. Its accuracy is competitive with state-specific ΔDFT and quasiparticle-energy DFT (QE-DFT), while being able to provide deeper mechanistic insight through the response vector. In particular, spin-adapted CV configurations provide selected higher-excitation character that strengthens the OO--CV dynamical-spin-polarization channel, which preferentially stabilizes the singlet states. We also identify an INVEST emitter with appreciable OO--OV mixing, suggesting a possible additional contribution to singlet stabilization when the CV contribution is small. The XSF-TDA method therefore provides practical singlet--triplet gap predictions together with interpretable state analysis for the screening and mechanistic understanding of MR-TADF and INVEST emitters.
authors: Hewang Zhao, Hongbo Wang, Liuxin Huang, Yunlong Xiao, Zhendong Li

articles.title: Synchronization-Induced Limit Cycles and Hysteresis in Spinor Exciton-Polaritons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the nonlinear dynamics of spinor exciton-polaritons in resonantly pumped microcavities. Using steady-state analysis and computing eigenfrequencies via Bogoliubov-like linearization, we show that multiple Hopf bifurcations beyond conventional bistability occur within specific power regimes and are not associated with stable solutions of the system. Owing to nonlinear excitonic interactions, these transitions occur at different pump powers during forward and backward pump sweeps, leading to pronounced hysteresis between fixed-point and limit-cycle states. In the spinor regime, multiple limit-cycle branches and associated dynamical hysteresis loops emerge due to the interplay of polarization coupling and spin-dependent nonlinearities. We show how the locations of the bifurcation points can be tuned by the pump frequency and other system parameters. Our results identify synchronization as the organizing principle underlying limit-cycle formation, dynamical hysteresis, and bifurcation cascades in driven spinor exciton-polariton microcavities.
authors: Saeid Asgarnezhad-Zorgabad, Zahra Jalali-Mola, Vladimir V. Konotop, Daniel Leykam

articles.title: Pushing beyond the memory barrier in propagation algorithms with randomization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Performant classical tools for simulating quantum circuits are important for benchmarking and supporting upcoming quantum devices. Pauli propagation offers promising capabilities, but deep circuits usually cause a rapid growth in the number of Pauli strings and can quickly exhaust the available memory. In this work, we introduce a randomized protocol that combines a specialized resampling schedule, merging, and a controlled amount of bias to keep the propagating Pauli sum within any prescribed memory budget. Additional computational resources can then be spent on embarrassingly parallel repetitions that systematically improve the estimate. Building on the open-source library PauliPropagation.jl, we show that 1) increasing memory of each simulation reduces the error systematically more than outside averaging, 2) resampling just enough to apply the next gate delays variance accumulation and gives better error-per-time trade-offs than more aggressive resampling, and 3) a small, controlled bias is crucial in cutting down variance and pushing far beyond unbiased randomization. The resulting framework can reproduce deterministic calculations while requiring several orders of magnitude less memory.
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Ricard Puig, Slimane Thabet, Zoë Holmes

articles.title: Bounds on Attainable Rate Modulation in Fermi's Golden Rule
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Controlling transition rates is a central objective across quantum optics, condensed-matter physics, and chemical physics, encompassing processes such as spontaneous emission, energy and charge transfer, spin relaxation, and chemical reactions. Although Fermi's golden rule provides a powerful framework for calculating such rates of weakly coupled transitions, conventional calculations require the interaction to be specified in advance; the range of rate responses attainable over a broader interaction space remains unknown. We formulate spectral-overlap golden-rule rates as quadratic forms of the interaction and derive rigorous bounds on rate modulation over a specified interaction space. As an example, application to energy transfer from a donor to a molecular vibration coupled to an optical cavity reveals that enhancement and suppression depend jointly on the interaction and cavity detuning, including continuous reversal of the rate response for a fixed interaction. The same approach may elucidate rate control for other golden-rule processes, including excitation-energy transfer, nonadiabatic electron transfer, nonradiative electronic transitions, vibrational and spin relaxation, and spontaneous emission.
authors: Kaisei Ohata, Jun-Yu Dong, Yasutaka Kitahama, Akihito Ishizaki, Keisuke Goda

articles.title: Photon Correlations Control Quantum Fisher Information in Coherent Multidimensional Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherent multidimensional spectroscopy probes interactions and dynamics of molecular systems through nonlinear optical signals. Quantum light excitation has been explored as a means of controlling these signals, raising the question of how excitation-light correlations affect the precision of molecular parameter estimation from the emitted signal. In this work, we show that photon-number correlations and two-photon coherence play distinct roles in encoding molecular information in the emitted rephasing signal. In the weak-emission regime and within the single Schmidt pair approximation, we derive a normally ordered information law in which the joint photon-number moment and the squared magnitude of the two-photon coherence weight the amplitude and phase sensitivities of the molecular response, respectively. For matched temporal modes and mean photon numbers in each input mode, two-mode squeezed vacuum enhances both weights relative to coherent excitation, whereas independent displaced squeezing preserves the amplitude weight but reduces the phase weight. The background population and its parameter dependence also affect the total quantum Fisher information, which therefore cannot be inferred from the coherent mean-field signal alone. We derive a leading-order bound on its enhancement over coherent excitation when the background population is nonnegative and common to the compared sources. These findings provide criteria for selecting excitation sources according to how the target molecular parameter affects the amplitude and phase of the response.
authors: Chenghong Huang, Yuta Fujihashi, Akihito Ishizaki

articles.title: A Broadband Room-Temperature Design for the Einstein Telescope
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29863v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The unique underground location of the Einstein Telescope (ET) is expected to substantially suppress seismic and gravity-gradient noise, providing a favorable environment for gravitational-wave detection at low frequencies compared with surface-based observatories. The baseline ET design aims to achieve broadband sensitivity through a xylophone configuration, in which separate cryogenic and room-temperature interferometers are optimised for low- and high-frequency gravitational-wave detection. However, achieving the target low-frequency sensitivity introduces substantial technical complexity caused by vertical suspension thermal noise, vibrations of the cryocooler, and detuned optical configuration. In this paper, we demonstrate an alternative, entirely room-temperature, fully resonant, single-interferometer architecture that addresses these challenges and achieves broadband sensitivity superior to that of the conventional ET xylophone configuration. Using mature fused-silica suspension technology, recent advances in optical coatings, and novel inertial isolation, we show that 4-m-long fused-silica fibres can meet the required suspension thermal-noise performance. We further demonstrate that vibrations, optical rigidity, and quantum back-action noise can be controlled through appropriate design of the interferometer, test mass suspensions, optical seismometers, and quantum states.
authors: Teng Zhang, Amit Singh Ubhi, Huan Yang, Alan V. Cumming, Mark Barton, Angus Bell, Fabio Bergamin, Giacomo Bruno, Katherine L. articles.title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with >17 dB of gain centred at sim5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with >100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across >1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.
authors: Boris Chesca, Tom Dixon, Narendra Acharya, Renuka D. Pothuraju, Jacob W. Dunstan, Connor D. Shelly, Oscar W. Kennedy

articles.title: Does hiding the post-processing from a memory-limited eavesdropper raise the noise tolerance of QKD? Timelocked advantage distillation and the 20% barrier
articles.abstract: Advantage distillation (AD) raises the finite-key threshold QBER of decoy-state BB84 from 9.5% to 17.3% [1]; asymptotically two-way post-processing tolerates 20%, and Bae and Ac´ın showed that an adversary who stores her probes until the AD parities are announced attains this limit, while one forced to measure each probe beforehand is held off until the 25% entanglement limit. We ask what a quantum computational timelock on the post-processing announcements can buy for this protocol, treating the parities, the block partition and the bases separately. Hiding the parities buys nothing: we prove that for every block size the best measurement made before the parities are known attains the adaptive Helstrom value, so the key length in the min-entropy accounting is the collective-attack value, 17.66% at 1014 pulses against the 17.30% certified by the entropic- uncertainty bound of Ref. [1]. Hiding the partition is different: the protocol of Ref. [1] partitions the sifted key at random after the quantum phase, so an adversary whose memory is shorter than the time between the probes of a block cannot bring them together. Modelling her by role-blind per-probe measurements, an assumption we state rather than derive, the Helstrom benchmark, which a numerical search over identical measurements does not improve at odd block sizes, gives 20.8% (Shannon) and 20.7% (min-entropy) at b= 9, 19.4% and 20.6% in a post-selection sensitivity check, with 25% as asymptote. Whether a memory holding many probes without the partition can do better is open; at up to six probes a joint measurement recovers most of the adaptive value, so at these sizes the gain rests on locality. Hiding the basis leaves the BB84 guessing probability unchanged at one- and two-bit blocks and, for six-state, shrinks the memoryless gain by an order of magnitude at two- and three-bit blocks.

articles.title: Quantification of sidewall defects and surface passivation strategies in blue InGaN/GaN micro light emitting diodes
articles.abstract: The efficiency of GaN-based micro-light-emitting diodes (µLEDs) degrades severely as the device size decreases, a phenomenon known as size-dependent efficiency droop. This degradation is primarily driven by an increased surface-to-volume ratio, where plasma-induced damage during dry-etching generates non-radiative recombination centers at the mesa sidewalls. To clearly elucidate the impact of these process-induced defects, this study investigates the physical extent of sidewall damage and its quantitative effect on the recombination dynamics of blue InGaN/GaN µLEDs across a size range of 5–100 µm. Spatially resolved micro-cathodoluminescence (MCL) mapping reveals a distinct damaged region approximately 1 µm along the mesa periphery. Furthermore, electrical characterization confirms that leakage current scales inversely with diode diameter, a challenge that is effectively mitigated through KOH wet etching and SiO2 passivation. By correlating the size-dependent shift in peak quantum efficiency current density (Jpeak) with the MCL-measured damage width using a modified ABC recombination model, we quantitatively extracted the defect density of the sidewall region. Our analysis indicates that the density of non-radiative recombination centers within the 1 µm-thick sidewall region is approximately 10–20 times higher than that of the bulk material. These results provide a rigorous physical basis for understanding the "efficiency cliff" in µLEDs and underscore the critical need for defect management in the sub-10 µm regime.

articles.title: Realization of decoherence-induced average symmetry-protected topological phases on quantum processors
articles.abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are conventionally formulated for pure states protected by exact symmetries. In open quantum systems, however, decoherence generates mixed-state ensembles in which average symmetry can instead emerge only after averaging over microscopic trajectories. In this work, we realize decoherence-induced average SPT (ASPT) order on programmable quantum processors. Starting from a one-dimensional cluster SPT, we engineer sublattice-selective Pauli-Z dephasing through ancilla-assisted quantum circuits. We diagnose the loss of strong symmetry through the decay of the symmetry charge, while the engineered channel preserves the corresponding symmetry at the ensemble level. Moreover, a two-replica Rényi-2 string correlator measured through destructive SWAP readout remains nontrivial, revealing the ASPT structure encoded at the density-matrix level. We further show that the engineered dephasing redistributes spectral weight among reduced-stabilizer sectors while preserving the characteristic twofold pairing of the half-chain entanglement spectrum. These results establish a gate-based route to engineering and probing ASPT order and demonstrate structured decoherence as a programmable resource for realizing mixed-state topological quantum matter.

articles.title: macroqc 2.0: An electronic structure theory software for large-scale applications
articles.abstract: macroqc is a quantum chemistry software package designed for high-accuracy electronic structure computations and large-scale molecular simulations. The macroqc framework provides efficient implementations of energies and analytic gradients for a wide range of many-body perturbation theory and coupled-cluster (CC) methods. In particular, the analytic gradient implementations of second-order Møller–Plesset perturbation theory (MP2), coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD), and CCSD with perturbative triples [CCSD(T)] exhibit excellent computational performance, even in comparison with established commercial quantum chemistry programs. In addition to conventional correlated methods, macroqc incorporates several advanced capabilities, including molecular fragmentation techniques for ground and excited state molecular systems and density-fitted analytic gradients. The software also supports interoperability with selected external packages through a flexible plugin framework, allowing developers to construct customized interfaces and extensions. The notable features of macroqc are the linear-scaling systematic molecular fragmentation (LSSMF) and the cluster-in-molecule (CIM) approaches, which enable the application of high-level post-Hartree–Fock approaches to large molecular systems that would otherwise be computationally prohibitive. Furthermore, the new machine learning (ML) library enables the integration of data-driven approaches into quantum chemical workflows, providing efficient tools for developing and applying ML-based models for molecular property prediction and electronic structure computations. With its combination of efficient implementations, advanced theoretical methods, and extensible design, macroqc is expected to serve as a useful platform for a broad range of computational chemistry applications.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Probing the potential for anti-Kasha behavior through direct measurements of S 2 lifetimes in xanthione and thioxanthone
articles.abstract: Several examples of “anti-Kasha” emission from higher excited electronic states (S n , n ≥ 2) have been reported recently for a variety of aromatic organic molecules. Even a modest suppression of the fast S n → S 1 internal conversion expected from the energy gap law, which underlies typical Kasha behavior, would have many advantages in photochemistry and in the development of photonic materials. Thus, it seems important to reassess the extent and reliability of the energy gap law. Here, we apply ultrafast spectroscopy and quantum chemical calculations to measure and interpret the S 2 relaxation times of a pair of structurally similar molecules, thioxanthone and xanthione. Our measurements broadly agree with earlier literature data, and the calculations suggest very different S 2 relaxation dynamics in these chromophores. The data are placed in the context of the energy gap law, which is found to work well for these and other planar aromatics regardless of the ππ * or nπ * character of the excited states involved. More flexible molecules placed on the energy gap law plot show enhanced rates of internal conversion. This reaffirmation of the broad applicability of the energy gap law suggests that where a molecule exhibits unexpectedly large “anti-Kasha” emission that result must be discussed in terms of particular features of vibronic coupling in that molecule.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Information content is a general-purpose collective variable for enhanced sampling
articles.abstract: Enhanced sampling methods typically require predefined collective variables (CVs) that presuppose knowledge of reaction coordinates, restricting the discovery of unanticipated transition mechanisms or intermediates. Here, we show that a local measure of information content in atomistic systems is a general-purpose CV for rare event sampling across molecular and condensed-phase systems. The method biases simulations toward information-changing configurations following a well-tempered metadynamics approach, thus balancing novelty and thermodynamic accessibility. Blind exploration of potential energy surfaces enables unsupervised discovery of metastable basins and reaction pathways, including competing transition channels inaccessible to conventional order parameters. We demonstrate the generality of the method across five systems spanning conformational sampling, homogeneous nucleation, glass formation, and solid-state phase transformations. Our approach uncovers non-classical phase transformation mechanisms despite its focus on general information theoretical quantities rather than kinetic or thermodynamic factors.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Introducing Vmol software: A highly parallelized multi-purpose DFT program based on real-space grid formalism
articles.abstract: We present a review of “Vmol,” a highly parallelized, multi-purpose density functional theory (DFT) software based on a real-space grid formalism. By utilizing higher-order finite difference methods and nonlocal pseudopotentials, “Vmol” serves as a versatile and computationally robust platform for Kohn–Sham DFT calculations. By virtue of the hybrid parallel implementation (message passing interface/OpenMP), it delivers high performance on massively parallel computers integrating many processors. In the development of these several decades, “Vmol” offered marked adaptability as an electronic structure program to various extensions, such as the hybrid Quantum Mechanical (QM)/Molecular Mechanical (MM) approach and its combination with a theory of solutions (QM/MM-energy representation) based on statistical mechanics. We provide brief reviews of these methods as well as the important results obtained by their applications. “Vmol” was also utilized to implement kinetic energy and static correlation functionals formulated within the novel framework of DFT. The outline of the method will also be reviewed.

articles.title: A machine learning closure for polymer integral equation theory
articles.abstract: Polymer reference interaction site model (PRISM) theory, a descendant of Ornstein–Zernike liquid state theory, is a powerful tool to predict the structure and thermodynamics of equilibrium polymer systems, but its accuracy and applicability can be limited in some important cases. Typically, these shortcomings are traced to the analytical closure relationships used to solve the integral equations. Here, we propose a machine learning (ML)-based closure relation trained on a dataset of coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of homopolymer melts and solutions. PRISM theory with the ML closure outperforms traditional atomic closures (e.g., Percus–Yevick) in predicting the structure of typical coarse-grained model systems. We also use the ML closure to accurately model the results of small-angle neutron scattering experiments. This ML-enhanced PRISM theory can, therefore, enable rapid soft materials discovery and design efforts.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Stress tensor in fundamental measure theory of hard-sphere fluids: A thermomechanical approach
articles.abstract: We derive the local pressure tensor generated by the original Rosenfeld fundamental measure theory (FMT) for hard-sphere fluids from an arbitrary infinitesimal deformation. The variation of a finite-distance FMT kernel is written via the line integrals of the local deformation gradient along the straight segment connecting its end points. The resulting symmetric pressure tensor consists of a local term expressed through the standard FMT weighted densities and a finite-range chord term. For a monodisperse hard-sphere fluid, differential relations between the Rosenfeld measures reduce the tensor to a closed one-body form. We demonstrate that no independent pair density or inhomogeneous Ornstein–Zernike equation is required. In the limit of homogeneous fluid, the tensor reproduces the Percus–Yevick compressibility equation of state. In planar confinement, the normal stress satisfies the hard-wall contact relation, the mechanical surface tension agrees with the surface excess grand potential, and the disjoining pressure agrees with the derivative of the confined grand potential with respect to slit width. The finite-range chord term extends the deformation method from local field theories to nonlocal weighted-density functionals.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Unraveling the electronic structure of 2-cyanonaphthalene: A cosmic PAH
articles.abstract: The recent astronomical detection of 2-cyanonaphthalene in Taurus Molecular Cloud-1 has highlighted the importance of substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in astrochemistry. Here, we present a combined experimental and theoretical study of the electronic absorption spectrum of 2-cyanonaphthalene in the ultraviolet (UV) and vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) regions (3.7–10.8 eV). Photoabsorption spectra in the UV region 3.7–4.9 eV are recorded in an n-hexane solvent at room temperature. Gas-phase photoabsorption spectra and absolute cross sections are measured at 343 K using synchrotron radiation in the VUV region (5.1–10.8 eV). Analysis supported by TDDFT calculations reveals that the UV region is dominated by valence π * ← π transitions, while the VUV region contains extensive Rydberg series converging to the first three ionization potentials. The strongest absorption band, arising from the HOMO–LUMO transition, peaks at 224 nm, close to the 217.5 nm interstellar extinction bump, suggesting that 2-CNN may contribute to this astrophysical feature. A well-resolved vibronic structure is observed throughout the spectrum. Franck–Condon simulations including the Herzberg–Teller effect for the S 1 , S 2 , and S 5 states reproduce the experimental spectra and identify the dominant progressions as arising from various C–H bending modes. Temperature-dependent simulations (15–500 K) of vibronic bands are used to study changes in spectral profile across various temperatures. Potential energy curves of singlet and triplet excited states with respect to C–H and C–CN bond lengths provide insights into the photostability of 2-cyanonaphthalene. The spectroscopic data and theoretical simulations presented here provide valuable inputs for understanding the photophysics and astrochemical evolution of 2-cyanonaphthalene.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Physically motivated iso-orbital indicator for meta-GGA exchange functionals
articles.abstract: The iso-orbital indicator α = ( τ − τ vW )/ τ UEG is a key ingredient of meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) functionals but diverges in low-density tails, causing unphysical exchange potentials and systematic bandgap errors as noted in Bartók and Yates [J. Chem. Phys. 150 , 161101 (2019)]. We replace the denominator of α with a physically motivated Pauli kinetic energy density drawn from the orbital-free density functional theory literature, eliminating the divergence in the low density atomic tail without any empirical regularization parameter. Testing two such enhancement factors, LKT and PGS, within the r 2 SCAN and MS2 exchange functionals, we find that the modified indicators suppress spurious oscillations in the semilocal exchange potential and restore correct electron localization in atomic tails. For a ten-member cubic semiconductor benchmark, the bandgap mean absolute error is reduced by 41.1% for r 2 SCAN@PGS and 48.8% for MS2@PGS, while cohesive energy accuracy is largely preserved. The consistent improvement across two functionals with distinct constructions confirms a physical rather than functional specific origin and motivates further development of meta-GGA functionals with constraint satisfying iso-orbital indicators.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: A cross-species comparison of excitation energy transfer in red-lineage photosystem I
articles.abstract: The photosystem I supercomplex (PSI) is a central component of photosynthesis in plants and algae. Its antenna subunits absorb light and transfer the excitation energy through an interconnected pigment network to the reaction center (RC), where it is converted to chemical energy. Although the excitation energy transfer (EET) in photosystems has been well characterized for individual organisms, evolutionary variation and inconsistent modeling settings have obscured cross-species comparisons, and it remains unclear which common structural features sustain EET efficiency. To address this, we combined kinetic modeling and rate theories to simulate EET processes in multiple red-lineage PSI complexes, each consisting of hundreds of chlorophylls, using the same set of experiment-derived parameters. We performed network analysis to probe how their EET processes respond to structural variation across distinct species. The exciton becomes increasingly delocalized as it approaches the core region of the PSI complexes. This, together with a radial site-energy bias, creates a strong exciton energy gradient (EEG) that funnels the exciton to the RC. However, the EEG is effective only over a limited distance range from the core region. In large PSI complexes, the pigments farther from the RC are weakly coupled, and the efficiency of long-range EET is maintained by additional features that complement the EEG, such as the pigment composition in the peripheral regions of the antenna, which also broadens the energy range of light absorption. By comparing red-lineage PSI complexes with a common parameter set, we provide a framework for relating EET to structural rearrangements in the pigment network.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Translation–rotation internal coordinates with splicing (TRICS): A new approach to molecular geometry interpolation
articles.abstract: We present TRICS (Translation–Rotation Internal Coordinates with Splicing), a novel internal-coordinate-based interpolation method for generating high-quality approximations to minimum energy pathways. Non-redundant internal coordinate (IC) systems can be used to generate chemically reasonable interpolated pathways between reactant and product structures, but it may fail for regions of configuration space where the IC system becomes numerically ill-defined. TRICS overcomes this limitation using multiple IC systems to generate separate interpolated paths that are iteratively spliced together into one continuous and smooth trajectory. We benchmarked the new method on 679 chemically diverse reactions, demonstrating excellent performance in generating interpolated pathways close to optimized transition-state structures. We further demonstrate the utility of TRICS for generating smooth and barrier-free interpolated pathways between critical points on excited-state potential energy surfaces. TRICS is available from the open-source geomeTRIC package.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: High magnetic moments in small rhodium-doped neutral cobalt clusters
articles.abstract: In the search for new magnetic materials, few atom metal clusters are of great interest because they can posses greatly enhanced magnetic moments with respect to bulk moments per atom. This is particularly the case for bimetallic transition metal clusters. Here, we report on the magnetism of Co n Rh m (n = 10–45 and m = 0–3) neutral clusters studied in molecular beam experiments using a combination of Stern–Gerlach magnetic deflection and mass spectrometry. Large dopant-induced and size-dependent increases in the total magnetic moment of the clusters were found, of up to 10% per added rhodium atom in the n = 15–30 size range. Density functional theory calculations indicate significant induced local spin magnetic moments on the rhodium atoms but fail to predict systematic enhancement of the spin magnetic moments on the cobalt atoms. The observed large enhancement of magnetic moments suggests an important role of orbital contributions.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Efficient and reliable modeling of large π -electron systems with the Pariser–Parr–Pople Hamiltonian and pCCD-based methods
articles.abstract: Model Hamiltonians offer a cost-effective way to capture the key physics of large π -conjugated systems. In this study, we combine the Pariser–Parr–Pople (PPP) model Hamiltonian with pair Coupled Cluster Doubles (pCCD)-based methods to study the excited-state electronic structures of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). The model Hamiltonian is implemented in the open-source PyBEST software package, which provides numerous pCCD-type models that have been shown to perform well for the electronic structure properties of large organic molecules when combined with quantum-chemical Hamiltonians and all-electron basis sets. Within the PPP model, we probe canonical Hartree–Fock and natural pCCD-optimized orbitals in predicting excited-state properties using the linear response formalism on top of pCCD. Their performance is compared with configuration-interaction-based methods and the conventional equation of motion coupled cluster singles and doubles (EOM-CCSD) approach. Our study demonstrates that pCCD/PPP-based approaches are an efficient, cost-effective, and accurate framework to compute excited-state properties in large π -conjugated organic systems, such as extended PAHs or other systems relevant to organic electronics.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Deriving initial kinetic energy and longitudinal spatial distributions of charged particles from time-of-flight profiles
articles.abstract: We present strategies for using time-of-flight (TOF) profiles to derive the kinetic energy distribution (KED) and the longitudinal spatial distribution (along the flight axis) of charged particles by varying the bias voltages on the acceleration electrodes. We take advantage of the spatial-focusing condition of the Wiley–McLaren design and, by applying a low field but a relatively high average potential in the acceleration region, can separate forward- and backward-flying ions in their TOF. Using an inversion method, the KED can be derived from the TOF of either forward- or backward-flying ions, and the overall TOF profiles can be reproduced. By grounding one of the electrodes in the acceleration region, the energy gained by a charged particle from the acceleration field becomes a sensitive function of its position along the flight axis. The time spread of the particles can then be used to directly derive the position of ionization along the flight axis when the initial kinetic energy of the charged particles is much lower than the acceleration energy. On the other hand, when both the initial kinetic energy and the longitudinal spatial distributions are significant, an optimization process involving an adjustable Gaussian spatial spread function and a few functions for the speed distribution can be performed. The TOF profile generated from the spatial spread function is convoluted with the TOF profile obtained from the speed distribution, allowing the longitudinal spatial spread and the kinetic energy distributions to be determined simultaneously. Both the theoretical framework and the experimental results are presented.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Effect of Mn²⁺ Substitution on the Structural, Magnetic, and Electrical Properties of Nanocrystalline Mg₀.₂MnₓCo₀.₈₋ₓFe₂O₄ Ferrites
articles.abstract: Nanocrystalline Mg₀.₂MnₓCo₀.₈₋ₓFe₂O₄ ferrites with Mn concentrations of x = 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 were synthesized by the citrate-assisted sol–gel auto-combustion method to systematically investigate the influence of Mn²⁺ substitution on their structural, morphological, magnetic, and electrical properties. X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns together with Rietveld refinement confirmed the formation of a cubic spinel ferrite structure without secondary phases. The structural parameters exhibited a composition-dependent evolution with Mn incorporation. The crystallite size decreased from approximately 50 to 20 nm with increasing Mn content, indicating progressive crystallite refinement, while the lattice parameter and hopping lengths showed an overall increasing tendency associated with the substitution of Co²⁺ by the comparatively larger Mn²⁺ ions and the accompanying redistribution of cations between tetrahedral and octahedral sites. Williamson–Hall analysis revealed composition-dependent microstrain, demonstrating the influence of Mn substitution on lattice distortion and defect-related structural characteristics. The calculated structural parameters, including X-ray density, dislocation density, and unit-cell volume, further established the correlation between Mn concentration and the evolution of the spinel lattice. FESEM and AFM investigations revealed nanoscale particles with composition-dependent agglomeration, surface morphology, and topographical characteristics. FTIR spectra exhibited the characteristic metal–oxygen vibrational bands associated with the tetrahedral and octahedral sites of the spinel lattice, confirming the structural framework of the synthesized ferrites. Magnetic measurements performed at 300 and 5 K demonstrated ferrimagnetic behavior for the investigated compositions. The M–H hysteresis loops showed relatively narrow loops at room temperature, whereas a pronounced increase in coercivity and remanent magnetization was observed at low temperature, reflecting enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy and reduced thermal fluctuations. The corresponding dM/dH curves provided further evidence of the temperature-dependent magnetic reversal mechanism. ZFC–FC magnetization measurements at different applied fields revealed significant thermomagnetic irreversibility, with stronger separation between the ZFC and FC branches at lower magnetic fields, indicating the contribution of magnetic interactions, anisotropy-energy barriers, and thermally activated spin dynamics. Impedance spectroscopy demonstrated strong frequency- and temperature-dependent electrical behavior characteristic of semiconducting ferrites. The decrease in impedance with increasing frequency and temperature suggests thermally activated charge-carrier hopping, while the broad and frequency-dependent relaxation features indicate non-Debye-type dielectric relaxation arising from the heterogeneous grain–grain-boundary structure. Among the investigated compositions, x = 0.6 exhibited particularly pronounced impedance and relaxation characteristics, suggesting enhanced grain-boundary polarization and charge-carrier localization. Overall, the results establish clear structure–morphology–magnetism–electrical property correlations induced by Mn²⁺ substitution and demonstrate that controlled compositional modification of Mg–Co ferrites provides an effective route for tailoring their magnetic anisotropy, magnetic reversal, charge transport, and relaxation behavior. The obtained multifunctional characteristics make Mg₀.₂MnₓCo₀.₈₋ₓFe₂O₄ ferrites attractive for potential applications in magnetic sensors, high-frequency devices, electromagnetic components, and related multifunctional magnetic technologies..

articles.title: Surface and pore co-functionalized ceramic membrane with Zr doped Co3O4 for SMX degradation through coupling peroxymonosulfate activation
articles.abstract: Peroxymonosulfate (PMS) based advanced oxidation has emerged as a promising strategy to decompose sulfamethoxazole (SMX). However, traditional powder catalysts commonly suffer from severe agglomeration and poor recyclability, In this work, Zr‑doped Co₃O₄ serving as an efficient PMS catalyst, was immobilized onto both surface and pore channels of an Al₂O₃ ceramic membrane, generating a dual functional CoZr@CM composite membrane. Such simultaneous surface‑pore functionalization delivers abundant accessible active sites, prolongs reactant retention duration and facilitates interfacial mass transfer. Benefiting from these merits, 97.1% SMX was degraded in optimized CoZr@CM and the first-order kinetic constant of SMX degradation was 90 times higher than that for powder catalyst. Moreover, the CoZr@CM/PMS system exhibited satisfactory removal capacity toward multiple recalcitrant organic contaminants including phenol, bisphenol A and rhodamine B. Long‑term continuous experiment demonstrated robust operational stability, with 87.5% SMX removal maintained after 17 h run time. Water‑matrix variables including solution pH and ubiquitous background anions were further evaluated for their influences on SMX degraation Quenching experiment and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) test confirmed SO₄•⁻ as dominant species, accompanied by a small amount of •OH and 1O2. Based on the liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) results, three plausible degradation pathways of SMX were proposed and the trends in toxicity changes of intermediate products were analyzed. This research offers an alternative route to mitigate the application bottlenecks of powder catalysts for wastewater remediation.

articles.title: Nanoporous graphene homojunction mediated by interface charge transfer
articles.abstract: The construction of carbon-based hetero- or homojunctions is a key strategy for expanding their functional boundaries and enabling new quantum devices. On-surface synthesis provides a promising route for the precise fabrication of such structures. Although significant progress has been achieved in one-dimensional graphene nanoribbon hetero- or homojunctions, analogous two-dimensional systems remain largely unexplored. Here, we developed an AgTe monolayer intercalation method to fabricate nanoporous graphene (NPG) homojunctions. By controlling tellurium deposition, NPG islands spanning both the Ag(111) substrate and the AgTe monolayer were successfully synthesized. Owing to the interfacial charge transfer differences, the NPG exhibits different semiconductor behaviors on Ag(111) and the AgTe monolayer, resulting in the formation of an NPG homojunction with the type-II band alignment. The entire fabrication process of the NPG homojunctions was examined by scanning tunneling microscopy, and evidence for the type-II band alignment was obtained by scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. This intercalation strategy circumvents the randomness inherent in the synthesis of carbon-based heterostructures and offers a promising route toward two-dimensional carbon-based junctions with controllable band alignment.

Here, the authors calculate SOT in monolayer Fe 3 GeTe 2 and Fe 3 GaTe 2 , van der Waals ferromagnets with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and no reliance on heavy atoms for strong spin–orbit coupling. Horizontal mirror symmetry forbids conventional in-plane spin accumulation for out-of-plane magnetization, while tilting the magnetization enables a strongly angle-dependent response. Combining density functional theory, Wannier interpolation, and Kubo formalism, they map the torque across the magnetization sphere. They reveal hidden torques on mirror-related Fe atoms up to 30 times the net torque, whose cancellation could be lifted through van der Waals engineering. [Phys. Rev.
