We then present VPFlow, a value-predictive planner that pairs the world models with a one-step flow policy and plans in its noise space via evolutionary search. It enables policy improvement with imagined generalized advantage and reduces out-of-distribution queries common in action-space planning. On 30 state and pixel OGBench datasets, VPFlow surpasses model-free baselines by at least 30.3 and 10.1 percentage points in success rate, respectively, and outperforms latent planners LeWorldModel, PLDM, and TD-MPC2. It achieves this despite a latent prediction error orders of magnitude larger than with state prediction, while minimizing this error lowers success rate. This demonstrates that value-predictive representations, not exact state prediction, are what offline planning requires.

articles.title: Integrity Assessment of Buried Pipelines under Surcharge Loading Based on a GA-BP Neural Network
articles.abstract: To enable rapid integrity assessment of buried natural gas pipelines subjected to construction surcharge loading, a three-dimensional ABAQUS finite element model incorporating nonlinear pipe–soil contact was developed. The model was validated through mesh-independence analysis and comparison with experimental data reported in the literature, yielding a mean error of 6.32%. The results showed pronounced stress variations in the pipeline within the surcharge-loaded region, with the maximum von Mises stress occurring at the pipe bottom. Based on 100 simulation samples generated using Latin hypercube sampling, a GA-BP neural network model was developed to predict the maximum pipeline stress, achieving a R² of 0.9691. An integrity assessment framework was subsequently established by integrating the prediction model with pipeline failure criteria, and stress contour maps were generated to characterize the coupled effects of multiple influencing factors. Engineering application to three in-service pipelines in the Penglai Dengying Block showed that Pipeline No. 3 reached a peak stress of 219.11 MPa, exceeding the allowable stress of 216 MPa and indicating a potential risk of failure. Therefore, surcharge loading should be restricted and appropriate reinforcement measures should be implemented.

articles.title: Bioprocessing of coconut husk to produce second-generation bioethanol using Zymomonas mobilis ZM4
articles.abstract: Coconut husk is an abundant lignocellulosic residue generated by the tropical coconut processing industry and remains largely underutilized despite its high carbohydrate content. However, its recalcitrant structure limits efficient conversion into fermentable sugars and bioethanol. In this study, an integrated strategy involving sequential pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, and microbial fermentation was developed for efficient valorization of coconut husk into second-generation bioethanol. Sequential pretreatment using dilute acid, alkaline treatment, and bleaching significantly improved cellulose accessibility, as confirmed by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy analysis. Enzymatic hydrolysis using a cellulase–hemicellulase cocktail released substantial fermentable sugars, yielding approximately 230 mg glucose and 161.25 mg xylose per gram of raw coconut husk. High-performance liquid chromatography analysis confirmed efficient saccharification, corresponding to sugar recovery efficiencies of approximately 50–60% following pretreatment and hydrolysis. Mass balance analysis indicated that enzymatic hydrolysis released 0.23 g glucose g⁻¹ biomass, of which Zymomonas mobilis converted approximately 83% into ethanol, resulting in a final yield of 0.0975 g ethanol g⁻¹ biomass. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of converting coconut husk into fermentable sugars and bioethanol and highlight its potential as a sustainable feedstock for second-generation biofuel production. The integrated bioconversion framework presented here provides insights for improving biomass utilization and supports the development of circular bioeconomy strategies for agricultural residue valorization.

articles.title: Assessment and Evolution of Surface-Subsurface Landform Connectivity of Jabal Al Qarah in Saudi Arabia: A Potential World-Class Geomorphological Heritage
articles.abstract: Worldwide, surface and subsurface connectivity of geomorphic processes, landform diversity, and their geoheritage importance are very interesting topics. Jabal Al Qarah is a mesa (residual hill), located in Al Ahsa, Saudi Arabia. This mesa offers unique diversity in surface and subsurface landforms. Therefore, the scope of this paper is a detailed geomorphological heritage assessment of Jabal Al Qarah, which was a gap. The geomorphological heritage assessment is considered based on scientific and additional value. The key landforms in Jabal Al Qarah are vertical slots, a rill network, a rectangular fault system, a rectangular cave system, a rock pillar, and an in-situ boulder, which belong to the IUCN Geoheritage Theme: Erosional, Cave and Karst System. Jabal Al Qarah comprises a deposition of marine sedimentation, which is followed by the orogeny of the tablelands and plateaus in the eastern part of Saudi Arabia. Due to weathering and denudation, this mesa unit detached from the Shedgum Plateau and formed the mesa. Following the rectangular fault system that is exposed at the surface, weathering forms a rectangular cave system. Jabal Al Qarah is a unique example with spectacular surface and subsurface landform diversity, high representation, well accessible, and a global example of the complex geomorphic process associated with cave formation. Therefore, Jabal Al Qarah is a strong candidate for inclusion in the world-class geomorphological heritage.

articles.title: An Effective Polyamine-Based Coagulation–Flocculation Approach for Cyanide and Color Removal from Steelmaking Wastewater
articles.abstract: The present work demonstrates the usability of organic polymers as coagulant/flocculation aids for successful removal of free cyanide and color from steelmaking industrial wastewater. The effluent was characterized using various analytical instruments and contained a high cyanide concentration of about 13.2 ppm and color intensity of 7350 Pt-Co due to the presence of suspended solids, iron-containing species, and other lipophilic colloids. The treatment process involved the sequential addition of 60 ppm copper sulfate catalyst, 300 ppm sodium metabisulfite, and 400 ppm ferrous sulfate to convert toxic cyanide into less toxic cyanate, followed by coagulation and flocculation. Four different polyamine coagulants with varying molecular architectures were evaluated for treatment performance. Among them, the linear polyamine coagulant PA-L exhibited superior performance compared with branched and highly branched analogues, owing to its enhanced bridging capability and improved accessibility of cationic functional groups. Using an optimum dosage of 100 ppm coagulant followed by 4 ppm anionic flocculant aid, the cyanide concentration was reduced from 13.2 ppm to 0.2 ppm and color from 7350 Pt-Co to 90 Pt-Co, corresponding to removal efficiencies of 98.5% and 98.8%, respectively. The treated effluent satisfied the prescribed discharge limits for cyanide and exhibited excellent clarification characteristics. The study further highlights the influence of polymer architecture on coagulation performance and demonstrates that polyamine-based coagulation–flocculation is a simple, scalable, and economically attractive treatment approach for steelmaking wastewater. Based on the optimized treatment conditions, a scale-up study was successfully carried out for the treatment of actual steel plant wastewater.

articles.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Atom-Resolved VOCs Adsorption and Reactivity on Metal Oxides
articles.abstract: The adsorption and reactivity of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) on metal oxides govern catalytic reaction pathways, yet predictive rules remain elusive because molecular functionality, surface chemistry, and adsorption geometry are strongly coupled. Here we report a transferable adsorption dual-tower framework (AdsDT) that independently encodes molecular and crystal features to predict adsorption energies directly from unrelaxed CIF structures. By pretraining on the Open Catalyst 2020 dataset and progressively transferring through intermediate adsorption systems, AdsDT enables rapid construction of metal oxides-VOCs interaction databases and achieves strong agreement with density functional theory calculations (R2 = 0.85). Using 816 TiO2 (anatase, 101)-VOCs adsorption configurations, we combine molecular fingerprints, SHAP analysis, and graph attention mapping to identify fragment-level and atom-resolved adsorption contribution. Saturated alkyl carbon environments increase predicted adsorption energies, whereas unsaturated and electronegative atoms, particularly carbonyl oxygen, favor stronger adsorption. Extension to eight representative metal oxides reveals material-dependent and functional-group correlation. Furthermore, a bond activation score integrating atomic attention, bond dissociation energy, and bond polarization links adsorption configurations to reaction pathways, showing that adsorption sites activate neighboring bonds through electronic redistribution rather than serving simply as cleavage centers. These results provide transferable atom-resolved descriptors for VOCs adsorption and catalytic reactivity across metal oxides.

articles.title: Chemical and Microstructural Characteristics of Soils Treated with Pulverised Charcoal and Gum Arabic
articles.abstract: Chemical and microstructural characterisation provides a basis for understanding interactions between locally available additives and soil. This study examined pulverised charcoal, gum arabic, and two soils from Ibadan treated with nominal charcoal–gum proportions of 2%–2%, 4%–2%, and 2%–4%. Proximate and ultimate analyses, reported oxide compositions, six X-ray diffraction patterns obtained after 14 days, and twelve scanning electron micrographs assigned to 7 and 14 days were evaluated. Charcoal contained 10.60% moisture, 40.40% volatile matter, 30.75% fixed carbon, and 18.25% ash. The revised oxide entries for gum arabic totalled 92.30%, with a loss on ignition of 7.70%. In treated soils, silica and alumina contents ranged from 49.01 to 56.46% and from 22.02 to 32.10%, respectively. The available oxide entries and loss on ignition summed to 99.97–100.00%, although one phosphate entry was unavailable. Changes between curing ages varied across treatments, indicating contrasting compositional patterns. Diffraction annotations identified quartz, feldspar, mica, kaolinite, and illite, while microscopy descriptions indicated heterogeneous granular, plate-like, and aggregated surfaces. This study provides a preliminary description of the reported analytical entries and author-assigned specimens. Interpretation remains subject to confirmation of the analytical reporting bases and specimen traceability, including a potentially repeated microscopy field. The findings inform further investigation of the combined treatment; confirmation of reaction mechanisms and engineering suitability will require complementary controls and performance testing.

articles.title: Magnet-free reconfigurable alterspin photonics at optical frequencies
articles.abstract: Altermagnetism is a compensated magnetic order in which spin polarization alternates between symmetry-related momenta despite zero net magnetization. Recently, an altermagnetic photonic crystal was demonstrated by mapping electron spin onto light spin, while still relying on gyromagnetic materials and magnetic bias. Hence, it is rather elusive to extend the altermagnetism concept to optical frequencies. Here we realize reconfigurable magnet-free alterspin photonics in an all-dielectric photonic crystal across 740–800 nm. The in-plane square lattice fixes the four-period angular form of the alterspin texture, while an extrinsic out-of-plane dielectric perturbation controls its sign and amplitude. A liquid droplet enables writing, erasing, and reversing the alterspin texture. We further establish a criterion to evaluate the alterspin order and quantify the measured texture. Our results provide a route toward visible-to-near-infrared alterspin photonic systems that are magnet-free and externally reconfigurable.

articles.title: Analytical Modeling of 12/10 stator/rotor pole configuration of Switched Reluctance Motors Considering Magnetic Saturation for Blood Pump Applications
articles.abstract: This paper presents a comparative analytical study of torque ripple and radial force characteristics in 3-, 4-, and 6-phase switched reluctance motors (SRMs) with a 12/10 stator/rotor pole configuration, accounting for magnetic saturation effects. While multi-phase SRMs are generally expected to offer improved torque smoothness over conventional 3-phase designs, a systematic comparison of their torque ripple and radial force behavior particularly under saturated conditions has not been thoroughly investigated in the literature. To address this gap, a unified two-dimensional analytical model is developed based on Fourier series, incorporating saturation effects through a modified flux-linkage characteristic. The model predicts electromagnetic torque and radial force as functions of rotor position and phase current for all three phase configurations, and is validated against finite element simulations. The comparative results reveal distinct performance trends across the different phase numbers, highlighting trade-offs between torque ripple suppression, radial force magnitude, and force ripple. A key contribution of this work is linking radial force behavior to bearingless motor technology, where unbalanced radial forces directly affect rotor suspension stability and increase the control effort required for magnetic levitation. This is particularly critical for blood pump applications, where mechanical oscillations and bearing friction impose excessive mechanical stress on blood cells, increasing the risk of hemolysis. By identifying the optimal phase configuration that minimizes both torque ripple and radial force fluctuations, this study provides a foundation for designing quieter, more reliable bearingless drives with reduced mechanical stress and improved hemocompatibility

articles.title: Dispersive Liquid-Liquid Microextraction for Arsenic Speciation in Complex Food Matrices
articles.abstract: Arsenic is a highly toxic metalloid that poses serious health risks through contaminated food and water. The World Health Organization (WHO) has established ultra-low permissible limits for arsenic, demanding analytical methods with exceptional sensitivity and accuracy. Dispersive liquid-liquid microextraction (DLLME) has emerged as an effective sample preparation technique for arsenic determination and speciation, offering high enrichment factors, rapid extraction, minimal solvent consumption, and operational simplicity. This review presents an overview of recent DLLME-based strategies for arsenic monitoring across food, aqueous, and biological matrices, with particular emphasis on food applications and related analytical challenges. Special emphasis is placed on advanced extraction media including deep eutectic solvents (DESs), ionic liquids (ILs), and magnetic ionic liquids (MILs), often integrated with magnetic solid-phase extraction or automated lab-in-syringe systems. Key performance metrics are compared for total arsenic, inorganic As(III)/As(V), and selected organic arsenic species across food, water, and biological matrices. By critically identifying matrix-specific challenges, speciation-related limitations, and gaps in method standardization, this review provides practical perspectives for developing more reliable DLLME-based strategies for arsenic monitoring through improved analytical approaches for food and water safety.

articles.title: Neural correlates of empathy in autism: a coordinate-based meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Purpose. Autistic and non-autistic people often differ in how readily they understand one another’s intentions and emotional states. Although empathy is commonly invoked to explain these differences, which components of empathic processing differ in autism, and their neural underpinnings, remain unclear. Methods. We conducted a pre-registered coordinate-based meta-analysis (activation likelihood estimation; ALE) of task-based fMRI studies of empathy in autism, examining within-group convergence, conjunction and between-group divergence separately for affective and cognitive components. Eleven studies (12 independent samples) met inclusion criteria, comprising 213 autistic and 216 non-autistic participants and 600 foci across 35 experiments; a multi-agent AI second reviewer supported screening and extraction. Results. Both groups shared a core empathy network (precuneus/posterior cingulate cortex, right middle temporal gyrus/posterior superior temporal sulcus, left inferior frontal gyrus, dorsomedial paracingulate), but the rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, a canonical cognitive-empathy hub, converged only in non-autistic participants. The between-group contrast was strongly asymmetric: non-autistic participants exceeded autistic convergence in ten regions, eight of them cognitive-empathy nodes, the largest in rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; autistic participants exceeded non-autistic convergence in one region only, the posterior right temporoparietal junction. Subdomain analyses indicated relatively preserved convergence for affective empathy, with sparser, more diffuse overlap for cognitive empathy. Conclusion. These findings are consistent with a dissociation between relatively preserved affective and altered cognitive empathy in autism, and suggest a redistribution of activation within the mentalizing network rather than a global absence of empathy-related processing. Key words: autism spectrum disorder; empathy; activation likelihood estimation; functional magnetic resonance imaging; dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; temporoparietal junction

articles.title: A Rule-Breaking Class of Planar Central Chiral Molecules in Planar Tetracoordinate Carbon Systems
articles.abstract: Unusual bonding, stability, and potential applications of planar tetracoordinate carbon (ptC) have captivated researchers over the past five decades. Chirality has been reported in both a central carbon in a non-planar structure and in a planar geometry without a central carbon. Here, for the first time, the present work introduces the concept of planar tetracoordinate chiral carbon (ptCC) systems, in which four distinct ligands create an asymmetric center while maintaining planar tetracoordination at the carbon. This study identifies eight ptC structures that exhibit chirality and form enantiomeric pairs. The chemical bonding and stability of the ptCC structures were analyzed using the Adaptive Natural Density Partitioning, and Electron Localization Function. The aromaticity of ptCC geometries was assessed using nucleus-independent chemical shift analysis. The chirality of the ptCC systems was confirmed by examining their chiroptical properties, as evidenced by electronic circular dichroism and vibrational circular dichroism spectra. The observed chiroptical spectral features show mirror-image profiles for the enantiomeric pairs investigated. As discussed, this rule-breaking class of ptC molecules exhibits chirality at the planar central carbon. The ptCC systems investigated exhibit structural features that suggest potential utility in asymmetric catalysis and materials applications.

articles.title: Inside an Arnoldi Mushroom: Minimally Invasive Multi-Analytical Characterisation of a Nineteenth-Century Papier-Mâché Object
articles.abstract: This work presents the adapted application of X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) for the analysis of painted historical papier-mâché objects, with particular focus on optimising the experimental parameters of the laser-based techniques to minimise potential damage. Mock-ups of the material, featuring different pigment finishes, were used to evaluate the analytical performance of the techniques and assess laser-induced alterations, establishing a balance between analytical signal quality and surface impact. The selected conditions were subsequently applied to a historically significant case study: a 19th-century papier-mâché model of the mushroom Amanita muscaria from the Arnoldi collection. The papier-mâché matrix was attributed to a mixture of a calcium-based component, including gypsum and calcium carbonate, and a silicate-based component, including quartz and kaolin. Red lead, chrome yellow, and a lithopone-based finishing layer were identified as the main pigments and surface treatments. To complement the spectroscopic analysis, ultraviolet-induced visible fluorescence (UVF) photography was used to further characterise specific pigments, while X-ray computed tomography (CT) was employed to non-destructively investigate the internal structure of the object, revealing wooden cores within the mushroom bodies and the depth of fractures. These results provide insights into the materials and conservation state of the model and demonstrate the value of combining complementary analytical techniques for the study and characterisation of fragile cultural heritage objects.Keywords: Papier-mâché, LIBS, Raman spectroscopy, XRF, X-ray CT Scan, Cultural heritage

articles.title: SimuScan-Agent: language-model orchestration of synthetic-data-driven autonomous atomic force microscopy
articles.abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) enables nanoscale characterization, but large-area investigations remain slow and require coordination of data preparation, model training and instrument operation. Here we introduce SimuScan-Agent, an LLM-orchestrated framework that translates natural-language objectives into adaptive AFM workflows. Combining multimodal morphological sources with physics-informed simulation, it generates annotated synthetic datasets without manual per-image labeling, trains and deploys segmentation and representation-learning models, and guides acquisition using online detections and class-specific sampling objectives. In simulations, probabilistic active exploration reduced measurements and sampled area by approximately 71% relative to raster scanning. Experimentally, SimuScan-Agent explored a ~10 mm² region by sampling 17.2% of available positions, estimating class-specific spatial distributions and assembling a morphological library to identify representative and atypical nanostructures. By linking synthetic-data generation, machine learning and adaptive acquisition through natural-language interaction, the framework lowers barriers to goal-directed nanoscale studies and offers a foundation for more intelligent, autonomous AFM systems that adapt experimental decisions to what they learn during measurement.

articles.title: Collaborative Mass Matrix Adaptation for Multi-Chain Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), together with its adaptive variant, the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS), is a standard tool for Bayesian posterior inference. In practice, however, its efficiency is often limited by warmup adaptation. In particular, the mass matrix is typically estimated from the trajectory history of a single chain. When the target posterior exhibits strong dependencies or the warmup budget is limited, this estimate can have high variance, leading to inefficient exploration and frequent treedepth saturation. We propose Collaborative NUTS (C-NUTS), a simple yet effective modification that pools gradient and position information across N parallel chains during warmup to construct a numerically stable, pooled covariance estimate for the mass matrix. This approach is particularly effective in the common N < d regime, where instantaneous cross-chain scatter matrices are rank-deficient and naive updates are unstable. To ensure robustness in multimodal targets, C-NUTS incorporates a lightweight safeguard that monitors between-chain dispersion and temporarily reverts to single-chain adaptation when the chains appear excessively separated. Under standard conditions for adaptive MCMC, we show that C-NUTS preserves the correct stationary distribution. Empirically, C-NUTS improves effective sample size per second by up to threefold over Stan’s dense Euclidean metric adaptation on a range of benchmarks, including correlated Gaussian targets, hierarchical models, and high-dimensional regression problems. The largest gains occur at moderate dimensions, approximately 50 sim 200, where single-chain covariance estimates are particularly unstable. These results suggest that sharing warmup information across chains can substantially improve adaptation efficiency without changing the underlying NUTS transition mechanism.

articles.title: Machine-learned potentials link vacancy-dependent copper transport to post-implantation profiles in silicon
articles.abstract: Copper contamination threatens silicon devices because mobile Cu can form electrically active defects and redistribute during thermal processing. Here we combine DFT-informed implantation simulations, an actively learned deep potential (DP) and large-scale molecular dynamics to connect elementary Cu migration with vacancy-dependent transport and annealed depth profiles. The DP reproduces DFT energies and forces with root-mean-square errors of 3.16–3.71 meV/atom and 35.10–88.30 meV/Å, respectively. Nudged-elastic-band calculations yield an interstitial migration barrier of 0.192 eV, close to the DFT value of 0.185 eV, and capture the energetic preference for Cu occupation of a Si vacancy. Across systems containing eight Cu atoms and 0, 2, 4 or 8 Si vacancies, atom-resolved trajectories reveal competition between mobile interstitial Cu and vacancy-associated Cu. Increasing vacancy number raises the prevalence of locally confined Cu and changes the ensemble-averaged transport behaviour. The vacancy-free system has an apparent activation energy of 0.202 eV, comparable in magnitude to reported experimental values of 0.15–0.18 eV. The combined DFT-MD + DP framework also reproduces the principal features of SIMS profiles before and after annealing. Relative to the MC/BCA + KMC workflow assessed here, it reduces mean-normalized NRMSE by 47–61% across the full profiles, with improvements in both the near-surface region and low-concentration tail. By linking Cu–vacancy interactions to measurable redistribution, this framework offers a route to jointly evaluating implantation-induced defects and annealing conditions when seeking to limit mobile Cu and residual Cu–defect complexes in silicon.

articles.title: Monolithic Vertically Stacked Carbon Nanotube Transistor with Emergent Negative Transconductance for Ternary Logic
articles.abstract: Vertical integration offers an opportunity to engineer transistor responses as well as device placement. Here, we demonstrate negative transconductance (NTC) using two carbon nanotube (CNT) network channels monolithically integrated on opposite sides of a common gate. The vertically stacked NTC transistor connects the channels internally through a via and retains three external terminals. Sequential processing yields a lower channel that is electron-dominant ambipolar under top-gate operation after HfO2 deposition, while the subsequently deposited upper channel remains p-type. Their contrasting gate responses shift the current bottleneck between layers, producing a local current peak. Channel geometry and upper-layer CNT density tune this response, yielding an extracted peak-to-valley current ratio above 104 at a drain-voltage magnitude of 0.1 V. Paired with an n-type CNT pull-down transistor, the device enables a ternary inverter at a 3 V supply, with three output states and two voltage-gain peaks exceeding maximum 6. Comparisons across fabricated variants link the NTC profile to intermediate-state formation and reveal a trade-off between static noise margins. These results establish vertical stacking as a route to single-semiconductor transfer-function engineering for ternary logic.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Assisted Synthesis of MXene-Grafted Coconut Husk Activated Carbon for Enhanced Adsorption of Carbamazepine: Batch Study and Optimization
articles.abstract: The presence of multiple pharmaceuticals in the water bodies as waste causes several hazardous environmental effects for both aquatic and terrestrial animals. The present study investigates the potential of novel MXene nanosheet grafted coconut husk-derived activated carbon (AcC/MXene) on the uptake of a pharmaceutical, i.e., carbamazepine, from the experimental solutions. Mxene nanosheet was synthesized from the MAX phase. Coconut husk was pyrolysed at a higher temperature and in an inert atmosphere to synthesise activated carbon, and Mxene nano-sheet was grafted on the activated carbon using ultrasonication and hydrothermal reaction. The highest adsorption capacity of 427.47 mg.g− 1 of the nanocomposite was calculated from the batch adsorption study. The detailed investigation of the physicochemical characteristics of the nanocomposite displayed micropores, a high surface area, with several functional groups responsible for the high uptake of the adsorbate molecule from the experimental solutions. The adsorption process was optimized using response surface methodology (RSM), in which 99.2515% of carbamazepine removal by the AcC/MXene nanocomposite was estimated in optimized conditions. Furthermore, the kinetic analysis and the isotherm analysis of the adsorption process were performed. The thermodynamic analysis revealed that the adsorption process was spontaneous at a negative ΔG value, and the adsorption process was endothermic, as concluded from the positive ΔH value of 59.47836 kJ. mol− 1. In the 7th cycle of the reusability study, 51.018% of the carbamazepine removed from the experimental solutions demonstrated the economic applications in wastewater treatment.

articles.title: Computational fracture modelling of polymer-bonded explosives and solid propellants: A critical review of local and nonlocal continuum formulations and discrete particle approaches
articles.abstract: Fracture behaviour is a critical determinant of the safety, reliability and service life of polymer-bonded explosives (PBXs) and solid propellants. Both are highly filled polymer composites whose damage evolution is governed by heterogeneous particle-binder architectures, rate- and temperature-dependent binders, interfacial debonding, matrix failure and particle or crystal fracture. A broad range of computational methods has been developed to describe crack initiation, propagation, coalescence and fragmentation, but suitability varies with the dominant mechanism, length scale and intended prediction. This paper reviews five approaches: the extended finite element method (XFEM), cohesive zone modelling (CZM), phase-field fracture modelling (PFM), peridynamics (PD) and the discrete element method (DEM). For each, the theoretical foundation, crack representation, numerical implementation, parameter requirements and applications to PBXs and solid propellants are examined, with emphasis on particle-binder debonding, constituent fracture, interacting crack networks, fragmentation and post-failure contact. The comparison indicates that XFEM enables the non-mesh-conforming representation of one or a few discrete sharp cracks; CZM represents progressive separation along predefined or explicitly resolved interfaces; PFM captures distributed nucleation and complex crack topology; PD accommodates dynamic fracture and fragmentation through a nonlocal continuum formulation; and DEM resolves contact-network evolution and particle rearrangement. These capabilities are conditional on compatible constitutive laws, identifiable and appropriately calibrated parameters, verified numerical implementation and solution, and validation against independent local as well as global experimental observables. Prospective hybrid formulations and machine-learning-assisted strategies are also discussed, together with the requirements for conservative coupling, uncertainty quantification and thermo-mechanical-chemical validation. The review provides a comparative basis for selecting and developing fracture models for the safety and structural-integrity assessment of PBXs and solid propellants.

articles.title: Physicists trap and tame single particle of antimatter for months
articles.abstract: For the first time, Northwestern University physicists have coaxed a single positron—the antimatter counterpart of an electron—into an exquisitely controlled quantum state.

articles.title: Steering electrons with extreme ultraviolet light—team achieves quantum coherent control
articles.abstract: Light is one of the most powerful tools scientists have for probing matter. By interacting with electrons, light reveals how atoms, molecules and materials are structured and how they evolve in time. Highly energetic ultraviolet and X-ray photons are particularly attractive because they can access electrons located close to atomic nuclei, where each chemical element carries its own distinctive electronic fingerprint.

articles.title: Zeeman Quantum Geometry of the Layer Pseudo-spin
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional layers coupled by position-dependent interlayer tunnelling host a layer pseudo-spin whose polarization is a controllable internal degree of freedom. We introduce the quantum geometry of this layer pseudo-spin: a mixed tensor formed from the interband Berry connection and the layer matrix element, which governs the response to an oscillating in-plane electric field. Because the layer pseudo-spin is an Ising-type scalar invariant under threefold rotation, its selection rules differ from those of a pseudovector spin. In a minimal two-band model, the layer-pseudo-spin quantum metric and Zeeman--Berry curvature are nonzero, while their zone integrals vanish. An in-plane drive therefore leaves the spatially averaged polarization unchanged at linear order but imprints a moiré-periodic intracell pattern, directly imageable by layer-resolved tunnelling. For twisted MoTe₂ bilayer, we quantify the local dipole modulation and identify the rectified, helicity-odd, and third-harmonic channels through which a net response appears at higher order.

articles.title: Achieving ultrahigh-temperature superfluidity in atomic Fermi gases by suppressing pairing fluctuations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving room-temperature superconductivity has been a long-sought goal of both the physics community and the industry. The superfluid transition temperature T_c of a Fermi system initially increases with increasing pairing strength between fermions following the mean-field prediction of the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory, and is then suppressed by pairing fluctuations as the strength increases further, which prevents T_c from becoming high. Here we propose a mechanism for suppressing pairing fluctuations using the synergy between population imbalance and momentum space confinement in lattice systems, enabling an ultrahigh T_c at moderately strong attraction. We show that in a three-dimensional optical lattice, strong Pauli exclusion between paired and excess majority fermions pushes up the pair excitation energy and suppresses finite-momentum pairing fluctuations. The mechanism is general to any lattice with a finite Brillouin zone; the optimal imbalance is modest (płesssim 0.1), keeping the Zeeman field small and avoiding orbital complications. The gapped pair dispersion at moderate imbalance exponentially suppresses thermal condensate depletion, providing a testable signature. The gapped dispersion, enhanced condensate fraction, and pseudogap reduction are all accessible in present-day experiments. This work opens new avenues toward room-temperature superconductivity.

articles.title: Field Theory of the Gutzwiller Projection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gutzwiller projection produces a well-known ansatz for spin-liquid and quantum Hall ground-state wavefunctions that is amenable to numerical simulation, with the Laughlin wavefunction being the most celebrated example. A long-standing issue is the precise relation between the Gutzwiller projection and the closely related parton gauge theory. Here, we clarify this issue by providing a field-theoretic description of the Gutzwiller projection. In a path integral description, the universal physics of the projected state is described in terms of a gauge field supported on a temporal slab of vanishing width ϵ i̊ghtarrow 0 coupled to the bulk matter fields. We analytically derive the universal physics of various Gutzwiller projected states. Our construction is also applicable to discrete symmetries, and we use it to analyze various projected SPT states. Among our results, we show that the Gutzwiller projection is not a good ansatz for the long-distance properties of U(1) Dirac spin liquids, spinon Fermi surface spin liquids or composite Fermi liquids, and that the Gutzwiller projection of a quantum spin Hall state has only quasi-long range order. In contrast, in examples where the gauge field is gapped, including Laughlin states, Z₂ spin liquids and Luttinger liquids, we show that the slab gauge theory from Gutzwiller projection reproduces the correct universal physics of the full parton gauge theory. We also present a generalization of our field theory that describes G-intertwining defects, with application to self-duality defects of recent theoretical interest.
authors: Abhijat Sarma, Cenke Xu, Chong Wang

articles.title: Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show that hidden order in doped spin chains can be directly probed through dynamical two-point response functions measurable by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and neutron scattering. Focusing on a minimal model, we numerically identify clear spectral fingerprints of both the hidden-order phase, its associated hidden quantum critical point as well as a specific group of gapless SPT phases. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.
authors: Reja H. Wilke, Henning Schlömer, Sebastian Paeckel, Annabelle Bohrdt, Fabian Grusdt

articles.title: Stacking-Induced Tuning of a Flat-Band Surface State in NbIrTe4
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ternary layered transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) offer high tunability and access to correlated and topological states. However, like the broader family of layered TMDCs, their properties are sensitive to stacking order and interlayer coupling. Here, we investigate the electronic structure and surface states of NbIrTe₄, a candidate Weyl semimetal in bulk, and predicted to be a quantum spin Hall insulator in monolayer form. Using scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM), angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), and density-functional theory (DFT), we attribute the strong resonance in tunnelling spectroscopy located approximately 8 meV below the Fermi level to a surface-derived flat band which shows sensitivity to the local stacking order at the surface. In regions where the top layer is laterally shifted, tunnelling spectroscopy instead shows a gap-like feature with intensity near the Fermi level shifted in energy. Combining DFT and quasiparticle interference (QPI) measurements, we find this dramatic change in the spectroscopy in the vicinity of the quasi-1D flat-band surface state becomes dispersive due to a change in the spatial distribution of the density of states in the top two layers. These findings establish NbIrTe₄ as a platform where surface band dispersion can be effectively tuned through local structural manipulation.
authors: Jiabin Yu, Mohamed Oudah, Giang Nguyen, Hsianghsi Kung, V. King, Rysa Greenwood, Adrian F. Rumson, Jisun Kim, Matteo Michiardi, Giorgio Levy, Andrea Damascelli, E. R. Johnson, Meigan Aronson, Lukas Muechler, Sarah A. Burke

articles.title: Diffusive Description of Superconducting Single-Photon Detectors Using Quantum Mechanics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The methodology of non-Hermitian quantum mechanics is employed to parameterize the dynamics of coupled classical diffusion equations describing low- and high-energy quasiparticles in superconducting single-photon detectors in one to three spatial dimensions.

articles.title: Symmetry Enriched Criticality from Kennedy Tasaki Self-Duality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between topology and quantum criticality has established symmetry enriched criticality as a new paradigm beyond conventional frameworks in condensed matter and statistical physics. However, the conditions under which such criticality emerges remain poorly understood. In this work, we show that a broad class of symmetry enriched critical points separating symmetry protected topological (SPT) and spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) phases is governed by Kennedy Tasaki (KT) self duality. At these criticalities, the KT transformation that interchanges the SPT and SSB phases acts as a self-dual noninvertible symmetry, endowing the critical points with nontrivial topological characteristics. We numerically demonstrate this mechanism in Zₙ × Zₙ cluster qudit chains and further argue that it naturally extends to higher dimensions, providing a duality based criterion for identifying symmetry-enriched criticality across dimensions.
authors: Mingyuan Chen, Sheng Yang, Xue-Jia Yu

articles.title: Andreev Scattering Driven Surface Photogalvanic Effect
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The surface photogalvanic effect is a powerful tool for generating macroscopic direct currents in centrosymmetric film structures via asymmetric scattering of carriers at film boundaries. Here, we uncover a fundamentally distinct regime of photoinduced transport in normal metal-superconductor heterostructures, in which the macroscopic photocurrent is governed by Andreev scattering at the interface rather than by classical scattering. We demonstrate that the interplay between asymmetric surface scattering and Andreev retroreflection yields a giant, strongly frequency-dependent anomalous photocurrent. Strikingly, the electron-hole conversion at the normal-superconducting interface dictates a macroscopic sign reversal of the photogalvanic current across the superconducting transition, and induces non-analytic spectral kinks exactly at the pairing gap frequency. Our results establish the Andreev reflection-driven surface photogalvanic effect as a platform for optical control of superconducting correlations and suggest a direct, non-invasive spectroscopic probe for gap dynamics in hybrid quantum devices.
authors: V. M. Kovalev, I. G. Savenko

articles.title: Non-uniform grids to accelerate electron-phonon coupling calculations for superconductivity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient and accurate evaluation of electron-phonon interactions is essential for predictive superconductivity calculations, but dense Brillouin zone sampling requirements pose a major computational bottleneck. To overcome this, we introduce an accelerated, highly scalable framework that combines a double delta truncation scheme with non-uniform Farey grids in both k and q space. The truncation strategy significantly reduces computational cost by restricting integration to states satisfying energy constraints near the Fermi level, while the Farey grids dynamically resolve sampling errors from localized scattering and stabilize convergence. Applied to elemental aluminium and several high-pressure hydrides, this combined methodology reduces computational cost by up to two orders of magnitude and yields electron-phonon coupling constants and superconducting critical temperatures Tc typically within about 5% of full-grid benchmarks. This approach overcomes sampling bottlenecks associated with dense uniform grids, making accurate, low-cost predictions of superconductivity in complex quantum materials feasible.
authors: Kang Wang, Siyu Chen, Sun-Woo Kim, Kieran Bozier, Chris Pickard, Bartomeu Monserrat

articles.title: Superconducting weak links at substrate steps in bilayer nickelate films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ambient-pressure superconductivity above 40 K has been realized in bilayer nickelate thin films on SrLaAlO₄ (001), yet resistive measurements often exhibit incomplete zero-resistance states and/or two-step superconducting transitions of unresolved origin. We show that these features arise from superconducting weak links at substrate step-terrace structures. A direct correlation between the azimuthal-angle-dependent two-step transition and step-terrace orientation establishes this connection, further supported by atomic-scale visualization of structurally disrupted regions at step terraces. Modeling the films as pristine (weak-link) regions with higher (lower) transition temperature reproduces essential features of the two-step transition using both a simple model and finite-element simulations. Transport measurements further reveal a strong dependence of transition characteristics - and even the occurrence of superconductivity itself - on average terrace width. These results identify step-induced weak links as the microscopic origin of two-step transitions in bilayer nickelate films, providing a framework for understanding anisotropic and percolative transport, and a route to superconducting devices.
authors: Yidi Liu, Yaoju Tarn, Lopa Bhatt, Puhua Zhang, Joonseo Song, Berit H. Goodge, David A. Muller, Harold Y. Hwang, Yijun Yu

articles.title: Good-Γ Numbers: A Shell-Optimized Route to the Thermodynamic Limit in Quantum Monte Carlo Calculations of the High-Density Two-Dimensional Electron Gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-particle finite-size errors remain a central obstacle in quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations of periodic systems, conventionally reduced via twist averaging (TA). Here we introduce Good-Γ (GG) particle numbers as system sizes N at which the Γ-point Hartree--Fock (HF) energy of the high-density two-dimensional uniform electron gas (2D UEG) lies anomalously close to its thermodynamic-limit (TL) value. All results in this work concern the 2D UEG in its high-density Fermi-liquid regime, rₛ₌₁₋₋₄. We systematically investigate the kinetic- and exchange-energy errors, Δ KE(N) and Δ EX(N), that underlie this one-body finite-size-error cancellation across four densities and both spin polarizations. We then compare diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) energies extrapolated to the TL from GG-N sequences against twist-averaged extrapolations at the same densities and polarizations, finding agreement to within a fraction of a millihartree in every case, independent of whether a 1/N or an N⁻⁵/⁴ extrapolation form is used.
authors: S. Azadi, T. D. Kühne, A. Principi, M. S. Bahramy

articles.title: Luther-Emery liquid in one-dimensional attractive Fermi gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One-dimensional (1D) interacting Fermi gases underpin a rich variety of quantum liquids, ranging from the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov paired state to the Luther-Emery liquid (LEL). Notably, the LEL-characterized by gapless excitations in charge or spin degree of freedom and gapped excitations in the other-has long been theoretically predicted but has eluded definitive experimental observation to date. By exactly solving the attractive Yang-Gaudin model via the Bethe ansatz, we fully determine the low-energy excitation spectra for both spin and charge channels. For fully paired fermions, the spectrum features gapped spin excitation coexisting with gapless charge excitation. We further employ bosonization to derive analytical expressions for the dynamical structure factor (DSF) of the gapped spin excitation, which is a long-standing challenge in this study. In the trapped gas, we find that the spin Bragg spectroscopy peak occurs at a much higher frequency than the charge-mode peak, where the splitting frequency between these two peaks scales approximately linearly with the interaction strength. Crucially, the spin gap manifests as a sharp threshold in the spin DSF, below which spectral weight is completely absent, proving a direct and unambiguous spectroscopic fingerprint of the LEL. Our work establishes quasi-1D trapped attractive Fermi gases as a pristine experimental platform for the long-sought direct observation of the LEL.
authors: Hai-Ying Cui, Yi-Cong Yu, Aashish Kafle, Han Pu, Randall G. Hulet, Thierry Giamarchi, Xî-Wen Guan

articles.title: Moments of Random Permanents and Hafnians: A Replica Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the 2k-th moment of N× N matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for k>2, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first 1/N correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the 1/N term. At k=2 the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.
authors: Paolo Facchi, Angelo Mariano, Giorgio Parisi, Saverio Pascazio, Antonello Scardicchio

articles.title: Computing excited states of dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates by constrained gentlest ascent dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs), i.e., BECs with long-range dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), exhibit extraordinarily rich physics and serve as a versatile experimental platform for exploring exotic quantum states of matter. Within the mean-field framework, a dipolar BEC can be described by the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) model with a DDI term. Its stationary states consist of the ground state, which minimizes the GP energy functional under the normalization constraint, and excited states, which are higher-energy critical points that typically correspond to constrained saddle points. Excited states encode collective excitation modes and play a key role in the dynamical stability and quantum phase transitions of cold-atom systems. However, in contrast to the extensively studied ground state, they remain far less explored numerically, especially in dipolar systems. In this work, we develop a numerical method based on the constrained gentlest ascent dynamics (CGAD) that systematically computes excited states of dipolar BECs by stably targeting constrained saddle points with any prescribed Morse index. Specifically, a semi-implicit sine-pseudospectral discretization with an orthonormalization correction step is adopted, and the nonlocal DDI terms are evaluated efficiently and accurately via the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT). The resulting scheme is applied to one-, two-, and three-dimensional dipolar BECs, enabling a detailed numerical investigation of their excited states. Remarkably, our simulations reveal that excited states can persist even in regimes where the ground state of the condensate becomes mean-field unstable. This work provides a computational framework for studying excited states in dipolar quantum gases and offers insights for future theoretical and experimental investigations.
authors: Fu Zheng, Wei Liu, Xu Qian

articles.title: Thermodynamic Stability of Classical mathbb Z₂ Lattice Gauge Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-temperature phases are traditionally studied through spontaneous symmetry breaking, but symmetry-breaking fields can remove their distinction, as in the Ising model. This motivates the search for stable nontrivial thermal phases without symmetry protection. For classical mathbb Z₂ lattice gauge models with spins on m-dimensional cells in a fixed spatial dimension d, we prove joint analyticity of the thermodynamic free-energy density in temperature and perturbation strength at sufficiently low positive temperatures under sufficiently weak local perturbations, whenever 1łe młe d-2. Perturbations need not preserve internal or gauge symmetries and may include noncommuting quantum interactions. A separate high-temperature expansion yields an analytic region reaching infinite temperature at any fixed finite perturbation strength. These results establish thermodynamic stability and support the conjecture that low- and high-temperature regimes remain separated by a thermal transition without symmetry protection.
authors: Shunsuke Sengoku, Weiguang Cao, Haruki Watanabe

articles.title: Adiabatic confinement and number-theoretic spectra of massless Dirac fermions in twisted trilayer graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrons in graphene move like massless relativistic particles, making them exceptionally mobile but difficult to trap because Klein tunnelling permits unimpeded passage through electrostatic barriers. This challenge extends to atomic collapse and hadron confinement. Twisted trilayers form Bernal and rhombohedral domains joined by smooth boundaries, bringing their carriers into contact. Here we show that a new mechanism, distinct from established approaches, confines massless fermions in equilateral triangular Bernal domains without mass barriers, bulk gaps or physical edges. Simulations and analytical modeling reveal that massless carriers have no adiabatic continuation into rhombohedral domains, while escape through nonadiabatic coupling to massive carriers is exponentially suppressed by smooth stacking variation. Perfect reflection in the adiabatic limit turns Bernal domains into quantum cavities in a gapless, edgeless metal. Striking density-of-states oscillations encode Eisenstein-integer arithmetic, linking energies and degeneracies to norms and prime factorizations. These findings bring relativistic confinement and number theory into experimentally accessible electronic spectra.
authors: Kunihiro Yananose, Changwon Park, Young-Woo Son

articles.title: Field theories and critical excitations at anyon condensation transitions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anyon condensation transitions remain challenging to characterize especially when the condensing anyons are non-abelian. We develop two complementary approaches for extracting information about the transition from the categorical data of the parent topological order and the condensate. The first adapts a Ginzburg-Landau procedure developed for 1+1D transitions in the SymTFT setting to 2+1D anyon condensation transitions. The construction applies when the anyons participating in the condensate have integer quantum dimensions. The second gives a criterion for identifying which point and loop excitations become critical at a continuous transition. The key step is to determine which anyon loops remain condensed throughout. All other loops become critical, while a point excitation becomes critical if it braids trivially with every condensed loop. We illustrate both proposals in several abelian and non-abelian examples.

articles.title: Saturating T² resistivity in iron-based superconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many correlated metals exhibit a crossover from low-temperature h̊o propto T² behavior to a slower increase of the resistivity at elevated temperatures. Distinguishing phonon scattering from electron--electron correlations as the origin of this crossover is experimentally challenging. We introduce a simple phenomenological framework that isolates the contribution responsible for the high-temperature saturating tendency. This approach reveals a clear contrast between systems well known for the predominance of electron--phonon scattering and several iron-based superconductors. For the latter, the conductivity can be expressed as the sum of a Fermi-liquid-like term (propto 1/T²) and a temperature-independent component, which together describe h̊o(T) up to sim 250 K in LiFeAs, KFe₂As₂, and KCaFe₄As₄. In FeSe, the same approach identifies a similar regime above the nematic transition, with a pronounced change toward nearly linear-in-T resistivity below it. We discuss these findings in the broader context of coherence and electronic correlations in Hund's metals.
authors: M. Lourdes Amigó, Jorge I. Facio

articles.title: Proliferation Transitions for Quantum Doubles of Groups
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proliferation transitions are phase transitions between a 2+1d topological order T and another T/A, obtained by condensing anyons in an algebra Asubset T. We consider such transitions in quantum doubles of groups, T=D(G, ømega), for finite groups G possibly with three-cocycle ømega, for which condensable algebras are fully classified. Given a condensable algebra A, we represent T in terms of a Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), that is tailored to the A proliferation transition. The SymTFT bulk is constructed from the Müger center of the subcategory generated by the algebra, i.e. the category of transparent lines, which can be bosons or fermions. Properties of the transition can then be inferred directly from the algebra classification data. For gauged Landau-Ginzburg (LG*) type transitions, we show that they do not only depend on the anyons in A through their field content, but the cubic interactions are fixed in terms of the multiplication structure of A. Applied to twin algebras, which have the same anyon content but different multiplication structures, we show that twins result in distinct proliferation transitions.

articles.title: Steady-state cooperative emission of interlayer excitons in atomically thin light-emitting diodes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an ensemble of emitters is confined within an optical wavelength, its radiation can become correlated, leading to cooperative emission. In two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) electron-hole bilayers, strong light-matter coupling enables the formation of interlayer excitons (IXs), long-lived dipolar excitations that provide an ideal setting for emergent collective phenomena. Here, we engineer an atomically thin light-emitting diode (LED) that generates electroluminescence (EL) from electrically injected IXs that are confined near the sample edges by an edge-enhanced fringing electric field. By measuring Hanbury-Brown-Twiss photon-photon correlations, we find pronounced signatures of collective decay in the form of large photon bunching followed by finite delay antibunching and bunching revivals. These emitter correlation signatures disappear when free charge carriers are doped to form a degenerate Fermi sea but are enhanced by the introduction of localized electrons. The results are consistent with a many-body quantum master equation that models the steady-state superradiant photon statistics of incoherently injected IXs. Our work establishes steady-state cooperative emission in a 2D TMD LED as a platform for studying strong light-matter interactions in electrically driven, non-equilibrium phases of Bose-Fermi mixtures.
authors: Andrés M. Mier Valdivia, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Grace H. Chen, Nadine Leisgang, Andrew Y. Joe, Stefan Ostermann, Deepankur Thureja, Yongxin Zeng, Dapeng Ding, Daniel Rhodes, Bumho Kim, Song Liu, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, James C. Hone, Susanne F. Yelin, Hongkun Park, Mikhail D. Lukin, Philip Kim

articles.title: Orbital-angular-momentum control of localized Floquet states and photocurrents in Weyl semimetals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structured light provides a route to controlling quantum materials not only through its polarization, but also through its spatial profile and orbital angular momentum (OAM). We develop real space theories of a Weyl semimetal driven by a vortex beam and show that optical OAM generates highly localized Floquet vortex states with pronounced circulating photocurrents. Exploiting cylindrical symmetry, we derive a Bogoliubov-de Gennes-like radial equation that resolves the states by angular momentum and reveals their evolution between the light-dressed Weyl cones. For Laguerre-Gaussian beams, the spatially varying drive produces strong hybridization between localized vortex states and bulk states. We complement this continuum description with a Wilson-lattice formulation that retains the full two-dimensional spatial structure and enables direct calculation of local photocurrents. Both approaches consistently identify OAM-induced vortex states localized around the beam axis. The lattice calculation further shows that these states support substantially stronger circulating current densities than the more extended surface states, with the largest current densities associated with the most strongly localized, low-angular-momentum vortex modes. Our results establish optical OAM as a tunable control parameter for creating and manipulating localized current-carrying states in Weyl systems and provide a real-space framework for studying photocurrents generated by spatially structured light.
authors: Kyle S. Netherwood, Juan I. Aranzadi, Nils Jacobsen, Michael A. Sentef, Sang Soon Oh

articles.title: Characterizing supersolid phase transitions in trapped quantum gases with tilted dipoles at finite temperature
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by a recent experimental work [hrefhttps://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20327arXiv:2608.20327], we theoretically investigate the nature of phase transitions in a trapped dipolar quantum gas upon tuning the contact interaction strength and dipole orientation. Using extended Gross-Pitaevskii simulations including thermal and quantum effects, we map the phase diagram comprising unmodulated superfluids, triangular droplet arrays, and stripe states. We further characterize the order of the transitions separating them through imaginary-time hysteresis analysis. The unmodulated-to-modulated transition evolves from discontinuous to continuous with increasing dipole tilt before becoming discontinuous again at large tilts. The degree of continuity is further affected by particle number, temperature, and confinement. While continuous behavior generally correlates with the emergence of stripe states, this correspondence is not systematic, and finite-size effects also influence the continuity of the transition. The triangular-to-stripe transition is found to be discontinuous at small contact interaction strengths and becomes increasingly continuous upon approaching the unmodulated-to-modulated phase boundary. Our results reveal a tunable transition order in finite dipolar quantum gases and provide guidance for its experimental investigation.
authors: Julian Kusch, Lauriane Chomaz, Wyatt Kirkby

articles.title: Nambu-Goldstone Bosons and Quantum Fisher Information
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantum Fisher matrix and geometric tensor are powerful tools for quantifying the nature of quantum systems. Unfortunately, the formalism needed to compute these quantities is opaque and has limited the development of physical intuition for their behavior, even in the ground state. For quantum systems with continuous symmetries, we know the ground state can be understood in a model-independent and intuitive way from the correlation functions of conserved currents and charges. In this paper, we demonstrate an equivalence between the quantum Fisher matrix associated with the ground states of systems with continuous symmetries and the Nambu-Goldstone. bosons produced by broken generators. We will show that the information metric defined by the Fisher matrix is the same as the Zamolodchikov metric that defines the coset space of the system. Next we show that the Uhlmann curvature associated with multi-parameter estimation is the same as the charge density matrix that defines the difference between type-A and type-B Nambu-Goldstone bosons. We demonstrate these connections in several examples and discuss the generalization to finite temperature.

articles.title: Bilocal flows and universality with field-dependent regulators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many functional renormalization group flows employ a regulator that depends on the fields, as in proper-time and spectrally adjusted flows and in background-independent formulations of gauge theories and quantum gravity. Such a regulator generates additional terms in the flow, and their omission may spoil universality. We introduce bilocal flows, in which the effective action depends on the field and on the cutoff kernel as independent variables. The construction identifies the additional terms, and an exact sum rule shows that the first nontrivial coefficient of the anomalous dimension coincides with that of a fixed-regulator flow for every admissible regulator profile, so that universality is restored. For massless łambdaφ⁴ theory with a proper-time regulator, the reduced flow gives a profile-dependent anomalous dimension, while the completed flow gives the universal two-loop coefficient C_η=1/6 for every profile.

articles.title: Quantum Fluctuations and Wigner Dynamics of a Carbon Nanotube Oscillator Driven by an Atomic Force Microscope
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Suspended carbon nanotubes provide a useful platform for studying controlled nanomechanical motion in regimes where environmental fluctuations, memory effects, and quantum coherence can all influence the dynamics. We model the fundamental flexural mode of a carbon nanotube driven by an atomic force microscope as a harmonic quantum Brownian oscillator subject to a prescribed classical force and coupled linearly to a thermal environment. Starting from the generalized Langevin equation, we formulate the reduced dynamics directly in phase space, where the Wigner function evolves through a Gaussian propagator determined by dissipative linear transport, a deterministic force-induced displacement, and bath-induced fluctuations. For a Drude memory kernel, the retarded response is expressed through the three roots of a characteristic cubic equation. In the classical-noise limit, the three independent entries of the finite-time covariance matrix reduce to explicit finite sums over these response poles, eliminating numerical double-time covariance integration. We extend the construction to the full quantum fluctuation spectrum, obtaining a thermal frequency series representation that retains zero-point and low-temperature fluctuations. For an initial two-packet superposition, we examine interference attenuation and the integrated negative part of the Wigner function, which provides a phase space measure of nonclassicality. These results provide an explicit analytical framework for finite-memory quantum Brownian motion of bound oscillators and a tractable phase space description of driven carbon nanotube dynamics relevant to future quantum state preparation and quantum tomography experiments.

articles.title: Invariant pseudo-unitary matrix ensembles and local statistics and conductance fluctuations of the DMPK ensemble
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the DMPK ensemble, which models quantum transport in a disordered wire, and describe its limiting local statistics as the number of particles tends to infinity. In the metallic regime, as well as at crossover I, we obtain sine statistics in the bulk, Bessel statistics at the hard edge and Airy statistics at the soft edge. In the insulating regime, we prove localization around certain explicit deterministic positions with Gaussian fluctuations. This confirms and quantifies the predicted universal and localized behavior in the physics literature. At crossover II, we obtain explicit limiting kernels in the bulk and at both edges, which interpolate between these regimes. The hard edge kernel involves Legendre functions and, to the best of our knowledge, is new, while the bulk and soft edge kernels agree with those derived for the squared singular values of critically scaled products of independent Ginibre matrices. To explain these similarities, we construct a class of invariant pseudo-unitary matrices that is closed under taking products and use it to interpret the DMPK ensemble as the joint density of the spectral variables of a product of such random matrices. More generally, the latter takes the form of a polynomial ensemble of derivative type involving a second order differential operator compatible with the Legendre functions. Finally, we obtain uniform asymptotic expansions of the mean and variance of the conductance and prove that the DMPK ensemble admits universal conductance fluctuations, i.e. the variance of the conductance tends to 1/15 throughout the whole metallic regime. This again confirms the predictions in the physics literature.

articles.title: Stabilizer Rényi moments beyond entanglement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stabilizer Rényi moments depend on a choice of operator basis and need not be determined by entanglement spectra. In this paper, we study their spatial decay in critical quantum chains described by two-dimensional conformal field theories. We derive an exact entanglement baseline for reductions of pure stabilizer states and a symmetry selection rule for the charged contribution at fixed support. An exact Ising example shows that an on-site rotation changes the full decay exponent while preserving every subsystem entanglement spectrum. For growing Ising intervals at index two, we obtain an exact Pfaffian representation and compare the charged amplitude with a candidate conformal boundary calculation. The data support this prediction, but its identification with the lattice limit still requires endpoint matching and control of the order of limits.

articles.title: Dynamical Mean-Field Theory for Real Materials using Variational Quantum Compressed Time Evolution on a Quantum Computer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28231v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We design a hybrid quantum-classical computational workflow, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory, to investigate the electronic properties of CaCuO2, a parent structure of high-temperature cuprate superconductors. Our approach uses a quantum algorithm as an impurity solver that is based on variational quantum compressed time evolution to compute the time-dependent Greens function on an IBM Heron quantum device. Utilizing error mitigation techniques and a Lehmann representation fitting procedure, we extract the density of states from the signal in the accessible time regime. Despite the significant challenges rooted in the residual imprecision of currently accessible NISQ devices, we successfully resolve the characteristic features of the spectral function. However, we find that the required numerical accuracy for full DMFT self-consistency exceeds current hardware capabilities, indicating that practical real-material DMFT applications will necessitate post-NISQ hardware developments.
authors: Stefan Wolf, Johannes Selisko, Timo Eckstein, Ludwig Nützel, Maximilian Amsler, Christopher Wever, Georgy Samsonidze, Thomas Eckl, Michael J. Hartmann

articles.title: Efficient Ground-State Manifold Amplification for Rydberg Atom Arrays via Houdayer Cluster Updates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.28528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate a hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring ground-state manifolds of maximum independent set problems, in which quantum hardware supplies the initial solutions and an entirely classical post-processing algorithm expands them, increasing the solution diversity of quantum hardware measurements by up to several orders of magnitude. Quantum optimization devices, while capable of generating high-quality solutions, can suffer from fundamental sampling limitations. This is particularly problematic for applications that strongly depend on a large variety of uncorrelated optimal solutions. We apply the Houdayer cluster update algorithm to systematically expand quantum-generated solution sets through classical post-processing. We validate our approach on a test bed of 43 problem instances from QuEra's Aquila analog annealing device, achieving diversity amplification factors, defined as the increase in the number of distinct solutions at a given set size, of up to 11923x with a median of 24.3x across different problem scales and hardness parameters. Because exact ground-state degeneracies are known for these instances, the recovered fraction of the manifold can be measured rather than bounded: post-processing recovers a median of 21% of the ground-state manifold, and provably all of it for six instances. We also demonstrate that, in some cases, the classical post-processing can discover independent sets larger than those found by the quantum hardware, thus improving on solution quality and not just diversity. While the method is non-ergodic and cannot guarantee complete manifold coverage, it consistently discovers a larger number of high-quality, and in some cases strictly better, configurations than quantum sampling alone. This work demonstrates how simple classical post-processing can enhance the utility of quantum optimization results.
authors: Andrew J. Ochoa, Martin J. A. Schuetz, Helmut G. Katzgraber

articles.title: Plasmon modes in three-dimensional multifold semimetals. I. Triple-point semimetal, its quadratic cousin, and Hopf semimetal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study collective charge excitations in pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals within the random-phase approximation, considering both the linearised model with a flat-band and its quadratic-corrected counterpart. We analyse their density response, Drude weights, screening, plasmon dispersion and damping, particle-hole continua, and Friedel oscillations from the long-wavelength to the arbitrary-momentum regime. The quadratic correction renders the flat-band dispersive and endows it with a Fermi surface, thereby affecting the overall response. Comparisons with Weyl and Hopf semimetals reveal how bandstructure and quantum geometry jointly govern collective charge dynamics. While the Drude weights are determined by the Fermi surface and band-velocities, interband screening, plasmon dispersion, and Friedel oscillations reflect the quantum geometry of the eigenstates.

articles.title: Temporal entanglement transition in chaotic quantum many-body dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.03846v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Temporal entanglement (TE) of an influence matrix (IM) has been proposed as a measure of complexity of simulating dynamics of local observables in a many-body system. Foligno et al. [Phys. Rev. X 13, 041008 (2023)] recently argued that the TE in chaotic 1d quantum circuits obeys linear (volume-law) scaling with evolution time. To reconcile this apparent high complexity of IM with the rapid thermalization of local observables, here we study the relation between TE, non-Markovianity, and local temporal correlations for chaotic quantum baths. By exactly solving a random-unitary bath model, and bounding distillable entanglement between future and past degrees of freedom, we identify a regime where TE is extensive and reflects genuine non-Markovianity. This memory, however, is entirely contained in highly complex temporal correlations, and its effect on few-point temporal correlators is negligible. An IM coarse-graining procedure, reducing the allowed frequency of measurements of the probe system, results in a transition from volume- to subvolume- (area or logarithmic) law TE scaling. We demonstrate the generality of this TE transition in 1d circuits by analyzing the kicked Ising model analytically at dual-unitary points, as well as numerically away from them. This finding indicates that dynamics of local observables are fully captured by a subvolume-law IM. We provide evidence that the compact IM MPS obtained via standard compression algorithms accurately describes local~evolution.
authors: Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Michael Sonner, Qi Camm Huang, Wen Wei Ho, Alessio Lerose, Dmitry A. Abanin

articles.title: On the Limits of a Space-Time Description and the Physical Meaning of Phase Space in a Nonlocal Continuum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a previous paper we derived an uncertainty relation for nonlocal fields by showing that the physical localization width in nonlocal quantum field theory is broadened by the response kernel generated from the entire-function regulator. In this follow up we will reinterpret that result as just the position-sector limit of a more symmetric statement as we did not take into account the inherent nonlocality of momentum. We find and we prove under normalized, centered response kernels for both position and momentum the variance laws and derive the corresponding nonlocal phase-space uncertainty relation. The result still preserves the conclusions of the original paper all while strengthening the interpretation as nonlocal quantum field theory implies not merely a minimal measurable length, but a finite phase-space cell. We also explore experimental routes to test the theory.

articles.title: Shaping the spectra of second harmonic laser by spatial focusing
