Anatomical pathways are commonly treated as fixed contributions that operate similarly across brain states. Instead, the same hippocampal–entorhinal relay degrades cortical theta organisation during sleep yet supplies it during spatial navigation. Brain state changes the effective spatial scale at which cortical geometry is read out, so anatomy constrains cortical function only jointly with state.

articles.title: Flux-map-based optimal current reference generation for copper-loss minimization and fault-tolerant control of a six-phase electrically excited synchronous motor
articles.abstract: Electrically excited synchronous motors (EESMs) provide an additional degree of freedom through independent rotor-field current, allowing same torque production by multiple combinations of stator d–q, and rotor field currents. However, magnetic saturation complicates the selection of the optimal currents for minimum-copper-loss operation. This paper proposes a variable-field look-up-table (VF-LUT) current-reference generation strategy for six-phase EESM. The LUT is generated offline over the full torque–speed range by optimizing the stator d-q, and rotor field currents subject to torque, current, and voltage constraints based on an experimentally-obtained three-dimensional nonlinear d-q flux-linkage maps to minimize the combined stator and rotor copper losses. The proposed VF-LUT control is experimentally evaluated under healthy and single open phase fault (1OPF) conditions and compared with the conventional FOC and a similar control approach to VF-LUT with constant field current. Over a wide range of healthy operating points, the VF-LUT reduces the total copper loss by an average of 21.9 W relative to the CF-LUT and 8.57 W relative to FOC, with a maximum reduction of 27 W (37%) relative to FOC. 1OPF results further demonstrate continued operation with stable speed and torque regulation, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed VF-LUT control for copper-loss reduction and fault-tolerant six-phase EESM operation.

articles.title: Assessing Climate-Driven Ground Movement Effects on Buried Pipelines Using Efficient 2D and 3D Finite Element Modelling
articles.abstract: Buried pipelines are critical components of UK infrastructure, but they are increasingly exposed to climate-driven soil movement, often resulting in differential settlement. There is therefore a need for computationally efficient tools to support large-scale risk assessment of buried pipelines under changing ground conditions. This study investigated whether a two-dimensional (2D) modelling approach can reproduce the key soil–pipe interaction behaviour predicted by a calibrated three-dimensional (3D) model under varying soil moisture conditions. A parametric analysis was carried out in PLAXIS 3D, which served as the high-fidelity reference model for the soil–structure interaction. The 3D model was first calibrated against experimental data for a concrete pipe and then used in a parametric study in which the water content within an active zone above and around the pipe was varied between 26% and 32%. In parallel, a two-dimensional (2D) finite element model (FEM) was developed in Python and can produce results within seconds. Comparative analysis indicates that the simplified model reproduces the displacement trends and magnitudes obtained from PLAXIS 3D simulations while reducing the computational cost by two orders of magnitude, highlighting its potential for large-scale climate resilience assessment of buried pipeline networks.

articles.title: Using a modified Cavendish experiment to measure dynamics of unexpected effect thanks to modern technology
articles.abstract: We present the results of our measurements of the dynamics of an unexpected effect, which we have provisionally namedthe electromagnetic-gravity effect. These results are compared with those of the interaction of the Coulomb force. Thesemeasurements were performed using a modified Cavendish experiment controlled by computers. The results of thesemeasurements were then compared with each other, with Newton’s laws, with a numerical simulation and with the gravitationalhypothesis. Reference experiments using high-voltage electrostatic stimulation agree with Newton’s laws and numericalsimulations with acceptable accuracy. However, experiments involving the unexpected effect produced significantly differentresults. These results partially agree with the gravitational hypothesis and the numerical simulations based on it. The timing ofthe periodic stimulation differs significantly, by a quarter of a period; that is to say, the phase differs by 90 degrees from that ofthe reference experiments and the results of the numerical simulations. This difference is reproducible. So far, it has not beenpossible to explain this using known physical laws.

articles.title: Refined Gradient-Based Temperature Optimization for the Replica-Exchange Monte-Carlo Method
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.13542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The replica-exchange Monte-Carlo (RXMC) method is a powerful Markov-chain Monte-Carlo algorithm for sampling from multi-modal distributions, which are challenging for conventional methods. The sampling efficiency of the RXMC method depends highly on the selection of the temperatures, and finding optimal temperatures remains a challenge. In this study, we propose a refined online temperature selection method by extending the gradient-based optimization framework proposed previously. Building upon the existing temperature update approach, we introduce a reparameterization technique to strictly enforce physical constraints, such as the monotonic ordering of inverse temperatures, which were not explicitly addressed in the original formulation. The proposed method defines the variance of acceptance rates between adjacent replicas as a loss function, estimates its gradient using differential information from the sampling process, and optimizes the temperatures via gradient descent. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through experiments on benchmark spin systems, including the two-dimensional ferromagnetic Ising model, the two-dimensional ferromagnetic XY model, and the three-dimensional Edwards-Anderson model. Our results show that the method successfully achieves uniform acceptance rates and reduces round-trip times across the temperature space. Furthermore, our proposed method offers a significant advantage over recently proposed policy gradient method that require careful hyperparameter tuning, while simultaneously preventing the constraint violations that destabilize optimization.
authors: Tatsuya Miyata, Shunta Arai, Satoshi Takabe

articles.title: Relaxation Dynamics of Superconducting/Normal Interfaces in the Intermediate State of a type-I superconductor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.17333v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dynamics of phase boundaries, such as superconducting/normal (S/N) interfaces in type-I superconductors, are typically obscured in conventional magnetic measurements, which are strongly influenced by surface barriers and global flux processes. Here, we employ the complex ac magnetostrictive coefficient as a sensitive probe of the bulk dynamics of S/N interfaces in the intermediate state of lead. The ac magnetostrictive coefficient exhibits an unusual complex response, with a negative real component and a positive imaginary component. Frequency-dependent measurements show that the magnitude of the real component decreases monotonically with increasing frequency, whereas the imaginary component first increases, reaches a broad maximum, and then decreases. In contrast, ac susceptibility displays a conventional Debye-type magnetic relaxation with a different phase relation between its real and imaginary components. We propose that the magnetostrictive response arises from ac-field-driven relaxation and rearrangement of metastable S/N domain configurations toward states of lower free energy. These results reveal a distinct interfacial relaxation channel in the intermediate state and establish the complex ac magnetostrictive coefficient as a sensitive probe of nonequilibrium S/N interface dynamics.
authors: Mengju Yuan, Yugang Zhang, Ying Zhu, Jingchun Gao, Aifeng Wang, Mingquan He, Jun-Yi Ge, Yisheng Chai

articles.title: Data-Efficient Indentation Size Effect Mitigation in Steels Using Machine Learning and a Physics-Constrained Neural Network
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.27775v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Shallow nanoindentation, needed for thin layers, individual phases and small volumes, gives hardness inflated by the indentation size effect (ISE). The Nix-Gao correction reduces this inflation but requires deep indentations of the same material, often impossible in such samples. We present a data-efficient workflow, trained on a few reference materials, that predicts a high-load reference hardness from a single shallow indentation. Seven models were trained on 703 indentations (5-350 mN) on three steels (2.0-6.5 GPa): Ridge regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, two feed-forward networks, and two physics-constrained neural networks (PCNNs) that apply a bounded learned correction q as Hₐₚₚ/sqrt(1+q). Over five seeds, models were tested on an external steel not used for training and indented at different loads, in leave-one-steel-out folds, and on fused silica, an out-of-domain material where all models failed. Random Forest and XGBoost, the best on the development set, transferred worst over all loads (MAPE 10.2 and 8.5%), whereas Ridge regression, the PCNNs and one feed-forward network reached 3.7-4.8%; with three training steels, development-set accuracy thus did not indicate accuracy on an unseen steel. From only the external steel's 3-15 mN indentations, the smooth (non-tree) models estimated the reference within 0.03-0.19 GPa on average. The PCNNs matched the linear baseline within the training hardness range and were the most accurate for a held-out steel softer than the training steels, but failed for a harder one. The workflow uses no steel-specific inputs and can be retrained for other material classes.

articles.title: Diversity-Aware Active Learning Builds Materials Datasets for Current and Future Objectives
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.05104v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Materials science data collection can be expensive, making dataset reuse and long-term utility important for future discovery. In practice, data collection often prioritizes properties of current interest while other properties are excluded from the acquisition process. This can produce datasets that are well suited for current objectives but lose information needed for properties of future interest. Here, we present how to construct datasets that remain informative for both. We develop and evaluate acquisition frameworks that combine predictive disagreement with diversity in material features, predicted outcomes, or both. We test these approaches across four DFT datasets and an experimental thermoelectric dataset. Diversity inclusion in dataset construction can reduce present and future objectives trade-off by preserving a broader range of materials and property behavior during acquisition. Across all datasets, the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II with disagreements and feature diversity (NSGA-II Dis. + diversity) framework developed in this work provides the most robust balance between current and future objectives. It maintains prediction performance above random sampling for current objectives while mitigating bias on excluded properties and, in many cases, improving their performance beyond random sampling. This diversity-aware acquisition framework provides a practical route to building materials datasets with unbiased quality entries and mitigating cold-start limitations in subsequent modeling and discovery campaigns.
authors: Rafael Espinosa Castañeda, Ashley Dale, Hongchen Wang, Yonatan Kurniawan, Hao Wan, Runze Zhang, Adji Bousso Dieng, Kangming Li, Jason Hattrick-Simpers

articles.title: Algebraic Structure of Finite-Size Bethe Solutions in the Heisenberg Chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.05589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain is the canonical example of an integrable quantum many-body model. Despite its exact solvability, explicit finite-size solutions are typically only accessible via numerical evaluation of the Bethe ansatz equations. Here, we analyse the algebraic structure of the exact, symbolic ground states for chains up to twelve sites using the Bethe ansatz. We find that the algebraic degree of the ground state magnon phases and Bethe roots scale with respect to system size at a different rate to the ground-state energy and wavefunction coefficients. The ground-state Bethe roots and energy are found to become Galois unsolvable for ten or more sites, thus demonstrating the lack of a symbolic analytical solution in a quantum integrable model due to algebraic complexity.
authors: Oliver R. Bellwood, William J. Munro

articles.title: On the bottom-up construction of many-electron relativistic QED Hamiltonian
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.15040v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It was shown more than a decade ago [J. Chem. Phys. 139, 014108 (2013)] that a many-electron relativistic quantum electrodynamics (QED) Hamiltonian for high-precision electronic structure calculations can be constructed in a bottom-up fashion, by virtue of charge-conjugated contraction (CCC) of fermion operators when normal-ordering the starting unbounded relativistic Hamiltonian (second-quantized in terms of the electronic Dirac field) with respect to the filled negative-energy Dirac sea of electrons. It is shown here that the same relativistic QED Hamiltonian can also be obtained by equal average of the two relativistic Hamiltonians resulting from the normal-ordering of the starting unbounded relativistic Hamiltonians (second-quantized in terms of the electronic and positronic Dirac fields, respectively) with respect to the filled negative-energy Dirac seas of electrons and positrons, respectively, via the standard contraction of fermion operators. In essence, both procedures incorporate properly the fundamental charge-conjugation symmetry of relativistic quantum mechanics to ensure the symmetric treatment of the electronic and positronic degrees of freedom.

articles.title: A fast summation method for the DFT-D3 dispersion correction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.15103v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The DFT-D3 dispersion correction is routinely added to machine learning force fields (MLFFs) trained on dispersion-deficient functionals such as PBE. Its environment-dependent pair coefficients, however, break the atom-centered separability that fast summation methods require, forcing practitioners either to truncate D3 or to accept a substantial slowdown. We introduce FourierD3, a method that uses a functional low-rank decomposition to restore this separability and enable particle-mesh evaluation in O(Nłog N) time without a real-space cutoff on the dispersion sum.
authors: Victoria Valeeva, Cheuk Hin Ho, Mario Geiger, Franco Pellegrini, Gábor Csányi, Emine Kucukbenli, Christoph Ortner

articles.title: Smoothed truncated Coulomb potential for periodic Gaussian-basis Hartree--Fock exchange
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.00203v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Truncated Coulomb (TC) potentials reduce finite-size errors and accelerate thermodynamic-limit convergence in periodic Hartree--Fock (HF) calculations, but their use with Gaussian basis sets is complicated by the evaluation of electron repulsion integrals (ERIs), particularly for nonspherical truncation domains and all-electron calculations. We introduce the smoothed truncated Coulomb (sTC) potential as a systematically improvable approximation to a parent TC potential. A real-space Gaussian convolution smooths the sharp truncation boundary, and a single dimensionless parameter, η, controls the width of the smoothing window, which can be tightened to systematically approach the TC reference. The smoothing by sTC enables a dual-space algorithm for evaluating periodic Gaussian-basis ERIs that requires neither a large plane-wave basis nor new molecular integral kernels and is applicable to both pseudopotential and all-electron calculations, including the important Wigner--Seitz-cell truncation boundaries. Benchmarks spanning insulating, semiconducting, layered, metallic, and molecular-crystal systems show that sTC-based HF closely reproduces TC results in pseudopotential calculations and extends TC-quality calculations to all-electron settings. Across these systems, sTC substantially improves thermodynamic-limit convergence relative to the probe-charge Ewald method while remaining practical for all-electron calculations in which direct TC-based calculations are computationally challenging.
authors: Gengzhi Yang, Aamy Bakry, Hong-Zhou Ye

articles.title: Symmetry-Adapted Eigensolver from Real-Space Sampling of Tensor-Network-Bridged Quantum Circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.19219v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a symmetry-adapted eigensolver for strongly correlated systems that separates where the wave function is emphsampled from where it is emphdefined. The lattice is divided into equal blocks: parallel quantum circuits absorb the entanglement within each block, while a matrix product state (MPS) backbone bridges the blocks and restores global correlations. The resulting real-space amplitude φ(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗ) acts only as a sample generator---configurations are drawn from |φ(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗ)|² directly, block by block, without any Markov chain. The variational state itself is defined in a symmetry-adapted basis by two separate rules: the modulus of ψ(aₘ̊ ₛyₘₘ) is the square root of the total weight accumulated over the entire equivalence class, widetildep(aₘ̊ ₛyₘₘ)=sumₐₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗᵢₙg ₐₘ̊ ᵣₑₚᵣ|φ(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗ)|², whereas its phase is inherited from the single representative amplitude φ(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₚᵣ). The modulus rule is what makes the scheme both exact and cheap: the distributionwidetildep(aₘ̊ ₛyₘₘ) sampled in the symmetric basis is exactly the one induced by the mapping from the real-space distribution p(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗ), so every generated configuration is an unbiased sample of |ψ(aₘ̊ ₛyₘₘ)|²; the phase rule then fixes the only freedom that remains. Because amplitudes within a class are combined in probability rather than summed with symmetry characters, ψ is emphnot a group projection of the circuit-MPS state; the class-wide aggregation instead supplies long-range, symmetry-enforced entanglement that the MPS never has to carry itself.

articles.title: When Does Cheap Physics Help? Gated Multi-Fidelity Physics-Informed Networks with Provable Sample Savings and Conformal Guarantees
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.01176v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-fidelity (HF) simulations of parametric partial differential equations are expensive, whereas low-fidelity (LF) models such as coarse grids or simplified physics are cheap but biased. Multi-fidelity physics-informed neural networks combine the two, yet it remains unclear when cheap physics actually reduces the number of HF solves, and existing methods silently fail when the LF model is misleading and offer no guaranteed uncertainty. We answer the first question with a sharp sample-complexity bound: learning the HF field through its discrepancy from the LF model reduces the number of HF samples needed for accuracy ǎrepsilon by the factor κ²γ, where κ is the ratio of the complexity of the discrepancy to that of the HF field and γ is the effective-dimension exponent, and we confirm the predicted scaling with exact risk computations in a kernel model. Guided by the analysis, we propose GaMF-PINN, a gated multi-fidelity PINN that learns where to trust the LF model and falls back to physics-only learning where it does not, together with a function-level conformal procedure that returns uncertainty bands containing the entire HF solution with probability at least 1-α in finite samples. We release MFPDE-Bench, an open benchmark of paired LF/HF solvers for four parametric PDEs with coarse-grid and simplified-physics LF models. Across MFPDE-Bench, GaMF-PINN reaches the accuracy of a standard HF-PINN with up to 8x fewer HF solves, remains robust when the LF model is deliberately corrupted, and attains the nominal coverage where Bayesian PINNs and deep ensembles under-cover.
authors: laf Yunus Laitinen Imanov, Rana Irem Turhan, Isgandar Jafarli

articles.title: A Unified Physics-Informed Neural Network for Modeling Coupled Electro- and Elastodynamic Wave Propagation Using Three-Stage Loss Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.13811v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks present a novel approach in SciML that integrates physical laws in the form of partial differential equations directly into the NN through soft constraints in the loss function. This work studies the application of PINNs to solve a one dimensional coupled electro-elastodynamic system modeling linear piezoelectricity in stress-charge form, governed by elastodynamic and electrodynamic equations. Our simulation employs a feedforward architecture, mapping space-time coordinates to mechanical displacement and electric potential. Our PINN model achieved global relative L2 errors of 2.34 and 4.87 percent for displacement and electric potential respectively. The results validate PINNs as effective mesh free solvers for coupled time-dependent PDE systems, though challenges remain regarding error accumulation and stiffness in coupled eigenvalue systems.
authors: Suhas Suresh Bharadwaj, Reuben Thomas Thovelil

articles.title: Quantum matter is weakly entangled at low energies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.14143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct upper bounds on entanglement entropies of many-body quantum states that have fixed energy expectation values with respect to local Hamiltonians. Our focus is on entanglement entropies of subsystems that make up approximately half of the full system. The upper bound on the von Neumann entanglement entropy is half the sum of the thermal entropies of two fictitious systems at the same temperature as one another, with an additional area-law contribution in some systems. The effective temperature is chosen such that the sum of the thermal energies of the two fictitious systems matches the constraint on the energy of the state in the original problem; at subextensive energies, this temperature decreases with increasing system size. Our upper bounds on Rényi entanglement entropies take an analogous form. These inequalities show that, in systems that are frustration-free (FF) and whose zero-temperature subsystem thermal entropies scale with surface areas (rather than subsystem volumes), ground states are area-law entangled. For physical models of quantum matter, which have well-defined specific heat capacities (and are not necessarily FF), our bounds provide a way to convert this thermodynamic data into constraints on pure-state entanglement at both subextensive and extensive energies. We also show that our general upper bounds on half-system entanglement entropies are optimal, up to subleading corrections, in systems with reflection symmetry and above a subextensive energy threshold. A key application of our results is to constrain the entanglement of quantum states relevant to simulations of zero-temperature response functions, which have energies of order unity. We prove that, in wide varieties of FF systems in two dimensions and higher, the contributions of excitations to von Neumann entanglement entropy are subleading compared with the contribution from the ground state.
authors: Samuel J. Garratt, Dmitry A. Abanin

articles.title: Emergence of Open Chemical Reaction Network Thermodynamics within Closed Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.14848v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Under which conditions do the dynamics and thermodynamics of open chemical reaction networks (CRNs), grounded on the notion of idealized chemostats that exchange selected species, emerge from underlying closed CRNs? While open CRNs provide the standard framework to describe out-of-equilibrium chemical systems, real systems are finite and ultimately relax to equilibrium, leaving the status of this description conceptually unresolved. Here, we address this fundamental question. We show that open-CRN behavior arises as an asymptotic regime of closed CRNs when two physically minimal and transparent conditions are met: a time-scale separation, whereby fast reactions effectively act as exchange mechanisms, and an abundance separation, whereby a subset of species behaves as chemostats with diverging chemical capacity. In this regime, both the stochastic dynamics and the thermodynamic structure - including local detailed balance, entropy production, and free-energy balance - emerge to leading order from the underlying closed CRN. We further predict that this regime persists up to a characteristic time proportional to the scale of the abundance separation, thereby providing an experimentally accessible criterion for estimating how long a finite closed system behaves as an open CRN. Our results apply to arbitrary stoichiometries. They show that chemostats need not be introduced as external idealizations, but instead arise as emergent thermodynamic structures within closed systems, providing a unified and physically grounded foundation for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of CRNs.
authors: Benedikt Remlein, Massimiliano Esposito, Francesco Avanzini

articles.title: AutoREC: A reinforcement learning platform for equivalent circuit model generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.27266v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper introduces AutoREC, an open-source Python platform for developing, training and evaluating reinforcement learning (RL) agents that automatically generate equivalent circuit models (ECMs) from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data. Although ECMs are widely used to interpret EIS measurements, their identification typically relies on manual trial-and-error, requiring domain expertise and limiting scalability, particularly in autonomous experimental pipelines such as self-driving laboratories. In AutoREC, ECM generation is formulated as a Markov decision process in which an RL agent sequentially modifies a circuit topology based on the current state, available actions and feedback from the resulting model. The platform supports an end-to-end workflow encompassing EIS preprocessing with selectable impedance representations, agent setup and training, ECM generation for new measurements and visualization-based evaluation and analysis of agent decision-making. AutoREC implements a configurable Double Deep Q-Network agent with prioritized experience replay and a dedicated deadloop mitigation strategy for navigating the complex circuit-generation action space efficiently. To demonstrate the platform, we trained a representative agent on 1350 synthetic spectra from five reference circuit families, evaluated it on 150 held-out synthetic spectra and applied it to 32 previously unseen experimental spectra from battery, corrosion, oxygen evolution reaction and CO2 reduction systems. These case studies illustrate the end-to-end capabilities of AutoREC while revealing challenges associated with experimental complexity and limited training-data coverage. The demonstrated agent serves as a reference implementation; AutoREC provides an extensible foundation through which users can develop and evaluate agents tailored to their specific electrochemical systems and research objectives.
authors: Ali Jaberi (Clean Energy Innovation Research Centre, National Research Council Canada, Mississauga, ON, Canada), Yonatan Kurniawan (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, Canada), Robert Black (Clean Energy Innovation Research Centre, National Research Council Canada, Mississauga, ON, Canada), Shayan Mousavi M. (Clean Energy Innovation Research Centre, National Research Council Canada, Mississauga, ON, Canada), Kabir Verma (Cheriton School of Computer Science, University of Waterloo, Waterloo, ON, Canada), Zoya Sadighi (Clean Energy Innovation Research Centre, National Research Council Canada, Mississauga, ON, Canada), Santiago Miret (Lila Sciences, San Francisco, CA, USA), Jason Hattrick-Simpers (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, Canada)

articles.title: AI estimation of partition functions with the PULSE method for the thermodynamic properties of disordered compounds
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.28594v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Predicting the thermodynamic properties of chemically disordered materials is constrained by the combinatorial growth of possible atomic configurations, which makes conventional sampling approaches computationally costly. In this work, we extend the PULSE (Partition function Unsupervised Learning Sampling and Evaluation) approach that enables the estimation of observable-dependent partition functions, thereby extending its applicability from local atomic quantities to general thermodynamic observables. This is based on a generative machine-learning approach in which a single model both generates statistically representative atomic configurations and provides explicit partition function estimates. Our primary goal is to assess it on the two-dimensional Ising model, an exactly solvable benchmark system sharing the same statistical-mechanical formulation as chemically disordered binary materials, and compare its performance against exact brute-force calculations as well as Wolff and Wang-Landau Monte Carlo algorithms. PULSE reproduces the relevant partition functions accurately using a limited number of configurations, at a sampling cost that does not grow with system size. These key results demonstrate the relevance of our method to enable the study of disordered materials at scales that are difficult to achieve using conventional approaches, and with limited computational effort.
authors: Baptiste Bernard, Luca Messina, Eiji Kawasaki, Emeric Bourasseau

articles.title: Learning Effective Bulk Fields from Fermionic Spectra: Application to an Extended Power-Law Liquid Model for Cuprate Strange Metals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.02861v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a Neural-ODE framework to infer effective bulk metric functions and the charge-weighted gauge potential from boundary fermionic spectra within a static, planar black-hole ansatz. Controlled benchmarks recover the known bulk profiles of the Einstein--Maxwell and Gubser--Rocha models. We then use normalized interaction self-energy targets generated from an extended power-law liquid model with parameters calibrated by angle-resolved photoemission measurements to test the proposed geometric explanation of cuprate strange-metal spectra in a semi-holographic setting. For this application, we use a massless probe in backgrounds with conformal-to-AdS₂×R² asymptotics and derive a spectral extraction formula from the conserved radial Dirac flux. We identify coordinate/Weyl redundancy and a degeneracy in the scaled Hawking temperature of the normalized inverse problem. The conformal factor remains undetermined, so bulk entropy and the associated contribution to electronic specific heat require independent input. Low-temperature targets are fitted accurately across the studied doping range. In the high-temperature test, however, the present ansatz and optimization search have not yielded a refined geometry that accurately reproduces the thermal spectral shape while preserving frequency symmetry. These results may guide the further development of semi-holographic models for cuprates, and the framework may also find applications in other strongly correlated electron systems.
authors: Hong-Zhi Xiao, Zhan-Zhi He, Zhuo-Yu Xian, Shao-Feng Wu

articles.title: Microstructure-Conditioned Surrogate Models for Graded Multiscale Optimization of Mycelium Composites
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.13688v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Emerging sustainable materials increasingly rely on engineered hierarchy and microstructure to achieve control of their properties and mechanical behavior. Optimizing these materials with controllable microstructures requires efficient multiscale simulations. Data-driven surrogate models for the microscale can accelerate multiscale simulations, but require large amounts of data even for a fixed microstructure. When a range of microstructures is considered, as is the case in multiscale optimization, even more data is needed to train a surrogate. To overcome this challenge, we condition a hybrid physics-data surrogate on microstructural variables using a hypernetwork. This approach enables accurate predictions of multiscale mechanical behavior for a mycelium-woodchip composite material, even when trained on small datasets. The conditioned surrogate makes multiscale simulations of functionally graded structures tractable, and we validate it against a full FE² simulation. We optimize a graded multiscale disk, and reduce the peak stress by 43% compared to one with a random microstructure. Then, we go one step further, conditioning the network directly on manufacturing variables that can have a complex influence on the microstructure. This is a practical route to engineer the microscale for desired macroscale behavior. This contribution highlights the benefits of microarchitectured structures and demonstrates how conditioned surrogate models enable their multiscale optimization, which will accelerate the development and design of future sustainable materials and structures.
authors: J. Storm, I. B. C. M. Rocha, S. Schyck, K. Masania, F. P. van der Meer

articles.title: STORM: RDMA-based Monte Carlo Transport Scheme for Distributed-Memory Particle Simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.20639v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Monte Carlo particle transport enables high-fidelity astrophysical radiation and neutrino simulations - from core-collapse supernovae and neutron-star mergers to accretion flows - by handling multidimensional geometries, frequency dependence, and moving media without angular discretization. However, inter-rank communication limits scalability on unstructured meshes: standard two-sided MPI requires receivers to post receives and poll completions, creating per-iteration progress overhead that grows with the number of communication partners. Such problems have not demonstrated high scaling efficiency at O(10⁴⁾ cores. We present STORM (Scalable Transport via One-sided Remote Memory), an open-source library for Monte Carlo transport on general meshes, physics, and boundary conditions. STORM provides a lock-free, mesh-independent communication layer that replaces MPI's matched-send/receive semantics with Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) - one-sided operations that write directly into a remote rank's memory without involving its CPU. Each rank pair shares a single-producer, single-consumer ring buffer; RDMA writes transfer particles while receivers remain passive. A two-sided MPI backend provides a portable fallback. In an adversarial uniform-emission benchmark, the RDMA backend sustains >97% weak-scaling and >88% strong-scaling efficiency up to 13,440~cores (112~cores per network adapter), with 1.14-1.27× speedups over the two-sided alternative. In a Hohlraum IMC benchmark at 4480 ranks, it is 1.41× faster because MPI progress overhead is reduced by 6.1×. By decoupling communication from physics models and mesh representations, STORM removes a barrier to scaling Monte Carlo transport in astrophysical multiphysics codes, enabling coupled radiation-hydrodynamics with energy- and angle-resolved photon or neutrino transport on dynamically evolving meshes at scale.
authors: Maor Mizrachi, Barak Raveh, Elad Steinberg

articles.title: Picosecond-resolved entanglement distribution over an urban free-space channel
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.21093v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Time-evolving entangled states describe quantum particles whose correlations evolve in time according to a well-defined dynamics. Such states can be generated in a variety of physical systems and are promising resources for several quantum technologies, ranging from quantum clock synchronization to quantum communication. However, their full potential is currently limited by the fact that the entanglement dynamics often occur on timescales comparable to the achievable synchronization precision, especially in experiments aimed at distributing entanglement through noisy urban channels. In this context, accurate timing is not merely a technical detail, but a fundamental requirement for faithfully observing and exploiting the underlying quantum correlations. Here, we demonstrate the faithful distribution of a fast-evolving entangled state over a 270 m free-space channel connecting two buildings in the center of Rome. The developed system incorporates a synchronization device capable of achieving sub-50 ps timing accuracy between the two ends of the link while simultaneously supporting channel stabilization. Our results demonstrate that time-evolving entanglement can be reliably transmitted through a noisy urban free-space channel, representing an important benchmark toward long-distance free-space quantum communication and the future implementation of time-correlated entangled states in demanding scenarios such as satellite-based quantum networks.
authors: Alessandro Laneve, Fabrizio Cienzo, Santiago Gomez, Paolo Barigelli, Philip Menz, Mattia Beccaceci, Giuseppe Ronco, Giorgia Grossi, Ievgen Brytavskyi, Thomas Oberleitner, Markus Wiener, Christian Weidinger, Tobias M. Krieger, Ailton Garcia Jr., Saimon Filipe Covre da Silva, Michele B. Rota, Nicolò Spagnolo, Henning Weier, Fabio Sciarrino, Armando Rastelli, Rinaldo Trotta

articles.title: Propensity Straight-Through Gradients for Discrete Stochastic Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.25631v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the propensity straight-through (PST) estimator for gradient-based learning through exact simulations of continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs). These models describe discrete stochastic dynamics across physics, chemistry, and biology, but their categorical event choices prevent ordinary differentiation. PST preserves exact forward trajectories and differentiates, in the backward pass, the normalized reaction propensities the simulator already computes. The affine state update makes this rule exact for the one-step conditional-mean sensitivity. We derive the per-step discrepancy for one-step sensitivities composed along nonlinear trajectories in closed form, show that it vanishes for affine downstream dependence, and bound it quadratically in the stoichiometric jump size. Across reversible dimerization, a genetic oscillator, a 50-task repressilator suite, and experimental patch-clamp recordings, PST recovers parameters to within 0.06-1.7% and converges 2.4-3.0-fold faster than the Gumbel-Softmax straight-through estimator at matched computational cost. At deep-learning scale, PST trains all 203,796 parameters of a stochastic reaction network using exact discrete events from initialization. By differentiating an exact conditional mean, PST eliminates reaction-selection temperature tuning and provides a scalable route to learning through exact stochastic dynamics.
authors: Jose M. G. Vilar, Leonor Saiz

articles.title: Quantum probability can't be derived without assuming it first
articles.abstract: For nearly a century, physicists have relied on the Born rule to calculate the chances of different outcomes when they measure a quantum system. Yet despite decades of effort, nobody has managed to derive the rule from more basic mathematical principles without making assumptions about probability along the way.

articles.title: A quantum pathway to entropy-free energy transfer
articles.abstract: For scientists, breakthroughs often stem from unexpected turns. A research team led by Oscar Dahlsten, an associate professor in the Department of Physics at City University of Hong Kong (CityUHK), set out to prove a theoretical limitation, only to discover a quantum solution. The finding breaks traditional physical constraints and introduces a strategy for harvesting energy from fluctuating sources.

articles.title: Scientists redetermine a key strontium frequency with 50 times better precision for quantum technologies
articles.abstract: The Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS) has remeasured a key transition frequency of the strontium (Sr) atom for the first time in 88 years, since 1938, using a photonic grating chip. It has established a new absolute frequency value with a measurement uncertainty reduced by more than 50 times. By providing an accurate reference value for next-generation quantum technologies, this achievement is expected to contribute to the precise control and miniaturization of quantum devices, including atomic clocks and neutral-atom quantum computers. The work is published in the journal Metrologia.

articles.title: Universal electrical resistivity in iron-based high-temperature superconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity h̊o(T) in cuprate, iron-based, and nickelate superconductors represents one of unresolved problems in modern solid-state physics, because of the high absolute value of h̊o(T), which, in many cases, exceeds the Ioffe-Rigel criterion, and a large difference in the h̊o(T) shape for samples with different doping. Here I show that the nearest neighbors parallel resistivity model (arXiv: 2607.23484) can well describe the in-plane resistivity h̊oₐb(T) in iron-based superconductors (IBS) of type 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144 and 42214 in which the spin density wave phase or nematic order is suppressed by doping. The model is based on the postulate that h̊oₐb(T) is a sum of two parallel conduction channels, where one channel is described by the Bloch-Grüneisen equation and the other by the Arrhenius hopping equation. Consequently, the variety of h̊oₐb(T) in the IBS is explained as a variation of the Debye temperature Θ_D and the hopping activation energy Eₐ. The derived Debye temperatures were used to estimate the electron-phonon coupling constant łambdaₑ₋ₚₕin the studied IBS.

articles.title: Resonant suppression of the π-type Josephson component in a Kitaev-ladder junction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate Josephson transport through a finite normal segment connecting two Kitaev-ladder superconductors and show that discrete-level detuning controls the sign of the equilibrium Josephson coupling through a branch-selection mechanism. Away from resonance, detuning separates two competing low-energy branches, allowing inter-leg hybridization to clamp the 0-phase-favoring branch while leaving the π-favoring branch dispersive. The resulting negative first harmonic evolves from a branch-switching response at weak coupling into a smooth π-junction regime. At resonance the two clamping thresholds coincide, so the finite interval in which only one branch remains dispersive disappears. Once the inter-leg coupling exceeds the resonant clamping threshold, both low-energy branches become independent of the Josephson phase. The remaining finite-energy states then generate a 0-type Josephson coupling. At φ=π, the helicity decomposition yields an exact clamping identity for arbitrary finite normal-segment length. Within the controlled sweet-point finite-segment theory, serial propagation fixes the off-resonant fourth-order harmonic to be negative, whereas an isolated resonance leaves a positive residual harmonic within the resonant clamping regime. Numerical calculations demonstrate that the resonance-induced suppression persists away from the solvable phase choice. Thus normal-level resonance does not merely enhance Josephson transmission; it changes which low-energy branches contribute to the Josephson coupling.
authors: Cheng-Rong Xie, Hiroki Tsuchiura, Yukio Tanaka

articles.title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kagome lattice materials host a remarkably rich landscape of novel quantum phenomena, all arising from the intrinsic interplay of topology, correlation, and frustration. While previous studies have been mostly limited to bulk three-dimensional (3D) kagome crystals, the realization of a true two-dimensional (2D) kagome system has remained a long-standing goal, to unlock fundamentally new physics and engineering pathways inaccessible in 3D systems. In this work, we establish the first ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattices by leveraging a novel and versatile van der Waals (vdW) kagome family, A2T3X4 (A = K, Rb, Cs; T = Ni, Pd, Pt; X = S, Se). Our nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) directly characterizes the electronic structure of A2T3X4 down to the monolayer limit, notably revealing an isolated kagome-derived flat band just below the Fermi level. Via gate-engineering of 2D A2T3X4, the kagome flat band can be further tuned to the Fermi level, allowing direct access to the partially filled flat band physics and establishing a qualitatively new 2D flat band platform. Compared to existing moire-based artificial flat band systems, this vdW kagome-based intrinsic flat band system realizes more than 220 times higher flat band electron density, opening an entirely new density and energy regime for exploring 2D flat band physics. Harnessing this high-electron-density flat band in 2D vdW kagome system provides a clear pathway to scale emergent flat band phenomena - such as fractional quantum anomalous Hall states - to far higher temperatures than currently achievable, as long-envisioned in theory and further supported by our many-body calculations.
authors: Hyungkun Bong, Choongjae Won, Seongyong Lee, Soomin Oh, Phuong X. Nguyen, Raghav Chaturvedi, Sehyun Oh, Jiyong Han, Paul Malinowski, Chad Mowers, Jimin Kim, Sae Hee Ryu, Hyunjong Lee, Jinhyeok Choi, Sangsu Yer, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Craig M. Polley, Matthew D. Watson, Timur K. Kim, Heejun Yang, Jieun Lee, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan, Jae-Hoon Park, Gil Young Cho, Kyle M. Shen, Mingu Kang

articles.title: Maximum-Temperature Theorem for a Nanothermometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The steady-state temperature predicted for an ideal point heat source diverges in conventional heat-conduction theory, but no physical thermometer measures a point value. We derive a sharp, shape-independent upper bound on the quasi-steady temperature rise of a sensor with thermometric volume Vₛ, placed anywhere inside a region enclosed by an isothermal reference surface. The bound requires only the total heat power generated in the region dotQ, a lower bound on its thermal conductivity κₘ, and the value of Vₛ. It is otherwise independent of the heat-source distribution, domain shape, and source--sensor distance. For dotQ=50~pW, κₘ = 0.1~mathrmW,m⁻¹K⁻¹, and Vₛ₌₁₀⁻²²,m³, approximately the volume of a 60~nm-diameter sphere, the theorem permits a maximum temperature rise of approximately 2~mK above the reference level. The result applies directly to nanodiamonds, upconversion nanoparticles, fluorescent polymer particles, and core-shell quantum dots. It shows that neither source localization nor uncertain source-sensor separation can account for kelvin-scale readings under steady-state heat conduction.

articles.title: Quantum state tomography through multi-frequency Josephson effect
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Macroscopic quantum effects emerge when the coherent behavior of countless microscopic quantum states manifests collectively at a visible scale, as exemplified by the supercurrent carried by innumerable finite-momentum Cooper pairs. By rigorously analyzing the time evolution of superconducting nanodevices including finite-momentum superconductors and quantum-dot Josephson junctions, we analytically derive the ubiquitous macroscopic supercurrent that originates from quantum interference between distinct many-body eigenstates, which we term as the dynamic interference supercurrent. The dynamic interference supercurrent in a system of two Andreev spin qubits exhibits multi-frequency Josephson effect in the absence of external voltage and is governed by the response of the many-body eigenfunctions (ěrt rångle) to variations in the superconducting phase φ, determined by the φ-space Berry connection Cᵣᵣ'=łangle r|partial_φ|r'ångle. The macroscopic dynamic interference supercurrent, an inherent property of the superposition state itself, enables an advanced quantum entanglement measurement of the Andreev spin qubits. These findings open new avenues for investigating superconducting nanodevice properties from a wave-function level, with substantial implications for advancing quantum science and technology in solid-state superconducting devices, such as quantum computer, communication, memory, and sensor.
authors: Xian-Peng Zhang, Ting-Rui Hu, Zhen-Biao Yang, Rubén Seoane Souto, Yugui Yao

articles.title: Surface corrections and vortex energetics in the Thomas--Fermi limit of a self-bound unitary Fermi superfluid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a spin-balanced unitary Fermi superfluid bound by an attractive 1/r interaction within an extended Thomas--Fermi density functional. Its large-particle-number limit is the Lane--Emden polytrope of index 3/2. We prove the leading gradient correction to the ground-state energy and strong convergence of the density amplitude. A rescaled surface problem predicts the next energy correction and the leading integrated density error. Matching a vortex core to the polytropic bulk gives the energetic threshold of a singly quantized central vortex, including the constant beyond the leading logarithm. Linearizing the same surface problem predicts a local energetic threshold for collective surface excitations that, in the natural TF frequency units, decreases more slowly with particle number than the central-vortex threshold. Radial stationary, spherical Bogoliubov--Poisson, and axisymmetric real-time calculations test the predicted energy corrections and vortex matching, and resolve finite-size surface-mode minima whose approach to the continuum surface coefficient is followed to Nsimeq4×10⁶. For the reference gradient coefficient the vortex constant is c₁₌₋₀.535, and the surface Landau scale is 1.417,ømega_K(hbarₘ̊ ₑff²/2Rₘ̊ TF)¹/⁶propto N⁻¹/⁹; sector energies at Nsimeq4.6×10⁵, computed after the fit, agree with the extrapolated vortex threshold to 10⁻⁴. These results distinguish the accuracy of the Thomas--Fermi bulk from the gradient physics that controls the surface and vortex core, and separate vortex energetics from the open problem of nonlinear vortex entry.

articles.title: Spontaneous particle-hole symmetry breaking in a disordered two-site quantum breakdown model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spontaneous particle-hole symmetry breaking in a disordered two-site quantum breakdown model. The model is solvable in the limit of a large number of fermionic modes on each site. For a small ratio of the numbers of modes on the two sites, we derive the free energy analytically and find a finite-temperature symmetry-breaking transition. This transition changes from continuous to first order as the number of fermions produced in each conversion increases. Numerical results show that both types of transition persist beyond this regime, with an order-parameter exponent close to 1/2 for continuous transitions.

articles.title: Epitaxial Displacement-etched GaAsSb Quantum Dots Emitting at Telecom Wavelengths
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are essential components for integrated photonic and quantum information systems, yet current epitaxial growth techniques face significant limitations in complexity of growth, material selection, and density tunability. Here we report a displacement etch technique that enables controlled formation of GaAsSb QDs with emission at telecommunications wavelengths. Our approach uses arsenic molecular flux (As₂₎ to react with antimonide surfaces through thermodynamically favorable displacement reactions, creating three-dimensional quantum confined nanostructures without requiring strain-driven growth or complex droplet-based processes. Density functional theory shows the two competing As-for-Sb exchange pathways to be nearly equivalent in both reaction energy and activation barrier, which places morphological control in the subsequent adatom kinetics rather than in the surface reaction itself. A single process parameter, the As₂ exposure, sets the QD areal density across three orders of magnitude, from 10² to 10⁵ μ m⁻², covering both isolated emitters and dense gain media. Structural analysis reveals well-defined GaAsSb QDs with a mixed GaAs/GaSb composition and no extended defects. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence measurements confirm emission at 1550 nm (0.8 eV) within the telecommunications C-band, with characteristic QD-like temperature dependence. Because the QDs form on a lattice-matched GaSb surface in a single growth step, the technique offers a practical route to C-band emitters built into the GaSb/AlGaSb device family already used for mid-infrared sources and detectors.
authors: Sadhvikas Addamane, Sanghyeok Park, Quinn T. Campbell, Evan M. Anderson, Thomas Rotter, Darryl Shima, Julia Deitz, Paul Kotula, Ganesh Balakrishnan, Oleg Mitrofanov, Igal Brener, Prasad P. Iyer

articles.title: Vortexable Chern Bands Sit Exactly on the Topological Floor of Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vortexable Chern bands host ideal fractional Chern insulators. Paired with time-reversed partners by orbital-diagonal on-site attraction, they are the least stiff flat-band superconductors at fixed Chern number C, filling, and pairing amplitude. For uniform pairing and a nondegenerate paired state, the exact T=0 stiffness determinant is the topological floor times 1+(Torb/2π|C|)²łe1+(TLVP/2π|C|)², where Torb and TLVP measure departures from vortexability. Enhancement costs vortexability, and the inequality is strict only if internal components share a site, as in heterostrained bilayers.

articles.title: Frustration and topology in the phase behavior of solute-frustrated q-clock models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frustration can enhance fluctuations and create new and interesting phase behavior. When combined with the ability to host topological defects, frustration can increase the complexity of a system's phase diagram through topological and frustrated topological transitions. To understand the interplay of frustration and topology on phase behavior, we introduce and study solute-frustrated q-clock (SFqC) models, in which solute sites are added to the q-clock model, a lattice model where each spin can take one of q orientations. The q-clock model can exhibit spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological transitions, and the interaction between the spins and a solute frustrates the system, in essence by creating a fixed lower bound on the concentration of positive topological defects or vortices. We perform Monte Carlo simulations and develop theoretical descriptions of SFqC models with q=4 and q=6 to understand their phase behavior. We find that these systems exhibit rich phase diagrams that depend on the choice of parameters. In particular, SFqC models have a wide range of interesting low-temperature phases, including the presence of strongly frustrated domains and the absence of long-range order. We also find topological effects even at low temperatures; for instance, we find that topological defects can drive crystallization. We anticipate these results to guide the development of materials that take advantage of frustration and topology to tune phase behavior and fluctuations.

articles.title: Synchronous and asynchronous Monte Carlo dynamics of mean-field spin glasses with rotationally invariant couplings: what they share and where they differ
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare two Markov chain Monte Carlo dynamics for Ising spin glasses with rotationally invariant couplings: the synchronous Monte Carlo method (SyncMC), which updates all spins in parallel with the help of Gaussian auxiliary fields, and asynchronous Metropolis-Hastings dynamics, which updates one spin at a time. Using the Guionnet-Maïda formula, we derive the dynamical mean-field theory of both dynamics in terms of the R-transform of the coupling spectrum. The two effective single-spin processes share a retarded self-interaction and a Gaussian noise; SyncMC has, in addition, an instantaneous self-coupling and a noise that depends only on the response function. These additional terms act only on the fastest time scale, so that the equations for slow time scales, including the fluctuation-dissipation ratio and, for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, the Parisi equation, are the same for the two dynamics. Simulations of the random orthogonal and Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models confirm that both dynamics approach the same fluctuation-dissipation relations, differing only in how many updates they need to do so.

articles.title: Scaling Dimensions and Two-Point Amplitudes from Operator Covariance Matrices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The long distance behavior of two-point functions of critical lattice statistical mechanics models depend on detailed information of the underlying quantum field theory. Yet these universal properties can be difficult to extract because generic lattice operators couple to the infinite hierarchy of continuum scaling operators with unknown coefficients. Recently in Physical Review E 114, 024146 (2026), one approach to disentangle some of this information was proposed using the eigen-decomposition of the operator covariance matrix constructed from cross correlations of a finite set of Nₑₗₗ lattice operators. In this work we analyze this method in detail. We provide an explicit proof that under the assumption of scale invariance the leading decay of the eigenvalues are controlled by the smallest Nₑₗₗ scaling dimensions, even after taking irrelevant perturbations into account. Based on this understanding, we propose a new method by which the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix can be used to construct the amplitudes of the continuum two-point correlation functions. This allows for a complete determination of the structure of the continuum two-point functions from the lattice covariance matrix. We demonstrate our ideas both on synthetic data sets (drawn from the scaling hypothesis) and numerically exact data for the two dimensional Ising model.

articles.title: Interaction-driven competing instabilities in two-dimensional checkerboard quadratic band crossing semimetals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals serve as a fertile platform for interaction-driven quantum criticality, nevertheless, the role of the complete fermion-fermion interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically investigate the low-energy physics of a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal by considering all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions. Using the momentum-shell renormalization group, we derive the coupled flow equations, which reveal that the low-energy physics is governed by a series of fixed points. Depending on the initial conditions, the system may exhibit a single stable fixed point, several discrete fixed points, or three continuous groups of fixed points parameterized by a few variables. By introducing source terms and evaluating susceptibilities, we identify the dominant and subdominant instabilities. The leading phases include nematic spin-nematic (NSN), quantum anomalous Hall (QAH), chiral superconducting (SC₁₎, and quantum spin Hall (QSH) orders. Moreover, several features distinguish our findings from previous simplified models. Off-diagonal interactions generate terms that promote orders absent in such models, the continuous groups allow systematic tuning of the leading instability, and trajectory-dependent instabilities emerge where the full RG flow, rather than the fixed point alone, determines the dominant state. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy quantum critical behaviors and phase instabilities in two-dimensional QBCP semimetals and related electron systems.
authors: Jia-Hao Wen, Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

articles.title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions and deconfined criticality in SrCu₂₍BO₃₎₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: SrCu₂₍BO₃₎₂ is the leading candidate for deconfined criticality, yet theories of its critical regime omit the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions, which gap the kagome Dirac spin liquid. Adding them to the SU(2) gauge theory, we show that time reversal and a spin-orbit-locked glide forbid any gauge-singlet spinon mass to all orders. In-plane DM only twists the spinons, reconstructing the nodes below 0.03-0.17 K, while out-of-plane DM is irrelevant and SO(5) anisotropy arises only at second order. The material thus remains a platform for deconfined criticality, which NMR can test, since a [100] field induces a Néel moment and a [001] field does not.

articles.title: Unconventional spin momentum locking and topological domains in twisted slabs of topological insulator Bi₂Te₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The three-dimensional topological insulator Bi₂Te₃ hosts topological Dirac states on its two-dimensional surfaces. These Dirac states show spin-momentum locking, which usually implies a tangential Rashba-like spin texture. One can alter the properties of the Dirac states by dividing a slab of such a material into two thinner halves, modifying the interface by twisting, shifting, and changing the interlayer distance. Using first-principles calculations, we investigate such modified slabs of Bi₂Te₃. The twisting degree of freedom deserves special attention. To this end, we follow two approaches. On the one hand, we probe different stacking configurations in order to extract parameters relevant for small twist angle Moiré structures. We find non-trivial topology only for some stackings, leading to topological domains on the Moiré scale. On the other hand, we calculate the properties of commensurate twisted supercells. The latter reveals not only flat bands, which are tunable by external pressure, but also radial spin textures with unconventional spin-momentum locking.

articles.title: Self-Trapping and Liouvillian Spectral Transitions in a Dissipative Bose-Hubbard Dimer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the self-trapping transition in dissipative double wells using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization. We find that, similar to the conventional interaction-driven transition from oscillatory dynamics to self-trapping, dissipation alone can also induce self-trapping-like localization in one well. The resulting state, although transient and decaying, persists for a substantial time. At the mean-field level, the interaction- and dissipation-driven transitions are discontinuous and continuous, respectively. When interaction and dissipation both are present, their interplay produces three dynamical regimes: (i) at weak interaction, increasing dissipation drives a transition from oscillations to self-trapping; (ii) at moderate interaction, self-trapping at weak dissipation, oscillatory dynamics at intermediate dissipation, and re-entrant self-trapping at strong dissipation; and (iii) at strong interaction, self-trapping persists but is weakened by dissipation. We connect the transition with the Liouvillian spectrum. It is observed that purely dissipation-driven transition coincides with an exceptional point in the spectra, and a peak in the Liouvillian gap, marking the onset of the quantum-Zeno regime. In the presence of interactions, however, the onset of the Zeno regime is shifted to dissipation strengths larger than that required for the self-trapping transition.

articles.title: Phase engineering of odd parity state in a quantum dot Josephson junction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling fermion parity in quantum-dot Josephson junctions (QDJJs) enables access to novel superconducting physics. While parity transitions are usually tuned electrically, we study phase-induced transitions in a strongly coupled QDJJ using the superconducting phase difference across the dot terminals, denoted by φ. We find that this phase allows control over the ground state parity, with parity transitions observed as the Andreev bound states (ABSs) energies crossing zero. These crossings occur near φ = π, and their behavior is in good correspondence to a simple model considering a single-level quantum dot proximitized by a superconductor. These results place phase-controlled QDJJ arrays as a promising platform for exploring exotic phenomena such as Majorana zero modes.
authors: Shohei Kobayashi, Tyler Lindemann, Sergei Gronin, Geoffrey Gardner, Peter Stano, Daniel Loss, Michael Manfra, Seigo Tarucha, Sadashige Matsuo

articles.title: Two-Dimensional Quantum Droplets in a Mixture of Bose-Einstein Condensates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum droplets represent a striking manifestation of beyond-mean-field physics, with properties that depend sensitively on dimensionality. Although quantum droplets have been experimentally realized in one and three dimensions, their realization in two dimensions has remained elusive. Here, we observe the formation of a two-dimensional (2D) quantum droplet in a quasi-2D geometry by transferring the single-component Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) into a spin mixture in the Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) regime, where the LHY effect evidently deviates from its three-dimensional form. We find that, in our scheme, 2D quantum droplets are more stable and exhibit longer lifetimes than previously reported quantum droplets. By instead transferring the initial BECs into another single-spin state with a negative scattering length, we generate 2D Townes solitons. A comparison between the two types of self-bound states shows that, whereas 2D Townes solitons are stable only near a critical atom number determined by the scattering length, 2D quantum droplets remain well-defined and self-bound over a much broader parameter range. These realizations of quantum droplets and Townes solitons in two dimensions provide new insights into self-bound states and open new avenues for exploring nonlinear dynamics in quantum liquids.
authors: Yue Zhang, Liangchao Chen, Wei Han, Linshan Gong, Yazhou Wang, Zekui Wang, Xinhao Liang, Wenjie Sui, Pengjun Wang, Lianghui Huang, Zengming Meng, Zhuxiong Ye, Jing Zhang

articles.title: Exploring ground state phase diagrams of Rydberg atom arrays with finite projected entangled-pair states
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rydberg atom arrays (RAA) have been advocated as a promising avenue for the quantum simulation of different exotic quantum states. Numerical predictions for the ground state properties of this experimental platform can, however, be challenging in two-dimensional setups. In particular, faithfully treating long-range interactions is often crucial for distinguishing the fate of competing phases, but it usually comes at considerable cost. Projected entangled-pair states (PEPS), optimized via a sampling-based approach, have been shown to deal with such terms on the same ground as shorter-range ones. In this work, we employ these tools to investigate debated physical questions in different frustrated geometries of RAA, from the emergence of spin-glass physics on the Kagomé lattice to topological order beyond the PXP model on the Ruby lattice. By that, we contribute to establishing PEPS as well-suited tools for creating digital twins of RAA experiments.
authors: Konrad Schröder, Erik Lennart Weerda, Matteo Rizzi

articles.title: Strain-induced disorder from Schottky gates on high mobility 2DEGs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrostatic gates on two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs) in GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures are essential for numerous studies of correlation driven phenomena, many performed within the fractional quantum Hall effect. However, the most commonly used type of gates, the metallic Schottky gate, has the propensity to adversely impact the electron mobility and suppress the fractional quantum Hall states. Here we demonstrate through commensurability oscillations under specially designed nanostructured superlattice gates, that strain effects are responsible for the mobility reduction. The experimental results agree well with COMSOL Multiphysics simulations. In a regular, unpatterned gate the disordered, granular nature of the metal film fills the same role as the superlattice in creating a strain field penetrating down to the 2DEG, as we show with a simplified model. These results will help in understanding, improving and finding novel methods to reduce strain-induced disorder in gated high-mobility 2DEGs.
authors: Sambit Mohapatra, Lukas Berg, Jean-Baptiste Cuvellier, Yan Sun, Abdelhanin Aassime, Alan Durnez, Antonella Cavanna, Dominique Mailly, Ulf Gennser

articles.title: Boundary-Sensitive Quantum Order on Non-Amenable Lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that quantum systems on non-amenable lattices, whose boundaries constitute an extensive fraction of the system, host novel forms of bulk ordering with no Euclidean counterpart. Combining boundary-retaining iDMRG with an exact symmetry-fixing duality, we investigate p<5 state clock models on the coordination-3 infinite Cayley tree. We find that between the ordered and disordered phases lies an emergent intermediate phase with bulk order induced by an arbitrarily weak boundary field rather than by conventional spontaneous symmetry-breaking. This establishes boundary-sensitive order as a distinct quantum ordering mechanism defying Landau's spontaneous symmetry-breaking paradigm. The intermediate phase realizes a bulk-boundary correspondence in which the unpolarized boundary selects a specific ordered bulk state.
authors: Xingzhi Wang, Zohar Nussinov, Gerardo Ortiz

articles.title: Development of microwave multiplexed readout for athermal phonon TES-based detectors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continued advancements in sub-eV calorimetric measurements are being enabled through the athermal phonon detection channel, with applications spanning a diverse array of fields, including low-mass dark matter searches, coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, and quantum information science. While Transition Edge Sensors (TESs) have achieved the lowest thresholds to date, they face significant scalability bottlenecks due to the inherent constraints of conventional SQUID readout architectures. To address this limitation, we present an update on R&D to develop practical, highly multiplexed, microwave readout for athermal phonon TESs, which can enable a dramatic increase in both sensor count and target mass, with a focus on sub-GeV dark matter searches as a target application. This work leverages advances from highly scaled mm-wave, x-ray, and gamma-ray TES systems, adapting them to the unique needs of low-threshold rare event measurements. We quantify the basic readout functionality and noise level in our dilution refrigerator testbed and demonstrate operation of a variety of TES devices with saturation powers significantly lower than mm-wave and x-ray devices. We demonstrate proof-of-concept multiplexed readout of background event pulses, bound the readout's contribution to the parasitic TES background load to <1 fW, and discuss a cryogenic inline RF filtering scheme. These results demonstrate practical solutions to several of the key challenges that must be solved before a next-generation athermal phonon detector at scale is realized.
authors: Tran Tsan (Physics Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA), Douglas A. Bennett (National Institute of Standards and Technology, Boulder, CO, USA), Daniel T. Becker (Department of Physics, University of Colorado, Boulder, CO, USA), Rebecca Carney (Engineering Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA), Johnathon D. Gard (Department of Physics, University of Colorado, Boulder, CO, USA), John A. B. Mates (National Institute of Standards and Technology, Boulder, CO, USA), Joel N. Ullom (National Institute of Standards and Technology, Boulder, CO, USA, Department of Physics, University of Colorado, Boulder, CO, USA), Michael R. Williams (Physics Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA), John C. Groh (Physics Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA)

articles.title: Certifying Nonlocal Spin Quantum Entanglement from Local Tunneling Spectra
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum entanglement is intrinsically nonlocal, whereas tunneling spectroscopy measures one site at a time. We show that this apparent mismatch can be overcome: local tunneling spectra can certify spin entanglement without coherent control or absolute intensity calibration. An exact spin sum rule turns the high-bias conductance into an internal normalization, allowing the inelastic spin-flip weight to place a lower bound on the local quantum Fisher information. Total-spin conservation then fixes the otherwise inaccessible intersite fluctuation, converting two local spectra into a bound on a collective entanglement witness. We incorporate coupling to the substrate through a spectroscopic bound on spin leakage, while a hierarchy of thresholds distinguishes entanglement between the spins from entanglement with their environment. Including instrumental broadening and noise, the resulting certificate holds at a stated confidence level. These results establish a route for extracting nonlocal quantum information from equilibrium local spectroscopy.
authors: Payman Kazemikhah, Ruolun Zhang, Xiangyu Luo, Byunghoon Kim, Yu-Peng Zhu, Md. Shafayat Hossain, M. Zahid Hasan

articles.title: Concatenated continuous-drive protection of exchange-based spin-qubit gates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exchange-based two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits are sensitive to low-frequency detuning noise and control errors. Here, we extend concatenated continuous driving (CCD), implemented by phase modulation of a global microwave drive, to exchange-based SWAP and sqrtSWAP operations between double-dressed spin qubits and investigate its effectiveness for protecting two-qubit gates. We find that CCD retains strong protection against quasistatic common-mode detuning errors while substantially improving robustness against Rabi-frequency errors and qubit-to-qubit Rabi-frequency mismatch compared with conventional continuous dressing. By contrast, the gate fidelity is impacted by differential detuning errors. By modeling partially correlated quasistatic detuning noise, we further show that the noise-averaged gate fidelity depends strongly on the spatial correlation of the qubit-frequency fluctuations, with positive correlations enhancing CCD protection by suppressing the differential-noise component. These results identify the symmetry and spatial correlation of qubit-frequency noise as key factors governing continuous-drive protection in coupled spin-qubit systems.
authors: Takuma Kuno, Takeru Utsugi, Andrew J. Ramsay, Hideo Arimoto, Tetsuo Kodera, Hiroyuki Mizuno

articles.title: The Anyon Atlas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify possible topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions with up to 22 anyons in the bosonic case and up to 26 in the fermionic case, through the modular data of modular and supermodular tensor categories. We construct such data via congruence representations of SL(2,Z) using a numerical optimization algorithm that scales to high rank. We chart the relations between the resulting theories, including anyon condensations and Chern-Simons realizations. We find examples of modular data that do not appear to arise from any Chern-Simons theory by any sequence of condensations of anyons or gaugings of ordinary global symmetries. These examples give qualitatively new topological quantum field theories, which go beyond any notion of gauge theory. For examples in this class with 11 and 12 anyon types, we solve the pentagon and hexagon equations explicitly, showing that these modular data are realized by full unitary topological quantum field theories. We also introduce https://www.AnyonAtlas.org, an online resource for exploring the data.
authors: Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham

articles.title: Subsystem quantum Rényi-Bhattacharyya distance in 2D CFTs and its holographic applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25685v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a systematic method to compute the subsystem fidelity and Rényi fidelity in two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) from the operator product expansion of twist operators, and apply it to the subsystem quantum Bhattacharyya distance (BD) and Rényi-Bhattacharyya distance (RBD). We validate the method against exact results in the free massless fermion and boson theories, and then use it to compute the BD and RBD in holographic CFTs between two heavy primary states, between two thermal states, and between a heavy primary state and a thermal state. When the two states differ in their classical, order-c data, the distances are of order c, and the states are distinguishable already at the level of classical gravity; when the leading data coincide, the distances are of order 1/c at every order of the short interval expansion, so that the distinguishability becomes a perturbative quantum gravity effect. For a heavy primary state and its thermal counterpart, the leading contribution to the BD appears at order ell⁸ and is of order c⁰, whereas the RBD is generically of order c, in line with the earlier finding that a heavy primary state and a thermal state share the same order-c entanglement entropy but have different order-c Rényi entropies in the short interval expansion.

articles.title: Phonon-dominated thermal conductivity of a superconducting amorphous MoSi thin film
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the differential 3ømega method to directly measure the temperature dependent thermal conductivity for about 90 nm Mo0.78Si0.22 thin films.
