The measurements are performed in a closed-cycle cryostat to access the temperature range between 50 K and 300 K. The MoSi thin films are capped with Al2O3 and probed with a Pt wire. The results show that the thermal conductivity does not satisfy the Wiedemann-Franz law. This implies that thermal transport in MoSi is not dominated by electrons but by phonon-like excitations, contrary to what is assumed in many electro-thermal models of superconducting devices. We argue that this property might be related to the weak localization visible in the resistivity as a function of temperature curves of the superconductor.
authors: Jacopo Piantanida Chiesa, Tom Q. Post, Martin P. van Exter, Michiel J. A. de Dood

articles.title: Universal Quantum Criticality from a Gaussian Variational Manifold
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26246v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Universal behavior at continuous phase transitions is encoded in long-wavelength fixed-point theories controlled by dimensionality and symmetries. It is a central question for which systems this universal behavior and the underlying long-wavelength description can be captured by a noninteracting theory allowing for analytical and accurate predictions. In this work we provide a systematic procedure for obtaining the best noninteracting fermionic description of a quantum phase transition through fermionic Gaussian states. We demonstrate the performance of our procedure for the interacting long-range transverse-field Ising chain. This formulation reduces the problem to a self-consistent Euler equation that yields a critical line in close agreement with independent numerical benchmarks, while its singular momentum structure provides analytic predictions for continuously varying critical properties. Yet exact diagonalization shows that Gaussian-state fidelity to the exact ground state is poorest, and non-Gaussianity strongest, near the transition. Thus, accurate predictions for critical properties can emerge from the Gaussian variational description even where its microscopic wave-function approximation is weakest.
authors: Reyhaneh Khasseh, Fabian Ballar Trigueros, Markus Heyl, M. A. Rajabpour

articles.title: End-to-End Optimization of Partial Fault Tolerance in Neutral-Atom Arrays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fault-tolerant (FT) quantum computation offers a pathway to quantum advantage, but its realization is hindered by its significant overhead. The partially FT "STAR" architecture reduces the cost of universal computation at the price of relaxing FT requirements for non-Clifford operations, increasing exposure to hardware noise. Therefore, maximizing its performance and applicability demands careful co-design with the underlying hardware. In this work we investigate the co-design of the STAR architecture with neutral-atom platforms, connecting the underlying atomic physics to logical error modeling and application-level performance. At the physical level, we identify a favorable noise bias in ¹⁷¹Yb Rydberg gates, and show how it can be enhanced through error-selective pulse optimization. At the logical level, we identify an intrinsic error suppression mechanism, yielding vanishing logical coherent noise in leading order. Detailed circuit-level simulations of surface code implementations show more than an order of magnitude reduction in logical error relative to previous estimates. As a concrete target application, we focus on the Fermi-Hubbard model with periodic boundaries, for which we design a simulation circuit particularly suited to early implementations. We quantify the resource tradeoff of partially and fully FT approaches to gate synthesis, with the former showing approximately an order of magnitude reduction in state-injection depth, and an even larger reduction in Clifford resources. Comparing with classical and fully FT approaches, we identify regimes where partial fault tolerance provides both lower overheads and lower error rates. In our estimates, this is accessible with moderate error rates psim 10⁻³ and a few thousand qubits, underlining that for these types of problems, partial FT approaches provide a compelling pathway to early quantum advantage.
authors: Stefano Veroni, Aydin Deger, Andrew J. Daley

articles.title: Non-Markovian exceptional points and information backflow: a Heisenberg reaction-coordinate approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The primary pathway to the investigation of exceptional points (EPs) in open quantum systems has been the use of Markovian master equations. However, recently it has been realised that they can arise in settings that show non-Markovian behaviour. The main approach in this direction has been the use of pseudomodes, which allow the influence of a structured environment to be replaced by new damped auxiliary modes. In this work, we use a Heisenberg-equation approach which relies on the reaction-coordinate formalism to obtain exact analytical dynamics. First, we show how our method considerably simplifies the analysis compared to the use of master equations. Second, we utilise it to discuss non-Markovian revivals in systems with second and higher-order EPs, showing that the notion that EPs demarcate the onset of revivals is not generally true. We then utilise our results to discuss the dynamical effects of higher-order non-Markovian EPs, deriving bounds on the number of revivals and investigating enhanced asymptotic relaxation near higher-order EPs. Finally, we investigate non-Markovian EPs with engineered reservoirs and show how they can be utilised to control the rate of irreversible information loss.
authors: Daniel Holst, Gianmichele Blasi, Shishir Khandelwal

articles.title: Absorbing state transitions with long-range annihilation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2409.03280v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a family of classical stochastic processes describing diffusive particles undergoing branching and long-range annihilation in the presence of a parity constraint. The probability for a pair-annihilation event decays as a power-law in the distance between particles, with a tunable exponent. Such long-range processes arise naturally in various classical settings, and increasingly play a role in the study of quantum dynamics: for example, quantum state preparation or error correction processes aim to prepare ordered ground states, which requires removing point-like excitations in pairs via non-local feedback operations conditioned on a global set of measurement outcomes. We analytically and numerically describe features of absorbing phases and phase transitions in this family of classical models as pairwise annihilation is performed at larger and larger distances. Notably, we find that the two canonical absorbing-state universality classes -- directed-percolation and parity-conserving -- are endpoints of a new line of universality classes with continuously varying critical exponents. These new classes follow from an interplay of long-range interactions and symmetries: decreasing the long-range exponent effectively weakens the local effects of global symmetry constraints. This competition significantly broadens known non-equilibrium phases and phase transitions.
authors: Nicholas O'Dea, Sayak Bhattacharjee, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Vedika Khemani

articles.title: Coherence and pairing enhancement in a trilayer cuprate with layer-selective charge order
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.01448v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Trilayer cuprates hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures (Tc), yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), we uncover a striking interplay between charge order, superconducting gap magnitude, and quasiparticle coherence in Bi₂Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O₁₀₊δ (Bi2223). We present ARPES-based evidence of charge order on the inner CuO₂ plane -- as confirmed via resonant x-ray scattering (RXS) -- and show that the same inner plane hosts a large superconducting gap matching its doping, firmly establishing it as underdoped. Despite its underdoped nature, the inner plane also exhibits an exceptional degree of quasiparticle coherence; suppressing charge-order fluctuations further enhances this, making it comparable to that of the overdoped outer planes at elevated electronic temperatures. At the same time, on the overdoped outer planes we find larger superconducting gaps than what is seen on comparably doped single and bilayer cuprates, indicating an unexpected and simultaneous enhancement of both coherence and pairing interactions in Bi2223. These findings, supported by complementary single- and three-layer Hubbard model calculations, reveal a unique interlayer mechanism in which both pairing strength and phase coherence are optimized when interfacing planes with distinct hole concentrations, providing new microscopic insight into the record Tc of Bi2223.
authors: S. Smit, M. Bluschke, P. Moen, N. Heinsdorf, E. Zavatti, G. Bellomia, S. Giuli, S. K. Y. Dufresne, C. T. Suen, V. Zimmermann, C. Au-Yeung, S. Zhdanovich, J. I. Dadap, P. Dosanjh, M. articles.title: Quantum Geometric Injection and Shift Optical Forces Drive Coherent Phonons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.17814v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a gauge-invariant quantum-geometric theory of light-induced Raman forces driving coherent lattice dynamics in solids. We show that the resonant interband response separates into injection and shift forces, providing the lattice analogue of injection and shift photocurrents. Crucially, the electronic quantum metric and Berry curvature directly govern these forces, weighted by distinct electron--phonon quantities. The injection force is controlled by the quantum geometric tensor and differences between band-diagonal electron--phonon couplings, producing the resonant displacive response. The shift force is a resonant impulsive response governed by quantum geometry and a phononic shift vector arising from interband electron--phonon coherence. We derive polarization selection rules, symmetry constraints, and temporal signatures. Applied to interlayer shear phonons in a bilayer Haldane model, the theory predicts tunability with optical frequency, topology, electronic temperature, and current-induced symmetry breaking. These results establish a quantum-geometric framework for coherent lattice dynamics and identify coherent phonons as experimentally accessible signatures of electronic quantum geometry in quantum materials.

articles.title: Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points and beyond of far-from-equilibrium dilute system: ultra-cold Fermi gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.18821v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The far-from-equilibrium dynamics driven by the scattering from next-to-leading-order (NLO) corrections in the quantum field theory has stationary solutions for the particle distribution characterized as the Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points corresponding to scale-invariant particle/energy flux. The dynamics of the spatially homogeneous dilute ultra-cold Fermi gas is investigated, and its kinetic equation confirms the Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points in the perturbation theory by the quasi-particle assumption, in contrast to the wave turbulence of the ultra-cold Bose gas. In addition, other stationary states are discussed when the the vertex correction becomes significant in the kinetic equation. It is found that conditions for the scale-invariant flux in this case no longer hold when the quasi-particle assumption is applied.

articles.title: Horizon-Boundary Localization of the Hawking Temperature in a Weak AdS/CFT Extension
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a conditional boundary-localization statement for the Hawking temperature. For a static, Euclideanizable black hole with a non-degenerate horizon, the temperature is determined entirely by the first non-vanishing near-horizon data. This result is obtained consistently through three approaches: removal of the Euclidean conical defect, the horizon boundary term in the two-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet theorem, and a complex residue calculation. In asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime, the Euclidean time periodicity selected at the horizon extends to the conformal boundary, so the boundary conformal field theory inherits the same thermal period up to time normalization. This provides only a weak, temperature-sector extension of the AdS/CFT framework and does not imply a full duality. For dynamical spherical spacetimes, the Hamilton-Jacobi analysis selects the trapping or apparent horizon as the local thermal boundary, whereas a separated event horizon is generally not associated with the relevant pole. Vaidya and charged-Vaidya examples support this boundary-selection picture and reduce to the standard stationary result when the horizons coincide. The construction is further checked using anti-de Sitter black holes, numerical contour calculations, limiting cases, and an extremal counterexample. The result concerns where the Hawking temperature is localized and does not replace the quantum-field-theoretic mechanism of Hawking radiation.

articles.title: Finite quantum gravity in locally conformally flat spacetime through covariant spectral regularization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pure gravity quantum gravity (pure gravity QG) is non-renormalizable at two and higher loop level. One of the main characteristics of objects occurring in QG is their Lorentz covariance. QG necessitates the analysis of a collection of Lorentz covariant terms of higher and higher order, which is not feasible using renormailization. This paper describes how the regularization technique known as covariant spectral regularization (CSR) can be used to analyze Lorentz covariant 4-tensor valued measures on Minkowski space. The graviton vacuum polarization tensor is cast as such a measure and CSR is used to obtain a well defined and finite function representing this tensor. This is then used to compute the Feynman amplitudes for examples of one-loop, two-loop and n-loop graviton-graviton scattering in pure gravity QG. The CSR method results in functions (densities) representing divergent Feynman integrals without requiring renormalization or counterterms. Therefore it can be used to analyze arbitrarily complicated multiloop QG Feynman diagrams without being crippled by a proliferation of counterterms, as is classical QG.

articles.title: Transient Heat Conduction on Quantum Hardware: Replicated Temperature-Field Reconstruction and Shot-Count Sensitivity with a Variational Quantum Linear Solver
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Implicit discretizations of transient heat conduction repeatedly generate sparse linear systems, making diffusion problems a natural test bed for quantum linear solvers. This study evaluates how accurately a variational quantum linear solver (VQLS) recovers the temperature field produced by one backward-Euler step of one-dimensional conduction on IBM quantum hardware. A pre-specified confirmatory experiment compares N=4 interior temperatures encoded on two qubits with N=8 temperatures encoded on three qubits using ten paired hardware blocks; a separately defined N=16, four-qubit extension is evaluated in five independently scheduled exploratory blocks. Local VQLS optimization reduces relative temperature-field error to approximately 10⁻⁸ for all three cases, establishing an essentially exact ideal reference at this scale. On hardware, mean relative L2 temperature-field error is 8.07% for N=4 and 20.14% for N=8, a paired increase of 12.06 percentage points (95% CI, 10.71-13.42; exact paired sign-flip p=0.001953). The exploratory N=16 mean is 24.75+/-1.84%. A pre-specified N=16 shot-count follow-up then evaluates the same locked circuit at 2,048, 8,192, and 32,768 shots in six independently scheduled blocks. Mean field error remains 23.64%, 24.57%, and 24.37%, respectively; the 32,768-minus-2,048-shot contrast is +0.74 percentage points (95% CI, -0.65 to 2.12; p=0.281). In contrast, ideal multinomial sampling predicts a reduction from 2.68% to 0.75%. Higher shot counts reduce block-to-block variability but do not recover the mean cold-side temperature field. The results show that full-field readout of a strongly nonuniform thermal state is limited by more than ordinary finite-shot sampling under the tested hardware conditions, motivating observable-focused quantum formulations for heat flux, stored energy, and selected temperatures.

articles.title: SIESTA-QCOMP: Bridging Classical and Quantum Computing for Strongly Correlated Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Density Functional Theory (DFT) is the established workhorse of computational materials science, yet it faces fundamental challenges with strongly correlated electrons, such as in transition metal complexes and bond-breaking processes. While quantum computing offers a theoretically exact path to resolve these problems, current hardware limitations prohibit fully quantum simulations of realistic material systems. To bridge this gap, we present SIESTA-QCOMP, a modular suite embedding quantum methodologies within DFT. Harnessing SIESTA's localised basis set, we implement a projection-based embedding scheme that treats the bulk environment classically while mapping the strongly correlated "impurity" subspace to a quantum processor. The architecture uses a socket-based driver to orchestrate workflows between the Fortran-based SIESTA engine and Python-based frameworks like Qiskit, ensuring high interoperability. We detail the hybrid workflow, currently utilising a Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and discuss the road map toward methods such as Sample-based Quantum Diagonalisation (SQD). We illustrate the framework on an hypothetical iron porphyrin calculation and argue that such hybrid architectures are not merely interim solutions but essential foundations for integrating quantum utility into materials design, as envisioned by our broader QCOMP4DFT initiative.
authors: Yann Pouillon, Federico Marchesin, Ivano Tavernelli, Emilio Artacho

articles.title: Decoherence of the pair entangled states at thermalization and interparticle interaction. Heisenberg--Wigner path integral Monte Carlo simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For deeper understanding of quantum non-local correlations a new path integral real-time quantum dynamics approach has been developed and applied to the Monte Carlo simulation of the decoherence of pair entangled states in many-body systems in the framework of the ``replica trick''. Calculations have been carried out for the Heisenberg-Wigner path integral representation of the entangled state correlation function (ESCF) in the modified unified electron gas model as example. The Wiener-Khinchin transformation of ESCF has been applied to random paths in path integral allowing for the Monte Carlo simulation of ESCF. Presented results include the spin-resolved radial distribution functions, ESCFs and estimations of the decoherence time of the entangled electron pairs due to thermalization and interparticle interaction.
authors: V. S. Filinov, P. R. Levashov, A. S. Larkin

articles.title: Study of non-uniformity-induced structured spectrum in a tapered optical fiber through stimulated four-wave mixing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tapered optical fibers offer tunable dispersion and a small mode area, yielding high nonlinearity, which makes them ideal for nonlinear and quantum optics. Because phase-matched four-wave mixing strongly depends on dispersion, the taper diameter becomes a key parameter. For sub-micrometer tapers, identifying the exact diameter is challenging. Here, we show that when seeding with a broad spectrum, stimulated four-wave mixing yields a comb-like spectrum that is directly linked to the overall taper profile opening possibility for non-destructive evaluation of sub-micron taper. Our model based on joint-spectral amplitude includes the phase accumulated over the fiber length.

articles.title: QRecoupling.jl: numerical and exact computation of classical and quantum recoupling coefficients
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: QRecoupling.jl is a Julia package for numerical, exact and symbolic evaluation of classical and quantum recoupling coefficients and generic finite sums of quantum factorials, with one interface across the classical limit, principal unitary levels and real or complex deformation. A compact factorial rule and its cyclotomic exponents expose factor cancellation, polynomial structure and level support. The package covers quantum Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, 3j and 6j symbols and user-defined sums. Its adaptive numerical evaluation is combined with exact decisions for sums that cancel to zero. Classical 3j and 6j symbols are evaluated at a speed comparable to that of WIGXJPF, which is based on prime factorization tables, at the smallest spins, and about 6 and 10 times faster at spin cutoff 500. Under real, root-of-unity and complex deformation, the largest relative error measured against independent high-precision references is 3.5 × 10⁻¹⁴ for spins up to 400. Fusion matrices with 401 channels are computed about 100 times faster than by loops over their entries.

articles.title: Probing wetting and solidification dynamics of neon thin films with a high-T_c superconducting circuit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrating condensed noble gases with superconducting circuits offers new opportunities for operating hybrid quantum devices. In particular, electrons on solid neon have recently emerged as exceptionally coherent charge qubits, however the growth of the underlying neon films on patterned devices remains poorly controlled. We monitor neon films near the triple point using a multimode resonator fabricated from high-T_c YBCO, which remains superconducting at temperatures where the liquid phase exists and whose geometry sets a thickness-sensing window near 1 μm. In the liquid state we observe rich film dynamics: uniform wetting that saturates near 20 nm, drainage of thicker films, and spontaneous thickness oscillations, reflecting the extreme sensitivity of thick films in this regime. A galvanic connection to our sensing volume enables in-situ electrostatic tuning of the liquid film thickness. Statistics of freezing the neon across various liquid levels reveal variations of the solid film thickness by approximately an order of magnitude. We also observe a two-fold increase in the quality factor of the resonators at the level of 10³ with added neon and rule out dielectric loss as the limiting factor. Our results demonstrate that hermetic packaging facilitates the investigation of both rich non-equilibrium fluid dynamics and the impact of condensed noble gas films on microwave loss in superconducting circuits, but may not be the best modality for growing solid neon films with precisely controlled thickness.
authors: Brennan Dizdar, Yueheng Shi, David I. Schuster, Christopher S. Lang

articles.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field. However, it was recently shown that this description is incomplete: their inherent gravitational self-interactions can squeeze the field, producing a quantum feature beyond the classical description. Here we analyze squeezing of light dark matter in the presence of decoherence. We show that squeezing is continuously generated, and rapidly enough to survive dissipation, and may also remain present under thermal fluctuations and dephasing. Our results demonstrate that dark matter might possess persistent quantum features and motivate further investigation of their implications for dark matter detection.

articles.title: Measuring the Quantum Phase of Multiphoton Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantum phase of a multiparticle system has remained a long-standing mystery in quantum physics. The absence of a phase operator that faithfully represents this physical quantity has prevented the formulation of a meaningful uncertainty relation with particle number. Here, we resolve this problem by measuring, for the first time, the quantum phase of multiparticle systems containing up to fifteen particles. We achieve this through a new quantum state tomography scheme that combines homodyne interferometry with photon-number-resolving detection. This approach enables us to reconstruct complementary photon-number and phase representations and establish the corresponding number-phase uncertainty relation. Our measurements further provide access to the mutually unbiased basis of a multiparticle system, a fundamental resource for multiparticle quantum information processing. Furthermore, we report the spatially resolved characterization of the quantum phase. These results provide an operational framework for measuring quantum phase in multiparticle systems, with implications for fundamental quantum physics and scalable multiparticle quantum technologies.
authors: Ian Baum, Riley B. Dawkins, Jannatul Ferdous, Omar S. Magana-Loaiza

articles.title: Time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy with quantum light
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a fully quantum theory of time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy, providing a general framework for describing the linear response of a nonequilibrium target to quantum probe fields beyond the semiclassical approximation. We elucidate how quantum correlations between probe-field frequency modes couple to coherences in the target and derive a simple expression for computing the resulting spectroscopic signals. We identify conditions under which quantum light can modify transient absorption spectra beyond the limits achievable with classical fields. Our work establishes a theoretical foundation for exploiting quantum light in ultrafast spectroscopy and suggests new routes for resolving dynamics in matter on timescales shorter than the duration of the probe pulse.

articles.title: Nanoparticle arrays levitated in a cavity for quantum sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2406.00366v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Levitated nanoparticles are being investigated as ultrasensitive quantum sensors of forces and accelerations, with applications ranging from fundamental physics phenomena such as dark matter or quantum gravity to real world applications. Attention is now turning to multiparticle regimes, and an important question is whether collective effects offer advantages for sensing. We investigate here the spectral characteristics of collective motion of N  trapped nanoparticles interacting via the optical mode of a cavity. We find the collective motion typically exhibit two generic spectral features: a broad spectral feature, the collective bright mode (CBM) which has been previously studied; but we find also a new structure of sharp peaks , the mechanical mode comb (MMC). We can describe all the detailed spectral features of the system, with a simple closed-form expression, by reducing the motion to a 1D generic collective mode which is non-Hermitian. We show that the MMC is more advantageous than the usual CBM for increased sensitivity in force sensing. We find that the mechanical comb can autonomously repair loss of `teeth' due to particle loss, a feature that may offer robustness in sensing.
authors: J. H. Iacoponi, M. Rademacher, T. S. Monteiro

articles.title: From Poincare Invariance to Gauge Theories: Yang-Mills and General Relativity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.02052v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article is founded on two fundamental principles: the principle field equations introduced in Refs. i̧teS, S1, S2 and the Fock-Ivanenko covariant derivatives i̧teFI, F. The former yields the equations of motion for free fields of arbitrary spin and helicity. In the massless case, it also dictates that Lorentz transformations for tensor fields acquire an additional term, which takes the form of a gauge transformation i̧teW, S1. The latter principle, the Fock-Ivanenko derivative, introduces interactions based on the intrinsic and Poincare groups. This framework allows us to recover a complete Yang-Mills theory, as well as general relativity in the connection-based formulations of Palatini and Ashtekar, both of which are theories with local gauge symmetries. While the standard approach begins with the symmetries of a matter action, we will instead derive dynamics directly from Poincare invariance. This perspective reveals that for free fields, Lorentz invariance induces the gauge symmetry of massless tensors. A proper definition of these gauge transformations, in turn, requires the covariant derivatives provided by the Fock-Ivanenko approach. Considering matter fields, we derive the interacting Dirac equation in the presence of Yang-Mills and gravitational fields from its free counterpart.

articles.title: Quantum oblique eigenprojection
articles.abstract: Every square matrix decomposes its underlying Hilbert space into generalized, nonorthogonal eigensubspaces. We show that a quantum computer can perform such an oblique eigenprojection Π given block encoding access to the input matrix. Our approach has a query complexity nearly linear in the inverse gap and a normalization factor close to ||Π|| under a spectral-set condition on the input. This covers common assumptions on the numerical range or diagonalizability and matches known results for orthogonal eigenprojections. We achieve this with a two-sided block preconditioning that uses a discrete Fourier transform of the matrix resolvent. As the oblique eigenprojection serves as a fundamental primitive in the design of quantum algorithms, our result can be used to extend and improve a variety of prior results. Specifically, we describe applications to: (i) preparing eigenstates of matrices with complex eigenvalues, extending the quantum eigenvalue transformation algorithm of Low and Su beyond real spectra; (ii) solving continuous-time algebraic Riccati equations, cubically speeding up a prior solver of Rodenas-Ruiz, Zhao, and Lee; and (iii) solving ordinary Sylvester equations, quadratically improving a direct augmented method of Wang and Liu. Our result suggests a promising route to applying nonanalytic matrix functions on quantum computers.

articles.title: Enhanced Localized surface plasmon resonance and Interfacial Charge Transfer in Cu/ZnO Nanosphere Heterostructures: Insights from Combined DFT and FDTD Simulations
articles.abstract: Localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) enhances light absorption and quantum conversion efficiency in photocatalysts. The LSPR mechanism in Cu nanospheres loaded on ZnO nanospheres was investigated using FDTD simulations, while DFT was used to analyze interfacial charge transfer in Cu/ZnO heterostructures. Structures include A, a Cu nanosphere on ZnO; B, a partially embedded Cu nanosphere in ZnO; and C, a Cu/ZnO core-shell structure. Cu nanoparticles exhibit a response around 570nm. Increasing nanoparticle size strengthens plasmon-interband coupling, enhances extinction intensity, induces a red shift, and produces local electric field enhancement up to ~ 1000 times the incident field. Embedding Cu nanospheres in ZnO to form a core-shell structure improves hot-electron utilization, suppresses corrosion, and tunes the dominant plasmonic response. Structure A shows LSPR peaks at 585nm (normal incidence) and 577nm (parallel incidence), with a three fold higher electric field under normal illumination. Structure B exhibits a peak at 594nm for both directions, indicating reduced angular sensitivity. Increasing ZnO radius (30–50nm) results in red shifts of 22nm, 23nm, and 47nm for structures A, B, and C, respectively. LSPR response depends on refractive index (1.333–2.25), with all structures converging to 658nm at n = 1.7843. PDOS analysis indicates strong Cu/ZnO orbital hybridization, leading to charge redistribution, Schottky barrier formation, and an upward shift of the Fermi level. Interfacial coupling enhances hot-electron transfer and contributes to LSPR strengthening and red-shift behavior, particularly in core-shell structures with larger contact areas. These results inform plasmonic heterostructure design for photocatalytic and plasmon-enhanced solar energy conversion applications.

articles.title: A 159-step auditable open-quantum-system chain links cerebral metabolism to a coherence-protected information channel in the myelinated axon at 310 K (V148)
articles.abstract: Background. The myelin sheath is increasingly described as an optical waveguide, yet whether a warm, wet biological structure can sustain a coherence-protected information channel remains contested. Methods. We present V148, a fully auditable 159-step open-quantum-system chain that links cerebral metabolism (CMRO2 3.5 ml/100g/min; Pₘₑₜ = 17.23 W) to ultra-weak photon emission (lambda = 500 nm; 2.5e5 phot/s; 134x the Landauer limit per photon at 310.15 K), a myelin Casimir cavity (L = 200 um, a = 500 nm, Q = 100), six THz phononic harmonics (nₜₕ = 1.48–11.15), photon-phonon optomechanical phase conversion (g = 0.02; C = 32; F = 0.9697), phonon-coherent-water coupling (g = 0.18; C = 25920; F = 0.99996), Dicke triads, a 2:1 phase-locking dial (eps* = 0.012 inside a +/-0.041 window), a coherence-gated conditional gate, and a perfect-state-transfer channel (F = 0.999888; t* = 1.77 ms, delta band). Dynamics were integrated with RK45 (rtol 1e-9); entanglement was probed with QuTiP. Results. The chain closes with global efficiency 0.9697 and an ON/OFF vacuum bit ratio of 10.33 (simulated 10.3289). Steady states reproduce the declared anchors (nph ON 0.1063 vs 0.1060; vac ON 0.6189 vs 0.612). Trace conservation holds at < = 4.4e-16 with positivity maintained. Photon-water negativity (7.0e-9) and mutual information (1.3e-6 bits) show the operative resource is phase coherence, not bipartite entanglement. Coherent stock is 4e12 bits, with a 1e9-bit fill time of 9.05 ms. Conclusions. A myelinated axon can operate as a thermodynamically funded, coherence-protected information channel at physiological temperature. Every step, dataset and script is open for inspection and refutation.

articles.title: Qudit-based scalable quantum algorithm for solving the integer programming problem
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.13906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integer programming (IP) is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem that is widely used to represent a diverse set of real-world problems spanning multiple fields, such as finance, engineering, logistics, and operations research. It is a hard problem to solve using classical algorithms, as its complexity increases with problem size. Most quantum algorithms for solving IP are highly resource-inefficient because they encode integers into qubits. In [1], the issue of resource inefficiency was addressed by mapping integer variables to qudits. However, [1] has limited practical value due to a lack of scalability to multiple qudits to encode larger problems. In this work, by extending upon the ideas of [1], a circuit-based scalable quantum algorithm is presented using multiple interacting qudits for which we show a quantum speed-up for solving the integer programming problem. The quantum algorithm consists of a distillation function that efficiently separates the feasible from the infeasible regions, a phase-amplitude encoding for the cost function, and a quantum phase estimation coupled with a multi-controlled single-qubit rotation for optimization. We prove that our algorithm yields the optimal solution with the maximum measurement probability. The time complexity for the quantum algorithm is shown to be O(r_P(mn²log d + dⁿ/²/Ny_ₛ¹/² + n ϵQPE⁻¹)) for a problem with the number of variables n taking d integer values, satisfying m constraints with a precision of ϵQPE and r_P repetitions required for reaching a success probability P. Compared to the classical time complexity of brute force O(dⁿ⁾ and the classical exact algorithm O((łogn)O⁽ⁿ⁾), it incurs a reduction of sim dⁿ/² in the time complexity (for a polynomial number of repetitions and precision requirements) for solving a general polynomial IP problem.
authors: Kapil Goswami, Peter Schmelcher, Rick Mukherjee

articles.title: Qudit Implementation of the Rodeo Algorithm for Quantum Spectral Filtering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.16049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Qudits, the multi-level generalization of qubits, provide a natural extension of the binary paradigm in quantum computation and offer new opportunities to enhance algorithmic performance. Beyond their direct applicability to the simulation of multi-level quantum systems, higher-dimensional ancillae can improve sampling efficiency in quantum algorithms by enabling the simultaneous implementation of multiple control operations, thereby reducing circuit complexity. In this work, we pursue three main objectives. First, we present a formulation of the Rodeo algorithm employing a general d-level ancilla qudit. Second, we introduce the concept of the emphRodeo kernel, defined as a two-frequency interferometer, which acts as a spectral filter in the energy domain. Finally, we propose a microcanonical protocol for the Rodeo algorithm. This protocol enables the estimation of entropic quantities through a single energy sweep and admits a natural interpretation as a Gaussian convolution of the density of states. To support the theoretical analysis, we perform numerical evaluations of the corresponding quantum circuit using ancilla qudits of dimensions three, four, and five. The simulations are performed for the one-dimensional Ising model, considering both spin-sfrac12 and spin-1 particles. The ancilla qutrit implementation exhibits an 18% reduction in fluctuations compared to the qubit implementation. Our results show that qudits provide a framework for spectral analysis and thermodynamic characterization of multi-level quantum systems.
authors: Julio Cesar Siqueira Rocha, Rodrigo Alves Dias

articles.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.24295v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV- decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts those frequencies. Were every defect on the same crystallographic site, all would shift alike and still match: worth only a factor 1.15. Real defects occupy symmetry-equivalent sites pointing in different directions, so neighbours land at different frequencies and stop exchanging: a further 2.7. What governs the coherence time is therefore the fraction of bath pairs sharing a transition frequency, not the zero-field splitting. Vacancy aggregation extends NV- spin coherence rather than shortening it.

articles.title: runner 2.0 : A software suite for high-dimensional neural network potentials
articles.abstract: We present runner 2.0 , the “Ruhr University Neural Network energy representation,” a highly optimized software suite for training and evaluating high-dimensional neural network potentials (HDNNPs) of the second, third, and fourth generations. Long-range electrostatics and charge equilibration (QEq) for the description of non-local charge transfer in fourth-generation (4G) HDNNPs are accelerated by quasi-linear-scaling plane wave methods, reducing QEq computational complexity from O(N3) to O(N⁡log2⁡N) such that linear or quasi-linear scaling is achieved across all HDNNP generations. An optimized memory management strategy eliminates the training overhead traditionally associated with long-range interactions, allowing 4G-HDNNPs to be trained with the same efficiency as their local counterparts. Developed in modern Fortran (2003/2008 standards), combined with a hybrid Message Passing Interface (MPI)/Open Multi-Processing (OpenMP) parallelization scheme, runner 2.0 has been designed to run efficiently in any central processing unit (CPU) environment, from cost-effective local workstations to massive high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. Its modular library architecture facilitates straightforward binding to external simulation software; native interfaces to the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS) and the atomic simulation environment (ASE) provide full access to all its features, including built-in committee-based uncertainty quantification. The high efficiency and scalability of the runner 2.0 ecosystem are demonstrated through detailed benchmarks.

articles.title: The std2 package: A computationally efficient program to calculate molecular response properties and excited states using simplified quantum chemistry methods
articles.abstract: The std2 modular program package is dedicated to the computation of excited states and molecular response properties using simplified quantum chemistry approaches. The framework involves several variants of the simplified time-dependent density functional theory, including sTDA, sTD-DFT, SF-sTD-DFT, XsTDA, XsTD-DFT, and SF-XsTD-DFT methods. Combining controlled approximations with efficient implementations, the std2 program enables routine calculations on systems containing thousands of atoms while retaining a favorable balance between computational cost and predictive accuracy. Therefore, the framework supports all-atom quantum mechanics (AQM) methodologies for the treatment of surrounding and dynamical structural effects considering realistic systems. In this contribution, the capabilities of the std2 package are illustrated for spectroscopic observables, such as one- and two-photon absorption, electronic circular dichroism, optical rotation, second-harmonic generation, and excited-state absorption. Among results, benchmark calculations show that the recent XsTD-DFT scheme improves the description of excited states relative to sTD-DFT especially, for charge-transfer excitations while preserving a speedup of two to three orders of magnitude compared to standard TD-DFT. Applications of AQM methodologies to explicitly solvated systems and ultra-large systems are also highlighted, showing the adequacy of the std2 program to treat such systems. Overall, std2 provides an efficient platform for large-scale excited-state and spectroscopic simulations, especially in AQM protocols.

articles.title: QMBL: the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard. A live record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In condensed matter physics, scientists explore phase diagrams of matter through various methods (analysis, numerics, experiment) and achieve consensus when enough methods agree. The quality of variational results for quantum many-body ground states is mainly judged by energy values and respective errors. Here, we present QMBL, the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard (https://www.qmbl.org), serving as the energy layer of the scientific consensus. It is a maintained, interactive record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians. The latest release v0.4.0 holds 1434 energies on 395 instances of six model families and collects all of the community's efforts into one view. Of those instances 153 have no exact solution and any new record serves as a direct improvement to an open science problem. They are the targets of a companion benchmark, QMBL: Open Problems.

articles.title: Thermodynamics of coupled electromagnetic and mass fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a unified thermodynamic framework for chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport by extending the Gibbs--Duhem relation to include kinetic free-energy contributions associated with material and field motion. The resulting kinetic Gibbs--Duhem relation establishes a thermodynamic connection between free-energy variations, generalized chemical potentials, pressure, and transport momentum, while preserving the invariance of the system free energy under changes of reference frame. Within a Lagrangian formulation of free-energy evolution, the relation provides a common structure for diffusion, momentum transport, and electromagnetic dynamics. For nonuniform chemical systems, the framework recovers the coupling between Cahn--Hilliard dynamics and the Korteweg stress arising from composition gradients. Its extension to electromagnetic systems incorporates electric, magnetic, charge, and mechanical contributions into the same thermodynamic formulation, yielding a unified description of electromagnetic and momentum evolution. The framework further separates dissipative from nondissipative transport and establishes a common thermodynamic form for mechanical and electromagnetic propagation. In the isentropic limit, the characteristic propagation velocity is determined by the derivative of the thermodynamic pressure with respect to density, yielding the speed of sound for mechanical systems and the speed of light for electromagnetic systems. These results show that kinetic contributions can be incorporated consistently into the Gibbs--Duhem framework, providing a common thermodynamic basis for coupled chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport without introducing separate thermodynamic principles for each mechanism.

articles.title: Synergistic Self-Driven Nanoconfinement and Dynamical Heterogeneity in Deeply Supercooled "No Man's Land" Water
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The 150--235 K ``no man's land'' (NML) of deeply supercooled water is a highly debated regime where rapid crystallization hinders experimental observation of the hypothesized liquid-liquid phase transition. Using TIP4P/2005 molecular dynamics simulations, we uncover a structurally and dynamically heterogeneous state at ambient pressure that exhibits novel physical features. Our results demonstrate that this low-density state (h̊o approx 0.925 g/cm³⁾ is a unique supercooled liquid, distinct from both glassy and spinodal states. Specifically, it emerges as a stable, structurally arrested phase driven by a self-generated ``soft skeleton'' of nanoclusters. This network forms an intrinsic nanoporous structure that imposes nanoconfinement on the remaining fluid, proving that NML confinement can be an entirely self-driven phenomenon. Finally, we resolve the temperature-dependent, nonlinear behavior of density and compressibility, highlighting a structurally driven anomaly that clarifies the thermodynamics of deep supercooling. Collectively, this work provides a transformative structural framework for understanding the anomalous nature of water within the NML.

articles.title: Comment on "Skyrmion Hall Effect in Altermagnets"
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In their Letter, Jin et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 196701 (2024)] predict a transverse velocity v_y for skyrmions driven by spin-transfer torque (STT), known as skyrmion Hall effect (SkHE), in d-wave altermagnets. Usually, the SkHE emerges from the skyrmion's topological charge which here cancels between sublattices. Instead, Jin et al. attribute the SkHE to the dimensionless quadrupole tensor Aᵢⱼ. The result in their Eq. (12) is fitted to micromagnetic simulations, yielding a finite value for Aₓy. However, via the divergence theorem, Aᵢⱼ simplifies to a boundary integral that vanishes for a sufficiently smooth and localized texture. In this Comment, we substantiate our claim from Ref. [2] that the numerically observed SkHE by Jin et al. for a micromagnetic model with standard Zhang-Li STT in the individual sublattices is merely a discretization artefact.

articles.title: Attraction from repulsion in an interacting Chern band: chiral superconductivity, generalized Hall crystals, and competing fractional Chern insulators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Experiments realizing strong interactions in partially filled Chern bands have observed fractional Chern insulators (FCIs), superconductors, and topological crystals in close proximity. Yet the microscopic relation between them remains poorly understood. Here, we use tensor network simulations to study repulsively interacting spinless fermions in a tunable topological band of the checkerboard lattice. We characterize the competing phases and identify key features of the experimental phenomenology. FCIs from the Jain sequence transition into chiral p-wave superconductivity both below and above half filling as the band dispersion is enhanced. By contrast, at half filling, a generalized Hall crystal with quantized Hall conductance and a doubled unit cell forms for sufficiently strong coupling. Surprisingly, a weak-coupling approach starting from a metallic parent state captures the nature of both ordered phases at intermediate coupling. We find that fluctuations in the metal generate longer-range attraction, which we analyze within the random-phase approximation. This approach captures the pairing symmetry as well as the radial form factors of the Cooper pairs, and incorporating this attraction into Hartree-Fock selects the observed Hall crystal. Together, these results identify fluctuation-induced attraction from repulsion as a common microscopic ingredient of ordering, while our tensor network computations establish the direct competition of both phases with FCIs.
authors: Fabian Pichler, Clemens Kuhlenkamp, Ashvin Vishwanath, Michael Knap

articles.title: Magnetic flux ring splitting near a Navier-Stokes singularity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: OpenAI reports a forced Navier-Stokes flow that becomes singular in finite time, raising the question of its physical consequences. Magnetic reconnection offers a test through the splitting and merging of flux structures. We use resistive magnetohydrodynamics to simulate a magnetic ring driven by an imposed, regularized flow that reproduces the geometry and scaling of the collapsing core. At the nominal singular time, we remove the imposed drive and allow the system to evolve freely. Reconnections before and after release split the ring into two or more daughter rings through bifurcations of the poloidal flux function, with Lorentz feedback selecting the bifurcation type. Unequal winding by the swirl above and below the midplane produces asymmetric toroidal magnetic stresses, unfolding the kinematic pitchfork-like transition into a fold. For single-island splits, the cusp normal form predicts the asymmetry of the daughter rings without adjustable parameters. Three-dimensional simulations retain the splits and merger, confirming that approach to hydrodynamic blow-up can trigger magnetic restructuring.

articles.title: Valley-Selective Transport through Structural Domain Walls in Rhombohedral Graphene Quarter Metals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain walls separating quarter metals with opposite valley polarizations have recently been imaged in rhombohedral graphene multilayers. Depending on their formation mechanism, these walls respond in distinct ways to external magnetic probes. Therefore, understanding their behaviors is critical to the interpretation of experimental results. In this work, we examine domain walls formed from strain-induced one-dimensional structural defects that separate domains with complementary rhombohedral stacking orders. We show that while transport across such domain walls is controlled by the valley degree of freedom, the coupling to a magnetic field is dictated by the momentum-space chirality encoded in the Hamiltonian. As a consequence, structural domain walls are rendered electronically opaque by an applied magnetic field, while intrinsic domain walls formed by spontaneous valley symmetry breaking are unstable in the presence of such an ordering field and can be eliminated. This dichotomy allows the two types of domain walls to be distinguished in a magnetotransport experiment.
authors: Vo Tien Phong, Pablo San-Jose, Bing Cheng, Zhengguang Lu, Elsa Prada, Long Ju, Eugene Mele, Cyprian Lewandowski, Francisco Guinea

articles.title: Bulk-Defect Correspondence in Algebraic Classical Spin Liquids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local constraints in algebraic classical spin liquids give rise to singular momentum-space correlations. This so called pinch-point singularity carries a momentum-space winding number that determines the low-energy structure of the algebraic spin liquid. We show that nonmagnetic vacancies in two dimensions reveal this topological invariant in the real-space winding of the surrounding spin textures. Under explicit conditions, we prove this bulk-defect correspondence for rank-n U(1) spin liquids and verify it numerically for the Coulomb spin liquids of the kagome and checkerboard lattices and the rank-2 U(1) spin liquid of the honeycomb-snowflake model. In this way we show that vacancies can be used as general probes for distinguishing the emergent gauge theories of strongly correlated classical disordered magnets.

articles.title: Zeta potential of magnetic-field-controlled silver nanoparticles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic-field-dependent nanoparticle size does not by itself determine zeta potential, which also depends on interfacial charge, electrolyte screening, and the location of the slipping plane. We extend the sphere-packing description of silver nanoparticles by distinguishing the structural surface, the effective charge plane, and the hydrodynamic slipping plane. The model uses structural radii of SI20nm and SI5nm at zero field and SI250mT, with reported zeta potentials of SI-13.2mV and SI-10.0mV. Effective charge is related to the defective-shell atom count. For field-independent interfacial parameters, the linear response without additional charge weighting decreases with decreasing radius. Its normalized form depends on three electrokinetic lengths through only two sums, preventing their independent determination from a field-dependent zeta curve. At ((κ⁻¹,tₗᵢg,δₛₗᵢₚ)=(3,0,1),nm), nonlinear Poisson--Boltzmann electrostatics changes the fitted shell coefficient from 0.316 to 0.299. Constant total charge still predicts an increase in zeta magnitude, opposite to the observed trend in the evaluated scenarios. Independently calibrated shell and area charge laws differ by less than SI0.05mV, so the endpoint agreement does not distinguish these mechanisms. Propagating the initial size frequencies gives a narrower endpoint size distribution than measured. With charge parameters determined from the measured size populations, its predicted mean zeta potential is SI-9.131mV, with standard deviation SI0.994mV. Imposing the measured mean by charge recalibration does not remove the discrepancy in size width. The combined structural and electrokinetic model thus identifies both the size-dependent contribution to zeta potential and the interfacial information needed to interpret it.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Response Tensors in Crystalline Magnets: Application to Kagome Metals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The prediction of response tensors from magnetic textures is a crucial challenge in the study of noncollinear magnets. Existing methods for constructing descriptors of a given response tensor are limited to first-order multipole expansions or restricted to simple magnetic structures. In this work, we construct a complete symmetry-invariant descriptor basis for arbitrary crystal structures and magnetic textures, providing interpretable features for machine learning modeling of response tensors. We modify the standard principal component analysis framework and derive uncorrelated order parameters that are hierarchically stable: extending the order parameter space to include higher-degree spin order introduces additional order parameters that are uncorrelated to the previous ones. We apply this framework to regression and classification of the anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) in a magnetic kagome lattice. In particular, in the regime where AHC is well modeled by linear regression of the symmetry-invariant order parameters, we find that the squared regression coefficients, ranked by their magnitude, obey a Zipf-like power law: βᵣ² propto r⁻α. Our method provides a systematic route to construct interpretable order parameters of all spin orders that connect the symmetry of a magnetic crystal to its response tensors.

articles.title: Coexistence of Griffiths phase and superparamagnetic-like behavior in La-doped antiferromagnetic CaMnO3
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The coexistence of a Griffiths phase and superparamagnetic-like short range interaction in a single-phase homogeneous manganite is of particular interest because it reveals multiple levels of magnetic clustering generated by disorder and competing exchange interactions. In bulk La₀.₁₉Ca₀.₈₁MnO₃, this unusual magnetic state develops in the antiferromagnetic regime, where A-site disorder strongly modifies the local magnetic landscape. Rietveld analysis confirms a single-phase orthorhombic structure, while magnetic measurements establish a Griffiths phase below TG = 280 K through the deviation from Curie-Weiss behavior. Superparamagnetic-like behavior persisting from 280 to 370 K further indicates that isolated magnetic clusters remain stable well into the nominally paramagnetic region. The presence of both phenomena highlights the crucial role of disorder-induced exchange randomness in stabilizing complex magnetic states in correlated perovskite oxides.
authors: Koustav Pal, Shuvendu Ghosh, N. N. S. V. Rama Raju, Chitrada Prasad, Kalipada Das, I. Das

articles.title: Interplay between high-entropy effects and the superionic transition in fluorite oxides: A liquid-like perspective
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minor actinide (MA)-bearing mixed oxide (MOX), a prominent high-entropy ceramic (HEC), is a promising candidate for advanced fast reactor fuels. Using a hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) approach, we reveal that Np and Am segregation establishes a distinct short-range order (SRO) that induces severe lattice distortion. We uncover a competitive mechanism between localized high-entropy blocking effects and collective superionic dynamics, where the anionic kinetic and structural evolution within the 2000-2800 K range is partitioned and governed by the Tammann crossover temperature and superionic transition temperature. In the low-temperature regime, severe lattice distortions induced by the SRO structures create localized electrostatic and strain-coupled potential wells, which spatially confine the O-ions and lead to their sluggish diffusion. The system exhibits increased dynamical heterogeneity as thermal activation alleviates these structural constraints. Crucially, these localized traps spontaneously transform into a highly interconnected, string-like polyhedral topological network. Driven by the maximization of configurational entropy, this structural change creates low-viscosity transport pathways that trigger confinement-enhanced diffusion. Consequently, a dramatic kinetic inversion occurs, where the O-ion mobility of SRO model surpasses that of random solid solution (RSS) model via an entropy-driven compensation mechanism. Finally, through Gibbs free energy minimization and defect analysis, structural and thermodynamic origins of the superionic transition in HEC are elucidated. This study unveils how local chemical ordering regulates ion transport under extreme conditions, providing theoretical support for the design of high-performance nuclear fuels with both superior radiation tolerance and optimized mass transfer capabilities.
authors: Fengnian Zhuang, Gaosheng Yan, Hong Chen, Yi Zhang, Wenshan Yu, Minglong Xu, Shengping Shen

articles.title: Pressure-Dependent hcp-to-fcc Phase Transition Path Derived from Exact Lattice Summations over Inverse Power Law Potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the phase transition between hexagonal close-packed (hcp) and face-centered cubic (fcc) structures along the Burgers-Bain transformation path at pressures up to several hundred gigapascals. We consider a hierarchy of interatomic potentials, from (n,m)-Lennard-Jones potentials to extended Lennard-Jones two-body interactions in terms of inverse-power expansions and the Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body term, alongside density functional theory (DFT) calculations for solid argon. For inverse-power potentials, free energies are evaluated through exact lattice sums and efficient integral representations based on generalizations of the Epstein zeta function to anisotropic interaction kernels, followed by lattice-parameter optimization. This methodology enables an accurate determination of the pressure-dependent Burgers-Bain minimum-energy path and the associated activation barrier for the phase transition. The transformation exhibits pronounced symmetry breaking connecting the Burgers and Bain paths, a feature confirmed by DFT calculations. At high pressure, the hcp-to-fcc activation barrier increases approximately linearly with pressure, owing to the dominant pressure-volume contribution. Including entropy and anharmonic effects yields excellent agreement with experimental temperature-dependent volumes up to the melting point. DFT results also highlight the increasing importance of many-body interactions under compression. Whereas two-body potentials predict that the path passes through the body-centered cubic (bcc) structure only at very high pressures, DFT generally predicts a pathway that bypasses bcc. The Axilrod-Teller-Muto term slightly reduces this discrepancy. Furthermore, DFT performs better at high pressures, where dispersion forces become less important.
authors: Tage W. Maltby, Andres Robles-Navarro, Jonathan K. Hartlaub, Andreas A. Buchheit, Øivind Wilhelmsen, Morten Hammer, Peter Schwerdtfeger

articles.title: Chirality-resolved imaging of spin waves with a quantum spin
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin waves carry their propagation direction in the handedness of their circularly polarized stray field, a property inaccessible to scalar magnetometers. In the Damon-Eshbach surface wave of an in-plane magnetized film, the dipolar field above the film rotates with a handedness fixed by the direction of travel. The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre in diamond is an intrinsic polarization analyser: a right-handed field about the NV axis drives one spin transition, and a left-handed field drives the other, in both the ground and the excited state. Here, we exploit the two excited-state transitions, which lie inside the spin-wave band of yttrium iron garnet (YIG), as a pair of chirality channels and image Damon-Eshbach waves in both directions. Because reflection from an etched boundary reverses the handedness, the incident and reflected waves appear as two lines in one spectrum and are imaged separately. In the ground state, the same rule applies, and the selected field drives Rabi oscillations, a route to chirality-selective control of the NV spin by magnons. Reading the two channels gives the direction of a spin wave at one point, without a phase reference. This advances chirality-resolved quantum sensing and provides insight into chiral spin-wave dynamics.
authors: Enbo Zhang, Tiancheng Zheng, Bo-Yuan Yang, Shreyes Nallan, Chengchao Xu, Mark Ku, Jian-Gang Zhu

articles.title: From Surface Reactions to Inhibitor Coverage: A Machine-Learning-Assisted Computational Study of Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. Coverage simulations show that inhibitors producing identical adsorbed fragments can yield different coverages because the intact molecules impose distinct steric constraints, leading to different accessible site densities and blocking capabilities. Beyond coverage, we highlight the importance of the reactivity of adsorbed inhibitor fragments toward precursors in determining inhibitor stability and blocking performance. Together, these findings demonstrate the need to consider both steric effects and chemical reactivity on realistic amorphous surfaces. Our calculations connect local reaction chemistry with inhibitor coverage and provide a computational basis for understanding inhibition mechanisms and selecting suitable inhibitor-precursor combinations for AS-ALD.
authors: Gijin Kim, Seungwu Han, Youngho Kang

articles.title: Fully Gapped Superconductivity in the Nonsymmorphic Centrosymmetric Superconductor In2Bi
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nature of superconductivity in nonsymmorphic In2Bi remains an open question, with ongoing debate over whether it exhibits conventional (BCS-like) or unconventional superconductivity. Here we report the physical characteristics and superconducting properties of polycrystalline In2Bi. Measurements of electrical resistivity, magnetization, penetration depth, and specific heat demonstrate the superconducting transition temperature about 6 K, with a sharp transition in resistivity (Delta_Tc = 0.1 K) and RRR = 57.32, reflecting the high quality of the sample. The upper critical field Hc2(0) obtained from resistivity and magnetization measurements are in good agreement with each other and are smaller than the Pauli limit, suggesting orbital limited mechanism. The coherence length = 35.43 nm, penetration depth = 101.9 nm and electron-phonon coupling constant = 1.05 suggest strongly coupled type-II superconductivity. For T
authors: Atul Gangwar, Kunal Yadav, Barnabha bandyopadhyay, S. Patnaik, K. G. Suresh, Sandip Chatterjee

articles.title: Hidden Staggered Superconducting Order in V2Se2O-Family Altermagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: η pairing describes a staggered superconducting condensate whose order parameter changes sign between neighboring unit cells while maintaining a uniform magnitude. Nearly four decades after its theoretical proposal by C. N. Yang, a material platform for stabilizing η pairing has remained elusive. Here, we reveal that altermagnetism, despite being pair breaking for conventional BCS pairing, naturally favors η-like pairing in V₂Se₂O-family altermagnets. Their valley-contrasting spin structure gives rise to oppositely spin-polarized, symmetry-related valleys centered at X=(π,0) and Y=(0,π), which form spin-singlet pairing partners separated by the commensurate momentum mathbf Q=(π,π), thereby favoring an η-like condensate. Self-consistent calculations demonstrate that the resulting η-like state remains robust over broad variations of chemical potential, hopping parameters, and Fermi-surface topology. To detect this hidden staggered order, we propose a phase-sensitive Josephson measurement with a uniform superconductor, where destructive interference suppresses single-Cooper-pair tunneling while preserving two-Cooper-pair processes. This constitutes a charge-4e-like Josephson response despite a bulk condensate composed of charge-2e Cooper pairs, providing a direct phase-sensitive signature of the otherwise elusive η-like condensate in V₂Se₂O-family altermagnets.
authors: Chun Yu Wan, Xiangxi Zhang, Fei Yang, Junwei Liu

articles.title: Kitaev, semi-Dirac, and spinon quantum spin Hall liquids on the square-hexagon-dodecagon lattice: A parent projective symmetry group classification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The square-hexagon-dodecagon (SHD) lattice hosts an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid, while further-neighbor couplings frustrate its Heisenberg magnet into classically degenerate lines where quantum fluctuations can melt the Néel order. To place this state among the lattice's spin liquids, we classify fermionic parton mean-field states with singlet and spin-orbit-coupled triplet amplitudes by their projective symmetry groups (PSGs). As SHD sites lack site symmetry, its Z₂ PSGs are the projective classes of p6mm with time reversal, from which those of every single-orbit p6mm lattice follow. In the idealized Kitaev model, where lattice operations do not rotate spins, these liquids carry a single Z₂ PSG descending from the SU(2) Lieb-flux state, and their projections are exact eigenstates. The PSG's sixfold-rotation sign, fixed by the dodecagon flux, doubles all Majorana bands, and the mirrors exclude a chiral phase in any uniform field, so only a sublattice-staggered three-spin term drives the non-Abelian Ising phase. Beyond the Kitaev state, we find a critical semi-Dirac spin liquid, with mean-field correlations propto r⁻³ along three directions and r⁻⁶ otherwise, and extended Dirac phases with up to 48 fermion flavors, among them an N_f=12 state whose PSG forbids every singlet mass. Out-of-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya couplings gap the Dirac states of its U(1) class into a mean-field spinon counterpart of the Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall insulator, with spin Chern number 1 or 3 and spin-carrying monopoles. Chiral states imply Kalmeyer-Laughlin, semion×semion, and three-fermion orders, rotation-breaking ones show q→ -q asymmetric neutron spectra, and sign-alternating fluxes break time reversal alone. Masses and monopoles in these many-flavor phases and the energetics of frustrated SHD Heisenberg models are natural next steps.

articles.title: Transport Signatures of a Kinetically Self-Trapped Nagaoka Polaron
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nagaoka polarons are canonical examples of kinetic magnetism. Although their spin structure is well understood, their transport remains unexplored. We compute the dynamical mobility of a single hole in the square-lattice t-model using resummation-based quantum Monte Carlo and analytic continuation. Upon cooling, an incoherent Drude-like response gives way to a finite-frequency peak as the dc mobility vanishes. The peak signals an internal mode of a hole confined by its ferromagnetic cloud. Our results establish transport as an incisive probe of polaron formation and kinetic self-trapping.

articles.title: Nonergodicity from Hilbert-Subspace Cloning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify a class of nonintegrable quantum many-body systems composed of single Pauli strings that possess an extensive number of noncommuting local conserved quantities and exhibit partial ergodicity breaking due to exponentially degenerate energy spectra. We show that such systems exhibit a novel mechanism, Hilbert-subspace cloning, where the identical chaotic Hamiltonian acts on each of exponentially many disconnected Hilbert subspaces. Although the dynamics within each clone thermalizes, quantum coherence between clones remains protected and detectable by local observables. Consequently, the long-time behavior of local observables is described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs ensemble, where the hidden subsystem retains its initial quantum coherence.

articles.title: Field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions in anisotropic magnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions (ICTs) in classical spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) D, strong easy-plane anisotropy, and weak easy-axis anisotropy A within the easy plane. This model describes systems with ferromagnetic layers coupled by exchange interaction with DMI. The magnetic field bf H is applied in the easy plane at an arbitrary angle δ to the easy axis stabilizing a soliton lattice in the ground state. We consider ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic in-chain exchange interactions within the continuum limit and show that the easy-axis anisotropy leads to qualitatively different effects in these two cases: the ferromagnetic chain is described by a double-sine-Gordon-type equation with phase-shifted harmonics, whereas the antiferromagnetic chain reduces to a sine-Gordon equation. For the latter case, phase boundaries between incommensurate and commensurate states are found analytically in (H,A,D,δ) space and confirmed by numerical calculations for certain D and δ values. Close to all ICTs, results of the continuum consideration become invalid due to a stochastic destruction of near-separatrix solutions which either make an ICT a first-order transition or stabilize states with spatially irregular soliton and antisoliton arrangements.
authors: P. T. Bolokhova, A. V. Syromyatnikov

articles.title: Light-induced local control of magnetic anisotropy and domain pattern in Co/Pt multilayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Control of magnetic anisotropy is essential for the fabrication of next-generation devices in spintronics and magnetic memory. While conventional approaches such as material composition, thermal annealing, and ion bombardment are widely used, achieving spatially resolved, continuous control remains a challenge. Herein, we demonstrate a dual-regime, localized control over both transient magnetic states and permanent intrinsic properties in perpendicularly magnetized Co/Pt multilayers using ultra-short laser pulses. By employing a multi-scale approach combining Kerr microscopy, magnetic force microscopy, and vibrating sample magnetometry, we reveal that low-fluence irradiation enables a reversible, helicity-dependent accumulation of magnetic phases without altering the intrinsic quasistatic properties. Conversely, high-fluence exposure acts as localized thermal annealing that permanently hardens the magnetic system. This structural relaxation leads to a substantial enhancement of the effective perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, driving a twofold increase in the local coercive field and expanding the equilibrium stripe domain width. By offering both reversible spin manipulation and deterministic engineering of 2D magnetic landscapes, this work paves the way towards flexible, lithography-free anisotropy structuring for advanced spintronic applications.
authors: Ivan Soldatov, Aman Singh, Volker Neu, Rudolf Schäfer, Andrei Sherstobitov, Yana Vaynzof, Stanislav Bodnar

articles.title: Confinement-induced toughening in delignified wood-polyacrylamide composite hydrogels
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With growing interest in environmental conservation, polymer composites incorporating wood-derived materials have attracted significant attention. While research has focused extensively on hard composites utilizing delignified wood or cellulose nanofibers (CNF) and soft composites reinforced with CNF, there have been a limited number of studies on the development of soft composites that utilize the porous cellular structure of wood, with few exceptions. In this study, we fabricated soft composites by infiltrating delignified wood with polyacrylamide hydrogel and subjected them to uniaxial compression tests. The results demonstrated that these materials exhibited far superior strength and toughness compared to either delignified wood or polyacrylamide hydrogel alone. Through systematic investigation and theoretical analysis, we identified the mechanisms underlying these enhancements in strength and toughness. Specifically, in addition to the sacrificial bond breakage known to enhance toughness in double-network hydrogels, we propose that mechanical confinement, arising from the soft, incompressible hydrogel filling the hollow cell lumens, generates excess stress and acts to resist compressive deformation. This approach, which utilizes the cellular structure as a filler, suggests the potential for creating a new class of high-toughness composite materials.

articles.title: Non-Adiabatic Spin-Induced Currents in Magnetic Weyl Semimetals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically study dc electric currents induced by rapid spin precession in noncentrosymmetric magnetic Weyl semimetals using the Floquet--Keldysh Green's-function formalism. The spin dynamics act as a time-dependent chiral gauge field and the geometric structure of electric currents is expressed in terms of the Berry curvature, the quantum metric, and the shift vector. For an isotropic Weyl cone, only an injection current is generated. This current scales quadratically with the driving frequency and linearly with the relaxation time associated with coupling to a fermionic bath. We further show that a finite Weyl-cone tilt modifies the available interband-transition phase space, smooths the frequency dependence of the current, and allows for a shift current and another type of injection current, both of which flow in directions determined by the tilt and the direction of the precession. A finite net current can remain after summing contributions from Weyl nodes of opposite chiralities when their transition phase spaces are inequivalent.
authors: Kota Watanabe, Akihiro Ozawa, Hiroaki Ishizuka, Hiroki Isobe, Kentaro Nomura

articles.title: Equal-spin pairing at finite Cooper-pair momentum in p-wave magnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The realization of Fulde-Ferrell (FF) superconducting states has long been pursued but remains challenging because of the large Zeeman splitting required.
