Here, we demonstrate that p-wave magnets can host equal-spin finite-pair-momentum states with p-wave symmetry, termed FF states, at arbitrarily weak fields. Our Bogoliubov-de Gennes analysis shows that, owing to the displacement of the Fermi surface, two equal-spin electrons in the FF states pair at the same energy, just as in the opposite-spin zero-pair-momentum states of the same gap symmetry. At zero field, the FF states are therefore exactly degenerate with these zero-pair-momentum counterparts. An arbitrarily weak Zeeman field lifts this degeneracy and makes the FF states the superconducting ground state, since they remain stable owing to their equal-spin nature, whereas their counterparts are suppressed by the formation of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. These findings identify the fermiology of p-wave magnets as a promising route toward long-sought finite-momentum superconductivity.

articles.title: The effect of oxygen on the surface tension of AlTi metallic alloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We perform molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of AlTi metallic alloy melts, with a specific focus on surface properties and the effect of oxygen. The simulations use a machine-learned inter- action potential (MLIP) that has recently been tested through experimental data for the statical and dynamical properties of AlTi melts in the bulk [Kato et al. (2026)]. We find that the surface- tension response to oxygen depends strongly on the AlTi composition. Element-resolved density profiles show that oxygen enrichment near the interface is accompanied by a suppression of the Al surface segregation observed in the oxygen-free liquid. The results are compared to experimental values obtained using levitation techniques in microgravity.
authors: Yuna Kato, Jürgen Brillo, Thomas Voigtmann, Linnea Heitmeier

articles.title: Termination-dependent surface Fermiology in the intercalated altermagnet CoNb₄Se₈
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnets have recently gained attention for hosting symmetry-enforced spin-split bands despite zero net magnetization. Angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES) offers direct access to their electronic structure. However, the intrinsic surface sensitivity of this technique complicates the identification of the observed features: Surface states can be misinterpreted as the spin-split counterpart of bulk bands. This issue becomes particularly relevant for layered intercalated systems, where micrometer-sized domains with distinct terminations often coexist on a cleaved surface. We discuss this scenario for CoNb₄Se₈, one of the first established layered altermagnets. Supported by density functional theory calculations, we employ micro-ARPES to probe individual domains and reveal two contrasting surface terminations. We identify Co- and Se-terminated domains with characteristic surface states arising from bulk-surface connectivity of the material. Our work shows that termination-dependent surface contributions are essential for the reliable spectroscopic identification of altermagnetism and for assessing its presence across the family of layered materials.
authors: Pietro Maria Forcella, Alessandro De Vita, Matthew D. Watson, Sammar Tayyab, Chiara Bigi, Iulia Cojocariu, Marcin Szpytma, Matteo Jugovac, Andrea Locatelli, Tevfik Onur Mentes, My Bang Petersen, Paolo Moras, Polina M. Sheverdyaeva, Christopher Candelora, Ilija Zeljkovic, Federico Motti, Jill A. Miwa, Vincent Polewczyk, Matthieu Jamet, Matteo Calandra, Younghun Hwang, Davide Romanin, Federico Mazzola

articles.title: Stability and Nonlinear Dynamics of Field-Driven Extended Domain Walls with Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the stability and non-linear dynamics of extended domain walls (DWs) with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) driven by an external magnetic field in the clean limit (i.e., in the absence of disorder and thermal fluctuations). We show that for moderate DMI strengths, the dynamics in both the low- and high-field regimes are accurately described by a rigid-wall Walker model that neglects flexural degrees of freedom. At intermediate fields, however, the system undergoes a transition into a non-trivial spatio-temporally chaotic regime characterized by dynamically roughened domain walls displaying single- or multi-valued profiles. The phase boundaries delimiting this regime in the magnetic field-DMI phase space are computed using a linear stability analysis based on Floquet theory applied to the extended domain wall, explicitly accounting for DMI and internal phase dynamics. Our theoretical analysis and predicted phase diagram are fully supported by numerical micromagnetic simulations solving the full Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
authors: Enzo Fabrizio Pusiol, Alberto Rosso, Alejandro B. Kolton

articles.title: Magnetic Field-assisted Crystallographic Selection During Grain Growth in Non-Magnetic Polycrystals: A Phase-Field Study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic fields drive grain boundary migration in non-magnetic systems through anisotropic susceptibility, yet how the local orientation can affect the resulting collective grain growth behavior remains unclear. We employ a phase-field model to investigate magnetic-field-assisted grain growth in the diamagnetic Bi. This study provides a mechanistic basis for using static and dynamically varied magnetic fields to control texture development and grain growth kinetics in weakly magnetic materials. We also identify the conditions under which magnetic-field-driven orientation selection produces a distinct bimodal grain-size distribution. The bicrystal studies establish that boundary migration is governed by the magnetic free-energy difference between differently oriented grains, while polycrystalline field-sweep simulations reveal a transition from capillary-dominated coarsening to magnetically biased texture selection. For unbiased orientation distributions, magnetic selection remains distributed; however, when a small population of grains is strongly favored, the driving force localizes and exhibits bimodal coarsening characterized by enlarged favored grains embedded within a fine-grained matrix, even without grain boundary energy anisotropy, particle pinning, or heterogeneity. The field removal and field reorientation simulations further show that magnetic field history can redirect the coarsening pathway.
authors: Rakesh Maurya, Soumya Bandyopadhyay, Somnath Bhowmick, Rajdip Mukherjee

articles.title: Topological Magnetism in 2D and 3D: Skyrmions and Hopfions. Classical and quantum approaches
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss the properties of ferromagnetic skyrmions in relation to the Dzyaloshinskii Moriya interaction, nonlinear sigma models, merons, vortices, frustration, and dipole dipole interactions. Particular attention is given to skyrmion skyrmion interactions and to the dynamical equations governing magnetic textures, including the Landau Lifshitz Gilbert, Thiele, and Landau Lifshitz Bloch equations. The review subsequently extends the discussion to antiferromagnetic systems and to topological structures in three dimensions, with emphasis on Hopfions and their topological characterization. We then examine quantum skyrmions, including approaches that go beyond the semiclassical description, and discuss the emergence of quantum Hopfions. The theoretical framework is complemented by appendices presenting analytical solutions and ansatzes for skyrmions, spin coherent states and path integrals, quantum antiferromagnets, spin torques, fiber-bundle concepts and the Hopf map, and the Euler Lagrange formalism in three dimensions. By connecting continuum field theory, magnetic dynamics, topology, and quantum mechanics, this review aims to provide a coherent framework for understanding the formation, stability, dynamics, interactions, and quantum properties of topological magnetic textures across different dimensions and magnetic systems.

articles.title: topas-editor and TOPilot: tools for AI-driven analysis of diffraction and total scattering data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper describes topas-editor and TOPilot, which provide a powerful interface to the TOPAS software suite and allow generative AI-driven automation of complex crystallographic tasks. topas-editor is a TOPAS-aware VS Code extension designed for the rapid creation and editing of TOPAS input files and for interacting with the software. It knows TOPAS syntax, has crystallographic-aware editing features and provides in-line user guidance via hover tips and automated links to reference manuals. TOPilot is a collection of Python routines and machine-accessible reference documents that allow AI-driven automated analysis in TOPAS. It uses a transferable topas-inp-writer skill that can be applied in all TOPAS application areas. We demonstrate the power and reliability of the approach using examples including: a complex Rietveld refinement with sample- and data-related complications; automatic analysis of multiple data sets; a pipeline from indexing through structure solution to refinement; automatic identification of the phases present in a sample; single crystal and powder diffraction analysis of incommensurate structures; and fitting PDF data. TOPilot can be used directly alongside topas-editor, via a stand-alone topilot-wizard, or via command line interfaces or desktop apps from major AI providers. TOPilot was developed and tested using Claude large language models, but can be configured to use other cloud or local models. topas-editor and TOPilot are freely available.
authors: John S. O. Evans, Oliver J. Wagstaff, Ivana R. Evans, Arnt Kern, Alan A. Coelho

articles.title: Linear response for machine-learned interatomic potentials: phonons at arbitrary wave vectors from the primitive cell
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phonon calculations with machine-learned interatomic potentials are almost exclusively performed with finite displacements in supercells, an approach that is exact only at wave vectors commensurate with the supercell and whose error depends on the range of the force constants. In message-passing networks this range grows with the number of layers, and reaches 140 angstrom for the deepest universal models. Here we show that the dynamical matrix of a message-passing potential can be obtained exactly in the primitive cell, at any wave vector, as the linear response of the forces to a displacement modulated by a Bloch phase, in the spirit of density-functional perturbation theory. The phase enters only where the features of neighboring atoms are gathered, and the trained model is used without modification. One further derivative yields group velocities and mode Grüneisen parameters analytically. We apply the method to NequIP and Prophet, and reproduce the Hessians of supercells to machine precision. Using these results as a reference, we find that the supercells commonly employed in high-throughput calculations lead to errors of several tenths of a THz in the phonon frequencies, and that these errors decrease slowly with the size of the supercell, in particular for deep models. For a low-symmetry silicate, the supercell predicts a dynamical instability that the model does not have. Quantities that depend on derivatives of the dispersion, such as the group velocities and the Grüneisen parameter at low temperature, are considerably more affected than the frequencies themselves. When both approaches are used to obtain the same force constants, their computational cost is comparable for crystals with symmetry.
authors: Thalis H. B. da Silva, Hai-Chen Wang, Miguel A. L. Marques

articles.title: Magnetic order in epitaxial (La2/3Sr1/3MnO3)3/(BaTiO3)3 trilayer heterostructures: Evidence for quasi-two-dimensional ferrimagnetism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The realization of artificial magnetic structures with high epitaxial quality and elevated critical temperatures remains a key challenge for spintronics. Here, we report the fabrication and characterization of epitaxial (La2/3Sr1/3MnO3)3/(BaTiO3)3 trilayer heterostructures grown by layer-by-layer laser ablation. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy, magnetization measurements, and neutron diffraction confirm their exceptional crystalline order and the absence of structural defects. Neutron diffraction reveals no antiferromagnetic Bragg peaks, ruling out most antiferromagnetic configurations with a non zero wave vector Q. Magnetic hysteresis loops instead evidence a ferromagnetic order with a remanent moment of about 0.5 bohr magneton per Mn atom at room temperature, persisting either in-plane or out-of-plane depending on the applied field. Our findings highlight neutron diffraction as a powerful tool for elucidating the magnetic structure of complex thin films and suggest that weak interlayer coupling through BaTiO3 leads to ferromagnetism with a high critical temperature (about 600 K).
authors: E. Rebolini, H. Himanshu, K. Beauvois, S. Grenier, B. Mercey, B. Domenges, B. Ouladdiaf, C. Simon, M. B. Lepetit

articles.title: Grain boundary strength and corrosion cracking susceptibility in TiN coatings under fission product segregation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: During fuel-cladding chemical interaction (FCCI), lanthanide fission products generated in the fuel can migrate into cladding grain boundaries (GBs), where segregation may reduce GB strength and promote corrosion cracking. We use first-principles segregation, decohesion, and bonding calculations to quantify Nd and Ce effects on six coincident-site lattice GBs in bcc Fe and TiN. For each material, segregation energies, work-of-separation values for complete interfacial cleavage, and traction-separation curves measuring ideal resistance to crack opening were evaluated within a consistent computational framework. Nd and Ce segregate favorably to both materials, and the median segregation energies are more negative in TiN, showing that TiN does not simply exclude these species from internal interfaces. The mechanical responses of Fe and TiN differ sharply. In Fe, Nd and Ce consistently reduce work of separation and peak traction, with median work-of-separation retentions of 0.72 and 0.65 and median peak-traction retentions of 0.47 and 0.43. In TiN, most decorated GBs preserve much of the clean response, with median work-of-separation retentions of 1.00 and 0.97 and median peak-traction retention of 0.85 for both fission products. Bonding analysis shows weak, occupied antibonding X-Fe replacement bonds in Fe, whereas the surrounding Ti-N network remains largely preserved after Nd/Ce segregation in TiN. These results provide atomistic support for the use of TiN and related nitride coatings to reduce FCCI damage by retaining GB strength if fission products segregate to coating internal interfaces. This retention of GB strength also provides a mechanistic descriptor for assessing coating susceptibility to FCCI-assisted corrosion cracking and environmentally assisted intergranular fracture.

articles.title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate atomistic simulations of materials under electric fields require long-range electrostatics and electrical-response modeling at length scales beyond the reach of conventional first-principles methods. Yet these capabilities remain difficult to reconcile with the scalability of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Strictly local models enable efficient spatial parallelization but neglect long-range interactions, whereas existing electrostatic extensions introduce global dependencies that hinder distributed computation. Here, we overcome this limitation by analytically separating the long-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges (BECs) into a global electrostatics calculation and strictly local derivatives of learned latent charges. This formulation preserves the spatial decomposability of equivariant MLIPs while enabling distributed evaluation of energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across different boundary conditions. Implemented as DPA4C-LR on the textttnvalchemi platform, the framework scales to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at approximately twice the computational cost of its short-range backbone. Trained on energies and forces, DPA4C-LR accurately infers BECs and reproduces the field-dependent infrared spectra of water. We further demonstrate its capabilities by recovering the characteristic slim polarization hysteresis of relaxor ȩPb(Mg₁/₃Nb₂/₃)O3, which is obscured by finite-size effects in smaller simulations; predicting a room-temperature field-driven ionic conductivity of 6.8 ± 0.7~mS/cm in amorphous ȩLi₀.₉NbO₀.₉Cl₄.₁; and modeling interfacial thermal transport across Si/diamond interfaces with slab-corrected electrostatics. By combining long-range physics, electrical-response inference, and distributed computation, this framework extends predictive atomistic modeling toward device-relevant length scales.
authors: Yicheng Chen, Xiaoyun Yu, Hyejeong Song, Xintian Wang, Zihui Li, Zixi Xia, Junmin Chen, Peichen Zhong

articles.title: Symmetry constraints on magnon-induced dynamics of skyrmion helicity in frustrated magnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The helicity of a magnetic skyrmion in a centrosymmetric frustrated magnet is a soft collective coordinate and a candidate variable for encoding quantum information. Its coherence is ultimately influenced by coupling to the magnon environment, which is commonly incorporated only phenomenologically. Here we combine a microscopic Keldysh treatment of the helicity--magnon coupling to resolve the contribution of individual magnon modes to the effective helicity dynamics. In the U(1)-symmetric model, the magnon bath generates, to leading order, a reactive helicity mass renormalization. When U(1) symmetry is broken, additional direct helicity--magnon couplings become allowed. In the presence of finite magnon lifetimes, these couplings generate an Ohmic contribution to the low-frequency helicity dynamics. The spatial symmetry of the perturbation determines which magnon sectors contribute to this damping, providing mode-resolved selection rules for the helicity--magnon coupling. Thus, we establish a microscopic connection between helicity dynamics and the excitation spectrum of frustrated skyrmions and identify the symmetry constraints governing dissipation of helicity-based quantum states.

articles.title: Learning the self-energy through equivariant neural networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The electronic self-energy determines the single-particle Green's function and, through it, quasiparticle energies and spectral functions, but computing it from first principles is expensive and it is a difficult machine-learning target: complex-valued, matrix-valued in a local-orbital basis, and dependent on a continuous frequency. We predict the dynamical correlation part of the imaginary-frequency G₀W₀ self-energy matrix of molecules from atomic species and coordinates with an E(3)-equivariant message-passing network, the rotational covariance of the orbital-space matrix being imposed by the architecture itself and the static exchange part taken from the density-functional reference. Frequency enters either as an explicit network input or through frequency-specific output heads, and the predicted matrices are continued to the real axis in a representation in which causality and a non-negative spectral density hold by construction. The frequency-conditioned model reproduces matrix elements to below 1 meV on the imaginary axis for the systems studied here, and that accuracy survives the continuation: for water clusters, including a tetramer absent from the training set, and for chemically diverse molecules from QM9, the reconstructed spectral functions follow the G₀W₀ reference peak by peak and the frontier quasiparticle levels are recovered to a few tens of meV. Learning the self-energy on the imaginary axis is therefore a practical route to real-frequency spectra: once the model is trained, and given the density-functional reference it is built on, a new geometry costs no explicit G₀W₀ calculation.
authors: Wudong Shen, Yang Zhong, Min-Ye Zhang, Xinyang Dong, Hongjun Xiang, Xinguo Ren

articles.title: Magnetic tunnel junctions of twisted La2/3Sr1/3MnO3 freestanding bilayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transition metal oxides (TMOs) host a variety of emergent spintronic or multiferroic functionalities owing to the intricate interplay between lattice, orbital, charge, and spin degrees of freedom. Recent advances in epitaxial lift-off and dry transfer techniques using water-soluble sacrificial layers enables stacking and twisting of freestanding membranes of such strongly correlated oxides, providing even richer physical properties and functionalities. To date, the twisted junctions of TMOs have been mainly investigated in insulators, focusing on their structural and dielectric properties. Here, we demonstrate that the twisted bilayer membranes of La2/3Sr1/3MnO3, a prototypical half-metallic ferromagnetic metal TMO, offer a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) with their van der Waals (vdW) gap acting as a tunnel barrier. The twisted junctions of La2/3Sr1/3MnO3 exhibit tunnelling magnetoresistance (TMR) effect with respect to relative orientation of magnetizations of top and bottom membranes. In addition, high-field magnetoresistance shows uniaxial anisotropy, which can be assigned to tunnelling anisotropic magnetoresistance (TAMR) effect reflecting rhombohedral distortion of fully-relaxed La2/3Sr1/3MnO3. The demonstration of TMR and TAMR effects suggests that spin and in-plane momentum degrees of freedom of 3d electrons are conserved across the twisted junctions of TMOs, opening a new avenue for realizing strongly correlated twistronics utilizing electron coherence through tunnelling processes.
authors: Kota Kanda, Shiho Irie, Kodai Niitsu, Masayuki Ochi, Takumi Yamazaki, Kouta Kondou, Kohei Ueda, Takeshi Seki, Jobu Matsuno, Junichi Shiogai

articles.title: Intercalation of Ultrathin Ferromagnetic Iron Films at the Graphene/SiC Interface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The intercalation of high-quality PASG-grown (polymer-assisted sublimation growth) zero-layer graphene on 4H-SiC(0001) with iron is studied using a deposition-and-annealing approach. We find that unlike other metals, Fe does not easily intercalate, and the intercalation procedure has to be balanced with the formation of iron silicides and graphitic carbon at the interface. After successful intercalation, the ultrathin iron films are protected against oxidation by the covering graphene sheet, and retain ferromagnetic behaviour with an in-plane easy axis even at room temperature. When exposed to a selenium-rich atmosphere at elevated temperatures, an almost complete exchange of Fe by Se is observed, imposing a major restriction for the formation of multi-element 2D compounds via sequential intercalation schemes.
authors: Niels Rösch, Rico Ehrler, Stefanie Suzanne Brinkman, Xin Liang Tan, Anders Christian Mathisen, Marc Stevens, Sascha Hermann, Olav Hellwig, Philip Schädlich, Hendrik Bentmann, Susanne Wolff, Thomas Seyller, Fabian Göhler

articles.title: Type 1.5 vortex bags in single component Ginzburg-Landau models with higher order potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the existence of type 1.5 like superconductivity in a single component Ginzburg-Landau model with a higher order potential. The model exhibits two competing superconducting Meissner states (MS), each of which has its own pair of length scales (coherence length and penetration depth). The solutions take the form of bags that contain vortices of one vacuum inside the other. This gives rise to four different types of vortex interaction, where one set of length scales determines vortex interactions inside the bags and the other set between the bags. Hence, within the bag the vortices can repel or attract and the bags themselves can repel or attract depending on the hierarchy of four length scales. When vortices repel within the bag, solutions act similarly to those in type 1.5 multicomponent superconductors, but in a single component system.

articles.title: Limits from nonlinear loss of spin-orbit-torque control of magnon transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling magnon currents is central to the development of magnonic devices, which exploit spin excitations for information transport without charge flow. Here, we use the spin-orbit torque (SOT) from a Pt gate to control the effective magnon damping in three-terminal devices fabricated from low-damping lithium aluminum ferrite (LAFO) thin films and identify the nonlinear damping that ultimately limits the gate response. With increasing gate current, the nonlocal magnon signal initially increases, but saturates and subsequently decreases above a critical gate current density. Brillouin light scattering microscopy reveals that this turnover coincides with the emergence of an SOT-driven auto-oscillation mode localized beneath the gate, whose frequency continuously redshifts with increasing gate current, characteristic of large-amplitude nonlinear dynamics, and with a suppression of the propagating magnon population away from the gate. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the observed nonmonotonic gate response only when an amplitude-dependent effective damping is included, indicating that nonlinear losses, rather than saturation of spin injection, limit the degree of magnon modulation. Our results show that SOT compensation of magnon damping is ultimately limited by nonlinear damping attributed to auto-oscillations, providing a framework for understanding the limits of magnon current modulation in magnetic insulators.
authors: Lerato Takana, Katya Mikhailova, Charles Zheng, Sauviz Alaei, Xiangcheng Liu, Junwei Tong, Kwangyul Hu, Michael Flatté, Xiaoqin Li, Yuri Suzuki

articles.title: Temperature and Thickness Dependent Spin Current Transmission through Epitaxial Antiferromagnetic α-Fe2O3
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antiferromagnetic insulator α-Fe2O3 is a potential medium for coherent motion of spin waves over relatively large distances, allowing non-dissipative transfer of information between circuit elements. However, the structural defects and temperature dependent spin reorientations in this oxide impact the propagation. Understanding how the magnetic state of an antiferromagnetic insulator affects spin-current transmission is therefore important for elucidating the mechanisms governing spin transport. Here, we report spin-current transmission through epitaxial α-Fe2O3 thin films sandwiched between Permalloy and Pt. Using spin pumping and inverse spin Hall effect, we observe a finite symmetric dc voltage across the Pt layer over the temperature range 1.6 to 300 K for alpha-Fe2O3 thicknesses of 0, 30, 40, and 100 nm. The symmetric voltage coefficient Ks exhibits two approximately linear temperature regimes, separated by a characteristic temperature T* whose value depends on the thickness of the α-Fe2O3 layer. Further, the dc magnetization measurements on some of the samples suggest that the T* is correlated with the spin reorientation transition (Morin transition) in α-Fe2O3. Interestingly, a significantly larger magnitude of dKs/dT is noted below the characteristic temperature T*. The observed thickness and temperature dependent spin-current transmission indicates a sensitivity to the magnetic state of the insulating hematite layer.
authors: Koushik Prabhakara, Rajeev Nepal, Subhashree Chatterjee, Rabindra Basnet, Ezana Negusse, Ramesh C Budhani

articles.title: Scaling of entanglement with distance between subsystems: detection of phase transitions in the t'-π-flux model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The system-size scaling of bipartite entanglement can be used to detect phase transitions. We develop a related approach for strongly correlated electron models where large density matrices or large system size scaling are inaccessible. To this end, we demonstrate that phase transitions of various kinds are signaled by a sharp signature in the first- or second-order logarithmic derivatives of the negativity measuring entanglement between small clusters at varying distances. Crucially, we show how to mitigate the effect of quantum Monte Carlo noise at large distances when computing the negativity. Our focus is on the t'-π-flux Hubbard model using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations. It has the particular advantage of showing three distinct phase transitions in a single model: semimetal to band insulator, semimetal to antiferromagnetic Mott insulator, and a magnetic order-disorder transition belonging to the Gaussian, Gross-Neveu, and O(3) Wilson-Fisher universality classes, respectively.
authors: Maksim Ulybyshev, Gergő Roósz, Gabriele Bellomia, Karsten Held, Fakher Assaad, Frederic Bippus

articles.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering. We develop an analytical theory for a conventional semiconductor coupled to a gapped d-wave altermagnet and demonstrate that virtual tunneling transfers the altermagnetic spin splitting to the semiconductor. Crucially, the induced nonrelativistic and relativistic spin splittings exhibit qualitatively different dependences on band alignment. Virtual processes involving the valence and conduction bands of the altermagnet can reinforce the altermagnetic splitting while contributing with opposite signs to the interfacial Rashba coupling. Consequently, electrostatic tuning can access a regime in which the Rashba splitting vanishes while a sizable d-wave spin splitting persists. Exact diagonalization of the full heterostructure model confirms the analytical theory and establishes the robustness of this mechanism beyond the perturbative regime. Our results identify altermagnetic proximity as a route for engineering nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states in established semiconductor platforms, providing a general strategy for disentangling magnetic and relativistic spin interactions in quantum heterostructures.

articles.title: Sampling the XY model with an attention-based neural network
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The architecture is combined with physics-informed ingredients: locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities. The resulting sampler significantly outperforms existing neural samplers. We train the model on lattices up to 96×96, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.
authors: Piotr Białas, Christian D. Morales, Tomasz Stebel, Dawid Zapolski

articles.title: Anti-synchronized collective rotation in magnetic colloidal particles under rotating magnetic fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collective synchronization is a common response of interacting magnetic particles subjected to rotating external fields. Here we demonstrate a distinct nonequilibrium state in a two-dimensional cluster of magnetic colloidal particles in which the ordered crystalline core rotates, on average, opposite to the direction of the applied rotating magnetic field, while the defect-rich outer region continues to rotate with the drive. We term this state anti-synchronized collective rotation. By combining structural, spectral, bond-resolved, and layer-resolved torque analyses, we show that anti-synchronization is associated with a broader defect-rich interface, enhanced and dynamically heterogeneous bond deformation, and a reorganization of torque transmission between the surface and the crystalline interior. In the synchronized state, steric torques compensate the opposing dipolar contribution in the outer core, maintaining a positive net interaction torque. In the anti-synchronized state this compensation becomes insufficient, producing a negative net torque in theouter core and enabling core-surface rotational decoupling. Increasing the driving frequency restores coherent rotation through a transition characterized by competing positive- and negative-angular-velocity populations and hysteresis, consistent with a discontinuous, first-order-like dynamical transition. These results demonstrate how deformation and spatial redistribution of interaction torques can generate counter-rotating collective states in driven colloidal matter.
authors: Adithya Bharath, A. V. Anil Kumar

articles.title: Orbital Angular Momentum Currents and Textures in a Multiorbital Double Helix
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The microscopic origin of chirality induced spin selectivity (CISS) in biomolecular structures has traditionally been discussed in terms of spin orbit coupling and spin angular momentum. However, orbital angular momentum (OAM) is increasingly recognized as a more direct electronic response to molecular chirality. A helical hopping network built only from s orbitals can support an itinerant orbital moment and an orbital Edelstein response, but such a basis has no local atomic OAM and therefore omits the complementary contribution arising from coherence among active p orbitals. Here we construct a six-band multiorbital double helix model parameterized by characteristic B form DNA geometry and hopping scales. The model incorporates major minor groove asymmetry, an axial base pair offset representing stagger, and compositional inequivalence between the two strands, providing structural control parameters with which the orbital response can be tuned. Inter strand hybridization generates a full three component atomic OAM texture in the corotating local helical frame, including a radial component absent in the corresponding single helix model. We separately evaluate the itinerant OAM using the Bloch wave packet formulation of orbital magnetization and identify an additional inter-strand circulation channel unique to the double-helix connectivity. The resulting atomic and itinerant responses have distinct microscopic origins, magnitudes, and temperature dependences, establishing a multiorbital framework for geometry controlled angular momentum generation and transport in chiral molecular conductors.
authors: Danny Cordova, Edwin Vásconez, Ernesto Medina

articles.title: Ionic switching between supermagnetic states
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supermagnetic states are typically set during synthesis. Changing and retaining these states requires sustained external stimulus. Without resynthesis or continued stimulus, we show, for the first time, a reversible magneto-ionic switching between superferromagnetic (SFM) and superspin-glass (SSG) states using room-temperature Li-ion transport. We utilize the incomplete lithiation of NiO into nanoscale Ni and Li2O to switch between the states. Lithiation generates a fragmented nano-Ni network that strengthens dipolar interactions and promotes SFM order with stronger memory and higher room-temperature moments. Delithiation partially regenerates NiO and drives the system into an SSG state with higher low-temperature coercivity and sharper temperature-selective memory. The interconversion between SFM and SSG persists at all measured subsequent lithiation-delithiation cycles, creating a general framework for supermagnetic switching.
authors: Sumaiyatul Ahsan, Yin-Ju Yen, Andrew H. Comstock, Tanya A. Balandin, Jason D. Azoulay, Jamie H. Warner, Dario A. Arena, Faisal M. Alamgir

articles.title: Automated end-station at the soft X-ray beamline featuring robotic air-to-ultrahigh-vacuum sample transfer, scanning probe spectroscopy, and machine learning analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Driven by the growing integration of artificial intelligence and robotics in experimental science, we redefine the execution of user experiments at synchrotron soft X-ray beamlines by developing a highly automated end-station that can be operated without on-site staff. Installed at beamline BL08U of NanoTerasu, the system comprises four chamber units and two robots that automatically transfer samples from ambient air to an ultrahigh vacuum measurement stage for spectroscopic evaluations, before returning them to their original locations post-measurement. Soft X-ray absorption spectra are automatically acquired once programmed by scanning the micro-focused beam over the designated sample area, followed by automated evaluation using machine learning techniques such as principal-component analysis, multidimensional scaling, t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, and uniform manifold approximation and projection. The high-throughput data are systematically accumulated in the database for remote user examination. This unstaffed end-station provides efficient beamtime for users and allows beamline scientists/technicians to pursue more human and creative endeavors.
authors: Keita Hiromori, Masashige Miyamoto, Masafumi Horio, Takeru Nakashima, Yasunobu Ando, Masato Kotsugi, Iwao Matsuda

articles.title: Exploring Quantum Phase Transitions Beyond Landau Theory on a Quantum Processor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22482v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct continuous quantum phase transitions between phases that break distinct symmetries challenge the conventional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm and provide a framework for deconfined quantum criticality. Here, we investigate a Landau-forbidden ferromagnetic-to-valence-bond-solid (FM-VBS) transition in a frustrated one-dimensional spin chain using superconducting quantum processors. Combining matrix-product-state-assisted circuit preparation with quantum-hardware measurements, we resolve the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic correlations and the redistribution of competing-order fluctuations across the transition. Distance-resolved correlations and finite-size analyses reveal signatures consistent with critical behavior. We further extend our investigation to nonequilibrium dynamics, directly preparing dimerized states and tracking the evolution of VBS order and joint FM-VBS fluctuations under local unitary interactions. Our results establish a versatile quantum-hardware framework for probing competing orders, critical correlations, and many-body dynamics beyond conventional Landau theory.
authors: Ruizhe Shen, Yin Zhong, Ching Hua Lee

articles.title: A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22548v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, Ting-Chun Lin, Ryan Thorngren

articles.title: Electrochemical Molecular Dynamics within the Finite-Field Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electrochemical processes at charged interfaces lie at the heart of modern technologies and their continued improvement depends on insights into the relevant atomistic processes. However, the necessary tools to impose constant-voltage conditions in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations typically directly target the electrode charge, making their extension to methods that go beyond an empirical description of metals more cumbersome. In this work, we propose an MD protocol to realize a thermodynamic ensemble in which voltage control is attained, but which is formulated purely within the framework of finite-field simulations in 3D periodic boundary conditions. We show a derivation and implementation of such a control device, which we coin an electrostat, in the ELECTRODE package within LAMMPS. Our simulations systematically benchmark the derived theory against other established approaches, for example, showing its equivalence to a potentiostat, and quantify the importance of properly accounting for ensemble fluctuations. We find that for systems of several thousands of atoms, one obtains the same equilibrium properties with the electrostat as with a simpler constant-field simulation. The difference between the two methods only manifests itself at smaller length scales, thereby establishing practical limits for the inclusion of voltage fluctuations in atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems. The strength of this framework also lies in its simplicity of extension to first-principles ab initio and reactive machine-learning potentials.
authors: Krystof Brezina, Ludwig Ahrens-Iwers, Mariana Rossi

articles.title: A GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for Generative Rheology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present GINNGER (GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for GEnerative Rheology), a framework for discovering thermodynamically admissible constitutive equations from microstructural flow data. Unlike existing approaches that learn constitutive operators, GINNGER reformulates constitutive discovery as the learning of the underlying thermodynamic generators from which constitutive equations emerge. Embedding the GENERIC formalism into the learning process restricts the search to constitutive models that satisfy the first and second laws of thermodynamics by construction, eliminating the need to prescribe phenomenological constitutive equations a priori. A second conceptual advance is a spectral formulation of constitutive discovery in the intrinsic eigenspace of the polymer conformation tensor. This provides a kinematics-independent thermodynamic state space in which the thermodynamic generators depend only on the instantaneous microstructural state, while flow kinematics acts solely as an external driver transporting the system through this space. Consequently, data from shear, extensional, and mixed flows contribute to the discovery of a single constitutive model that generalizes across deformation protocols and flow geometries. By learning thermodynamic generators rather than high-dimensional constitutive operators, GINNGER substantially reduces the complexity of the discovery problem while preserving thermodynamic consistency, material objectivity, and physical interpretability by construction. The framework is validated using high-fidelity simulations, accurately reconstructing constitutive behavior and predicting complex flow fields across previously unseen geometries. GINNGER establishes a new paradigm for constitutive discovery by combining generative, spectral, and thermodynamically grounded learning within a unified framework for data-driven modeling of complex fluids.
authors: Imanol García de Beristain, David Nieto Simavilla, Marco Ellero

articles.title: Sub-Landau levels in two-dimensional electron system in magnetic field
articles.abstract: arXiv:2406.06212v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study two interacting electrons in a two-dimensional system under a strong magnetic field and show that their numerically exact solutions organize into a set of em sub-Landau levels characterized by relative angular momentum quantum number m. These sub-levels define correlation-resolved subspaces of the Landau-level Hilbert space, while retaining the full degeneracy associated with center-of-mass motion. Within this structure, the accessible states in each correlation channel are effectively reduced, leading to a natural organization of guiding-center states consistent with a fractional occupancy. We further analyze the role of electron correlation, Zeeman splitting, and disorder in stabilizing spin-polarized electron-pair states. Building on the two-electron states, we construct a class of many-electron trial wavefunctions based on correlated electron pairs with fixed m, which encode short-range correlations through the vanishing of the pair wavefunction at small separation. Our results establish a direct connection between exact two-body physics and the organization of correlated many-electron states in the lowest Landau level, providing a microscopic perspective on how relative angular momentum structures can underpin the emergence of correlated phases in quantum Hall systems.

articles.title: Towards decoding the structure of water-magnetite interface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2410.12717v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The molecular structure of water at iron-oxide interfaces is determined by the protonation state, orientation and population of interfacial OH species. These microscopic features can be decoded by combining surface-specific vibrational spectroscopy with reactive and accurate molecular dynamics simulations. In this way, it could be possible to connect the measured nonlinear optical response to specific molecular configurations at the magnetite-water interface, resolving the interfacial water structure. We investigated magnetite films in contact with liquid water at neutral and alkaline pH using phase-resolved sum-frequency generation (SFG) spectroscopy in the OH/OD stretching region and Fresnel correction of the optical response. In parallel, neural-network-potential molecular dynamics simulations were used to model the water-magnetite interface and identify interfacial water species, quantify their orientations, hydrogen-bonding environments and lifetimes, and compute species resolved SFG spectra. The combined analysis assigns distinct spectral features to dissociated surface OH groups, hydroxyls and water molecules adsorbed on octahedral iron sites, water bound at dissociation sites and water molecules above tetrahedral rows. The simulations reveal a reactive interfacial hydroxyl network with nanosecond-scale rearrangements and strong species-dependent hydrogen bonding. Experimentally, the SFG spectra show pronounced pH dependence, consistent with changes in surface charge and hydroxylation. A systematic difference between measured and computed SFG spectra indicates that the assumed surface model of magnetite does not fully represent the aqueous interface. This discrepancy provides a molecular constraint for improved models of magnetite-water interfaces and highlights SFG spectroscopy/ML-MD comparison as a valuable route to resolving oxide-water interfacial structures.
authors: Salvatore Romano, Harsharan Kaur, Pablo Montero de Hijes, Moritz Zelenka, Moritz Eder, Min-Ju Choi, Yingge Du, Gareth S. Parkinson, Yair Litman, Ellen H. G. Backus, Christoph Dellago

articles.title: Electron--phonon matrix elements from eigenvalue projection within the projector augmented-wave method
articles.abstract: arXiv:2503.11013v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a finite-displacement approach to electron--phonon matrix elements that requires only eigenvalues and wave functions from the displaced calculations, for both norm-conserving pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave (PAW) method. Extending the eigenvalue-projectability approach, previously formulated for norm-conserving pseudopotentials, we reconstruct the displaced Hamiltonian from the displaced eigenvalues and from overlaps evaluated in the PAW metric of each displaced structure. Analytic terms constructed from the PAW dataset then yield the all-electron matrix element, without derivatives of the local potential or of the PAW strengths. The approach therefore applies in principle to any electronic-structure method available in PAW. To reduce the supercell cost, we combine it with nondiagonal supercells that sample the Brillouin zone equivalently to the primitive cell and recover the full matrix elements by crystal symmetry. Implemented in the ARES-EPC code, the method reproduces matrix elements from density-functional perturbation theory and from VASP+phelel for seven materials with mean absolute errors below 0.5 meV. Nondiagonal supercells reproduce the diagonal-supercell results to the same accuracy and reduce the cost of the displaced calculations by up to a factor of 23.
authors: Qian Wang, Yu Xie, Yanming Ma

articles.title: Parasitic Two-Level Systems in Merged-Element Transmon Qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.22593v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In conventional transmon qubits, decoherence is dominated by a large number of parasitic two-level systems (TLS) residing at the edges of its large area coplanar shunt capacitor and junction leads. Avoiding these defects by improvements in design, fabrication and materials proved to be a significant challenge that so far led to limited progress. The merged-element transmon qubit (''mergemon''), a recently proposed paradigm shift in transmon design, attempts to address these issues by engineering the Josephson junction to act as its own shunt capacitor. With its energy mostly confined within the junctions, efforts required to improve qubit coherence can be concentrated on the junction barrier, a potentially easier to control interface compared to exposed circuit areas. Incorporating an additional aluminium deposition and oxidation into the in-situ bandaged Niemeyer-Dolan technique, we were able to fabricate flux-tunable mergemon qubits achieving mean T₁ relaxation times of up to 130μ s (Q approx 3.3 × 10⁶). TLS spectroscopy under applied strain and electric fields, together with systematic design variations, revealed that even for mergemon qubits - despite their significantly reduced footprint and increased junction barrier volume - careful design considerations are still essential to avoid coherence limitations due to surface loss.
authors: Etienne Daum, Benedikt Berlitz, Steffen Deck, Alexey V. Ustinov, Jürgen Lisenfeld

articles.title: Magnetic-field-free parity-protected qubit based on a narrow altermagnet Josephson junction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.18145v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnets provide a new route to engineer superconducting circuits without magnetic fields. We theoretically study the Andreev bound state (ABS) spectrum of a finite-width altrmagnet-based Josephson junction and show how the d-wave altermagnetic symmetry and geometric confinement shape its low-energy excitations. We find a clear distinction between the two d-wave symmetries: dₓ^₂₋y^₂ order produces spin splitting, whereas dₓy order preserves spin degeneracy and exhibits splitting of the ABS spectrum induced by intermode hybridization. Leveraging these novel features, we propose applying a transverse electric field to tune the system and realize a magnetic-field-free, parity-protected superconducting qubit that we call altermon.

articles.title: Orbitally Tuned Composite-Fermion Pairing Transitions in Bilayer Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.21383v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The effective interaction between composite fermions, set entirely by the Coulomb potential and the underlying electronic Landau level orbitals, can stabilize exotic fractional quantum Hall states. In particular, half-filled Landau levels with different orbital character can host either metallic or paired phases of composite fermions. Here, we leverage experimental control over the orbital composition to realize a composite-fermion pairing transition in the first excited Landau level of bilayer graphene. Transport measurements at filling factors ν = 9/2 and 11/2 reveal conductive states giving way to well-developed plateaus with increasing displacement fields. These states are insensitive to an in-plane magnetic field, indicating single-component ground states and thus pointing at non-Abelian orders. Our numerical study, based on displacement-field-dependent Landau-level wave functions, supports the orbital origin of the pairing transition and suggests Moore-Read or anti-Pfaffian ground states.
authors: Ravi Kumar, Tomer Firon, André Haug, Misha Yutushui, Alon Ner Gaon, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, David F. Mross, Yuval Ronen

articles.title: Light-Induced Even-Parity Unidirectionally Polarized Spin Splitting in Coplanar Antiferromagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.03358v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When a coplanar antiferromagnet (AFM) with xy-plane magnetic moments exhibits a spin-split band structure and unidirectional spin polarization along z, the spin polarization is forced to be an odd function of momentum by the fundamental symmetry [barC₂z|T]. Coplanar AFMs displaying such odd-parity, unidirectionally polarized spin splittings are known as odd-parity magnets. In this work, we propose the realization of their missing even-parity counterparts. We begin by deriving the symmetry conditions required for an even-parity, out-of-plane spin splitting. We then show that irradiating a spin-degenerate coplanar AFM with circularly polarized light lifts the [barC₂z|T] constraint, dynamically generating this even-parity state. Specifically, the light-induced unidirectionally polarized spin splitting exhibits a d-wave texture in momentum space, akin to that of a d-wave altermagnet. We prove this texture's robustness against spin canting and propose time-, spin- and angle-resolved photoemission photocurrent as a direct probe. Our work demonstrates that optical driving can generate novel spin-split phases in coplanar AFMs, thereby diversifying the landscape of materials exhibiting distinct spin splittings.
authors: Di Zhu, Dongling Liu, Zheng-Yang Zhuang, Zhigang Wu, Zhongbo Yan

articles.title: Tissue shape from cell-scale active tensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.14467v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Connecting cell and tissue mechanics is a fundamental challenge in the physics of morphogenesis. Conventional elasticity theory is generally inapplicable: cytoskeletal turnover precludes a fixed reference state, and the dominant forces are generated actively, independently of strain. Here, we study epithelia in quasi-static force balance between intracellular pressure and active interfacial tensions. The theory starts from a prescribed set of active tensions, represented as a Maxwell-Cremona tension triangulation dual to the cell tiling. This geometric formulation brings to bear the mathematics of discrete conformal geometry. Using generalized Voronoi diagrams, we construct the mechanically balanced cell tiling resulting from the given tensions and compute the tissue-scale stress. Conceptually, we treat cell interfaces as force dipoles whose embedding in physical space -the cell tiling- is determined by force balance. The tensions define an effective reference state in which the macroscopic stress vanishes as pressures and tensions cancel locally. Deformations from this reference result in macroscopic stress, constituting an emergent form of elasticity. Adiabatic tension dynamics change the reference shape. Thus, rather than fluidizing, tissues can deform -or "morph"-, while resisting external forces like a solid. We also define a conformal-geometric representation of cell network topology, remodeled by plastic cell rearrangement. We make experimentally testable predictions, notably that macroscopic stress is independent of local tension anisotropy. Overall, the unified description of emergent elasticity and plastic flow in epithelia is a step towards a theory of morphogenesis that puts active forces first and reflects the differences between inert and biological matter. Our framework also applies to 2D fluid foams and to frictionless granular media via a mechanical duality.
authors: Nikolas H. Claussen, Fridtjof Brauns, Boris I. Shraiman

articles.title: From Atomistic Impurity Landscapes to Two-Level-System Distributions and Microwave Loss: Hydrogen-Induced Losses in Nb₂O₅₋δ and Ta₂O₅₋δ
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.17194v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a first-principles-guided framework for predicting statistical TLS distributions from mobile impurities in disordered materials. Machine-learned interatomic potentials, with DFT and minimum-action-path validation, connect impurity landscapes to tunnel-splitting and asymmetry distributions, TLS densities, and dielectric loss. Applied to amorphous Nb₂O₅₋δ and Ta₂O₅₋δ, the framework implicates interstitial hydrogen as a source of microwave loss. Loss tangents match Nb-pentoxide measurements at inferred H concentrations, while weaker H uptake in Ta reproduces the Nb/Ta TLS contrast.
authors: Cristóbal Méndez, Sarvesh Chaudhari, Tomás A. Arias

articles.title: Thermal Conductivity and Temperature-Induced Band Gap Renormalization in Crystalline and Amorphous Ga₂O₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.29484v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) and electron-phonon interactions in crystalline and amorphous gallium oxide are herein determined by coupling a machine-learned interatomic potential, namely the moment tensor potential (MTP) model, to first-principles calculations. Crystalline β-Ga₂O₃ exhibits a substantial band gap renormalization (BGR) of sim0.45 eV at 700 K, with sim0.2 eV caused by zero-point BGR. The computed temperature dependence of BGR induced by classical nuclear motion in β-Ga₂O₃ is stronger than that in amorphous Ga₂O₃, with the difference in BGR reaching sim0.18 eV at 900 K. Thermal transport calculations reveal that the LTC of amorphous Ga₂O₃ remains near 0.9 Wḑot m⁻¹ḑotK⁻¹ for temperatures between 300 K and 700 K, which is approximately an order of magnitude lower than that of crystalline β-Ga₂O₃. Overall, the presented framework provides a computationally tractable and reliable route for predicting properties of semiconductors (both crystalline and amorphous) under operating conditions relevant to microelectronics and optoelectronics.
authors: Rustam Arabov, Jiaxuan Li, Xiaotong Chen, Nikita Rybin, Alexander Shapeev

articles.title: Level statistics of the disordered Haldane-Shastry model with 1/r^α interaction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.14695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding how the interaction range and various types of disorder affect the level statistics of many-body quantum systems, leading to the emergence of many-body localization (MBL), is a challenging open frontier. We study the level statistics of a variant of the spin-1/2 Haldane-Shastry model with 1/rα interactions, where α≥0 parametrizes the range of the interactions, in the presence of position disorder and/or random magnetic fields. We find that neither position disorder nor random magnetic fields alone yields pristine Poisson statistics in this system; however, Poisson statistics emerge in their combined presence, suggesting the emergence of MBL when both types of disorder coexist. Interestingly, once random magnetic fields break the SU(2) symmetry, the strength of the position disorder, δ, appears to play an important role, as evidenced by an approximate scaling collapse of the disorder-averaged gap ratios that is parametrized in terms of a single parameter, α δ.
authors: Vengatesan Ganapathy, Pranay Patil, Ajit C. Balram

articles.title: Perspective: Quantum Computing on Magnetic Racetrack
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.19304v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic domain walls have long been pursued as carriers of classical information for storage and processing. With the ability to create, control, and probe domain walls at the nanoscale, they are recently recognized as an ideal platform for studying macroscopic quantum effects and provide a natural blueprint for building scalable quantum computing architectures. In particular, the experimentally demonstrated high mobility of domain walls makes them not only suitable as stationary qubits but also as flying qubits, which may offer advantages over currently explored quantum computing platforms. In this Perspective, we outline our current understanding of the essential ingredients and key requirements for realizing universal quantum computation based on magnetic domain walls. We highlight promising concrete material platforms and identify the experiments that are still needed to advance this concept. We also discuss the potential challenges and point to new opportunities in this emerging research direction at the interface between magnetism and quantum information science.
authors: Ji Zou, Jelena Klinovaja, Daniel Loss

articles.title: Spatial statistics for screening molecular structures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.17147v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dominant paradigm in computational materials discovery relies on heavily parameterized deep architectures, including message-passing graph networks and equivariant models, that require millions of DFT-labeled training structures and produce non-convex latent representations that complicate continuous optimization for inverse design. These architectures are impractical in data-scarce regimes, which is the typical case in molecular screening, and exhibit well-documented limitations in capturing chemically disordered configurations and chiral geometries. This review presents feature engineering based on spatial statistics as a physically rigorous and immediately deployable alternative. Molecular structures are encoded as voxelized scalar fields, and two-point auto- and cross-correlations are evaluated deterministically via Fast Fourier Transforms, explicitly transferring the burden of spatial pattern recognition from the learning algorithm to a closed-form, physics-informed operation. Principal component analysis of the resulting correlation maps yields low-dimensional, strictly convex representations that support lean neural networks (<100k trainable parameters) and non-parametric surrogate models, achieving sub-2% prediction error with as few as 10 training samples. Demonstrated across periodic crystals, chemically disordered high-entropy alloys, and non-periodic organic molecules, this framework enables Bayesian active learning and zero-shot extrapolation on commodity hardware, which current large-scale architectures cannot replicate at equivalent data budgets.

articles.title: Mass-imbalanced two-dimensional Bose-Fermi mixtures with boson-fermion pairing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.14338v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze a two-dimensional Bose-Fermi mixture at zero temperature in the presence of a tunable Bose-Fermi attraction. We adopt a diagrammatic T-matrix approach and study the behavior of several thermodynamic quantities for the two species as functions of density, mass ratio, and coupling strength. These include the chemical potentials, the boson momentum distribution function, the condensate density, and Tan's contact parameter. We analytically demonstrate that the present T-matrix formalism recovers the correct second-order perturbative expansion of the chemical potentials in the weak-coupling regime, and test it numerically. The near-universal behavior of the condensate fraction already found in prior work for the mass-balanced case is confirmed for different masses and becomes even more accurate when the boson mass is large. The mass imbalance emerges as an additional control parameter that qualitatively affects the bosonic momentum distribution. In particular, we found that it can be used to allow for the experimental observation of a peculiar peak in the boson momentum distribution at finite momentum.
authors: Cristiano Luigi Kosman Chiarappa, Pietro Bovini, Pierbiagio Pieri

articles.title: Fully gapped superconductivity in magic-angle graphene Cooper-pair islands
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.14685v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The mechanism behind superconductivity in magic-angle graphene systems remains an open question. Recent tunnelling and superfluid stiffness measurements have suggested a nodal superconducting gap, but these probes are typically applied to large-area devices, where twist-angle inhomogeneity and disorder can hinder resolving the intrinsic superconducting spectrum. Here we introduce quantum dots in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and access a regime where gate-tunable superconductivity competes with strong Coulomb repulsion upon adding an additional carrier to the island. The islands exhibit 2e-periodic Coulomb blockade, revealing a well-defined quasiparticle gap in the island spectrum, inconsistent with the presence of nodes in the order parameter. Within the same device, we also realize coupled superconducting islands and proximitized quantum dots, establishing a monolithic platform for hybrid dot devices. Our results point to a nodeless quasiparticle gap in moiré graphene and demonstrate the potential of mesoscopic hybrid structures to probe their correlated phases.
authors: Alexandra Mestre-Torà, Marta Perego, Clara Galante Agero, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Thomas Ihn, Klaus Ensslin, Artem O. Denisov

articles.title: Temporal Interference from Topological Transitions in Monitored Quantum Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.27045v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum interference is conventionally associated with the coherent superposition of alternative paths. We uncover a temporal form of interference in repeatedly monitored quantum systems, appearing directly as fringes in the stochastic first-detection-time distribution. This temporal interference becomes remarkably long lived near a class of topological transitions at which a pair of dark states emerges in Hilbert space. Close to such transitions, the corresponding quasi-dark modes dominate the late-time dynamics and interfere coherently, producing pronounced temporal fringes whose decay becomes arbitrarily slow upon approaching the transition. We identify the symmetry conditions underlying this mechanism and relate the fringe frequency to the energy spectrum of the Hamiltonian. Our results reveal how the interplay of quantum superposition, topological transitions, and dark-state formation generates long-lived temporal interference in monitored quantum dynamics.
authors: Qingyuan Wang, Ruoyu Yin, Eli Barkai

articles.title: Negative thermal expansion, lattice dynamics, and complex magnetism in TbFeO₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.00469v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a temperature-dependent investigation of orthoferrite TbFeO₃ using x-ray diffraction, DC magnetization, and Raman scattering, complemented by room-temperature x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. X-ray diffraction reveals negative thermal expansion over 5-300 K, with a small but systematic increase in unit-cell volume upon cooling in the absence of any structural phase transition. Raman scattering measurements identify the Raman-active phonon modes and show clear deviations from the conventional Klemens anharmonic decay model, particularly in phonon frequencies, indicating the presence of spin-phonon coupling. Two modes of A_g and B₁g symmetry exhibit a crossover from Gaussian-dominated line shapes at low temperatures to mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian profiles at higher temperatures, reflecting a transition from inhomogeneous broadening to lifetime-driven dynamics. High-energy Raman spectra reveal two-magnon excitations associated with the Fe sublattice, consistent with linear spin-wave theory, whose spectral weight shows only weak temperature dependence. In addition, a broad Raman mode emerging below sim 175 K exhibits an order-parameter-like temperature evolution and coincides with the onset of phonon anomalies, while no corresponding strong anomaly is observed in the two-magnon response. Taken together, these results establish TbFeO₃ as a system with pronounced interplay among lattice dynamics, spin correlations, and emergent local magnetic-lattice anomalies.
authors: Shubham Farswan, Reshma Kumawat, Dipankar Sarkar, Deeksha Singh, Md. Atif Hasan, Devajyoti Mukherjee, Kaushik Sen

articles.title: Blinking membrane patterns induced by protein binding/unbinding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.13016v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nonequilibrium membrane pattern formation is studied using meshless membrane simulation. Bound proteins are considered to have two states that generate different membrane spontaneous curvatures. Protein binding and unbinding occur cyclically owing to chemical potential differences, as an off-lattice active Potts model. It is found that this cyclic binding/unbinding can induce blinking domains, with oscillating size: convex domains of the proteins with a higher spontaneous curvature grow, and subsequently, the proteins change to the other state with a lower spontaneous curvature, resulting in domain shrinkage. These processes repeat. In thermal equilibrium, hexagonal convex domains are formed by the competition between bending and surface tension energies, so that they are stably formed only under positive surface tension. However, blinking domains can form even in tensionless membranes.

articles.title: Landau theory and exchange instabilities in Mn₅Si₃: A case against strain-induced altermagnetism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.13483v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thin-film Mn₅Si₃ is a prominent altermagnetic candidate owing to its metallicity, demonstrated anisotropic anomalous transport, and proposed d-wave exchange splitting that could enable spin-polarized transport. Its postulated altermagnetic structure has zero propagation vector, unlike the bulk collinear antiferromagnetic AFM2 phase, which orders at the M star. We analyze both phases using Landau theory, first-principles paramagnetic-instability calculations, and Monte Carlo simulations. AFM2 appears in Landau theory as a symmetry-protected inversion-even, permutation-odd mode at a single arm of the M star. At Γ, the same intracell pattern belongs to the collinear sector of an E₂g order parameter; both phases require higher-order terms for their selection. Disordered-local-moment calculations identify the leading exchange instability at M, and the resulting classical Heisenberg model orders at the bulk experimental temperature scale into the orthogonal 3M phase favored by single-site entropy. Magnetostructural coupling to E₂g deformations favors single-M AFM2 ordering. The estimated homogeneous-strain contribution to the relevant quartic coefficient is about a quarter of the competing entropic term near the bulk transition, while internal E₂g relaxations are expected to provide additional stabilization. The Γ-point E₂g mode, whose Landau theory contains the altermagnetic sector, is substantially weaker and further suppressed by epitaxial strain comparable to that reported for Mn₅Si₃/Si(111) films exhibiting anomalous transport. The same strain reduces the leading magnetic exchange scale. These results explain the bulk M-point instability but strongly disfavor relocating the propagation vector from M to Γ in a moderately strained bulklike Mn₅Si₃ film, leaving the identity of the Hall-active phase unresolved.

articles.title: No source-free exchange-correlation magnetic fields in non-collinear spin-density functional theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.01533v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The source-free condition, nablaḑotBₓc=0, where Bₓc=δ Eₓc/δm is the exchange-correlation (xc) magnetic field of non-collinear spin-density functional theory (SDFT) and m the magnetization, is widely believed to be exact. Recent studies report that projecting the field of a parent functional onto its source-free part improves the predicted magnetic moments. We show that the condition violates the global spin-rotation symmetry of Eₓc and therefore cannot be exact. A source-free field is exact only in a transverse theory whose xc functional differs from Eₓc and is itself not invariant under spin rotations. We examine a source-free (SoF) construction, an exchange-correlation energy given by a parent SDFT functional evaluated at the transverse magnetization mₚₑᵣₚ. Its field is divergence-free, remains a functional derivative and exerts local torques, but still, it breaks global spin-rotation symmetry. With the LSDA as parent we examine the ȩMn2 molecule. The SoF and the locally collinear (LoC) LSDA both give too short a bond and too large a bond energy, but SoF finds a broken-symmetry antiferromagnetic solution, consistent with the experimentally observed ¹Σ⁺g ground state, with a coupling of the right sign and roughly the right size, while LoC finds a high-spin ¹¹Πᵤ ferromagnet and the wrong sign. The broken symmetry of SoF, however, produces severe errors in directional properties: a rigid spin rotation of the magnetization changes the energy by about 1,eV, in a weak uniform field the magnetization points perpendicular to the field instead of antiparallel to it, and the molecule develops a spurious magnetic anisotropy.

articles.title: Angular compliance, not amplitude, governs the dielectric response of BaTiO3
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.07219v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Soft-mode theory specifies a frequency, not what a local polar unit does. What real-space motion underlies the dielectric response of BaTiO3 therefore remains unclear. Using electric-field-induced molecular dynamics with a machine-learning force field, we show that the permittivity tracks the field-induced angular redistribution of local Ti-O off-centering, not its magnitude. Temperature and biaxial strain modify the local structure through different microscopic routes, yet both dielectric responses collapse onto a common relation with the same orientational descriptor, providing a real-space counterpart to soft-mode behavior.
authors: Ryotaro Sahashi, Po-Yen Chen, Teruyasu Mizoguchi

articles.title: Chiral Valence-Bond Solid and Chiral Triplons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.12856v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a chiral valence-bond solid (VBS) in which spin-singlet bond order itself spontaneously acquires handedness without magnetic order. Using a spin-lattice model on the diamond lattice, we demonstrate two enantiomorphic VBS states. In the presence of anisotropic spin interactions, this emergent handedness is inherited by chiral triplons with spin-split bands and spin textures that reverse between the two enantiomers. These textures generate a temperature-gradient-induced net spin response whose sign is set by the VBS handedness. The imaginary off-diagonal components of the dynamical spin structure factor encode the triplon polarization and change sign between the two enantiomers, enabling direct detection of chiral triplons and the selected handedness by polarized inelastic neutron scattering. Our results establish a direct connection between spontaneous chirality and magnetic excitations, opening avenues for exploring the interplay between quantum magnetism and chiral physics.

articles.title: ZStar: A unified toolkit for polarization, Born effective charges, dielectric and piezoelectric responses, and infrared and Raman spectra
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.16802v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Born effective charge (BEC) tensors link atomic displacements to polarization, thereby connecting lattice vibrations with dielectric response and infrared activity. We present ZStar, an open-source Python toolkit that automates calculations of polarization, BEC, phonons, static and frequency-dependent dielectric response, and infrared and Raman spectra. ZStar supports bulk crystals, two-dimensional materials, one-dimensional structures, and molecules through an integrated workflow for input preparation, execution, and response analysis. Berry-phase polarization and real-space dipoles describe responses along periodic and open directions, respectively. Its unified, symmetry-adapted finite-displacement framework jointly determines BEC and zone-center force constants from the same calculations, improving computational efficiency while preserving numerical accuracy. Strain-response calculations further provide proper piezoelectric coefficients and their internal-relaxation contributions for bulk crystals. In the ABACUS+PYATB route, electronic Hamiltonian data are reused to obtain Raman response without additional self-consistent calculations. Native response implementations from VASP and CP2K are also integrated. Matched infrared/Raman benchmarks against the implemented separate workflows achieve speedups of up to 8.4. An accompanying agent skill provides an agent-friendly interface for workflow integration. ZStar therefore offers an efficient and automated route for exploring polarization, BEC, dielectric and piezoelectric responses, and vibrational spectra across different material dimensionalities.
authors: Xudong Zhu, Junhong Li, Gan Jin, Zheng Guan, Meng Zhang, Lixin He

articles.title: Electrified Metal-Water Interfaces at Constant Potential: Data-Efficient Transfer Learning for Machine-Learning-Based Molecular Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.19338v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Simulating electrified metal-water interfaces with explicit solvent under constant potential is essential for understanding electrochemical processes, yet remains prohibitively expensive with ab initio methods. We present TRECI, a data-efficient workflow for constructing machine learning force-fields (ML-FFs) that achieve ab initio-level accuracy in electronically grand-canonical molecular dynamics. By leveraging transfer learning from general-purpose and domain-specific models, TRECI enables stable and accurate simulations across a wide potential range using a reduced number of reference configurations. This efficiency allows the use of high-level meta-GGA functionals and rigorous surface-electrification schemes. Applied to Cu(111)-water, models trained on just one thousand configurations yield accurate molecular dynamics simulations, capturing bias-dependent solvent restructuring effects not previously reported. TRECI offers a general strategy for characterising diverse materials and interfacial chemistries, significantly lowering the cost of realistic constant-potential simulations and expanding access to quantitative electrochemical modelling.
authors: Michele Giovanni Bianchi, Michele Re Fiorentin, Francesca Risplendi, Candido Fabrizio Pirri, Michele Parrinello, Luigi Bonati, Giancarlo Cicero
