articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model's own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at 92-100% of positions, but not which position comes next. Based on this observation, we introduce Speculating Positions Order Trajectory (SPOT), which learns to predict this order. A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state. On the verification side, our analysis shows that prior block-diffusion verification approaches either assume T=0 or a sequential proposal interface. To support tree-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared-Gumbel-noise coupling approaches. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at T=0 and T=1. In addition, we show that the learned drafter transfers across models, demonstrating successful transfer across six different DLMs. Project page: https://eliezer318.github.io/SPOT-dLLM/
authors: Eliezer Shlomi, Eliron Rahimi, Avi Mendelson, Chaim Baskin

articles.title: Initiating Removal from Operational Symptoms in Federated Vehicular Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Connected vehicles train a driving model through federated learning (FL) and drive with it, so a faulty contribution often surfaces only as a delayed symptom on the road. Federated unlearning (FU) assumes that a removal request names what to forget. A symptom names no vehicle or round, and aggregation has already spread its cause across the fleet. We propose n̆derlineAggregation-n̆derlineTime n̆derlineOperational-evidence n̆derlineNeutralization of n̆derlineEffects (method{}), which makes unlearning a term of the FL aggregation rule. method{} projects everyday driving errors and reported symptoms onto a subspace spanned by recent global increments. It propagates the surviving effect of every contribution with curvature estimated from these increments and scores all contributions in one backward pass. A two-tier correction suppresses suspected effects in every round and eliminates confirmed ones after a one-round probe. We prove that backward scoring matches forward scoring and that the elimination is exact when training is flat outside the subspace. On three driving datasets, method{} leaves 43% to 61% less residual harm than the strongest baseline in eight of nine settings while staying within 0.36 points of full retraining in utility.
authors: Zihao Ding, Jun Huang, Qiang Duan

articles.title: Spectral Limits of Polynomial Graph Filters on the Long-Range Ising Model Benchmark
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Long-Range Ising Model benchmark (LRIM) guarantees long-range dependence by construction: each label is the node's spin times the spin field convolved with a power-law coupling, so any model's distance from the target is measurable. We prove that a readout whose filter is a polynomial in the adjacency, the linear core of isotropic message passing and spectral graph networks, leaves an error floor that no degree lowers, because the target varies along a level set of the spectrum on which every such filter is constant. Computed exactly, the floor and the best filter of each degree predict two spectral networks adapted from published architectures to within a tenth of a decade. A filter escapes the floor only if it weighs separately the offsets the adjacency lumps together, and must still resolve the coupling across the whole lattice. A strided filter of about fifty coefficients does both: fitted to the training labels, its test error is 52 times below the best published network's. A dilated convolutional network beats the best published result at 256 nodes, matches it at 1,024, and gives the first in-domain results at the three larger sizes, while a Fourier neural operator with its standard modes falls further behind as the lattice grows. At its standard budget the dilated network stays two to four orders of magnitude short of a larger strided filter fitted to the labels. The analysis carries over to the benchmark's second coupling.

articles.title: Structural Affinity: An Algorithm for Coherent Cage-Based Shape Design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cage-based deformation (CBD) parametrises 3D geometry through a small set of control handles, effectively enabling a variety of tasks from animation and interactive modelling to tool-based co-design, neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic shape optimization. Many optimization approaches relying on CBD employ regularisation strategies to reduce the distortion of the deformed mesh by encouraging smooth, regular cage deformations. These techniques offer soft guidance to an optimization algorithm towards desirable deformations, but compete with the task objective rather than changing the deformation parameterization itself. In this work we introduce Structural Affinity for CBD, an explicit regularisation method which enables smooth deformations through control cages by exploiting a two-cage structure to couple cage-handle motion directly. Structural Affinity precomputes an affinity matrix using mean-value coordinates, binding the inner control-cage to a coarser outer-cage. This matrix defines how much a cage handle displacement propagates to neighbouring handles which substantially decreases and often eliminates cage self-intersections, reduces mesh distortion, and adds linear overhead at deformation time. Across robotic control--morphology co-design, source-to-target neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic wing shape optimization, Structural Affinity produces more regular deformations and substantially reduces reliance on hand-designed structural loss terms. We report consistent gains on three complementary diagnostics: the cotangent Laplacian, a proxy for surface smoothness; cage distortion, capturing whether control handles move coherently; and surface roughness, which measures undesirable oscillation in wing geometry.
authors: Aviraj Newatia, Shengan Yang, Hantao Zhong, Rika Antonova

articles.title: HiPredict: Predicting the missing HiRISE RED4 spectral channel with machine learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE) onboard the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) acquires imagery of Mars at 25--30 cm/pixel, supporting studies of martian geology, climate history, and landing-site characterization. Its 14-detector focal plane assembly includes several overlapping detectors that enable the acquisition of three-channel colour-infrared images, which are important for identifying compositional variations and studying active surface processes. In 2023, a detector in the center of the focal plane assembly (RED4) began failing intermittently, creating a gap in acquired imagery and reducing the instrument's colour-imaging capability by half. The HiRISE processing pipeline provides a synthetic red (SYN4) channel obtained by linearly scaling the co-located infrared (IR10) channel. However, this approach cannot capture observed non-linear relationships between the colour channels, limiting its accuracy and applicability. Here, we present HiPredict, a machine-learning framework that reconstructs RED4 from co-located IR10 and blue-green (BG12) imagery, neighbouring red-channel observations, and acquisition metadata. The model employs a U-Net architecture to learn non-linear spatiotemporal-spectral relationships between these inputs and is trained on 81,717 training samples, representing 13,625 observations. Evaluated on 23,348 test samples, representing 3,892 pre-failure observations, HiPredict reconstructs RED4 with a Normalised Mean Absolute Error of 1.1%, substantially outperforming SYN4 (3.1%). The reconstructed products improve colour image recovery and more closely represent features of interest such as icy craters, stratigraphy exposed along ridge crests and chloride deposits. We release HiPredict as an open software tool. This work demonstrates the potential of machine learning to mitigate data loss as planetary missions age and naturally degrade.
authors: Ardan Suphi, Ben Moseley, Gareth S Collins, Valentin T Bickel, Vidhya G Rangarajan

articles.title: A Topological Signature of Learning under Noisy Labels
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How does noisy supervision change the representations learned by a neural network? Training accuracy measures agreement with training labels but provides little information about representation geometry. We use persistent homology to track loop structure across distance thresholds in neural activations. Experiments span image classification, text classification, and modular arithmetic. On a fixed CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 training probe, equally sized clean-label and corrupted-label subsets show no detectable persistence difference at epoch 10, whereas corrupted-label subsets have higher persistence at epoch 50. The contrast survives uniform-scale controls, even though predictions match the assigned noisy labels for only 7-11% of corrupted probe examples at that checkpoint. Normalisation preserves the crossover between clean and noisy training trajectories on CIFAR-10/ResNet-18, whereas CIFAR-100/ResNet-18 shows no crossover under any of the five evaluated constructions. In a separate noise-rate calibration comparison across five pipelines, mean activation norm achieves a higher mean in-sample R2 than raw persistence (0.936 versus 0.908). These findings show that noisy supervision leaves a measurable geometric signature even when agreement with corrupted labels is low. Comparing persistence under scale controls with label-fitting measurements offers a way to study how representations respond to label corruption beyond what training accuracy reveals.
authors: Zhongtian Sun, Fan Mo, Prayag Tiwari, Kelin Xia

articles.title: Explainable Machine Learning Analysis of Temperature Effects on Mechanical Strength of Fiber-Reinforced High-Performance Concrete
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting the compressive strength of fiber-reinforced high-performance concrete subjected to temperature exposure is challenging because to the intricate interdependencies of mixture composition, fiber properties, curing conditions, and temperature. A data-driven framework to predict compressive strength utilizing 1,204 experimental records containing a diverse array of material designs and exposure situations. This study evaluates eight machine-learning models and demonstrate that ensemble approaches routinely surpass individual learners. Both gradient boosting and extreme gradient boosting exhibit superior performance on unseen data, each attaining a R² of 0.903. Gradient boosting produces the minimal root mean square error (6.67 MPa), whereas extreme gradient boosting achieves the lowest mean absolute error (3.97 MPa) and mean absolute percentage error (10.60%). The models are further interpreted utilizing Shapley additive explanations and partial dependence analysis, which reveal temperature as the primary factor influencing compressive strength, succeeded by fine aggregate, superplasticizer, cement content, water-to-binder ratio, and water content. Strength diminishes significantly with rising temperature, albeit the extent of deterioration is contingent upon the specific combination design. The best performing models are subsequently implemented in a Python-based graphical user interface for expedited prediction. Our findings offer a precise and comprehensible methodology for evaluating temperature-dependent compressive strength and facilitate the practical, data-driven design of fiber-reinforced high-performance concrete.
authors: Jagaran Chakma, Zhiguang Zhou, Badhan Chakma, Priyanta Chakma

articles.title: How language model agents reshape price competition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.21711v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Repeated Bertrand competition is a stringent benchmark for algorithmic pricing: in homogeneous-goods markets, standard learning procedures typically select the stage-game Nash outcome with prices near marginal cost. We show that LLM pricing agents can escape this benchmark, depending on deployment decisions. LLMs outperform standard online learners through faster adaptation, but this advantage largely disappears against full-information learners. An extracted surrogate algorithm illustrates how LLMs in specific deployments profit from regularly undercutting slower learners. Agents that post one price every period from raw market histories that include rival prices can sustain supracompetitive regimes in self-play. Agents that periodically emit probability distributions from summarized histories of their own profits instead move toward the competitive region in self-play. Markets mixing these interfaces can generate dynamic regimes in which LLMs establish a high-price anchor and regularly undercut it to capture demand. These regimes can keep both competitors' prices above marginal cost. Deployment choices shape these outcomes, shifting the focus from stationary equilibria to dynamic pricing regimes.
authors: Martin Bichler, Philip Hierhager, Kassian Köck, Fabian Pieroth

articles.title: Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a promising approach for simulating open quantum systems, yet their expressive power and trainability remain poorly understood. We propose a variational framework for solving Lindblad master equations by minimizing a residual cost function using a compositional ansatz obtained by combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit. The density matrix is represented through a purification on an enlarged Hilbert space, ensuring positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace by construction, while all gradients are evaluated exactly via the parameter-shift rule. Beyond the algorithmic formulation, we derive an upper bound for the covering number of the proposed compositional model and compare it with that of purely quantum neural networks. Our analysis shows that the classical parametrization enlarges the effective hypothesis class while providing finer control over its complexity, thereby establishing a theoretical connection between expressivity, covering numbers, effective dimension, and the barren plateau phenomenon. Numerical experiments validate both the accuracy of the proposed method for representative Lindblad master equations and the theoretical predictions regarding gradient concentration. These results provide a unified variational and theoretical framework for the simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics using compositional quantum machine learning models.
authors: Rafael Florencio Díaz, Julio Guerrero García, Elvira Romera Gutiérrez

articles.title: Shape-Aware Neural Time Fields for Rigid-Body Motion and Manipulation Planning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rigid-body motion planning is fundamental to robotic transport and manipulation, where both object position and orientation determine whether a body can move through cluttered environments. This coupling makes planning chal- lenging because translation and rotation can be constrained very differently by surrounding geometry. We propose Shape- Aware Neural Time Fields, a physics-informed neural motion planning framework that learns a reusable travel-time, or cost- to-go, representation for rigid-body motion while explicitly accounting for these distinct geometric restrictions. The learned field captures local motion difficulty in translation and rotation and is paired with a sampling-based planner that balances progress toward the goal with the cost of reaching nearby poses. We evaluate the framework across 2D and 3D rigid- body planning tasks and non-prehensile manipulation through object pushing in diverse environments. Results show substantial improvements in planning success and inference efficiency over physics-informed neural planning baselines, while remaining competitive with classical sampling-based planners at significantly lower planning times. Ablation studies further validate the contributions of both the learned representation and the proposed planning strategy. Finally, closed-loop pushing experiments under execution deviations and external disturbances demonstrate that fast replanning enables reactive and adaptive task execution.
authors: Yanming Zhou, Yuchen Liu, Ahmed H. Qureshi

articles.title: Causal Edit Serialization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated. Causal Edit Serialization (CES) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream. Special pointer tokens are paired with predicted source addresses, allowing insertion, deletion, replacement, copying and movement to be localized explicitly. A lightweight localization head and dual-index rotary position encoding support both address prediction and conditioning on previously emitted pointers, while retaining a standard causal attention mask. A pretraining procedure combines ordinary language modeling with serialized repairs derived from random corruptions, model-generated edits and repeated text. Across model scales and editing baselines, CES models demonstrate complete applied edits with modestly higher clean-text bits per byte than clean autoregressive models. Supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training provide a grammatical-error-correction proof of concept, producing more beneficial than harmful changes under reference-blind model judging. Correct repair programs also improve subsequent text prediction while the original context and its cached states are retained. CES provides a common interface for generation and localized revision, with potential extensions to iterative refinement and additional pointer-addressed transformations.

articles.title: CIIR - Class-Indexed Interface Representation Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal learning commonly assumes paired or synchronized observations, yet independently collected datasets rarely provide such correspondence. We introduce CIIR, a modular encoder--decoder framework that connects heterogeneous datasets through a class-indexed address space while preserving each dataset's native input format and output module. A known local index selects address k, and an input-dependent 128-dimensional address representation Zₖ₍ₓ₎ is written to that address. To demonstrate CIIR, we learn this address space from handwritten digits, clothing images, spoken-digit spectrograms, and hand signs without synchronized or instance-matched samples. Newly trained label-free receivers recover the requested addresses with 94.7% macro-average Address Realization Accuracy. We then attach the unseen SVHN dataset after freezing the base address space and train only lightweight adapters, achieving 90.2% MNIST>SVHN and 82.3% SVHN>MNIST end-to-end Address Transfer Accuracy without target-side decoder labels. To demonstrate generalizability of CIIR, we reuse the ten addresses as code elements in collision-free arithmetic and hierarchical address codes for all 100 CIFAR-100 classes and evaluate direct arithmetic-code realization through the existing receivers. These results establish CIIR as a compact interface for modular cross-dataset communication and post-hoc dataset attachment without exhaustive paired multimodal supervision.

articles.title: Learning angles for quantum approximate optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23296v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and its variants are leading algorithms to help solve challenging combinatorial optimization problems. QAOA maps these problems to Ising Hamiltonians such that their ground state is the desired solution. Candidate solutions are then drawn from a variational quantum circuit. The performance of QAOA hinges on a set of variational angles. However, finding good angles is an instance-specific and computationally expensive non-convex classical optimization task. Here, we learn the mapping from the problem instance to high-quality QAOA angles. Our learned models replace the per-instance optimization, that we call the solver, with a single forward pass that is several orders of magnitude faster than the solver with a near identical quality. Our models further generalize to unseen topologies such as Barabási-Albert and 2D grid graphs. Experiments on quantum hardware confirm that QAOA samples with angles produced by our open-source models are indistinguishable from solver angles. Crucially, models sensitive to the topology of the problem instance increase the quality of the QAOA angles. Our work amortizes a major bottleneck in QAOA by an up-front data generation and training cost. Importantly, this cost can be amortized over time in settings where many similar problems are optimized on a regular basis, as is often the case in applications for industry.
authors: Johannes Jakubik, Isabelle Wittmann, Zaheed Gaffoor, Gciniwe Simphiwe Baloyi, Craig Mahlasi, Etienne Vos, Thomas Brunschwiler, Daniel J. Egger

articles.title: Learning without relearning physical symmetry: an SO(3)-equivariant convolutional network (CNN) on the sphere
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many of the most important datasets in the physical sciences live natively on the sphere, and these data often carry no preferred position or orientation. Using methods that do not reflect this symmetry leads to far higher simulation requirements, which can be catastrophic for scientific analyses (forcing reliance on cheap, imperfect models that bias results). We present a novel spherical implementation of a gauge equivariant mesh architecture that is specifically designed for the Hierarchical Equal Area isoLatitude Pixelization (healpix{}) of the sphere. The SO(3)-equivariant convolution is built from steerable filters, parallel transport and spin-weighted features. The architecture supplies the exact symmetry, so the network does not spend training data learning it. The convolution operations are constructed to give provably exact equivariance, given a band-limit. Our full CNNs can achieve SO(3)-invariance error at per-cent-level and lower, which is controlled through well-understood hyperparameters. On benchmarks, our technique gives the most accurate dense gradient regression and competitive cosmic microwave background foreground removal and denoising. The improved simulation efficiency matters most in simulation-based inference (SBI), where high-fidelity simulations are expensive and neural compressors require large training sets, so a fixed budget forces analyses with less accurate simulators. In cosmology lensing SBI, our technique yields the tightest posteriors at matched simulation count. This approach is a novel method that will enable new convolutional neural network analyses, including generative and inference tasks, for processes and data on the sphere.
authors: Joshua Williamson, Niall Jeffrey, Lorne Whiteway

articles.title: Adversarial Attack on Deep Learning Based Network Intrusion Detection Systems: An Empirical Analysis across Datasets and Features
articles.abstract: The use of deep learning (DL) based classifiers as detection engines in network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) has been shown to be effective; nevertheless, these models remain vulnerable to adversarial evasion attacks that undermine their effectiveness in security-critical applications. In this work, we present a cross-dataset study on the adversarial vulnerability of a DNN-based NIDS classifier with the KDD Cup 1999 and CICIDS2017 traffic datasets collected at different time periods and featuring distinct sets of extracted features. For each dataset, we train and evaluate a dedicated DNN classifier against three white-box attacks, Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM), Basic Iterative Method (BIM), and Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) with random restarts, with five perturbation budgets ϵ in 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3. While the classifiers achieve high accuracy (94.4% and 97.8%) on the KDD Cup 1999 and CICIDS2017 datasets, respectively, they suffer from severe accuracy drop (to 5.6% and 2.3%, respectively) with relative drops of 94.1% and 97.7%, respectively) when exposed to the strongest perturbation (PGD, ϵ = 0.3). Moreover, confusion matrix analysis reveals that the degradation is not the result of chance predictions but the result of systematic misclassification due to the shift in the decision boundary induced by the adversarial perturbations, with a substantial number of samples changing their predicted class label. Furthermore, we propose a Feature Vulnerability Index (FVI) to characterize the vulnerability of each input feature with respect to the amount of adversarial perturbation required across different attacks and perturbation budgets. The analysis reveals that CICIDS2017 data features related to timing and packet size statistics such as Flow Packets/s, Fwd IAT Max, and Packet Length Variance exhibit high vulnerability, whereas features representing the volume of network flows show significantly less vulnerability. These results suggest that adversarial vulnerability could be a property of the learned decision surface of the DNN-based NIDS classifier rather than being dataset-specific. The findings suggest that feature-level adversarial robustness should be carefully considered in the deployment of DL-based NIDS in critical security scenarios.

articles.title: Fungi dominate microbial necromass while bacteria dominate living biomass in tea plantation soils
articles.abstract: Background and Aims: Fungal and bacterial contributions to soil organic carbon (SOC) depend on both biomass production and the fate of their residues, so fungal–bacterial dominance in living communities may differ from that in accumulated necromass. We examined biomass–necromass relationships and their associations with SOC quantity and chemical composition in strongly acidic tea plantation soils. Methods: Soils (0–30 cm) were sampled from four Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze varieties cultivated for approximately 19 years. We measured SOC and phospholipid fatty acids (PLFAs), estimated necromass C from amino sugars, and characterized SOC chemistry using solid-state ¹³C nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Results: Soils planted with ‘Fuding Dabaicha’ (FD) had the highest SOC content and stock and the highest alkyl C/O-alkyl C ratio. Bacteria accounted for 61–67% of total PLFAs and fungal markers for only 9–10%, whereas fungal residues represented approximately 89–93% of estimated microbial necromass C (MNC). MNC accounted for approximately 45.4–71.2% of SOC, whereas lignin-phenol-derived C (PDC) accounted for 3.6–7.3%. Total, fungal, and bacterial PLFAs were positively associated with their corresponding necromass C pools across plots. Redundancy analysis was significant, with SOC and microbial necromass oriented toward positive RDA1 scores and PDC, O-alkyl C, and lignin acid-to-aldehyde ratios toward negative scores. Conclusion: Living microbial biomass and accumulated necromass were positively related in quantity but strongly contrasted in bacterial–fungal composition under acidic tea plantation conditions. This contrast highlights post-mortem processing and residue preservation as links between contemporary microbial communities and SOC pools.

articles.title: Exploring the Synergy between Structural Stability and Functional Properties of FrXH₃ (X = Sc, Ti, and V) Hydride Perovskites for Hydrogen Storage
articles.abstract: With the current energy crisis, environmental challenges, and the urgent demand for sustainable energy solution, has gained significant consideration in perovskite hydrides because of their compositionality flexibility and tunable physicochemical characteristics. In this study, DFT based first-principles calculations are employed to investigate the hydrogen storage performance along with structural, electronic, magnetic, elastic, optical, and thermodynamic properties of FrXH3 (X = Sc, Ti, V) perovskite hydrides. The optimized structural parameters along with negative formation energies from − 2516.15 to -3190.70 confirm phase stability, while the calculated elastic constants (C11, C12, and C44) meet the Born stability criteria, ensuring mechanical stability for all compounds. Derived mechanical parameters, such as bulk modulus (B), shear modulus (G), Voigt shear modulus (Gv), Reuss shear modulus (GR), and anisotropy factor (A), also show systematic trends in stiffness, ductility and anisotropy: FrVH3 > FrScH3 > FrTiH3. The gravimetric hydrogen storage capacities of FrScH3, FrTiH3, and FrVH3 are calculated as 1.116 wt % hydrogen, 1.104 wt % hydrogen, and 1.092 wt % hydrogen, respectively. The electronic properties confirm the metallic character of the series, and DOS is dominated by the d-states, with smaller contributions from s- and p-states. The transition from the non-magnetic behavior of FrScH3 to the spin-polarized states of FrTiH3 and FrVH3, originates from significant exchange-induced splitting of d-states, with minor p-state and negligible s-state contributions. Optically, high absorption, high conductivity and strong interband transitions observed in the low-energy region. Moreover, the thermodynamic parameters suggest that the lattice stiffness and thermal stability are enhanced for the case of FrTiH3 compared to FrVH3, whereas the lattice behavior is intermediate for FrScH3 and the anharmonicity is almost constant. Among the studied compounds, FrScH3 is potentially suitable for hydrogen storage applications because of its structural stability, lattice flexibility, and thermal behavior.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Flow Reconstruction from Sparse 3D Lagrangian Particle Tracking: A Systematic Comparison with FlowFit and Binning
articles.abstract: Reconstructing continuous Eulerian flow fields from sparse three-dimensional Lagrangian Particle Tracking (LPT) data remains challenging, particularly for velocity gradients and pressure. In this study, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are systematically evaluated over a wide range of particle concentrations and compared with polynomial Binning and FlowFit using identical TrackFit-processed LPT data. Two synthetic datasets, homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) and a turbulent boundary layer (TBL), together with an experimental turbulent-boundary-layer dataset, are used to assess velocity, pressure, vorticity, acceleration, incompressibility, and flow-structure reconstruction. PINNs yields the lowest velocity and pressure errors over the investigated sparsity levels and generally shows slower degradation as particle density decreases. Although FlowFit provides exact divergence-free velocity fields and outperforms PINNs in vorticity reconstruction at several densely seeded conditions, PINNs preserves coherent flow structures more robustly over time and under sparse seeding. In the experimental case, PINNs also achieves the lowest validation acceleration error despite not using measured acceleration as a training target. A broader comparison of the PINNs approach used in this study with other flow-reconstruction methods is available in the results of the 2nd LPT and DA challenges.

articles.title: Tunable Anisotropic Heat Transport in Structurally and Chemically Modified 3D Graphene
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional graphene (3DG) networks offer a route to translate the high intrinsic thermal conductivity of graphene into macroscopic, freestanding architectures. However, heat transport in 3DG is not governed by the intrinsic conductivity of graphene alone, but by a hierarchy of pores, sheet orientation, network connectivity, and graphene-graphene junctions. Here, room-temperature cross-plane and in-plane thermal transport in pristine, compressed, welded, and doped 3DG structures is reported. Cross-plane thermal conductivity is measured using a differential 3ω method with transferable polyimide-supported metal heater lines, while in-plane thermal conductivity is obtained using a suspended four-probe electrothermal method. Mechanical compression strongly modifies the directional thermal response: cross-plane thermal conductivity decreases with densification, while in-plane transport remains comparatively enhanced, indicating that compression redistributes the graphene network into a more anisotropic, aligned architecture. Welding introduces an additional discrete thermal resistance, with increasing weld-plane numbers. Chemical modification suppresses both directions without producing the strong anisotropy amplification caused by rolling, suggesting that cross-plane heat flow remains dominated by phonon-mediated networks and junction resistance rather than electronic heat conduction. These results establish structural compression and weld-plane insertion as practical routes for programming anisotropic heat flow in freestanding 3DG.

articles.title: Milling force-induced elastic deformation modeling and physical constraint transfer prediction of thin-walled grid conical shell
articles.abstract: The thin-walled grid conical shell is affected by the coupling effect of cutting load and local weak stiffness in the process of grid milling, which easily leads to elastic tool deflection along the shell normal, resulting in the actual material removal thickness less than the theoretical cutting depth, and the wall thickness error is formed after unloading springback. This phenomenon will directly cause uneven wall thickness distribution in the component. The key difficulty lies in the coupling between the local stiffness mutation caused by the distribution of the ribs, the fluctuation of the cutting load at the tool position, and the limited real milling samples. In view of the above problems, this paper proposes a cutting force-induced tool deflection prediction method for grid conical shell milling process. Firstly, the deflection response of conical shell under normal load is analyzed based on Donnell shell theory, and the periodic “rib-skin” structure is equivalent to a stiffened conical shell with direction-dependent stiffness characteristics. The analytical relationship between cutting load, local structural stiffness and normal deflection is established. Secondly, taking the finite element simulation sample as the source domain and the real milling experiment sample as the target domain, the physical constraint transfer learning model is constructed to realize the synergy between the normal cutting force prediction and the elastic deformation analytical calculation under the condition of small samples. Finally, the proposed method is verified by finite element simulation and milling test. The results show that the method can effectively improve the accuracy and stability of the elastic deformation prediction for thin-walled grid conical shell, and can provide the manufacturing process modeling basis for the milling error prediction, process parameter optimization and deformation compensation of thin-walled stiffened curved surface components.

articles.title: Synthesis and Application of Novel Reactive Dyes for Cotton Fabric with Enhanced Properties
articles.abstract: The consumption of inorganic electrolytes in typical existing methods of reactive dyeing of cotton contributes to the chemical pollution in textile effluents and motivates the development of reactive dyes capable of producing effective salt free coloration. This study involves the development of novel azo-based reactive dyes containing a monochlorotriazine reactive group and choline-derived functionality. The dye was synthesized and investigated for salt-free dyeing of 100% cotton fabric. Ortho- and para positional dye structures were synthesized through consecutive diazotization, azo-coupling, and nucleophilic replacement reactions and applied at (0.5–4% o.w.f.) under controlled conditions of 60°C for 60 min at pH 10.8–11.2 using sodium carbonate as the alkali, without the addition of inorganic salt. Following dyeing, the fabrics were treated at 90°C with commercially available detergent and subjected to three consecutive hot washing cycles to remove unfixed dye. FTIR and UV–visible spectroscopy confirmed the characteristic functional and chromophoric features of the synthesized dyes. Dyeing considerably improved the cotton fabric from ultraviolet radiation, enhancing UPF from approximately 7 to 40 with increasing dye concentrations, meanwhile UVA and UVB blockage up to 90%. The dyed fabric demonstrated outstanding dry rubbing ≈ 4.5, good to excellent wet rubbing 4.0–4.5, and satisfactory washing fastness, aiding efficient dye absorption and fixation without addition of salt as an electrolyte in dyeing process. The ortho derivative showed comparatively better light and washing fastness, whereas the para derivative provided slightly higher UV protection. No detectable antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus was observed under the applied agar-diffusion conditions. The findings demonstrate the potential of the synthesized choline-functionalized monochlorotriazine dyes as salt-free reactive colorants for producing durable and ecofriendly and sustainable cotton textiles by removing salt consumption, providing a promising approach for reducing electrolyte use in conventional reactive dyeing.

articles.title: Cellulose microfibril interactions with water: A density functional theory study of H2O incorporation into the cellulose microfibril structure
articles.abstract: Periodic density functional theory calculations were performed on the 234432 model of primary plant cell wall cellulose microfibrils. Energy minimization calculations of dry, water external, water internal and water internal+external were carried out to explore the structure of cellulose hydration and energetics of H-bonding. Results indicate that the cellulose structure can accommodate a significant amount of H2O without disrupting the XRD-determined structure. H2O-cellulose H-bonds form in the interior that strengthen the cellulose microfibril. The external H-bonding was also analyzed to assess potential pathways for C-O-C linkage hydrolysis. The potential for D2O to diffuse into the structure and lead to H-D exchange between water and cellulose was also tested.

articles.title: Aerodynamic Effects of Localized Textured Calf Tapes in Triathlon: A Wind Tunnel Screening Investigation
articles.abstract: Cycling is the fastest discipline of long-distance triathlon, where aerodynamic drag represents the main resistive force opposing forward motion. Consequently, even small reductions in drag may translate into meaningful performance gains. This preliminary engineering investigation evaluated the aerodynamic potential of a localized textured calf tape concept and identified promising surface configurations for subsequent athlete-based validation. Wind tunnel testing was performed using a standardized rigid leg model to maximize measurement repeatability during early-stage product development. Six textured tape configurations, combining three dot widths (7, 15 and 30 mm) with two thicknesses (1 and 2 mm), were compared with an untreated control and a commercially available aerodynamic calf sleeve. Testing was conducted at air velocities of 40 and 45 km·h⁻¹ and yaw angles of 0°, 5°, 10° and 15°. Aerodynamic performance was assessed from measured drag force, estimated aerodynamic drag area, and aerodynamic power requirement. Measurement repeatability was high, with a mean coefficient of variation of 0.36%. All textured tape configurations reduced aerodynamic drag relative to the control, although the magnitude of the reduction depended on dot geometry, air velocity, and yaw angle. The 15 × 2 mm configuration demonstrated the best overall performance, producing up to an 11% reduction in estimated aerodynamic drag area and a 5.1 W reduction in aerodynamic power requirement at 45 km·h⁻¹ and 15° yaw, compared with 6.2 W for the reference calf sleeve. These findings identify promising localized surface architectures for further validation using full-body mannequins, athlete-based wind tunnel testing, and field studies.

articles.title: Chalcogenide perovskites BaTi(OS)3 with band gap in the optimal Shockley-Queisser range
articles.abstract: In the constant search for more efficient and economical alternatives to renewable energy, perovskite-based solar cells have emerged as a promising technology in the field of solar energy. Among them, chalcogenide perovskites have gained considerable attention because of their unique properties and potential to overcome some of the limitations associated with traditional solar cell materials. In this study, a perovskite compound BaTi(O 1−X S X) 3 was synthesized by sulfiding barium titanate (BaTiO 3) by heat treatment in a reactive atmosphere of CS 2 , using three different temperatures: 600, 700 and 800 • C. The structural, vibrational, and optical properties of the synthesized samples were determined as a function of the treatment temperature. Elemental analysis showed a sulfur content between 14.6 % and 20.2 %, depending on the treatment temperature. XRD showed a transition from tetragonal to hexagonal perovskite with increased sulfur concentration, recording interplanar distances of 4.069 Å, 3.366 Å and 2.453 Å in the planes (101), (110) and (201), with lattice parameters a= 6.73 Å, c= 5.793 Å and a crystallite size of 258.96 Å. IR spectroscopy identified predominant SO bonds. The UV-Vis analysis indicated a reduction in the band gap from 1.53 eV to 1.47 eV as the temperature increased.

articles.title: Preparation and Electrochemical Performance of NCM622/Carbon-Fiber-Network Composite Cathodes via Electrospinning and Carbonization
articles.abstract: LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 (NCM622) is a representative nickel-rich layered cathode material for lithium-ion batteries, but its practical performance can be limited by discontinuous electronic pathways and contact deterioration within composite electrodes. In this work, an NCM622/carbon-fiber-network composite (NCM622-C) was prepared by electrospinning followed by nitrogen-protected carbonization at 600°C. NCM622 particles were incorporated into a polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP)/ethanol spinning precursor and subsequently integrated with the PVP-derived carbon-fiber framework. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed a particle/fiber interwoven morphology, while X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed preservation of the layered alpha-NaFeO2-type NCM622 structure after carbonization. The estimated I(003)/I(104) ratio was approximately 1.80, indicating that the layered ordering was maintained. At 1 C, NCM622-C delivered initial charge and discharge capacities of about 147 and 146 mAh g− 1, respectively, with an initial Coulombic efficiency of 99.3%, compared with 143/140 mAh g− 1 and 97.9% for pristine NCM622. After 50 cycles at 1 C, NCM622-C retained about 141.6 mAh g− 1 (96.1% retention), exceeding the 129.8 mAh g− 1 (92.7%) of pristine NCM622. NCM622-C also showed higher capacities at low-to-medium rates and better capacity recovery after returning to 0.5 C. These results support electrospinning-derived carbon-fiber networking as a practical route to improve electronic connectivity and short-term capacity retention of NCM622 cathodes.

articles.title: Modulation Recognition Method with Dual-Branch Feature Fusion Based on Lightweight CNN and Dual-Attention Network
articles.abstract: Aiming at the problems of high-order MPSK/MQAM signals being easily confused, poor robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio, and incomplete coverage of modulation types in automatic modulation recognition under complex electromagnetic environments, a dual-branch feature fusion modulation recognition method based on lightweight CNN and IQ-2AttNet is proposed. First, a unified mathematical model of MPSK, MQAM, and signals without IQ components is constructed to analyze the differences in IQ characteristics of different modulation signals. Then, a dual-branch parallel architecture of “wide-coverage preliminary screening + high-precision fine recognition” is designed, where the lightweight CNN performs fast preliminary screening for 12 signal types, and IQ-2AttNet focuses on fine recognition of 6 types of core orthogonal modulation signals. Finally, confidence-weighted decision fusion is adopted to output the optimal results. Ablation experiments show that the dual-branch structure and decision fusion strategy can effectively improve recognition accuracy and generalization ability. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing typical modulation recognition models under the same conditions. Experimental results indicate that the overall recognition accuracy of the proposed method reaches 86.1% over the SNR range from − 10 dB to 25 dB. Especially over the low-SNR range from − 8 dB to 0 dB, the average recognition rate is 71.8%, which is 1.5% to 17.5% higher than the comparison models, showing strong noise robustness.

articles.title: Battery-free ambient FM backscatter nodes reaching 150 metres through digital chirp synthesis and MISO diversity reception
articles.abstract: Wireless sensors are often placed where changing a battery is costly or impractical. Powering them from harvested energy is attractive but a conventional radio spends milliwatts to generate a carrier. Ambient backscatter removes that cost by reflecting existing broadcast signals instead of creating new ones. This work turns frequency modulation (FM) broadcast stations up to 34.5 km away into free carriers for a battery-free sensor node that uses Long Range (LoRa) style chirp spread spectrum. The chirps are synthesised in the digital domain by the inter-IC sound (I2S) peripheral of a commercial microcontroller while its processor sleeps. No digital-to-analog converter or voltage-controlled oscillator is needed and a single radio-frequency switch performs the modulation. At a 1% duty cycle the node draws only 22 µW yet its packets reach 150 metres. A multiple-input single-output receiver built from low-cost software-defined radios captures the same packet reflected from many FM stations at once. Fusing these copies in the frequency domain with soft-decision decoding lowers the bit error rate. Solar harvesting and a supercapacitor power the 45 mm × 50 mm node along with its environmental sensors plus motion and magnetic sensors. The result is a practical path toward maintenance-free wireless sensing.

articles.title: Deriving the Continuous β-FPUT Model for Decayless Solar Coronal Oscillations Directly from Resistive MHD
articles.abstract: We present an analytical framework deriving the fluid-continuum β-Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou (β-FPUT) system directly from a third-order resistive magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) expansion to explain persistent, decayless transverse oscillations observed in solar coronal loops. For a continuous wave field propagating along a longitudinal magnetic field with cross-field density variations, a multi-scale expansion demonstrates that quadratic O(2) advective and Maxwell tension terms vanish identically due to out-of-plane polarization symmetry. Instead, the quadratic longitudinal ponderomotive force drives field-aligned density modulations that back-react on the primary transverse wave, yielding a cubic O(3) restoring force. In the long-wavelength limit, the governing equations reduce to a fluid-continuum Modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV) system where cross-field profile variation provides the non-linear dispersive mechanism. We prove that this internal fluid mechanism establishes stable, amplitude-dependent frequency self-focusing, which phase-locks adjacent elements and prevents phase-mixing wave attenuation without requiring external steady driving parameterizations. This framework enables macro-scale coronal seismology, providing closed-form expressions to invert observed decayless wave-packet durations to compute the unresolved cross-field density gradient scale length (Lₓ₎ and the internal volumetric filling factor (f_V) without relying on traditional emission measure or spectroscopic line-ratio diagnostics. Much like famous Enrico Fermi's historic use of macro-scale displacements to estimate complex atomic explosion yields, this framework establishes a paradigm where monitoring macroscopic oscillation durations empowers observers to extract fine-scale, otherwise unresolvable waveguide properties.

articles.title: X-rays reveal surprisingly long-lived spin waves in copper oxide
articles.abstract: Today's computer technology, based on silicon chips, is slowly reaching its physical limits. Components cannot be miniaturized indefinitely, and clock speeds cannot be increased indefinitely. At the same time, huge AI data centers are being built in many places, and these consume an immense amount of electricity. This is why scientists around the world are searching for novel materials that can replace or complement silicon technology and consume significantly less electricity.

articles.title: New monolithic ion trap opens quantum simulations to more researchers
articles.abstract: Some quantum systems are so complex that even the most powerful supercomputers struggle to simulate their behavior. One solution is quantum simulation: building a controllable quantum system in the lab and tuning it to mimic the one researchers want to understand.

articles.title: A new way to detect stabilizing properties of optical devices
articles.abstract: In optical fibers, chips and other light-guiding devices, minor defects can scatter photons and disrupt their path. A new study demonstrates a way to reveal properties which, in certain systems, help light wave behavior withstand such flaws. The method could help speed up the search for new kinds of electronics and optical technologies, and contribute to more reliable quantum devices.

articles.title: Physicists prove a long-suspected quantum speed limit for thermalization
articles.abstract: Whether we are waiting for a car windshield to defrost in winter or a warm drink to cool down, how long it takes for an object to settle into a stable, even temperature within its environment (thermal equilibrium) depends on numerous factors. These can include surface area, the material properties of an object and airflow.

articles.title: Semiclassical Analysis of Wave Dynamics via Wigner Transforms: Applications to the Quantum Harmonic, Anharmonic, and Dirac Oscillator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this Master's thesis, we give a pedagogical introduction to the semiclassical analysis of wave dynamics in single-band and multi-band systems. We show how the semiclassical evolutions of Wigner functions can approximate the dynamics of wave packet centers and wave packet deformations. Three systems of increasing complexity are considered: the quantum harmonic oscillator and the quantum anharmonic oscillator as single-band systems, and the Dirac oscillator as a two-band system. We explain the origins of the first-order semiclassical corrections (Moyal, Littlejohn-Flynn, and Berry) in the equations of motion and examine their effects on predictive accuracy. Another focus is set on the conditions for validity of the semiclassical analysis. For both the quantum anharmonic and the Dirac oscillators, a dimensionless parameter controlling the accuracy of the approximation is identified. In multi-band systems, the formalism applies only to states within a single adiabatic subspace, which, for the Dirac oscillator, corresponds to an energy branch. This motivates the construction of single-branch almost coherent states: approximately Gaussian wave packets formed by superpositions of states from a single energy branch. Their centers undergo oscillations with an aperiodic envelope. These states enable comparison between semiclassical Wigner function evolution and the commonly used Sundaram-Niu formalism. We show that semiclassical Wigner function evolution captures deformation-related dynamics, including the initial decay of oscillations, which the Sundaram-Niu formalism cannot describe by construction. Additionally, exact quantum evolution reveals partial relocalization of these single-branch almost coherent states, a phenomenon that cannot be captured by the semiclassical evolution.

articles.title: Probing nonequilibrium transport and density profiles in tilted interacting fermion chains with local reservoirs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how local particle reservoirs can probe transport and density profiles in tilted spinless fermion chains with nearest-neighbor interactions. Using finite-chain Lindblad calculations with particle injection and extraction at opposite ends, we define a threshold-dependent transmission range from the stationary current as the chain length is varied. This range decreases with increasing tilt and follows the trends of the equilibrium density-crossover width in the parameter regimes studied. Interactions can enhance transmission by compensating field-induced energy costs, whereas strongly polarized configurations suppress transport. A third, weakly coupled extraction reservoir provides a complementary spatial probe: its current is exactly proportional to the local occupation in the presence of the probe, and the normalized current approaches the unperturbed nonequilibrium density as the probe coupling vanishes. We illustrate the detection of staggered density modulations and show that bulk densities can continue to relax after boundary currents have nearly stabilized. These protocols connect current measurements to spatial transmission and density structure in driven interacting chains.
authors: Andrea Nava, N. Aucar Boidi, Reinhold Egger, Karen Hallberg, C. R. Proetto

articles.title: Anyon bound states in MoTe₂ Fractional Chern Insulators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binding anyons to optically active excitons offers a route to manipulate fractional excitations and reveal the internal spatial structure of anyons. We establish the formation of anyon bound states between a mobile dipolar exciton and an e/3 quasihole in a twisted bilayer MoTe₂ fractional Chern insulator. Using exact diagonalization of a continuum-based interacting model, we identify a regime of meV-scale binding and strong exciton-quasihole entanglement controlled by exciton mobility and the distance between the exciton and the FCI. Spatial correlations resolve a localized depletion core carrying approximately e/3 charge around the exciton, providing a real-space characterization of the bound state. Beyond its fractional charge, the quasihole exhibits a moiré-induced octupolar structure. Interlayer tunneling anisotropy strongly deforms this structure while leaving the enclosed charge nearly unchanged, linking the internal profile of the anyon to the underlying electronic quantum geometry. These findings establish conditions for robust exciton-anyon binding in moiré heterostructures and show how these composites provide access to properties of fractional excitations beyond their total charge.

articles.title: Fractional Chern insulators and composite Fermi liquids vs. charge order in twisted MoTe₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The bandstructure of twisted MoTe₂ around 3.7ⁱ̧rc consists of spin-valley locked Chern bands with a bandwidth that is smaller than the interaction scale. As such, the strongly correlated phases familiar from Landau levels can be realized: Quantum Hall states, composite Fermi liquids and charge order. These states have in common that they are all favoured by strong interactions, however changing the quantum geometry and topology of the bands as well as their bandwidth via the displacement field and twist angle tilts the balance between them. We provide a comprehensive exact diagonalization analysis of the competition between these states and in particular elucidate the nature of the charge order at fillings ν=-frac14,-frac13,-frac12,-frac23. Furthermore, we analyze the effect of band mixing by going beyond a single band per valley. This effect of band mixing is crucial for reconciling the numerical phase diagrams with experimental observations.

articles.title: Quantum-interference correction to conductivity in disordered electronic bands with non-uniform quantum geometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weak localization in two-dimensional disordered electron systems originates from constructive interference between time-reversed scattering paths, giving rise to a logarithmically divergent quantum-interference correction to the dc conductivity. This behavior is generally suppressed when time-reversal symmetry (TRS) is broken. In this study, using a band-projected framework motivated by spin- and valley-polarized rhombohedral N-layer graphene (RNG), we show that nonuniform quantum geometry can qualitatively modify quantum-interference corrections to dc transport. In particular, continuously tuning the quantum geometry can change the sign of the conductivity correction, corresponding to a crossover between localization and antilocalization tendencies. Remarkably, at special values of the parameter controlling the quantum geometry, weak-localization (WL) or weak-antilocalization (WAL) can re-emerge despite broken microscopic TRS. At these special points, the orbital structure of the Bloch states gives rise to an emergent antiunitary symmetry that protects a gapless Cooperon mode and restores the logarithmically divergent quantum-interference correction characteristic of WL or WAL. Our results establish nonuniform quantum geometry as a mechanism for controlling quantum interference and electron localization in multiorbital electronic systems.
authors: Yip Chun Wong, Asimpunya Mitra, Yong Baek Kim

articles.title: Universal Threshold Laws for Dipolar Evaporation of Molecular Fermi Gases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fermi statistics suppress the elastic collisions that rethermalize a Fermi gas during evaporative cooling, creating a fundamental low-temperature bottleneck for producing quantum degenerate gases. We show that, for shielded single-component ultracold dipolar molecular Fermi gases in the Wigner threshold regime, this bottleneck is governed by universal threshold laws fixed by the effective dimensionality of the gas. In this regime, Fermi suppression of rethermalization scales quadratically with temperature in 3D but only linearly in 2D. Consequently, the thermalization-to-loss ratio is more favorable in 2D than in 3D, and these results suggest that 2D geometries are better suited for reaching deep degeneracy. We also present ab initio close-coupling calculations that agree well with experimental measurements on Fermi degenerate gases of KRb molecules, supporting our conclusions.
authors: Kevin B. Xu, John L. Bohn, Reuben R. W. Wang

articles.title: From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.
authors: Klaus D. Jöns, Dorian A. Gangloff, Doris E. Reiter

articles.title: Universal Long-distance Tail of Particle-number Density near a Wall in Superfluids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the long-distance recovery of the particle-number density near a static, impermeable wall in a d-dimensional Galilean-invariant superfluid. Using superfluid effective field theory (EFT) on a half-space, we show that quantum phonon fluctuations produce a z⁻⁽d⁺¹⁾ tail in the smooth density profile at zero temperature, where z is the distance from the wall. The tail coefficient is fixed by the bulk equation of state and is independent of microscopic wall details. At low temperature T, the thermal length cₛ/T, with cₛ the bulk sound speed, separates the zero-temperature behavior at intermediate distances from a thermal Tz⁻d tail at larger distances for d>1. For d=1, the long-distance phonon contribution instead decays as exp(-4π Tz/cₛ₎. The EFT applies to both Bose and Fermi superfluids, including strongly interacting Fermi gases at unitarity. We estimate the normalized tail amplitude in three dimensions across the BCS--BEC crossover using experimental sound-speed data.

articles.title: Fractionalized Fermi Liquid and d-wave Superconductivity in Ba2CuO3+x
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strongly enhanced superconductivity (SC) (Tc = 73 K) in Ba2CuO3+x (BCO) challenges the longheld paradigm of the irrelevance of the dz2-like states in cuprates. Using tight-binding band structure plus dynamical mean-field theory (TB+DMFT), we find that a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FFL) is the normal state for the parameters realistic for BCO. Transport properties exhibit strange metal behavior above Tcoh~38 K, supporting a direct instability of this strange metal to SC. Irrelevance of one-fermion inter-band mixing, itself a non-trivial consequence of the FFL state, preferentially enhances two-fermion hopping processes and provides a novel route for both SC and competing excitonic order(s) arising directly from the FFL. The proposed scenario also clarifies the role of dz2 band in shaping the physical responses of BCO.
authors: M. S. Laad, S. Koley, A. Taraphder

articles.title: Inducing Extraordinary-log Criticality through a Quantum Spin Chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the emergence of extraordinary-log criticality in a quantum many-body system by coupling a spin-1/2 Heisenberg chain to a two-dimensional quantum critical Heisenberg bilayer. Under the quantum-to-classical mapping, the chain acts as a plane defect in a three-dimensional critical environment for which the extraordinary-log universality class has recently been predicted. Using large-scale sign-problem-free quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we directly probe the renormalization-group flow of the effective defect coupling through the spin stiffness. We observe the characteristic logarithmic growth with linear system size L, corresponding to a stable weak-coupling fixed point and a running coupling g(L)sim 1/łog L. Furthermore, the extracted step-scaling function quantitatively follows the universal renormalization-group flow predicted for the extraordinary-log universality class, including the leading and subleading universal coefficients. Our results establish extraordinary-log criticality in a genuine quantum many-body setting and show that its universal behavior persists despite the topological θ-term present in the low-energy field theory of the isolated spin chain.
authors: Grigorios Makris, Francesco Parisen Toldin, Stefan Wessel

articles.title: Statistics-controlled topological phases in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger ladder
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In strictly one-dimensional lattices, free fermions and hard-core bosons exhibit equivalent physical properties in many-particle systems. However, this statistical equivalence generally breaks down upon moving to higher dimensions. Our work investigates the significant effects of this difference on the topological phase transition in a minimal system lying away from one dimension: the two-leg Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) ladder. Starting in the limit of two decoupled SSH chains having opposite hopping dimerization patterns (staggered dimerization), we demonstrate that introducing inter-leg coupling drives a transition from a topological to a trivial phase for both spinless fermions and hard-core bosons. However, the topological to trivial phase transition boundary is strongly sensitive to the underlying particle statistics. We find that this intriguing effect favors a trivial phase sandwiched between the two topological phases with opposite characters for the case of hard-core bosons, resulting in a reentrant topological phase transition. In contrast, this reentrant phenomenon is absent for spinless fermions, with the topological phases being separated by a gapless line instead of an intervening trivial phase. This study demonstrates the interplay between particle statistics and topological features, revealing fundamentally different properties in an experimentally accessible set-up.
authors: Rajashri Parida, Biswajit Paul, Smitha Vishveshwara, Diptiman Sen, Tapan Mishra

articles.title: Finite-temperature phase diagram of dipolar bosons in a cylindrical setup
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temperature plays a non-trivial role in dipolar systems, being able to either induce or destroy spatial density modulations. In order to shed light into the interplay between thermal effects and quantum correlations, we employ the path integral Monte Carlo method (PIMC) to obtain the phase diagram of a system of dipolar bosons in an infinite cylindrical geometry and at finite temperatures. For a fixed total density, we vary the scattering length of the interaction and the temperature, and characterize the structure and superfluidity of the emerging phases. The PIMC method accounts for thermal effects and quantum correlations at all orders, and can be used to quantitatively estimate the superfluid fraction of the system. Remarkably, we find a regime of parameters where, starting from a supersolid, the spatial order vanishes with temperature before the superfluidity does. We also find a region of the phase diagram where the superfluid fraction displays a non-monotonous dependence with temperature. Our results extend previous descriptions, relying on Bogoliubov theory, to larger temperatures in the thermodynamic limit and illustrate how spatial modulations and superfluidity are lost as temperature is increased.
authors: Juan Sánchez-Baena, Raúl Bombín, Jordi Boronat

articles.title: Transport and thermalization under noncommuting localized constraints
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. We consider several related models: the integrable quantum Volterra model, its nonintegrable classical limit, and two cellular automata derived from the latter. Although localized constraints are often associated with lattice gauge theories, our models do not admit such an interpretation. In systems with discrete degrees of freedom, these constraints induce uniform fragmentation of the Hilbert or configuration space. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.
authors: Amir Nesturov, Attila Takács, Lenart Zadnik

articles.title: Discrete time crystals and classical logic gates in coupled open Dicke models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the dynamics of coupled discrete time crystals (DTCs) in the coupled Dicke model or Dicke dimer (DD) with dissipation. By numerically simulating the mean-field dynamics of the system, we show that coupling two DTCs decreases their oscillation amplitude following a transient relaxation period. For sufficiently strong coupling, the coupled DTCs become unstable, resulting in the system relaxing towards the normal phase (NP). We demonstrate that the relaxation time diverges near the critical coupling strength, suggesting a continuous phase transition. Using the truncated Wigner approximation (TWA), we explore how the dynamics are affected by the introduction of quantum fluctuations. We also consider a scenario in which an NP is briefly coupled to a DTC, seeding the NP to transform into a DTC that is either synchronized or anti-synchronized relative to the DTC. We investigate the robustness of this phenomenon in the presence of noise. Using these results, we propose a scheme to perform NAND and NOR operations with three DTCs by sequentially coupling the input and output sites. We identify the parameter regimes in which the logic gate architecture remains valid, and investigate how the protocol is affected by the presence of quantum fluctuations.
authors: Emmanuel D. G. U, Roy D. Jara Jr., Jayson G. Cosme

articles.title: Renormalization Group Domain Walls from Phantom Symmetries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a systematic construction of renormalization group (RG) domain walls between two-dimensional rational conformal field theories. Using phantom currents, we consider an auxiliary chiral extension linked to the folded ultraviolet--infrared theory by a topological interface. The construction of RG walls then reduces to identifying suitable automorphism-twisted Cardy states in the auxiliary theory. We find two such types of automorphisms: outer automorphisms exchanging identical current algebra factors, as in Gaiotto's construction, and continuous inner automorphisms generated by the zero modes of spin-one phantom currents. In the latter case, the RG domain walls generically admit a continuous defect conformal manifold. We further show that, when an RG flow can be orbifolded to another one, the orbifold may lift defect conformal moduli of the RG brane constructed using inner automorphisms. The two types of RG branes can then be mapped to each other via a topological interface defined by the orbifold. We demonstrate the two types of RG brane construction via various examples of flows between non-unitary minimal models, from parafermions to minimal models, and between generalized parafermions. Many physical observables of the RG walls are computed non-perturbatively, including boundary entropies and spectra, and UV--IR operator mixings. We also find interesting nontrivial boundary monodromy: a closed cycle in the defect conformal moduli space can carry an RG domain wall into other distinct non-trivial conformal interfaces.

articles.title: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23810v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) provide broadband gain, low added noise, and high dynamic range, making them attractive for applications requiring wide instantaneous bandwidth. This is crucial for amplifying multiplexed narrow band signals spread over a wide frequency range, such as qubit resonator arrays, or amplifying inherently wide band signals, such as in spectrometers or radiometers. In many cases, however, the useful bandwidth of a TWPA is limited by the production of the idler tone at an image frequency. For three-wave-mixing (3WM) TWPAs, for example, an input signal at fₛ is indistinguishable from one at fₚ - fₛ, which can produce spectral ambiguity when the input spectrum is broadband or not known in advance. We experimentally demonstrate a balanced architecture that doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth available to a 3WM TWPA by spatially separating the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler, which resolves the sideband degeneracy. The architecture consists of two amplifiers connected between a pair of 180ⁱ̧rc hybrid couplers, with the signal and pump injected and output through the sum and difference ports, respectively. Using two kinetic-inductance TWPAs, we demonstrate approximately 20 dB of signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, together with pump rejection below --20 dB and an average image rejection of approximately --15 dB over the operating band. These results establish balanced TWPAs as a practical approach to broadband parametric amplification, enabling improved contamination free bandwidth and eliminating the need for complex filtering.
authors: Nikita Klimovich, Peter K. Day, Henry G. Leduc, Boon-Kok Tan

articles.title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.

articles.title: Fast-driving spectroscopy of current-phase relationships of individual Josephson elements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.14313v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Extracting the current-phase relationship (CPR) of a single superconducting junction is challenging in practice and traditionally involves embedding the junction in a larger superconducting circuit containing SQUIDs and/or resonators. Applying ac driving to the junction has proven to be a viable and less invasive way to extract information about the few lowest harmonics of the CPR, by locating the integer and fractional Shapiro steps in the IV-curve of the driven junction. Here, we present an alternative driving-based method that allows to extract the full harmonic content of a CPR in a relatively non-invasive way, by fitting the measured critical currents of the driven junction as a function of driving power. We test our method, both using numerical simulations and in experiments, and we show that it works accurately.
authors: Maxim Tjøtta, Devashish Shah, Kanishk Modi, Marco Valentini, Rubén Seoane Souto, Georgios Katsaros, Jeroen Danon

articles.title: Exponential clustering of bipartite quantum entanglement at arbitrary temperatures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2108.12209v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Macroscopic quantum effects play central roles in the appearance of inexplicable phenomena in low-temperature quantum many-body physics. Such macroscopic quantumness is often evaluated using long-range entanglement, i.e., entanglement in the macroscopic length scale. The long-range entanglement not only characterizes the novel quantum phases but also serves as a critical resource for quantum computation. Thus, the problem that arises is under which conditions can the long-range entanglement be stable even at room temperatures. Here, we show that bi-partite long-range entanglement is unstable at arbitrary temperatures and exponentially decays with distance. Our theorem provides a no-go theorem on the existence of the long-range entanglement. The obtained results are consistent with the existing observations that long-range entanglement at non-zero temperatures can exist in topologically ordered phases, where tripartite correlations are dominant. In the derivation of our result, we introduce a quantum correlation defined by the convex roof of the standard correlation function. We establish an exponential clustering theorem for generic quantum many-body systems for such a quantum correlation at arbitrary temperatures, which yields our main result by relating quantum correlation to quantum entanglement. As a simple application of our analytical techniques, we derived a general limit on the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information and the quantum Fisher information, which will attract significant attention in the field of quantum metrology. Our work reveals novel general aspects of low-temperature quantum physics and sheds light on the characterization of long-range entanglement.

articles.title: Bottlenecks in quantum channels and finite temperature phases of matter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2412.09598v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an analog of the "bottleneck theorem," well-known for classical Markov chains, for Markovian quantum channels. In particular, we show that if two regions (subspaces) of Hilbert space are separated by a region that has very low weight in the channel's steady state, then states initialized on one side of this barrier will take a long time to relax, putting a lower bound on the mixing time in terms of an appropriately defined "quantum bottleneck ratio." Importantly, this bottleneck ratio involves not only the probabilities of the relevant subspaces, but also the size of off-diagonal matrix elements between them. For low temperature quantum many-body systems, we use the bottleneck theorem to bound the performance of any quasilocal Gibbs sampler. This leads to a new perspective on thermally stable quantum phases in terms of a decomposition of the Gibbs state into multiple components separated by bottlenecks. As a concrete application, we show rigorously that weakly perturbed commuting projector models with extensive energy barriers (which include certain classical and quantum expander codes) have exponentially large mixing times
authors: Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, Vedika Khemani

articles.title: Mean-Field Dynamics of the Bose-Hubbard Model in High Dimension
articles.abstract: arXiv:2501.05304v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Bose-Hubbard model effectively describes bosons on a lattice with on-site interactions and nearest-neighbour hopping, serving as a foundational framework for understanding strong particle interactions and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition.
