Now, researchers have shown that it is possible to come close.

articles.title: From spin wave to superconducting circuit: A one-way street for quantum information
articles.abstract: Quantum information systems could one day shape everyday life through faster computing, sharper sensing and more secure communication. A new result from the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (U. of I.) marks an important step toward enabling magnetic spins—a quantum property of matter that can be used to store and manipulate information—to play a role in the future of quantum information processing.

articles.title: Archaeometallurgical Study of a Han Dynasty Thin-Walled Bronze Basin Excavated from the Fengzhou Cemetery, Baoji, Shaanxi, China
articles.abstract: Archaeometallurgy of Han Dynasty thin-walled bronzes is a hot topic of current research and has made some achievements. But several issues remain insufficiently understood. These include alloying and production strategies, technological variation among social groups, and metal-resource circulation. This study analyze a thin-walled bronze basin excavated in Feng County, Baoji, using SEM–EDS, metallography, and MC–ICP–MS to investigate alloy composition, production techniques, and lead provenance. The basin was made from a ternary Cu–Sn–Pb alloy through casting, repeated hot forging and hammering, followed by trimming. Its thin walls were formed through combined hot forging and cold working. Lead isotope ratios suggest that the lead was derived from the Xiaoqinling region of western Henan and may have circulated through established transportation networks. Comparative analysis shows regional and social variation in alloy composition and production practices. The results indicate that Han Dynasty thin-walled bronze vessels shifted from ritual functions toward everyday use and commodity circulation, reflecting changes in production organization, social demand, and metal-resource circulation.

articles.title: Dust-ion-acoustic Flat-top Solitons and Supersolitons in dusty plasma with two superthermal electrons: Application to the Earth's Ionosphere
articles.abstract: The nonlinear propagation of dust-ion-acoustic (DIA) structures is investigated in a homogeneous, unmagnetized dusty plasma containing positive cold ions, negatively charged cold dust grains, and cold and hot superthermal electrons. The Sagdeev pseudopotential approach is employed to investigate the existence and characteristics of nonlinear electrostatic structures, including compressive and rarefactive solitary waves, double layers, flat-top solitons, and supersolitons. The negatively charged dust significantly modifies the equilibrium charge balance and nonlinear response, allowing the existence of both positive- and negative-potential supersolitons, whereas the corresponding dust-free system supports only positive-potential supersolitons in the plasma. The transition from ordinary solitons to flat-top solitons and supersolitons is associated with changes in the Sagdeev potential and the emergence of complex, wiggle-like electric-field profiles. The propagation domains are strongly affected by electron superthermality and the relative densities of the cold and hot electron populations. Increasing the spectral index generally shifts the admissible Mach-number limits toward higher values and, as the electron distributions approach the Maxwellian limit, modifies and broadens the corresponding propagation domains. The dust-free limit recovers previously reported results, confirming the consistency of the model. Furthermore, the coexistence of compressive double layers with rarefactive solitons is identified, with their distinct phase-space trajectories reflecting the difference between homoclinic and separatrix-connected nonlinear states. The results demonstrate that negatively charged dust and non-Maxwellian electrons play a crucial role in determining the polarity and nonlinear characteristics of DIA excitations in the Earth’s ionosphere dusty plasmas.

articles.title: Test-Retest Reliability of Motor Evoked Potentials Across Eight Bilateral Lower-Limb Muscles
articles.abstract: Objectives TMS is widely used to probe corticospinal excitability by eliciting MEPs in targeted muscles, with MEP characteristics such as magnitude and latency reflecting the physiological state of the pathways being stimulated. Although numerous studies have examined MEP reliability in upper extremity muscles, less is known about the reliability of this measurement across the lower extremity. We hypothesized that inter-session, test-retest reliability of MEPs recorded simultaneously from multiple lower-limb muscles, from a single TMS location, would differ by muscle, stimulation intensity, and quantification method.Materials and Methods Ten healthy participants (5 males, 5 females) completed three TMS sessions separated by one week. At each session, the stimulation hotspot was identified using a five-location virtual grid anchored at the vertex, with EMG recorded from all eight muscles of interest at each grid location; the grid location producing the largest and most consistent MEPs in the TA, the primary target muscle, was selected as the stimulation site and held constant across all three sessions. MEPs were then recorded bilaterally from the TA, soleus, rectus femoris, and biceps femoris muscles at two stimulation intensities (110% and 120% RMT). MEP size was quantified using mean rectified magnitude and peak-to-peak amplitude, and inter-session reliability was assessed using ICC. Bland-Altman analysis was used to characterize the range of measurement variability across all eight muscles.Results MEP size differed across sessions, and reliability varied by muscle, intensity, and quantification method. The highest reliability was observed in the right TA, the muscle used to establish the stimulation hotspot, using mean rectified magnitude at 120% RMT. Reliability was comparatively lower in the seven non-target muscles recorded from the same fixed stimulation site, indicating that MEP consistency was not uniform across the lower-limb musculature.Conclusions MEP reliability in the lower extremity varies by muscle, stimulation intensity, and quantification method. MEPs were most reliable in the TA, the muscle used to establish the stimulation site, while reliability was lower in the other seven muscles.

articles.title: Decoupling Steric-Dependent Adsorption Mechanisms in "Covalent-Ionic" Dual-Orthogonal Crosslinked GO/CS Hydrogels for Efficient Dye Sequestration
articles.abstract: Bulk hydrogel adsorbents show great promise in water remediation, yet overcoming the intrinsic contradiction between mechanical skeleton stability and high-density active sites remains a core challenge. Herein, a novel "covalent-ionic" dual-orthogonal crosslinking strategy based on sodium tripolyphosphate (TPP) and genipin was proposed to construct hierarchical mesoporous graphene oxide/chitosan (GO/CS) composite hydrogels. Compared to traditional highly toxic single-crosslinked systems, this strategy achieves robust spatial confinement of GO sheets while preserving abundant polar adsorption sites. By integrating comprehensive characterizations (SEM, BET, XRD, FT-IR, Raman, and XPS), the microscopic physicochemical synergistic adsorption mechanisms of the hydrogel toward planar methylene blue (MB) and bulky malachite green (MG) were systematically elucidated. The results suggest a strong steric-dependent interfacial behavior: the capture of MB primarily relies on face-to-face π-π conjugated stacking with the GO basal plane and localized charge transfer, whereas the adsorption of sterically hindered MG is dominantly driven by Coulombic electrostatic attraction and hydrogen bonding provided by deprotonated carboxyl and polar nitrogen sites. Furthermore, the hydrogel maintained over 80% of its retention capacity after five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles without macroscopic structural deterioration or GO leakage. This study offers an engineering solution to the solid-liquid separation difficulties of powdered adsorbents and establishes a theoretical paradigm for steric-dependent confined adsorption in complex polymer networks.

articles.title: Quantum calculations reveal how spin defects lose energy
articles.abstract: When light hits a tiny defect embedded in a solid material like diamond or silicon carbide, it can kick the defect's electrons into an excited state. These spin defects have the potential to be used as stable, readable qubits for quantum technologies, for example, quantum sensing. But modeling the full physics of their energetics over time—a key step in developing spin defects into new technologies—is a challenging task.

articles.title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells struggle to predict devices made from new materials. Most treat device layers as arbitrary categorical labels and represent perovskite absorbers either through featureless composition vectors or through rigid crystal graphs that require a pre-solved unit cell. As a result, they cannot generalize to unrecorded alloys or unfamiliar cell architectures. We present the Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System (V-PaSS), an architecture built around the physical continuity of perovskite solid solutions. V-PaSS represents arbitrary mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers by interpolating relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoint compounds via Vegard's law with learned bandgap bowing. For the device stack, it couples layer sequence and cell polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n) with interfacial band offsets and encodes chemical descriptions with a scientific language model. Evaluated under an institution-grouped protocol where test devices come exclusively from unseen laboratories, an untuned default configuration of V-PaSS achieves the lowest error among fourteen tested models (2.861% MAE, a 5.2% relative reduction over a gradient-boosted baseline at 3.017%, and outperforming the best tuned benchmark at 2.912%). V-PaSS pulls furthest ahead where test devices differ most from training: reducing error by 15.7-19.0% on unseen absorber alloys, by 16.1% on mixed absorbers from new laboratories, and widening its lead over the baseline by 3.6× on devices with unobserved transport layers. Combined with tree ensembles, V-PaSS sets a new state of the art across all five benchmark splits.

articles.title: Measurement-induced criticality for non-Abelian anyons: The monitored golden chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Abelian anyon chains whose interactions favor a single fusion channel host quantum critical ground states described by minimal-model conformal field theories (CFTs) protected by a topological symmetry. We show that their measurement-only counterpart, where non-commuting fusion charge measurements act locally on the anyons of a chain of L sites, provides a fundamental example of a non-unitary CFT controlling a non-Abelian learning problem. Mapping the monitored dynamics to a random tensor network, we numerically find 1/L scaling Lyapunov gaps, logarithmic entanglement scaling with the chord length, and an effective central charge in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record. The conserved topological charge sharpens with dynamical exponent z= 1 and is learnable by a decoder on an O(L) time scale. As the topological symmetry is a non-invertible symmetry of the SU(2)ₖ anyon theories, we establish the monitored golden chain (k=3) as a non-Abelian generalization of the weakly (Kramers-Wannier) self-dual quantum critical point of the toric code (k=2), and the first of a family for k≥ 3.
authors: Zhaohui Zhi, Bo Han, Romain Vasseur, Andreas W. W. Ludwig, Simon Trebst, Guo-Yi Zhu

articles.title: Non-Abelian quantum Hall states at strong Landau level mixing: finding anyons with first-principles AI
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Abelian anyons, strange particles forming the basis of fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, are predicted to emerge in fractional quantum Hall states at even-denominator filling factors. Identifying which topological order is realized has proven to be a challenging problem that requires an accurate, non-perturbative treatment of realistic Landau level mixing, which has so far been missing from theoretical studies. Here we present the first complete solution of non-Abelian quantum Hall problem that includes all electrons and all Landau levels, for spin-polarized electrons at filling factor ν = 3/2. We develop a momentum-resolved neural-network variational wave function, optimized solely on the microscopic Hamiltonian, which gives direct access to the topologically degenerate ground states. Without any physics input about the expected outcome, it discovers a degenerate ground-state manifold whose entanglement reveals anyons with quantum dimension sqrt2, the hallmark of Ising-type non-Abelian order. By directly computing the overlap with trial wave functions, we further show that Landau level mixing favors the anti-Pfaffian over other candidate states. Our results demonstrate the power of neural-network wave functions in finding and characterizing non-Abelian anyons from first principles, in regimes of strong Landau level mixing, relevant to many recent experiments.
authors: Pierre-Antoine Graham, Ahmed Abouelkomsan, Liang Fu

articles.title: Nanoscale Mapping of Strain-engineered Excitons in Monolayer WSe₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Excitons in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are highly sensitive to external stimuli, allowing control of resonance energies and lifetimes through electric and magnetic fields, heterostructures, moire potentials and mechanical strain. Observations of single-photon emission (SPE) near sample edges, wrinkles, and strained nanobubbles have motivated strain-engineering aimed at realizing localized emitters in 2D materials. The origin of these emitters remains unclear and prior studies have relied on far-field spectroscopy with strain profiles inferred separately through topography, limiting direct correlation between local strain and excitonic response. We directly probe strain-modified excitonic spectra in monolayer WSe₂ using cryogenic scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM). We compare two strain-engineering techniques, nano-indentation and patterned substrates, used to produce SPEs. At 9 K, we spatially resolve exciton resonance shifts with sub-diffraction limit resolution, simultaneously measuring near-field optical response and topography. We observe that strain transferred from nano-indentation into a deformable polymer substrate differs from that produced by draping TMDs over patterned dielectric pillars. Adhesion and tearing during plastic deformation drive a compressive exciton blueshift, while draping produces dominant tensile strain. Comparing the strain model results to the experimentally observed energy shifts shows that the nano-indentation strain is over an order of magnitude smaller than previously inferred, due to puncturing of the fragile monolayer, whereas pillar-strained devices remain intact under more modest strain. These differences suggest SPE arises from complex, strain-mediated interactions rather than simple confinement potentials, establishing s-SNOM as a powerful probe of quantum emission in strained 2D materials.
authors: Anna S. Roche, Nicholas V. Proscia, Paul D. Cunningham, Kathleen M. McCreary, Dante J. O'Hara, Hsun Jen Chuang, Cory Cress, Collin Sanborn, Samuel W. LaGasse, Jose J. Fonseca, Jeremy T. Robinson, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, John R. Schaibley, Brian J. LeRoy

articles.title: Topological superconductivity in layered d-wave altermagnetic metals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate multilayer d-wave altermagnetic metals with odd-parity helical p-wave pairing. In the minimal bilayer system, interlayer tunneling reconstructs the spin-split Fermi surfaces and generates two layer-hybridized sectors with distinct effective chemical potentials. Without Rashba spin-orbit coupling (RSOC), the emergent mirror symmetry and subsystem chiral symmetry stabilize phases with different numbers of helical Majorana edge-mode pairs and additional counterpropagating pairs, jointly characterized by the mirror Chern number and the winding numbers defined along high-symmetry lines. The combination of RSOC and the altermagnetic exchange field gaps out the helical Majorana pairs while, in a certain parameter regime, leaving another pair of counterpropagating Majorana edge modes gapless, giving rise to second-order topological phases with isolated or twofold Majorana corner modes, as well as a hybrid-order phase in which gapless Majorana edge modes coexist with Majorana corner modes. We identify a layer symmetry that elucidates the physical origin of these phases. For an arbitrary N-layer system, such a symmetry naturally arises from the interlayer-coupling matrix, allowing N-fold Majorana corner modes to emerge when all layer-hybridized sectors enter the nontrivial second-order regime. Our results establish the interplay among the layer degree of freedom, odd-parity pairing, and Fermi-surface configurations as a controllable route to engineering topological superconductivity in layered altermagnetic systems.

articles.title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for PHREEQC-Coupled Reactive Transport with Cell-Based Surface Complexation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a mass-conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes (DBS) formulation for reactive transport with cell-based surface complexation in image-based porous media, coupled to PHREEQC and implemented in GeoChemFoam, an OpenFOAM-based toolbox. Dissolved species are transported in the physical mobile-water fraction, adsorbed species are stored as conservative cell-scale surface inventories, and each reactive cell is coupled to PHREEQC. Reactive surface area is prescribed independently as a cell field, so that internal area left unresolved by segmentation of microporous phases can be represented while DBS flow and transport are retained in the resolved pore space. The implementation is verified with a test suite that isolates the coupling of transport and chemistry from the construction of reactive surface area. Aqueous and adsorbed mass balance is evaluated against a one-dimensional analytical retardation benchmark and closed-system batch calculations. The smooth-interface surface-area algorithms are tested on idealised two- and three-dimensional geometries. In a two-scale lithium micromodel, DBS reproduces fully resolved aqueous and sorbed inventories within 0.6% across Pe=0.1-10. The applications comprise Pb2+ retardation by hydrous ferric oxide coatings in a two-dimensional fracture network, competitive Mn2+/Mg2+ exchange in a three-dimensional Kelvin-cell sorbent, and Sr2+/Ca2+ exchange in Estaillades limestone. In the fracture-network and limestone cases, the formulation yields spatially resolved aqueous and adsorbed inventories even where reactive surface area is only partly resolved at the image scale. The framework therefore supports conservative surface-complexation modelling in both resolved and unresolved pore structures, with relevance to contaminant retention, selective ion capture, and radionuclide transport.
authors: Hannah P. Menke, Florian Doster, Julien Maes

articles.title: Pseudo-relativistic fermions and topological states in zinc-blende semiconductors and their heterostructures (Habilitation thesis)
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tracing my scientific path from many-body physics in semiconductor nanostructures to topological quantum matter, this Habilitation à diriger des recherches (HDR) memoir presents only part of my research since defending two PhD theses in Toulouse and Nizhny Novgorod in 2011. Focusing on pseudo-relativistic fermions and topological states in zinc-blende semiconductors and their heterostructures, it highlights my independent research program: identifying physical problems, developing predictive theories, and initiating new directions with experimentalists. The first part addresses Kane fermions in bulk HgCdTe: temperature-driven band inversion, domain-wall states, the collapse of Landau levels in crossed electric and magnetic fields, and disorder-induced topological transitions. The second examines pressure-, temperature-, and disorder-driven phase transitions in single and double HgTe quantum wells (QWs), including bilayer-graphene-like semimetals and a two-dimensional higher-order topological insulator (2D HOTI) phase beyond the minimal BHZ model. The third develops three-layer InAs/Ga(In)Sb QWs as a III-V platform for massless Dirac fermions, large-gap quantum spin Hall insulators, 2D HOTI phases, and semimetals with quadratic band touching, and discusses InAsₓSb₁₋ₓ/InAsySb₁₋y heterostructures as a promising alternative. Several of these predictions are supported by experimental observations, including quantized helical edge transport up to 60 K and the unconventional quantum Hall effect. Defended on March 25, 2026, at the University of Montpellier. Jury: Michel GOIRAN (chair and rapporteur, LNCMI-CNRS, Toulouse); Alexey KAVOKIN (rapporteur, Westlake University, Hangzhou); Robson FERREIRA (rapporteur, LPENS-CNRS, Paris); Alexei BARANOV (member, IES-CNRS, Montpellier); Benoit JOUAULT and Frédéric TEPPE (members, L2C-CNRS, Montpellier).

articles.title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped, among other results, to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two ensembles allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and free-probability methods, the generic case of independently random Hamiltonian and dissipative components requires a novel framework that combines operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging. For this ensemble, our approach preserves the underlying tensor-product structure of the Lindblad operator and derives a general equation for the spectral boundary. We characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing and explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component.
authors: Mykhailo Hontarenko, Wojciech Tarnowski, Sergey Denisov, Karol Życzkowski

articles.title: Spectral signatures of spin textures and the emergence of a pseudogap
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodic solids with strongly interacting electrons display phenomena -- from Mott localization to high-temperature superconductivity -- that escape conventional band theory. Efforts to address this unconventional physics have been typically cast in the language of Green's function theories and the associated frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies capturing strong correlations beyond the reach of mean-field theories. Here, we underscore that frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies emerge also from mean-field solutions that break translational symmetry, and that these self-energies can display the characteristic fingerprints of strong correlations for certain, physically meaningful, spatial patterns. We showcase this perspective by studying the paradigmatic case of the 2D Hubbard model. We find that already at the mean-field level the doped antiferromagnet displays, in addition to stripes, many quasi-degenerate self-consistent solutions with antiferromagnetic textures organized into antiphase domains separated by hole-rich interfaces, reminiscent of the phase-separation scenario. Remarkably, these solutions map into spectral functions that display very distinctively the phenomenology of the pseudogap, including the nodal-antinodal dichotomy of the self-energy, Fermi arcs, and a complementary Luttinger surface. The result is a conceptually simple description of such an intricate many-body state: the pseudogap emerges as the momentum-space spectral portrait of the real-space interplay between antiferromagnetic domains and the metallic interfaces, which echoes the role of spin-fluctuations identified by nonperturbative methods.
authors: Matteo Quinzi, Andrea Pintus, Tommaso Chiarotti, Massimo Capone, Nicola Marzari

articles.title: Evidence for hidden order and its potential correlation with electron-hole asymmetry in iridate superlattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hidden order refers to an order that shapes the properties of quantum materials yet remains difficult to identify. Here we report signatures of a hidden order in doped iridate superlattices through an unexpected electron-hole asymmetry in the coupling between the insulating state and the antiferromagnetic (AFM) state. While carrier doping suppresses both states, they remain coupled in the electron-doped regime but decouple in the hole-doped regime. Structural analysis rules out octahedral rotation and tilting as the dominant origin of this asymmetry. Instead, magnetic characterization reveals evidences of a hidden order that only appears in the hole-doped regime. This hidden order emerges above TN and is closely associated with the AFM state, coinciding with an exceptionally strong magnetic scattering intensity and an anomalously robust magnetic coherence. Our results highlight that hole-doped iridates can be a promising platform for exploring hidden and unconventional ordering phenomena in spin-orbit-entangled quantum materials.
authors: Zhihan Qiao, Han Zhang, Hangtian Wang, Deyang Li, Haiyang Zhang, Enyang Men, Junlei Jiang, Jingxin Chen, Yizhou Liu, Sang-Youn Park, Xiangnan Xie, MingLiang Tian, Haifeng Du, Ning Hao, Lin Hao

articles.title: Phase Stability and Anisotropic Superconductivity in Ternary M2B4C2 (M=Ca, Mg) Monolayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the phase stability, electronic structure, and superconducting properties of the two-dimensional ternary borocarbides MB₄C₂ (M = Ca, Mg) using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Ab initio molecular dynamics, phonon dispersion, and elastic constant calculations confirm that both monolayers are dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable. Electronic structure analysis reveals an intrinsic metallic nature with a multiband Fermi surface, where states near the Γ point are dominated by in-plane B-pₓ, p_y orbitals, while zone-boundary states are primarily derived from out-of-plane B-p_z orbitals. The electron-phonon coupling is determined to be łambda = 0.64 for both materials, driven by the rigid covalent B-B and B-C honeycomb networks. By solving the anisotropic Eliashberg equations, we predict that CaB₄C₂ and MgB₄C₂ are nodeless two-gap superconductors with critical temperatures (T_c) of 33.4 K and 33.8 K, respectively, at a Coulomb pseudopotential of μ = 0.10. Furthermore, the superconducting state remains robust under increased Coulomb repulsion (μ = 0.13), retaining elevated T_c values of 31.2 K and 30.9 K, respectively. These findings establish MB₄C₂ monolayers as promising candidates for nanoscale superconducting applications and enrich the family of two-dimensional multigap superconductors.
authors: Jakkapat Seeyangnok, Udomsilp Pinsook, Graeme J Ackland

articles.title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reticular chemistry allows metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to be designed from their building units, yet their synthesis remains constrained by sparse experimental data, noisy crystallization outcomes, and the absence of benchmarks for comparing active-learning strategies. While data-driven approaches such as Bayesian optimization (BO) can improve synthesis success rates, selecting appropriate optimizers beforehand for mapping MOF crystallization landscapes remains largely empirical. Here we present ActMOF, an experiment-grounded benchmark for comparing search strategies in aluminum-carboxylate MOF synthesis. ActMOF is emulated from experimentally measured microwave syntheses with each encoded condition assigned a crystallinity index calculated based on diffraction peak intensity and full width at half-maximum. By benchmarking policies guided by Gaussian processes (GP), tree ensembles and large language models (LLM), ActMOF placed the GP family among the leading policies for active learning in sparse synthesis landscapes. It then demonstrated transferability by guiding the microwave synthesis of six reticularly related aluminum MOFs. All six campaigns gave crystalline products within a fixed budget of 12 experiments each, and established a reusable testbed for AI-driven MOF synthesis.
authors: Hongrui Sheng, Shutian Liang, Reid A. Coyle, Shyam Chand Pal, Peter Walther, Bin Feng, Xinyu Ding, Zhiling Zheng

articles.title: Multiple Superconducting Phases under Pressure for Different Field Directions in UTe2
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The existence of multiple superconducting phases is a striking feature of UTe2, arising from the spin and orbital degrees of freedom and supporting a spin-triplet superconducting state. We present field-temperature phase diagrams under pressure for fields applied along the three principal crystallographic axes, as determined by AC calorimetry measurements. The pressure evolution of the multiple superconducting phases is highly anisotropic with respect to magnetic field direction, revealing rich superconducting phenomena arising from complex fluctuations.
authors: Dai Aoki, Atsushi Miyake, Ai Nakamura, Yoshiya Homma, Dexin Li, Shota Mizuno, Georg Knebel, Daniel Braithwaite, Jean-Pascal Brison, Jacques Flouquet

articles.title: Pressure engineering of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moiré superlattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. Moreover, we demonstrate efficient pressure control over the interplay between charges and both intralayer and interlayer excitons: the intralayer charge-transfer exciton becomes less sensitive to doping, likely due to reduced charge-transfer character; in contrast, the interlayer exciton exhibits enhanced exciton-charge repulsion. Our results establish hydrostatic pressure as a powerful tuning knob for engineering bosonic quasiparticles and Bose-Fermi interactions in moiré materials.
authors: Wenbing Li, Tianhao Yue, Wenjian Su, Zhexu Shan, Chen Xu, Jichen Zhou, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Liguo Ma, Yuanfeng Xu, Shiyao Zhu, Yang Gao, Yanhao Tang

articles.title: Magnetic proximity beyond the interface: Layer-sequence-dependent exchange in WSe₂/CrI₃ heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic proximity effects in transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD)/2D-magnet heterostructures are often described in terms of the magnetization of the interfacial magnetic layer. Here, we show that this picture is sufficient to describe the neutral-exciton valley splitting of the TMD, but incomplete for its hole-doped electronic structure. We study a gate-tunable van der Waals heterostructure composed of monolayer WSe₂ in direct contact with trilayer CrI₃. By combining spatially and helicity-resolved reflection-contrast spectroscopy with magnetic circular dichroism, we identify two distinct magnetic domains in the trilayer CrI₃: one with purely antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling and one with a mixed antiferromagnetic (AFM)/ferromagnetic~(FM) coupling. In both domains, the sign of the neutral-exciton valley splitting of WSe₂ switches with the magnetization reversal of the adjacent CrI₃ layer. In contrast, helicity-resolved positive-trion spectroscopy of WSe₂ reveals a qualitatively different response. While the AFM domain shows a strongly helicity-selective trion resonance, the mixed AFM/FM domain exhibits trion resonances in both helicities. This behavior disappears when all CrI₃ layers are aligned in a parallel magnetization direction. Our results demonstrate that charged excitons are sensitive to the full layer-resolved magnetic sequence of the adjacent 2D-magnet, revealing magnetic proximity beyond the interface.
authors: Natalie Kuhn, Marc Schütte, Joachim Emming, Felix Hellenkamp, Leo Dreyer, Frank Volmer, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Lutz Waldecker, Christoph Stampfer, Bernd Beschoten

articles.title: Emergent medium-range order in amorphous silicon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medium-range order (MRO) is an important feature of amorphous materials, but its nature in terms of atomic arrangement has remained elusive. Here, using large-scale machine-learning-driven atomistic simulations of amorphous silicon, we probe the MRO of this archetypal network glass. By characterizing the structure in three dimensions, we reveal that the symmetry of the atomic arrangement around a central atom shows a crossover as a function of distance. At short distances, the structure is determined by local bonding constraints, which evolve from predominantly tetrahedral environments in low-density amorphous silicon to highly coordinated and strongly disordered local environments in very-high-density amorphous silicon. At larger distances, however, distinct cubic- and octahedral-symmetry patterns emerge in the three-dimensional atomic-density distribution, despite the absence of these symmetries at shorter length scales. We find that this crossover is accompanied by a quasi-periodic spatial organization of the topological rings in the structure. The characteristic spacing between ring centers matches the length scale of the first sharp diffraction peak (FSDP) in the structure factor, establishing a direct connection between this reciprocal-space signature of MRO and its real-space organization. These results demonstrate that the FSDP, the spatial correlation of the rings, and emergent orientational symmetries are not independent manifestations of MRO, but reflect different aspects of a common structural organization. Our findings provide a unified real-space picture of MRO in amorphous silicon and suggest that intermediate-range structural order in network glasses emerges from the interplay between local bonding constraints and extended atomic arrangements driven by efficient packing.
authors: Zhen Zhang, Stephen R. Elliott, Yujie Wang, Walter Kob

articles.title: Room-Temperature Metallic 2D Ferromagnetism Stabilized by Quantum Metric
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recent discovery of long-sought dice-lattice bands in layered electride YCl opens up unprecedented opportunities for studying correlated electrons in real dice lattice systems. While the weakly dispersive band at the Fermi level is partially filled and density-wave states are expected due to Fermi surface nesting based on conventional theories, the ARPES measurement nevertheless revealed a uniform flat band splitting of 0.5 eV, suggesting unusual ferromagnetism (FM) borne out of the metallic 2D dice lattice. In this Letter, we propose that the uniform metallic FM order is stabilized by the prominent quantum metric near topological band crossing points at K and K', which reconstructs the magnetic instability in the dice metal and tips the density-wave instability toward a uniform FM order. Importantly, our analysis based on random phase approximation (RPA) and Hartree-Fock theory predicts a remarkably high Curie temperature above room temperature for the 2D FM order. These findings establish the first example of a room-temperature 2D metallic magnet stabilized by quantum metric, which not only exemplifies the fundamental significance of quantum geometry in solids but also bears far-reaching applications in energy-efficient high-density magnetic memories.
authors: Teng-Fei Ying, Jianqi Zhong, Songyuan Geng, Fangjie Chen, Haoxiang Li, Benjamin T. Zhou

articles.title: Role of Gd 5d-Au 5d hybridization for the magnetic properties of Au-Al-Gd quasicrystal approximants
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have studied the electronic states of magnetic Au-Al-Gd quasicrystal approximants, which exhibit different magnetic ground states at low temperatures, by orbital-selective soft and hard x-ray electron spectroscopies in the paramagnetic phase. Our results reveal that the valence electronic states vary among the Au-Al-Gd approximants with different magnetic ground states, whereas the Gd 4f electrons are localized in all of them. In particular, we find that the Gd 5d states are hybridized with the Au 5d states around the Fermi level, providing information about a local pathway for the intersite exchange interaction between the localized Gd 4f electrons. This hybridization strength varies among these samples. Our findings bring an orbital-resolved microscopic picture to the magnetism of rare-earth-based quasicrystals and approximants.
authors: Goro Nozue, Hidenori Fujiwara, Satoru Hamamoto, Yuto Torii, Mai Sakaguchi, Sho Nakajima, Takuya D. Nakamura, Nonoka U. Sakamoto, Takayuki Kiss, Masaki Oura, Akira Yasui, Kotaro Higashi, Naomi Kawamura, Kojiro Mimura, Arata Tanaka, Asuka Ishikawa, Farid Labib, Shintaro Suzuki, Takafumi D. Yamamoto, Ryuji Tamura, Akira Sekiyama

articles.title: Resolving Structural Uncertainty in Stochastic Dynamical Systems via Ensemble-Based Bayesian Inference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovering the interaction structure of complex stochastic dynamical systems from sparse time-series observations is an inherently ill-posed inverse problem. The posterior over network configurations is high-dimensional, highly degenerate, and shaped by the non-equilibrium nature of the available data. To address this, we propose a fully Bayesian, ensemble-based inference framework. Our approach grounds a continuous-time Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) likelihood formulation---acting mathematically as an Onsager-Machlup quasi-potential for non-equilibrium paths---within a non-parametric Minimum Description Length (MDL) structural prior. This framework rigorously penalizes model complexity and avoids kinetic overfitting by forcing continuous parameters into a finite vocabulary of discrete categories. The joint posterior is optimized using a block-coordinate scheme combining sub-quadratic Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) topological sampling with deterministic Nelder-Mead parameter optimization. Using highly non-linear macroscopic population dynamics as a benchmark, we demonstrate that inference requires non-stationary transient data to resolve causal information. Furthermore, we prove that propagating structural uncertainty via ensemble-based posterior analysis produces significantly more robust and reliable predictions for downstream perturbation outcomes than traditional single-point (MAP) estimates. The framework is highly generalizable, capturing fundamental topological constraints even under severe generative model mismatches, offering a robust tool for uncertainty-aware inference in complex stochastic systems.
authors: Francesco Zambelli, Valeria D'Andrea, Manlio De Domenico

articles.title: Beyond Kitaev exchange: Γ'-driven magnetism in Ag₃LiRh₂O₆
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Kitaev magnets, frustration arises from bond-dependent spin anisotropic interactions, which can potentially realize sought-after quantum spin liquid phases. However, material realizations with dominating Kitaev exchange are scarce and the broad parameter space of extended Kitaev models remains largely unexplored experimentally. Here, we use density-functional theory, cluster many-body, spin-wave, and density-matrix renormalization calculations to show that the recently discovered honeycomb rhodate Ag₃LiRh₂O₆ hosts an off-diagonal exchange Γ₁' that is second in magnitude only to the ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange K₁. This combination of K₁ and Γ₁' explains key experimental observations, an unusually high magnetic ordering temperature of 94 K at ambient pressure and its rapid decrease under hydrostatic pressure as Ag₃LiRh₂O₆ evolves from ferromagnetic toward zigzag order within the honeycomb planes. Our spin-wave calculations further predict an unusual topology of the magnon bands arising from the Γ₁' term in the spin Hamiltonian of the honeycomb layer. We show that the large trigonal splitting of t₂g states enhances Γ₁', the hitherto underappreciated term in Kitaev magnets, and opens the way to new interesting regimes of the extended Kitaev model.
authors: Efrain Insuasti Pazmino, Shi Feng, Ramesh Dhakal, Ioannis Rousochatzakis, Stephen M. Winter, Johannes Knolle, Alexander A. Tsirlin

articles.title: Orientation-Dependent Universality of Spin-Transport Fluctuations in Two-Dimensional Altermagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Universal conductance fluctuations are conventionally organized by symmetry class, but crystalline anisotropy introduces additional structure in spin transport. Here we demonstrate orientation-dependent universal spin-transport fluctuations in disordered two-dimensional d-wave altermagnets without spin-orbit coupling. Rotating the altermagnetic orientation changes both longitudinal spin-conductance and transverse spin-Hall conductance fluctuations, while each conserved-spin sector remains in class AI. Altermagnetic orientation controls both the fluctuation amplitudes and the development of disorder-insensitive plateaus. These plateaus become flatter and less sensitive to the altermagnetic strength over the studied parameter ranges as the orientation approaches 45ⁱ̧rc, with representative fluctuation amplitudes of approximately 0.60e/(4π) for the longitudinal spin conductance and 0.40,e/(4π) for the spin-Hall conductance. The longitudinal fluctuation amplitude correlates strongly with anisotropy of the clean-band Fermi-velocity tensor. Spin-sector covariances explain how the conserved channels combine into total fluctuations. Our results extend anisotropy-sensitive universal-fluctuation physics to conserved-spin altermagnetic transport and establish crystalline orientation as a control parameter within a fixed symmetry class.
authors: Yihan Zhang, Zheng Qin, Donghui Xu, Junjie Zeng, Zhen Ning, Rui Wang

articles.title: Interplay of electric field and electronic correlations in pairing competition in bilayer nickelates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Layer polarization provides a means of tuning the competition between interlayer and intralayer pairing in bilayer nickelates. Using ground-state constrained-path quantum Monte Carlo, we study interlayer s± and intralayer d pairing in a bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model with a layer potential-energy difference ǎrepsilon representing an effective perpendicular electric field. Within the parameter range studied, increasing ǎrepsilon generally enhances the finite-size pairing vertex contribution V_d and reduces Vₛ±, shifting the relative pairing preference toward the d-wave channel. Increasing the onsite repulsion enhances both vertex contributions, more strongly in the d-wave channel, whereas increasing the crystal-field splitting reduces both and makes s± pairing relatively more competitive. Hund's coupling increases the relative competitiveness of s± pairing at weak bias, while enhancing the relative strength of d-wave pairing at large bias. The bias primarily redistributes charge between layers within each orbital sector, accompanied by an increase in the antiferromagnetic spin structure factor. Hund's coupling also enhances local interorbital parallel-spin correlations. These observations suggest possible connections between charge redistribution, magnetic correlations, and pairing competition, offering insight into how layer polarization and multiorbital interactions influence the relative pairing tendencies in the bilayer nickelate model.
authors: Yanmei Cai, Yicheng Xiong, Ying Liang, Tianxing Ma

articles.title: Magnetic field induced modulation of heat transport in CrPS₄ probed by TaIrTe₄ transverse Seebeck thermometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding and controlling heat flow in low-dimensional magnetic materials is central to thermoelectrics and spin caloritronics. One of the challenges is the absence of sensitive probes of small, field-dependent modulations in thermal transport. Here we demonstrate transverse Seebeck thermometry using exfoliated TaIrTe₄ as a probe of thermal conductivity modulated by an external magnetic field on a van der Waals magnet, CrPS₄. With a temperature gradient oriented at 45ⁱ̧rc to its principal crystallographic axes, TaIrTe₄ exhibits a transverse thermopower exceeding 200~mathrmμ V,K⁻¹ for 900 nm wide and 30 μm long electrodes, enabling precise detection of variations in the local temperature gradients. Exploiting this with CrPS₄ in a nonlocal geometry, we resolve distinct field dependent thermal conductivity changes associated with both the spin-flip and spin-flop magnetic transitions which we attribute to variations in the magnon-phonon coupling in CrPS₄. At 5 K, the transverse Seebeck response is modulated by more than 8% by an external magnetic field, demonstrating strong magnetic control of heat transport in CrPS₄. This all van der Waals platform offers high sensitivity to modulations of thermal conductivity and a broad adaptability to a wide range of exfoliated magnetic systems.
authors: Krishnaraajan Sundararajan, Sergio Alvarruiz, Cédric A. Cordero-Silis, Majid Ahmadi, Marcos H. D. Guimarães, Jagoda Sławińska, Joseph Barker, Bart J. van Wees

articles.title: Error-controlled switching between discrete and continuum dislocations in a unified defect framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating defects of every dimension together is expensive, and the savings of adaptive methods are rarely tested at equal accuracy. We present a variational framework in which fields, dislocation lines and defect densities share one free energy, one dissipation law and exact ledgers of mass and Burgers vector, so that a region can change its representation without gaining or losing defects. On this basis, an allocator switches the dislocations themselves between discrete particles, where they are sparse, and a continuous density, where they are dense. The switch is made block by block from local counts, conserves the Burgers vector exactly and is controlled by a single threshold. For 5×10⁵ dislocations, the allocator reproduces the discrete model to within 1% in the sparse region at 14-37 times lower cost, depending on the machine; the advantage grows to 81 times at 10⁶ dislocations, and a threshold calibrated on one ensemble meets its error target on an independent one. For an idealized array of dislocation walls in copper, the allocator is 37.5 times cheaper than particle dislocation dynamics and, at almost the same cost, six times more accurate than continuum dislocation dynamics between the walls. In a three-dimensional copper model coupling grain-boundary cavitation with damage, ligaments left at nominal coalescence delay creep rupture by 25-48% (post hoc sweep). By contrast, grids refined at interfaces gain less than twofold once the active region exceeds about 30% of the domain, so representation switching, rather than grid refinement, is the effective form of adaptivity for defect-rich microstructures.

articles.title: Nonadiabatic polaron dynamics from machine-learned hopping trajectories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The formation and motion of small polarons are ubiquitous in energy materials and influence photoinduced processes. Polaron transport is governed by thermally activated lattice dynamics and rare hopping events, requiring spatial and temporal scales only attainable with machine-learning molecular dynamics, which enables extensive sampling of atomic trajectories and polaron configurations over nanoseconds. Moreover, the Born-Oppenheimer approximation underlying standard ab initio molecular dynamics cannot describe the nonadiabatic coupling between electronic states mediated by nuclear motion, which controls energy exchange and excited-state relaxation. Here, we develop a simulation framework that combines machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics to bridge these complementary aspects of polaron physics, and determine how different polaron-hopping mechanisms affect excited-state dynamics. The enlarged trajectory space allows us to provide the first direct dynamical confirmation of the adiabatic or nonadiabatic classification of polaron hopping regimes originally proposed on the basis of static Marcus-theory arguments, and to connect individual hopping events directly to nonadiabatic electronic transitions. In bulk TiO₂, nonadiabatic hoppings occur preferentially when the energy of the polaron-induced gap state approaches the conduction-band manifold, promoting both electronic de-excitation and, via a Landau-Zener mechanism, excitation from the ground state. In MgO, the predominantly adiabatic character of hole-polaron hopping suppresses these effects, leading to longer charge-carrier lifetimes and an absence of thermally activated excitations. At the rutile TiO₂₍₁₁₀₎ surface, hopping events are rarer than in bulk because the excess electron is strongly stabilized in the subsurface region, leading to correspondingly longer de-excitation times.
authors: Daniela Mangano (University of Vienna, Faculty of Physics and Center for Computational Materials Science, Vienna, Austria, Department of Physics and Astronomy Augusto Righi, Alma Mater Studiorum - Università di Bologna, Bologna, Italy), Luca Leoni (Department of Physics and Astronomy Augusto Righi, Alma Mater Studiorum - Università di Bologna, Bologna, Italy), Zhongfei Xu (College of Environmental Science and Engineering, North China Electric Power University, Beijing, China), Li-Min Liu (School of Physics, Beihang University, Beijing, China), Cesare Franchini (University of Vienna, Faculty of Physics and Center for Computational Materials Science, Vienna, Austria, Department of Physics and Astronomy Augusto Righi, Alma Mater Studiorum - Università di Bologna, Bologna, Italy)

articles.title: A practical route to amorphous solid-state electrolyte structures by hybrid reverse Monte Carlo with foundation potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Amorphous alkali oxychlorides are fast ion conductors, but their atomic structure remains unresolved. Total scattering sums all partial pair correlations into one curve that has no unique inversion, so the structure must be modeled. Melt-quench molecular dynamics builds a model from the interatomic potential alone, and reverse Monte Carlo (RMC) builds one from the measurement alone. The two have rarely been compared with all else held fixed. We benchmark both routes and two hybrid schemes on amorphous ȩLi₀.₉NbO₀.₉Cl₄.₁ against one neutron pair distribution function with one foundation potential. The hybrid schemes put the energy either in the acceptance rule (inline) or in short relaxations between blocks of refinement (alternating). Each refinement starts from a melt-quench glass or from a random packing of isolated units. The glass has the lowest energy and places the first-shell peaks correctly, but carries almost none of the oscillation beyond 6~Å{} (goodness of fit R² = 0.29). Pure RMC fits the measurement to within its counting noise (R² = 0.99), but at more than 1.3~eV/atom above the glass, and niobium loses about half of its first-shell chlorine. Started from the glass, both hybrid schemes reach R² = 0.92 within 0.1~eV/atom of its energy and keep its coordination chemistry. Structures from the two inputs fit almost equally well and differ in energy by a tenth of the RMC penalty, yet they differ in whether their polyhedra are connected. The input is therefore part of the method. We recommend quenching a glass with a foundation potential and refining it against the measurement with a hybrid scheme. The resulting structure carries both the local chemistry and the medium-range order, and it is the starting point for modeling ion transport in these conductors.
authors: Xintian Wang, Xinyu Zhang, Denys Butenko, Bolong Hong, Jinlong Zhu, Peichen Zhong

articles.title: Understanding the Mpemba Effect through a Rule of Thumb
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Mpemba effect, a system prepared farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than one prepared closer to it. Its persistence across diverse systems, and under different dynamics of the same system, suggests that it is largely rooted in equilibrium properties, with the dynamics deciding only which mode relaxes slowest. Here we propose a simple rule of thumb for anticipating the Mpemba effect: the effect is expected when a single low-order equilibrium moment is nonmonotonic in temperature. The bath singles out this moment as the slowest to relax, so that its displacement from its bath value sets the amplitude of the slowest relaxation mode. We establish this relation exactly for low-dimensional Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes. We then extend the rule to mean-field models by approximating their relaxation near the final equilibrium state by an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process. For the mean-field Ising antiferromagnet, which we solve exactly in the thermodynamic limit, this approximation reproduces the main structure of the Mpemba phase diagram, including strong effects far from any phase transition. Finally, we give a general prescription for mean-field systems: identify the slowest symmetry-allowed moment of the normal coordinates at the bath, and follow its equilibrium value as a function of preparation temperature. This offers a practical route from equilibrium observables to anomalous relaxation without diagonalizing the dynamics.

articles.title: Deep Learning of Phase Transitions for Bilinear-Biquadratic Spin-1 Chains from Correlation Aspects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the role of different correlation functions in reconstructing the phase diagram of the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic chain, parametrized by the angle θ between the bilinear and biquadratic couplings, using our previously developed label-free machine-learning pipeline i̧teMing21, Ming23, in which an autoencoder compresses iDMRG correlation matrices into latent features and K-means clustering with silhouette analysis groups them into phases. Without any prior labels, the scheme reveals four natural phases, the Haldane, dimerized, critical trimerized, and ferromagnetic phases, and accurately locates the Takhtajan-Babujian (θ=-π/4), SU(3)-symmetric Uimin-Lai-Sutherland (θ=π/4), and Ferro-Dimer (θ=5π/4) transition points; a shallow supervised refinement further sharpens the phase boundaries. We find that different correlation functions play fundamentally different roles in phase identification. The SU(3)-symmetric correlation alone selects a four-cluster partition that can be associated with the four phases, whereas the spin-spin and dimer-dimer correlations must be combined to recover the complete phase diagram. In contrast, the trimer-trimer correlation behaves as a marginal correlation: it is insufficient for phase identification by itself but improves the precision of the predicted phase boundaries when combined with the other correlations. Furthermore, the latent representations and silhouette values reveal signatures that we relate to the θ dependence of the correlations within each phase and, tentatively, to the underlying renormalization-group structure. These results demonstrate that machine learning can not only identify quantum phases but also uncover the physical information encoded in different correlation functions.
authors: Ming-Chiang Chung, Yu-Ting Kuo, Ian McCulloch, Yuan-Hong Tsai

articles.title: Transverse magneto-gyrotropy driven by spin-induced ferroaxiality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photon chirality is inherently sensitive to structural handedness and magnetism, which break spatial inversion and time-reversal symmetries, respectively. Ferroaxial order, by contrast, hosts two-dimensional chirality while preserving both symmetries, thereby precluding its direct coupling to photon chirality. Intertwining ferroaxiality with magnetic order, however, may lift such constraints and enable unconventional coupling to photon chirality. Nevertheless, the optical response arising from such intertwined order has yet to be demonstrated experimentally. Here, we demonstrate transverse magneto-gyrotropy arising from spin-driven ferroaxiality in the Weyl magnet EuCd2Sb2. Whereas the conventional polar magneto-optical Kerr effect is governed by magnetization parallel to the light-propagation direction, we observe a gyrotropic response associated with magnetization transverse to the light-propagation direction. The optical rotation exhibits a characteristic 120-degree periodicity upon rotation of the in-plane magnetic field, reflecting the threefold symmetry of the emergent ferroaxial state and revealing the ferroaxial origin of the transverse gyrotropic response. This coupling to photon chirality enables vectorial control of the gyrotropic response through the magnetic field direction. Our findings establish an interaction between photon chirality and transverse magnetization enabled by intertwined ferroaxial and magnetic orders, demonstrating a novel form of multiferroicity with functional light-matter interaction.
authors: Yoshihiro Okamura, Takumi Kagawa, Ayano Nakamura, Shinichi Nishihaya, Masaki Uchida, Susumu Minami, Ryotaro Arita, Youtarou Takahashi

articles.title: Disorder-Induced Griffiths like Phase and Charge Localization in Sr2FeRuO6
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A comprehensive understanding of complex transition-metal oxides is key to designing next-generation spintronic materials with tailored magnetic and transport functionalities. We investigate the interplay among structural disorder, frustrated magnetism, and localized charge transport in the 3d-4d hybrid double perovskite Sr2FeRuO6. The compound adopts a monoclinic structure with significant B-site antisite disorder that drives its unconventional behavior. Magnetic measurements uncover a robust Griffiths phase extending well above the ordering temperature, evidencing stable short-range ferromagnetic clusters within a disordered matrix. Electrical transport remains strongly localized, transitioning from small-polaron hopping at high temperatures to variable-range hopping at intermediate temperatures. These results position Sr2FeRuO6 as a representative 3d-4d hybrid system in which quenched disorder stabilizes spin inhomogeneity, while polaronic and hopping transport are also observed.
authors: Koustav Pal, Shuvendu Ghosh, I. Das

articles.title: Access Rate-Dependent Endurance Behavior of Ferroelectric Hafnium Zirconium Oxide Capacitors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluorite-structured ferroelectrics, such as hafnium zirconium oxide (Hf₁₋ₓZrₓO₂), are among the most promising materials for developing the next generation of low-power nonvolatile memories. Emulating realistic operating scenarios for ferroelectric memories requires performing access rate-dependent endurance tests. The access rate-dependent reduction of the switched polarization cannot be described as a mere superposition of fatigue and imprint effects, which are observed in conventional endurance and retention tests, respectively. The interplay between these degradation mechanisms and its correlation with the delay time in between the programming pulses remains unclear. Combining electrical testing through voltage pulses with ab initio and drift-diffusion simulations provides a comprehensive perspective on the microscopic origin of the access rate-dependent reduction of the switched polarization of ferroelectric capacitors based on product-relevant 5 nm thick Hf₀.₅Zr₀.₅O₂ films. The role of oxygen vacancy defects accumulating at the electrode-ferroelectric interface with delay time in reducing the fraction of switchable domains is elucidated considering electron transfer processes which change the defect charge state. Building upon this theoretical understanding, a physics-based model to extrapolate the long-term access rate-dependent endurance performance is developed and experimentally verified for temperatures up to 135degC and delay times up to 2 ms.
authors: Roberto Guido, Julie Laguerre, Pramoda Vishnumurthy, Florian Wunderwald, Kristina Holsgrove, Thomas Mikolajick, Sou-Chi Chang, Alfred Kersch, Uwe Schroeder

articles.title: A Topological-Geometrical Descriptor (TGD) for Scalable and Interpretable Modeling of Two-Dimensional Carbon Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a compact Topological-Geometrical Descriptor (TGD) for planar two-dimensional carbon networks. Atomic coordinates are mapped to a periodic planar graph and represented through ring populations, topological-charge statistics, projected ring geometry, and dual-graph defect adjacency. The resulting modeling vector contains 19 physically interpretable features. We evaluate TGD on 120 published planar carbon allotropes using the DFT relative energy per atom with respect to graphene as the target. Repeated five-fold cross-validation with gradient boosting yields a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0826 +/- 0.0138 eV/atom and R2 = 0.803 +/- 0.074. Under the same validation protocol, TGD gives a mean MAE of 0.0828 eV/atom, compared with 0.0929 eV/atom for a 203-feature Matminer representation. We further analyze 360 vacancy-defected graphene configurations spanning 12 vacancy concentrations from 2 to 24 percent. When entire vacancy concentrations are held out, TGD gives a pooled MAE of 0.269 eV/vacancy and R2 = 0.861, outperforming simple baselines based on vacancy concentration alone or non-hexagonal-ring fraction alone. Sensitivity tests show that the inferred edge sets are stable to moderate changes in the adaptive bond factor. Finally, the mean absolute topological charge is examined as a one-variable empirical surrogate for the allotrope dataset and is treated explicitly as dataset-specific rather than universal. These results show that TGD combines compact prediction with direct structural interpretation while making clear the present restriction to single-layer planar carbon networks.
authors: Rômulo Uriel Liberal de Oliveira, Raphael Matozo Tromer

articles.title: Bulk superconductivity in quintuple-layer square-planar nickelate La6Ni5O12
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nickelate superconductors, sharing a similar electronic environment with cuprate superconductors, offer a promising platform for unraveling the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. However, the realization of superconductivity in these systems has so far been restricted to thin films or bulk samples under high-pressure. This limits the applicability of various experimental probes to study the mechanism of superconductivity, and hinders the potential application of the nickelate superconductors. Exploring bulk superconductivity at ambient pressure is therefore essential to understand its origin and enable broader experimental research. Here, we report the realization of bulk superconductivity at ambient-pressure in quintuple-layer square-planar (SP) nickelate La6Ni5O12. The SP phase is obtained by performing topotactic reaction on the quintuple-layer Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) compound La6Ni5O16. Optimized reduction condition endows La6Ni5O12 with a superconducting state that exhibits onset transition temperature of ~ 18 K, as verified by both zero resistance and diamagnetic shielding effect. Pronounced hysteresis loops revealed by magnetization and torque magnetometry demonstrate the occurrence of vortex pinning. Specific heat measurements on a polycrystalline pellet of La6Ni5O12 reveal a clear superconducting transition at ~18 K and a superconducting volume fraction of ~ 25%, which strongly supports the presence of bulk superconductivity. Our results establish an unprecedented bulk sample platform for investigating superconductivity in nickelates at ambient pressure, which paves the way for further experimental studies into the superconducting mechanism.
authors: Mengzhu Shi, Mei Du, Hongyu Li, Zhiwei Wang, Zhengjie Wang, Ziji Xiang, Tao Wu, Xianhui Chen

articles.title: Transport regimes in tunnel ferromagnetic Josephson junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a systematic study of the temperature-dependent transport properties of Nb- and Al-based superconductor--insulator--thin superconductor--ferromagnet--superconductor (SIsFS) Josephson junctions. By varying the superconducting material and the thickness of the intermediate superconducting layer, we identify three distinct transport regimes: a tunnel-dominated SIS-like regime, a temperature-driven crossover, and a complex weak-link regime. A unified Usadel-based description connects these regimes through the self-consistent pair potential of the intermediate s-layer. While for Al-based devices an SIS-like transport regime is observed, a self-consistent calculation of the s/F/S proximity electrode, combined with perturbative tunnel coupling to the outer electrode, accounts for Nb devices with different thickness of the superconducting interlayer. The calculation places the 10-nm-interlayer sample in a proximity-supported, strongly suppressed s state, close to the SInFS limit in which the interlayer is effectively driven normal (n). A reduced nonlinear long-junction description captures the same limiting physics. The evolution of I_cR_N(T) thereby provides a direct experimental signature of the three transport regimes. Beyond the fundamental interest, the results establish practical design guidelines: Nb junctions with sufficiently thick s interlayers are well suited for high-speed cryogenic memory elements and tunable superconducting parametric amplifiers, while Al junctions are natural candidates for coherent superconducting quantum circuits
authors: R. Satariano, A. A. Golubov, E. Raja, R. Ferraiuolo, F. Calloni, H. G. Ahmad, A. Vettoliere, N. Poccia, L. Parlato, G. Ausanio, C. Granata, G. P. Pepe, M. Yu. Kupriyanov, F. Tafuri, D. Montemurro, D. Massarotti

articles.title: Coherent and dissipative coupling of multiple photon-magnon hybrids in a chiral microwave resonator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate control between level repulsion and level attraction of photon-magnon coupling spectra in a chiral microwave-photon resonator loaded with a 2 mm YIG sphere. By systematically varying the coupling mode volume via the YIG position and the dc-field orientation, we tune the ratio between coherent and dissipative coupling strengths, J/Γ, and thereby switch between level repulsion and level attraction in the hybrid spectra. Full-wave electromagnetic and magnetization-dynamics simulations reveal multiple photon-magnon hybrid modes with distinct spatial overlap factors, which quantitatively account for gap sizes and their angular dependence. Strong nonreciprocity appears near J/Γ approx 1, yielding 28.6 dB isolation ratio in agreement with a unified single-bath input-output model and full-wave simulations. Angular dependence of spectral characterization confirms a picture of the chirality-selection rule and our method of geometric tuning might be useful for considering reconfigurable on-chip isolators.
authors: Supanat Chantarattana, Charlie W. F. Freeman, Daniel Prestwood, Nimisha Arora, Vincent Castel, Hidekazu Kurebayashi

articles.title: Designing Hamiltonians with Exactly Flat Higher-Vortexable Bands
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The zero modes of the Aharonov-Casher Hamiltonian form an exactly flat, vortexable Chern band in any nonuniform magnetic field, analogous to the lowest Landau level. We ask which local Hamiltonians host exactly flat higher-vortexable bands. For a scalar Hamiltonian, an exactly flat first-vortexable band requires a mass proportional to the local field; the Dirac analogue has the same structure. For periodic Bernal bilayer graphene with nonzero mean flux, the exact zero-mode pair is genuinely first-vortexable if and only if the interlayer hopping has nonzero mean; zero-mean hopping instead gives a decomposable pair. Multiorbital models yield exact higher-vortexable chains to arbitrary order, while remaining first order in momentum.

articles.title: Influence of the Néel vector on the bulk electronic structure of MnTe measured from the (1 bar1 00) surface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnetism gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization. Here, we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to investigate bulk α-MnTe single crystals cleaved along the (1bar100) plane - an orientation that preserves the compensated magnetic symmetry at the surface and substantially reduces surface effects and k_z broadening. We resolve the three-dimensional bulk band structure with markedly enhanced spectral clarity. The d-wave band splitting, driven by the altermagnetic order and spin-orbit coupling in the Γ-K-M nodal plane, shows a perfect match to theoretical predictions. We further establish that the valence-band maximum occurs near the A point, identifying the corresponding hole pockets as the states governing the transport properties. Spatially resolved measurements reveal systematic variations of the band dispersion along Γ-K and A-L, associated with different pinning of the Néel vector at the surface. Our results establish a surface-sensitive route to resolving the bulk altermagnetic electronic structure of MnTe and provide direct spectroscopic evidence for Néel-vector-dependent band splitting.
authors: D. A. Usanov, A. B. Hellenes, S. Hahn, M. Leandersson, J. Osiecki, K. Uhlířová, D. Evtushinsky, L. Šmejkal, T. Jungwirth, J. H. Dil

articles.title: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La₃Ni₂O₇ via ¹³⁹La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the Am2m Structure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The lower-symmetry Am2m structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La₃Ni₂O₇ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted Amam structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La₃Ni₂O₇ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via ¹³⁹La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the Am2m structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the Amam framework. Within the Am2m framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La₃Ni₂O₇, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-T_c superconductivity under high pressure.
authors: Mitsuharu Yashima, Hongnam Lee, Takumi Ino, Nina Seto, Masataka Kakoi, Hiroya Sakurai, Yoshihiko Takano, Hidekazu Mukuda

articles.title: Orbitronics in Zero-dimensional Graphene Nanoflakes via Electrode Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that graphene nanoflakes realize a previously unexplored form of orbitronics in which orbital currents emerge in the absence of intrinsic angular momentum of the constituent atoms. Starting with a hexagonal graphene nanoflake, we demonstrate the presence of energy-degenerate eigenstates with opposite non-zero expectation values of the angular momentum. Placing electrodes in an appropriate configuration on the flake couples the reservoirs more strongly to one of the two opposite-angular-momentum states, yielding a chiral current that carries a net orbital angular momentum. The resulting circulating orbital currents generate magnetic fringe fields that are experimentally accessible with spin centers or superconducting quantum interference magnetometers, providing avenues for their experimental realization. Finally, our work establishes a new platform for exploring and studying orbitronics in zero-dimensional systems.
authors: Washington F. dos Santos, Eudes Gomes da Silva, Denis R. Candido, Alexandre Reily Rocha

articles.title: Magnetic Susceptibility of Superconducting Films in the Meissner-London Regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extracting the London penetration depth, łambda(T), from the measured magnetic susceptibility, ḩi(T), of a superconducting platelet in a perpendicular magnetic field requires knowing the function ḩi(łambda) computed for the actual sample geometry. Thin films are increasingly important in quantum computing and superconducting electronics, most of which operate at ultra-low excitation fields in the vortex-free regime. Understanding their electromagnetic response in the Meissner--London (finite-łambda, no vortices) state is therefore essential for extracting intrinsic properties such as the London penetration depth and superfluid phase stiffness. While numerous prior works have addressed different aspects of this problem, here we focus on providing an analytical semi-empirical representation of ḩi(łambda) based on the 2D sheet-current model and establishing the limits of its applicability using two independent full 3D numerical solutions: finite-element modeling and a volume-current integral equation. As a result, we provide ḩi(łambda) for a disc of radius a and thickness d in closed form, valid for all łambda and for aspect ratios δequiv d/(2a)łe0.05, and accurate to 0.1%. The two-dimensional sheet description with Pearl length Łambda=2łambda²/d is adequate for δ łesssim10⁻⁴ and łambda gtrsim 4d. Thicker films require the full closed form, which includes the three-dimensional corrections. Using the same numerical analysis, we provide an empirical formula that maps rectangular samples---the geometry most commonly used in experiments---onto a disc with an ``effective radius'' for subsequent calculation of ḩi(łambda), and formulate a complete calibration protocol for whole-sample susceptibility measurements.

articles.title: Testing Replica Symmetry Breaking in the three-dimensional Edwards-Anderson model by using vanishing fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Replica Symmetry Breaking (RSB) theory for spin glasses, which is exact in infinite dimensions, provides detailed predictions for the behavior of these systems. One of these predictions is that vanishing magnetic fields induce chaotic behavior. Here, vanishing has a precise meaning: we refer to an externally applied magnetic field with intensity scaling as 1/sqrtN, where N is the number of spins in the system. RSB predicts that this chaotic behavior depends only on the probability density function of the overlap, P(q), as computed at zero field. We proceed to test the RSB prediction in the 3D Edwards-Anderson model, by first computing the P(q) numerically in the absence of a magnetic field. We then use this function as input to analytically compute the statistics of the states in the regime of a vanishing magnetic field, using a representation based on the Bolthausen-Sznitman coalescent process (which is exact for the mean-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model). This mixed numerical-analytical approach allows us to determine the prediction of RSB for the overlap distribution function measured in the presence of a small vanishing field, as well as the increase in chaoticity as the field strength grows. The above RSB predictions are quantitatively compared with the outcome of numerical simulations of the three-dimensional Edwards-Anderson in the presence of a small vanishing field, finding very good agreement. This agreement provides strong support for the idea that three-dimensional spin glass at zero magnetic field and low temperature is well described by RSB theory.
authors: Miguel Aguilar-Janita, Silvio Franz, Victor Martin-Mayor, Javier Moreno-Gordo, Giorgio Parisi, Federico Ricci-Tersenghi, Juan J. Ruiz-Lorenzo

articles.title: Structural identification in general crystalline systems via Voronoi cell topology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Widely used methods for identifying crystal structure in atomistic simulations are limited in practice to a handful of simple structures, leaving many important crystalline systems without automated classification techniques. Voronoi topology analysis offers a route to classifying arbitrary crystalline and defect environments, but realizing this potential first requires enumerating the Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under thermal perturbation of a structure of interest. We present an algorithm that deterministically enumerates all Voronoi cell topologies arising from generic infinitesimal perturbations of an arbitrary crystal structure, producing structural classifiers that extend automated identification to general crystalline systems. We demonstrate the approach on several structures of general interest.
