Notably, among the two positively selected sites in npc1l1, the 77th amino acid resides within the Niemann-Pick C1 N-terminus domain, suggesting a potential role in the adaptive evolution of carotenoid absorption. Collectively, these findings imply that the golden coloration in L. crocea may result from a combination of optimized carotenoid uptake, transport, and storage, alongside melanin regulation and optical enhancement mediated by iridophores. This study provides comparative genomic insights into the evolutionary characteristics of coloration‑related genes in L. crocea, enriches the molecular understanding of fish pigmentation mechanisms, and lays a foundation for future research and selective breeding targeting body color traits in this species.

articles.title: Investigation of the Performance of Machine Learning Algorithms of Casson-Micropolar Nano Particles Around a Cylindrical Shape: ANN and PINN
articles.abstract: Present study deals with a comprehensive analysis of Micropolar-Casson fluid model in two dimensional through a porous cylinder. In order to represent an accurate complex transport scenario encountered in Industrial and engineering applications formulated mathematical model incorporates Joule heating, heat source, mixed convection, chemical reaction and radiation. Convective boundary conditions were assumed. Non-similar transformations were employed to proposed system of nonlinear equations to get ordinary equations. Transformed system of nonlinear differential equations were resolved via two intelligence-based approaches i.e. Physics-informed neural network and artificial neural network. PINN based predictivity is examined at different number of iterations i.e. 1000-20,000. Mean absolute error decays as we increased number of epochs. ANN and PINN based highly authentic and stable solutions compared with BVP4c solutions were obtained. Comprehensive analysis of ANNPINN and BVp4c shows overlapped, stable, authentic and convergent outcomes at 20,000 epochs. It guarantees efficient, robustness and reliable approach for solving nonlinear system of equations alternate to conventional numerical approaches.

articles.title: Design, Physical Modeling, and Circuit Verification of a 4-Bit Quasi-Delay-Insensitive (QDI) Room-Temperature Molecular Processor
articles.abstract: As silicon CMOS technology approaches thermodynamic and quantum scaling limits, room-temperature molecular electronics represents a promising Beyond-CMOS paradigm. However, designing reliable computing systems at the single-molecule scale faces critical challenges, including stochastic channel variations, absence of global clock distribution networks, and quantum transport sensitivities. In this paper, we present the design, quantum physical transport modeling, and circuit-level transient verification of a 4-bit asynchronous Quasi-Delay-Insensitive (QDI) molecular processor. The architecture leverages quantum interference (Fano resonance) within single-molecule junctions to implement the core logic gates (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, ADD, SUB), dynamic latches, and a 4-bit Ripple Carry Adder (RCA). Computational sequencing is governed by a 4-phase Return-to-Zero (RTZ) dual-rail handshake protocol, eliminating global clock dependencies and ensuring strict delay insensitivity under wire-length and quantum transport variations. Comprehensive physical-to-circuit co-simulations confirm an active hardware core area of 0.0216 µm2 (147 nm × 147 nm across 1,296 molecular switches), an active dynamic power of 116.43 mW at 300 K, an energy efficiency of 4.93 pJ/token, and an Energy-Delay Product (EDP) of 116 aJ·ns. Verilog-A behavioral transient modeling validates physical noise margins (SNML = 3.12 mA, SNMH = 9.26 mA), an on/off switching ratio of ION/IOFF = 7.55, an SNR of 60.1 dB across a 50 GHz bandwidth, and an ultra-low Bit Error Rate (BER = 1.05 × 10− 12).

articles.title: Chiral Cartograph3R: A Quick Filtering Framework for Stereochemical Enumeration Integrating Chemistry Rules, 3D-Aware SDF Atom Mapping, Chirality Validation, and Spectral Geometry Features
articles.abstract: Stereochemical enumeration pipelines often overproduce candidate structures that are topologically admissible yet chemically impossible, mechanistically implausible, or silently corrupted by atom-order mismatch between canonical molecular representations and three-dimensional embeddings. These failure modes become increasingly costly in workflows that must explore large stereochemical chemical spaces, preserve chirality, and feed candidates into expensive downstream quantum-chemical, docking, or machine-learning stages. We present Chiral Cartograph3R, a correctness-first quick-filter framework that integrates literature-grounded chemical feasibility rules with a three-dimensional, chirality-preserving atom-mapping and validation layer operating directly on SDF-style structural assets. The system first enumerates candidate stereochemical states and then applies a hierarchical filter stack comprising structural impossibility checks, aromaticity validation, ring-closure feasibility logic, stereochemical preference heuristics, and kinetic-versus-thermodynamic plausibility weighting. Surviving candidates are passed to a 3D-aware graph isomorphism mapper that reconstructs connectivity from coordinates, enumerates graph-consistent atom correspondences against canonical structures, and scores mappings using a directional N×N×3 coordinate-difference tensor, topology-versus-geometry agreement, bond-length consistency, and collapse detection. Final validation uses signed tetrahedral volumes and related orientation tests to preserve chirality and detect hidden inversions. Spectral or distance-geometry embeddings are then emitted as downstream descriptors for equivariant graph neural networks or reranking modules. We ground the manuscript using stereoisomer SDF exemplars containing 196 atoms and 196 bonds each; they exhibit identical elemental composition and near-identical pairwise distance spectra while differing in local stereochemical flags, illustrating the exact regime in which global geometry can be similar while local chirality remains decisive. Compared with current mainstream capabilities in RDKit, OMEGA, ChemAxon, StereoMolGraph, and recent chirality-aware molecular models, the proposed framework occupies a distinct role: not as a replacement conformer generator or end-to-end GNN, but as a fast stereochemical correctness filter that reduces wasted downstream computation, broadens practical exploration of stereochemical chemical space at fixed budget, and improves trustworthiness of ML-ready molecular representations [1–12].

articles.title: Machine Learning for Gene-Expression-Based Prediction of Alcohol Use Disorder with an Integrate Web-Based Dashboard
articles.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex condition associated with molecular alterations in brain regions involved in reward, motivation, and behavioral regulation. Gene-expression profiling can provide valuable molecular information for studying AUD; however, the high dimensionality and correlation structure of transcriptomic data present challenges for predictive modeling and interpretation. This study develops a machine-learning approach for predicting AUD status from gene-expression profiles and introduces GENO, a web-based dashboard designed to support laboratory users in interpreting the resulting predictions. Publicly available bulk RNA-sequencing data from postmortem brain tissue of 114 individuals, including 58 AUD cases and 56 non-AUD controls, were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus repository (GSE253155). Gene-expression data were standardized, and dimensionality was reduced using ANOVA F-test and mutual-information-based feature selection. An Elastic Net logistic regression model was then developed to manage high-dimensional and correlated predictors while maintaining model interpretability. On the held-out test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 86%, an F1-score of 0.865, and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.895. For each input profile, the model generates a probability-based prediction of membership in the AUD class and estimates gene-level contributions to the prediction. GENO integrates this predictive pipeline into a web-based interface that supports data upload, automated analysis, result visualization, and structured report generation. A preliminary task-based usability assessment with laboratory users further demonstrated the feasibility of completing the platform’s primary workflow. These findings provide preliminary evidence that interpretable regularized machine learning can predict AUD status from postmortem gene-expression profiles within the analyzed dataset.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Dual-Modality Monitoring for GNSS Spoofing Detection
articles.abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) underpin positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), but open civil signals remain exposed to jamming and spoofing. When neither the radio-frequency configuration nor the attack is known in advance, the receiver must still identify the spoofed satellite channels before those measurements can be mitigated. Physics-informed dual-modality cross-attention networks (PI-DMCANs) are introduced for this channel-wise task. A short tracking-feature sequence and a local cross-ambiguity-function image are fused by causal cross-attention, and a residual bank—code–carrier consistency, signal-quality monitoring (SQM), peak walk, a secondary peak, and clock drift—sets the weight of each stream. On TEXBAT, OAKBAT, and the multi-constellation dataset MuCoGS, PI-DMCANs were compared with five baselines. Within-scenario accuracy at a Neyman–Pearson threshold was 0.965. Under within-dataset cross-scenario evaluation and cross-dataset evaluation, accuracy was 0.928 and 0.932 respectively, about 3.5 and 5.1 percentage points above the strongest baseline. Ablations of modality fusion and of the gate confirm that dual-modality residual gating is most helpful under hold-out. The resulting channel flag marks which satellite a GNSS receiver should de-weight or exclude, and thereby supplies a basis for interference mitigation.

articles.title: Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics for Multimodal Transport Accident Investigation: A Governance, Risk and Compliance Framework
articles.abstract: Multimodal transport accident investigations increasingly depend on digital control systems, networked communications, and sensor-rich operational data across aviation, rail, maritime, and road domains. This dependence expands the evidentiary surface and creates cyber-enabled failure modes that can alter records, undermine evidence integrity, and complicate attribution. This study develops a Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) framework that integrates cybersecurity and digital forensics across the accident-investigation lifecycle. A structured conceptual synthesis of 34 academic, professional, and standards-oriented sources was used to identify recurring governance, threat, evidence-handling, and compliance requirements. The framework was then operationalised in a deterministic prototype using 10,000 synthetic access requests. Under the baseline configuration, 61.13% of requests passed the governance gate; final decisions comprised 52.65% permits, 38.87% governance denials, 4.33% multi-factor authentication challenges, 3.08% algorithmic-risk denials, and 1.07% compliance denials. The prototype is illustrative rather than a measure of field performance. Its contribution is a traceable decision architecture that links authority, contextual cyber risk, evidentiary integrity, and lawful handling. The framework supports earlier preservation of volatile evidence, clearer decision rights, and more defensible cyber-aware investigations across transport modes.

articles.title: From Hours to Daily Extremes: Evaluating ERA5 and ERA5-Land Biases Across Morocco’s Diverse Climates
articles.abstract: Reanalysis products increasingly serve as ground-truth references and training/verification data for statistical and machine-learning applications in regions with sparse in-situ networks. This study evaluates ERA5 and ERA5-Land against 36 quality controlled synoptic stations over Morocco, across hourly, seasonal, Köppen-climate, and daily-extreme timescales, from 2016 to 2024. Both reanalysis reproduce the mean diurnal and seasonal cycle of near-surface variables with high fidelity (Pearson r frequently > 0.9 for temperature), and the two reanalysis products are broadly interchangeable for climatological applications, with small, systematic differences per variable (ERA5 ahead for temperature, humidity and wind bias; ERA5-Land ahead for wind-speed RMSE in complex terrain). Categorical verification of daily extremes reveals a threshold-dependent, rather than uniformly poor, skill: moderate warm/cold/wind thresholds are detected well by both products, but skill collapses specifically at the most extreme, rarest thresholds (POD falling from ∼0.85 to ∼0.4 for the hottest T2M_MAX class; near-zero for the strongest WS_MAX class), a pattern consistent with the known degeneracy of traditional contingency-table scores for rare events rather than with a specific flaw of either reanalysis. We additionally document a structural ERA5-Land limitation: its land-only grid leaves no valid nearest-neighbour match at some coastal/island-adjacent stations (e.g. Dakhla), a gap that is easily mistaken for missing observations if not checked explicitly. The results argue for anomaly- or percentile-based extreme definitions, and for explicit reporting of land-mask coverage, when ERA5/ERA5-Land are used for impact studies or as an AI-model verification baseline over Morocco’s complex, station-sparse terrain.

articles.title: Enhanced Electrical, Dielectric, and Optical Properties of Fe₂O₃-Decorated MWCNT/Epoxy Nanocomposite Thin Films
articles.abstract: In this study, Fe₂O₃ nanoparticle-doped epoxy/multi-walled carbon nanotube (Fe₂O₃@CNT/EP) nanocomposite thin films were fabricated, and their structural, electrical, dielectric, and optical properties were investigated. EP/CNT nanocomposites containing different MWCNT concentrations (0.1, 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt%) were prepared, followed by the incorporation of Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles into the EP/CNT matrix. The structural, chemical, and morphological characteristics of the prepared nanocomposites were investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The electrical and dielectric properties were evaluated using impedance spectroscopy over a broad frequency range, while the optical properties were investigated using UV–visible absorption and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy. The results demonstrated that the incorporation of MWCNTs significantly modified the electrical and dielectric properties of the epoxy matrix. Among the investigated CNT concentrations, the 1.0 wt% CNT-loaded EP/CNT nanocomposite exhibited a high capacitance of 8.1 × 10⁻⁹ F, dielectric constant of 71.5, and AC conductivity of 6.7 × 10⁻⁸ S m⁻¹. Further incorporation of Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles into the EP/CNT matrix resulted in a further enhancement of the electrical and dielectric responses. The optical absorption measurements revealed a decrease in the optical band gap from 4.15 eV for pristine EP to 3.86 eV for EP/CNT and 2.69 eV for Fe₂O₃@CNT/EP nanocomposites. The observed changes in the electrical, dielectric, and optical properties demonstrate the potential of these hybrid nanocomposite thin films for applications in electronic and optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Mechanism and Inhibition of Preferential Corrosion of Cold-Sprayed Copper in Dilute Nitric Acid
articles.abstract: Cold-sprayed copper is a promising additive manufacturing material for a range of applications, including used nuclear fuel containers. Under aggressive dilute nitric acid conditions, it exhibits preferential corrosion associated with the oxide network incorporated during fabrication, a phenomenon that remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate the mechanism of this preferential corrosion by varying the presence of dissolved oxygen and the concentrations of copper ions and chloride. By exploiting the inhibitive effect of chloride on nitrate reduction, we show that nitrate reduction is necessary before the initiation of preferential attack at the oxide-rich particle-particle boundaries can occur. In addition, dissolved copper ions substantially accelerate corrosion, providing direct experimental evidence for their proposed catalytic role. Material loss is ultimately dominated by particle detachment following preferential dissolution along the oxide network. These findings provide new insight into the corrosion mechanism of cold-sprayed copper in dilute nitric acid and indicate that preferential corrosion is specific to nitrate-containing, chloride-free environments.

articles.title: Termination controlled Phase-Pure Ti3C2Tx MXenes Towards Efficient Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: MXenes are promising electrocatalysts for sustainable hydrogen generation, but establishing reliable structure–activity relationships to achieve phase purity and control surface terminations remains challenging. Here, we report phase-pure Ti3C2-F and Ti3C2-O MXenes synthesised via a molten-salt process, achieving purities >99.6%. Ti₃C₂-F exhibits excellent performance in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic solutions, with a very low overpotential of 86 mV at 10 mA cm-2 and a Tafel slope of 55 mV dec-1. Ti₃C₂-O shows bifunctional catalytic activity in alkaline conditions, with HER and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) overpotentials of 76 and 134 mV at 10 mA cm⁻², and Tafel slopes of 86 and 102 mV dec⁻¹, respectively. Their outstanding activities and stabilities are attributed to phase-purity and tunable surface terminations, enabling different pathways for hydrogen and hydroxide activation. These findings not only elucidate the underlying reaction mechanisms but also demonstrate the potential of termination-controlled MXenes for efficient energy conversion.

articles.title: A Hybrid High-Spin Molecular Magnet for an Integrated Sensing–Storage Quantum Register
articles.abstract: Hybrid quantum molecular systems combining high-spin electrons and nuclear spins possess enlarged Hilbert spaces that can encode multiple qubits within a single molecule and therefore hold great promise for constructing quantum registers. However, the full potential of their multilevel spin manifolds remains underexplored. Herein, we synthesize P@C60 (electron spin S = 3/2, nuclear spin I = 1/2), a representative hybrid high-spin molecular magnet, via an improved, hazard-free synthetic route and systematically investigate its full electron–nuclear spin manifold. All ten spin transitions within an eight-dimensional Hilbert space, separated by hyperfine coupling and zero-field splitting, are individually addressed using pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). We demonstrate coherent control across multiple electron-spin levels, quantitatively characterize the multi-quantum coherence times of the high-spin electron system, and reveal that such coherence enhances sensing of the surrounding magnetic environment, increasing the signal-to-noise ratio by a factor of 2.4. We further demonstrate integrated quantum sensing and storage by transferring electron-spin sensing information to the 31P nuclear spin, where it is preserved beyond the electron-spin coherence time. Finally, we quantify nuclear-spin storage by transferring coherence from the electron spin to the 31P nuclear spin, obtaining a phase-memory time of 20.8 ms, approximately 1,300 times that of the electron spin. These results establish an electron–nuclear molecular spin register in which quantum sensing and storage are integrated within a single molecule.

articles.title: Quantum sensor could measure how Earth drags spacetime
articles.abstract: Einstein's theory of general relativity describes gravity as the bending of spacetime, a mathematical model that combines three-dimensional space and time into a single, four-dimensional continuum. The theory also predicts that a rotating object, such as Earth, slightly drags the surrounding spacetime as it rotates, a phenomenon known as frame-dragging.

articles.title: IBM executive warns of risk of quantum computing hacks
articles.abstract: Organizations are unprepared for the risks posed by quantum computing, IBM's Europe and Africa vice president Alessandro Curioni told AFP Wednesday, referring to the high-speed technology that could crack security encryptions and enable large-scale cyberattacks.

articles.title: Software advance brings complex quantum simulations to standard computers
articles.abstract: A major software advance could aid the creation of bigger, more reliable quantum computers, a study suggests. Researchers have developed an algorithm that enables off-the-shelf computers to run quantum simulations previously only possible using the world's most powerful supercomputers.

articles.title: Full-Continuum Ultrafast Quantum Gas Microscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum gas microscopy provides single-shot access to many-body configurations, but their microscopic reconstruction has so far largely relied on a predefined discrete spatial basis during fluorescence readout. Here we realize ultrafast atom-resolved fluorescence microscopy of an ultracold ¹⁶²Dy gas directly in continuous space, with all external confinement removed during imaging. Exploiting the large mass and broad optical transition of dysprosium together with a high numerical aperture in-vacuum objective, we detect single atoms within 4,μs while maintaining an effective point-spread function with a full width at half maximum of 254.8(3),nm, and an isolated single-atom classification fidelity of 99.72(3)%. We use the measured single-atom response to construct a statistical configuration-inference model that recovers atomic positions and multiplicities, coming from overlapping atoms, directly from single fluorescence snapshots. Benchmarking our model on Monte-Carlo generated images shows a total reconstruction fidelity of 98.7%. Our approach extends quantum gas microscopy beyond predefined detection lattices, enabling atom-resolved measurements of counting statistics and higher-order spatial correlations directly on the intrinsic length scales of continuum many-body systems.
authors: Andrea Litvinov, Clemens Ulm, Eva Casotti, Gerard Solà Berga, Manfred J. Mark, Francesca Ferlaino

articles.title: Electron-Mediated Phonon Polaritons in Quantum Cavities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phonon-photon coupling in quantum materials is commonly treated as an effective direct interaction, neglecting the crucial role played by electrons. Here we develop a gauge-invariant theory of cavity phonon polaritons that captures electronic screening, dissipation, and hybridization. We show that screening can suppress polariton formation in metals, severely constraining cavity control of phonon-mediated superconductivity. By contrast, interband electronic resonances in time-reversal-symmetric gapped systems can strongly enhance phonon-photon coupling, enabling robust polariton formation down to the monolayer limit despite electronic absorption. We illustrate these effects in NbSe2, hBN, and gapped graphene. Finally, we show that gauge invariance enforces photon decoupling from a critical soft phonon, establishing a general no-go mechanism for photon condensation.
authors: Mattia Udina, David Hagenmüller, Indranil Paul

articles.title: Viscous hydrodynamics from correlated losses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactions turn a gas into a fluid. We show that two-body loss can take their place. Correlated loss induces elastic scattering, as required by the optical theorem, which dominates at strong loss via the quantum Zeno effect. A nondegenerate gas with only two-body loss thus flows hydrodynamically, with viscosity and thermal conductivity close to those of the unitary Fermi gas. As loss heats the gas, both grow in time with a universal exponent 3/8. Unlike single-particle loss, two-body loss can engineer collisions, and hence transport, in quantum matter.
authors: Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Orjan Ameye, Oded Zilberberg, Jeff Maki

articles.title: Atomic ironing for conformal interfaces in freestanding oxide nanomembranes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomically well-defined interfaces are essential for realizing functional interlayer coupling in stacked and twisted oxide heterostructures, yet transferred freestanding oxides can develop structural inhomogeneities, including local curvatures, interfacial voids, and incomplete contacts with substrates. Here, we demonstrate that these transfer-induced structural disorders and imperfections evolve substantially and can be suppressed by post-transfer thermal treatments, yielding bulk-like crystalline freestanding oxide nanomembranes. Using freestanding SrTiO3 membranes as a model system, we report a systematic understanding of the role of "atomic ironing" and the associated evolution of lattice mosaicity, interfacial roughness, and optical bandgap. We further demonstrate atomically bonded conformal interfaces in twisted SrTiO3 heterostructures, highlighting the importance of post-transfer thermal processes. These results establish a synthetic strategy to restore the structural integrity and intrinsic bulk-like functionality of freestanding oxide nanomembranes, enabling stacked, twisted, and heterogeneously integrated oxide architectures with atomically well-defined interfaces for emerging quantum functionalities.
authors: Jeongkeun Song, Keaghan Knight, Keun-Yeol Park, Young-Hoon Kim, Tyler J. Sachs, Hu Miao, Jiaqiang Yan, Celesta S. Chang, Ambrose Seo, Ho Nyung Lee

articles.title: Active Sculpting: morphodynamics of internally stirred active vesicles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active flows are often confined by soft, deformable boundaries that they can push against, reshape, and in turn get reorganized by. Motivated by this interplay, we combine theory and numerical simulations to analyze the morphodynamics of an elastic vesicle enclosing a dilute suspension of extensile active particles. We model the two-dimensional vesicle as a weakly extensible elastic ring with bending rigidity, immersed in a Stokesian fluid, and describe the confined active suspension using a kinetic theory. The vesicle and the suspension are coupled hydrodynamically, through the kinematic and dynamic boundary conditions at the interface, and energetically, through a single alignment interaction that simultaneously aligns active particles with the membrane and the membrane with the particles. We show that this interaction reduces to a weak-anchoring boundary condition familiar from passive liquid crystals and derive a closed-form quiescent equilibrium state in which the nematic order in the suspension organizes into a vortex with a +1 defect core. A stability analysis of this state predicts an ordered hierarchy of activity thresholds at which successive shape modes of the vesicle are destabilized, as well as a purely passive, anchoring-driven instability of floppy vesicles. Nonlinear simulations, performed with a volume-conserving immersed boundary method, reveal that each threshold crossing gives rise to a distinct emergent state: a static spindle with boundary-pinned defects, a rotor that tank treads against its own rotation, a fluctuating spinner, and a turbulent state in which the vesicle acts as a self-stirring compartment. Beyond demonstrating how boundary deformability sculpts, and is sculpted by, confined active matter, our results open the door to study hydrodynamic interactions between such active vesicles and to use membrane fluctuations as a probe of activity of suspensions.

articles.title: Nonadiabatic dynamics under slow parametric modulation in nonlinear graphene resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonantly driven nonlinear systems, from superconducting circuits to nanomechanical resonators, are often described in a rotating frame, where amplitude and phase evolve slowly within a fixed landscape of stable and unstable states. How such systems behave when this landscape moves on their intrinsic timescale remains to be understood. Here, we exploit the strong tension sensitivity of a graphene drum's resonance frequency to reshape the rotating-frame phase space of a bistable mechanical mode in real time, combining an MHz-frequency resonant drive with kHz-frequency tension modulation. When the modulation rate becomes comparable to the mechanical relaxation rate, adiabatic tracking of the fixed points breaks down. Instead, parametric instabilities emerge in the slow dynamics at frequencies set by libration around these points rather than by the mechanical resonance; stronger modulation drives period doubling and chaos. A slow-variable theory predicts where the instabilities occur, and Melnikov analysis captures the onset of chaos. These results show that the rotating frame itself can be parametrically driven, offering a general route to controlling nonadiabatic dynamics in systems ranging from Josephson bifurcation amplifiers to cold atoms.
authors: Chris F. D. Wattjes, Haemin Lim, Pierpaolo Belardinelli, John E. Sader, Peter G. Steeneken, Farbod Alijani

articles.title: Andreev-reflection spectroscopy of SrPt3P single crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between inversion symmetry breaking and superconducting pairing mechanisms is a long-standing puzzle of solid-state physics. Ternary platinum phosphide SrPt₃P is an excellent case study in this regard, since it shares the distorted anti-perovskite crystal structure of non-centrosymmetric superconductor CePt₃Si but preserves the inversion symmetry center, enabling a direct comparison between the two compounds. Despite intense scrutiny, the superconducting pairing strength, gap symmetry, and magnitude of SrPt₃P remain an open question. Here, we study the gap structure of high-quality SrPt₃P single crystals with T_c = 8.6 K by using point-contact Andreev-reflection spectroscopy. The spectra systematically showed symmetric conductance maxima and a zero-bias minimum, as is typical of fully gapped superconductors, and dips at finite voltage V_dip due to the local transition of the contact region to the resistive state. In contacts with high resistance, where the dips fall sufficiently far from the gap features, the conductance curves can be well fitted with a single isotropic s-wave gap. The temperature dependence Δ(T) of the gap amplitude extracted from the fit is in good agreement with the one predicted by the BCS theory, with a zero-temperature mean value Δ(0)=1.88±0.08 meV, and a mean gap ratio 2Δ/k_BT_c = 5.2±0.2.
authors: Valeriy A. Stepanov, Nikolai D. Zhigadlo, Erik Piatti, Dario Daghero

articles.title: Observation of correlations beyond the single-particle picture in fermionic counting statistics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The analysis of charge fluctuations in a mesoscopic device can shed light on the fundamental question of whether or not a single-particle picture of electron transport is appropriate, even in the presence of Coulomb interaction. It has been shown on general grounds that mapping the interacting system onto a fermionic single-particle description is subject to strict constraints on the charge-transfer statistics. These constraints can be formulated in terms of a sign rule for the factorial cumulants of the full counting statistics. We report here on the experimental observation of a sign-rule violation in a most elementary model system, i.e. a single-level quantum dot, and provide theoretical modeling that can quantitatively reproduce the experimental data. This reveals the presence of correlations introduced by electron-electron interaction.
authors: Johann Zöllner, Hendrik Mannel, Daniel Oppers, Martin Geller, Axel Lorke, Jürgen König

articles.title: Dicke model of open-shell atoms with tensor polarizability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the extended Dicke model obtained from the scalar--vector--tensor polarizability of open-shell atoms coupled to a shared cavity mode. For a single electric-dipole channel, rotational symmetry fixes the tensor to vector ratio; we use ¹⁶⁸Er with J=6 as a product-state example. A circular pump produces a chiral Raman vertex whose tensor-dependent matrix elements select the occupied Zeeman sector. The resulting first-order transition occurs before the empty-cavity branch loses local stability, and the ordered state is read out through łanglehat J_zångle. A linear pump instead produces an empty-cavity ± x cat and a continuous transition into an even-m cat-like state with order parameter łanglehat J_z²ångle. With cavity loss alone, the circular trajectory emits a photon burst and approaches a Raman-dark Zeeman pole rather than a finite-field condensate. In the linear geometry, cavity-bright modes are damped toward the cat-like branch while a dark spin mode remains undamped. These are phenomena of that model; the vector-only controls show that they depend on the channel-fixed tensor coupling.

articles.title: Unconventional quantum spin mixing of two spin-1 atoms beyond the single-mode approximation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The single-mode approximation (SMA) has been widely employed in ultracold spinor gases, where all spin components share the same spatial mode. By adopting generalized Van Vleck (GVV) perturbation theory, we achieve a relative error of 10⁻⁶ in the ground-state energy with a reduced effective Hilbert space dimension of sim 10³ for two spin-1 bosons confined in a one-dimensional hard-wall trap. With the accurate GVV method, we explore the validity of the SMA across ground-state properties and quench spin dynamics for two ⁷Li, ⁸⁷Rb, or ²³Na atoms. Numerical results show that the quadratic Zeeman energy q provides a powerful control knob: by increasing |q|, the fidelity between the spin components in the ground state gradually decreases, leading eventually to the breakdown of the SMA (due to the competition between the kinetic energy and the quadratic Zeeman energy). Quench spin dynamics with abruptly increased q further reveals multiple resonances, where the SMA-predicted micromotion and beyond-SMA macromotion appear simultaneously. These results point to a direction to investigate the quantum spin-mixing dynamics beyond the SMA, particularly in recent experiments of strongly interacting spin-1 atomic gases.
authors: Yanhong Liu, Fulin Deng, Haoxue Qiao, Wenxian Zhang

articles.title: Analog Cosmology in a Quenched Bose-Einstein Condensate Bubble
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent interest and realization of ultracold bosons confined in shell-shaped, or bubble, traps have opened up several directions in the study of Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) in intrinsically curved geometries. Here, we explore the prospect of using thin spherical shell-shaped BECs as analog gravity simulators of an expanding or contracting curved universe. We study an interacting BEC bubble subject to a temporal quench of the interaction strength. Our theoretical approach, which uses a Bogoliubov treatment following a dimensional reduction of a spherical BEC to the low-energy excitations of a shell-shaped structure, demonstrates how this system serves as a laboratory analog for a positively curved universe having a time-varying scale factor. We investigate spontaneous pair production triggered by quenches associated with exponentially decaying or growing interaction strengths, focusing on the emergence of oscillations in the structure factor---analogous to Sakharov oscillations in the Cosmic Microwave Background angular power spectrum. We quantify the entanglement of the produced pairs via logarithmic negativity, and show how this measure may be extracted from the power spectrum. These findings establish a bridge between quantum information science and early-universe cosmology in a laboratory setting.
authors: Ruotong Zhai, Brendan Rhyno, Zain Mehdi, Naceur Gaaloul, Smitha Vishveshwara, Daniel E. Sheehy

articles.title: Metallic electron crystals in rhombohedral graphene as a bridge to twisted WSe₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting phases have recently been discovered both in twisted bilayers of transition metal dichalcogenide WSe₂ (tWSe₂₎ and in rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG). While both have generated extensive interest, they appear to be driven by qualitatively different physics. Here, we propose a unified picture in which the superconductivity in RMG arises from a strongly correlated metallic state with a spatial length scale that is compatible with the moiré length scale of tWSe₂. Central to this mechanism is a Wigner crystal phase in RMG that is metallic, driven by a "W"-shaped dispersion in the flat part of the underlying graphene band structure. We demonstrate this effect through calculations of Wigner crystal states in pentalayer RMG, focusing on dilute electrons in the quarter-metal regime relevant to experiment. In a region of the phase diagram we find the Wigner crystal breaks three-fold rotation symmetry, which guides our construction of a t-V model on a triangular lattice as an effective description of the low-energy electronic physics. This construction suggests a surprisingly similar low-energy description of RMG and tWSe₂. Broader implications for superconductivity in dilute carrier systems are also discussed.
authors: Wentai Deng, Chenyuan Li, Naoto Nakatsuji, Fang Xie, Lei Chen, Qimiao Si, Jennifer Cano

articles.title: Landau quantization of C₃ high-fold fermions in honeycomb lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the theory of the Landau levels of C₃ high-fold fermions in honeycomb lattices. These fermions arise as a generalization of the tight-binding model in a honeycomb lattice with one orbital per site, known to describe graphene, to a family of models with several orbitals per site transforming according to representations of C₃, relevant for triangulene two-dimensional crystals. The models are defined by the number of orbitals nₐ and n_b at the a and b sites of the unit cell. They feature energy bands that combine flat bands and Dirac cones, that are isomorphic to those of graphene, the Lieb, pₓy honeycomb, and the Kagome tight-binding models. Combining tight-binding and kḑot p methods, here we compute the Landau levels of the (1,1), (1,2), (2,2) and (3,3) models, we compare them to those of the reference models, and we explore the similarities and differences with the Landau levels in graphene. Our findings reveal that the nature of C₃ high-fold fermions combine Dirac-type Landau quantization, originating from the linear crossings and associated relativistic band dispersion, with anomalous Landau quantization rooted in the quantum geometry of the singular flat bands.

articles.title: Anomalies, higher symmetries, and homotopy theory I: crossed precosheaves and a nonabelian Cech construction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection. To a crossed precosheaf and a finite family of regions we attach a pointed connected homotopy type, the Cech-Loday classifying space. As the family of regions ranges over finite covers of space, the classifying spaces form a pro-object in the homotopy category. There is a canonical map from the ordinary classifying space of the symmetry group to this pro-type. Composing this map with a group action gives an anomaly whose nontriviality obstructs gauging. In favorable cases, the Cech-Loday space is essentially independent of the cover. In such cases, the homotopy fiber of the canonical map is a candidate for the classifying space of the higher group of symmetries. We give examples of crossed precosheaves arising from gauge transformations in continuum field theory and from quantum cellular automata and finite-depth circuits. For quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, our construction recovers the Else-Nayak index and its generalizations to two dimensions.

articles.title: Cavity-assisted dynamic nuclear polarisation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamic nuclear polarisation transfers polarisation from electron to nuclear spins by relying on a dissipative channel. Here we introduce a cavity-based DNP mechanism which uses the radiative relaxation of the electronic spin through the Purcell effect to bring about the nuclear spin polarisation. We implement this protocol on an ensemble of bismuth donor spins (I=9/2, S=1/2) in isotopically purified silicon coupled to a superconducting resonator. A single cycle, combining adiabatic microwave and radio-frequency pulses with Purcell relaxation, increases a target ground state's population by a factor of 1.79±0.04; a cumulative enhancement of 4.6±0.2 is reached with additional cycles, to be compared with the theoretical limit of ninefold set by the degeneracy of the ground manifold. We explain this difference by the competition between Purcell and intrinsic relaxation on the one hand and a collective effect that slows down the electronic spin radiative decay as the nuclear spin population grows on the other hand. Our results place radiative DNP as an available mechanism at millikelvin temperatures where phonon-mediated relaxation is frozen.
authors: Tristan Lorriaux, Yutian Wen, Patrice Bertet, Benjamin Huard, Audrey Bienfait

articles.title: Dynamical Decoupling of Nonclassical States in a Biased-Noise Spin Qudit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19676v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Encoding quantum information in d-dimensional systems (qudits) with d>2 offers appealing new directions for resource-efficient quantum computing. However, protecting the coherence of nonclassical qudit resource states remains an open challenge. Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a well-established technique for extending coherence, but its application to qudits is hindered by the quadratic scaling of the decoupling sequence overhead with the dimension d. As a result, demonstrations of qudit DD have so far been limited to low-dimensional qudits. Here, we show that noise-biased qudits enable a nontrivial reduction of this overhead, for example, from quadratic to linear. We perform qudit DD on a model d=8 qudit, the nuclear spin of an antimony donor in silicon. We benchmark DD performance on highly nonclassical states such as uniform superpositions, cat states, and Haar random states and measure coherence improvements up to a factor 5 to 10. For a spin-cat error correction code, continuous DD extends the coherence time of the logical superposition |+ångle_L to 225~ms, compared to 19~ms under free evolution and 85~ms with a Hahn echo. This improvement shows that DD sequences tailored to a system's noise bias can significantly enhance the lifetime of encoded logical qubits.
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Namit Anand, Rocky Y. Su, Akram Youssry, Ritik Sareen, Jeffrey Marshall, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Danielle Holmes, Benjamin Wilhelm, Bibek Pokharel, Xi Yu, Laura A. O'Neill, Martin Nurizzo, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Andrea Morello

articles.title: Single and coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators: Wigner-function dynamics, exact qutrit solutions, and synchronization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study quantum van der Pol oscillator in which single-photon pumping competes with a nonlinear two-photon dissipative channel to produce a quantum limit cycle, and the question of how two such oscillators with non-identical intrinsic frequencies synchronize in the sense of phase locking when coupled dissipatively to one another. For a single oscillator, starting from a Lindblad description of the dynamics, we derive the exact Wigner-function evolution equation, and show that its Fokker--Planck approximation admits in the appropriate regime an equivalent classical Itô stochastic description that reproduces remarkably well the full Lindblad dynamics. Notably, the stochastic approach provides an efficient means of capturing system dynamics in the semiclassical regime, where a large number of energy eigenstates contribute and direct numerical simulations become computationally demanding. Restricting to the three lowest Fock states and using a parity symmetry, we obtain in closed form the stationary-state density matrix and its Wigner-function representation that displays pronounced nonclassical features. For two non-identical oscillators, we study the full Lindblad dynamics numerically and characterize synchronization through the stationary-state order parameter as a function of frequency mismatch and dissipative coupling. We find that increasing the effective nonlinear dissipative strength suppresses the synchronized region. Restricting the two oscillators to the three-level qutrit subspace, a parity symmetry reduces the stationary-state problem to an exact 41-dimensional linear system, allowing to compute the synchronization order parameter. In this reduced description, results in the limit of large dissipation agree closely with those from the full dynamics, while exhibiting in the limit of small dissipation a double-peak synchronization structure accompanied by a phase reversal.
authors: Rohitashwa Chattopadhyay, Vinayak Pendse, Shamik Gupta

articles.title: Majorana Edge Modes Reshape Kibble-Zurek Scaling in Kitaev Honeycomb Ribbons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19923v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent progress in programmable quantum simulators motivates exact benchmarks for nonequilibrium dynamics in topological quantum matter. We study the Kitaev honeycomb model driven through its critical regions by a linear ramp of the bond coupling J_z over a ramp time τ, comparing zigzag and armchair ribbons with fully periodic tubes. The production of excitations exhibits a geometry-dependent finite-size crossover controlled by N₂/sqrtτ, the ratio of the ribbon width to the Kibble--Zurek length. Periodic tubes obey the expected critical-line Kibble--Zurek scaling and serve as the boundary-free benchmark. Zigzag ribbons follow the same scaling until defect production is exponentially suppressed by a finite-width algebraic gap floor associated with the formation of Majorana edge modes, whose occupation is pinned by inversion parity. Armchair ribbons instead support transient Majorana edge modes with exponentially small gaps, producing width-parity-dependent defect plateaus: exactly one defect per unit length for odd widths and an approximate, transient plateau near one half for even widths. The quench-generated entanglement entropy and fermionic logarithmic negativity inherit the same geometry-dependent structure, and the negativity further distinguishes the coherence-borne entanglement of the Kibble--Zurek regime from the population-borne entanglement of the edge-mode plateaus. These results identify boundary Majorana modes as the mechanism controlling departures from ideal Kibble--Zurek dynamics and provide geometry-resolved benchmarks for programmable simulations of topological matter.
authors: Hyesung Choi, Antonio Mandarino, Mahn-Soo Choi

articles.title: In-Plane Differentiation and Out-of-Plane Coherence in Superconducting K₂₋ₓFe₄₊ySe₅
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.10443v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The structural link between superconductivity and anomalous d₂ diffraction signatures in K₂₋ₓFe₄₊ySe₅ remains unresolved. Their appearance is accompanied by pronounced host-lattice evolution rather than a static structural background. Using high-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we show that excess Fe alters the vacancy-ordered host lattice, with structural differences between superconducting and nonsuperconducting states emerging before the d₂ features appear. All observed d₂ reflections can be described using two characteristic in-plane spacings and a nearly common low-temperature c parameter. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal that superconductivity is associated with persistent in-plane differentiation and enhanced Fe-layer coherence along the c axis. These results establish host-lattice evolution as the common structural origin linking the d₂ family and superconductivity, and suggest that the host-lattice differentiation identified here represents a structural analogue of the symmetry redistribution in FeSe.
authors: Chih-Han Wang, Wu Phillip M, Gwo-Tzong Huang, Ming-Jye Wang, Maw-Kuen Wu

articles.title: A quantum annealing approach to the minimum distance problem of quantum codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2404.17703v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) are at the heart of fault-tolerant quantum computing. As the size of quantum platforms is expected to grow, one of the open questions is to design new optimal codes of ever-increasing size. A related challenge is to certify the quality of a given code by evaluating its minimum distance, a quantity characterizing code's capacity to preserve quantum information. This problem is known to be NP-hard. Here we propose to harness the power of contemporary quantum platforms to address this question, and in this way help design quantum platforms of the future. Namely, we introduce an approach to compute the minimum distance of quantum stabilizer codes by reformulating the problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem and leveraging established QUBO algorithms and heuristics as well as quantum annealing (QA) to address the latter. The reformulation as a QUBO introduces only a logarithmic multiplicative overhead in the required number of variables. We demonstrate the formulation using the D-Wave Advantage 4.1 quantum annealer and the hybrid quantum-classical algorithm Qbsolv, and benchmark the resulting QUBO-based implementations against specialized classical distance-finding methods. The QA- and SA-assisted implementations show broadly comparable performance, while the classical comparison clarifies the relative strengths of heuristic optimization and exact distance certification. Our results establish a solver-independent QUBO formulation with only a logarithmic multiplicative overhead in the number of variables and characterize connectivity and minor embedding as central limitations of its present implementation on quantum-annealing hardware.
authors: Refaat Ismail, Ashish Kakkar, Anatoly Dymarsky

articles.title: Renormalisation of Quantum Cellular Automata
articles.abstract: arXiv:2407.12652v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a coarse-graining procedure for quantum cellular automata on hypercubic lattices that consists in grouping neighboring cells into tiles and selecting a subspace within each tile. This is done in such a way that multiple evolution steps applied to this subspace can be viewed as a single evolution step of a new quantum cellular automaton, whose cells are the subspaces themselves. We derive a necessary and sufficient condition for renormalizability and use it to investigate the renormalization flow of cellular automata on a line, where the cells are qubits and the tiles are composed of two neighboring cells. The problem is exhaustively solved, and the fixed points of the renormalization flow are highlighted.
authors: Lorenzo Siro Trezzini, Alessandro Bisio, Paolo Perinotti

articles.title: Work statistics of sudden quantum quenches: A random matrix theory perspective on Gaussianity and its deviations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.09640v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that, for sudden quenches, the work distribution reduces to the statistics of the traces of powers of Haar unitaries, which are random unitary matrices drawn uniformly from the unitary group. For translation-invariant quadratic fermionic chains with interactions extending to m neighbors and periodic boundary conditions, the Loschmidt amplitude admits a unitary matrix model / Toeplitz representation, which yields a work variable of the form W=sumᵣłₑ ₘ aᵣ ReøperatornameTr U^r (and in models with pairing terms -superconducting pairing- additional bᵣ ImøperatornameTr U^r terms appear). By invoking multivariate central limit theorems for vectors of traces of unitaries, we obtain a Gaussian distribution for P(W) with variance Var(W)=frac12sumᵣ r (aᵣ²⁺bᵣ²⁾ and asymptotic independence across different powers. We also characterise the conditions under which non-Gaussian tails arise, for example from many interaction terms or their slow decay, as well as the appearance of Fisher-Hartwig singularities. We illustrate these mechanisms in the XY chain. Various numerical diagnostics support the analytical results.

articles.title: Exploring the proximity effect of thin tungsten-aluminum films for phonon-mediated kinetic inductance detectors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lowering the energy threshold of phonon-mediated kinetic inductance detectors is a key step toward next-generation cryogenic calorimeter arrays with large target mass and high sensitivity. In this work, we demonstrate the feasibility of integrating thin tungsten films, so far used for transition-edge sensors, into the fabrication of Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs). Here we present the results from the characterization of a single KID prototype composed of a tungsten-aluminum bilayer of respectively 15 nm and 35 nm thicknesses. The detector was successfully calibrated, and the superconducting film characteristics were measured by operating the device at different temperatures. We show that, by exploiting the proximity effect of superconductors, the device combines the relatively high critical temperature of aluminum with the large kinetic inductance contribution of tungsten. The main feature is a high kinetic inductance, which accounts for 36% of the total inductance, combined with a superconducting critical temperature of around 630 mK.
authors: G. Del Castello, M. Mancuso, A. Langenkämper, A. Bento, C. Bonomo, M. Cappelli, F. Casadei, E. Cipelli, A. Cruciani, D. Delicato, F. Dominsky, M. Folcarelli, D. Hauff, B. Mauri, C. Moore, L. Pesce, F. Petricca, F. Pröbst, D. Quaranta, M. Vignati, M. Zanirato

articles.title: Cavity-tunable Pseudospin-Hall Topology and Edge Transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological edge states are a hallmark of topological phases, with their existence tied to bulk band topology through bulk-edge correspondence. In photonic pseudospin-Hall systems, these states exhibit pseudospin-momentum locking, with lattice interactions and interface geometry determining each pseudospin's propagation direction. Reversing the pseudospin-dependent propagation direction without altering the lattice configuration or excitation handedness remains a fundamental challenge in controlling topological edge transport. Here, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate cavity-tunable topological edge transport in a microwave metasurface embedded within a metallic cavity. Varying the cavity height reshapes resonator interactions, driving band inversion and topological phase transition while preserving the lattice geometry. For a fixed domain-wall configuration, this transition reverses the propagation direction associated with each pseudospin while preserving pseudospin-momentum locking. Excitations with the same handedness are observed to launch edge waves propagating in opposite directions at their respective edge-band frequencies determined by the cavity height. These results establish cavity electrodynamics as an external means of controlling the bulk topology and reconfiguring the directional response of topological interfaces, creating new opportunities for topological wave routing in fixed photonic lattice structures.
authors: Minghui Niu, Yan Meng, Chengle Fan, Xiaoyuan Jiao, Jidong Song, Perry Ping Shum, Zhen Gao, Mengyao Li

articles.title: Cartesian and Curvilinear Anharmonic Frequencies and Intensities: Perturb-then-Diagonalize Polyad Transport and Adiabatic Discrete-Variable Representation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.20488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anharmonic intensities reveal vibrational coupling that band positions alone cannot determine. We derive explicit second-order infrared transition moments in curvilinear normal coordinates, including kinetic metric derivatives and transport through variational resonance polyads. The vibrational perturbation-to-second-order-then-diagonalization (VP2TD) treatment covers fundamentals, overtones, three-quantum transitions, and hot bands. A general computational platform combines Extended Symmetry-Adapted Local Coordinates (ESALCs), using Cartesian (ESALC-C) or internal (ESALC-I) primitives, with interchangeable quantum-chemical programs and parallel finite differences. Independent oscillator matrices verify the intensity equations; a molecular water check reproduces second-order amplitudes within 8.4×10⁻⁸ atomic units. Comparisons with established tools reproduce a formaldehyde Fermi polyad within 0.163 cm⁻¹ and 0.061 km mol⁻¹ and water Raman activities within 10⁻⁷ Angstrom⁶. For 29 matched formaldehyde rotational line pairs, the predicted hot-to-fundamental intensity ratio, using the measured lower-state energy, is consistent with the nuclear-spin-corrected median: the differences are 3.9% (ESALC-I) and 3.8% (ESALC-C), compared with a 15% uncertainty estimate for individual measured line intensities. Common analytic reference derivatives ensure identical harmonic observables, while internal coordinates reduce and localize intermode anharmonic couplings. Rotation-vibration constants extend the same tensor treatment. An integrated adiabatic discrete-variable representation treats large-amplitude motions, and finite-level partition functions provide anharmonic thermochemistry.

articles.title: Quantum-enhanced phase interrogation of a fiber-optic strain sensor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.19752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fiber-optic sensors enable high-sensitivity measurements of various physical parameters. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-enhanced interrogation of an all-fiber-optic Fabry-Perot resonator, employing entangled two-photon interference to probe directly strain-induced optical phase shifts. The resonator is interrogated by a narrow-linewidth laser that is frequency-locked to its resonance mode, thereby exploiting the cavity's inherent sensitivity to variations in the fiber length. To access the phase fluctuations transferred to the interrogation field due to external perturbations on the sensor, we implement an in-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer readout. This configuration allows the sensor to operate both with classical coherent light and with entangled photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. Harnessing two-photon entangled states corresponding to an N = 2 NOON state, we experimentally demonstrate a reduction of the measurement noise below the standard quantum limit. These results provide clear evidence of the quantum advantage in enhancing fiber-optic sensors under practical constraints on optical power.
authors: Romain Dalidet, Marialuisa Capezzuto, Hugo Degert, Davide D'Ambrosio, Saverio Avino, Anthony Martin, Sebastien Tanzilli, Laurent Labonte, Paolo De Natale, Gianluca Gagliardi

articles.title: A heuristic sketch how it could fit all together with time
articles.abstract: arXiv:2405.10335v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On a scientific meta-level, it is discussed how an overall understanding of the physical universe can be built on the basis of well-proven theories, observations, and recent experiments. In the light of almost a century of struggle to make (common) sense of Quantum Mechanics and to reconcile it with General Relativity, it is proposed to (for some time) forget about quantizing gravity or striving for one Theory of Everything or 'Weltformel', which would describe the whole of reality seamlessly without any joints or suture marks. Instead of one single monolithic formalism, a three-legged compound approach is argued for. Quantum Mechanics, Relativity and Thermodynamics are proposed as the main pillars of reality, each with its well-defined realm, specific features, and clearly marked interfaces between the three of them. Not only classical reality, which is rather directly accessible to us, is then comprehensively modelled by their encompassing combination. Quantum phenomena are understood as undoubtedly lying at the bottom of classical physics and at the same time, they become 'fully real' only when embedded in classical frames, i.e., preparation and measurements in time. It is then where thermodynamics steps in and provides the mediating glue as it does at interfaces towards gravity. Decoherence is understood as a smooth way of gradually transferring information and basically dumping entropy to a suitable environment. The aim of this short contribution is not to deliver novel quantitative results but rather to propose a comprehensive research program and to coarsely lay out a very roughly coherent sketch starting from the beginning of the one universe, which we inhabit. The all-embracing picture is claimed to be one of ('mutually induced') emergence.

articles.title: The Soul of Waves: Physical Interpretation of Dispersion Relations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.17098v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This pedagogical paper presents a comprehensive framework for interpreting dispersion relations across fundamental physical systems. We adopt a novel approach that starts from the mathematical form ømega(k) and systematically extracts its physical content, rather than deriving it from first principles. Through an in-depth case study of the massive Klein-Gordon dispersion relation ømega² = ømega₀² + c²k², we demonstrate how this single equation encodes phase velocity, group velocity, density of states, effective mass, and impedance. The analysis reveals the universal nature of this dispersion form, which manifests in quantum fields, plasmas, superconductors, and photonic crystals with different physical interpretations of its parameters. We complement this with detailed examination of classical systems including mass-spring chains and hydrodynamic waves, providing tangible analogies that bridge conceptual understanding between quantum and classical wave phenomena. The paper includes eleven carefully designed figures that visualize key concepts and a comprehensive catalog of dispersion relations in the Appendix. Aimed at advanced undergraduates and instructors, this work emphasizes conceptual understanding through physical interpretation, offering a unified pedagogical framework for teaching wave propagation across physics curricula while maintaining mathematical rigor and depth.

articles.title: Fundamental Limits on QBER and Distance in Quantum Key Distribution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.22319v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretic secure communication, yet its ultimate tolerance to noise and achievable transmission distance remain fundamentally constrained. We establish the maximum quantum bit error rate (QBER) compatible with secure QKD and derive corresponding upper bounds on communication distance. Our results follow from a fundamental capacity threshold for qubit Pauli channels and apply to protocols based on two or more mutually unbiased bases, using either single-photon or weak coherent sources. By connecting information-theoretic limits to realistic physical noise models, we obtain universal bounds on achievable distances in fiber and free-space links, including diffraction-limited constraints relevant to deep-space quantum communications. These findings clarify the ultimate noise robustness of QKD and delineate the fundamental boundaries of secure quantum communication.

articles.title: A symmetry-field theoretical framework for quasi-stationary interfaces in fully miscible fluids
articles.abstract: Long-lived sharp interfaces in fully miscible fluids exhibit a transient quartic excess free-energy landscape and a Fermi–Dirac logistic concentration profile, whose microscopic statistical-mechanical origin has remained unresolved. Here, we develop an independent statistical-mechanical theory based on a microscopic pair Hamiltonian and the corresponding grand partition function. Exchange symmetry naturally introduces the invariant p=c1−c, whose regular local expansion uniquely generates the quartic excess free-energy density as the leading nonvanishing contribution after coarse-graining the microscopic Hamiltonian. The resulting free-energy functional completely determines the Euler–Lagrange equation of the quasi-stationary interface, whose exact solution is the Fermi–Dirac logistic profile. The independently derived microscopic formulation converges to the same quartic free-energy functional obtained previously from a continuum variational approach, thereby establishing a unified microscopic statistical-mechanical framework for quasi-stationary interfaces.

articles.title: Optical skyrmions can control the motion of magnetic skyrmions
articles.abstract: Magnetic skyrmions (MSks) are swirling patterns of magnetization that form inside certain magnetic materials. They can behave like actual particles in many ways, exhibiting a stable internal structure and distinct boundaries. Because they are extremely small and can be pushed around with relatively little energy, MSks are regarded as promising information carriers in emerging technologies, including low-power memories and logic circuits. However, a major goal in the field has been to find practical ways to control their motion with high precision.

articles.title: Platonic Projection Structures: Operator-Induced Observability in Representation Learning
articles.abstract: We introduce Platonic Projection Structures (PPS), an operator-theoretic framework for analyzing observability in representation learning systems. Rather than treating observable outputs as direct reflections of latent representations, PPS models observation as a geometry induced by a self-adjoint positive semidefinite operator acting on a latent Hilbert space. Within PPS, a system is represented as a triple (H, Π, O), where Hdenotes a latent representation space, Π ⪰0 is an observation operator, and O(v) = ⟨v, Πv⟩defines an induced observable quantity. The framework characterizes observability through the quotient geometry H/ ker(Π), which represents equivalence classes of latent states that are indistinguishable under observation. From this perspective, observable behavior is governed not by latent representations themselves, but by the geometry induced through the observation operator. We show that both quantum measurement and deep learning inference can be formulated within this common operator-theoretic structure while differing in the algebraic properties of their observation operators. Within this perspective, quantum measurement serves primarily as a mathematically canonical example of projection-mediated observability. The correspondence developed in PPS is therefore structural rather than physical. Within the same framework, representation transfer and knowledge distillation can be interpreted as approximate preservation of observable geometry through the intertwining condition ΦΠT ≈ΠSΦ. PPS further reveals a structural limitation of output-based interpretability: latent components contained in ker(Π) are fundamentally inaccessible from observables generated through the induced observation process. Accordingly, attribution and explanation methods inherit intrinsic constraints imposed by the observation geometry itself. We provide controlled empirical validations demonstrating kernel-invariant observability, projection-induced attribution gaps, and rank-controlled observable geometry in latent representation spaces. Overall, PPS provides a mathematically explicit operator-theoretic perspective for analyzing observability, interpretability, and representation transfer in projection-mediated learning systems

articles.title: Quantum network test checks entanglement without having to trust detectors
articles.abstract: Quantum networks are systems that connect different users or devices using principles of quantum mechanics. In the future, these networks could help improve the security of communications.

articles.title: Non-Monotonic Exciton Transport Efficiency in Multi-layer Ring-shaped Quantum Networks inspired by Photosystem I
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photosystem I (PSI) is one of the most efficient natural photosynthetic complexes and serves as a structural prototype for understanding excitation energy transfer (EET) and designing artificial light-harvesting systems. Here, we construct a multilayer elliptical-conical quantum network inspired by PSI to investigate how antenna architecture affects EET. Excitation dynamics are simulated using the quantum jump approach combined with coherent modified Redfield theory (QJA-CMRT). The transfer efficiency exhibits a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence on pigment density, reaching a maximum of 0.86 at x=6 in the five-layer network. The optimal configuration contains 91 pigments, close to the number of core antenna pigments in natural PSI. Our combined density-of-states and kinetic analyses reveal that this nonmonotonic dependence originates from a trade-off: at low pigment densities, enhanced band overlap promotes energy transfer, whereas at high densities, excessive exciton delocalization compromises funnel directionality and reduces efficiency; the optimal configuration is consequently achieved at x=6. These findings provide insights into PSI antenna organization and offer guidelines for designing efficient artificial light-harvesting systems.
authors: Yi Li, Rui Li, Kai-Ya Zhang, Ming-Zi Jin, Tao Liu, Qing Ai

articles.title: Electric-dipole-induced nuclear electric resonance in silicon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nuclear spin of a phosphorus atom in silicon is considered as a promising quantum information carrier for quantum computing due to its long coherence time. Coherent control of the nuclear spin is typically realized using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). In this work, we theoretically propose that with the aid of hyperfine interactions and magnetic field gradients, fast electric-dipole-induced nuclear electric resonance (EDNER) can be achieved. The stronger EDNER (compared with NMR) arises from the combined effects of hyperfine interaction between the nuclear and electron spins and coupling between the electron spin and charge degrees of freedom mediated by magnetic field gradients in this scheme. By operating at specific working points, the nuclear-spin splitting becomes less sensitive to electrical noise, enabling long coherence times and high-fidelity quantum operations. All elctrical, addressable control of nuclear spins paves the way for scalable silicon-based quantum computing.
authors: Jiyun Su, Shihang Zhang, Peihao Huang

articles.title: Exact SU(N) symmetry resolution of bosonic Hubbard models: general boson-fermion mappings and flat-band singlet-cluster states
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how to perform exact diagonalization of SU(N)-symmetric Bose-Hubbard models separately in each irreducible representation of SU(N), by exploiting the Howe duality between U(L) and U(N). Three structural consequences follow for any lattice and any Hamiltonian built from the U(L) generators: (i) the spectrum in a given orbital sector is independent of N and of the particle statistics, (ii) the canonical partition functions for bosons and fermions obey the exact identity Zb(-N)=(-1)N_bZf(N), (iii) with unfrustrated hopping the groundstate is always a color ferromagnet, so that the color-resolved method we introduce is useful to study excited sectors, frustrated lattices and finite temperatures. As applications, we first derive the finite-temperature phase diagram of attractive SU(N) bosons on few-site rings at large N for arbitrary filling. We then show the emergence of singlet-cluster states from frustrated hopping, the counterpart of fermionic ferromagnetism, with the example of the sawtooth and kagome lattice.

articles.title: Emergence of quantum transport in SnTe films upon structural refinement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological crystalline insulators are distinguished from the conventional Z2 topological insulators by crystalline symmetry protection of the surface states. Quantitative characterization of these states requires magneto-transport measurements from which the phase coherence length and number of independent coherent channels can be extracted. Here we report such measurements on textured thin films of SnTe grown on Bi2Te3 buffered c-plane sapphire (Al2O3) by pulsed laser ablation. A post deposition annealing protocol was implemented to control the crystallographic texture, which reveals improved crystallinity and enhanced epitaxial alignment along the [111] direction in films annealed at elevated temperatures. The higher carrier density and lower resistivity seen in films annealed at 100 oC are suggestive of Sn vacancies which act as native acceptor defects, while films annealed at 200 oC approach the 1:1 stoichiometry. The magnetoresistance of all samples at T < 10 K characterized by a cusp centered around zero-field is suggestive of weak antilocalization and interpreted in the framework of the Hikami-Larkin-Nagaoka theory in the strong spin-orbit coupling limit. At T > 20 K, the MR is small and positive, and deviates from conventional Kohler scaling. An approximate collapse of the MR curves between 50 and 250 K is obtained using an empirical temperature-dependent scaling factor, indicating that changes in the Hall-derived carrier density alone cannot account for the observed scaling behavior. These results demonstrate that post growth annealing strongly influences the interplay between stoichiometry, crystallinity, and coherent transport in SnTe thin films.
authors: Shrinkhala Sharma, Rabindra Basnet, Thomas Parker, Afolabi Akinfaderin, Alexander Samokhvalov, Rajeswari Kolagani, Ramesh C. Budhani

articles.title: Benchmarking machine-learning interatomic potentials using classical force fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a rational comparison between several well-known machine-learning interatomic potentials (linear atomic cluster expansion, the Behler-Parrinello high-dimensional neural network potential, and the graph neural network-based MACE potential) by testing their performance for fitting classical potentials such as the Lennard-Jones and Stillinger-Weber potential. With this we assess their advantages and limitations regarding several aspects: varying training dataset size, robustness to noise, carbon footprint, as well as the ability to reproduce the radial distribution function as an example observable. Overall the MACE models are shown to most accurately reproduce the potential energy surface, with little sign of overfitting, but at a significant computational cost, highlighting important questions regarding the choice of models in computational materials science.
authors: Johannes Sandberg, Geneviève Dusson, Julien Lam

articles.title: Establishing the role of thickness in LaOBr; an alternative gate dielectric for vdW heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In electronic devices, the quality of the dielectric material is determined by figures of merit such as the band gap, leakage onset field, breakdown field and the number of built-in defects, which can all limit device performance. An additional and important metric to consider is the strength of the dielectric constant. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is the benchmark gate dielectric for two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures, owing to its wide bandgap, and atomically flat interface. At the same time, its dielectric constant (2--4) highlights the opportunity to explore alternative higher-permittivity van der Waals dielectrics that provide stronger electrostatic control. Previous work established lanthanum oxybromide (LaOBr), a layered dielectric with a predicted dielectric constant of 12.5, as a potential dielectric for van der Waals heterostructures. Using graphene field-effect devices with LaOBr, we show that the leakage-onset and breakdown fields decrease systematically with thickness. Dual-gate capacitance measurements combined with a dead-layer model reveal a bulk dielectric constant of ǎrepsilonbᵤₗₖ = 12.2, in agreement with theory, while interfacial dead-layers cause the effective dielectric constant to vary from 6 to 11 across multiple thicknesses. Benchmarked against established gate dielectrics, LaOBr combines breakdown fields comparable to hBN with dielectric constants 2 to 3 times larger. By establishing the operating regime of devices with various thicknesses, we further confirm the advantage of LaOBr over hBN for high-capacitance gate-dielectric operation. These results validate LaOBr as a promising dielectric for integration into two-dimensional heterostructures, and establish thickness-dependent benchmarking as essential for evaluating emerging layered dielectric materials.
authors: Isaac Antoine Lagaud, Justin Boddison-Chouinard, Antoine Labbé, Ayse Melis Aygar, Alex Bogan, Li-Lin Tay, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Aljoscha Söll, Zdeněk Sofer, Adina Luican-Mayer, Louis Gaudreau

articles.title: A Solution-Processed Ti/Pt/NiOx/Ag RRAM Device with Multiple Forming-Free Non-Volatile Intermediate States
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANN) implemented on crossbar arrays of non-volatile synaptic devices are known to consume much less energy compared to that implemented on conventional computing units. Solution-processed resistive random-access memory (RRAM) devices based on transition-metal oxides are suitable as such synaptic devices because of their cheap and easy fabrication method, stability, and suitable memristive properties.
