articles.title: Valley-resolved high harmonics probe symmetry breaking beyond the Dirac cone
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-energy electrons in graphene obey an emergent, rotationally invariant Dirac equation, while the honeycomb lattice enters only through higher-order, symmetry-breaking corrections, the leading one being trigonal warping. This provides a unique solid-state arena to address a cornerstone challenge in quantum gravity: how to detect ultraviolet symmetry-breaking granular corrections, suppressed by a fundamental scale, atop an emergent infrared relativistic continuum. We show that intense counter-rotating ømega-2ømega fields and valley-resolved high-harmonic generation (HHG) provide such a probe. Within a family of models that interpolates continuously between the isotropic Dirac cone and nearest-neighbour graphene at fixed Fermi velocity, the valley contrast of the harmonic yield vanishes identically in the symmetric theory, grows linearly with the warping coupling, and its valley-even counterpart appears only at second order, as expected from effective-field-theory power counting. The stronger the laser, the farther it drives electrons from the Dirac points, so the laser intensity plays the role of the collision energy. For the fourth harmonic, the leading warping correction alone accounts for the valley contrast of real graphene up to fundamental intensities of about 10¹¹ W/cm², below the damage threshold of monolayer graphene, whereas the fifth harmonic already reveals higher-order lattice corrections at intensities around 10¹⁰ W/cm². The two harmonics, which rotate in opposite directions, are emitted by opposite valleys. Valley-resolved harmonics are far more sensitive than the residual valley populations, making them a practical detector of lattice-scale physics hidden beneath an emergent Dirac theory.
authors: Pablo Pais, Alfredo Iorio, Marcelo F. Ciappina

articles.title: Matrix-product-state GPLHR for non-Hermitian many-body eigenproblems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing multiple eigenstates of non-Hermitian many-body operators plays an important role in investigating excitation spectra, spectral properties, and relaxation dynamics in interacting and open quantum systems. However, this task is challenging because the eigenvectors are generally nonorthogonal and the Hilbert space dimension grows exponentially with system size. Here, we formulate the generalized preconditioned locally harmonic residual (GPLHR) method in a matrix product state (MPS) framework to efficiently compute multiple targeted right eigenstates whose eigenvalues lie near a specified shift in the complex plane. Successive randomized compression (SRC) is employed to accelerate operator applications. We test the method on transcorrelated and complex Hubbard chains, an interacting non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain, and a Liouvillian model. The results demonstrate that GPLHR combined with MPS provides an efficient and accurate approach for computing multiple eigenstates of non-Hermitian many-body operators.
authors: Xingyao Wu, Zhangyu Yang, Yanbin Chen, Yu Wang, Feng Chen

articles.title: Ergodicity breaking transition beyond qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The local Hilbert space dimension is a fundamental parameter in quantum many-body systems, but its role in controlling the ergodicity-breaking transition remains less explored. We systematically study this question by introducing toy models of qudits in zero dimensions that exhibit an ergodicity-breaking transition. Using the hybridization condition, we analytically obtain the dependence of the critical value of the interactions on the local Hilbert space dimension. Numerical studies of spectral correlation measures show agreement with the theoretical predictions, hence confirming the existence of the ergodicity-breaking transition in these models. We further introduce a distinct higher spin version of the model and numerically obtain the same critical behavior, demonstrating that the observed critical point is independent of the microscopic structure of interactions considered.

articles.title: Eigenstate transitions and critical transport in 3D Aubry-André model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We numerically study spectral and wave-function properties, as well as time evolution, in finite-size commensurate approximations of the 3D Aubry-André model. We explicitly show, through scaling analysis, the existence of two critical points. One of the critical points is a localization-delocalization transition in real-space, similar to the critical point in the 3D Anderson model. The other is a localization-delocalization transition in a dual momentum space, which does not have any analog in the 3D Anderson model. We estimate their values from spectral measures, such as the gap ratio and the spectral form factor, as well as from wave-function measures, such as the inverse participation ratio and the participation entropy. Additionally, we demonstrate that both critical points exhibit hallmarks of critical points between quantum ergodicity and localization. First, the eigenstates and the eigenspectrum at the critical point fulfill the mutual universal relation between the eigenspectrum compressibility ḩi and the eigenstate fractal dimension d⁽¹⁾ [S. Jiricek et al., Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. 123, e2518027123 (2026)]. Second, the dynamics of the wave packet at the critical point is governed by the critical dynamical exponent z, characterized by the spectral fractal dimension and the dimensionality of the lattice [M. Hopjan and L. Vidmar, Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 060401 (2025)]. Thus, similarly to the 3D Anderson model, the critical dynamical exponent is sub-diffusive with the value of z=3.
authors: Pragna Das, Lev Vidmar, Miroslav Hopjan

articles.title: Epitaxial Oxide Thin Films with High Entropy and Anomalous Crystallinity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD) expands the compositional and structural possibilities of high-entropy oxide (HEO) thin films through far-from-equilibrium growth and kinetic arrest of metastable configurations. This review connects growth kinetics and epitaxial constraints to the roles of individual cations in shaping the resulting films. We focus primarily on rock salt MgCoNiCuZnO and its derivatives, with selected fluorite, spinel, and perovskite examples illustrating broader applicability. In MgCoNiCuZnO, Co valence and Cu coordination illustrate how chemistry and growth conditions jointly enable lattice tuning and coherent nanostructure formation, while aliovalent and size-misfit additions expand the accessible defect and compositional landscapes. These coupled degrees of freedom underpin anomalous crystallinity, the coexistence of extensive chemical disorder with exceptional crystalline quality and epitaxial order, including full coherence in selected systems, particularly rock salts grown on MgO. This combination opens opportunities to discover and engineer functional configurations in high-quality single-layer films and heterostructures.
authors: Joseph Petruska, Christina M. Rost, Jon-Paul Maria, Saeed S. I. Almishal

articles.title: High-mobility spin transport mediated by indirect excitons in a van der Waals heterostructure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient spin transport with high spin mobility is of both fundamental and practical significance for spintronics. Spin can be transferred by moving particles. However, particle scattering limits spin transfer and prevents high spin mobilities. In this work, we study the kinetics of spin transport mediated by a quantum system of indirect excitons (IXs) in a van der Waals heterostructure composed of atomically thin transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). This spin transfer mechanism allows for the realization of efficient spin transport characterized by a high spin mobility reaching 10⁵ cm²/(eVḑots), which is orders of magnitude higher than that achieved via standard diffusive spin transport in TMD materials. The suppression of IX scattering enables high-mobility spin transport.
authors: Zhiwen Zhou, W. J. Brunner, Luc M. Nguyen, C. A. Lozano, G. Mercado, L. H. Fowler-Gerace, L. V. Butov

articles.title: Pressure Evolution of the Superconducting Order Parameter of Kagome Superconductor CsV3Sb5
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A = K, Rb, Cs) offer an outstanding platform for exploring the interplay among charge-density-wave (CDW) order, superconductivity (SC), and nontrivial topological electronic states. For CsV3Sb5, moderate hydrostatic pressure induces a double-dome superconducting phase diagram while monotonically suppressing the CDW phase, which signals an unconventional coupling between SC and CDW. Nevertheless, the microscopic nature of the pressure-modulated superconducting state and its relationship with CDW order remain poorly understood. Here we employ soft directional point-contact spectroscopy (SDPCS), combined with superconducting resistive measurements, to probe the superconducting order parameter of CsV3Sb5 under hydrostatic compression. Our anisotropic PCAR measurements resolve two distinct s-wave superconducting gaps along the c-axis and a strongly anisotropic gap within the ab plane. Two-band Blonder-Tinkham-Klapwijk (BTK) fits to the c-axis spectra yield a large gap satisfying 2Delta1/kBTc > 3.52 and a small gap with 2Deltas/kBTc < 3.52. The spectral-weight-averaged coupling ratio 2Deltaavg/kBTc is enhanced in the pressure window between P1 and P2, suggesting that pressure-induced modifications of the low-energy electronic structure may contribute to the evolution of superconductivity. For ab-plane junctions, the superconducting gap anisotropy is gradually suppressed above P1, accompanied by the emergence of a pronounced peak-dip-hump structure suggestive of enhanced coupling between superconducting quasiparticles and a bosonic excitation. These results shed new light on the intricate entanglement between CDW and SC in kagome superconductivity.
authors: Haiyan Zuo, Wangju Yang, Zhifan Wu, Yuqing Zhao, Qiuxia Chen, Weiming Lao, Yangpeng Qi, Hechang Lei, Haizi Cong, Cong Ren

articles.title: Molecule-intercalated van der Waals Josephson junctions uncover complex multiband superconductivity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intercalation of molecular species provides a route to tailor the electronic structure in van der Waals superconductors, yet intercalated compounds have rarely been integrated into phase-sensitive quantum devices. Here, we realize hybrid molecular Josephson junctions based on TaS2/NbSe2 heterostructures. Selective intercalation of the TaS2 electrode induces monolayer-like Ising superconductivity, while the junctions exhibit asymmetric Fraunhofer interference, field-induced and spontaneous Josephson diode effects. The zero-field diode disappears upon reversing the electrode stacking and re-emerges after intercalating the lower NbSe2 electrode. These findings indicate that the hybrid superconducting electrode hosts unconventional superconductivity underlying the nonreciprocal transport, while molecular intercalation acts as a tuning knob for its internal phase structure. This behavior is consistent with a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking multiband superconducting state characterized by a nontrivial relative phase between superconducting condensates. Our results establish hybrid molecular Josephson junctions as a quantum-device platform for phase-sensitive investigation and integration of molecularly engineered superconductors, opening opportunities to uncover and engineer unconventional superconducting phases.
authors: Daniel Margineda, David Caldevilla-Asenjo, Covadonga Álvarez-García, Daniel Tezze, Raul Arenal, Maxim Ilyn, Celia Rogero, Luis E. Hueso, Marco Gobbi

articles.title: Optically driven ultrafast lattice contraction in a topological crystalline insulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ability to dynamically control topological order remains a central challenge in the exploration of quantum materials. Here, we investigate the lattice and electronic response of the topological crystalline insulator (TCI) Pb₁₋ₓSnₓSe to ultrafast optical excitation using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) in combination with X-ray diffraction (XRD) and first-principles calculations. Static XRD measurements establish the lattice constant as the key control parameter for the topological transition, with a critical value a_c=6.073 Å separating the normal-insulator and topological phases. Despite generating electronic temperatures far above the topological-to-normal transition temperature T_c, optical excitation in the TCI phase does not induce a phase transition. Instead, it drives an ultrafast lattice contraction of Δ a approx -0.45 pm within less than 1 ps that counteracts thermal expansion and prevents the system from reaching a_c. The optical excitation therefore pushes the system deeper into the topological phase, providing a direct explanation for the absence of an optically driven transition. Total-energy calculations reveal that this behavior originates from the band inversion in the topological regime, which reverses the character of the photoinduced charge transfer and transiently strengthens atomic bonding. These findings identify band inversion as a mechanism that fundamentally alters the nonequilibrium lattice response, with general implications for ultrafast optical control of topological materials.
authors: M. H. Berntsen, W. Chen, D. Phuyal, J. Wu, A. Grubišić-Čabo, M. Dendzik, Q. Guo, A. Orthaber, C. Li, R. M. Geilhufe, J. Weissenrieder, O. Tjernberg

articles.title: Probing quantum nonlinear phononics in multilayer graphene with time-resolved Raman scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherently driven phonons are conventionally described classically. Nonlinear phonon-phonon interactions, however, allow an infrared drive to reshape the fluctuation spectrum and generate substantial nonthermal enhancement of phonon fluctuations, motivating a description beyond the coherent displacement alone. We benchmark classical and semiclassical approximations against the full quantum theory and find that the semiclassical treatment substantially improves agreement with the quantum dynamics. We propose nonequilibrium spontaneous Raman scattering as a sensitive probe of these effects and apply our framework to recent experiments suggesting quantum nonlinear phononics involving the E₁ᵤ and E₂g modes in multilayer graphene. At very strong pump fields, driving the E₁ᵤ mode significantly modifies the E₂g Raman spectrum; however, reproducing the reported response at experimental field strengths requires accounting for pump-induced Raman matrix element dynamics or alternative energy pathways into the E₂g mode. Our findings extend nonlinear phononics beyond average atomic displacements to the dynamics of lattice fluctuations, highlighting the interplay between coherent motion and quantum correlations in driven materials.
authors: Jakob Dolgner, Michael Rübhausen, Dirk Manske

articles.title: Emergent Spinorial Structure in Mesoscopic Irreversible Thermodynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reconstruct a geometry of thermodynamic coordinates from transport coefficients within a mesoscopic canonical model. Self-adjoint flux observables determine a compatible evolution generator containing symmetric and antisymmetric transport coefficients. When the Hermitian transport tensor is positive, an exact graded first-order factorization reproduces this generator on its scalar sector. Its commutators define a spectral distance whose metric depends only on the symmetric tensor. Gradients of the antisymmetric tensor can change the evolution while leaving the metric unchanged. The construction allows coordinate-dependent coefficients. In the constant Onsager regime, a Clifford representation gives the same distance and an algebra fixed by the transport matrix. Published transport data for a Bi₂Te₃ film give a principal-distance ratio of approximately 2.12 in normalized coordinates at ZTsimeq0.68. We also examine a separate quadratic entropy-production observable and distinguish its discrete spectrum from the spectrum of the evolution generator. The spinorial representation adds no physical spin degrees of freedom.

articles.title: Transport Determines Spectral Distance in Mesoscopic Thermodynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a distance between thermodynamic states from a positive Hermitian transport tensor within a mesoscopic canonical model. An exact first-order factorization of the evolution generator gives a commutator norm and the metric G=2g⁻¹, where g denotes the symmetric transport tensor. Gradients of the antisymmetric tensor can change the evolution, but they leave this distance unchanged. The construction allows coordinate-dependent coefficients. For constant Onsager coefficients, a Clifford representation gives the same metric. In a two-channel thermoelectric system, the ratio of normalized principal distances is sqrt1+ZT+sqrtZT. Transport coupling thus fixes the anisotropy of this metric. The construction requires neither an independent metric nor a physical spin variable.

articles.title: Mutual information across the commensurate--incommensurate crossover and near the Kosterlitz--Thouless point of the spin-tfrac12 J₁₋₋J₂ Heisenberg chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What quantum mutual information adds to conventional correlation functions is often unclear. We study the spin-1/2 J₁₋J₂ Heisenberg chain, using DMRG on infinite chains and periodic rings and an SU(2) decomposition of the mutual information into correlation channels. For singlet ground states the two-site mutual information is an exact function of the spin correlator, so any additional content must come from blocks. In the dimerized phase, blocks resolve bond-energy correlations in the SU(2)-scalar channel without an independent asymptotic length: singlet and triplet correlation lengths agree to about 1%. The scalar channel dominates block mutual information at large distances in the commensurate regime up to J₂/J₁₌₀.40, but falls to a few percent beyond the disorder point, which coincides numerically with the Majumdar-Ghosh point J₂/J₁₌₁/2; the structure-factor peak splits only at the Lifshitz point J₂/J₁₌₀.520622(2). On the gapless side we compare block mutual information on rings extrapolated to infinite size with the two-interval prediction of SU(2)₁ conformal field theory across the Kosterlitz-Thouless point J₂/J₁₌₀.241167. There, for block lengths lłe6, the correction decays as l⁻p with p=1.96-2.07, and any logarithmic term is at least 60 times smaller than in the Heisenberg chain. Expanding in the marginal coupling (from level spectroscopy) the first-order coefficient is consistent with l⁻² scaling and the second-order coefficient is positive for xłe1/4, suggesting that the mutual information relative to the field-theory value becomes stationary at the KT point for large blocks. The scalar-channel share approaches 1/4 at small cross ratio x, as expected from SO(4) symmetry; under two stated assumptions its first-order response to the coupling is (3/8)łn x-5/8 at small x, matched by the l=4 data within 1-3% at xłe1/9.

articles.title: Microscopic Modeling of Interlayer Tunneling in Twisted Bilayer Cuprates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The field of twistronics, recently extended to twisted bilayer cuprate systems, has generated considerable interest due to the prediction of d+id' states close to a 45ⁱ̧rc twist, as suggested by multiple experimental probes. Theoretical studies of these systems using a variety of models and many-body theoretical techniques have revealed multiple competing order parameters. The large variability in experimental results and theoretical predictions demands an accurate microscopic model for these systems, in particular a more realistic description of the interlayer tunneling. In this study, we fit the in-plane hopping and compute the interlayer tunneling amplitudes by calculating the orbital overlap between dₓ^₂₋y^₂ wave functions at each site of the twisted square-lattice model. We observe sign-changing tunneling amplitudes, a strong twist-angle dependence of the direct tunneling term, and long-range tunneling amplitudes that often dominate over direct tunneling. We investigate the band structure, Fermi surfaces, and spectral functions in comparison with those obtained from the phenomenological model and find a substantial redistribution of spectral weight that modifies the competition between different superconducting ground states. We determine the phase diagram as a function of twist angle, filling, and direct tunneling strength, which is controlled by the c-axis distance between the monolayers, and observe a reduction in the region of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking (TRSB) d+id' states compared with the phenomenological model. Finally, we investigate the Josephson critical current across the phase diagram and find strongly suppressed critical currents close to a 45ⁱ̧rc twist, consistent with experimental observations.
authors: Siddhant Panda, Andreas Kreisel, Laura Fanfarillo, P. J. Hirschfeld

articles.title: H₂₋Like Units and Pressure-Tunable High-T_c Superconductivity in NaH₆
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.17148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hydrogen-rich materials offer a route to high-temperature conventional superconductivity, but often require extreme pressures. Here we report a first-principles study of NaH₆, identified in our large-scale hydride search and independently predicted in a subsequent high-throughput study. Several phases compete, with Rbar3m and Pmbar3m dominant over broad pressure ranges. The Rbar3m phase remains dynamically stable down to 10 GPa, where its calculated T_c is 34 K, rising to 99 K at 50 GPa. Cubic Pmbar3m becomes thermodynamically competitive at higher pressures and reaches a calculated T_c of 230 K at 50 GPa, decreasing only weakly upon further compression. Molecular dynamics and phonon-renormalization calculations support structural persistence over the sampled timescale and indicate relatively small anharmonic effects. Despite their high T_c, both phases contain elongated H₂₋ₗᵢₖₑ units, often considered unfavorable for high-T_c hydrides. Mode-resolved electron-phonon coupling links Raman-active hydrogen vibrations to superconductivity. In Rbar3m, the linewidths of these modes increase with the pressure-induced tilt of H₂ units relative to the threefold axis, alongside the rise in T_c. A minimal symmetry-based model of the vibration-induced second-moment tensor of the hydrogen sublattice shows that these trends are consistent with a significant contribution from response components perpendicular to the threefold axis. NaH₆ thus represents an unusual molecular-like hydride in which hydrogen-sublattice reorganization may enable high-T_c superconductivity at comparatively moderate pressures.

articles.title: Pairing from repulsive interactions in twisted WSe2 from functional renormalization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.17222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the observation of superconductivity in twisted bilayer WSe₂ over an extended range of displacement fields, reaching from the correlated insulator down to zero field, we analyze the correlated electron phases of this system at hole filling ν = -1 and twist angle 3.65ⁱ̧rc using Hartree--Fock, random phase approximation, and functional renormalization group calculations. We derive a continuum model with gate-screened Coulomb interaction from first principles and compare its instabilities to those of a realistic three-orbital Wannier model with a Hubbard interaction and an artificial single-orbital Hubbard model. In both cases, we find a superconducting instability of mixed d-wave singlet and p-wave triplet character, arising adjacent to inter-valley-coherent spin-density-wave order in the phase diagram spanned by displacement field and interaction strength. Our additional analysis of the pairing mechanism points to inter-valley coherent spin fluctuations as the pairing glue. The extent of the pairing regime and the associated critical temperatures depend on the model input, and we trace differences to the interaction range entering the projected interaction. Within the continuum model, the gate-screened Coulomb interaction yields pairing down to zero displacement field, bringing theory into agreement with experiment.
authors: Hannes Braun, Dumitru Călugăru, Pietro M. Bonetti, Haoyu Hu, Yan Zhang, Yi Jiang, Quansheng Wu, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan, B. Andrei Bernevig, Michael M. Scherer, Laura Classen

articles.title: Turning a superconducting diode into a Feynman ratchet to realize a nanoscale heat engine
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.17257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feynman's ratchet illustrates how work can be extracted from thermal fluctuations in the presence of two heat baths at different temperatures. While some experimental realizations of the ratchet effect have been studied, most lack miniaturization, which is important for some applications. Here, we propose a physical implementation of Feynman's ratchet based on Josephson junctions exhibiting the superconducting diode effect. This setup functions as a heat engine that generates work solely from a temperature gradient via thermal fluctuations. We analyze its output power and efficiency, and, through the Seebeck coefficient, identify the conditions under which the device operates in reverse, functioning instead as a Peltier cooler.
authors: Konstantinos Kontogeorgiou, İnanç Adagideli, Géraldine Haack, Fabian Hassler

articles.title: Definition of Multi-Parameter Super-Resolution for Optical Telescopes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Super-resolution techniques in microscopy are opening new frontiers in biology, and super-resolution for telescope imaging may provide similar benefits for astronomy and space domain awareness. Telescope super-resolution techniques such as multi-plane light conversion and photonic lanterns have been inspired by the ability of mode sorting measurements to extract classical Fisher information closer to the quantum bound than standard telescope imaging. Fisher information analyses for super-resolution imaging systems commonly consider the case of imaging point sources, but often only consider estimating a small subset of the parameters. Furthermore, there has been no demonstration of an estimation algorithm with performance that follows the limit set by the Fisher information when all point source parameters are considered. We provide a framework for defining and analyzing super-resolution using the classical and quantum Fisher information for the multi-parameter estimation problem and demonstrate an algorithm that can achieve the classical Fisher information bound for all the parameters simultaneously.
authors: Peter Menart, Seungman Choi, Zubin Jacob

articles.title: Interpretation of chirality imprinted on photoelectron momentum spectra by three-dimensional light fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic three-dimensional (3D) light fields provide a new route to imprinting chirality on achiral matter through light--matter interaction. Although previous work has numerically demonstrated that chirality can be imprinted on the photoelectron momentum spectrum of atoms, a transparent analytical physical picture that links the structure of the driving field to the chirality of the spectrum is still an open question. Here, using frequency-domain theory based on nonperturbative quantum electrodynamics (QED), we demonstrate that this chirality originates from coherence between adjacent quantum transition channels. We further find that a symmetry transformation introduces into the coherence term a symmetry-breaking phase shift (ΦSBPS), which can be tuned by varying the laser-field parameters to preserve or break the corresponding symmetry in the spectrum. Once all such symmetries are broken, the momentum spectrum becomes chiral. In particular, for the noncollinear two-color 3D light field considered here, the spectrum is chiral for even f=ømega₂/ømega₁ and achiral for odd f. Our results provide a microscopic interpretation of chirality imprinting and establish a framework for predicting and controlling chiral electron wave packets with synthetic 3D light fields.
authors: Junxin Yuan, Yuhong Li, Fei Li, Jinkai Zhang, Shiyang Zhong, Hao Teng, Yujun Yang, Yingchun Guo, Zhiyi Wei, Jing Chen, Xiaojun Liu, Bingbing Wang

articles.title: A quantum algorithm for meshless lattice Boltzmann method with unitary interpolation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a mass-weighted meshless formulation for the shifted incompressible lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) whose streaming step is exactly unitary, combining with the Carleman embedding. In traditional meshless LBM, on a scattered node set the semi-Lagrangian streaming step is an interpolation, which is not unitary; a generic block encoding of this matrix therefore requires a normalization proportional to its sparsity and logarithmically many ancillas. To overcome the non-unitarity, we instead express the interpolation as the exponential exp(a Dx + b Dy) of mimetic derivative operators. Endowing each node with its Voronoi mass and applying a mass-weighted similarity transform renders these derivative operators skew-Hermitian by enforcing moment constraints together with low-wave number trigonometric differentiation conditions, so that the interpolation becomes exactly unitary. Such unitarization of interpolation leave the local collision step unchanged up to a rescaling of its quadratic term, where the same weights define the amplitude encoding of the distribution functions. For quasi-uniform node sets, the mass-weighting diagonal remains within a unit-order normalization that degrades only mildly as the Carleman truncation order grows, thereby mitigating the cost of block encoding. Numerical experiments on the Taylor Green vortex confirm that the method reproduces the full meshless LBM, with the velocity error decreasing as the Carleman order increases.
authors: Chi Zhang, Hefeng Wang, Hua Xiang

articles.title: Direct growth of crack-free stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire for wide-band photonics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-loss stoichiometric silicon nitride on oxidized silicon has emerged as the major wide-band photonics platform for nonlinear and quantum photonics. These films, deposited by low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD), are well known to have around 1000 MPa of residual tensile stress, which often leads to cracking when film thickness exceeds 400 nm. Although various stress-mitigation approaches can isolate or prevent cracking, this stress issue remains a major fabrication challenge. Low-residual-stress LPCVD stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire has also been reported and recently explored for photonics at telecommunication wavelengths. Here, we advance its development through systematic characterization, including thin-film stress analysis, ellipsometry and prism-coupling measurements of refractive index and loss, and swept-wavelength spectroscopy of fabricated photonic devices across a broad range of wavelengths. We demonstrate the direct growth of crack-free stoichiometric silicon nitride up to 2 μm thick with only 200 MPa of stress. Our fabricated devices show propagation losses of 0.35 dB/cm around 780 nm, 0.37 dB/cm around 1064 nm, and 0.25 dB/cm around 1630 nm. In addition, prism-coupling measurements indicate film losses below 1 dB/cm at wavelengths down to 500 nm. Our work highlights stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire as a promising wide-band photonics platform.
authors: Zhaohui Ma, Ashish Chanana, Zhiquan Yuan, Khoi Hoang, Yiliang Bao, Daron Westly, Kartik Srinivasan, Xiyuan Lu

articles.title: Photon-efficient readout of optical cavity arrays via spatial heterodyne
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical cavity arrays are an emerging tool for efficiently interfacing optical photons to quantum emitters for applications such as quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate a metrology technique for such cavity arrays by interfering cavity array outputs against a tilted reference beam on a camera, constituting a spatial heterodyne. Both the amplitude and phase of each cavity's transmitted field can be extracted from the resulting images. Enabled by the improved scaling of heterodyne detection over intensity detection in the presence of technical noise, we demonstrate signal-to-noise ratio greater than one down to the single detected photon level, even in the presence of hundreds of noise equivalent photons. This readout technique holds promise for fast, non-destructive imaging of atomic qubits in cavity arrays by requiring fewer scattered photons while allowing the use of fast cameras with higher electronic readout noise.

articles.title: The RAS-CCSD model, with applications for open-shell molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The restricted active space coupled cluster singles and doubles (RAS-CCSD) model, and its pilot implementation is detailed. The approach offers a simple, pragmatic way to formulate a coupled cluster theory for open-shell and multireference systems. For ground state energies, errors (compared to FCI) are shown to be similar to those of unrestricted (spin-orbital) CCSD. For excited states, the errors of RAS-CCSD are generally larger, and adaptations to the methodology are needed to achieve an approach which is balanced for both ground and excited states. However, unlike unrestricted CCSD, the approach is spin-adapted and can be used to add dynamical correlation to a multideterminantal reference state.

articles.title: Quantum tomography of bright squeezed vacuum via strong-field ionization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong-field physics uses intense optical fields to probe and control electron motion on ultrafast timescales. Recent advances in bright squeezed vacuum have brought macroscopic quantum states of light into the ultrafast strong-field regime, opening prospects for high-harmonic generation and photoionization. Yet linking its phase-space structure to subcycle electron dynamics remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate strong-field tunneling ionization of xenon using a phase-referenced combination of coherent and squeezed fields, with the coherent field defining the ionization clock and quadrature fluctuations of the zero-mean squeezed field providing control. The squeezed field selectively modulates atomic tunneling barriers and electron wave packets, imprinting signatures on photoelectron momentum distributions, number statistics, and energy spectra. Using coincidence measurements of photon number and phase-sensitive photoelectron momentum distributions, we perform quantum state tomography of the driving field by reconstructing its Wigner function. These results establish a bidirectional interface between quantum optics and nonperturbative strong-field electron dynamics, in which the driving quantum field shapes subcycle electron motion while photoionization provides a phase-sensitive probe of the field's quantum state. This work opens new routes toward controlling electron dynamics with quantum light and phase-sensitive quantum state metrology through ultrafast strong-field electron dynamics.
authors: Peizeng Li, Xiaoxiao Long, Haodong Liu, Xi Li, Yongkai Deng, Chuan Cheng, Yunquan Liu

articles.title: Readout chain of SPD DAQ system
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Spin Physics Detector (SPD) experiment at the NICA collider of the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research (JINR) aims to study the spin structure of the nucleon and spin-related phenomena. The experimental conditions, including the high interaction rate and the large number of readout channels, require a triggerless data acquisition system with high throughput and a scalable architecture. This work presents a hardware implementation of the readout chain that extends the previously proposed SPD DAQ architecture. The chain is based on two levels of concentrators. The L1 concentrator provides the interface between the front-end electronics and the next system level and distributes synchronous signals. The L2 concentrator aggregates data streams from several L1 concentrators before transmitting them to the computing system. A key feature of the L2 implementation is the offloading of data reception, buffering, and aggregation from the host CPU to the FPGA, motivated by the large number of small packets generated by the readout electronics. The developed hardware platforms and their operating logic are presented, together with experimental results for the main interfaces and data-path components. The obtained results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed hardware architecture and its application in a scalable SPD data acquisition system.
authors: L. Afanasyev, A. Berngardt, A. Boikov, V. Borshch, D. Erofeev, V. Frolov, K. Gritsay, V. Olshevsky, A. Kulikov, S. Tereshchenko, V. Tereshchenko

articles.title: Cavity-modified static polarizabilities of atoms and small molecules within QED full configuration interaction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static dipole polarizabilities of H₂, LiH, and helium confined in a single-mode optical cavity are computed using quantum-electrodynamical full configuration interaction (QED-FCI). Response properties are obtained as finite-field derivatives of the coupled electron-photon energy. The cavity-induced modification is found to arise from the competition of two contributions of opposite sign, the dipole self-energy and photon exchange, whose relative strength depends on both the cavity frequency and the number of photons involved in the exchange. The residual change suppresses the response of the molecular ground electronic states. For the metastable states of helium atom this balance changes qualitatively, and the differential response of the 2,³S₁ → 2,¹S₀ clock transition, which governs its sensitivity to static electric fields and to thermal radiation, is strongly enhanced instead. Cavity confinement can therefore either reduce or increase the dc Stark and blackbody-radiation shifts of a frequency standard, depending on the electronic structure of the states involved. The reported data serve as a reference for cavity-modified response and underscore the need for an exact treatment of light-matter correlation in cavity-QED predictions.

articles.title: Exact Gaussian--Hermite closure of the mapping quantum--classical Liouville equation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liouville equation contains an excess coupling term in addition to the Poisson bracket. Neglecting this term yields the Poisson bracket mapping equation (PBME). We expand the mapping dependence of the density in Hermite functions about the Gaussian factor common to all physical mapping densities. In this basis, the excess coupling term acts purely as a raising operator and exactly cancels the raising contribution generated by the back--reaction force. Consequently, the exact dynamics does not generate higher Hermite orders and closes on a finite, sparse system of equations for the coefficient fields. Within the physical sector, these equations reduce to the subsystem quantum--classical Liouville equation. In contrast, the PBME retains the raising contribution of the force, modifying the back reaction within the physical sector while continuously generating higher Hermite orders. For Tully's dual avoided crossing model, direct propagation of the coefficient equations confirms this finite closure and agrees with independent solutions of the subsystem equation. Comparison with converged full quantum dynamics further shows that, across all regimes examined, the PBME is less accurate than the quantum--classical description for populations, coherences, and momentum distributions.
authors: Sahand Nikzat Ali Nassimi, Rony Modak Parai

articles.title: Foundations for a Lens of Quantum Governance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The second quantum revolution is a revolution of information. Advances in quantum computation, communication, and sensing offer new capabilities while raising questions about how quantum infrastructures will be organised, accessed, and governed. We argue that their significance for governance lies not in transforming political principles, but in how their technical and infrastructural requirements may affect existing relationships of authority, responsibility, legitimacy, and power. This paper develops a quantum governance lens that connects governance scholarship with quantum information science, examining interactions between technical design, institutional arrangements, and infrastructural dependencies. We apply this lens to five areas: quantum computation, quantum key distribution, Quantum Byzantine Agreement, blind quantum computation, and dual-use quantum sensing. These applications illustrate how technical capabilities may influence access, trust, privacy, oversight, and accountability, while demonstrating that technical guarantees cannot resolve institutional questions independently. We conclude that quantum technologies do not necessarily introduce unique governance challenges or require entirely new governance frameworks. Rather, they provide a context in which established questions of legitimacy, accountability, and equity must be reconsidered in relation to emerging technological capabilities and institutional choices.
authors: Shira K. Huizing Lemstra, Tzula B. Propp

articles.title: Development of a Minimal Auxiliary Basis for the Particle--Particle Random Phase Approximation (ppRPA): Accelerating Excited-State Calculations in Diradical Nanoparticles and Periodic Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Singlet--triplet gaps set the energy scale of the two-spin manifold in molecular quantum information materials, and such systems frequently carry diradical character: metal nanoclusters, metal--organic frameworks with radical linkers, and the nitrogen--vacancy center in diamond. Time-dependent density functional theory is the standard tool at this size but describes multireference systems poorly. A closed-shell reference is inadequate for a multiconfigurational ground state, and the adiabatic kernel excludes doubly excited configurations. The particle--particle random phase approximation (pprpa{}) changes the particle number rather than the spin. Singlet and triplet states descend from one closed-shell reference, and double excitations enter on the same footing as single ones. Computational cost has confined pprpa{} to small systems, and the two-electron integrals that drive it are factorized through an auxiliary basis. We develop pprpa{}--as, which reduces that basis to a minimal set of atom-centered Gaussian shells whose exponents follow from free-atom radii and one global scaling factor. The approximation enters only the excited-state step, so both calculations proceed from the same self-consistent reference. We test molecules and clusters of up to 286 atoms, including heavy elements, and seven point defects in four periodic hosts, obtaining both multiplicities and their splitting without symmetry breaking or spin projection. We optimize the scaling factor and give guidance on choosing it. An order-of-magnitude smaller auxiliary basis delivers a speed-up of up to eightfold while staying within 0.03~eV of conventional pprpa{}, bringing diradical nanoclusters and periodic systems within reach.

articles.title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work proposes an exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion (EKDD) model that bridges device-level charge transport with singlet and triplet excited-state kinetics. State populations and reversible photophysical transitions are solved self-consistently, enabling transient and steady-state device response calculations. We investigate how LE-CT, CT-CS, and LE-T energy offsets, together with triplet-transfer kinetics, govern charge generation, recombination, voltage loss, and extraction in organic photovoltaics. We identify CT-CS offset as a primary, largely overlooked factor controlling charge generation and voltage loss. A positive offset makes CT3-CS separation exothermic and improves generation, but lowers CS energy and increases voltage loss; a negative offset makes separation endothermic and highly temperature-sensitive. The model reproduces triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends. We propose design rules for balanced generation and voltage loss via two charge-transfer channels: the LE-CT-CS pathway favors a moderate LE-CT offset of about 0.15-0.20 eV and a weakly exothermic CT-CS offset of about 0.05-0.075 eV; the T-CT3-CS pathway requires the same CT-CS alignment plus a small CT-T offset, no more than about 0.1 eV, corresponding to a recycling factor K greater than about 10⁻², to maintain fast T-to-CT3 recycling. CT-CS alignment is the main determinant of the charge-generation-voltage-loss trade-off, while triplet-recycling kinetics determines whether this balance survives at the device level. This work provides a unified theoretical description from exciton generation to free charge collection, offering a convenient tool for transient and steady-state analysis in organic photovoltaics.
authors: Jun Du, Liming Liu, Jun Yan

articles.title: Collision inside an atom: quantum ion-atom dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rydberg atoms occupy a central role in quantum science; their loosely bound outer electron gives rise to properties that enable quantum information processing1 or the formation of exotic molecular bonds2. Beyond these roles, they have been proposed as a neutral platform for the observation of quantum effects in collisions and reactions of the ionic core with neutral particles3, 4, a long-standing goal of ion-based chemistry and physics. However, all of the experimental results so far could be explained using a classical description of the internuclear motion5. Here we demonstrate cold collisions inside a Rydberg helium atom, achieved by merging helium Rydberg and ground-state helium beams and imaging individual scattering events. We resolve the fully quantum-coherent motion and observe matter-wave diffraction and tunnelling-driven shape resonances down to collision energies of 90 mK. In the case of identical helium nuclei, we demonstrate a new regime of identical-particle Mott interference6, where quantum statistics begin to govern the total scattering cross section. For distinct isotopes, we show the breakdown of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation and benchmark parameter-free, state-of-the-art theory. We directly measure the helium isotope ionization-energy difference to be 15.0 +/- 0.1 K. Our experiments establish Rydberg atoms as a platform for the direct observation of quantum dynamics with a general class of ions, atoms and molecules.
authors: Arijit Das, Yufeng Wang, Marcin Welter, Karl Horn, Dawid Dkabrowski, Michał Przybytek, Julia Narevicius, Michał Tomza, Edvardas Narevicius

articles.title: Theory of Sub-Doppler Spectroscopy of Alkali Metal Vapors in the Field of Counterpropagating Bichromatic Laser Beams: Probe Beam Regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sub-Doppler resonances observed in miniature cells (V łl 1 cm³⁾ with Rb or Cs atoms in the field of counterpropagating bichromatic laser beams are of interest for the creation of a miniature quantum frequency standard (QFS) of the optical range. However, a theory of these resonances that takes into full account the real structure of energy levels in an atom has not yet been constructed, which would make it possible to obtain explicit analytical expressions for the absorption coefficient of the medium. This paper addresses this gap using the density matrix formalism and the algebra of irreducible tensor operators. Namely, we obtained an analytical expression for the absorption coefficient of the probe beam in the presence of a more intense counterpropagating beam (pump-probe regime). Moreover, the calculations were carried out for arbitrary parameters of laser beam polarization, arbitrary angular momenta of optical dipole transitions in the atom and various relaxation processes. The constructed theory allows us to correctly take into account the simultaneous action of various nonlinear optical effects, in contrast to the simplified three-level model of the atom, and also to investigate the partial contribution of each of them to the overall observed resonant circuit. The analysis performed, in particular, made it possible to predict an increase in the amplitude of the sub-Doppler resonance when using counterpropagating light beams with opposite circular polarizations in relation to the configuration of counterpropagating beams with orthogonal linear polarizations, which is often used in practice.
authors: A. M. Mikhailov, D. V. Brazhnikov

articles.title: Phase Memory Controls Radiative Depolarization Near an Isolated Spin Resonance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radiative depolarization near spin resonances in electron storage rings is conventionally described by correlated-sideband and local resonance-density theories, but a quantitative description of the crossover between them has remained lacking. Here we derive a unified finite-memory response from stochastic spin dynamics near an isolated resonance. By separating the coherent resonance contribution from stochastic fluctuations, we show that the connected correlation of the accumulated resonance-relative spin phase determines the leading off-center weak-resonance depolarization rate. Both conventional theories emerge as controlled asymptotic limits of this response, which also captures the surviving synchrotron phase memory governing the crossover. Monte Carlo spin tracking validates the predicted rates throughout the crossover and reproduces the recurrence-induced generalized-sideband structure. More broadly, the connected-correlation formulation provides a basis for extending radiative depolarization theory to more general stochastic spin-orbit dynamics in storage rings.

articles.title: Directed percolation in higher-order social dilemmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiplayer social dilemmas on hypergraphs show a variety of emergent phenomena, which has been attributed to group interactions. Here we test whether pairwise dynamics can reproduce them as well. We derive the mesoscopic Langevin equation of a testbed model and find the operator content of absorbing phase transitions: a directed-percolation line, a tricritical point, and a first-order region whose spinodal is the explosive transition. In our analysis, three-player games only set the values of the Landau coefficients. We construct a strictly pairwise model with short-lived memory, in which every event involves at most two entities, that reproduces these coefficients term by term and has exactly the same mean-field fixed points. Simulations confirm that the two dynamics share mean-field critical and tricritical scaling and the size of the critical mass, and that a purely three-player game on a two-dimensional triangular lattice lies in the directed-percolation class. For these games, the explosive transition and the critical mass therefore do not require group interactions, and the critical behavior is that of the pairwise theory.

articles.title: QPE-Inspired Adaptive Phase Tracking for Discrete-Variable Quantum Key Distribution under Unitary Channel Drift
articles.abstract: Environmental phase drift is a critical impairment in discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), particularly when phase coherence is required for superposition-basis measurements or entanglement-based correlations. This work proposes a QPE-inspired adaptive phase tracking framework for mitigating unitary channel drift in BB84 and BBM92 protocols. Across both evaluated phase-drift regimes, the proposed QPE-inspired tracking framework reduced the mean QBER by factors ranging from approximately 5× to 10× relative to the corresponding untracked baselines. The proposed approach combines a discretized quantum phase-sensing stage with a classical feedback loop, enabling adaptive estimation and compensation of residual phase rotations at the receiver. Unlike full quantum state tomography, the method is designed to operate as a lightweight hybrid quantum-classical feedback mechanism, using phase-sensitive calibration information without explicitly reconstructing the transmitted quantum states. State-vector simulations implemented in Qiskit Aer compare untracked BB84 and BBM92 baselines with the proposed QPE-inspired tracking architecture under stochastic phase drift. Simulations with (:N=1000) transmission rounds show that the proposed framework maintains the QBER below the 11% asymptotic threshold for both BB84 and BBM92 under two phase-drift regimes: a moderate fiber-like regime with (:γ:=0.04) rad/round and (:σ:cₕin:łeft[0,0.35i̊ght]) rad, and a high-drift aeronautical regime with (:γ:=0.15) rad/round and (:σ:cₕin:łeft[0.02,0.25i̊ght]) rad. In contrast, the corresponding untracked baselines remain above the threshold and yield vanishing asymptotic secret-key rates. A further intercept-resend scenario is evaluated to verify that non-unitary adversarial disturbances remain observable in the total QBER. The proposed framework is therefore positioned as a simulation-based phase-tracking strategy for DV-QKD under unitary channel noise, rather than as a complete security proof against general attacks.

articles.title: Effects of the choice of the exchange-correlation functional on high-temperature superconductivity predictions in covalent-cage M(BN)5 family
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recent experimental synthesis of covalent cage superconductors has ignited hopes for ambient-pressure high-temperature superconductivity, while the computational strategy for discovering new materials poses challenges for accurately estimating superconducting properties. Here, we quantified the response of electron-phonon coupling (EPC) properties in M(BN)5 superconductors to different exchange-correlation (XC) effects using high-throughput first-principles calculations. We found that the metallic covalent bonds responsible for superconductivity exhibit anomalously high sensitivity to functional selection uncertainty, distinguishing them from conventional superconductors mediated by metallic bonding. The widely used PBE functional systematically overestimates lattice volumes, inducing phonon softening, enhanced EPC, and consequent Peierls instability. In contrast, PBEsol, which is more accurate through enhanced treatment of short-range interactions, eliminates imaginary frequencies in Rb(BN)5 that appear at the PBE level, yielding an outstanding superconducting critical temperature (Tc) of 113 K at ambient pressure and 138 K at 2 GPa. Enhanced electron localization and short-range correlation in covalent bonds manifest through dual mechanisms: phonon hardening at the lattice scale and band widening at the electronic scale, which collectively suppress Peierls distortion and delocalize antibonding states. Pressure-dependent analysis reveals that compression attenuates phonon discrepancies between XC functionals, whereas electronic properties remain notably sensitive to XC-induced perturbations of fine electronic bands near the Fermi level.
authors: Zhongyu Wan, Guo-Hua Zhong, Cheng-wei Ju, Ruiqin Zhang, Hai-Qing Lin

articles.title: Quantitative Impact of Occupation Smearing Methods on Conventional Superconductivity: from Electronic Structure through Lattice Dynamics to Electron-Phonon Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In first-principles calculations of metallic systems, the discrete electronic mesh in the Brillouin zone necessitates a smearing function and its width (e.g., the widely used 0.02 Ry Methfessel-Paxton scheme) to enforce continuity of energy and occupation at the Fermi surface. However, the quantitative impact of such empirical parameters on phonon-mediated superconductivity has long been overlooked, leading to their habitual selection by mere convention. Here, using hexahydride CsH6 as a benchmark, we systematically investigate the magnitude and propagation mechanism of smearing-induced errors against the parameter-free optimized tetrahedron method. Long-tailed smearing delocalizes the occupation window, causing substantial Fermi-level shifts, flattening of the density of states, and hardening phonon modes, thereby weakening electron-phonon coupling. Conversely, short-tailed smearing suffers from insufficient sampling, producing density-of-states oscillations and enhanced Fermi-surface nesting; via amplified electronic screening and Peierls instabilities, this softens acoustic modes and generates imaginary frequencies, causing CsH6 to be dynamically unstable and discarded. However, the optimized tetrahedron method reveals that CsH6 is dynamically stable under ambient pressure with a remarkable superconducting transition temperature of 121 K. To prevent subjective empirical parameters from obscuring theoretically promising high-temperature superconductors, we derive a simple scaling relation for the smearing width, applicable to different smearing functions, from the free-electron-gas model, offering an objective, precise, and efficient protocol for parameter selection in high-throughput screening.

articles.title: Direct growth of crystalline spinel GaON films: A wide-bandgap mixed-anion semiconductor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-anion semiconductors offer opportunities for bandgap engineering beyond conventional multication alloys, but competing phases and disorder complicate their synthesis and the identification of their electronic properties. Gallium oxynitride (GaON) could connect the technologically important GaN and Ga2O3 systems, yet establishing a clear relation between its crystal structure, composition and bandgap remains challenging. Here we report the direct growth of crystalline spinel gamma-GaON films by nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed-laser deposition. Varying the nitrogen and oxygen supply yields monoclinic beta-Ga2O3, predominantly disordered films and crystalline spinel GaON. Complementary diffraction, atomic-resolution microscopy and elemental analysis establish the spinel structure and nitrogen incorporation. Temperature-dependent photocurrent spectroscopy reveals a clear redshift of the crystalline gamma-GaON response, supporting assignment of a band-edge transition near 4.3 eV at room temperature. These results open opportunities to investigate mixed-anion wide-bandgap semiconductor physics and develop heterostructures.
authors: Baikui Li, Zecheng Yang, Wenhao Yin, Zijing Wu, Haitao Zhao, Yunwei Sheng, Honglei Wu, Jiannong Wang

articles.title: Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.14165v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological n-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an n-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. The net-theoretic perspective admits a natural categorification, in which the category of topological n-nets carries the structure of a higher Morita category. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs. Our main result identifies the group of locality-preserving symmetries of (3+1)-dimensional quantum spin systems (i.e. quantum cellular automata modulo stabilization, finite-depth quantum circuits, and translations) with the full Witt group of nondegenerate braided fusion categories, thereby answering a question posed by Haah.

articles.title: Machine-learned, finite temperature Fermi-operator expansions suitable for GPUs and AI-hardware
articles.abstract: We present several finite-temperature recursive Fermi–operator expansion schemes based on the second-order spectral projection (SP2) method. Our approach builds on a previous observation that the electronic structure problem, as formulated through a recursive SP2 expansion, can be mapped onto the architecture of a deep neural network. Using this perspective, we generalize SP2 to finite electronic temperatures by constructing machine learning models that determine optimized recursive expansion coefficients. The same approach is also applied to the prediction of the electronic entropy for fractional occupation numbers. The coefficients are trained for a specified chemical potential and electronic temperature and are not available in closed analytical form. However, by employing an appropriate affine rescaling strategy to the Hamiltonian matrix, we eliminate the need to retrain the model for different temperatures and chemical potentials. Our approach avoids explicit diagonalization and relies solely on highly optimized matrix–matrix multiplication kernels. Compared to state-of-the-art diagonalization, we achieve an order-of-magnitude speedup in the single-particle finite-temperature density matrix calculation for small and moderately sized matrices on modern graphics processing units and dense matrix multiply units.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Low-energy electron collisions with BH +
articles.abstract: BH + ions are expected to play an important role in boron-containing plasmas relevant to fusion environments such as ITER, where low-energy electrons drive a variety of inelastic and reactive scattering processes. In particular, dissociative recombination, vibrational excitation, and de-excitation strongly influence the ion balance and energy distribution in such plasmas. We present a theoretical study of electron collisions with BH + using a combination of ab initio electronic structure calculations and electron scattering methods. Potential energy curves for bound states of BH and BH + are obtained using multireference configuration interaction, while autoionization widths of electronic resonant states are computed with the complex Kohn variational method. The collision dynamics is modeled within multichannel quantum defect theory, including both the “crossing”—i.e., Feshbach-resonances-mediated—and the “non-crossing”—i.e., Rydberg-mediated—mechanisms. Cross sections and thermal rate coefficients for the processes are provided for the lowest vibrational levels of BH + and its isotopologues—BD + and BT + —showing significant isotope effects, especially at low electron temperatures.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Ultrafast spin-transfer dynamics and single-qubit logic gate design in monocyclic carbon rings with transition metal atoms adsorbed
articles.abstract: We present a first-principles study of ultrafast spin-transfer dynamics and single-qubit logic gate design in transition metal (TM) atom-adsorbed monocyclic carbon ring systems. The structure- and size-dependent features of geometries, electronic structures, and spin localizations are analyzed. Notably, the TM 2 –C 4 n +2 systems generally prefer out-of-plane configurations and exhibit localized states with spin localized singly on one TM atom or doubly on two TM atoms, rather than the carbon ring-related localized states found in the mostly coplanar TM–C 4 n +2 systems. Driven by well-tailored nonchirped ultrafast laser pulses, sub-picosecond, high-fidelity spin transfer is achieved in most structures (except for the ones with only one type of spin localized states). The laser detuning and chirp effects on these scenarios are further explored. The tolerance and sensitivity characteristics of them can provide valuable guidance for both experimental implementation and sensor applications. In addition, based on the achieved ultrafast dynamics for the representative structures FeC 14 and Fe 2 C 18 , four basic single-qubit quantum logic gates Pauli X, Pauli Y, Pauli Z, and S are all constructed, with an additional non-Clifford T gate achieved in the latter one. All these results demonstrate the great potential of the TM atom adsorbed carbon ring structures and provide significant guidance for experimental realization of the ultrafast spin dynamics and design of carbon-based molecular spintronic devices toward quantum computing.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Semiclassical model of nonadiabatic energy transfer in atom-molecule collisions
articles.abstract: The recently developed semiclassical theory of nonadiabatic energy transfer in three-dimensional atom-atom collisions is extended to predict the electronic excitation and quenching in atom–molecule collisions. The two main assumptions of the present model are (i) the critical role of orbiting collisions, which result in multiple crossings of the seam between the potential energy surfaces in a resonance state of the atom-diatom complex, and (ii) a statistical distribution of the atom–diatom complex over the resonance vibrational states. The cross sections and rate coefficients predicted by the model are compared with quasi-classical trajectory/surface hopping calculations and quantum wavepacket scattering for N( 2 D) + N 2 ↔ N( 4 S) + N 2 , N( 2 D) + CO ↔ N( 4 S) + CO, and C( 1 D) + N 2 ↔ C( 3 P) + N 2 , using the ab initio potential energy surfaces and nonadiabatic couplings, and with the experimental data where available. The quenching rate coefficients predicted by the semiclassical model are in good overall agreement with the quasiclassical trajectory calculations and quantum scattering. The semiclassical excitation rate coefficient for N + N 2 is in good agreement with that obtained from quasiclassical trajectory calculations with Landau–Zener surface hopping (QCT-LZ) using the detailed balance, over a wide range of temperatures. Both the semiclassical and QCT-LZ excitation rates at high temperatures are significantly higher compared to those predicted by QCT with coherent switches/decay of mixing with zero-point energy correction and by quantum scattering. The approximate analytic expressions for the semiclassical transition probabilities and rate coefficients have been obtained.

articles.title: Two-atom interaction potential database supporting physics-informed features for machine learning and material property prediction
articles.abstract: Accurately predicting the energy and relevant properties of molecules and complex crystalline systems remains a cornerstone of computational materials science. While density functional theory (DFT) offers high accuracy, its computational cost scales prohibitively for large-scale materials. In this work, we present a comprehensive, first-principles-derived database of two-atom interaction potentials and interatomic forces to accelerate the property prediction via physics-informed machine learning. Computed using spin-polarized DFT via the GPAW package, the database encompasses all 2346 possible atomic pairs generated from 68 unique elements as a function of interatomic distance. The practical utility of this database was demonstrated within the many-body expansion framework by engineering highly descriptive features to predict three distinct types of energy for benchmarking. First, the framework was applied to predict the total energy of molecules within the G2/97 database. Second, for defect energetics on 2D materials (the IMP2D database), localized concentric shell potentials and spatial gradients were introduced to capture the formation energy of adsorbate defects. Finally, for molecular energetics within the QM9 database, we developed advanced descriptors, including a potential-based matrix, a two-body Bag of Bonds, and a three-body Ray’s asymmetric parameter histogram to evaluate atomization energy. Evaluated using kernel ridge regression, the combined two-body and three-body feature set yielded an outstanding test result with the mean absolute error of 0.186 eV ( R 2 = 0.9994) on a 10 000-samples subset. This framework showcases the power of utilizing explicit, database-derived potentials as robust descriptors for high-fidelity predictions of energy and relevant properties.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: PolyFKAN: Integrating Fourier-KAN layers into graph neural networks for polymer property prediction
articles.abstract: Graph neural networks have become a central tool for polymer property prediction, but their fixed activation functions can impose a low-pass spectral bias that smooths over the sharp, multi-scale structure–property variations that distinguish chemically similar polymers. We address this limitation with PolyFKAN, a multitask graph-learning architecture that augments the prediction head of a polyGNN backbone with Fourier Kolmogorov–Arnold network layers. PolyFKAN represents edge-wise activations as truncated Fourier series and couples the resulting spectral branch to the standard multilayer perceptron (MLP) pathway through a bounded residual gate, thereby increasing functional expressivity without disrupting the learned graph embeddings. Across 17 polymer properties spanning electronic, thermodynamic, optical/dielectric, thermal, and gas-permeability domains, PolyFKAN achieves statistically significant improvement over a tightly controlled polyGNN baseline on 11 of 17 targets (one-sided t -test, p < 0.05), with one additional target showing marginal improvement. The gains are especially pronounced for multi-scale properties, including more than 15% average root mean squared error reduction for large-penetrant gas permeabilities and more than 15% improvement across optical and dielectric targets. Hierarchical ablation further reveals that optimal Fourier bandwidth is property-dependent: difficult, multi-scale targets require broader spectral capacity with stronger amplitude control, whereas high-fidelity targets benefit from lighter regularization. These results establish Fourier-KAN prediction heads as a minimally invasive and physically aligned inductive bias for polymer informatics.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Multi-state switching of topological magnetic textures via enhancing ferroelectric polarization in van der Waals multiferroic heterostructure LaBr/In 2 Se 3
articles.abstract: Topological magnetic textures hold great promise for non-volatile memory applications, owing to their topological stability and low energy consumption. Conventional manipulations focus on the creation/annihilation of one topological state or switching between two states, however, the multi-state switching remains largely unexplored. Here, we proposed that enhancing ferroelectric polarization can drive multi-state switching of topological magnetic textures, as evidenced in van der Waals multiferroic heterostructures LaBr/In 2 Se 3 . Using first-principles calculations and micromagnetic simulations, we revealed that increasing In 2 Se 3 thickness triggers phase transitions among three distinct topological magnetic textures, including bimeron, trimeron, and skyrmionium-like structure. The intrinsic mechanism of the phase transitions originates from the competition among LaBr’s exchange interaction, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, and magnetic anisotropy energy, which are significantly tuned by the enhanced ferroelectric polarization of In 2 Se 3 . Our work offers a theoretical guidance for voltage-controlled multi-state switching of topological magnetic textures, which sheds lights on the applications of topological spintronics.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Material and thermal properties of MgCl 2 molten salt by ab initio and machine-learning molecular-dynamics simulations
articles.abstract: We study the structural, thermophysical, and dynamical properties of molten MgCl 2 over a wide temperature range using Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics (AIMD) and molecular dynamics simulations based on machine-learning interaction potentials (MLIPs). MLIPs can achieve near-AIMD accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling simulations of larger systems and longer timescales. This opens up the possibility of studying the system under out-of-equilibrium conditions, which in turn allows for the calculation of physical properties, such as the thermal conductivity or viscosity, that cannot be obtained reliably for the typical time and length scales accessible to AIMD. We follow two complementary approaches to develop and evaluate the MLIPs. First, we develop a Deep Potential (DP) from scratch using AIMD trajectories at different temperatures. Second, we also evaluate two out-of-the-box foundation models and a fine-tuned version of one of them. The fine-tuning is performed using configurations from the AIMD trajectories originally used to train the DP. We compare the predictions of the trained DP, the foundation models, and AIMD simulations with the available experimental data and provide a comprehensive calculation of the most important physical quantities of molten MgCl 2 . We compute densities, radial and angular distribution functions, thermal conductivity, heat capacity, viscosity, and diffusion coefficients over the 1000–1600 K temperature range. This range is relevant to important technological applications such as thermal energy storage, generation IV nuclear reactors, and concentrated solar power systems. Finally, we briefly review the accuracy and performance of the different MLIP versions used throughout the work.
