articles.title: Magnetic sculpting transforms single-source fields into predetermined shapes with mathematical precision
articles.abstract: Magnetic fields are invisible yet essential components in technologies ranging from MRI scanners and particle accelerators to atomic clocks and future quantum computers. Each of these applications requires magnetic fields with specific shapes and properties. Today, creating such tailored magnetic fields requires researchers and engineers to design specialized, carefully optimized magnets or large systems of coils for each individual application—a complex and resource-intensive process.

articles.title: From nonmagnetic to magnetic: A 2D semiconductor with electrically tunable magnetism
articles.abstract: Researchers from the National University of Singapore (NUS), in collaboration with scientists from institutions in Switzerland, the Czech Republic and Germany, have demonstrated a way to introduce magnetism into an otherwise nonmagnetic two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor and subsequently control its magnetic properties using an electrical voltage. The findings, published in Science Advances, establish a new platform for investigating electrically controllable magnetism in atomically thin materials, with potential implications for future spintronic technologies.

articles.title: Speculative Decoding Shortcuts Can Undermine Language Model Safety Guarantees
articles.abstract: Safety evaluations of large language models (LLMs) are typically conducted using full-precision reference weights under exact autoregressive decoding, despite production systems commonly deploying quantized models, evicted or quantized key–value (KV) caches, and speculative decoding. Recent audits show meaningful safety degradation from weight and cache compression individually, but the safety impact of deployed, non-exact speculative decoding and the interaction among multiple transformations remain poorly understood. We address two open questions. First, we examine non-preserving speculative decoding variants, including typical acceptance, entropy-adjusted thresholds, tree-structured drafting, and n-gram paths verified by argmax match. Second, we investigate whether composing weight compression, KV-cache compression, and speculative decoding produces sub-additive or super-additive safety degradation. Across five production serving frameworks, we find that although most default to exact rejection sampling, all expose non-preserving alternatives, with practitioner guidance recommending their use for quantized target models which is a potentially high-risk combination. We formalize acceptance relaxation and decompose its distributional shift into two opposing channels, a mode-seeking term that sharpens toward the target model’s distribution and may be safety-protective, and a draft-leakage term that substitutes the draft model’s distribution for the target’s and represents the primary hazard. GPU-free Monte Carlo experiments validate this decomposition and show that exact rejection sampling remains at the noise floor, whereas typical acceptance and argmax-match reach 25× and 12× the noise level, respectively. We further falsify our initial hypothesis of a positive relaxation-by-alignment interaction, obtaining a coefficient of − 1.23 (R² = 0.92). Finally, we introduce the Composed Safety Tax Ratio and propose alignment-gated acceptance, whose worst-case behavior provably reduces to exact decoding.

articles.title: Catalytic dehydration of fructose to 5-HMF by a lignin-derived carbon solid acid catalyst modified by non-thermal plasma
articles.abstract: Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) as a critical biomass-derived platform chemical shows significant potential for synthesizing diverse value-added products. However, conventional 5-HMF preparation methods often suffer from inherent drawbacks including high energy demand, environmental pollution, and high cost. A solid acid catalyst (LDSA-COOH) was prepared using solvent-extracted lignin as the carbon support and modified by non-thermal plasma grafting in an acrylic acid atmosphere. The structure and properties of the catalyst were comprehensively analyzed by various spectroscopies (FTIR, XPS) and SEM microscopy, and the porosity structure was detected by BET method. The catalytic performance of LDSA-COOH was systematically assessed through measurements of acidic group density and dehydration of fructose to 5-HMF. In a DMSO/water biphasic solvent system, high fructose conversion of 99.2% and 5-HMF yield of 85.7% was obtained at 180 ℃ and 30 min by LDSA-COOH. Notably, the LDSA-COOH catalyst also demonstrated excellent stability and reusability through five consecutive reuse cycles. This method offers advantages including shorter solid acid preparation time, lower energy consumption, lower environmental pollution, and higher catalytic stability, providing a promising strategy for the preparation of solid acid catalyst.

articles.title: Reaction kinetics and microstructural evolution of alkali-activated electric arc furnace slag
articles.abstract: Electric arc furnace slag (EAFS) is a steelmaking by-product with potential for use as a precursor in low-clinker or clinker-free cementitious materials. However, the reaction mechanisms governing its alkali activation, particularly in Fe-rich systems, remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the alkali activation of EAFS as the sole precursor using sodium- and potassium-based activating solutions with different silica moduli and alkali contents. The results show that activator chemistry strongly influenced early reaction kinetics, setting behaviour and mechanical performance. Sodium-activated systems generally exhibited higher reactivity and greater compressive strength, whereas potassium-activated mixtures showed slower but sustained strength development. Semi-adiabatic calorimetry indicated that early-age behaviour was mainly governed by rapid precipitation processes, followed by progressive structural reorganisation during curing. FTIR analysis revealed a gradual shift of the main Si–O–T band towards lower wavenumbers, suggesting changes in the bonding environment and continued gel evolution. Electrical resistivity—used as an indirect indicator of pore network connectivity—and drying shrinkage were not controlled solely by total open porosity or mass loss, but were strongly affected by gel organisation. Overall, the study provides an integrated interpretation of how reaction kinetics, gel evolution and the developing matrix structure govern the performance of alkali-activated EAFS systems.

articles.title: Probabilistic recovery of high-impact urban convective rainfall from radar-assimilation experiments using conditional diffusion and distributional attribution
articles.abstract: Localized convective rainfall is difficult to predict because small storm-displacement errors can produce large grid-point forecast errors over cities. This study develops, implements, and evaluates a physics-first hybrid forecasting workflow for a flash-flood-producing event over Baltimore, Maryland, on 28 July 2026, combining convection-permitting Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations, Weather Research and Forecasting Data Assimilation (WRFDA) using three-dimensional variational (3DVAR) radar assimilation, and conditional-diffusion probabilistic postprocessing. Three 3 km WRF experiments were conducted and compared. These included a control without radar assimilation (CTRL), assimilation of KLWX NEXRAD radial velocity (RV), and assimilation of radial velocity plus reflectivity (RV+RF), with the two radar-assimilation experiments performed using a single 21 UTC WRFDA. Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor (MRMS) quantitative precipitation estimates were the primary verification data. Radar assimilation produced measurable analysis increments but did not correct the dominant rainfall displacement: six-hour root mean squared error (RMSE) remained about 21.7 mm, Pearson correlation remained near -0.06, and rainfall-centroid displacement remained about 40 km. A neural-network diffusion model was then evaluated using five geometry-defined spatial folds, 30 km blocks, and a 9 km exclusion buffer. Across all experiments, postprocessing reduced hourly RMSE by 15-16%, continuous ranked probability score by about 39%, and six-hour RMSE by 25-27%, while six-hour correlation increased to 0.521-0.540. Paired spatial-block bootstrap replicates supported improvement in every primary continuous and probabilistic metric, and centroid displacement decreased to 0.84-3.86 km. Distributional Reliability Explanation Attribution across 80 independently retrained model realizations identified 10 m wind, rainwater, surface pressure, 33 km mean precipitation, and ice as the most reliable distributional controls. Extreme rainfall remained challenging at the highest thresholds. For this event, convection-permitting WRF, radar-informed analyses, and neural-network probabilistic postprocessing formed a hybrid framework that substantially improved localized high-impact rainfall prediction while retaining explicit uncertainty and interpretable model controls.

articles.title: Adversarial Robustness of Quantum Supervised Learning for Network Intrusion Detection: White-Box Attacks, PGD-Aware Training, and Classical Benchmarking
articles.abstract: Quantum supervised learning (QSL) is increasingly investigated for intrusion detection, yet its behavior under adversarial manipulation remains insufficiently characterized in network-security settings. This study presents a controlled white-box evaluation of a four-qubit variational QSL intrusion detector and a matched classical multilayer perceptron (MLP) on the UNSW-NB15 benchmark. Categorical encoding, standardization, principal component analysis to four dimensions, and scaling to [0, π] were applied consistently. A clean QSL model and a PGD-aware QSL model using 50% clean, 25% FGSM, and 25% PGD samples were evaluated against FGSM and seven-step PGD attacks at ε = 0.02π, 0.05π, and 0.10π over ten matched random seeds. Clean and adversarially trained MLP controls used the same representation and attack protocol. PGD-aware QSL improved accuracy over clean QSL from 9.10% to 26.90% at PGD 0.05π and from 2.60% to 20.73% at PGD 0.10π, with large paired effect sizes. The improvement was accompanied by a clean-accuracy reduction from 70.73% to 61.57%. Robust MLP retained higher absolute adversarial accuracy, reaching 64.27% and 50.50% at PGD 0.05π and 0.10π, respectively. The results demonstrate that adversarial training materially strengthens the tested QSL model but do not support a quantum-advantage claim. The study provides a reproducible robustness benchmark emphasizing attack validation, repeated seeds, effect sizes, and classical controls. The implementation notebook and supporting experimental outputs used for reproducibility are publicly archived on Zenodo (Bhoge et al. 2026).

articles.title: Iridium-Ruthenium Oxide for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction: Correlation between Calcination Temperature–Morphology–Activity Interplay
articles.abstract: A key challenge in water electrolysis is establishing structure–activity relationships to understand and improve IrRuOx-based catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in a PEM water electrolyser. We report a simple, scalable modified Adams fusion method for preparing highly OER-active IrRuOx with various sizes and shapes. This practical approach enables investigation of how heat treatment affects particle size, morphology, and the nature of surface species, and how these factors influence the OER activity of IrRuOx. P-XRD, HR-TEM/SEM-EDS, and TGA/DSC studies indicate a transition from an amorphous hydrated oxide (IrRuOx@350) to a crystalline hydrated phase (IrRuOx@400°C, IrRuOx@450°C, IrRuOx@500°C, and IrRuOx@520°C), with surface species strongly linked to OER activity. IrRuOx synthesized at 500°C, consisting of 22.22 nm particles with an electrochemical surface area of 903 cm2, shows the highest OER activity in 0.5 M H2SO4 (E = 220 mV and a Tafel slope of 24.41 mV/dec at 10 mA/cm2). In contrast, amorphous IrRuOx synthesized at 350°C shows better stability at a potential of 1.27 V. A variation in intrinsic OER activity was associated with the predominant termination of rod-shaped particles by highly ordered (110) and (200) facets. These results highlight the important role of calcination temperature in achieving the best balance between activity and durability of materials towards OER in PEMWE applications.

articles.title: Systematic Literature Review of Security and Privacy Management in LoRaWAN Networks
articles.abstract: LoRaWAN, a leading Low-Power Wide-Area Network (LPWAN) technology, is widely adopted for IoT due to its wide coverage and low energy consumption, yet it remains vulnerable to multilayer security threats, including replay attacks, node tracking via static identifiers, metadata exposure, and limited cryptographic key management. This study presents a systematic literature review (SLR) following the PRISMA 2020 methodology. From 550 records identified across IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, ACM Digital Library, MDPI, Scopus, and Google Scholar, 50 peer-reviewed studies published between 2019 and 2026 were selected using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The review analyzes five research domains: cryptographic key management, privacy and pseudonymization, machine learning-based security, physical layer security, and emerging architectures such as blockchain and edge computing. It proposes a novel multiaxis taxonomy classifying existing solutions according to cryptographic strength, privacy protection, energy overhead, validation rigor, and scalability, providing a structured framework for comparison. Five major research gaps are identified, including the lack of lightweight dynamic pseudonymization schemes and automatic rekeying protocols ensuring forward and backward secrecy. Finally, the review outlines best practices and future directions, including duty cycle-aware rekeying, lightweight post-quantum cryptography, and federated or TinyML-based intrusion detection for next-generation LoRaWAN-based IoT deployments.

articles.title: Lateral photovoltaic effect in SiO2/TeO2/Bi2Te3/n-Si structure
articles.abstract: The lateral photovoltaic effect (LPE) in a SiO2/TeO2/Bi2Te3/n-Si hybrid heterostructure was investigated as a function of light wavelength, temperature, illumination position, and magnetic field. The Schottky barrier height of the structure was estimated to be ΦB = 0.3 eV using the thermionic emission model. A pronounced change in the LPE is observed near λ = 1 µm, including a reversal of the photovoltage polarity. This indicates the transition between two dominant photovoltaic channels associated with carrier photogeneration in the Si substrate and Bi2Te3 film. The Si-related contribution was found to be sensitive to the magnetic field, whereas the Bi2Te3-related contribution remains nearly unaffected. The magnetic-field effect on the Si-related LPE is attributed to interface states localized near the Bi2Te3/n-Si interface. These results demonstrate the coexistence of distinct photovoltaic channels in Bi2Te3/Si-based hybrid structures and provide insight into the mechanisms governing their photoelectric and magnetically sensitive response.

articles.title: Multicomponent Magnetic Domain Walls in Rhombohedral Graphene
articles.abstract: Spatial textures of magnetic order, such as domain walls and skyrmions, are fundamental objects in magnetism. In rhombohedral multilayer graphene, magnetic order involves spin and valley degrees of freedom, opening the possibility of qualitatively new spatial textures. Here, we explore this possibility through a microscopic study of a one-dimensional domain wall in the valley-imbalanced quarter-metal phase of rhombohedral graphene. We uncover two different classes of domain walls. One resembles a conventional magnetic domain wall, locally rotating between the two bulk states, whereas the other is intrinsically multicomponent and explores states that are not occupied in either bulk domain. Which texture is realized is controlled by the competition between intervalley Hund's coupling and spin-orbit coupling, and we identify experimental signatures to distinguish them. For a superconducting junction formed across the wall, we further show that the superconducting phase difference couples directly to the intervalley-coherent phase of the texture, allowing precession of this internal phase to generate a voltage. This mechanism provides an explanation for the resistive domain walls recently observed in chiral superconductors [arXiv2605.13303] and predicts accompanying magnetization oscillations that could be detected using GHz-frequency AC probes. Our theory establish a microscopic connection between multicomponent magnetic textures, their internal dynamics, and superconducting transport.

articles.title: Substorm Triggering Processes During Different Phases of Geomagnetic Storms: A Case Study
articles.abstract: Using observations from satellites and ground-based stations, we investigate the possible mechanisms triggering the expansion phases of two substorms that occurred during different phases of a geomagnetic storm. The main findings are summarized as follows. For the substorm occurring during the storm commencement and initial phase, the energy storage process is primarily modulated by enhanced solar wind speed and dynamic pressure, whereas a southward turning of the interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) appears to be a key trigger for the onset of the expansion phase. For the substorm occurring during the storm recovery phase, energy storage is primarily associated with the southward IMF, while the expansion phase begins after a time delay following the southward turning of the IMF. Detailed analysis of these two events suggests that the mechanisms triggering substorm expansion during geomagnetic storms may differ from those operating during isolated, non-storm substorms. In contrast, previous studies have identified northward turnings of the IMF as an important indicator of expansion-phase onset in substorms under non-storm conditions. These results provide new insight into the relationship between geomagnetic storm evolution and substorm development in Earth’s magnetosphere.

articles.title: SlaKoNet-VQD: A universal Slater-Koster tight-binding Hamiltonian for variational quantum band-structure calculations on near-term hardware
articles.abstract: Variational quantum algorithms such as the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and variational quantum deflation (VQD) have emerged as leading candidates for computing electronic structure on near-term quantum hardware. For periodic solids, however, their reach has been limited not by the quantum algorithm itself but by the cost of constructing a faithful second-quantized Hamiltonian for each material, typically via density-functional theory (DFT) followed by Wannierization or by hand-fitted empirical tight-binding parameters. SlaKoNet, a recently developed method, significantly reduces the computational cost of electronic Hamiltonian construction with a small accuracy tradeoff. It integrates modern deep-learning methods and the Slater-Koster tight-binding formalism to fit thousands of onsite and distance-dependent hopping and overlap tight-binding parameters across 65 elements of the periodic table. After fitting, these parameters can be used to deterministically construct an electronic Hamiltonian for any crystal made up of any of the 65 elements in the training set, and the crystal's band structure can subsequently be computed. In this work, we combine a SlaKoNet model trained on the JARVIS-TBmBJ dataset with a Qiskit-based variational quantum deflation algorithm, replacing the traditional and costly Hamiltonian construction step with a universal neural Hamiltonian generator. Within the 65-element set, the resulting SlaKoNet-VQD workflow is structure-agnostic, fully differentiable, fast, and suited to high-throughput screening of band structures. We benchmark the workflow on silicon, recovering the full eight-band band structure along the standard high-symmetry k-path with a mean absolute deviation of 1.78 meV from exact diagonalization on a 3-qubit statevector simulator. We further compute the full band structure for five additional conventional superconductors, Al, Ta, Nb, V, and ZrN, achieving a mean absolute deviation within approximately 1.8 meV, and demonstrate full execution of SlaKoNet-VQD on IBM Quantum hardware for a representative k-point ground-state calculation on aluminum with a mean absolute error of roughly 0.37 eV. Beyond the single-particle level, we promote the same SlaKoNet Hamiltonian to a correlated Hubbard model and solve it with dynamical mean-field theory, recovering the weakening of correlations across the group-5 metals and strong quasiparticle renormalization in the cuprate La₂CuO₄, and we identify the resulting impurity problem as the natural target for a quantum solver. The pipeline opens a path to high-throughput benchmarking of variational quantum algorithms across the periodic table and to gradient-based co-optimization of ansatz and Hamiltonian for materials discovery. An interactive web app is available at https://atomgpt.org/quantum.

articles.title: Orientation Mechanics and Kinetic Constraints of In-Situ Low-Field Magnetic Alignment in Vat Photopolymerization
articles.abstract: In-situ magnetic alignment of microfillers during vat photopolymerization (VP) offers a route to fabricating functional composites, but electromagnetic hardware retrofits introduce significant spatial, kinematic, and thermal trade-offs. This technical note evaluates the operational boundaries of a low-field Helmholtz coil retrofitted to a commercial liquid crystal display (LCD)-based VP printer. Despite single-particle models predicting sufficient torque to overcome viscous drag, active-field operation (0.31- 0.40 mT ) yielded modest directional alignment (S2D=0.156±0.104, R2=0.60±0.26, across N=5 samples, 10 total region of interests (ROIs), 0.092 wt%  / 0.038 vol% ) compared to isotropic controls (S2D=-0.004±0.044, R2=0.45±0.15). This work delivers two key contributions: (1) it establishes that low-field conditions (0.31–0.40 mT) mark the lower sensitivity threshold required to initiate weak, statistically verifiable microscale directional bias above background noise, while quantifying the substantial field deficit relative to the ~15–50 mT needed for macro-scale functional anisotropy, and (2) it presents an analytical framework decoupling physical order parameters (S2D) from distribution curve fitting (R2), demonstrating that fit accuracy alone cannot confirm alignment. Primary performance bottlenecks-including fibre agglomeration, field magnitude deficits, and rapid particle sedimentation restricting printing to single layers-are quantified to provide critical engineering scaling criteria for future high-field magnetic additive manufacturing systems.

articles.title: Comparison of calcined and sulfonated α-hematite as catalysts for biodiesel production from cow tallow
articles.abstract: Calcined iron (CI) and sulfonated calcined iron (SCI) catalysts prepared from alpha-hematite derived from waste iron filings were compared for biodiesel production from cow tallow. The study reports calcination at 900 °C for CI and subsequent treatment of CI with concentrated sulfuric acid to obtain SCI. X-ray diffraction gave reported crystallite sizes of 1.237 nm for CI and 1.944 nm for SCI. Brunauer-Emmett-Teller analysis showed a higher specific surface area for SCI (337.13 m²/g) than for CI (294.72 m²/g), together with a larger pore volume (0.201 versus 0.152 cm³/g), a narrower pore width, and a smaller reported pore diameter. Both catalysts were evaluated at methanol-to-oil ratios of 3:1, 4:1, 5:1 and 6:1 in a 100 mL glass reactor on a digital magnetic stirrer with yield calculated as (mass of biodiesel produced / mass of cow tallow used) × 100. The highest yield for both catalysts occurred at 5:1, reaching 60.953% with CI and 62.159% with SCI. Across all tested ratios, CI had the higher reported arithmetic mean yield (51.79% versus 49.36%), largely because SCI showed a pronounced decrease at 4:1. The evidence therefore supports SCI as the higher-performing catalyst at the reported optimum ratio, while CI appears more consistent across the tested methanol-to-oil range. Because the source manuscript contains conflicting statements about some preparation conditions and does not provide numerical fatty acid methyl ester composition data, these points are not reconstructed or supplemented.

articles.title: Mathematical Modeling of the Ni(OH)₂/NiOOH Reaction on a Nickel Rotating Disk Electrode: A Foundation for Studying Organic Electrooxidation
articles.abstract: Nickel is a low-cost, widely available metal well suited to large-scale applications such as wastewater treatment, sensors, and electrosynthesis, where the electrochemically active species is a thin Ni(OH)2/NiOOH surface layer. Existing models are largely battery-oriented, limiting their transferability across these applications. Here, the Ni(OH)2/NiOOH reaction was modeled on a nickel rotating disk electrode (RDE) to simulate cyclic voltammetry, combining species conservation equations, Butler–Volmer kinetics, and a Nernst expression with composition-dependent activity coefficients, with kinetic and thermodynamic parameters fitted to experimental data. Hysteresis between oxidation and reduction was captured by assigning distinct equilibrium-potential parameters to the forward and reverse scans. A kinetics-limited Surface Model was compared to a proton-diffusion-limited Layer Model using a block permutation test, which found no statistically significant difference in fit quality; the Surface Model was therefore preferred for its simpler structure and better-constrained parameters. The dominant factor in reproducing experimental voltammograms was the description of the activity coefficients in the equilibrium-potential expression; among several candidates, a Wohl expansion using four proton–proton self-interaction coefficients was selected. Model predictions were extended across 0.1–1.0 M NaOH by introducing an empirical correction that made the maximum concentration of electroactive material depend on surface OH⁻ concentration. Simulated and experimental voltammograms were both insensitive to rotation speed, indicating that OH⁻ transport does not limit the reaction at 100 mV s− 1. Because the RDE geometry defines mass transport unambiguously, the model provides a foundation, extensible to organic substrates, for mathematical modeling of organic electrooxidation on nickel electrodes.

articles.title: A Framework Based on hp-Finite Elements for Solving the Time-Harmonic Maxwell Equations
articles.abstract: The accurate computational solution of the time-harmonic Maxwell equations remains a central challenge in computational electromagnetics due to the indefinite nature of the double curl operator, the presence of spurious modes, and the high computational cost of resolving oscillatory solutions at large frequencies. In this work, we develop a hp-finite element method to solve the double-curl operator of time-harmonic Maxwell equations, as well as the resulting oscillatory modes. The approach uses Engquist-Majda absorbing boundary conditions and adaptive hp-refinements to efficiently handle unbounded domains and complex field behavior. To complement the analysis, a complete adaptive implementation is developed based on residual error estimation, and automatic selection between hand p-refinement using a local smoothness indicator. This provides a practical realization of the proposed adaptive strategy. We present stability analysis and establish a priori and a posteriori error estimates that ensure optimal decay of the discretization error. The numerical results confirm mathematical rigor of the formulation and demonstrate that the balance between hand p-refinements yields optimal convergence with respect to the degrees of freedom. This method provides a substantial improvement in accuracy and efficiency compared to conventional finite element for time-harmonic electromagnetic fields. One can show [4] that the solution of problem (8) coincides with that of (7).

articles.title: Hydrocolloid-Driven Structure-Property Relationships and pH-Responsive Release of C-Phycocyanin from Alginate-Chitosan Composite Hydrogel Beads
articles.abstract: C-phycocyanin (CPC) is a natural blue pigment with high functional value, but its limited stability restricts its use in food systems. This study developed alginate–chitosan composite hydrogel beads containing carrageenan, pectin, or gellan gum to improve CPC retention and control its release under gastrointestinal conditions. Hydrocolloid and chitosan concentrations were optimized using response surface methodology, and the selected formulations were characterized for encapsulation performance, physicochemical properties, morphology, molecular interactions, surface charge, storage stability, and in vitro release. Among the composite systems, alginate–carrageenan–chitosan (Al-Car-Chi) showed the highest CPC encapsulation efficiency (99.69%), whereas alginate–pectin–chitosan (Al-Pec-Chi) gave the highest bead production yield (78.91%). SEM, FTIR, and zeta potential analyses showed clear differences in network organization and interfacial properties among the formulations, indicating that CPC retention was governed by the combined effects of polymer composition rather than by a single physical property. During storage, wet beads deteriorated rapidly at 30°C, while refrigeration at 4°C delayed deterioration. Under simulated gastrointestinal conditions, all formulations limited CPC release to below 2% during the gastric phase. Release increased in simulated intestinal fluid, reaching 41.63% for Al-Chi and only 22.45% for Al-Car-Chi at 240 min. The Korsmeyer-Peppas model provided the most consistent fit to intestinal release data ((:R²) = 0.967–0.992), indicating complex non-Fickian transport in the composite systems. Although, hydrocolloid type strongly affected CPC encapsulation, storage behavior, and release, with Al-Car-Chi providing high initial CPC retention together with relatively slow intestinal release.

articles.title: Generative Quantum Search for Combinatorial Optimization: Learning Shallow Quantum Samplers for Classically Refined Solution Subspaces
articles.abstract: We port the Generative Quantum Eigensolver + Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction (GQE+QSCI) architecture from quantum chemistry to combinatorial graph optimization. Our framework, GQO+QSS (Generative Quantum Optimization + Quantum-Selected Search), follows the same principle: ML generates circuit programs, quantum samplers produce bitstrings, classical recovery repairs and expands them into a restricted subspace, and a classical solver finds the optimum within that subspace. We formalize the key quantity as the recovery-basin mass pr(qθ,G) = Prx∼qθ [x ∈ Ar(G)], where Ar(G) = x : Er(R(x))∩X∗(G) ̸= ∅ is the preimage of the optimal set under repair R and r-flip expansion Er. Under B independent shots, success probability becomes Psuccess = 1 − (1 − pr)B. The quantum-benefit question reduces to: does pr(qquantum,G) > pr(qclassical,G)? We test this on MaximumWeighted Independent Set (MWIS) with a preregistered, frozen protocol. All 150 ground truths are certified with CBC + brute-force verification. Exact recovery-basin masks are enumerated for all n ≤ 20 instances. Nine samplers are compared on a held-out test set: uniform, greedy, simulated annealing, tabu search, multi-start local search, Metropolis, warm-start QAOA, oracle QAOA, and a matched learned classical policy. Key findings:  1. Tabu search dominates at all sizes (pr = 0.82–0.94), followed by simulated annealing. All quantum samplers and the learned classical policy lose to both at every problem size under the frozen test protocol.  2. Oracle QAOA loses to SA under fair evaluation: With random QAOA configurations (not per-instance optimized), oracle QAOA achieves pr = 0.014 at n = 28 vs SA’s 0.088. The earlier positive result (pr = 0.185 vs 0.130) required per-instance best-of-50 configuration selection—an oracle upper bound, not a deployable method.  3. Learned classical policy matches oracle QAOA: A matched 140K-parameter classical policy achieves pr = 0.005–0.101, comparable to oracle QAOA’s 0.014–0.113. The quantum circuit’s proposal distribution provides no structural advantage over a matched learned classical model in this setting.  4. Recovery-basin masks reveal the phase structure: At r = 2, uniform-sampling Precover drops from 0.975 (n = 16) to 0.775 (n = 20) at B = 200, identifying the regime where sampler quality matters.  5. Hardware robustness without advantage: 136 cores on Piast-Q show 93.4% recovery consistency between QPU and simulator, but no basin-mass advantage.  This is a falsification study: Under rigorous, preregistered evaluation with matched learned baselines, shallow QAOA-derived proposal distributions do not outperform matched classical proposal models, and both lose to strong classical baselines (SA, tabu). The earlier positive oracle result was an artifact of per-instance configuration selection. We claim no quantum advantage.

articles.title: Experimental demonstration of a reconfigurable three-user quantum digital signature network
articles.abstract: Quantum digital signature (QDS) provides information-theoretic security and enables fundamental cryptographic functionalities, including integrity, non-repudiation, and data origin authentication. Existing QDS implementations, however, assign fixed user roles - signer, authenticator, and verifier - which limits their applicability in practical quantum networks, where role flexibility is essential. In this work, we implement a QDS protocol on a three-user fiber-optic quantum network in which any participant can dynamically assume the role of signer. Every node uses an identical design for encoding and decoding time-bin quantum states, enabling flexible signer assignment without hardware reconfiguration. We evaluate the signature rate and secret key rate for all possible signer configurations and show that valid signatures can be generated even in regimes where quantum key distribution (QKD) fails to produce a secret key. This result highlights a fundamental practical advantage of QDS over QKD at small classical post-processing block sizes, where key distillation is not achievable. Our results establish the feasibility of reconfigurable quantum signature networks and represent an important step toward scalable and robust quantum communication infrastructures.

articles.title: Does learning when to look pay for home service robots? A preregistered test of adaptive perception scheduling in closed-loop navigation
articles.abstract: A household service robot has to watch for objects on the floor while it moves, and on a small, battery-powered computer the object detector is often the most expensive part of that job. Adaptive perception, which runs the detector only when and where it seems necessary, is a popular way of reducing this cost, but it is rarely evaluated in a closed loop where a missed detection can leave a task unfinished or cause a collision. We tested it in 25 photorealistic home scans that were held out from all training, with obstacles that reach the planner only through the detector. The evaluated controller learns when to run the detector and adds hand-designed rules for where to look and which model size to use, a safety shield and an experience memory. The task, its validity gates and the success criterion were fixed in a preregistration, and the comparison against twelve baselines was run once (120 paired episodes per policy). The controller cut computation by 85% relative to running the heavy detector on every frame, but it reached the goal in 55.0% of episodes, against 79.2% for that baseline, and collided in 8.3%, against 0.8% for the light detector run on every frame, so it did not meet the criterion. For designers of home service robots the message is practical: running the cheapest adequate detector on every frame is a strong default, and on the measured processor it is also the only detector tier that completes within the 0.1 s control period. An adaptive scheduler should be adopted only after it beats that default in closed-loop tests.

articles.title: Memory Physics, Finite Capacity, and Topology in Heterogeneous Quantum Networks
articles.abstract: Quantum-network capacity planning couples memory physics, finite storage, topology, and traffic. We study these interactions using a discrete-event simulator with six representative memory profiles. A memory–topology atlas contains 9,360 completed runs, complemented by 8,730 confirmatory runs and an extended per-node memory-budget sweep. We distinguish a threshold relative to the best performance observed on a finite grid from a physical saturation limit. Among 840 reported threshold estimates, 22.3% reach 95% of the observed maximum by four slots per node, while 35.5% first reach it at the upper grid boundary of 64 slots. Four tested scalar reductions do not provide a topology independent collapse; the best pooled quadratic fit explains 37.9% of response variance. The retrieval-window parameter χr = τr pgen/tattempt provides an interpretable descriptor, but an independent-channel approximation does not establish a network memorysizing law. In 5,310 heterogeneous-placement runs, hub and betweenness-based placement outperform peripheral placement in aggregate, with topology-specific exceptions. Coupling assumptions change absolute performance while preserving the aggregate strategy ordering. Harmonized model comparisons provide limited robustness evidence, not1 independent native-protocol validation. The results support model-specific capacity and placement analysis with explicit metric definitions, finite-grid limitations, and interface assumptions

articles.title: A Mini Review of Direct Aqueous Carbonation of Calcium Carbide Residue and Ferrous Slag for Carbon Mineralization and Cementitious Applications
articles.abstract: Direct aqueous carbonation of alkaline industrial residues has emerged as a promising pathway for CO₂ sequestration and waste valorization; however, its effectiveness is strongly constrained by material-specific reaction mechanisms. Carbonation of calcium carbide residue (CCR) alone is limited by rapid surface passivation caused by localized CaCO₃ precipitation, while iron- and steel-making slags often exhibit sluggish carbonation due to kinetically inert silicate matrices and restricted calcium availability. Recent studies demonstrate that combining CCR with slag fundamentally alters the carbonation pathway by redistributing carbonate precipitation away from CCR particle surfaces, mitigating passivation, and enabling sustained calcium dissolution. This mini review synthesizes recent advances in aqueous carbonation of CCR and CCR–slag systems with a mechanistic focus on rate-controlling regimes, precipitation topology, and interfacial processes. Particular attention is given to reconciling contradictory trends in operating parameters and elucidating how carbonation-derived products perform as supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs). Available evidence indicates that carbonated CCR and CCR–slag products primarily function as fillers and hydration nucleation agents, with strength enhancement confined to low replacement levels and fresh-state behavior governed by carbonate morphology and surface characteristics. Durability performance remains largely unverified, representing a critical barrier to practical deployment. By integrating mechanistic insights with performance considerations, this review identifies key design principles and research priorities necessary to advance carbonation-based valorization of CCR and related industrial residues.

articles.title: Enhancing Predictive Analytics in Industrial Robot Operations with Cycle-Consistent Encoding and Quantum Multi-Output Networks: A Control Theory-Inspired Solution
articles.abstract: Industrial robotic systems rely on predictive maintenance to prevent failures and optimize operational efficiency. However, accurately detecting faults such as protective stop and grip loss remains challenging due to high-dimensional sensor data and inherent noise. To address this, we propose a quantum multi-output network combined with cycle-consistent autoencoders, leveraging quantum feature encoding to enhance fault detection. The model effectively reduces dimensionality while mitigating quantum noise propagation, ensuring computational efficiency with fewer qubits. Our approach achieves 77% training accuracy and 76% validation accuracy, with F1 scores of 0.70 for protective stop and 0.68 for grip loss, significantly outperforming conventional deep learning models such as CNN-RNN (54.9%) and gradient boosting (67.6%). Compared to baseline multi-output networks, our quantum-enhanced framework provides a notable performance boost while maintaining robustness across large-scale datasets. By integrating quantum computing principles with structured sensor processing, our method demonstrates superior predictive capability for industrial fault detection. This study underscores the potential of hybrid quantum-classical architectures in industrial automation and sets the foundation for further advancements in quantum-enhanced predictive maintenance systems.

articles.title: Measurement Error Evaluation Method for Distribution Network Voltage Transformers Based on an Attention-RBF Physics-Informed Neural Network
articles.abstract: To address the problems of power interruption and low efficiency in the conventional verification of distribution network voltage transformers (VTs), this paper proposes a physics-informed neural network integrating an attention mechanism and radial basis functions (Attention-RBF-PINN) method for online error evaluation of distribution network VTs. In this method, Kirchhoff’s voltage law (KVL) topological constraints of switching stations and the cable thermal equation are embedded into the neural network as soft loss terms. Meanwhile, radial basis functions (RBFs) are adopted to extract multi-scale temporal features, and a residual attention mechanism is employed to adaptively weight multi-branch inputs, thereby enabling VT error estimation. Experiments conducted on a laboratory physical simulation platform demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms comparable methods in all evaluation metrics. Compared with the second-ranked MRSA-DGCN, the RMSE is reduced by 35.2%, the MAE is reduced by 36.4%, and the R² is improved by 2.63 percentage points. In field application, one out-of-tolerance VT was successfully identified, and the evaluation result was consistent with the de-energized verification result. This study indicates that the fusion of physical guidance and data-driven modeling can effectively improve the accuracy and physical interpretability of transformer error evaluation, providing an effective approach for online error evaluation of distribution network voltage transformers.

articles.title: Gravity and quantum information linked through a derivation of Einstein's equations
articles.abstract: Recent research shows that gravity and quantum information are deeply connected and that the shape of spacetime can be traced back to the way information is stored in quantum fields.

articles.title: Hybrid Robotic Meta-gripper for Tomato Harvesting: Analysis of Auxetic Structures with Lattice Orientation Variations
articles.abstract: The agricultural sector is rapidly evolving to meet growing global food demands, yet tasks like fruit and vegetable handling remain labor-intensive, causing inefficiencies and post-harvest losses. Automation, particularly selective harvesting, offers a viable solution, with soft robotics emerging as a key enabler. This study introduces a novel hybrid gripper for tomato harvesting, incorporating arigid outer frame with a soft auxetic internal lattice. The six-finger, 3D caging-effect design enables gentle yet secure grasping in unstructured environments.Uniquely, the work investigates the effect of auxetic lattice orientation on grasping conformability, combining experimental validation with 2D Digital Image Correlation (DIC) and nonlinear finite element analysis (FEA). Auxetic configurations with unit cell inclinations of 0◦, 30◦, 45◦, and 60◦ are evaluated, andtheir grasping forces, deformation responses, and motor torque requirements aresystematically compared. Results demonstrate that lattice orientation stronglyinfluences compliance, contact forces, and energy efficiency, with distinct advan-tages across configurations. This comparative framework highlights the novelty of tailoring auxetic geometries to optimize robotic gripper performance. The findings provide new insights into soft–rigid hybrid gripper design, advancing automation strategies for precision agriculture while minimizing crop damage.

articles.title: Bandwidth, Representation Loss, and Temporal Drift in Quantum Kernel Fraud Detection: A Pre-Specified Falsification Study
articles.abstract: Quantum kernel results are often reported without holding the input representation, training sample, tuning budget and temporal evaluation protocol fixed against a matched classical kernel. This pre-specified, protocol-locked falsification study uses the Elliptic++ transaction tables (203,769 transactions, 49 time steps) under a locked temporal split (training steps 1–24, validation 25–29, test 30–49 in 4 locked windows). The primary metric is pooled Recall@5%. A frozen full-dimensional gradient-boosting model reached 0.381, and every model, including this one, collapsed in the final window. Graph structure and selective reranking were tested first and falsified. Compressing 182 features to 4, 6 and 8 principal components retained 34%, 43% and 51% of the variance and 64%, 50% and 33% of the full-dimensional model’s pooled Recall@5%. In the primary, default-bandwidth analysis, an entangling fidelity quantum kernel was below the strongest matched classical kernel at 4, 6 and 8 qubits (pooled Recall@5% differences −0.078, −0.203 and −0.146). In a secondary, post hoc bandwidth correction, explicit scale tuning raised the entangling kernel’s Recall@5% by 0.070, 0.121 and 0.109; the corrected kernel remained below the strongest matched classical kernel at 6 and 8 qubits and was statistically unresolved at 4 qubits. The selected scale lay at the lower boundary of the tested grid, and the apparent effect of entanglement depended on bandwidth. No repeatable predictive benefit of the quantum kernel over matched classical kernels was observed in the tested setting; the findings do not extend beyond this dataset, protocol, representation, feature-map family, sample size and bandwidth range.

articles.title: Woody Species Diversity and Conservation Value of Ethiopian Orthodox Church Forests: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
articles.abstract: Background Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahido Church (EOTC) forests are small, isolated sacred groves that have persisted for centuries within a landscape that has been largely deforested. These church forests are increasingly recognized as critical refugia for the nation's native woody flora. However, the evidence base for their conservation value remains fragmented across numerous primary studies, and no comprehensive quantitative synthesis has been conducted to date. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize empirical evidence on woody species diversity and conservation contributions of Ethiopian Orthodox Church forests.Methods A systematic literature search was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and the Ethiopian National Academic Digital Repository (NADRE). Studies were included if they focused on EOTC church forests, monastery forests, or sacred groves; reported quantitative data on woody species composition, richness, or diversity; and provided species-level data. Data were extracted on study metadata, church forest characteristics, species composition (scientific name, family, local name, growth habit, origin status), and diversity metrics. All scientific names were standardized against the iNaturalist/Kew taxonomic backbone. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled mean species richness per church forest. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic, and subgroup analyses were conducted by region and church forest type.Results A total of 14 studies met the inclusion criteria, representing approximately 80 church forests across four major regions of Ethiopia (Amhara, Oromia, Tigrai, and South Ethiopia) and Addis Ababa. A total of 330 woody species records were compiled, of which 310 were retained after excluding herbaceous species and unresolved taxa. These species belonged to approximately 85 families, with Fabaceae being the most species-rich family (n = 42), followed by Euphorbiaceae (n = 18), Asteraceae (n = 15), Malvaceae (n = 12), and Rubiaceae (n = 11). Of the 310 species, 180 (58.1%) were trees, 108 (34.8%) were shrubs, and 22 (7.1%) were lianas. A total of 280 species (90.3%) were indigenous, 27 (8.7%) were exotic, and 3 (1.0%) were endemic to Ethiopia. The most frequently recorded species were Juniperus procera, Olea europaea subsp. cuspidata, Croton macrostachyus, Cordia africana, Ficus sur, Carissa spinarum, and Maytenus arbutifolia. Species richness per church forest ranged from 7 to 166 species, with a mean of 62.4 species (SD = 38.7) across single-church studies. The random-effects meta-analysis estimated a pooled mean species richness of 74.8 species per church forest (95% CI: 58.3–91.4), with high heterogeneity (I² = 87.4%). Subgroup analysis revealed significant regional differences (p = 0.001), with the highest species richness in the Amhara region (mean = 84.2) and the lowest in the Tigrai region (mean = 52.7). Egger's regression test indicated no significant publication bias (p = 0.238).Conclusion This systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrates that Ethiopian Orthodox Church forests are critical in-situ conservation sites for the nation's native woody flora. The 310 woody species documented in this review represent at least 12.5% of Ethiopia's estimated woody plant diversity and 48% of its endemic species. The dominance of indigenous species (90.3%) confirms that traditional EOTC management practices are effective in conserving native biodiversity. These findings justify the formal recognition of church forests as priority sites for national biodiversity conservation and call for enhanced support for traditional management practices. Future research should prioritize floristic surveys in underrepresented regions and longitudinal monitoring of church forest dynamics.

articles.title: Correlating Charge-Storage Kinetics, Quantum Capacitance, and Surface Charge Density in Bi2O2S: An Experimental-DFT Study
articles.abstract: Understanding charge storage in layered electrode materials requires distinguishing electrochemical kinetics from the intrinsic ability of the electrode to accumulate electronic charge. Here, phase-pure Bi2O2S was investigated using electrochemical measurements and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to establish this relationship. Cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge-discharge, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed a strongly rate-dependent charge-storage response, with a specific capacitance of 866 F g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹. The scan-rate dependence gave an average b-value of ~ 0.61, while Dunn analysis showed that diffusion-dependent processes dominate the charge-storage response. DFT calculations further demonstrated that surface modification alters the electronic charge-storage ability of Bi2O2S. The calculated quantum capacitance increased from 493.14 (:μ:Fcm⁻²) for the pristine surface to 638.75 (:μ:Fcm⁻²) following OH adsorption. Surface charge densities of 513.46 and 506.76 (:μ:C:cm⁻²) were obtained for K-top and K-hollow configurations, respectively. Experimental surface charge densities approached the DFT-derived range at higher current densities, whereas larger deviations at lower current densities indicate additional contributions from electrolyte-mediated and Faradaic processes. These results establish an experimental-DFT framework for relating rate-dependent electrochemical charge storage to the intrinsic electronic charge-accumulation behaviour of Bi2O2S.

articles.title: Optimize the Optimization: QPU-Efficient Quantum Graph Optimization through HPC-First Experimentation
articles.abstract: This paper studies how much Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) work can be avoided while preserving optimization quality in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). Using exact statevector simulation of QAOA on six graph optimization problems across seven graph families, three baselines are compared: a naive QPU-centric workflow with 30 quantum evaluations, a best-practice workflow that separates classical parameter optimization from a single QPU evaluation, and a classical-only solver. Six QPUminimization strategies are evaluated: preprocessing, pretraining, surrogate modeling, adaptive stopping, adaptive shots, and measurement reuse. Quality is measured using normalized expected value rather than the saturated best-of-b metric. The key findings are: the best-practice baseline achieves 510- to 2070-fold shot reduction across 8 to 16 qubits with at most 0.4 percent quality loss relative to naive QAOA; quality improves with QAOA depth from 0.82 to 0.91 while the gap between naive and best-practice remains negligible; four of six strategies achieve 100 percent quality retention at depth 3; quality is stable across graph families ranging from 0.77 to 0.87; and a structural predictor achieves perfect prediction on held-out graph families. These results support the thesis that the required QPU budget is a structured, predictable function of the problem instance and workflow policy, rather than a fixed algorithmic constant.

articles.title: Hidden magnetic complexity in the simple van der Waals ferromagnet Ce₂Te₅
articles.abstract: Author(s): Rajesh Tripathi, D. T. Adroja, C. Ritter, Leandro Liborio, Manuel dos Santos Dias, Leon Petit, D. Khalyavin, Yu Liu, T. Shiroka, M. Aouane, S. Langridge, S. Patil, and Eric D. Bauer Van der Waals magnets provide a platform for exploring how reduced dimensionality, competing interactions, and local electronic degrees of freedom shape magnetic order. Here, the authors uncover hidden complexity in Ce 2 Te 5 , a layered f -electron ferromagnet whose apparently simple magnetic ground state masks a richer microscopic landscape. Although the system develops a single long-range ferromagnetic structure, the two inequivalent Ce sites play markedly different roles in the ordered state, and subtle magnetic changes persist well below the ordering temperature. The combination of site-selective magnetism and strong single-ion anisotropy highlights how competing interactions can produce complex low-temperature behavior without generating additional long-range magnetic phases. articles.title: Local chemical softness as a reactivity probe in mixed-valence compounds of class I and class II (Cr 2 F 5 and Co 3 O 4 ): The importance of site-dependent Hubbard U parameters
articles.abstract: In this work, we employ local softness as a key reactivity descriptor to systematically analyze class I (Cr 2 F 5 ) and class II (Co 3 O 4 ) mixed-valence materials. We evaluated the performance of several exchange–correlation functionals, including PBEsol, NCAPR (Nearly Correct Asymptotic Potential Revised), SCAN (Strongly Constrained and Appropriately Normed), and PBE+U (Perdew–Burke–Ernezerhof + Hubbard U), to determine their ability to resolve electron donor and acceptor capacities. Our results demonstrated that local softness is a powerful tool for distinguishing non-equivalent metallic centers and coexisting oxidation states. Crucially, we found that the PBE+U functional, utilizing site-specific Hubbard parameters (U) calculated via density functional perturbation theory, is the most robust approach, consistently reproducing the expected one-electron transfer. This study highlights the necessity of integrating local reactivity descriptors with differentiated Hubbard corrections for the accurate design and characterization of redox-active functional materials.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevents overfitting and matches the performance of iterative refinement baselines with significantly reduced overhead. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated by recovering accurate physical observables for liquid water from unconverged reference data, including diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we validate its scalability by training a foundation model for organic chemistry on the SPICE dataset, where it reduces both energy and force errors. This framework provides a simple, automated solution for training robust models on imperfect datasets across dataset sizes.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Building new non-empirical hybrid and double-hybrid density functionals from the TCA family of GGA expressions
articles.abstract: The Tognetti–Cortona–Adamo (TCA) correlation functional, and their subsequent variants, constitutes an important family of nonempirical generalized gradient approximations that have found successful applications in molecular and solid-state electronic structure calculations. In this work, we present a systematic assessment of the original TCA functional together with the revTCA, gracTCA, and transTCA variants within nonempirical hybrid (TCA0) and double-hybrid (TCA-QIDH) frameworks. Their performance is evaluated using the comprehensive GMTKN55 benchmark database, including more detailed analysis of the challenging MB16-43 and SIE4x4 subsets, as well as three different global performance metrics: WTMAD-2A, WTMAD-2B, and the recently proposed WTMAD-4. The results reveal a consistent improvement in accuracy upon ascending “Jacob’s ladder,” with the nonempirical double-hybrid models reducing the global errors by approximately a factor of 2–3 relative to their GGA counterparts. Among the semilocal functionals, the original TCA correlation provides the most balanced overall performance, while the differences among the various TCA-based models become much less pronounced at the double-hybrid level. Importantly, the relative ranking of the functionals is essentially unaffected by the choice of the WTMAD metric, demonstrating the robustness of the conclusions with respect to the weighting scheme adopted for the GMTKN55 database. The remaining deficiencies are associated with dispersion-dominated intermolecular interactions, highlighting the potential use of some long-range correlation corrections. Overall, this study confirms that the TCA functional, particularly when adopted in a double-hybrid scheme, constitutes a reliable and transferable framework for the development of accurate density functional approximations applicable to a broad range of chemical problems.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Cooling down trees for finite-temperature quantum dynamics: Purification within ML-MCTDH
articles.abstract: Simulating multidimensional quantum systems at finite temperature is inherently challenging as the system is no longer described by a single, pure-state wavefunction but by a density operator, squaring an already exponential scaling of the Hilbert space. Building upon the compact wavefunction ansatz of the multi-layer multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (ML-MCTDH) method, we present a new scheme for simulating finite-temperature quantum dynamics based on purification. Here, a density operator is mapped to a single ML-MCTDH wavefunction in an enlarged Hilbert space, comprising physical and auxiliary degrees of freedom. In the key step, one obtains a pure-state representation of the canonical density operator via imaginary time-propagation of the infinite-temperature state. The most important observation is that this state can be exactly decomposed as a Hartree product of maximally entangled combined modes, each combined mode consisting of a physical degree of freedom and its auxiliary counterpart. Through dynamically pruning the node ranks of the ML-tree during the “cool down” stage yields a compact finite-temperature wavefunction, thus accelerating the real-time propagation and enabling finite-temperature simulations of multidimensional, correlated molecular systems. Our method circumvents both intensive statistical sampling and costly tensor-decomposition of the full density-operator, while being broadly applicable to model Hamiltonians and general ab initio potential energy surfaces alike. Two applications of the method are presented: benchmark results on the thermal ground-state of H 2 O, as well as temperature-dependent infrared absorption spectra of the more challenging, floppy H3O2− anion.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Cluster-resolved associating-fluid theory for patch-geometry-dependent phase behavior in patchy particle mixtures
articles.abstract: The spatial arrangement of binding patches is a key design variable in programmable self-assembly because it determines which local motifs, network connectivities, and ordered states are accessible at equilibrium. Yet this geometric information is often lost in analytical theories of associating fluids, which typically distinguish particles by valence and interaction strength but not by local patch arrangement. This limitation is especially pronounced in quasi-two-dimensional and interfacial assemblies, where reduced coordination enhances the thermodynamic impact of steric and bonding constraints. Here, we present a cluster-resolved statistical associating fluid theory (SAFT-P) that promotes a chosen local cluster (superparticle) to an explicit thermodynamic degree of freedom. This approach preserves an analytical free-energy description while retaining local motif information. Using binary and ternary patchy mixtures on two-dimensional square lattices with identical valence but different patch arrangements, we show that local geometry can shift phase boundaries and bias demixing in ways that conventional monomer-level SAFT does not capture. In particular, SAFT-P predicts an excess-composition coexistence curve for a mixture of four-patch geometric isomers that conventional monomer-level SAFT cannot distinguish at matched valence and interaction strengths. We also test the theory on two-dimensional triangular and three-dimensional cubic lattices, which are included primarily to demonstrate the extensibility of the framework. SAFT-P therefore provides a practical route to connect nanoscale patch placement with mesoscopic assembly and macroscopic thermodynamics in patchy colloids and related interfacial assemblies.

articles.title: Tensor train compression of molecular orbitals
articles.abstract: This work systematically investigates the tensor train (TT) compressibility of grid-represented Hartree–Fock (HF) and Density Functional Theory (DFT) orbitals across a range of molecular systems and TT formats (standard, quantized, and z-permuted quantized). To overcome limitations of current TT solvers, we employ a novel orthogonal tensor train cross approximation (TT-Cross-Orth) to decompose Hartree–Fock and DFT orbitals into TTs, enabling the study of large molecules. We find that the approximation error decreases exponentially with TT-rank for all systems studied and identify quantized tensor train as the most efficient TT format. Furthermore, we identify quasi-periodic and symmetric structures—including graphene, graphite layers, and polyalanine helices—as particularly favorable candidates exhibiting sublinear rank growth with system size. The tensor train approach automatically compresses quasi-symmetries and systems with symmetry defects, which makes it an attractive approach for materials science applications. TT-Cross-Orth enforces orthogonality during the decomposition, thereby improving stability and reducing the number of function evaluations compared to standard TT-Cross. These findings establish an empirical foundation for the development of scalable tensor network methods for HF and DFT.

articles.title: Holographic generative flows with AdS/CFT
articles.abstract: Holography, in the form of the anti-de Sitter/conformal field theory correspondence, offers a natural setting for generative modelling. Data on a boundary manifold lifts into a higher-dimensional bulk through a propagator, and this extra dimension plays the role of a flow parameter. We exploit this structure to build Generative AdS (GenAdS), an approach to generative flow matching in which the dynamics are represented by the evolution of fields in AdS, together with a residual correction learned by a neural network. Boundary samples are encoded as scalar sources, transported into the bulk along the flow, and decoded after numerical integration. Our paradigm combines a Fourier-space encoding scheme for the data as AdS sources, a normalised radial phase space in which to stage the flow-matching dynamics, and a Klein–Gordon backbone to guide the flow. On a two-dimensional checkerboard benchmark, our experiments show that most of the benefit of GenAdS comes from the Fourier representation and convolutional architecture. However, when we remove momentum-channel regularisation, our most physics-informed GenAdS variant rivals the strongest physics-free control on boundary violation. On modified National Institute of Standards and Technology, GenAdS models remain close to a convolutional baseline on fidelity while achieving significantly higher recall at comparable precision, suggesting a fidelity-coverage trade-off. Our findings establish GenAdS as a physically interpretable and experimentally controllable framework for generative modelling, with many avenues for future extension.
authors: Ehsan Mirafzali, Sanjit Shashi, Sanya Murdeshwar, Edgar Shaghoulian, Daniele Venturi and Razvan Marinescu

articles.title: Frustrated Topological Orbital Magnetism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By studying the interplay of geometric frustration with Aharonov-Bohm fluxes in three dimensions, we unveil a rich playground exhibiting topological semimetallic ground states with orbital magnetic dipole, quadrupole and ferrotoroidic orders, akin to spin patterns in classical spin ices - a class of phenomena which we dub frustrated topological orbital magnetism. We demonstrate that the ground-state toroidizations underpinned by non-Abelian topological nodal lines induce measurable current-induced Hall phenomena. We further find that distinct 2-in-2-out and 3-in-1-out frustrated orbital current patterns can be associated with topological Weyl node charges, and corresponding anisotropic linear and nonlinear Hall effects. We propose signatures for experimental validation of distinct frustrated topological orbital magnetic orders in candidate materials.
authors: Sergio Garrido Bourkhaeva, Claudio Castelnovo, Wojciech J. Jankowski

articles.title: Enhanced Coulomb pseudopotentials in high-pressure hydrides from first principles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Eliashberg theory of superconductivity, Coulomb interactions oppose the phonon-mediated attraction and suppress the superconducting critical temperature Tc. However, most first-principles predictions continue to treat this repulsion with an empirical Coulomb pseudopotential μ^*ME in the range 0.1-0.15. Here we present first-principles calculations of the Coulomb parameter μ and pseudopotential μ^*ME in superconducting hydrides across a range of pressures. The screened Coulomb interaction is evaluated at the random phase approximation level with the Mantel code. We demonstrate that several hydride systems, including H₃S, YSbH₆ and Mg₂IrH₆, have strong Coulomb repulsions driven by a large density of states at the Fermi energy, NF. For Mg₂IrH₆ we obtain μ=0.62 and μ^*MEapprox0.39, leading to a 40 K suppression in Tc relative to a standard μ^*ME=0.16. Our obtained μ^*ME is far above the conventional range and, accounting for the energy dependence of the density of states, resolves the factor-of-two discrepancy between Tc estimates of previous studies. Across all systems and pressures studied, we find that μ closely tracks NF, suggesting that commonly used μ^*ME values lead to overestimated Tc in materials where the density of states at the Fermi energy is large.

articles.title: Odd-parity surface magnetism in a Kondo insulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a theory of spin-polarized tunneling between a nanowire tip of a topological Kondo insulator SmB₆ and the bi-collinear antiferromagnet Fe₁₊ₓTe in which the tunneling conductance which measures magnetic contrast changes sign when the bias is reversed. First we show that no time reversal symmetric tip, however strong its spin-momentum locking is, can produce experimentally observed magnetic contrast, which implies that time reversal must be broken at the tip surface. Within a mean-field treatment of the surface theory of SmB₆ we find that the interaction between conduction d-and f-electrons drives a surface phase transition near T_c ~10 K in which the time reversal odd component of the Kondo hybridization amplitude condenses in the same symmetry channel as an out-of-plane surface magnetization, gapping out the Dirac surface states. Below the transition the spin-resolved spectral function of each gapped surface Dirac cone is odd in energy about its node. For a charge-neutral apex the Fermi level lies between the surface Γ and X Dirac nodes, so the spin-polarized conductance, which is determined by this function at the bias energy, reverses its sign close to zero bias. This sign change is thus a spectroscopic signature of time reversal symmetry breaking on the surface of SmB6.

articles.title: Homogeneous to multi-scale inhomogeneous complex magnetism in Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho), Revealed by muSR and Machine-Learned Muon-Site Calculations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a comprehensive muon spin rotation and relaxation (muSR) study of the hexagonal 6H-perovskites Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho) to investigate the role of rare-earth anisotropy in the magnetic ground state of 4d-4f coupled systems. Ba3HoRu2O9 exhibits two successive magnetic orderings at TN1 = 46 K and TN2 = 10 K, leading to a complex magnetic ground state, whereas Ba3GdRu2O9, with Gd3+ (L = 0) S-state ions, shows primarily single magnetic ordering at TN = 14.5 K. Zero-field (ZF) and longitudinal-field (LF) muSR measurements reveal markedly different magnetic behavior despite their structural similarity. Ba3HoRu2O9 displays a multi-scale inhomogeneous magnetic state characterized by two-component exponential relaxation, broad local-field distributions, incomplete LF decoupling, and persistent spin dynamics. The muSR results identify two characteristic magnetic energy scales near 46 and 10 K, associated with correlated Ru-Ho interactions and quasistatic magnetic ordering, respectively. Redfield analysis further demonstrates strong local magnetic fields and distributed spin fluctuation timescales, confirming magnetic inhomogeneity. Machine-learning-assisted muon-site and dipolar-field calculations show that the broad field distribution naturally arises from muons sensing distinct coexisting magnetic domains at different structural sites. In contrast, Ba3GdRu2O9 exhibits a comparatively homogeneous antiferromagnetic ground state below 14.5 K, with Gaussian relaxation consistent with a narrow static field distribution. These results establish that the rare-earth ion in Ba3LnRu2O9 is a powerful tuning parameter, driving the ground state from homogeneous to complex, multi-scale inhomogeneous behavior through competing 4d-4f magnetic interactions.
authors: S. Ghosh, K. Sharma, E. Kushwaha, M. Kumar, G. Roy, A. Pandey, F. L. Pratt, S. Cottrell, D. T. Adroja, T. Basu

articles.title: The quantum geometry of the chemical bond
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electronic properties of materials depend both on band energies and quantum geometry of electronic states. We relate bonding indices to the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), showing how chemical bonding dictates the momentum-space texture of bands, bridging chemical and physical descriptions of solids. We show the QGT decomposed into the three center bond index, weighted by their oriented area. Resolving these contributions by orbital pair reveals the donor--acceptor character that distinguish ionic, covalent, hypervalent, and metavalent bonding. We identify the bonding pattern for topology in materials: noncollinear three center bonds, which are the source of Berry curvature in solids. Bond fluctuation can be directly linked to electromagnetic response by resolving their energy spectrum, opening a quantitative route towards the design of physical properties of materials from bonding motifs.
authors: Gabrielle Carrel, Nishchhal Verma, Fatmagül Katmer, Leslie M. Schoop, Raquel Queiroz

articles.title: Nonlocal Josephson coupling and current redistribution in a large-area graphene multiterminal Josephson junction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) extend conventional two-terminal Josephson physics to devices defined by multiple superconducting phases, where rich phenomena have been predicted. However, in conventional MTJJs, superconducting transport is often dominated by local coupling between neighboring leads, obscuring physics that goes beyond simple connectivity. Here, we realize a multiterminal Josephson network in a graphene Hall bar geometry with micron-scale dimensions, enabling substantial nonlocal coupling between distant terminals. Our key observation is a pronounced negative differential longitudinal resistance (NDLR) in the four-probe response near switching currents, while no such feature appears in two-terminal measurements. We reproduce the NDLR response with a network containing the interplay between two distinct forms of nonlocality: nonlocal Josephson coupling, which determines the switching sequence of the superconducting network, and nonlocal normal-state conductance, which redistributes current after different regions switch. Our results highlight the potential of the emergent NDLR for characterizing superconductor--semiconductor hybrid systems and for nonlinear circuits. Further, this Josephson Hall bar geometry provides a platform for exploring the interplay between mesoscopic superconductivity and many-body ground states in graphene-based heterostructures.
authors: Luojia Zhang, Kushagra Aggarwal, Jay D. Sau, Ethan G. Arnault, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Valla Fatemi

articles.title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of two-dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXenes into Halide Perovskite (HaP) optoelectronics has shown immense potential for enhancing device performance, yet the fundamental chemical interactions within the precursor ink (a critical stage determining the final material state) remain largely unexplored. This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the chemical stability and surface evolution of Ti3C2Tx MXenes when exposed to the individual and combined components of a model methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) solution. By combining detailed X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) analysis with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, we decouple the complex interactions between MXenes and the ink constituents. We demonstrate that elemental iodine (I2) and polyiodides (In-) act as aggressive oxidizers, triggering rapid degradation and dissolution of the MXene flakes. Conversely, lead iodide (PbI2) induces a slower oxidation process driven by the strong adsorption of Pb2+ ions onto oxygen terminated sites. In stark contrast, methylammonium iodide (MAI) exhibits a stabilizing effect: it adsorbs onto the MXene surface via hydrogen bonding, effectively passivating the flakes and retarding degradation. In addition, our results reveal that the sequence of precursor addition governs the MXene surface state, requiring extra caution, but also enabling further tunability. These findings provide a critical view on how MXene integration with materials, in general, and HaP in particular, should be perceived, providing a fundamental for their rational engineering.
authors: Kirill Sobolev, Nagaprasad Reddy Samala, Mariela J. Pavan, Sharon Hazan, Vladimir Ezersky, Shakked Schwartz, Omer Bartov, Adi Yakir, Michal Leskes, Tamar Goldzak Mizrachi, Yevgeny Rakita

articles.title: Realizing Two-Dimensional Altermagnets with 100% Spin Polarization along the [110] Direction in Ambidentate-Ligand Based Square Organometallic Lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnetism, as a novel magnetic paradigm, not only possesses a zero net magnetic moment, but also exhibits a substantial nonrelativistic spin-splitting effect. Currently, developing a simple and experimentally feasible method for designing altermagnets is eagerly pursued. Moreover, achieving 100% spin polarization along certain directions in valence or conduction bands for altermagnets remains challenging. To address these issues, based on a tight-binding model, we propose a viable chemical strategy for constructing organometallic altermagnets by using ambidentate ligands. Furthermore, in these organometallic altermagnets, direction-dependent 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in band edges can be induced via the coexistence of altermagnetically spin-split dispersive and flat bands, where the flat band suppresses electron transport in one spin channel and the dispersive band enables conduction in the other spin channel.
