articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Applications of quantum devices and simulators require an accurate understanding of their dynamics as well as the effects of environmental noise. While some sources of noise can be modeled as Markovian dissipation, coupling to resonators or vibrational modes often produces non-Markovian dynamics as well, making it difficult to characterize the system, particularly for interacting many-body systems. Here, we identify a broad class of exactly solvable many-body quantum systems with both non-Markovian dynamics and Markovian dissipation. We consider a prototypical model of spins coupled to lossy bosonic modes that mediate Ising-type interactions. We exclude a transverse field but allow local spin dissipation that need not commute with the interactions, including dephasing, relaxation, pumping, and even processes that generate coherences. Using an exact stochastic representation, we decouple the many-body dynamics into the evolution of individual spins, yielding exact spin observables and correlations without adiabatically eliminating the bosons. In the Markovian limit, our solutions describe Ising models with correlated dephasing and nonreciprocal interactions. An example of spin squeezing shows that both the achievable squeezing and its optimal preparation time depend strongly on the interplay between non-Markovian dynamics and Markovian dissipation.

articles.title: Correlated Pair Creation with Positive- and Negative-Frequency Oscillators in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spin-dependent forces enable independent control over the effective frequencies of bosonic motional modes and their coupling strengths to spins in trapped-ion spin-boson quantum simulators. We show that the relative signs of these effective frequencies provide an important programmable resource for engineering distinct multimode dynamics. Focusing on a two-mode quantum Rabi model, changing the frequencies of the two modes from the same sign to opposite signs reorganizes the resonance structure of the spin-mediated bosonic interaction, converting the dominant resonant process from excitation exchange to correlated pair creation. In the dispersive regime, the resulting effective interaction realizes a two-mode parametric amplifier with stable oscillatory, critical, and exponentially amplifying regimes separated by a spin-dependent instability threshold. Across these regimes, the dynamics generate collective-quadrature squeezing and bipartite motional entanglement. Preparing the spin in a coherent superposition further allows different spin components to experience distinct stability regimes, generating tripartite spin-boson entanglement, while spin postselection can coherently combine the conditional bosonic branches to generate non-Gaussian entangled bosonic states. Finally, we outline an implementation using parameters within reach of current trapped-ion platforms.
authors: Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Han Pu, Guido Pagano

articles.title: Error correction and quantum information spreading on sparse random graphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12597v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes on graph geometries beyond regular euclidean lattices have emerged as a promising route toward robust quantum information processing. A major challenge in quantum error correction is the trade-off between favorable properties of codes constructed in high dimensionality and the need for locality in practical implementations on near-term hardware. Sparse intermediate geometries may combine the advantages of both, but how their structure governs quantum information dynamics and code performance remains unclear. Here we show that the spectral dimension dₛ, defined from the low-energy spectrum of the graph Laplacian, is the universal parameter connecting these properties. Using Floquet random Clifford circuits on two distinct sparse graph architectures with tunable spectral dimension, we find that dₛ governs both quantum information spreading and the scaling of the resulting quantum error-correcting code distance. We identify a geometry-induced entanglement phase transition from localized area-law to ergodic volume-law, whose universality is determined by dₛ and exhibits long-range percolation criticality. In the ergodic phase, the circuit acts as a CSS code encoder whose code distance is set by the competition between two logical sectors --- the cost of severing the graph and the length of its shortest winding cycle --- which connectivity pushes in opposite directions. The spectral dimension organizes this trade-off, highlighting a maximum at intermediate dₛ retaining sparse connectivity and physical realizability.
authors: Giovanni Cemin, Marin Bukov, Andrea Solfanelli

articles.title: Dissipative Majorana Chain---Anomalies and Non-Invertible Symmetries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study symmetries and anomalies of dissipative Majorana chains described by Lindblad dynamics. Using the operator-state mapping, we represent the Lindbladian as a non-Hermitian operator on a doubled Hilbert space. In this formulation, the ket and bra contours admit strong fermion parities and strong translations, while their diagonal combinations define weak symmetries. For even and odd chain lengths, we diagnose anomalies by comparing symmetry algebras with and without weak fermion-parity defects. These algebras retain the lattice precursor of the modulo-8 anomaly of the closed Majorana chain and exhibit projective relations between strong fermion parity and weak translation, as well as between weak fermion parity and strong translation, which are intrinsic to open quantum systems. We establish the IR correspondence between the lattice symmetry algebras and those of the doubled Majorana CFT in four spin sectors, identifying chiral fermion parities emanated from the lattice translations. Finally, we develop the lattice bosonization of the dissipative chain. For even length with collective energy dephasing, combining the defect and no-defect sectors and imposing GSO projections gives rise to an Ising Lindbladian with non-invertible Kramers--Wannier symmetries descending from the anomalous strong translation and fermion parity of the Majorana chain. For odd length, constructing mutually commuting ket- and bra-sector spin operators instead yields an Ising Lindbladian with a Kramers--Wannier duality defect. Our results provide a controlled framework for extending lattice anomalies and non-invertible symmetries to open quantum systems.

articles.title: Tropical QFT and the sine-Gordon model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A tropical quantum field theory is an exactly solvable deformation limit of an ordinary QFT, governed by a non-linear partial differential equation. We use the integrable two-dimensional sine-Gordon theory as a testbench to compare the exact features of an undeformed model with its tropical counterpart. We classify scale-invariant tropical QFTs in D=2 and leverage functional renormalization group methods to demonstrate that all scale-invariant theories with periodic effective actions are infrared fixed points of flows originating from sine-Gordon Lagrangians. For the tropical sine-Gordon model, we compute the β-functions exactly, solve the renormalized theory both via a convergent expansion and numerically for all admissible couplings, and illustrate the complete renormalization group flow from the Gaussian to the IR fixed point. Finally, we study the large-order behaviour of the loop expansion and relate it to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, whose solutions we interpret as tropical instantons.
authors: Michael Borinsky, Jury Radkovski, Suriyah Rajalingam Kannagi

articles.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays emphalgebraically and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.

articles.title: When irrelevance governs: dissipation-regression scaling in open quantum criticality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The real-time dynamics of quantum phase transitions in open systems coupled to finite-temperature environments sits at the heart of contemporary condensed-matter and quantum-information science. Here, invoking a Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we uncover that, within the coherence-dominated regime of critical real-time evolution, a dissipative coupling deemed naively irrelevant determines, counterintuitively, the longest timescale that holds sway. Possessing a well-defined temporal scaling dimension, it engenders a novel dissipation-regression scaling that systematically reproduces the unusual Kibble-Zurek scaling and relaxation observed in recent numerical studies. By contrast, dissipation-dominated dynamics behaves qualitatively differently. There, furthermore, we show that the discretized and diagonalized formulations of the same open quantum Ising chain realize distinct universality classes.

articles.title: Modelling Josephson Junctions with Boundary Conditions: Towards High-Fidelity Models for Superconducting Qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Josephson junctions are the central nonlinear element of superconducting qubits, yet their standard description is reached through a chain of approximations. We propose a purely quantum-mechanical model of the junction, formulated directly in Hilbert space: a charged particle moves on a one-dimensional loop, and the junction is a point at which the wave function obeys self-adjoint boundary conditions, labelled by a coupling strength łambda, which controls the transparency of the junction, and a phase jump δ, which plays the role of the superconducting phase difference. For a loop with a single junction we solve the spectral problem and show that the ground-state momentum expectation, identified with the supercurrent, factorises exactly as łanglehatp₀ångle = I_c(δ,łambda)sinδ. For opaque junctions I_c becomes independent of δ and the first Josephson relation I=I_csinδ is recovered; for strongly attractive coupling, where the ground state is bound to the junction, the sinδ law is also recovered, but with an exponentially suppressed amplitude. For more transparent junctions, however, the model emphpredicts deviations from the pure sinδ law: I_c acquires a dependence on δ already at order łambda⁻², compatible with the higher Josephson harmonics recently found necessary to describe superconducting qubit spectra, and a fully transparent contact yields a current linear in δ. When the phase varies in time, a gauge transformation shows that the voltage drop across the junction is proportional to dotδ, so that the second Josephson relation emerges without being imposed. The boundary-condition approach thus reproduces both Josephson relations from first principles and predicts corrections to them, offering a route towards higher-fidelity models of superconducting qubits.
authors: Luis Bueno Blanco, Juan Manuel Pérez-Pardo

articles.title: Encoding Matters: A Qubit-Efficient Reformulation for Quantum Resilient Routing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Qubits are powerful computational resources because each additional qubit doubles the size of the accessible state space. This expressive power comes at a cost: adding qubits also increases circuit size, constraint overhead, and exposure to hardware noise. These limitations are especially critical for near-term quantum computers, making the number of qubits required to formulate a problem a central practical concern. In this work, we present a method for efficiently mapping logistics and routing problems onto qubits through structure-aware encoding reduction. We demonstrate the method on a benchmark problem of latency-resilient routing under dual-link failures. For this benchmark, the reduced formulation substantially lowers both the qubit count and the compiled circuit complexity while preserving the original optimization task. By running the reduced model on the same trapped-ion quantum computer as the benchmark, we obtain a 100X improvement in the success probability. This finding shows how careful problem formulation can make current quantum hardware substantially more effective for practical optimization.
authors: Emanuele G. Dalla Torre, Bat-El Friedman, Daniel Porat

articles.title: Locality-Preparation Time Tradeoffs in Dissipative Quantum Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dissipative state preparation engineers quantum many-body states as steady states of an open-system dynamics. The spatial range of the required dissipation sets both the feasibility of analog implementations and the connectivity and control complexity of digital ones. Yet how this locality quantitatively constrains preparation times remains largely unknown. Here, we establish an exact locality-preparation time relation for quadratic fermionic systems and develop a construction that optimizes the locality of the dissipative dynamics while preserving the target state. Applied to the Kitaev chain, our framework reveals sharply different locality-preparation time tradeoffs in critical and gapped regimes. At criticality, suppressing the algebraic tails of the jump operators necessarily forces the preparation time to grow algebraically with system size. By contrast, both trivial and topological gapped phases admit exponentially localized dissipation with a finite preparation time in the thermodynamic limit. Our results identify when fast dissipative preparation is compatible with local control and when criticality imposes an unavoidable dynamical cost.
authors: Philipp Westhoff, Sara Murciano, Mattia Moroder

articles.title: An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scattering of quasiparticles provides direct access to the interactions that govern strongly correlated systems. In this work, we realize the quasiparticle scattering experiment of the Fermi-Hubbard model on a digital quantum processor by colliding a doublon and a holon in the half-filled chain of 21 sites encoded on 42 qubits of the ibm_boston processor. For the first time, we measure the transmission probability of quasiparticles of the Hubbard model on quantum hardware, which agrees with the Bethe-ansatz scattering matrix without free parameters. Beyond the scattering probabilities, the collision generates entanglement by superposing the transmitted and reflected components, which we infer from the particle-number fluctuation. In sharp contrast, a control collision between two doublons shows neither the interaction dependence nor the number fluctuation, as expected for indistinguishable particles. Our work demonstrates that the ability to create quasiparticles of a chosen flavor on demand and program their motion and interactions makes a digital quantum processor a new experimental toolset for probing the entanglement structure generated by quasiparticle scattering.
authors: Chan Bin Bark, Hanbyul Kim, Yoonil Koo, SeungBeom Hong, Seik Pak, Kwang Jun Ahn, Sangmo Cheon, Youngseok Kim, Moon Jip Park

articles.title: Josephson junctions, superconducting circuits, and qubit for quantum technologies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2405.20911v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the realm of physics, a pivotal moment occurred six decades ago when Brian Josephson made a groundbreaking prediction, setting in motion a series of events that would eventually earn him the prestigious Nobel Prize eleven years later. This prediction centered around what is now known as the Josephson effect, a phenomenon with far-reaching implications. At the heart of this effect lies the Josephson junction (JJ), a device that has become a linchpin in various scientific applications. This chapter delves into the foundational principles of the Josephson effect and the remarkable properties of JJs. From their role in metrology to their application in radiation detectors, these junctions have ushered in a new era of electronics. Exploiting the unique features of superconductive devices, such as high speed, low dissipation, and dispersion, JJs find today practical implementation in the development of superconductive qubits and nanotechnology applications.
authors: Roberta Citro, Claudio Guarcello, Sergio Pagano

articles.title: Physics-inspired Generative AI models via real hardware-based noisy quantum diffusion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2505.22193v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum Diffusion Models (QDMs) are an emerging paradigm in Generative AI that aims to use quantum properties to improve the performances of their classical counterparts. However, existing algorithms are not easily scalable due to the limitations of near-term quantum devices. Following our previous work on QDMs, here we propose and implement two physics-inspired protocols. In the first, we use the formalism of quantum stochastic walks, showing that a specific interplay of quantum and classical dynamics in the forward process produces statistically more robust models generating sets of MNIST images with lower Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) than using totally classical dynamics. In the second approach, we realize an algorithm to generate images by exploiting the intrinsic noise of real IBM quantum hardware with only four qubits. Our work could be a starting point to pave the way for new scenarios for large-scale algorithms in quantum Generative AI, where quantum noise is neither mitigated nor corrected, but instead exploited as a useful resource.
authors: Marco Parigi, Stefano Martina, Francesco Aldo Venturelli, Filippo Caruso

articles.title: Quantum-like Architecture of the Social Atom: Mental Marker Coherence and the Triple-Resonance Mechanism of Cognitive Activation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Social Laser Theory (SLT) provides a rigorous quantum-like mathematical formalism for modeling collective social activation. While its macroscopic effects mimic laser physics, the fundamental driver of the lasing regime resides in the internal state dynamics of the social atom. In this paper, we propose a quantum-like architecture for the individual cognitive system, formalizing the social atom as a composite quantum system where mental markers - spanning cognitive, affective, and valence dimensions - are represented as internal degrees of freedom in a complex Hilbert space. We show that social activation is not a classical linear response but is governed by a Triple-Resonance Mechanism: the simultaneous quantum-like matching of semantic topic, energetic impact, and valence stance between the agent's internal state and the informational field. We detail how the repeated processing of quantized informational units (infons) leads to a state of cognitive population inversion. We further establish a link to Human Entanglement Theory (HET), suggesting that the emergence of coherent informational fields is rooted in the phase alignment of these internal mental markers across a population. By situating SLT within the broader framework of Social Quantum Field Theory (SQFT), this paper provides a neuro-cognitive foundation for collective phenomena such as emotional contagion and rapid narrative amplification. Our results suggest that the Social Laser is a macroscopic manifestation of quantum-like effects across the human cognitive and neuro-social architecture.
authors: Andrei Khrennikov, Christian Aspalter, Likan Zhan

articles.title: MolP2SBench: Do LLMs Really Reason from Molecular Properties to Structure?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in molecular discovery and structure elucidation, where decisions depend on physical observations. Existing evaluations primarily focus on end-to-end molecular reconstruction, where correct predictions do not necessarily indicate reliance on the supplied properties. We introduce MolP2SBench, a benchmark for molecular property-to-structure (P2S) reasoning in LLMs. Each task presents a masked molecular scaffold with given properties and asks the model to select the missing structure from plausible candidates. We shuffle or replace properties to test reliance on correct property-structure pairing and responsiveness to counterfactual property changes. A channel-wise leaderboard uses Property-Grounded Recovery (PGR), giving equal weight to source and counterfactual recovery. Evaluating seven models, we find that LLMs can use physical properties for structure prediction, but performance varies substantially across property types. Higher accuracy with a property does not necessarily imply greater responsiveness to it: a model may benefit more from ¹H NMR than from ¹³C NMR, yet be less likely to change its prediction when the ¹H data is replaced. LLM performance also need not reflect the relative difficulty of these properties for human chemists. Although UV-Vis spectra provide less direct structural information than NMR spectra, Astra achieves higher accuracy with UV-Vis data than with NMR peaks. MolP2SBench supports studying how LLMs extract and use physical-property information, revealing patterns that may differ from conventional chemical intuition and providing a foundation for more reliably property-grounded models for molecular and quantum-chemical inference. Code and dataset: https://github.com/DUAL-Xiao/MolP2SBench.
authors: Yuhang Xie, Zhiyi Shi, Zeyi Zhang, Zhisheng Qi, Yushun Dong, Yu Wang, Xiongye Xiao

articles.title: Spin Migration in the Argon Dimer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the concept of emphspin migration, i.e. time-dependent spin density, and the absolute smallest example of molecular spintronics. We illustrate the concept by emphab initio calculations of the coupled vibronic motion of the electrons and the nuclei in the argon dimer cation, in which the vibrational level spacing is similar to the spin--orbit splitting of the atomic argon cations. We find that the spin density varies on multiple time scales, given by the natural time scales of the electronic and nuclear wavepackets.
authors: Stefanos Carlström, Serguei Patchkovskii, Misha Yu Ivanov

articles.title: A Review on the Properties and Nature of Light
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The following paper is a detailed review on the properties and nature in relation to the phenomena known as 'light'. The paper tries to chronologically detail the development of theories and related experiments from the philosophical Greco-Roman and Indian schools of thought to the modern quantum theories.

articles.title: All-optical deconvolution via quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy with bright twin beams
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The resolution of spectroscopic measurements is fundamentally limited by the convolution between a system's intrinsic response and the instrument response function, creating an ill-posed inverse problem. While entangled photons can theoretically bypass these limits, low photon flux has hindered their experimental realization. Here, we propose quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy (QCCS), utilizing macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler beams) to physically circumvent this convolution limit in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering. Employing the signal beam as a broadband probe, QCCS achieves all-optical deconvolution through a correlation-enhanced sum-frequency generation channel between the convoluted anti-Stokes and idler beams. By subtracting the uncorrelated background using a 500-femtosecond temporal window, we successfully retrieve narrow Raman bands (8 cm⁻¹ and 15 cm⁻¹) completely obscured by a 75 cm⁻¹ probe bandwidth without numerical deconvolution or prior knowledge. Our results establish macroscopic quantum correlations as a robust resource for high-fidelity spectroscopy, paving the way for ultrashort-pulse-free operando studies under natural, incoherent excitation conditions.

articles.title: Judd-Ofelt analysis and coherent spectroscopy of europium-based molecular complexes for quantum information applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rare-earth-ion based molecular crystals are emerging as a promising platform for quantum information applications, combining long optical coherence times with the chemical tunability of coordination chemistry. Here we present a comprehensive optical characterisation of twelve Eu³⁺-based molecular complexes, with a focus on the coherent ⁵D₀ łongrightarrow  ⁷F₀ transition at sim580 nm. Judd-Ofelt analyses are performed across all complexes, providing insights into ligand-field environments, local point-group symmetries, and the resulting branching ratios of the coherent transition. We find that lower point-group symmetry (C₁, C₂₎ yields higher branching ratios of the ⁵D₀ łongrightarrow  ⁷F₀ transition, exceeding 1% in several complexes. Optical inhomogeneous linewidths measured at 4.2 K reveal narrow linewidths for some complexes of below ten GHz, indicative of a highly ordered crystalline environment. Optical coherence measurements of one of the complexes, 5-Eu, yields an optical coherence time of T₂opt = 2.3~μs at 4.2 K, comparable to the best-performing molecular systems reported to date. Systematic characterisation and quantitative comparison will be key to find structure-property relations guiding rational design of optimised complexes for quantum information applications.
authors: Nicholas Lester Jobbitt, Sascha Weis, Timo Schweizer, Vishnu Unni Chorakkunnath, Evgenij Vasilenko, Tobias Haas, Barbora Brachnakova, Senthil Kumar Kuppusamy, Hartmut Schubert, Mario Ruben, Michael Seitz, David Hunger

articles.title: Topological Origin of Neutrino Mass and Mixing: From the SU(3)₃ Modular Tensor Category to the PMNS Matrix
articles.abstract: We propose a topological origin for neutrino masses and mixing: neutrinos are boundary topological flows of a string-net condensed phase, and their mass matrix is determined by boundary dynamics that inherits the hierarchical parameters of the bulk (:SUłeft(3i̊ght)₃øtimes:SUłeft(2i̊ght)₂) modular tensor category. Using the conformal-weight spacing (:Δ:ℎ=1/3) and the topological temperature (:β:=π:²/14) of this category, we read the Cabibbo angle (:łambda:=e⁻¹⁴/łeft⁽³π:ⁱ̊ght⁾approx:0.225), without any free parameters, in agreement with the experimental value to within 0.04%. On this basis, we propose a mass matrix whose coefficients are mapped directly to the S-matrix elements of the (:SUłeft(3i̊ght)₃) modular tensor category, with diagonalization yielding mixing angles close to the experimental values. Further introducing the CP phase (:ϵ:=łambda:²) arising from the quadratic effect of topological suppression, and reading the charged-lepton mixing parameters (α, β, γ) from the quantum-dimension ratios and conformal weights of the category, we can simultaneously fit the four observables of NuFIT 6.0. The parameters (:α:=-3łambda:/5), (:β:=-łambda:²/2), and (:γ:=2łambda:/3) are read from (:d₈/(d₈+d₃)=3/5), (:ℎ₈=1/2), and (:ℎ₁₅=2/3) respectively. The CP phase (:η:=π:/10:)has a proposed reading mechanism (:η:=π:/Nₛᵢₘₚₗₑ), pending confirmation; we have systematically excluded several possible algebraic origins (T-matrix phases, R-matrix phases, topological entropy change) and leave its full derivation as an open problem.

articles.title: Designing dielectrics for microchip capacitors
articles.abstract: Nature Electronics, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41928-026-01726-w The miniaturization of capacitors for advanced electronics requires dielectrics that balance high permittivity, low loss and stable temperature response. Now, a hierarchical machine learning approach is developed for the design of such materials. The resulting Bi–Ge co-substituted tungsten bronze ceramic exhibits balanced dielectric properties, enabling a substantial volume reduction of chip capacitors.

articles.title: Structural and energetic signatures of SO 2 and CH 4 incorporation in imidazolium-based ionic liquids
articles.abstract: A systematic molecular dynamics study of sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) incorporation in 24 imidazolium-based ionic liquids is presented, spanning different anion families and cation alkyl chain lengths. The two gases represent limiting cases of solvation behavior in ionic liquids: SO 2 exhibits strong electrostatic interactions and Lewis amphoteric character, whereas CH 4 is governed primarily by weak London dispersion forces. Radial distribution functions, coordination numbers, cluster-size distributions, and interaction energies were analyzed to elucidate the molecular organization of the mixtures. The results show that neither SO 2 nor CH 4 substantially disrupts the polar network of the ionic liquids. SO 2 partitions between the polar and nonpolar regions of the ionic liquid, leading to reduced self-association and more gas distributions, whereas CH 4 preferentially occupies alkyl-rich regions and exhibits only weak self-association with minimal dependence on cation chain length. Interaction energy decomposition highlights the dominant role of electrostatics in SO 2 solvation and the free volume-driven, weakly interacting nature of CH 4 incorporation. These findings provide a molecular-level framework for rationalizing incorporation trends and for guiding the design of ionic liquids for gas separation, highlighting how polarity, anion charge distribution, and cation alkyl chain length can be tuned to enhance specific SO 2 stabilization while controlling nonspecific CH 4 accommodation in alkyl-rich free-volume domains.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Symmetry-driven correlation patterns in one-dimensional periodic fermionic systems: Closed-form expressions and exact selection rules for correlation functions, entanglement entropies, and mutual information
articles.abstract: We present an analytical study of the spatial structure of correlations in periodic fermionic systems at the single Slater determinant level, focusing on the cyclic case. Exploiting cyclic symmetry, the transformation from localized orbitals to molecular orbitals is simultaneously a discrete Fourier transform, a Vandermonde matrix on the roots of unity, a complex Hadamard matrix, and the character table of the cyclic group C m . Within this framework, the spatial structure of correlations is fully determined by the occupied irreducible representations (Fourier modes), independently of the specific Hamiltonian generating them. In particular, the fermionic two-point correlator is expressed as a truncated Fourier sum over the occupied orbitals, leading to exact analytical expressions for symmetric occupation patterns of Fourier modes ( ℓ and − ℓ pairs), corresponding in quantum chemistry to aromatic fillings, i.e., fillings satisfying Hückel’s 4 n + 2 rule. For the half filling case, we derive exact spatial selection rules. In particular, the two-point correlator vanishes identically for all even distances along the ring. This property propagates to reduced density matrices and implies a complete absence of mutual information between the corresponding orbitals. These results reveal that, despite the global delocalization of molecular orbitals, the correlation structure in cyclic systems is highly non-uniform and governed by symmetry-induced interference. Although formulated in terms of cyclic lattice systems, the present results extend straightforwardly to one-dimensional fermionic chains with periodic conditions, reflecting the underlying translational symmetry of the problem. The framework, therefore, provides a Hamiltonian-independent and universal reference for understanding correlation patterns in one-dimensional periodic fermionic systems.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Inclusion of three-body corrections in the relativistic equation-of-motion coupled cluster method: Application to electron detachment
articles.abstract: We present the formulation and implementation of a triples-correction scheme for relativistic equation-of-motion coupled-cluster calculations of ionization potentials. Both full and partial triples-correction schemes are implemented using the exact two-component atomic mean-field (X2CAMF) Hamiltonian in combination with Cholesky decomposition (CD) of two-electron integrals and a frozen natural spinor (FNS) truncation scheme to reduce computational cost. Benchmark calculations on halide anions, noble-gas atoms, hydrogen halides, and dihalogen molecules demonstrate the importance of triple excitations for the quantitative prediction of ionization potentials. The CCSD(T)(a)* scheme achieves a mean absolute error of ∼0.01 eV relative to full CCSDT for halide anions and noble-gas atoms and ∼0.08 eV relative to the experiment for dihalogen molecules. The X2CAMF approximation reproduces four-component Dirac–Coulomb results with negligible deviations, while the CD-FNS strategy substantially reduces the computational cost. The resulting partial triples-correction scheme scales as O(n7) with storage comparable to CCSD, providing an accurate and practical approach for relativistic ionization-energy calculations in heavy-element systems.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Gate-controlled optical bistability via tunable self-action feedback in a semiconductor quantum dot–graphene nanodisk hybrid
articles.abstract: We theoretically examine how electrostatic gating can tune the steady-state response of a semiconductor quantum dot (SQD)–graphene nanodisk hybrid between monostable and bistable regimes. The model combines the optical Bloch dynamics of a driven two-level SQD with a gate-dependent polarizability of the graphene nanodisk. Through this polarizability, the gate voltage controls the SQD self-action, represented by the complex feedback parameter G ( V g ) = G R ( V g ) + iG I ( V g ). The bistable response results from saturation of the SQD transition combined with graphene-mediated feedback. As V g is varied, G ( V g ) traces a trajectory in the complex feedback plane relative to the saddle-node boundary. Bistability occurs only along the part of this trajectory for which the steady-state input–output relation has two physical turning points. Within this segment, adiabatic sweeps of gate voltage or input intensity remain on a stable branch until a turning point is reached, giving a hysteresis loop. The stability of these branches is verified from the local Jacobian eigenvalues. The same turning-point criterion locates the gate–detuning domain for fixed-input branch switching and identifies the coupling–dephasing window in which the feedback trajectory can reach the bistable domain. These results identify gate-controlled complex self-action as the mechanism governing the opening and closing of the bistability window and the associated branch switching in the SQD–graphene nanodisk hybrid.

articles.title: Nonclassical condensation pathways revealed by the multivariable theory of nucleation
articles.abstract: Classical nucleation theory (CNT) provides a simple conceptual framework for nucleation but often fails to quantitatively reproduce experimental and numerical observations. In this work, we extend the theory by explicitly incorporating the multidimensional nature of nucleation and the coupled roles of kinetics and thermodynamics. Specifically, we treat the cluster density as an independent variable, within both sharp-interface and diffuse-interface descriptions. The kinetics are governed by dynamical density functional theory. Applied to liquid condensation in the Lennard-Jones system, our self-consistent, parameter-free two-variable (size–density) and three-variable (size–interface width–density) models reveal nonclassical nucleation mechanisms. At low supersaturation, both models recover the classical picture, in which clusters nucleate and grow at the equilibrium liquid density. As supersaturation increases, nonclassical behavior emerges: the critical cluster density decreases, and the nucleation pathway involves concomitant evolution in cluster size, density, and within the diffuse-interface description, interfacial width. Our diffuse-interface model reveals a rapid increase in interfacial diffuseness at high supersaturation. Near the spinodal limit, both models predict the critical cluster with diverging sizes, densities approaching that of the metastable initial phase, and vanishing work of formation, which provides a smooth connection between nucleation and spinodal decomposition. Comparison with molecular dynamics simulations demonstrates that both models substantially outperform CNT. However, the weak nonmonotonic dependence of the critical cluster density observed at very low supersaturation is captured only by diffuse-interface models. Overall, our findings indicate that CNT should be applied only in the low-supersaturation regime, and our work provides a robust foundation for its refinement beyond this limit.

articles.title: High-performance parallel implementation of spin-free high-order coupled-cluster theories
articles.abstract: High-order coupled-cluster theories with iterative triples (CCSDT), perturbative quadruples [CCSDT(Q)], and iterative quadruples (CCSDTQ) provide benchmark-quality correlation energies, but their steep computational scalings, O ( N 8 ), O ( N 9 ), and O ( N 10 ), together with the large memory requirements of high-order amplitude tensors, have historically limited their application to small molecules. In this work, we develop efficient open-source implementations of spin-restricted CCSDT (RCCSDT), RCCSDT(Q), and RCCSDTQ within the pyscf package and a Message Passing Interface (MPI)-based extension, distributed-cc . The shared-memory implementation combines compact triangular storage of the highest-order amplitude tensors with the multithreaded tensor contraction backend pytblis , enabling efficient use of modern many-core central processing unit (CPU) architectures. This design delivers near-ideal thread scaling up to 90 cores and achieves wall times shorter than or comparable to existing single-node implementations for representative benchmark molecules. We further extend RCCSDT, RCCSDT(Q), and RCCSDTQ to distributed-memory architectures using MPI-based algorithms. By distributing compact high-order amplitudes across MPI ranks and overlapping communication with computation through nonblocking data transfers, the distributed implementation achieves near-ideal strong scaling on up to 32 nodes, corresponding to ∼3000 CPU cores. These developments substantially extend the practical reach of canonical high-order coupled-cluster theory, enabling CCSDT and CCSDT(Q) calculations on systems with ∼100 correlated electrons in 450 orbitals and CCSDTQ calculations on systems with ∼50 correlated electrons in 115 orbitals. Applications to π -stacked noncovalent dimers, the CO dissociation energy of Cr(CO) 6 , and the Cope rearrangement of semibullvalene demonstrate that canonical high-order coupled-cluster benchmarks are now feasible for chemically realistic molecular systems.

articles.title: Ultraviolet laser pulses engineer diamond defects selectively, leaving quantum qubits intact
articles.abstract: When we think about a diamond, we often think about a material whose value comes from its perfection. In my research, however, I am interested in something almost opposite: the tiny imperfections inside diamonds. These atomic-scale defects can give diamonds new optical and electronic properties, and some of them can serve as quantum systems. The challenge is learning how to control these defects without disturbing the others.

articles.title: New stability rules distinguish quantum phases of matter that an older method wrongly groups together
articles.abstract: Most of us recognize basic phases of matter and their properties: solids maintain their shape, liquids flow freely with constant volume, and gases expand to fill their container. Quantum phases, on the other hand, are much harder to categorize, overturning traditional notions of what a phase even is and forcing physicists to rethink their definitions.

articles.title: Three quantum-inspired cores leave opposite fingerprints on the ringing of black holes
articles.abstract: Every black hole hides a question at its center. Einstein's theory predicts that whatever falls in is crushed into a singularity, a point of infinite density where the theory itself breaks down. Most physicists expect quantum gravity to replace that point with something finite. But the center lies hidden behind the horizon. How could we ever learn what is there?

articles.title: Explainable graph-based meta-reinforcement learning for cognitive UAV swarms under partial observability and adaptive jamming
articles.abstract: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning frameworks for cognitiveunmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly bundle graph coordination,meta-learning and explainability, yet it is rarely shown when that machineryactually helps. We present XM-MADRL, an explainable meta-learning graphframework for UAV swarms in contested electromagnetic environments, togetherwith a controlled study that isolates when its components pay off. Under fullobservability against a predictable jammer, coordination and meta-adaptationgive no measurable benefit: the framework merely ties a vanilla proximal policyoptimisation (PPO) baseline. Under partial observability against an adaptive,reactive jammer, the same framework is better on every spectrum metric, raisingpacket delivery ratio sixfold (16.8% versus 2.5%; Cohen's d of 4.45),anti-jamming from approximately 0% to 11.1%, and meansignal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio from ((-3.7)) to ((-1.3)) dB, allsignificant after Holm--Bonferroni correction (adjusted P below0.0001) over ten seeds. A recurrent control that adds memory but notcommunication fails as badly as PPO, and a component ablation shows the gain isnot due to graph message passing. Meta-learning improves zero-shotgeneralisation to unseen jammers (packet delivery 32.0% versus 4.2%).Coordination and meta-adaptation are conditional capabilities, not universalimprovements.

articles.title: Bio-based benzoxazine electrically conductive adhesives for sustainable and epoxy-free hybrid printed electronics
articles.abstract: Electrically conductive adhesives (ECAs) are critical for the assembly of surface-mounted devices in printed and hybrid electronics; however, conventional epoxy-based systems are associated with toxicity and limited working life. In this work, we present a benzoxazine-based anisotropic conductive adhesive (ACA) derived from a bio-based diphenolic acid benzoxazine (DPA-Bz) copolymerized with 1,12-diaminododecane (DIADO), combined with environmentally preferable metallic fillers. The developed system enables reduced curing temperatures (~ 150°C) compared to conventional benzoxazines, improving compatibility with temperature-sensitive substrates. From an electrical standpoint, the optimized Cu-based ACA exhibits low contact resistance and clear anisotropic conductivity with electrical performance comparable to a commercial epoxy-based adhesive. Furthermore, the ACA maintains stable electrical behavior under accelerated aging (85°C / 85% RH) and thermal shock testing, indicating robust reliability under environmental stress. Finally, life cycle assessment reveals a reduced global warming potential (5.48 kg CO₂/kg) compared to a reference Ni-based adhesive (6.27 kg CO₂/kg), with further reduction potential through solvent-free formulations and increased recycled copper content. The presented benzoxazine-based ACA achieves comparable electrical and mechanical performance to commercial systems while delivering improved environmental performance and reduced toxicity, highlighting its potential as a sustainable alternative for next-generation electronic assembly and opening the path towards greener electronics.

articles.title: Unsteady MHD flow of Heat generating / absorbing fluid through porous plate with variable temperature and concentration in a slip flow regime
articles.abstract: The present study investigates the unsteady magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) free convective heat and mass transfer flow via an infinite vertical porous plate immersed in a porous material under slip flow circumstances of a viscous, incompressible, electrically conducting fluid. The plate is subjected to a consistent transverse magnetic field. The perturbation approach provides an analytical solution to the non-dimensional governing equations. Physical parameters that affect velocity, temperature, and concentration distributions are graphically analyzed and thoroughly discussed. These parameters include thermal Grashof number, modified Grashof number, magnetic parameter, permeability parameter, radiation parameter, heat generation/absorption, Prandtl number, Schmidt number, chemical reaction parameter, as well as Soret number. According to the findings, the velocity profile rises as the buoyancy and permeability parameters increase, while it falls with the magnetic parameter and slip effects due to the resistive Lorentz force. Thermal radiation and heat source significantly enhance the temperature distribution and thermal boundary layer thickness, while higher Prandtl number reduces the temperature field because of lower thermal diffusivity. The concentration profile decreases with increasing Schmidt number and chemical reaction parameter, whereas it increases with increasing Soret number due to enhanced thermal diffusion effects. The effects of the governing parameters on engineering quantities such as skin friction coefficient, Nusselt number, and Sherwood number are also discussed. The present investigation provides valuable insight into radiative MHD transport phenomena through porous media and has potential applications in geothermal engineering, chemical reactors, nuclear reactor cooling systems, petroleum engineering, energy transport systems, and thermal insulation technologies.

articles.title: Assessing Climate Change Impacts on Wetland Vegetation and Water Resources through Rainfall-Driven Ecohydrological Indices: Satellite-based evidence from the Kabartal Wetland Region, Bihar
articles.abstract: Wetlands are dynamic socio-ecological systems whose persistence and ecological functioning are strongly regulated by hydroclimatic variability. Changes in precipitation, surface-water availability, vegetation dynamics, and atmospheric evaporative demand can alter wetland hydrology, ecosystem productivity, and resilience, particularly under increasing climatic and anthropogenic pressures. This study evaluates the long-term ecohydrological transformation of the Kabartal Wetland Region (KWR) sBihar, India, by integrating climatic, hydrological, evapotranspiration, and satellite-derived ecological indicators. Long-term rainfall variability and trends were assessed for 1901–2024 using the Seasonality Index (SI), Rainfall Anomaly Index (RAI), 90% dependable rainfall, Modified Mann–Kendall (MMK) test, and Sen’s slope, while actual evapotranspiration (ET) and potential evapotranspiration (PET) were analysed for 2002–2024. Landsat-derived Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) were used to quantify changes in surface-water extent and vegetation cover during pre- and post-monsoon periods between 1989 and 2024. The results reveal a substantial contraction of wetland surface-water extent, declining from 31 to 14 km² (54.83%) during pre-monsoon and from 44 to 19 km² (56.81%) during post-monsoon between 1989 and 2024. Rainfall exhibited strong seasonality, with SI values predominantly ranging from 0.8 to 1.4, indicating prolonged dry periods and concentration of precipitation within a short monsoonal window. RAI analysis indicates a progressive shift from predominantly wet conditions towards more frequent negative rainfall anomalies, particularly after 2000. Annual rainfall declined significantly across Begusarai, Samastipur, and Khagaria, with Sen’s slopes of − 1.54, − 1.72, and − 2.34 mm yr⁻¹, respectively, while monsoonal rainfall also exhibited significant decreasing trends. Historical mean annual rainfall of approximately 1,131, 1,170, and 1,154 mm in the three districts is projected to decline to about 1,025, 1,054, and 985 mm by 2044, respectively. Despite the region's generally humid, water-surplus character, the ET–PET relationship shows pronounced seasonal moisture limitation, with annual PET ranging from approximately 1,950–2,450 mm compared with ET of only 350–650 mm. Rainfall was positively correlated with ET (r = 0.5) and latent heat flux (r = 0.5) but negatively correlated with PET (r = − 0.5), demonstrating the sensitivity of ecosystem water use to precipitation availability and atmospheric demand. The convergence of declining rainfall, increasing rainfall variability, reduced surface-water extent, vegetation degradation, and persistent ET–PET disequilibrium indicates that KWR is undergoing a progressive transition from a predominantly water-surplus wetland system towards increasing seasonal hydro ecological stress. These findings highlight the need to restore river–wetland connectivity, protect wetland catchments and vegetation, regulate water extraction and land-use conversion, enhance monsoon-water retention, and strengthen community-based and climate-resilient wetland governance. Such integrated interventions are essential to maintain wetland ecological integrity, strengthen regional water security, and advance Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6) on sustainable water management.

articles.title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
articles.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78376-1 Superconducting diodes can provide nonreciprocal elements for superconducting and quantum circuits, but the role of diode efficiency in quantum-device performance remains unclear. Here, the authors demonstrate an enhanced superconducting diode effect in twisted NbSe2 and show that even a moderate degree of nonreciprocity is sufficient to stabilize anharmonic qubit circuits.

articles.title: Hybrid quantum computer observes foundational quantum effect in a new setting
articles.abstract: Physicists in the Department of Physics at the University of Oxford have used a hybrid quantum computer, made up of qubits and quantum oscillators, to observe the Aharonov–Bohm effect in a quantum simulation. The effect is a quantum phenomenon in which a particle can acquire a measurable phase by traveling around a magnetic flux, even though it never passes through a region where a magnetic field is present.

articles.title: Quantum chip holds multiple photons at once, opening path to scalable memory
articles.abstract: For highly fragile quantum information systems, the ability to store quantum information is vital—but also challenging. Quantum information is transported in particles of light called photons, which often must be temporarily paused (or "stored") while other, slower quantum operations catch up. This storage must be performed on microchips as small as 1 centimeter (0.4 inches)—a distance covered by light in a few trillionths of a second. Storing photons for a microsecond would represent a massive leap forward for the capabilities of quantum chips.

articles.title: Layered semiconductor unlocks magnetic control of light emitted by quantum condensates
articles.abstract: Quantum technologies are considered key technologies of the future. However, research in this field requires not only scientific expertise but sometimes also highly specialized laboratory conditions. Bose–Einstein condensates are a remarkable example, in which atoms move in lockstep, making quantum-mechanical effects visible not only at the level of individual atoms but also on a macroscopic scale. The first Bose–Einstein condensates were observed in ultracold atomic gases at temperatures close to absolute zero. The cooling required to achieve this was technically demanding, costly and restricted to specialized laboratories.

articles.title: Liquid-crystal-like magnetism explains puzzling properties in a rare-earth compound
articles.abstract: In some materials, physical properties don't emerge from their individual particles, but from the collective behavior of their quantum spins. Now, researchers led by Pengcheng Dai at Rice University in the U.S. have discovered that in one compound containing the rare-earth element ytterbium, these spins can behave much like the molecules in a liquid crystal: favoring a certain direction without lining up to create magnetism on larger scales.

articles.title: Development of yeast-based integrated bioprocess for xylitol and ethanol production from xylan-rich lignocellulosic materials
articles.abstract: Xylan-rich agricultural residues can serve as cheap and abundant raw materials for biorefinery processes, however development of efficient and sustainable processes for their bioconversion into high-value products is still a major challenge. Integrated bioprocess, combining enzyme production, substrate hydrolysis and product formation into a single process by using a single microorganism, represents a promising strategy for overcoming this issue. In this study, selected nonconventional wild-type yeast strains were screened for their ability to produce extracellular xylanases and xylitol, aiming to identify multifunctional biocatalysts that are suitable for an integrated bioprocess of xylan-rich lignocellulosic residues. Among the investigated strains, Sugiyamaella novakii NCAIM Y.00987 was found to be suitable for xylan-based integrated bioprocess applications due to its revealed capability of producing extracellular xylanases and xylitol. Process parameters affecting xylanases production and xylitol fermentation were determined and optimised, and the scalability of the optimised conditions was verified in batch processes performed in 500-mL bench-top bioreactor. The strain maintained stable enzyme production and product formation under the controlled cultivation conditions in bench-top bioreactor, forecasting its applicability in an industrial bioprocess. Application of Su. novakii in integrated bioprocess for xylitol and ethanol was subsequently assessed using xylan and barley husk as model and real lignocellulosic substrates, respectively. Although a two-stage bioprocess was proposed to provide optimal conditions for both xylanases and xylitol productions, enzyme and product synthesis was simultaneously obtained, indicating the possibility of using the strain as a microorganism for consolidated bioprocessing of lignocellulosic materials. The developed bioprocess resulted in direct substrate conversions, producing 1.1 g/L xylitol and 1.8 g/L ethanol after 48 h on xylan, while 0.12 g/L xylitol was obtained from barley husk, without external enzyme supplementation. In addition, Candida allociferrii NCAIM Y.02114 was confirmed experimentally for the first time, identifying it as an industrially relevant strain. The findings contribute to advancing sustainable biomass processing and support the implementation of circular bioeconomy strategies through the direct conversion of agricultural by-products into value-added biochemicals. Overall, this study highlights the potential of nonconventional yeasts as multifunctional platforms for the integrated valorisation of hemicellulose-rich residues and provides a basis for the development of lignocellulose-based consolidated bioprocesses. The findings contribute to advancing sustainable biomass processing and support the implementation of circular bioeconomy strategies through the direct conversion of agricultural by-products into value-added biochemicals.

articles.title: Long-Term Extrapolation of Data-Driven Models for Multibody Dynamics: A Unified Evaluation Framework and Comparative Investigation
articles.abstract: Although numerous data-driven models have recently been developed for multibody dynamics (MBD), their ability to perform reliable long-term extrapolation remains insufficiently understood. Existing studies often adopt different prediction horizons, benchmark problems, and evaluation criteria, making direct comparisons between learning approaches difficult and obscuring their respective strengths and limitations.To address this issue, this paper presents a literature-informed comparative investigation and controlled numerical study of representative data-driven models for long-term extrapolation in MBD. A unified framework is first established by defining long-term extrapolation, identifying the principal mechanisms responsible for recursive error accumulation, classifying representative learning approaches according to their underlying learning strategies, and introducing complementary evaluation perspectives and metrics for long-term prediction.Based on this framework, five representative approaches, multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), long short-term memory networks (LSTMs), physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), neural ordinary differential equations (Neural ODEs), and sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy), are systematically evaluated under four complementary benchmark scenarios, including increasing system complexity, increasing chaos, high-frequency dynamics, and robustness to measurement noise. The numerical results demonstrate that long-term extrapolation performance depends strongly on both the underlying learning strategy and the characteristics of the target dynamical system. The results reveal distinct strengths and limitations among the representative learning strategies, with SINDy consistently exhibiting the most robust long-term extrapolation performance and LSTM generally providing the second-best performance.The proposed unified evaluation framework and controlled benchmark study provide practical guidelines for selecting appropriate data-driven models for long-term prediction in MBD and establish a consistent reference framework for future comparative studies.

articles.title: Excitation-Aware On-Track System Identification at Full Scale
articles.abstract: On-track system identification learns tire models from ordinary racing laps instead of dedicated manoeuvres. We study one such residual-learning pipeline at full vehicle scale, inside a simulator that publishes per-wheel forces as ground truth. Transplanted unchanged from a 1:10 platform, it converges on a tire with less than half the vehicle’s grip ceiling and most Pacejka coefficients resting on their bounds. The cause is a loss of excitation created by the pipeline’s own virtual-data step: the friction the synthetic rollout can demand is a property of the rollout configuration and not of the tire, as a grid on a known tire con-firms. Two further defects share that source. The objective the coefficients are fitted against depends on them only through one product, so the peak factor is not recoverable from the rollout at any excitation, and the loop that feeds each fit its own previous answer is not a contraction. We correct all three, and gate the controller interface on derived physical quantities rather than on coefficient bounds. On a static surface 33% below the one the tire prior was measured on,axle cornering stiffness is recovered to within 3.2% and the peak factor to 11%. On a surface losing half its grip under the moving vehicle, the corrected pipeline tracks the decay rate to 7% and completes three timed laps at unchanged lateral tracking error for 18% of lap time, where the inherited configuration holds a grip ceiling nearly four times the plant’s and leaves the track.

articles.title: I ∝ √V characteristic resulting from a Fermi pinning region in polysilicon nanowire Schottky-contacted resistors
articles.abstract: Herein, we present an analytical formulation for the current-voltage characteristic of an undoped polycrystalline silicon nanowire Schottky-contacted resistor. This type of nanowire is characterised by high defect density, which is modelled using a double-exponential density of states (DOS) describing both band-tail states and deep states within the bandgap for acceptor and donor traps. At equilibrium, the potential profile reveals an electrostatic screening effect: perturbation induced by the contact is attenuated by the trapped charge over a characteristic screening length, beyond which the potential stabilises to a typical value determined by the DOS parameters. Out of equilibrium, a Fermi pinning region forms near the metal/polycrystalline silicon nanowire interface, which is distinct from depletion regions observed in classical Schottky junctions. This Fermi pinning region exhibits a quasi-frozen trap occupancy and a free-hole concentration around the intrinsic concentration. Beyond this region, quasi-neutrality is restored, with a residual electric field deep in the nanowire ensuring the drift of free holes. The model shows that this field, proportional to the square root of the voltage, is an attenuated replica of the field at the metal/polycrystalline silicon nanowire interface transmitted through the Fermi pinning region and screening region into the core of the nanowire. Based on the drift-diffusion equation, the current-voltage characteristic exhibits a distinctive dependence of the form (:Ipropto:sqrtV). The developed analytical expressions are quantitatively supported by numerical simulations.

articles.title: Multi-class quantum k-nearest-neighbour classification in a single quantum circuit
articles.abstract: In this paper we present a novel quantum k-nearest-neighbour circuit. The k-nearest-neighbour problem asks for the K closest stored points to a query among all data; quantum interference allows every stored point of every class to be compared in a single execution, a substantial computational gain. Quantum k-nearest-neighbour designs to date have rested on assumed primitives—quantum random-access memory, oracle access, amplitude-amplified search—which remain hypothetical and serve mainly to set limits on what the algorithms could achieve, or they restrict the distance metric or the number of classes. Our design uses none of these: no quantum random-access memory, no oracle, no metric restriction, no binary-class limit, and every operation is a practically implementable gate. Training members of each class are loaded into a dedicated register in superposition, a butterfly network of controlled-SWAP stages routes all classes to a common comparison position, and the class and member identity of every neighbour is read directly from the measurement statistics. The architecture rests on closed-form expressions for the post-selected probabilities and a geometric analysis showing that inverse stereographic projection carries the Euclidean nearest-neighbour ranking onto state fidelity with a sharp distortion bound. In simulation the circuit reproduces its intended decision rule exactly, and its accuracy matches classical k-nearest neighbours across a controlled benchmark at a realistic measurement budget. Every loading and sampling cost is stated in full—costs that most prior work hides by assuming quantum random-access memory.

articles.title: Analytical Construction of the CKM Matrix Using a Single Electroweak Constant
articles.abstract: We present closed analytical expressions for all nine elements of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) quark mixing matrix within the (SU(2)_LøtimesSU(2)_RøtimesU(1)B₋L) model, based on a (emphmixing-equilibrium condition) for a quark flavour state, postulated as beginequation*     α_q (1 - α_q) = C_q , łambda², endequation* where (0 < α_q < 1 - α_q) represents the equilibrium mixing-weight of the sector, (łambda² = 1/(2π²⁾) is the inverse Haar volume measure of (SU(2)_L), and (C_q = 1 + (B-L)_q/2) is the quark coupling factor, with ((B - L)_q) denoting the gauge charge. We define (łambda) as the fermion mixing constant, which numerically matches the empirical Cabibbo scale ((łambda approx sinθ_C)) and serves as the baseline mixing scale for both the quark and lepton sectors. We have constructed the CKM matrix as the Hadamard product of the isospin activity matrix G and the inter-generational suppression matrix S, followed by exact row unitarization. The matrix elements are expressed directly in terms of łambda and α_q, with exact analytical forms provided for every component of G and S. The proposed closed-form formulation of the CKM matrix achieves sub-sigma agreement with 2024 Particle Data Group (PDG) world averages (mean absolute pull of 0.22,σ, maximum pull of 0.59,σ at ěrt{}Vᵤběrt{}), offering clear advantages over the standard Wolfenstein expansion.   The mixing scale łambda_W = łambda and the Wolfenstein amplitude A approx 0.819 (0.58,σ from PDG), alongside the CKM unitarity triangle coordinates barh̊o approx 0.143 and barη approx 0.379 derived from the equilibrium retention-weight 1 - α_q = sinδ₁₃, achieve agreement with global fits within 0.02,σ (for the unitarity apex). Consequently, the phase angle γ = arcsin(1 - α_q) approx 69.54ⁱ̧rc uniquely determines the Jarlskog invariant as Jₘ̊ CP^q approx 3.22 × 10⁻⁵, matching the PDG global fit to within 0.82,σ. The same constant łambda underpins the closed-form formulation of the PMNS lepton mixing matrix, where the lepton-sector coupling factor Cₑₗₗ = 1/2 yields the corresponding lepton parameter αₑₗₗ via αₑₗₗ₍₁₋αₑₗₗ₎ = Cₑₗₗłambda², demonstrating that łambda = 1/(πsqrt2) is the single universal invariant for quarks as well as leptons. Regardless of the broader interpretation of electroweak symmetry breaking, the proposed analytical approach provides closed-form, parameter-free expressions for CKM observables, with potential insight into flavour-mixing behaviour.

articles.title: GIS and Statistical Modelling for Open Cast Mining Surface Risk Assessment and Sustainable Mine Safety and Environmental Management
articles.abstract: Open-cast mining has become the dominant method of coal extraction in many developing countries because of its high productivity and economic efficiency. However, extensive surface excavation has resulted in severe environmental degradation, landscape alteration, slope instability, land subsidence, groundwater contamination, dust pollution, and threats to nearby communities. Conventional mine safety assessments are generally based on field observations and engineering investigations, which often fail to capture the spatial variability of environmental risks over large mining regions. This study proposes an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS) and statistical modelling framework for assessing surface risks associated with open-cast mining operations. The framework combines remote sensing datasets, Digital Elevation Models (DEM), land use and land cover information, vegetation indices, drainage characteristics, transportation networks, settlement distribution, and mine boundary information using a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) approach based on the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). A Surface Risk Index (SRI) is generated through weighted overlay analysis and validated using regression and correlation techniques. The resulting risk zonation map classifies mining areas into very low, low, moderate, high, and very high risk categories. The study demonstrates that slope, vegetation degradation, proximity to mine pits, drainage density, and settlement concentration are significant determinants of mining-related surface risk. The proposed framework provides a scientifically robust and transferable methodology for sustainable mine planning, environmental monitoring, disaster prevention, and mine closure management.

articles.title: Pformer: a plug-and-play periodicity-aware embedding for crystal property prediction
articles.abstract: Predicting macroscopic properties of crystalline materials from atomic structure remains a central challenge in computational materials science. We introduce Pformer, a modular crystal representation framework built around a Fourier-inspired source encoder. The source model is trained by supervised scalar-property regression from atom attributes and Cartesian coordinates; its Fourier analysis network (FAN) transformation applies sine, cosine, and GELU branches to learned latent projections before Transformer encoding. After source training, Pformer extracts the learned atom-embedding weight matrix, adapts its width when required, and uses it to initialize message-passing graph neural networks and transformer-based crystal encoders for downstream property prediction. We denote each initialized downstream variant as FAN-Backbone (e.g. FAN-PotNet); here FAN identifies the source-encoder component that produced the transferred weights, whereas Pformer denotes the complete transfer framework. On the Materials Project benchmark, FAN-PotNet reduces the bandgap mean absolute error (MAE) from 0.204 to 0.149 eV, and FAN-GATGNN lowers the shear modulus MAE from 0.075 to 0.022 log(GPa). On JARVIS-DFT, FAN-PotNet decreases the total energy MAE from 0.032 to 0.017 eV atom , and FAN-ComFormer improves the MAE from 0.048 to 0.045 eV. These benchmark comparisons show lower MAE for selected backbone–property combinations and ties for others, indicating that the effect of FAN-derived initialization depends on the downstream architecture and target property.

articles.title: Two-stage projection physics-informed neural networks for preserving conservation laws
articles.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can attain small residuals for partial differential equations while drifting from global invariants. We separate residual-based training from invariant enforcement: a standard PINN is trained first, and its output is then projected onto a selected invariant manifold at inference. The correction requires neither retraining nor a conservation penalty in the training objective. We derive explicit projection maps for the Korteweg–de Vries and nonlinear Schrödinger equations and for a mean-conserving Kuramoto–Sivashinsky benchmark. Spatial field evaluation and quadrature are accelerated on a graphics processing unit, while one scalar update is computed for each evaluation time. Across these three one-dimensional benchmarks, projection reduces the selected-invariant violation by a factor of approximately – relative to the unprojected PINN, while prediction errors against the supplied numerical comparison trajectories change little. These results establish a benchmark-level post-processing correction over a unit time horizon; they do not establish long-horizon stability or generality beyond equations with a tractable scalar invariant.

articles.title: Projected Hessian learning: fast curvature supervision for accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: The Hessian matrix of second derivatives contains substantially richer information about the local geometry of the potential energy surface than energies and forces alone. Although incorporating full Hessians into machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) training can significantly improve accuracy and robustness, the quadratic computational and memory cost of explicitly constructing and storing Hessian matrices has limited its practical use. Here, we introduce Projected Hessian Learning (PHL), a scalable second-order training framework that incorporates curvature information using only Hessian–vector products (HVPs). By avoiding explicit Hessian construction and instead projecting curvature along stochastic probe directions, PHL reduces the cost of second-derivative supervision to near force-level complexity. The resulting dense-probe trace estimator is unbiased and exhibits favorable scaling with system size, enabling curvature-informed training without quadratic memory growth. We evaluated various training approaches on a chemically diverse dataset of reactants, products, transition states, intrinsic reaction coordinates, and normal-mode sampled geometries generated at the theoretical level B97XD/6-31G(d). Four training schemes are considered: energy-force training (E-F), two HVP-based approaches (E-F-HVP with one-hot or dense Gaussian vectors) and energy-force-Hessian training (E-F-H). When probe vectors are randomized for each minibatch, both HVP-based approaches achieve energy, force, and Hessian accuracy comparable to full Hessian training while providing more than speedups per epoch for the small molecular systems studied here. In a more realistic fixed-vector regime with only one HVP per molecule, dense Gaussian projections consistently outperform one-column probing, particularly for far-from-equilibrium geometries. Paired follow-up training with Rademacher probes gives no statistically significant change in model accuracy relative to the original Gaussian choice, although Rademacher probes have lower single-probe estimator variance and bounded component magnitudes. Overall, PHL effectively replaces explicit Hessian supervision with force-complexity curvature training, retaining most of the accuracy benefits of full second-order methods while enabling scalable MLIP development for larger and more complex molecular systems.
authors: Austin Rodriguez, Justin S Smith, Sakib Matin, Nicholas Lubbers, Kipton Barros and Jose L Mendoza-Cortes

articles.title: Deterministic and probabilistic neural surrogates of global hybrid-Vlasov simulations
articles.abstract: Hybrid-Vlasov simulations resolve ion-kinetic effects in the solar wind–magnetosphere interaction, but even 5D (2D + 3 V) configurations are computationally expensive. We show that graph-based machine learning emulators can learn the spatiotemporal evolution of electromagnetic fields and lower-order moments of the ion velocity distribution function (VDF) in near-Earth space from four 5D Vlasiator runs, each driven by steady solar wind conditions. The upstream ion number density is varied between runs at fixed grid spacing, scanning the ratio of ion inertial length to grid size. Using a graph neural network (GNN) operating on the 2D spatial simulation grid comprising 670k cells, we demonstrate that both a deterministic forecasting model (Graph-FM) and a probabilistic ensemble forecasting model (Graph-EFM) based on a latent variable formulation produce accurate predictions of future plasma states. A divergence penalty is incorporated to encourage divergence-freeness in the magnetic fields. For the probabilistic model, a continuous ranked probability score objective is added to improve the calibration of the ensemble forecasts. In terms of wall time per output step, the trained emulators run over two orders of magnitude faster on a single GPU than the Vlasiator simulations on 100 CPUs, although this comparison involves different hardware and the emulators predict only moments of the ion VDF rather than the full distribution. Most forecasted fields have Pearson correlations above 0.95 at 50 s lead time. Fields that exhibit degenerate (near-zero) distributions in the 5D setting are more challenging for the emulator to keep well correlated. The ensemble forecasts remain underdispersive, with spread–skill ratios of approximately 0.2–0.3, and thus provide spatially structured relative uncertainty estimates. Overall, GNNs offer a viable framework for rapid ensemble generation in hybrid-Vlasov modeling. We diagnose where such moment-based emulation succeeds and fails, and release the dataset and code as an open benchmark for the community.
authors: Daniel Holmberg, Ivan Zaitsev, Markku Alho, Ioanna Bouri, Fanni Franssila, Haewon Jeong, Minna Palmroth and Teemu Roos

articles.title: Magnetic localization and spectral asymmetry of a charged particle at a screw dislocation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a charged particle moving outside a spiral (screw) dislocation in a uniform magnetic field. Although the geometry is locally Euclidean, its global screw identification couples the conserved axial and azimuthal quantities through the combination (J=ell-β k) After eliminating the cyclic coordinates, the radial motion is governed by an inverse-square term determined by J and a harmonic confining term generated by the magnetic field. The corresponding reduced quantum problem is exactly solvable for qB₀≠0, yielding an equally spaced spectrum with an orientation-dependent energy shift. The radial probability density depends on J, and opposite values of the screw-modified quantum number have identical spatial profiles but different energies for a fixed magnetic-field orientation. The radial size scales as (sqrtłangle r²ångleₙpropto |qB₀|⁻¹/²), with the magnetic length setting the localization scale. At qB₀₌₀, the confining term vanishes, and the problem reduces to a scale-free inverse-square system. Thus, the screw parameter enters the dynamics through the global coupling of the conserved axial and azimuthal quantities, whereas the magnetic field provides radial confinement and its orientation determines the spectral asymmetry.
authors: Claudio Furtado, Omar Mustafa, Hassan Hassanabadi, Abdullah Guvendi

articles.title: Competing symmetry breaking and topology in quantum spin chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how spontaneous symmetry breaking and symmetry-protected topology compete and cooperate in one-dimensional quantum spin-1/2 systems. We introduce two families of local Hamiltonians with Z,₂×Z,₂×ZT₂ symmetry which host a zoo of broken-symmetry phases with and without gapless boundary spins, namely, six long-range-ordered gapped phases that differ by their Z,₂-symmetry-breaking patterns (FM,ₓ,y,z and Neel,ₓ,y,z), their partner symmetry-protected topological phases (FMSPTₓ,y and NeelSPTₓ,y), and two gapless phases (gFM,z and gNeel,z) with incommensurate ZT₂-breaking magnetic long-range order and central charge mathsfc=1. Direct transitions between competing gapped phases can be continuous or weakly first order. We demonstrate that continuous phase transition lines have exotic critical properties.
