articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.04657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Directed graphs naturally model many real-world systems in which interactions are asymmetric, such as citation networks, web graphs, and information-flow networks. However, graph learning methods commonly rely on message passing with symmetrized graph representations or positional encodings that only partially exploit edge directionality. We introduce PathLapPE, a novel spectral positional encoding (PE) derived from the path Laplacian on directed graphs. PathLapPE provides node- and edge-level features that encode directional higher-order structure and can be incorporated into standard graph learning architectures. Empirical results on node- and graph-level benchmark tasks show that PathLapPE yields consistent improvements across several architectures, especially when combined with direction-aware message passing. Compared with magnetic Laplacian positional encodings, a widely studied spectral positional encoding for directed graphs, PathLapPE does not require additional fine-tuning of directionality hyperparameters while offering competitive runtime and performance.
authors: Lydia Mezrag, Semih Cantürk, Michael Perlmutter, Bastian Rieck, Guy Wolf

articles.title: Localized Operator Learning with Adaptive Partition-of-Unity Mixture-of-Expert Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.04708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operator learning methods such as DeepONets and FNOs often struggle with PDE families featuring sharp interfaces, heterogeneous coefficients, and localized multiscale structures. We introduce a partition-of-unity (POU) mixture-of-experts framework for localized operator learning, in which geometry-aware gating networks produce smooth spatial partitions which blend the contributions of local expert networks. Our main contribution is HiRefPOU, a residual-style hierarchical POU architecture for DeepONets that organizes localized representations through nested parent-child partitions while preserving global continuity. We also show that the same POU principle can be incorporated into Fourier Neural Operators to introduce spatial adaptivity without modifying the underlying spectral layers. On heterogeneous Darcy and reaction-diffusion benchmarks, HiRefPOU achieves substantially lower error than global DeepONet and static POU-MoE baselines, while the broader operator-learning experiments show that the benefits of localization depend on the PDE structure and the chosen neural-operator backbone. The learned partitions are interpretable and align with interfaces and regions of rapid solution variation. These results show that explicit geometric localization can improve both accuracy and interpretability in neural operator learning.
authors: Madison Cooley, Ramansh Sharma, Shandian Zhe, Robert M. Kirby, Varun Shankar

articles.title: MAGIC: Topology-Aware Analytic Graph Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.04963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph few-shot class-incremental learning (GFSCIL) requires a model to continually recognize emerging classes from only a few labeled nodes while preserving previously acquired knowledge. Beyond the catastrophic forgetting inherited from conventional graph continual learning, GFSCIL presents two distinctive challenges: extremely limited novel-class supervision causes severe overfitting, while cross-session edges---edges connecting newly arriving nodes with historical nodes---alter historical propagation neighborhoods and thereby induce representation drift. We propose MAGIC, a replay-free GFSCIL framework that combines a frozen graph representation backbone (e.g., an intrinsically parameter-free backbone such as SGC or a pretrained graph foundation model) with closed-form analytic continual learning. To alleviate novel-session overfitting, MAGIC learns a topological prior from the base graph that can characterize both homophilous and heterophilous relations, and injects this prior through Potts Markov random field inference to refine supervision for novel classes. To mitigate representation drift, MAGIC transfers previous predictions from the old representations of affected historical nodes to their updated representations through drift-aware analytic distillation. Experiments across five datasets and eight baselines demonstrate the effectiveness of MAGIC. Under the 5-shot setting, MAGIC improves Mean Accuracy and Final Accuracy by 5.48 percentage points and 9.33 percentage points on average, and reduces Performance Drop by 10.78 percentage points on average compared with the best baselines. MAGIC also shows clear advantages under the 1- and 3-shot settings, with larger gains as the number of supports increases. Moreover, MAGIC requires substantially less training time.
authors: Junlin Chen, Yuhan Wang, Xuefei Wang, Xiao Wang, Ruijie Wang, Jianxin Li

articles.title: Discrete Action Matching: Learning Stochastic Dynamics from Samples via State Graphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning population dynamics from unpaired temporal marginals is an ill-posed inverse problem that requires structural assumptions on the underlying dynamics. We introduce Discrete Action Matching (DAM), a finite-state counterpart of Action Matching based on discrete Wasserstein geometry. For a prescribed marginal path and transport geometry, we derive an action-minimization objective for its canonical minimum-kinetic-energy current. Our key observation is that the density dependence of the discrete action reduces to neighboring density ratios. Along an empirical interpolation of the snapshots, DAM first estimates these ratios and then learns an action potential. The learned fields also define a graph-supported Markov sampler. Experiments on controlled synthetic dynamics and real mouse gastrulation data evaluate marginal reconstruction and interpolation. Additional experiments approximate numerical surface-transport paths from paired samples.

articles.title: Direction-Conditioned Policies for Online Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contrastive Reinforcement Learning (CRL) learns representations that estimate goal reachability, yet its policy remains conditioned on raw goals and therefore does not directly exploit the geometry encoded by its critic. We introduce Direction-Conditioned Policies (DCP), a method built around a small modification to CRL: DCP selects previously visited states as waypoints during online training and conditions the policy on their direction and distance in representation space. At deployment, DCP applies the same interface directly to the final goal, requiring neither waypoint selection nor planning. Across nine navigation and manipulation tasks, DCP attains higher final success rates than CRL on seven tasks and spends more time near the goal on seven. Controlled maze experiments further show that DCP captures shortest-path geometry more accurately and that the supplied direction causally influences the actor's behavior. We identify waypoint coverage and ranking as limits to exploration, and show that learned candidate generation improves goal reaching in two controlled mazes.
authors: S K Swaminathan, Damiya Gondha, Theyanesh Eswaramoorthy Rajahkrishnan, Aritra Hazra

articles.title: Component-Level Evaluation of Adaptive PINN Training for CFD-Oriented Crystal Growth Simulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) training minimizes a weighted combination of partial differential equation (PDE), boundary-condition, and initial-condition losses. Because adaptive methods modify these weights during training, their weighted total losses are not always directly comparable. We compare fixed-weight PINN, gradient-normalized PINN (GNPINN), and a rule-based adaptive controller (AgenticPINN) under matched settings on a heat-equation benchmark and a simplified Czochralski-oriented thermal-fluid problem. In the crystal-growth MLP experiment, adaptive control reduced the PDE residual from the order of 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁶, while the boundary-condition loss increased from the order of 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻². On the heat-equation benchmark, GNPINN achieved the lowest relative L₂ field error (0.054), whereas AgenticPINN obtained the smallest PDE residual but a relative L₂ error of 1.368. Gaussian-process surrogates were additionally evaluated using case-wise holdout tests on corrected Czochralski CFD parameter sweeps. The temperature-field error for the temperature sweep was approximately 6%, whereas the axial-velocity error for the crystal-rotation sweep was approximately 42%. These findings show that adaptive control can improve equation satisfaction while weakening other physical constraints. PINN training should therefore be evaluated using separate PDE, boundary-condition, and solution-error metrics rather than weighted total loss alone.
authors: Niruta Chapagain, Rohit Raj, Bertwin Kurisinkal Shine, Aditya A S

articles.title: Ranking Bandits for Carousel Interfaces with Observable Browsing Depth
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Carousel interfaces allow a recommender system to directly observe how far a user has browsed. This signal distinguishes displayed but unclicked items from items that were never displayed, whereas conventional ranking-bandit models, including cascade and position-based models, generally treat examination as latent. We formulate a ranking-bandit problem in which a learner presents a list of L items, observes the user's maximum browsing depth, and receives click feedback only for positions up to that depth. The objective is to maximize the expected number of clicks under an unknown item-attractiveness vector and a browsing-depth distribution. We propose three algorithms based on UCB, Thompson Sampling, and DMED, all of which update item statistics only from observed exposures. We derive an instance-dependent logarithmic upper bound for our UCB-based algorithm and an asymptotic upper bound for our DMED-based algorithm that coincides with the lower bound as its parameter αdownarrow 0, establishing asymptotic optimality in this limit. Simulations in synthetic shallow- and deep-browsing environments, together with experiments parameterized from RecGaze interaction logs, show that OD-TS attains final mean regret similar to PBM-TS, while the proposed methods achieve lower final mean regret than PBM-UCB.

articles.title: EMG-GPT: Predictive Pretraining on Residual-Quantized EMG Tokens for Hand Pose Estimation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) is a low-power, cost-effective biosignal for hand-pose estimation and gesture classification. In this work, we examine whether self-supervised pretraining on sEMG can yield transferable representations for continuous hand-pose estimation. We introduce EMG-GPT, a causal transformer-based model that operates on discrete sEMG representations from a frozen residual vector quantization (RVQ) tokenizer and learns temporal dynamics through depth-autoregressive future-code prediction. The model combines within-frame integration with causal temporal modeling while preserving the geometry of the pretrained codebook. EMG-GPT shows competitive results in both Regression and Tracking tasks, supporting EMG-only pretraining as a viable approach for learning transferable sEMG representations.
authors: Ettore Magni, Rolandos Alexandros Potamias, Stefanos Zafeiriou, Konstantinos Barmpas

articles.title: No Concept Escapes the Audit: Auditing-Aware Unlearning for Verifiable Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models can generate prohibited content, which motivates concept erasure through machine unlearning. Most erasure methods intervene at the text interface, through prompt modification or localized updates to text-conditioning weights, and they are evaluated by what the model outputs for given prompts. Such evaluation cannot see what the network still encodes. Latent-space auditing, which bypasses text conditioning and probes the denoising network directly, shows that erased concepts remain recoverable from internal representations. We find that this also holds for methods built to be robust against adversarial prompts, and that the problem grows with the number of erased concepts. We propose Auditing-Aware Unlearning for Verifiable Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models (AVCE), a framework that grounds erasure in the model's latent representations. AVCE audits the embedding neighborhood of each concept and condenses the discovered vulnerable directions into an anchor at the weakest geometric point. It edits cross-attention and self-attention projections in closed form at this anchor, then fine-tunes the two pathways with pathway-level auditing losses, using orthogonal gradient projection to consolidate multiple concepts. Experiments on SD v1.5, SDXL, and Flux 1.0 across object, explicit-content, and artistic-style unlearning show that AVCE reduces attack success rates by 5.07x and improves auditing scores by 3.84x over the strongest baseline, while preserving competitive generation quality.
authors: Kaiyuan Deng, Yuchen Li, Gen Li, Yang Xiao, Geng Yuan, Xiaoyong Yuan, Bo Hui, Xiaolong Ma

articles.title: Shapley-based Structural Analysis of Neural Calibration for Stochastic Volatility Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.03076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural network-based approaches have emerged as efficient alternatives to traditional optimization-based procedures for the calibration of stochastic volatility models. However, existing work has focused primarily on predictive accuracy, with comparatively little attention devoted to understanding the structure of the learned inverse calibration mappings. In this work, we analyze neural calibration mappings for the Heston and rough Heston models across multilayer perceptron, highway, and softmax-parametrized highway architectures, using complementary Shapley-based methods from explainable AI. Specifically, we consider SHAP and νSHAP explanations, which capture distinct, complementary notions of feature relevance, corresponding to sensitivity and sufficiency of feature subsets, respectively. Short maturities and smile wings consistently dominate parameter inference, and the dominant attribution structure remains qualitatively stable across architectures despite differences in predictive accuracy and parameter count. Parameter-specific differences between SHAP and νSHAP further reveal how distinct regions of the implied volatility surface contribute to parameter recovery and expose substantial redundancy in the calibration input. Building on this redundancy, we show that νSHAP explanations can guide a significant reduction in input dimensionality for the rough Heston model while matching calibration accuracy relative to the full implied volatility surface. These findings demonstrate that complementary Shapley-based methods provide structural insight into learned inverse calibration mappings beyond predictive error metrics, and offer a practical route to feature selection in neural calibration problems.
authors: Shaïn Afzali, Serena Della Corte, Antonis Papapantoleon

articles.title: Global error estimators for parametric monotone nonlinearities and neural approximations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct computable error estimators, which double as loss functions for neural networks, for a class of parametric nonlinear partial differential equations with a monotonicity property, and prove that they are globally reliable and efficient. The value of such a loss function is bounded above and below by the squared error in the natural trial norm, for every trial function, not merely for those near the exact solution; this global property rests on monotonicity. The construction rests on splitting the nonlinear operator into a linear part and a strongly monotone closure, and on measuring the linear residual in a discrete dual norm. Since the closure contributes a dual norm that admits no closed form when the trial norm is stronger than an L₂ norm, the estimator is built around a computable surrogate for it, required only to satisfy a pairing bound and a Lipschitz bound. The main theorem then yields two-sided bounds with explicit constants and covers two instances. A first-order system least-squares estimator on conforming trial spaces is the first instance studied: its two-sided bound holds on the whole trial space and therefore applies to arbitrary approximations, including those not in a discrete finite element space. The second instance is a discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin estimator on trial spaces of finite element functions for each parameter value, built with broken test spaces, for which no conformity is required and the dual norm is computed by independent element-local problems. All assumptions are verified for a model class of nonlinear fluxes, with the constants tracked explicitly in terms of the parameter range. Being computable for an arbitrary input, both estimators serve as variationally correct loss functions for neural network approximations of parameter-to-solution maps.
authors: Pablo Cortés Castillo, Wolfgang Dahmen, Jay Gopalakrishnan

articles.title: LinearPFN: Amortized Variable Selection for Linear Models with Interactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.06580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spike-and-slab regression is a standard Bayesian formulation of variable selection: it returns a posterior distribution over which candidate effects are active rather than a single selected subset, so that every candidate effect carries an inclusion probability. Its cost grows exponentially with the number of candidate effects, so the posterior can be enumerated exactly only when the number of predictors is small. Beyond that reach, the posterior has to be approximated, typically by Markov chain Monte Carlo over the model space, which requires a fresh run for every dataset and, within a fixed budget of steps, may fail to converge. We present LinearPFN, a prior-data fitted transformer network that amortizes spike-and-slab inference for linear models with main effects and pairwise interactions. The network is pretrained once on synthetic datasets, drawn from an explicitly specified prior, and a single forward pass over a new dataset returns posterior inclusion probabilities, posterior-mean coefficients and posterior predictive distributions with no per-dataset fitting. The prior is conjugate by design, so that the posterior for each fixed set of active effects has a closed form, and wherever the exact posterior is still computable by enumeration we verify the network's outputs against it. On real predictor matrices from published social-science datasets, with outcomes drawn from the prior so that the true active set is known, LinearPFN attains a higher per-dataset selection AUC and a higher F1 under the median probability model rule than five classical baselines. The lead holds when the coefficients, the interactions or the noise depart from the prior. Code: https://github.com/schiekiera/LinearPFN. Trained model: https://huggingface.co/schiekiera/LinearPFN.
authors: Louis Schiekiera, Max Zimmer, Christophe Roux, Manuel Arnold, Sebastian Pokutta, Fritz Günther

articles.title: Personal VAD: Speaker-Conditioned Voice Activity Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:1908.04284v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose "personal VAD", a system to detect the voice activity of a target speaker at the frame level. This system is useful for gating the inputs to a streaming on-device speech recognition system, such that it only triggers for the target user, which helps reduce the computational cost and battery consumption, especially in scenarios where a keyword detector is unpreferable. We achieve this by training a VAD-alike neural network that is conditioned on the target speaker embedding or the speaker verification score. For each frame, personal VAD outputs the probabilities for three classes: non-speech, target speaker speech, and non-target speaker speech. Under our optimal setup, we are able to train a model with only 130K parameters that outperforms a baseline system where individually trained standard VAD and speaker recognition networks are combined to perform the same task.
authors: Shaojin Ding, Quan Wang, Shuo-yiin Chang, Li Wan, Ignacio Lopez Moreno

articles.title: Ordinary Least Squares as an Attention Mechanism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2504.09663v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: I show that ordinary least squares (OLS) predictions can be rewritten as the output of a restricted attention module, akin to those forming the backbone of large language models. The connection comes from viewing OLS as a similarity-based prediction rule in a learned embedding space. In this representation, least squares does not estimate coefficients per se. Instead, it selects an embedding that minimizes squared prediction error by matching training and test vectors through inner products. This maps directly onto the query-key-value structure of attention mechanisms. I then discuss extensions to dimensionality reduction, nonlinearity, and time series econometrics. Monte Carlo simulations and real-data experiments on UCI/OpenML benchmarks show that nonlinear Attention Regression performs competitively against standard machine learning baselines. In the reverse direction, I replace the attention sublayer of a transformer for tabular data with an explicit regression on polynomial features. The resulting model performs comparably to the standard transformer at a fraction of its parameter count.

articles.title: BKP: An R Package for Beta Kernel Process Modeling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.10447v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Estimating input-dependent probability surfaces from binary, binomial, categorical, or multinomial response data is a common task in statistics and machine learning. Latent Gaussian process classifiers provide flexible nonparametric models for such problems, but posterior inference with discrete responses typically requires approximation or simulation. We discuss an implementation of probability-scale beta and Dirichlet kernel models in the pkgBKP package for proglangR. The package implements the Beta Kernel Process (BKP), which uses kernel-weighted pseudo-count aggregation and beta-binomial conjugacy to obtain closed-form conjugate posterior summaries and posterior predictive distributions for binomial probabilities. It also implements the Dirichlet Kernel Process (DKP) for multi-class responses, together with TwinBKP and TwinDKP, scalable twinning-based global-local approximations for larger datasets. The resulting workflow supports transparent kernel-weighted evidence borrowing, several kernel families, fixed and data-adaptive priors, effective-sample-size calibration, loss-based hyperparameter tuning, and standard S3 methods for fitting, prediction, simulation, visualization, and extraction of posterior summaries. Reproducible examples demonstrate probability-surface estimation, binary and multi-class classification, computational comparison, and real-data applications to emphLoa loa infection prevalence mapping and Mourning Warbler distribution modeling.
authors: Jiangyan Zhao, Kunhai Qing, Jin Xu

articles.title: SLIM: Stochastic Learning and Inference in Overidentified Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.20996v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose SLIM (Stochastic Learning and Inference in overidentified Models), a scalable stochastic approximation framework for nonlinear GMM. Independent mini-batches of moments and derivatives yield unbiased update directions with martingale difference noise. Under suitable regularity conditions, SLIM yields consistent and asymptotically normal estimators without a consistent initial estimator or a globally convex GMM criterion. Our theory covers fixed-sample and random-sampling asymptotics. An optional second-order refinement achieves full-sample GMM efficiency. Random-scaling and plug-in inference account for sampling and computational uncertainty, while debiased J-tests permit specification testing with SLIM. We extend the framework to clustered data with unequal cluster sizes, preserving the form of the inference procedures. Monte Carlo experiments for a nonlinear demand system with 576 moments and 380 parameters demonstrate computational gains and scalability to one million observations. A large-scale LinkedIn application with 4.8 million college graduates illustrates clustered estimation and inference for first employment destinations.
authors: Xiaohong Chen, Min Seong Kim, Sokbae Lee, Myung Hwan Seo, Myunghyun Song, Ling Zhong

articles.title: A PAC-Bayesian View of Generalisation for Physics-Informed Machine Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.26341v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) integrates mechanistic knowledge, typically through partial differential equations (PDEs), into data-driven models. Despite strong empirical performance, its statistical generalisation properties remain poorly understood, especially for regression with unbounded losses. We develop a PAC-Bayesian framework for PIML that provides high-probability generalisation guarantees under potentially unbounded losses. Exploiting the structure of physics-informed objectives, we derive component-wise bounds whose complexity scales with the input-gradient energy of each loss, establishing a direct link between physical regularity and generalisation. We further introduce a PAC-Bayesian calibration procedure that yields computable gradient-based complexities while controlling rare large-gradient events through a residual-tail correction. Adopting a multi-task view of data fidelity, PDE residuals, initial conditions, and boundary conditions, we obtain a refined certificate with a single PAC-Bayesian complexity penalty, avoiding the looseness of independently bounding each component. Building on this certificate, we propose a bound-aware learning procedure that promotes empirical accuracy, proximity to a physics-informed prior, and low input-gradient complexity. Experiments on six PDE benchmarks yield substantially tighter certificates than bounded-loss and sub-Gaussian alternatives, while ablations quantify the effects of posterior-training data, calibration data, gradient envelopes, and hypothesis localisation.
authors: Thien V. Nguyen, Amaury Habrard, Benjamin Guedj

articles.title: SGAnalog: An End-to-End Circuit Benchmark from Open-Source Silicon Tapeouts
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.03934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing analog integrated circuit design benchmarks make two questions hard to answer: whether a model has learned transferable circuit skills rather than recalled familiar examples, and whether its output works under defined process and test conditions. We introduce a benchmark built from human-designed, open-source circuits associated with Tiny Tapeout manufacturing shuttles. The collection contains 273 topologically distinct top-level designs. Every source is retrieved at the revision recorded for its shuttle submission and processed in a fixed containerized environment. The pipeline exports each eligible schematic image and its SPICE netlist from the same source file, giving transcription an exact structural reference. Commit dates support model-specific training-cutoff analysis, while author testbenches provide the simulation context for sizing. The benchmark evaluates schematic-to-netlist transcription and device sizing. Across seven models on a fixed set of 66 transcription tasks, the strongest model reaches 56.1% exact graph isomorphism, and six of seven models drop sharply from the small to the medium tier. For one frontier model, removing author-chosen labels reduces exact matches while preserving aggregate structural F1, suggesting that labels can aid connectivity tracing. On the 17 sizing tasks, the leading model converges on all 17 proposals and reaches 91.2 out of 100 against the human reference, while the two newest Claude models refuse 4 and 11 of the same prompts they transcribe without objection; a proposal without sizes scores zero. The two tasks produce different model rankings, exposing distinct visual and design capabilities and, in one family, a policy rather than capability limit.

articles.title: Beyond the Parameter Monolith: Reconstructive Memories, Executable Skills, and Residual Assembly for Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.04012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model systems can separate contextual computation, persistent storage, and exact execution instead of updating all capabilities through one shared parameter system. We investigate FEM-ASM, a finite-element-method-inspired organization in which independently constructed document states and deterministic executable skills contribute typed proposals to a shared language-model state. An explicit residual operator reconciles proposals attached to common interface nodes. We evaluate this organization through controlled experiments and negative results rather than claiming a physical finite-element formulation of language. An attention-free Multi-Mesh prototype learns causal language modeling but does not establish competitive general capability. A versioned store contains 52,809 reconstructive memory elements near a 1.7-billion-floating-value budget; reconstruction is incomplete, with approximately 75% token accuracy. Support-aware lexical indices make these elements addressable under provenance-controlled query construction. For executable arithmetic, positional result observations substantially improve neural rendering relative to a repeated global result vector, and output substitutions change the model's preferred answer. A bounded attachment demonstration further measures the effect of making selected evidence available, without establishing the utility of loading an entire multi-billion-value store. The results support a separation of storage, execution, and neural coordination, while identifying unresolved limitations in question-only retrieval, unrestricted answer generation, and end-to-end efficiency.

articles.title: A Tropical Geometry View of Forgetting: A Per-Unit Projector for Knowledge-Preserving Fine-Tuning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.04670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning a language model on new text degrades what it already does. Replay-free projectors such as Adam-NSCL and GPM forbid one shared subspace of a layer's inputs in every row of the update. The tropical geometry of a ReLU layer shows why this is too coarse. In data space, the units' walls are tropical hypersurfaces whose cells are dual to the upper vertices of a zonotope; in weight space, each old token is a hyperplane, and the tokens cut out a polyhedron, the closure of the weights that keep every token on its side. An exact identity joins the two pictures: the squared change of the layer's output under any weight change splits into in-cell, open-to-closed and closed-to-open terms, and the first two live on the tokens each unit fires on. The identity names a gate-aware per-unit projector, and a budget-separation theorem prices exact protection: it costs a unit the rank of its own open tokens, while a shared subspace pays at least the rank of their union in every row. On OPT-1.3b, where 96% of (token, unit) pairs are closed, the projector forgets less than Adam-NSCL at all six matched budgets from 9 to 60 constrained directions per row, the gap widening from 1.1× to 4.3×; with 1/5.5 of the directions it halves the forgetting of Adam-NSCL at GPM's energy threshold. On OPT-6.7b, it matches Adam-NSCL's forgetting at matched budget while learning more. As the theory predicts, the open/closed partition is the operative variable: open tokens beat random, sign-blind and anti-gate token sets on 18 of 18 seed-pairs. In pruning repair, every derivative-based local model of the output error at the dense weights is blind to pairs that open: the minimisers of the gate-weighted objective can leave the polyhedron, the objective's closed-form solution is 1.94 nats worse than no repair on OPT-1.3b, and a convex one-sided penalty bounds the escape.
authors: Yuyang Zhang, Xiaoyin Chen, Chunlin Ren, Qihuang Zhang

articles.title: When Debate Helps: Proposal Supply and Verification-Aware Readout in Multi-Agent Reasoning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.04686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent debate can improve reasoning, yet often fails to beat simple majority voting. We argue that successful debate requires two distinct mechanisms: proposal supply must surface a correct answer, and readout must identify that answer when voting misses it. We formalize the first requirement through recoverable headroom, which measures cases where a correct proposal is available but the majority answer is wrong. For the second, we develop Latent Verification Debate (LVD), an accounting model in which candidate proposals receive answer-specific verification evidence before final generation. Controlled fixed-proposal interventions estimate this latent effect in equivalent peer-support units and show that correct evidence changes answer probabilities and generated decisions while proposal supply remains fixed. To improve proposal supply, we construct societies from neural-thicket agents using labeled and label-free coverage objectives. Across two backbones and matched-budget reasoning benchmarks, coverage-selected societies increase complementary proposal supply and improve aggregate accuracy in repeated stochastic evaluations. Round-level controls further show that interaction provides gains beyond applying the same finalizer directly to the initial proposals. These results identify proposal coverage and truth-sensitive evidence use as complementary conditions for debate to outperform voting. Code is available at https://github.com/Wang-ML-Lab/when-debate-helps.
authors: Zihao Zhao, Tunyu Zhang, Haizhou Shi, Yusong Zhao, Xinxi Zhang, Hao Wang

articles.title: How corner is a corner case? Percentile control for highway scenario generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating corner-case scenarios with appropriate adversity in a simulation environment is critical for testing an autonomous vehicle (AV) software stack's safety performance before deployment. Existing autonomous-driving scenario generators can enforce specific behavior, adversity, or feasibility conditions, but they provide limited control over how extreme a generated scenario is relative to plausible futures in the same traffic context. This study represents the adversity of a generated scenario as its percentile in the conditional distribution of future risk given the observed history. This view supports calibrated answers to two questions: how "corner" a generated corner-case scenario is and how its "cornerness" can be fine-tuned. To this end, we formulate history-conditioned risk-percentile requests and learn a reference risk distribution that maps each requested percentile to a physical risk target. We then use a percentile-conditioned joint diffusion model with sampling-time risk guidance to generate multi-agent futures, together with a reference-based criterion for evaluating percentile realization. Experiments use the minimum post-encroachment time (PET) between the ego and its surrounding vehicles as the risk surrogate on highD. On the primary evaluation set, our method realizes 1,422 of 1,440 requests within a 0.05 percentile tolerance (98.75%), with mean percentile error 0.00673 and PET-target error 0.00991 seconds. The resulting interface connects context-relative risk specification, physical realization, and evaluation through a common risk scale. Project website and videos of generated scenarios are available at https://hhj233.github.io/CornerPercentile/.
authors: Jiaxi Liu, Hang Zhou, Hangyu Li, Yifan Wang, Keke Long, Chengyuan Ma, Bin Ran, Xiaopeng Li

articles.title: LexiHorizon: Stabilizing Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Deep Search
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep search agents tackle complex knowledge tasks through iterative retrieval, multi-hop reasoning, and evidence synthesis across multiple sources. Existing approaches typically assume relatively stable retrieval systems and operate over short-horizon tool interaction. However, when retrieval is sensitive to query formulation, even a semantically appropriate query may fail to surface critical evidence because of mismatched entity names, aliases, or keyword combinations. Recovering from such failures requires repeated query reformulation and longer interaction trajectories. This setting poses a distinct training challenge, as the policy must sustain long-horizon query exploration while managing an expanding volume of retrieved content. We propose LexiHorizon, a framework for training search agents over long horizons that expands the trajectory context budget, manages accumulated retrieval content using a window over recent tool observations while preserving the reasoning history, and introduces an outcome-gated search-effort reward that provides a bounded bonus for tool invocations to trajectories with nonzero answer reward. Experiments on XBench, WebWalkerQA, and BrowseComp-ZH show that the resulting 9B model consistently outperforms both its base model and MiroThinker-1.7-mini, with maximum absolute gains of 8.7 and 23.8 percentage points, respectively. These results suggest that combining an extended context budget with reasoning-preserving context management benefits long-horizon deep search agents.
authors: Zhiqing Nong, Liang Wen, Chao-Hsuan Liu

articles.title: R1A-PC: Physics-Guided Electromagnetic Inversion of Three-Dimensional Human Point Clouds in Complex Static Environments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.05144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovering three-dimensional human geometry from electromagnetic measure?ments in a complex static environment is difficult because strong multipath responses from walls, floors, and other objects obscure the weak target per?turbation. We propose R1A-PC, a physics-guided method that reconstructs a 2048-point human cloud from paired complex fields measured with and without the target. Complex background subtraction emphasizes target-induced ampli?tude and phase changes, while the background field remains available as an environmental condition. A frequency-balanced discrete Born adjoint produces a three-dimensional spatial knowledge map. At each of two bounded deformation stages, the decoder combines complex measurement features, background fea?tures, and multiscale physical features queried at the current point coordinates; the second stage queries again after the first coordinate update. We analyze the residual of paired subtraction, the weighted normal-operator structure of the raw adjoint, and the feasible set of the predicted cloud. In a held-out background generated by full-wave simulation under a fixed acquisition geometry, R1A-PC obtains a squared Chamfer distance of 0.001434 m2 and an F-score of 0.963080 at 0.05 m. Compared with TopNet, the Chamfer distance decreases by 70.28%. Removing physical guidance or background subtraction increases the Chamfer distance by 242.06% or 241.18%, respectively. Experiments across background layouts and poses support the complementary roles of paired subtraction and position-dependent adjoint features.
authors: Xudong Yuan, Ruyun Xu, Jingtai Yang, Xianzheng Sun

articles.title: DPNL: A DPLL-based Algorithm for Probabilistic Neurosymbolic Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.06270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probabilistic Neurosymbolic Learning (PNL) combines neural predictions with symbolic reasoning, enabling end-to-end learning from final-output supervision without labels for intermediate concepts. A central challenge is probabilistic inference: state-of-the-art approaches often rely on materializing the logical provenance of a query, which can itself become a major computational bottleneck. We introduce Dynamic Probabilistic Neurosymbolic Learning (DPNL), an oracle-guided framework that avoids requiring complete provenance materialization before inference. DPNL lazily explores the space of intermediate assignments, while oracles resolve entire regions that can already be certified to produce or exclude the target output. We establish conditions ensuring soundness and termination. ApproxDPNL extends the same search with early termination while maintaining certified bounds on the exact output probability, providing controlled approximation guarantees. The oracle interface decouples inference from the representation of the symbolic component, enabling problem-specific reasoning within the same framework. Experiments on several neurosymbolic tasks show that DPNL and ApproxDPNL substantially extend the range of problem instances tractable by probabilistic neurosymbolic inference.
authors: Thomas Jean-Michel Valentin (ENS Paris Saclay,TYREX), Pierre Genevès (LIG,TYREX), Luisa Sophie Werner (LIG,TYREX), Sarah Chlyah (TYREX), Nabil Layaïda (TYREX), Nils Gesbert (Grenoble INP ENSIMAG,TYREX)

articles.title: Persistent Enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) Rains over Luzon in July and August 2026: The Combined Role of a Stalled Madden–Julian Oscillation and El Niño
articles.abstract: During the summer of 2026, a severe and prolonged southwest monsoon episode delivered extreme accumulated rainfall across Western Luzon, Philippines, driven by a Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) event that became stalled in Phases 6–7 over the Western Pacific. Using ERA5 reanalysis and GPM-IMERG precipitation data, this study traces the multi-scale atmospheric sequence connecting this intraseasonal stagnation to localized monsoonal inundations. Equatorial (5°S–5°N) cross-section diagnostics reveal that eastward MJO propagation was halted by a perturbed Walker circulation, wherein an upper-level subsidence trap east of the dateline (170°E–140°W) combined with a lower-tropospheric moist static energy deficit to the west to geographically anchor the ascending MJO convective core over 120°E–150°E. Spectral Poisson solutions for 200 hPa velocity potential confirm persistent upper-tropospheric mass outflow, which induced a stationary, off-equatorial Gill-type cyclonic Rossby gyre over the northern South China Sea. This monsoon gyre sustained a continuous, humidity-rich Moisture Conveyor Belt directed straight into Luzon. Column moisture budget decomposition confirms that vertically integrated mass convergence, rather than horizontal moisture advection or local surface evaporation, served as the primary thermodynamic driver. Finally, zonal transects along 16°N–17°N demonstrate how this deep boundary-layer moisture flux was mechanically forced upward by the Zambales Range, triggering localized heavy rainfall. These findings demonstrate how planetary-scale atmospheric suppressions can stall intraseasonal oscillations, converting transient MJO passages into prolonged regional hazards.

articles.title: ReWater-DC Evo: A Three-Stage, Renewable-Assisted System for Recovering Data-Center Cooling Water
articles.abstract: Data-center expansion driven by artificial intelligence is increasing demand for cooling water, while the blowdown discharged from cooling towers carries concentrated salts, heavy metals and organic residues that make reuse difficult. This paper presents ReWater-DC Evo, a three-stage, renewable-assisted water-recovery concept: (1) electrically driven separation of heavy metals and other suspended or dissolved contaminants, (2) solar-assisted degradation of harmful organic substances, and (3) salinity reduction with a specialized carbon-based material. The project reports an approximately 95% water-recovery potential with lower energy and chemical requirements than conventional chemical-intensive treatment. We develop the mathematical framework for the system (water balance, reject concentration, removal efficiency, electrochemical dose, photocatalytic kinetics and specific energy), present a process flow diagram, and specify a complete experimental and data-collection plan. Using the reported 95% recovery and standard cooling-tower relations, we model an illustrative facility and show that recovery lowers fresh make-up water demand by about 16–32% at 3–6 cycles of concentration, while an ideal reject stream becomes 20 times more concentrated than the feed. We also assess practical utility across applications and identify the limitations that laboratory, pilot and long-term studies must resolve before full-scale adoption.

articles.title: Combining phytoremediation potential of Lemna gibba with biochar adsorption technology for cadmium, nickel and lead removal from wastewater
articles.abstract: The removing of cadmium (Cd), nickel (Ni), and lead (Pb) from industrial wastewater using phytoremediation by aquatic plant (Lemna gibba) and adsorption onto biochar derived from the same plant. In the phytoremediation experiments, synthetic wastewater solutions containing Cd, Ni, and Pb at varying concentrations (0.5, 1.0, 3.0, and 5.0 mg/L) were exposed to the aquatic plant. Metals concentrations were monitored daily, while the percentage removal was calculated to assess uptake efficiency. In parallel, batch adsorption studies were conducted using biochar prepared from the same plant (L. gibba) to evaluate the capacity for heavy metal removal under controlled conditions. The metal uptake L. gibba exhibited good removal rates, particularly for Pb and Cd, followed by Ni. At the same time L. gibba biochar showed good yield (44.5%) and adsorption performance, with removal ranked Pb > Cd > Ni. Overall, results demonstrate that the combined use of aquatic plants for phytoremediation and their conversion into biochar for adsorption provides an effective, low-cost, and environmentally sustainable strategy for removing heavy metals from industrial wastewater. The dual use of biomass not only maximizes remediation efficiency but also reduces plant waste, offering a circular and eco-friendly treatment solution. Keywords:

articles.title: A Parallel Quantum–Classical Hybrid Architecture for Image Classification
articles.abstract: This paper presents a parallel quantum–classical hybrid architecture for image classification that integrates classical feature extraction with parallel quantum processing while maintaining competitive performance and improving parameter efficiency. Low-level and intermediate image features are first extracted by a shared convolutional neural network and then processed by multiple parallel quantum branches. Each branch employs a multilayer variational quantum circuit with a rotation–entanglement–rotation structure. To enhance representation diversity, two encoding-specific strategies are introduced. For amplitude encoding, deterministic spatial permutations generate distinct structural views of the same feature map across branches. For angle encoding, a layer-wise data re-uploading mechanism injects complementary feature subsets into different branches and circuit layers. Heterogeneous entanglement topologies with dynamic routing further diversify qubit interactions without increasing the number of trainable parameters. The measured expectation values from all branches are concatenated and fed into a compact linear classifier. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and a thermal image dataset show that the proposed architecture achieves 98.35% accuracy on MNIST and competitive results on the other two datasets, while using substantially fewer parameters in the classification head than a fully classical baseline with the same feature extractor. These results demonstrate that parallel quantum processing combined with structured data embedding can serve as an effective and parameter-efficient decision stage for image classification.

articles.title: Absorber Doping Controls Internal Electric Field and Transport- Recombination Trade-Off in Perovskite Solar Cells: A SILVACO ATLAS TCAD Study
articles.abstract: Perovskite solar cells combine strong optical absorption with favorable carrier-transport properties, but their performance remains highly sensitive to the electrical properties of the absorber, particularly its doping level. In this work, SILVACO ATLAS TCAD is used to investigate how absorber doping modifies the electrical response of a planar (:CH₃NH₃PbI₃) absorber layer in an (:ITO/NiO/CH₃NH₃PbI₃/ZnO/Au) architecture. Photovoltaic parameters, including open-circuit voltage (:łeft(Vₒci̊ght)), short-circuit current density (:łeft(Jₛci̊ght)), fill factor (FF), efficiency (:łeft(η:i̊ght)), together with effective series and shunt resistances, were extracted from the simulated current–voltage characteristics. Spatially resolved energy-band bending, electrostatic potential, internal electric field, photogeneration, and recombination profiles were then analyzed to connect the microscopic electrostatic response to the macroscopic photovoltaic behavior. The results show that a doping concentration of (:5×:10¹⁶:cm⁻³) provides the compromise between carrier transport, resistive losses, and recombination, yielding a maximum efficiency of 23.35%. Two competing regimes emerge: from low to intermediate doping, improved conductivity and interfacial electrostatics enhance charge extraction, whereas at high doping, field localization and strongly increased bulk recombination progressively reduce carrier collection despite continued gains in some voltage- and fill-factor-related indicators. Because photogeneration remains essentially unchanged, the efficiency optimum results from a transport-recombination trade-off rather than an optical effect

articles.title: Hybrid CRITIC-VIKOR-Taguchi method of evaluating mechanical properties of magnesium alloy welded joint with cerium powder addition at weld interface
articles.abstract: Magnesium alloys reactivity with oxygen is very high and produce more defects when welded by employing fusion welding processes. Solid state welding processes do not melt the material and hence the problem can be reduced to a greater extent. Friction stir welding (FSW) is one of the solid state welding processes has gained popularity,of late, due to higher productivity coupling to achieve superior mechanical properties. In the present research, a hybrid CRITIC–VIKOR–Taguchi framework was developed in tackling the multi criterion decision making issues. Taguchi method was employed for selection of experimental matrix efficiently, while the CRITIC (Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation) method was used to objectively determine the relative weights to the responses under consideration. Subsequently, the VIKOR multi-criteria decision-making technique was applied to identify the optimum welding conditions based on Taguchi technique. The proposed methodology simultaneously considered ultimate tensile strength (UTS), impact toughness, and microhardness as the key performance characteristics. At optimal parameter condition the UTS is 103MPa, Impact toughness is 1.63J while micro hardness is 6.95Hv. The tool rotational speed is governing the achievement of responses to the extent of 47.83%, weld speed is contributing by 18.73% while tool tilt angle is to the tune of 10.51%. Microstructural characterization using scanning electron microscopy revealed significant grain refinement within the stir zone, contributing to enhanced mechanical performance and improved joint integrity. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid CRITIC–VIKOR–Taguchi approach effectively balances multiple conflicting performance objectives and provided an optimal solution.

articles.title: A Compact Flexible EBG Wearable Antenna with Hybrid Dual Annealing and PSO Optimization for 2.4 GHz WBANApplications
articles.abstract: Wearable antennas for wireless body area networks (WBANs) must maintain stable impedance matching and radiation efficiency while operating near lossy, high-permittivity human tissue. This study introduces a compact, flexible wearable antenna backed by an electromagnetic band-gap structure, designed to operate near 2.4 GHz. The antenna is developed on a 0.4-mm-thick polyimide substrate with a relative permittivity of 3.5 and loss tangent of 0.0027, occupying only 26 × 20 × 0.4 mm³. An S-shaped slotted radiator, defected ground structure, and rectangular-ring EBG reflector are integrated to improve impedance matching, suppress backward radiation, and reduce body-loading effects. The proposed antenna achieves a S11 of − 53 dB, a peak gain of 6.5 dB, and a maximum radiation efficiency of 93% near 2.4 GHz. Numerical evaluation using a CST voxel human-body model indicates low specific absorption rate with values of 0.0135 W/kg averaged over 1 g and 0.00229 W/kg averaged over 10 g of tissue. A hybrid Dual Annealing–Particle Swarm Optimization technique is employed for geometry optimization, achieving MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and R² values of 1.25 dB, 1.60 dB, 4.2%, and 0.97, respectively. The antenna also maintains stable impedance characteristics under bending, demonstrating its suitability for flexible WBAN communication and wearable sensing applications.

articles.title: Field evidence for rapid precipitation of non-crystalline secondary phases during enhanced rock weathering
articles.abstract: Terrestrial enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is a proposed carbon dioxide removal strategy based on the application of silicate rock powder to soils. By introducing fresh mineral surfaces into soils, ERW can lead to the formation of reactive secondary phases, including poorly crystalline aluminosilicates such as allophane and imogolite. Despite their potential impact on both soil properties and the effectiveness of ERW, direct field evidence for the formation of these secondary phases remains elusive. Here we applied a basaltic rock powder (20 t ha− 1) to three temperate fields and investigated the formation of secondary phases using selective dissolution and scanning electron microscopy. We show that secondary phases formation occurs as early as seven months after rock powder application. In surface soils (0–3 cm), oxalate-extractable aluminum and silicon increased by 108% ± 30% and 682% ± 302%, respectively, suggesting a rapid formation of poorly crystalline aluminosilicate phases. Imaging further revealed the presence of allophane-like spherules and smectite precursors on the weathering rock powder surfaces. These findings demonstrate that ERW initiates rapid pedogenic transformations on annual timescales, highlighting the need to consider secondary phase formation when assessing the effectiveness and soil impacts of ERW-based CO2 removal.

articles.title: A VAR(1)-Regularized Spatial Pattern Regression for Temporally Coherent Reconstruction of High-Resolution Meteorological Fields
articles.abstract: Accurate reconstruction of high-resolution meteorological fields from sparse station observations remains challenging, particularly in poorly instrumented regions where spatial and temporal information is limited. Most spatial interpolation methods treat observations independently in time and may therefore introduce artificial day-to-day variability in the reconstructed fields. We introduce Temporally-constrained Spatial Pattern Regression (T-SPR), an extension of Spatial Pattern Regression (SPR) that combines anomaly-based spatial interpolation with temporal regularization of the pattern coefficients. An intermediate anomaly-based formulation (A-SPR) is considered to isolate the contribution of the anomaly decomposition. The three approaches are evaluated using high-resolution regional climate model simulations across three station densities and validated with real daily observations of precipitation, minimum temperature, and maximum temperature in southern Québec, Canada. Results show that anomaly decomposition substantially improves spatial reconstruction under sparse observational conditions, with the largest gains for temperature variables. Temporal regularization provides additional improvements under extremely sparse conditions and, more importantly, increases robustness by reducing sensitivity to station configuration while improving temporal consistency. Validation with 100 Monte Carlo station configurations further demonstrates that T-SPR produces more stable spatial and temporal performance, with reduced variability in reconstruction errors and temporal diagnostics.These results demonstrate that combining climatological information with temporal coherence provides a robust and computationally efficient framework for reconstructing meteorological fields from highly sparse observation networks.

articles.title: Lightweight Edge-Based Telemetry Parsing for Navigation Systems via Deterministic Spatial-Text (LODTE)
articles.abstract: The traditional methods for parsing real time navigation telemetry in digital map interfaces rely on cloud centric vision architectures or heavy convolutional neural networks. The former systems cause high network latency, large bandwidth overhead and risks to data privacy - this paper presents the Lightweight Edge Based Telemetry Parsing (LODTE) framework, which is a deterministic spatial text bounding architecture made for edge execution on hardware with limited resources. By removing cloud dependencies, the system uses a localized contour geometry filter that limits dimensions to target specific spatial boundaries between 52 and 168 pixels in width and 38 and 54 pixels in height. It integrates high speed screen-capture buffering through mss and it extracts ETA plus distance tokens in real time while it uses little computational power. In empirical benchmarking, the results show an average total processing latency of under 35 milliseconds per frame across edge hardware nodes. The framework removes all cloud roundtrip overhead and it maintains high optical recognition fidelity when background complexities vary.

articles.title: A corrosion-aware digital-twin framework for condition monitoring of saline-water centrifugal pumps
articles.abstract: Coexisting corrosion surface degradation and Metallo mechanical condition evolution in marine centrifugal pumps are rarely captured in a condition-monitoring paradigm. A corrosion-aware digital-twin paradigm for saline-water centrifugal pumps is demonstrated by secondary analysis of a 200-h saline-water experimental data. Empirical data are separates from derived quantities, model-form assumptions, and virtual-model outputs; an ambiguity in surface-roughness uncertainty is included in the formation of an equivalent sand grain-roughness parameter for computational fluid dynamics model of as-created pumps. A 316L stainless-steel centrifugal pump operating in 30 parts per thousand synthetic seawaters at 2900 rpm is studied at 0, 50, 100, 150, and 200 h. Over 200 h, head decreased from 12.0 to 10.7 m, flow from 1.50 to 1.38 L/s, electrical-input efficiency from 70.6% to 58.0%, vibration from 0.20 to 0.75 mm/s, and Ra from 0.8 to 3.4 µm. The dataset is reorganized into a multidomain state representation. Using kₛ = αRa with α = 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 gives a 200 h screening envelope of 1.7–6.8 µm. The framework combines sensing, state estimation, virtual modeling, residual analysis, and maintenance support without claiming validated CFD, machine-learning, failure probability or RUL models. The contribution is thus probably a reproducible, explainable digital-twin framework, with the right evidence, state representation, and model interfaces, for enabling and validating fleet management. MSC2020: 90B25 — Reliability, availability, maintenance, inspection in operations research

articles.title: Development of a Quasi-Static MHD Solver for Turbulent Flows with Non-Uniform Applied Magnetic Fields in OpenFOAM
articles.abstract: The magnetic-induction implementation of low-magnetic-Reynolds-number (low-Rm ) magnetohydrodynamics develops a severe discrete cancellation error when the applied magnetic field is not uniform. The Lorentz force is evaluated in Maxwell-stress form as the difference of two terms of order B02 /(µ0ρL), an acceleration in m.s−2 — the force per unit volume divided by ρ; that cancellation is exact at the continuous level, but its discrete counterpart is exact only for a uniform imposed field. A non-uniform field therefore leaves a residual body force that grows with the square of the applied field and, as Sect. 5.6 shows, does not decrease over the refinement range investigated. For a 10 T field in a 0.15 m duct it reaches 103 m.s−2 , two orders of magnitude above the physical Lorentz acceleration, and the solution diverges within two time steps. Then, was developed the mhdturbFoamQS (QS for quasi-static), a finite-volume OpenFOAM solver that removes the residual by construction. The current density is obtained from the electric-potential (quasi-static) formulation and the Lorentz force is evaluated directly as j×B0 , so that no quantity of order B02 /(µ0ρL) is ever subtracted from another. The applied field is prescribed as a general volVectorField rather than a constant; the insulating-wall condition j · n = 0 is imposed consistently on both sides of the discrete potential equation; and the stiff magnetic sink is discretised implicitly, so that magnetic damping no longer restricts the time step. The standard OpenFOAM closures are used unmodified, which isolates the electromagnetic formulation from additional turbulence-model changes. Verification against the exact Hartmann solution reproduces the friction factor within 0.17 % and the velocity profile within 0.5 %, and the solver is further assessed against the Shercliff–Gold solution for a circular pipe with insulating walls. The solver and its verification case are released under GPL v3 with a concept DOI on Zenodo.

articles.title: Reproducibility of Spin-Dependent Band Edges in Ordered Invere-Spinel NiFe2O4: Magnetic-State Resolution and Convergence Verification
articles.abstract: First-principles calculations of correlated magnetic materials can converge to different magnetic and Hubbard states. A calculation can therefore satisfy a strict numerical threshold and still end in a different electronic state from another run. This paper studies that problem for an ordered tetragonal model of inverse-spinel NiFe2O4 (NFO) in space group 𝑃4122 using spin-polarized PBE+𝑈 calculations. Three questions are treated separately: numerical convergence, magnetic-state ordering, and reproducibility of the spin-dependent band edges. The wave-function and charge-density cutoffs converge at 160 Ry and 1080 Ry. Spin-reversal and MPI tests reproduce the same reference state through different numerical paths. A separate magnetic-state comparison at a 10−8 Ry SCF threshold places uud 135.825 meV per NiFe2O4 formula unit below uuu under the same calculation settings. Independent 6 × 6 × 4 and 8 × 8 × 4 NSCF calculations both give a conduction-band separation of Δ𝐸C = 0.4405 eV. The corresponding PBE+𝑈 gaps are 𝐸g↑ = 0.1548 eV and 𝐸g↓ = 0.5556 eV. The spin-up conduction edge has strong O-2𝑝 and Ni-3𝑑 character, while the spin-down edge has much more Fe-3𝑑 character. The two spin channels therefore differ in both energy and orbital composition. These results give a reproducible electronic reference for this ordered NFO model and show that a small SCF residual alone does not prove that a unique electronic state has been found.

articles.title: Broadly Applicable Approximate MCMC for Switching Stochastic Differential Equations Using Uniformization and Time-Conditioned Factorized Neural Likelihood Estimation
articles.abstract: Switching stochastic differential equations (SSDEs) describe continuous-time dynamics whose parameters switch according to a latent regime process that follows a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). By allowing dynamics to change between regimes, SSDEs represent heterogeneous system behavior and have been applied across diverse fields. However, Bayesian inference for SSDEs remains difficult, and existing SSDE inference methods have limited applicability, with restrictions such as noise-free observations, univariate states, linear drift, or state-independent diffusion. In this study, we propose an approximate Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler for SSDEs using uniformization and factorized neural likelihood estimation (FNLE), a simulation-based inference method. Uniformization provides an exact representation of the CTMC but requires SDE transition densities over arbitrary time intervals. We approximate these densities by training a time-conditioned FNLE model. The resulting sampler is broadly applicable to SSDEs without requiring analytically tractable transition densities. In synthetic-data experiments, our method recovered regime paths and parameters for three SSDE models for which previous methods have limited applicability. We also applied our method to a real dataset and detected a regime transition.

articles.title: Physical neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
articles.abstract: Physical neural networks promise low-power machine learning by computing directly with analogue device physics, yet many architectures require nonlinear devices to act as scalar weights or as fixed, identical activation functions, discarding potential computational resources. Inspired by Kolmogorov--Arnold networks, we place a trainable nonlinear function on every connection, making each physical edge a learnable computational element. We realise these edges as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays and transfer trained networks directly to hardware, with quantified fidelity across approximately 35,000 experimentally realised connections. On smooth, continuously valued tasks learned from imperfect signals---six-axis robotic kinematics from actuator-corrupted observations, continuous-action reinforcement learning, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking---the networks match or exceed multilayer perceptrons with substantially fewer trainable parameters and far fewer physical connections. A dedicated CMOS implementation of the photovoltaic controller is projected to consume approximately 35 muW. Replacing the filters with simulated memristor circuits reproduces the advantage, showing that it follows from the architecture instead of one particular device. Making device nonlinearity trainable, instead of suppressing it, offers a route to compact analogue networks for the types of smooth, continuous inference and control tasks studied here.

articles.title: Resource Percolation and Consensus Formation in Multiplex Research Networks
articles.abstract: Innovation is increasingly viewed as a product of complex interactions within multi-actor networks rather than the output of isolated institutions. While theoretical models like the Triple Helix describe the interplay between university, industry, and government, traditional analyses often treat these systems as single-layered, overlooking the hierarchical and striated nature of modern research organizations. This paper proposes a mathematical framework to analyze innovation networks as strategically focused multiplex systems, where distinct layers of actors—ranging from core research hubs to peripheral assistants—interact across complex dyadic linkages. Utilizing longitudinal data from Center Y, a research centre of excellence in a Sub-Saharan African university (name withheld to protect institutional and individual identities), we apply Laplacian consensus dynamics and percolation theory to evaluate system robustness and resource efficiency. By modeling intra-layer and inter-layer topologies, we demonstrate how external funding signals diffuse through the network to foster institutional consensus. Our findings reveal a "Rich-Club" core characterized by high clustering and density, which facilitates rapid information exchange but also creates a "Percolation Gap" that can starve the periphery of innovation signals. The empirical network exhibits Scale-Free properties, suggesting that while the system is resilient to random disruptions, it remains highly sensitive to the connectivity of core hubs. The study concludes that effective resource mobilization is fundamentally a topological challenge. To maximize institutional sustainability, funding strategies must prioritize inter-layer bridging to narrow the percolation gap. By shifting toward connectivity-centric models, research management can ensure that innovation successfully permeates all levels of the organizational ecosystem.

articles.title: Quantifying Epistemic Uncertainty in Ground Motion Prediction Using Bayesian Neural Networks: Application to Peninsular India
articles.abstract: Ground-motion models (GMMs) for probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA) in data-sparse regions are constrained by limited recordings and incomplete sampling of magnitude, distance, and site conditions. Inadequate characterization of epistemic uncertainty can therefore produce overconfident ground-motion predictions and poorly constrained hazard estimates. This study develops a Bayesian neural network GMM (BNN-GMM) for Peninsular India that separately characterizes epistemic uncertainty and aleatory variability. The model predicts PGA, PGV, and 5%-damped pseudo-spectral acceleration at 20 periods from 0.01 to 3.0 s as functions of moment magnitude, Joyner–Boore distance, (:VS₃₀), and focal depth, using data compiled from NGA-East, regional strong-motion records, and the NEar-Source Strong-motion flat file. The network contains two Bayesian hidden layers with mean-field Gaussian parameter distributions and is trained through variational inference, with its architecture and hyperparameters selected by Bayesian optimization. On the test dataset, the model achieves an (:R²)of 0.817 and a mean squared error of 0.824 while reproducing physically consistent magnitude, distance, site, depth, and spectral scaling. Epistemic uncertainty is quantified from Monte Carlo samples of the posterior network parameters, whereas aleatory variability is estimated by mixed-effects decomposition of logarithmic residuals. Aleatory standard deviations range from 0.76 to 0.89 natural-log units, compared with scenario-dependent epistemic standard deviations of approximately 0.04–0.11. Validation against significant PI earthquakes and established GMMs demonstrates consistent attenuation and spectral trends. PSHA sensitivity analyses demonstrate that propagation of BNN-derived epistemic uncertainty through the hazard integral produces systematic increases in spectral acceleration estimates relative to an aleatory-only treatment, with the magnitude of this effect varying as a function of site, spectral period, and annual exceedance rate, and becoming most pronounced at long return periods for Mumbai and Hyderabad. This site and exceedance rate dependent behaviour indicates that epistemic uncertainty cannot be represented adequately by a uniform adjustment to the median ground-motion prediction. Instead, it should be propagated through the hazard calculation using period- and scenario-dependent epistemic branches to obtain a more complete characterization of ground-motion exceedance probabilities in regions with sparse strong-motion data.

articles.title: Exploration of High-Entropy Engineered Skutterudite as a Route to Tunable Electronic and Magneto-Thermal Functionalities
articles.abstract: High-entropy alloys have in recent years emerged as a transformative materials design paradigm offering vast compositional space to explore various properties of interest. However, their exploration has largely focused on simple metallic solid solutions. Here, we extend the high-entropy concept to complex caged intermetallic systems, specifically the Skutterudites, RT4X12 (R = rare-earth or alkaline-earth filler atom, T = transition metal, X = pnictogen), as a new viable platform for entropy-stabilized electronic materials. The Skutterudite structure provides multiple crystallographic sublattices, allowing controlled configurational disorder while preserving structural integrity. Using the Special Quasirandom Structure (SQS) approach coupled with density functional theory studies to predict phase stability and electronic properties of the novel high-entropy composition, (La0.25Ce0.25Pr0.25Nd0.25(Fe0.5Co0.5)4(As0.25Se0.25Sb0.25Te0.25)12. Its formation energy is −0.17495 eV/atom, and the configurational entropy, Sconf = 1.223R/f.u., which is significant for a material that reflects substantial multisublattice chemical disorder and strong site ordering. The As/Se/Sb/Te sublattice has a lattice mismatch of 7.37%, a feature which is attributed to the observed local lattice strain and could be beneficial for improved thermodynamic stability. The magnetism is driven by the Fe/Co sublattice and is itinerant in nature. Electronic structure calculations indicate features reminiscent of metals or semimetals, and the band structure reveals broadened electronic bands with the loss of sharp Bloch character. These results indicate that Skutterudites exhibit exceptional tolerance to multicomponent site mixing, with formation energies remaining within the stable regime. The lattice distortion coupled with alloy disorder scattering, impurity scattering, and inherent structural intricacy are expected to strongly suppress lattice thermal conductivity.

articles.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence-Based Maximum Power Point Voltage Prediction for Photovoltaic Systems under Varying Environmental Conditions
articles.abstract: In PV solar system, the MPPT controller plays a vital role by continuously extracting maximum available power by the custom of DC/DC converter and an embedded electronic system with a control algorithm. Though, the complex nonlinear relationship among PV parameters poses significant challenges for traditional and machine learning approaches. To overcome the issues, this study introduces a Fine-Grained Attention-Aware Deep Learning-Based Maximum Power Point Voltage Prediction (FGADL-MPPVP) Model, aiming to develop an interpretable and accurate MPPVP of a PV system under varying environmental conditions. The PV model employed attention-aware residual deep neural architecture to enhance nonlinear representation learning and support stable feature propagation, whereas the attention mechanism highlights the most significant environmental features for model prediction. Furthermore, the schedule-free AdamW optimizer is used to improve the model transparency, generalization capability and minimize overfitting. The experimental outcomes demonstrate that the proposed model precisely estimates the maximum power point voltage using temperature and solar irradiance; these findings highlight the potential of the proposed model over existing techniques and validate its superiority for maximum power point voltage prediction in PV energy management and MPPT applications.

articles.title: The Refutation Gap: Certifying Both Halves of an Optimality Claim
articles.abstract: Synthesis pipelines increasingly claim not just that a program is correct, but that it is optimal. Such a claim has two halves with radically different verification stories. The upper bound, “a program of size m exists”, is witnessed by an artifact that can be re-executed, proved equivalent to its specification, and shipped with a machine-checked certificate. The lower bound, “no program of size m − 1 exists”, has no witness at all, and is discharged by running a solver until it reports UNSAT. Combinatorial optimization has known this for a long time and has largely fixed it: certifying algorithms make the asymmetry explicit [18], and pseudo-Boolean proof logging now certifies optimality end to end with a formally verified checker [1, 14]. That discipline has not reached circuit minimization. We call the asymmetry, where it persists, the refutation gap: twenty-five years of published gate counts for minimal XOR circuits ship no certificate for either half of the claim, no lower bound is published in the metric those counts report, and neither did 121 optimality results we ourselves produced. We close it in a working pipeline that synthesizes minimal linear straight-line programs over GF(2), where every decisive UNSAT answer now emits a DRAT proof checked by an independent third-party checker. We certify all 121 optimality results the project had established, across n = 6–9: 111 carry a refutation that an independent checker verifies, 10 are closed by a free counting bound, and none disagrees with the uncertified value. The median proof is 1.1MB and checking costs 1.9× solving. Along the way we give five case studies in which a verification layer caught a real defect code review did not; report two interface obstacles: a solver whose proofs the checker rejects, and a fast equivalence check that silently returns unknown, each pushing practitioners toward the uncertified path; and describe an adversarial audit of our own write-up, which found that a failure tail we were about to report as a property of the problem was an artifact of our own budget.

articles.title: Eddies on the Edge: Cyclonic Frontal Dynamics along the Agulhas Current
articles.abstract: Cyclonic frontal eddies frequently occur inshore of the Agulhas Current along the east coast of South Africa where numerous Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) have been designated, yet their structure, evolution, and role in coastal circulation remain poorly quantified due to observational limitations. Here, we investigate the frequency, life cycle, and dynamics of these eddies using a realistic ocean simulation combined with an eddy detection algorithm. Over the 5-year simulation, 366 cyclonic frontal eddies were identified, recurring approximately every 5 days and exhibiting a wide range of lifespans (4–42 days), spatial scales (11–28 km), and velocities (translation: 0.15 --0.18 m s((⁻¹)); tangential: 0.1 - 0.74 m s((⁻¹))) that are comparable to local and global observations. Two distinct eddy types are identified in the KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) Bight: stationary eddies confined to the KZN Bight and propagating eddies that advect downstream along the coast. Potential vorticity analysis and Lagrangian particle tracking from a long-lived case study reveals that these eddies are surface-intensified features originating from the inshore frictional boundary layer of the Agulhas Current. The associated circulation governs their spatio-temporal evolution and drives strong vertical mixing along the coast. Through particle retention and transient counter-currents the frontal eddies strongly influence coastal connectivity, with important implications for MPAs along the South African east coast.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Optimization of Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Energy-Efficient 6G Communication Systems
articles.abstract: The potential of Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) in upcoming 6G wireless communication systems is drawing a lot of attention due to their capacity to improve communication performance with low power consumption and reduced hardware complexity. By intelligently manipulating wireless signal propagation, IRS can enhance both spectral efficiency and energy efficiency while supporting reliable connectivity in dynamic communication environments.
